śāntidevaviracitaḥ bodhicaryāvatāraḥ /
prajñākaramativiracitayā pañjikākhyavyākhyayā saṃvalitaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> composed by <s>Śāntideva</s>, accompanied by the commentary called <s>Pañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.

body.text: // om namo buddhāya /
body.translated_text: // Oṃ, homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! /

body.text: 1. bodhicittānuśaṃso nāma prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter 1, entitled "The Benefits of <s>Bodhicitta</s>" (<s>Bodhicittānuśaṃsa</s>).

children.translated_text: Having reverently bowed to the <s>Sugatas</s> together with their sons and the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, and to all who are worthy of veneration,
I shall briefly describe, in accordance with scripture, the entry into the discipline of the sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>. // Bca_1.1 //

body.text:
............ akhilāṃśca bandyāniti kalyāṇamitraprabhṛtīnām / sugatātmajasaṃvarāvatāramiti abhidheyakathanam / kathayiṣyāmīti prayojanābhidhānam / saṃbandhapratipādanapadaṃ tu na vidyate, sāmarthyādeva tu sa pratipattavyaḥ / yathāgamamiti svātantryaparihārapadam / samāsāditi punaruktatāparihāravacanam / iti samudāyārthaḥ / avayavārthastu ucyate / sugatānityatra gataśabdena sarvapṛthagjanebhyo bhagavatāṃ vyavacchedaṃ darśayati, teṣāṃ saṃsārāntargatatvāt, bhagavatāṃ tu saṃsāravinirgatatvāt / suśabdastu praśastādyarthatrayavṛttiviśiṣṭaṃ suga.......... / tenāyamarthaḥ- praśastaṃ yathā bhavati evaṃ madhyamapratipadā kleśādyāvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ gatāḥ sugatāḥ / anena prahāṇasaṃpattiruktā / yadi vā / praśastaṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatātattvaṃ gatā adhigatāḥ sugatāḥ / anena adhigamasaṃpadupadarśitā / ya[di vā]..............tīrthikaśāstṛbhyo bhagavatāṃ viśeṣaścopadarśito bhavati / teṣāmātmādibhāvābhiniveśavaśāt praśastagamanābhāvāt / ātmādīnāṃ ca pramāṇabādhitatvāt / saṃsārāpratipakṣatvācca apraśastaṃ gamanam / apunarāvṛttyā vā gatāḥ, punarjanmano rāgādinā ......... haṃkāraśuddhayā ahaṃkārabījasya avidyāyāḥ sarvathā prahāṇāt sugatāḥ / anena strotaāpannasakṛdāgāmibodhisattvebhyo 'pi bhagavatāṃ viśeṣo darśitaḥ / teṣāṃ praśastagamane 'pi sarvadhātvaprahāṇāt punarāvṛttisaṃbhavāt / niḥśeṣaṃ vā ..........sarvavāsanāyā api kāyabāgbuddhivaiguṇyalakṣaṇāyāḥ svayamadhigatamārgoktāvapāṭavasya vā sarvathā prahāṇāt sugatāḥ / etāvatā saṃpūrṇagāmitvaṃ bhagavatāṃ pratipāditam / anenāpi anāgāmiśrāvakapratyekabuddhebhyo bhagavatāmasādhāraṇaguṇatvamāveditam / teṣāṃ..........kāyavāgbuddhivaiguṇyasya svādhigatamārgoktayapāṭavasya ca saṃbhavāt / evaṃ ca buddhatvamaśeṣaguṇasarasamasādhāraṇamaparayogibhiḥ
sugataśabdena khyāpitam / tānevaṃbhūtān sugatānādarataḥ paramaprasādena praṇipatyeti
body.translated_text: ............ "And to all who are worthy of veneration" — the spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) and others. "The entry into the discipline of the sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>" — this is the statement of the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>). "I shall describe" — this is the statement of the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>). The word establishing the connection (<s>saṃbandha</s>), however, is not found [explicitly], but it should be understood by implication. "In accordance with scripture (<s>yathāgamam</s>)" — this is a word disclaiming independence. "Briefly (<s>samāsāt</s>)" — this is a statement avoiding redundancy. Such is the meaning of the whole [verse]. Now the meaning of the individual [words] is explained. In "<s>Sugatas</s>" — here by the word "gone" (<s>gata</s>) he shows the distinction of the Blessed Ones from all ordinary persons, since those [ordinary persons] are within <s>saṃsāra</s>, while the Blessed Ones have gone beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>. The prefix "su" (well/good) operates in three senses of excellence, etc., distinguishing.......... The meaning is thus: they have "gone well" (<s>sugata</s>) — i.e., they have gone by the Middle Way to the abandonment of the obscurations of defilements and so forth, in such a way that it is excellent. By this, the perfection of abandonment is stated. Or alternatively: they have "gone to" — i.e., realized — the excellent reality of the naturelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. By this, the perfection of realization is indicated. [Or alternatively].......... the distinction of the Blessed Ones from the teachers of the <s>tīrthikas</s> is shown. Since those [<s>tīrthikas</s>], due to their adherence to the existence of a self and so forth, lack an excellent going. And since a self, etc., are refuted by valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). And since [their going] is not an antidote to <s>saṃsāra</s>, their going is not excellent. Or alternatively: they have "gone without return" — since, through the purification of the I-making (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), the seed of I-making, namely ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), has been completely abandoned — [they are] <s>Sugatas</s>. By this, the distinction of the Blessed Ones even from stream-enterers, once-returners, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is shown — since those [others], even though their going is excellent, can still return due to the non-abandonment of all [defilement-]elements. Or alternatively:.......... since [they have attained] complete abandonment of all residual tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) as well — which are characterized by deficiencies of body, speech, and intellect — and of the lack of skill in expressing the path they have realized — [they are] <s>Sugatas</s>. By this, the complete perfection of going of the Blessed Ones is established. By this too, the uncommon qualities of the Blessed Ones are made known, distinguishing them even from non-returner <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — since those [others].......... may still have deficiencies of body, speech, and intellect, and lack of skill in expressing their realized path. Thus, Buddhahood — the fullness of all qualities in their entirety, uncommon and not shared by others — is proclaimed by the word <s>Sugata</s>. Having reverently bowed with supreme devotion to such <s>Sugatas</s> —

body.text: namaskṛtya sugatātmajasaṃvarāvatāraṃ kathayiṣyāmiti saṃbandhaḥ / kiṃbhūtān? sasutāniti / sutāśca munīnāmiha labdhapramuditādibhūmayo bodhisattvā eva gṛhyante / teṣāmeva atra adhikṛtatvāt / taiḥ saha / anena viśeṣaṇena āryasaṃghasya namaskāro 'ntarbhāvitaḥ / aparaṃ viśeṣaṇamāhasadharmakāyāniti / sarvāpa [dvimu]kto bhagavatāṃ svābhāviko dharmakāyaḥ / sa eva ca adhigamasvabhāvo dharmaḥ / samūhārtho vā kāyaśabdaḥ janakāyo balakāya iti yathā / tena pravacanasyāpi grahaṇam / tena saha / anenāpi dharmasya namaskāro 'ntarbhāvitaḥ iti / ratnatrayanamaskāro 'yamityu[ktaṃ bhavati] //
body.translated_text: — that is, having paid homage — "I shall describe the entry into the discipline of the sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>" — this is the syntactical connection. Of what kind [are they]? "Together with their sons" — and the sons of the sages here are understood as the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the first <s>bhūmi</s>, <s>Pramuditā</s>, and the others — since they alone are the primary subject here. "Together with" them. By this qualifier, homage to the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> is included. He states another qualifier: "together with the <s>Dharmakāya</s>." The inherent <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the Blessed Ones is free from all adversity. And that very [<s>Dharma</s>] is [their] realization-nature (<s>adhigamasvabhāva</s>). Or the word "body" (<s>kāya</s>) means "collection," as in "a body of people" or "a body of forces" — by which the [Buddha's] teaching (<s>pravacana</s>) is also included. "Together with" [that]. By this too, homage to the <s>Dharma</s> is included. [Thus] it is said that this is homage to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>). //

body.text: nanu buddhāddharmo dharmataśca āryasaṃgha iti kramaḥ / tat kimiti buddhānantaramāryasaṃghaḥ, tadanu dharma iti vyatikramanirdeśaḥ? satyam / iha ślokabandhānurodhād vyatikramanirdeśo veditavyaḥ / yojanāttu sugatān sadharmakāyān sasutān praṇipatya, iti anukrameṇaiva / na kaścidatra doṣaḥ / athavā / bodhisattvānāmapi adhigatadharmatvādānurūpyeṇa dharmakāyo vidyata eva / teṣāmapi saha dharmakāyena namaskaraṇaṃ pratipādanīyam / te 'pi hi samadhigatadharmatayā sugatatvaniyatāḥ sugataprāyāḥ / iti dharmāt pūrvaṃ nirdeśaḥ / iti na kiṃcidayuktam / kimetāneva? netyāha- akhilāṃśca bandyāniti / aparānapi samastān vandanīyān ācāryopādhyāyaprabhṛtīnapi / ādarataḥ praṇipatyeti / iti pūrvārdhena sugatādīnāṃ namaskṛtimabhidhāya aparārdhena abhidheyādīni pratipādayannāha- sugatātmajetyādi / ātmano jātāḥ ātmajāḥ / sugatānāmātmajāḥ jinaputrāḥ, bodhisattvā ityarthaḥ / teṣāṃ saṃvarāvatāram / saṃvaraṇaṃ saṃvriyate vā aneneti saṃvaraḥ, bodhicittagrahaṇapūrvakaṃ bodhisattvaśikṣāsamādānam / tacca yathāvasaraṃ vakṣyāmaḥ / tasya avataraṇam / avatīryate tasmin vā anenetyavatāro mārgaḥ, yena bodhisattvapadaprāptau sugatatvamavāpyate / taṃ kathayiṣyāmi pratipādayiṣyāmi / anena granthenetyarthaḥ / evamanena pratipādyamānatvāt saṃvarāvatāraḥ abhidheyamasya, ayamabhidhānaṃ saṃvarāvatārasya, iti abhidhānābhidheyalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandho 'pyarthāt kathitaḥ / tatkathanaṃ ca abhidhānaprayojanam / paramārthatastu abhidheyasvarūpavyutpattireva tatprayojanam / abhidheyasya punaḥ śrutamayyādiprajñotpādanakrameṇa sarvāvaraṇavigamād buddhatvameva prayojanamiti prayojananiṣṭhā / idaṃ ca sugatātmajasaṃvarāvatāraśabde eva antarbhāvitam / tadanantaramevokteḥ / yadanuśaṃsakathanena ca sūcayiṣyati /
body.translated_text: Objection: The order is: from the <s>Buddha</s> [comes] the <s>Dharma</s>, and from the <s>Dharma</s> [comes] the noble <s>Saṃgha</s>. Then why is the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> [mentioned] immediately after the <s>Buddha</s>, and then the <s>Dharma</s> — a transposed exposition? True. Here the transposed exposition should be understood as due to the requirements of verse composition. But in construing [the meaning]: "Having bowed to the <s>Sugatas</s> together with the <s>Dharmakāya</s> and together with their sons" — this is in proper order. There is no fault here. Alternatively, since <s>Bodhisattvas</s> too have realized the <s>Dharma</s>, they appropriately possess the <s>Dharmakāya</s> too. Paying homage to them too along with the <s>Dharmakāya</s> is to be demonstrated. For they too, by virtue of having equally realized the <s>dharmatā</s>, are determined for <s>Sugata</s>-hood, are as good as <s>Sugatas</s>. Hence the exposition before the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus nothing is inappropriate. Are these the only [objects of veneration]? No — he says: "and to all who are worthy of veneration" — also to all others who are to be venerated, such as preceptors (<s>ācārya</s>) and teachers (<s>upādhyāya</s>) and the rest. "Having reverently bowed" — thus. Having stated homage to the <s>Sugatas</s> and others in the first half [of the verse], he sets forth the subject matter and the rest in the second half, saying: "Of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>," etc. Those born from oneself are one's sons (<s>ātmaja</s>). The sons of the <s>Sugatas</s> — the sons of the Conquerors (<s>jinaputra</s>), i.e., the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Their discipline-entry (<s>saṃvarāvatāra</s>). The disciplining, or that by which one is disciplined, is the discipline (<s>saṃvara</s>) — the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training preceded by the adoption of <s>Bodhicitta</s>. And that we shall explain in due course. Its entering-into (<s>avataraṇa</s>): that by which one enters into it is the entry (<s>avatāra</s>) — the path by which, upon attaining the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, one achieves <s>Sugata</s>-hood. "I shall describe" that — i.e., I shall set it forth, by means of this treatise. Thus, since it is being set forth by this [treatise], the discipline-entry is the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>), and this [treatise] is the expression (<s>abhidhāna</s>) of the discipline-entry — thus the connection (<s>saṃbandha</s>) characterized by the relation of expression and subject matter is also implicitly stated. And the describing of that is the purpose of the expression (<s>abhidhānaprayojana</s>). But the ultimate purpose is the generation of understanding of the nature of the subject matter — the arising of wisdom, from hearing and the rest. And the final purpose of the subject matter is Buddhahood itself, through the removal of all obscurations by the progressive development of wisdom from hearing and the rest — this is the culmination of purpose (<s>prayojananiṣṭhā</s>). And this is already included within the very expression "entry into the discipline of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>." Since it was stated immediately thereafter. And which he will indicate by describing the benefits [of <s>Bodhicitta</s>].

body.text:
aśucipratimāmimāṃ gṛhītvā jinaratnapratimāṃ karotyanardhām /
[bodhi 1.10]
body.translated_text: "Taking this unclean image, he transforms it into the priceless image of a <s>Jina</s>-jewel." [Bodhi 1.10]

body.text: iti saṃbandhābhidheyaprayojanāni pravṛttyaṅgatayā pratipāditāni / anyathā anabhidheyādiśaṅkayā prekṣāvatāmatra pravṛttirna syāt / nanu tvayā svātantrayeṇa kathitaṃ kathanaṃ kathaṃ grahīṣyantītyāha- yathāgamamiti / āgamānatikrameṇa / yathaiva pravacane bhagavadbhiḥ pratipāditaḥ,
body.translated_text: Thus the connection, subject matter, and purpose have been set forth as the factors of engagement. Otherwise, through the suspicion that there is no [proper] subject matter, etc., the discerning would not engage with this [text]. Objection: Since you have spoken independently, how will [others] accept your teaching? He replies: "In accordance with scripture" — without transgressing scripture. Just as the Blessed Ones have taught in the canonical texts,

body.text: tathā mayāpi tadarthānativṛttyā pratipādayitavyaḥ / anena āgamāt svātantryaṃ parihṛtaṃ bhavati / utsūtramidaṃ na bhavatītyarthaḥ / pravacanārthāvagāhanamapi ca avakratayā anena ātmano darśitam / idamapi pravṛttyaṅgameva / nanu yadi yathāgamaṃ kathayitavyaḥ, tarhi āgame eva tadabhilāṣiṇaḥ pravartiṣyante, tatkimanenetyāha- samāsāditi / saṃkṣepāt / yadi nāma āgame 'pi kathitaḥ, tathāpi tatra ativistareṇa nānāsūtrānteṣu pratipādanāt / ahaṃ tu piṇḍīkṛtya saṃkṣepeṇa kathayiṣyāmīti viśeṣaḥ / anena punaruktamidaṃ bhavatīti parihṛtam / ayamapi ca apravṛttyaṅgatāparihāraḥ / tasmāt pravṛttyaṅgattvādabhidheyādikathanamasaṃgataṃ na bhavati- tarhi praṇāmakaraṇamapārthakam / tadapi śreyolābhādyarthamabhidhīyamānaṃ kathamapārthakam? ayamasyābhiprāyaḥsugatādipraṇāmasamudbhūtapuṇyasaṃbhārasamākrāntacittasaṃtānasya pratanutarapurākṛtapāpavṛtterūpaśāntavighnasya ārabdhārthaparisamāptirupajāyate / samastasādhujanagatamārgānugamanamapi ca anena ātmanaḥ prakāśitaṃ bhavet / iṣṭadevatādinamaskṛtiśravaṇādāstikatvasaṃbhāvanayā śrotṛṇāmātmagranthe ca gauravamāpāditaṃ syāt / atra ca sugataśabdena udbhāvitabhagavanduṇamāhātmyaśravaṇāt tadabhilāṣiṇaḥ tadupārjanapravaṇamānasāḥ sugatātmajasaṃvarāvatāraparijñānāya yatnavantaḥ asmin pravartante / idamabhimatadevatādipraṇāmaphalam / etena idamapi- yena yadabhimatamabhipretaṃ kartum, sa tadeva karotu nānyat / anyakaraṇe aprastutābhidhānamatiprasaṅgaśca syāt / tadayamapi saṃvarāvatārakathane kṛtābhiprāyaḥ kimaprastutamiṣṭadevatādipraṇāmaṃ karoti? prāguktadoṣadvayaprasaṅgāditi yaducyate, tadapi nirākṛtaṃ bhavati, tadupayogasya varṇitatvāt nāprastutābhidhānam / yat prakṛtopayogi tadvaktavyaṃ nānyat, ityatiprasaṅgo nāstīti sarvaṃ sustham //
body.translated_text: so too must I set it forth without exceeding that meaning. By this, independence from scripture is disclaimed. The meaning is: this does not deviate from the <s>sūtras</s>. And by this, he has shown his own penetration of the meaning of the canonical texts through [his] straightforwardness. This too is a factor of engagement. Objection: If it must be described in accordance with scripture, then those who desire it will turn to scripture itself — so what is the need for this [treatise]? He replies: "Briefly" — in summary. Even though it has indeed been stated in scripture, nevertheless there it is taught at great length in various <s>sūtrāntas</s>. But I shall teach it in condensed form, in summary — this is the distinction. By this, the [objection that] "this is a redundancy" is refuted. And this too is the removal of a factor of non-engagement. Therefore, since the stating of subject matter, etc., serves as a factor of engagement, it is not incongruous. "Then the paying of homage is purposeless." That too, being stated for the purpose of obtaining blessings and the like — how can it be purposeless? This is his intention: for one whose mental continuum is imbued with the accumulation of merit arising from bowing to the <s>Sugatas</s> and others, whose past evil deeds have become attenuated and whose obstacles are pacified — the accomplishment of the undertaken task arises. And by this, his own following of the path traversed by all virtuous people would also be made evident. And by hearing the homage to one's chosen deity and so forth, through the presumption of [the author's] piety, the audience's reverence for his treatise would be produced. And here, through hearing of the greatness of the Blessed One's qualities evoked by the word <s>Sugata</s>, those who aspire to those [qualities], with minds inclined toward acquiring them, make effort and engage in this [text] for the purpose of fully understanding the entry into the discipline of the sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>. This is the fruit of paying homage to one's chosen deity and so forth. By this, the following [objection] is also refuted: "Whatever one intends to do, one should do that very thing and not something else. Doing something else would constitute an irrelevant statement and an over-extension. So this [author], whose intention is the description of the discipline-entry — why does he perform the irrelevant homage to his chosen deity and so forth? Since the fault of the two [objections] mentioned above would follow" — this is what is said, but it is refuted, since its utility has been explained; it is not an irrelevant statement. Since what is useful to the subject at hand should be stated and nothing else, there is no over-extension — all is well. //

body.text: nanu āgamānatiriktaṃ saṃkṣepeṇābhidhīyamānamapi kathamarthaviśeṣādyabhāvādviśeṣeṇa pravṛttyaṅgatayā kasyacidupādeyaṃ syāt? tasmādāgamādadhikamapi kiṃcidatra vaktavyamityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: Objection: Even when described briefly and not exceeding scripture, how could this, lacking any distinctive meaning or the like, be specially worth adopting by anyone as a factor of engagement? Therefore, something additional beyond scripture should also be stated here — with this apprehension, he says:

children.text: na hi kiṃcidapūrvamatra vācyaṃ na ca saṃgrathanakauśalaṃ mamāsti /
children.translated_text: "There is nothing whatsoever new to be said here, nor do I possess skill in composition;

children.text: ata eva na me parārthacintā svamano vāsayituṃ kṛtaṃ mayedam // Bca_1.2 //
children.translated_text: therefore I have no thought for the benefit of others — I have composed this to habituate my own mind. // Bca_1.2 //

body.text: naiva kiṃcidapūrvamaparamāgamādatiriktamasmin vaktavyamasti mama / yasmādarthe vā hiśabdaḥ / tarhi tadadhikaprameyānabhidhāne 'pi padārtharacanāviśeṣo bhaviṣyati / tasmādapi viśeṣeṇa pravṛttiḥ syāditi / atrāha- na ceti / nāpi saṃgrathanamarthapadavinyāsaviśeṣaḥ, tatra kauśalaṃ naipuṇyaṃ mamāsti / avadhāraṇe vā cakāraḥ / yadyevam, kathamasya parārthopayogitvamiti /
body.translated_text: "Indeed there is nothing whatsoever new — i.e., additional to and exceeding scripture — to be said by me in this [treatise]." Since — or the word "hi" is [used] in the sense of "because." "Then at least there will be a distinction in the arrangement of words and meanings." "Therefore at least there would be a special reason for engagement" — to this he replies: "Nor" (<s>na ca</s>) — "nor do I possess skill (<s>kauśala</s>) — i.e., expertise — in composition (<s>saṃgrathana</s>) — i.e., in the distinctive arrangement of meanings and words." Or the particle "ca" is for emphasis. "If so, how can this be useful to others?"

body.text: āha- ata eveti / paraprasañjitameva abhyupagacchati / yasmādapūrvaṃ vaktuṃ mama śaktirnāsti / nāpi saṃgrathanakauśalamasti / na ca parārthacintāpi / parārthopayuktamidaṃ bhavatīti vikalpo 'pi me nāsti, tatra śktivaiguṇyāt / kimarthaṃ karaṇāya yatna iti cedāha- khamana iti / ātmacittaṃ sugatātmajasaṃvarāvatārābhyāsarasena adhikādhikaṃ vāsayituṃ kṛtaṃ praṇitaṃ mayā prakaraṇamidam / saṃvarāvatārakathanaṃ vā / atītakālanirdeśaḥ antastattvaniṣpannaṃ manasi nidhāyeti //
body.translated_text: He replies: "Therefore" (<s>ata eva</s>) — he accepts what has been argued by the opponent. "Since I have no ability to say anything new, nor do I have skill in composition, nor do I even have thought for the benefit of others — nor do I even entertain the idea that this might be useful to others, due to my deficiency in those capacities. Then for what purpose is the effort of composing?" To this he replies: "My own mind" (<s>svamanas</s>) — this treatise has been composed by me to increasingly habituate my own mind with the flavor of practicing the entry into the discipline of the sons of the <s>Sugatas</s>. Or [alternatively]: the description of the discipline-entry [was the purpose]. The reference to the past tense is made having placed in mind the inner reality already accomplished. //

body.text: nanu nātmārthaṃ granthapraṇayanaṃ dṛṣṭam, na ca svayaṃkṛtenaiva ātmani viśeṣādhānam, tāvataḥ saṃskāraviśeṣasya prāgevātmani vidyamānatvāditi / atrāha-
body.translated_text: Objection: The composition of a treatise for one's own sake is unprecedented, nor does one bring about a special [accomplishment] in oneself merely by one's own composition, since the particular mental formation for that already exists in oneself. To this he replies:

children.text: mama tāvadanena yāti vṛddhiṃ kuśalaṃ bhāvayituṃ prasādavegaḥ /
children.translated_text: "By this, at least my own momentum of faith toward cultivating the wholesome shall increase;
and if another of the same nature as myself should see this, then this too would be meaningful. // Bca_1.3 //

body.text: anena granthena vā / kuśalaṃ śubhamanaskāraṃ bhāvayitumārādhayitum / vṛddhiṃ yāti prasādavegaḥ / uttarottaravardhamānasya prasannacittasaṃtānasya pravāhavāhitayā pravṛttiḥ / anena svārthakāritvamanubhavasiddhamasya nidarśayati / parārthakāritvamapi leśataḥ saṃbhavati iti darśayannāha- atha matsametyādi / atheti prakārāntaropanyāse / svārthakāritvamasya tāvadanubhavasiddham / yadi punarmama samānaprakṛtireva kaścidanyaḥ paśyedīkṣeta, enaṃ granthamarthaṃ vā, ato 'pi parārthopayuktatvādapi sārthakaḥ saprayojano 'yam / parārthopayogasyāpi kathaṃcit saṃbhavāt / anena ślokena nirabhimānatāmātmano darśayati //
body.translated_text: Or, by this text, one's wholesome mental attention is cultivated and accomplished; the force of faith increases. The continuation proceeds through the stream-like flow of an increasingly purified mental continuum. By this, he demonstrates that its self-benefiting nature is established through experience. To show that benefiting others is also slightly possible, he says 'atha matsame' etc. 'Atha' introduces another manner. Its self-benefiting nature is first established through experience. But if some other person of the same nature as mine should see or examine this text or its meaning, then from this too, being useful for the benefit of others, it is meaningful and purposeful — since benefiting others is somehow possible. By this verse he demonstrates his own lack of pride.

body.text: idānīṃ saṃvarāvatārakathāṃ grāhayitumupoddhātaṃ racayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, composing a prologue in order to introduce the discourse on undertaking the vow, he says —

children.translated_text: This attainment of a [favorable] moment is extremely difficult to obtain, [yet] it accomplishes the aims of a person;

children.text: yadi nātra vicintyate hitaṃ punarapyeṣa samāgamaḥ kutaḥ // Bca_1.4 //
children.translated_text: if benefit is not reflected upon here, how could this conjunction come again? // Bca_1.4 //

body.text: aṣṭākṣaṇavinirmuktasya kṣaṇasya saṃpattiḥ samagratā / iyaṃ sudurlabhā suṣṭhu duḥkhena labhyata iti kathaṃcitprāpyā /
body.translated_text: The attainment, that is, the completeness of a [favorable] moment free from the eight unfavorable conditions (<s>akṣaṇa</s>). This is 'extremely difficult to obtain' — it is obtained only with extreme difficulty, that is, attainable only somehow.

body.text: mahārṇavayugacchidrakurmagrīvārpaṇopamā /
body.translated_text: Like the analogy of a blind turtle inserting its neck through a hole in a yoke floating on the great ocean.

body.text: pratilabdhā prāptā, sā ca puruṣārthasādhanī / puruṣasya arthaḥ abhyudayaniḥśreyasalakṣaṇaḥ, tasya sādhanī niṣpādanī / tadaṅgatvāt tatra samartheti yāvat / yadi ca evaṃbhūtāyāmapi asyāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Obtained' means attained. And it 'accomplishes the aims of a person.' The aim of a person is characterized by worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>); it 'accomplishes' — that is, brings about — that. Being a constituent thereof, it is capable of that. If even in such [a favorable condition]

body.text: na hitaṃ vicintyate, svaparasukhahetuḥ svargāpavargasādhanaṃ nopādīyate, tadā punarapi bhūyo 'pi eṣa tathāgatotpādaḥ śraddhākśaṇavimukto manuṣyabhāvaḥ ityayaṃ samāgamaḥ samāveśo milanamiti yāvat / kutaḥ katham? na kathaṃcidbhaviṣyati sudurlabhatvāt / akṣaṇāvasthāyāṃ dharmapravicayasya kartumaśakyatvāt, ityabhiprāyaḥ / yathoktamāryagaṇḍavyūhasūtre āryajayoṣmāyatanavimokṣe-
body.translated_text: 'benefit is not reflected upon' — if the cause of one's own and others' happiness, the means to heaven and liberation, is not undertaken — then 'again,' that is, once more, 'this conjunction' — this meeting, coming together — meaning: the arising of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, a human state free from the [unfavorable] moment of lacking faith — 'how could [it come]?' It will not come about in any way, because of its extreme rarity. The implication is that in an unfavorable condition, investigation of the <s>Dharma</s> is impossible to perform. As stated in the <s>Āryagaṇḍavyūhasūtra</s>, in the liberation of <s>Āryajayoṣmāyatana</s> —

body.text: durlabhā aṣṭākṣaṇavinivṛttiḥ / durlabho manuṣyabhāvapratilambhaḥ / durlabhā kṣaṇasaṃpadviśuddhiḥ / durlabho buddhotpādaḥ / durlabhā avikalendriyatā / durlabho buddhadharmaśravaṇaḥ / durlabhaṃ satpuruṣasamavadhānam / durlabhāni bhūtakalyāṇamitrāṇi / durlabho bhūtanayānuśāsanyupasaṃhāraḥ / durlabhaṃ samyagjīvitaṃ manuṣyaloke iti // [gaṇḍavyūhasūtra 116]
body.translated_text: Rare is freedom from the eight unfavorable conditions. Rare is the attainment of a human existence. Rare is the purity of a favorable moment. Rare is the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>. Rare is the completeness of faculties. Rare is hearing the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharma</s>. Rare is encounter with true persons. Rare are genuine spiritual friends. Rare is instruction through the genuine method. Rare is right livelihood in the human world. [<s>Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra</s> 116]

body.text: idamevābhisaṃdhāyoktam-
body.translated_text: With precisely this intention it was said —

children.translated_text: Humanity is rare in the world; the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is extremely rare;
rarer still is faith, going forth, and practice.
A firm mind toward awakening, out of compassion for all beings,
for the sake of the pacification of all suffering — this is the succession of rare [things].

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: akṣaṇāḥ punarime-
body.translated_text: The unfavorable conditions (<s>akṣaṇa</s>) are these —

children.translated_text: Hell-beings, hungry ghosts, animals, barbarians, long-lived gods,
wrong views, a <s>Buddha</s>-less era, and being mute — these are the eight unfavorable conditions.

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tasmādidānīmeva udyogaḥ kartavya iti //
body.translated_text: Therefore, exertion should be made right now.

body.text: sāṃprataṃ bodhicittagrahaṇāya tatrābhilāṣamutpādayitumanuśaṃsāmavatārayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, introducing the benefits in order to generate aspiration for the taking of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), he says —

children.text: rātrau yathā meghaghanāndhakāre vidyut kṣaṇaṃ darśayati prakāśam /
children.translated_text: Just as at night, in the darkness of thick clouds, lightning shows a flash of light for an instant,

children.text: buddhānubhāvena tathā kadācillokasya puṇyeṣu matiḥ kṣaṇaṃ syāt // Bca_1.5 //
children.translated_text: so too, by the power of the <s>Buddhas</s>, sometimes the mind of the world might turn toward merit for a moment. // Bca_1.5 //

body.text: niśāyāṃ yathā jaladāgamasamaye meghairbahule tamasi sati saudāmanī kṣaṇalavamātramālokayati kiṃcidvastujātaṃ prakāśayati / saivopamā atrāpi ityāha- buddhānubhāvenetyādi / buddhā eva hi bhagavanto hitasukhopasaṃhārāya sadā bhavyābhavyatayā sarvasattvasaṃtānamavalokayantastiṣṭhanti / yadā yatra yenopāyena yasmai yaṃ bhavyaṃ paśyanti tadā tatra tenopāyena tasmai tamadhitiṣṭhanti / abhavyāvasthāyāmupekṣya viharanti / iti tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena kathaṃciddurlabhotpattikatvāt / lokasya janasya puṇyeṣu hitasukhahetuṣu kuśaleṣu karmasu buddhirmuhūrtamekaṃ bhavet / tatra tasyā asthiratvāt / anādisaṃsāre lokena akuśalapakṣasyaiva abhyastatvāt //
body.translated_text: In the night, at the time of the arrival of rain-clouds, when there is darkness thick with clouds, lightning illuminates for merely a fraction of an instant, revealing some object. The same simile applies here also, thus he says 'by the power of the <s>Buddhas</s>' etc. For indeed the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, for the purpose of conveying welfare and happiness, always abide observing the continua of all beings according to their readiness or unreadiness. When they see, through whatever means, for whomever, whatever is ready — then and there, through that means, for that [being], they bless [them]. In the state of unreadiness, they abide with equanimity. Thus, through the blessing of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, since [favorable conditions] arise only rarely in some way, the mind of the world, of people, might for a single moment turn toward merit — toward wholesome actions that are the cause of welfare and happiness. Because of its instability therein, and because in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> the world has habituated only the unwholesome side.

body.text: yadi nāma evam, tataḥ kimityāha-
body.translated_text: 'If that is so, what follows?' he says —

children.text: tasmācchubhaṃ durbalameva nityaṃ balaṃ tu pāpasya mahatsughoram /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the wholesome is always weak indeed, while the power of evil is great and terrifying;

children.text: tajjīyate 'nyena śubhena kena saṃbodhicittaṃ yadi nāma na syāt // Bca_1.6 //
children.translated_text: by what other wholesome [factor] could that be overcome, if the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) did not exist? // Bca_1.6 //

body.text: yata evam, tasmācchubhaṃ puṇyaṃ durbalaṃ sāmarthyavikalameva, vidyudunmeṣaprāyatvāt ati kṛśam / nityaṃ sarvakālam / kasya tarhi atiśayavad balamastītyāha- balaṃ tviti / sāmarthyaṃ punaraśubhasya mahat, meghaghanāndhakārasadṛśattvāttasya / sughoramatibhayaṃkaraṃ narakādiduḥkhadāyakatvāt, sudurjayatvācca / bhavatu nāma mahat sāmarthyamasya, tathāpi tadapareṇa balavatā puṇyena jeṣyate, tathā ca na kācit kṣatiriti, āha- tadityādi / tat tādṛśaṃ mahāsāmarthyaṃ jīyate abhibhūyate / anyena itareṇa / kena? na kenāpītyarthaḥ / kutaḥ punarevamucyate? saṃbodhītyādi / samyaksaṃbodhau buddhatve yaccittaṃ sarvasattvasamuddharaṇābhiprāyeṇa tatprāptyarthamadhyāśayena manasikāraḥ / tadyadi nāma na bhavet, mahāsāmarthyaṃ hi tadapareṇa mahīyasā parājīyate sūryeṇeva niśāndhakāraḥ / na ca saṃbodhicittāt pratipakṣo mahīyānaparaḥ saṃbhavati / tasmāt tatpratighātāya saṃbodhicittameva upādeyaṃ nānyadityabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Since it is so, therefore the wholesome, merit, is 'weak' — deficient in power — since it is like a flash of lightning, extremely thin. 'Always' — at all times. 'Whose then is the supreme power?' he says 'but the power' etc. But the power — the strength — of the unwholesome is great, because of its resemblance to the darkness of thick clouds; and 'terrifying' — extremely frightening — because it gives the suffering of hell-realms and such, and because it is extremely difficult to conquer. 'Granted that its power is great, but even so, it will be conquered by another powerful merit; and thus there is no harm' — he says 'that' etc. 'That' — such great power — 'is overcome,' conquered. 'By another' — by some other [factor]. 'By what?' By nothing [else] — that is the meaning. 'Why then is this said?' [He answers] 'saṃbodhi' etc. The mind directed toward perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), <s>Buddhahood</s> — the mental attention with the aspiration of attaining that, with the intention of rescuing all beings — if that should not exist, [then] a great power is indeed defeated by another still greater [one], just as the darkness of night [is defeated] by the sun. And no antagonist greater than <s>bodhicitta</s> is possible. Therefore, for overcoming that [evil], only <s>bodhicitta</s> should be adopted, not anything else — this is the intent.

body.text: ito 'pi saṃbodhicittamupādeyamityāha-
body.translated_text: He says that <s>bodhicitta</s> should be adopted for this further reason —

children.translated_text: Having reflected for no few <s>kalpas</s>, the Lords of Sages have seen that this alone is beneficial,
since, through happiness alone, an ever-increasing happiness floods immeasurable multitudes of beings. // Bca_1.7 //

body.text: eko 'ntarakalpaḥ kalpaḥ / viṃśatirantarakalpāḥ kalpaḥ / aśītirantarakalpāḥ kalpaḥ / sa ca mahākalpa ityabhidhīyate / tadiha mahākalpasyaiva grahaṇam / analpān bahūn prathamāsaṃkhyeyāntargatān / pravicintayadbhiḥ tātparyeṇa paribhāvayadbhiḥ / dṛṣṭamadhigatam / munīndraiḥ buddhairbhagavadbhirbodhisattvāvasthāyām / hitaṃ sarvārthasādhanayogyam, tadbījabhūtatvāt / etadeva saṃbodhicittameva / kathaṃ punaridameva hitamityāha- yata ityādi / yasmāt sukhaṃ pravṛddhaṃ prakarṣagataṃ buddhatvalakṣaṇam / apramitān aprameyān / janaughān sattvasamūhān / utplāvayati uttārayati saṃsāraduḥkhamahārṇavāt / tasmādidameva hitam //
body.translated_text: One intermediate <s>kalpa</s> is a <s>kalpa</s>. Twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> is a <s>kalpa</s>. Eighty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> is a <s>kalpa</s> — and that is designated a <s>mahākalpa</s> (great <s>kalpa</s>). Here, it is the <s>mahākalpa</s> that is intended. 'No few' means many, contained within the first incalculable [<s>kalpa</s>]. 'Having reflected' means having pondered with deliberation. 'Have seen' means have realized. 'The Lords of Sages' — by the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, during the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage. 'Beneficial' — capable of accomplishing all aims, because it is the seed thereof. 'This alone' — <s>bodhicitta</s> alone. 'How then is this alone beneficial?' he says 'since' etc. Because 'happiness, ever-increasing' — gone to excellence — characterized by <s>Buddhahood</s> — 'immeasurable' — beyond measure — 'multitudes of beings' — assemblies of sentient beings — it 'floods,' that is, rescues from the great ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>-suffering. Therefore this alone is beneficial.

body.text: athavā / yasmāt sukhaṃ devamanuṣyasaṃpattilakṣaṇam / pravṛddhaṃ vṛddhiṃ gatam / arthāt saṃbodhicittādeva / utplāvayati atiśayena saṃtarpayati / saukaryādadhikataraṃ yadbhavati tadutplāvanamucyate / yathā dadhnā vayamutplāvitā iti saukaryādadhikataraṃ dadhi bhūtamityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Or alternatively: because 'happiness' — characterized by the attainments of gods and humans — 'ever-increasing' — gone to increase — namely, from <s>bodhicitta</s> itself — it 'floods,' that is, exceedingly satisfies. What exceeds one's capacity [to enjoy] is called 'flooding.' Just as 'we have been flooded with yogurt' means that the yogurt exceeded [what could be consumed] — that is the meaning.

body.text: yadi vā / yataḥ saṃbodhicittāt sukhaṃ pravṛddhamiti yojanīyam //
body.translated_text: Or, 'because from <s>bodhicitta</s>, happiness is ever-increasing' — thus it should be construed.

body.text: kathaṃ pravṛddhamityāha- sukhenaiveti / na akṛcchreṇa / na śiroluñcanādinā mahatā kaṣṭena / tathā hi bodhicittasaṃvarādeva bodhisattvo 'mitapuṇyajñānasaṃbhārāt pravardhamāno devamanuṣyasaṃpattīḥ sukhamadhigacchan sattvāneva adhikataraṃ tābhiḥ saṃtarpayatīti / yadvakṣyati-
body.translated_text: 'How is it ever-increasing?' he says 'through happiness alone' — that is, without hardship, not through the great difficulty of pulling out one's hair and so forth. For indeed, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, increasing through immeasurable accumulations of merit and knowledge from the <s>bodhicitta</s> vow alone, happily attaining the accomplishments of gods and humans, exceedingly satisfies beings all the more with those [attainments]. As will be stated —

children.translated_text: Thus going from happiness to happiness, what conscious person would despair,
having obtained the chariot of <s>bodhicitta</s> that removes all weariness and fatigue?

body.text: iti // [bodhi. 7.30]
body.translated_text: [<s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> 7.30]

body.text: nanu bhagavatāmapi maitrībalādijātakeṣu [jātakamālā-8] mahadduṣkaraṃ śrūyate / tat kathaṃ sukhenaiva sukhaṃ pravṛddhamiti? naiṣa doṣaḥ / yataḥ utpādyameva parahitasukhādhāyakaṃ duḥkhaṃ svaparayoḥ / kṛpātmabhiḥ / sukhameva tādṛśaṃ duḥkhaṃ paraduḥkhaduḥkhināṃ dhimatāmiti pratipādayiṣyate //
body.translated_text: But even for the Blessed Ones, great hardship is heard of in the <s>Jātakas</s> born of the power of loving-kindness [<s>Jātakamālā</s> 8]. Then how can 'through happiness alone, happiness is ever-increasing'? This is not a fault. Because even the suffering that produces welfare and happiness for others, for those whose nature is compassion, will be demonstrated [to be] truly happiness — such suffering for the wise who suffer at others' suffering.

body.text: asmādapi svaparahitahetutvādbodhicittaṃ na parityājyameveti darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing that <s>bodhicitta</s> should never be abandoned since it is the cause of one's own and others' welfare, he says —

children.translated_text: By those who wish to cross the hundreds of sufferings of existence, and by those who wish to remove the misfortunes of beings,

children.text: bahusaukhyaśatāni bhoktukāmairna vimocyaṃ hi sadaiva bodhicittam // Bca_1.8 //
children.translated_text: and by those who wish to enjoy hundreds of happinesses — <s>bodhicitta</s> should never be relinquished. // Bca_1.8 //

body.text: saṃsāraduḥkhaśatāni narakādigatiduḥkhānāmasātaveditānāṃ śatāni aparyantasamūhāṃ startukāmaiḥ parityaktumicchadbhiḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhagotraiḥ / na kevalamātmīyāni, lokānāṃ jātyādiduḥkhānyapi hartukāmairapanetukāmairbodhisattvagotraiḥ / na kevalaṃ svaparaduḥkhāni hartukāmaiḥ, api ca, bahūni sukhānyeva saukhyāni teṣāṃ śatāni devamanuṣyopapattilabhyāni anubhavitukāmaiḥ saṃsārasukhābhilāṣukairapi / sadaiva sarvakālaṃ na vimocyamaparityājyaṃ bodhicittam / svīkartavyamityarthaḥ / athavā saṃbodhikāṅkṣiṇāmeva viśeṣaṇāni //
body.translated_text: 'Hundreds of sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>': the hundreds — the limitless multitudes — of unsatisfactory feelings that are the sufferings of the destinies such as hell. 'By those who wish to cross' — by those of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> lineages who wish to abandon [them]. Not only one's own [sufferings]: 'by those who wish to remove' — to take away — the sufferings of the world such as birth and the rest — by those of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> lineage. Not merely wishing to remove one's own and others' sufferings, but moreover: 'by those who wish to enjoy' — to experience — 'many happinesses' — hundreds of pleasures — obtainable through divine and human rebirths, even by those who desire <s>saṃsāric</s> happiness. 'Never' — at all times — <s>bodhicitta</s> 'should not be relinquished' — should not be abandoned. It should be embraced — that is the meaning. Or alternatively, all the qualifiers belong to those who aspire to awakening.

body.text: asmādapi guṇaviśeṣādbodhicittaṃ grāhyamityāha-
body.translated_text: He says that <s>bodhicitta</s> should be taken up because of this further special quality —

children.text: bhavacārakabandhano varākaḥ sugatānāṃ suta ucyate kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: The wretch who is bound in the prison of [cyclic] existence is called a son of the <s>Sugatas</s> in an instant;

children.text: sanarāmaralokavandanīyo bhavati smodita eva bodhicitte // Bca_1.9 //
children.translated_text: he becomes worthy of veneration by the world including gods and humans, the moment <s>bodhicitta</s> arises. // Bca_1.9 //

body.text: saṃsāra eva bandhanāgāram, tatra bandhanaṃ bandho rāgādaya eva yasyeti vigrahaḥ / tādṛśo varākastapasvī san / udite eva bodhicitte prathamataraṃ bodhicittasaṃvaragrahaṇasamaye / sugatānāṃ suta ucyate, buddhaputra ityabhidhīyate / kṣaṇena tatkṣaṇameva / na kevalamevamityāha-
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> itself is the prison; bondage therein is one's bonds — one whose [bonds] are passion and the rest. Such a 'wretch,' a pitiable one. 'The moment <s>bodhicitta</s> arises' — at the very first time of taking the <s>bodhicitta</s> vow. He 'is called a son of the <s>Sugatas</s>' — is designated a son of the <s>Buddhas</s>. 'In an instant' — at that very moment. 'Not only that,' he says

body.text: sanarāmaretyādi / saha narāmaraiḥ manuṣyadevairvartante ye asurādayo lokāḥ, tesāmapi vandanīyo namaskaraṇīyaḥ stavanīyaśca bhavati sma / smaśabdena atītakālābhidyotanādbodhicittodayasamaye eva bhūtaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'including gods and humans' etc. Together with humans and gods — those worlds that exist including <s>Asuras</s> and others — he becomes 'worthy of veneration' — worthy of homage and praise — by them also. The word 'sma' indicates past tense, [meaning] it happened at the very moment of the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>.

body.text: asmādapi guṇānuśaṃsadarśanādbodhicittagrahaṇe yatnaḥ karaṇīya ityāha-
body.translated_text: He says that effort should be made in taking <s>bodhicitta</s> because of seeing this further beneficial result —

children.translated_text: Taking this impure image, it makes it into the priceless image of the <s>Jina</s>-jewel;

children.text: rasajātamatīva vedhanīyaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ gṛhṇata bodhicittasaṃjñam // Bca_1.10 //
children.translated_text: grasp firmly the elixir known as <s>bodhicitta</s>, which is supremely transformative, like the philosophers' stone! // Bca_1.10 //

body.text: amedhyapratimāmimāṃ manuṣyādikalevarasvabhāvāṃ taddhātukāṃ tatsvabhāvām / tena saṃvardhitāmityarthaḥ / tāṃ gṛhītvā ādāya / jina eva ratnam, durlabhapratilambhādiguṇayogāt / tasya pratimāṃ karoti niṣpādayati bodhicittam / tathāgatavigrahaṃ nirvartayatītyarthaḥ / kiṃ bhūtām? anarghām / na vidyate argho mūlyaṃ yasyāḥ / sarvatraidhātukātiśāyiguṇatvād guṇaparyantāparijñānācca / tathoktāṃ tām / ata eva rasajātaṃ rasaprakāram / atyuccavedhakāritvādatīva vedhanīyam / kartari anīyaḥ karaṇe vā / tat tādṛśam / bodhicittaṃ saṃjñā asya rasajātasya / bodhicittāparavyapadeśam / sudṛḍhaṃ gṛhṇata yathā gṛhītaṃ punarna calati gṛhṇīteti prāpte gṛhṇateti yathāgamapāṭhāt / tasmājjinaratnamātmānaṃ kartukāmairbodhicittamahārasaḥ sudṛḍhaṃ grahītavyaḥ / uktaṃ ca āryamaitreyavimokṣe [gaṇḍavyūhasūtra 502]
body.translated_text: [The word <s>amedhya</s> (impure) refers to] this [body], which is a likeness of an impure [vessel] — whose nature is the physical frame of humans and so forth, belonging to those [bodily] elements, of that nature. 'Nourished by it' is the meaning [of <s>saṃvardhitām</s>]. Having taken it (<s>gṛhītvā</s>), meaning having adopted it. The Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>) himself is the jewel, because of the conjunction of such qualities as rarity of attainment. One makes (<s>karoti</s>), meaning produces, an image (<s>pratimā</s>) of him — [that is,] the awakening mind (<s>bodhicitta</s>). The meaning is: one brings about the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Of what kind? Priceless (<s>anarghā</s>) — that of which no price or value exists, because of its quality surpassing the entire triple world and because the extent of its qualities is unknowable. Thus described. Therefore, [this is] the elixir (<s>rasajāta</s>), meaning a type of alchemical substance — exceedingly penetrating because it effects the highest transmutation; [the suffix] <s>anīya</s> is in the agent or instrument [sense]. That [is its nature]. <s>Bodhicitta</s> is the designation of this elixir — an alternative name for the awakening mind. 'Seize firmly' (<s>sudṛḍhaṃ gṛhṇata</s>) means so that what is grasped does not slip away again. Although 'gṛhṇīta' (the optative) would be expected, 'gṛhṇata' [the imperative] is used following the reading of the received text. Therefore, by those who wish to make themselves into the jewel of the Conqueror, the great elixir of <s>bodhicitta</s> should be firmly grasped. And it is said in the Noble <s>Maitreya</s>-chapter [of the <s>Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra</s>]:

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra asti hāṭakaprabhāsaṃ nāma rasajātam / tasyaikaṃ palaṃ lohapalasahasraṃ suvarṇīkaroti / na ca tadrasapalaṃ śakyate tena lohapalasahasreṇa paryādātuṃ lohīkartuṃ vā / evameva ekaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādarasadhātuḥ kuśalamūlapariṇāmanājñānasaṃgṛhītaḥ sarvakarmakleśāvaraṇalohāni paryādāya sarvadharmān sarvajñatāsuvarṇān karoti / na ca sarvajñatācittotpādarasadhātuḥ śakyate sarvakarmakleśāvaraṇalohādibhiḥ paryādātuṃ tatkartuṃ veti //
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O son of good family, there is an elixir called <s>Hāṭakaprabhāsa</s> (Lustre of Gold) — a single <s>pala</s> (measure) of it turns a thousand <s>palas</s> of base metal into gold, and that <s>pala</s> of elixir cannot be overcome or turned into base metal by that thousand <s>palas</s> of base metal — even so, a single element of the elixir of the arising of the mind directed toward omniscience, when conjoined with the knowledge of dedicating wholesome roots, overcomes all the base metal of <s>karma</s>-obstructions and defilement-obstructions and turns all <s>dharmas</s> into the gold of omniscience; and the element of the elixir of the arising of the mind directed toward omniscience cannot be overcome or turned into that by all the base metal of <s>karma</s>-obstructions, defilement-obstructions, and so forth.'

body.text: bhavagatiṣu vibhūtikāmairapi nātra saṃśayo viparyāso vā kartavyaḥ ityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing that even by those who desire prosperity in the realms of existence, no doubt or error should be entertained here, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.translated_text: 'Thoroughly examined by those of immeasurable wisdom, of great value, the sole caravan-leaders of the world —

children.text: gatipattanavipravāsaśīlāḥ sudṛḍhaṃ gṛhṇ ata bodhicittaratnam // Bca_1.11 //
children.translated_text: you who habitually sojourn in the ports of [various] destinies, firmly seize the jewel of <s>bodhicitta</s>!' // <s>Bca</s> 1.11 //

body.text: gataya eva pattanāni paṇyadravyakrayavikrayanagarāṇi iha pattanāni / tadvat śubhāśubhakarmapaṇyadravyakrayavikrayasthānāni gatipattanāni / teṣu vipravāso vipravasanameva śīlaṃ svabhāvo yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ / teṣāṃ saṃbodhanam / he gatipattanavipravāsaśīlāḥ, sudṛḍhaṃ gṛhṇata bodhicittaratnam / bodhicittameva ratnaṃ ratnamiva / yathā cintāmaṇimahāratnaṃ sarvadāridyadurgatipraśamanahetuḥ,
body.translated_text: The destinies (<s>gatis</s>) themselves are the 'ports' (<s>pattanas</s>) — just as ports are cities for the buying and selling of merchandise, so here, the places for the buying and selling of the merchandise of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> are the destiny-ports. Those for whom sojourning (<s>vipravāsa</s>), that is, dwelling abroad in those [ports], is their habitual nature (<s>śīla</s>) are called thus. Addressing them: 'O you who habitually sojourn in the ports of destinies, firmly seize the jewel of <s>bodhicitta</s>!' <s>Bodhicitta</s> itself is the jewel — [or] like a jewel. Just as the great jewel of the wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) is the cause of pacifying all poverty and misfortune,

body.text: tathā idamapi bodhicittaratnam / ayamabhiprāyaḥ- vaṇija eva sukhasaṃpattilābhārthino yūyam / ataḥ idameva mahāratnaṃ mahatādareṇa gṛhṇata / kutaḥ? bahumūlyamiti hetupadametat / yasmādanarghamidaṃ sarvātiśāyi laukikalokottarasaṃpattinidānabhūtatvāt, tasmādidameva grāhyamityarthaḥ / kathamidaṃ jñāyata iti cedāha- suparīkṣitamiti / suṣṭhu nirūpitaṃ samyaṅ nirṇītamityarthaḥ / kairityāha- aprameyadhībhiḥ / aprameyā pramātumaśakyā dhīrbuddhiryeṣāṃ taiḥ mahāprājñaiḥ buddhabodhisattvaiḥ / etāvatā parīkṣāyāṃ skhalitamapi nāsti iti suparīkśitamucyate / punarapi kiṃbhūtaiḥ? jagadekasārthavāhaiḥ / sārthaṃ vāhayantītyaṇ / jagatāmeka eva sārthavāhāḥ karuṇāvaśavartino buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvāśca, taiḥ / yathā khalu vaṇijāṃ hitāhitaprāptiparihārayorhitaiṣiṇo jñānavantaśca sārthavāhā netāro bhavanti, iti na tatra visaṃvādasaṃbhāvanā, tathā atrāpītyabhiprāyaḥ / tasmādidameva bodhicittaratnamanarghaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ grāhyamiti / etacca tatraivoktam-
body.translated_text: so too is this jewel of <s>bodhicitta</s>. The intended meaning is: you yourselves are like merchants desiring the attainment of prosperity and happiness. Therefore, seize this very great jewel with great care! Why? 'Of great value' (<s>bahumūlya</s>) — this is the word indicating the reason. Since this is priceless, surpassing everything, being the source of all worldly and supramundane prosperity, therefore it alone should be grasped — this is the meaning. If one asks, 'How is this known?' — [he answers:] 'Thoroughly examined' (<s>suparīkṣita</s>), meaning well-investigated, properly ascertained — this is the meaning. By whom? [He says:] 'By those of immeasurable wisdom' (<s>aprameyadhībhiḥ</s>) — those whose wisdom, intelligence, is immeasurable, that is, incapable of being measured — by those of great wisdom, the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. By this much, there is no error even in the examination — hence it is said to be 'thoroughly examined.' Furthermore, of what kind? 'The sole caravan-leaders of the world' (<s>jagadekasārthavāhaiḥ</s>) — [the word means] those who lead (<s>vāhayanti</s>) the caravan (<s>sārtha</s>). The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who act under the power of compassion, are the sole caravan-leaders of the world — by them. Just as, for merchants, the caravan-leaders who are well-wishing and knowledgeable are the guides for attaining benefit and avoiding harm, and therefore there is no possibility of deception there, so too here — this is the intended meaning. Therefore, this very priceless jewel of <s>bodhicitta</s> should be firmly grasped. And this too is stated in that very [text]:

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra yāvaccandrasūryau manḍalaprabhayā avabhāsete / atrāntare ye keciddhana dhānyaratnajātarūparajatapuṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanaparibhogāḥ, te sarve vaśirājamahāmaṇiratnasya mūlyaṃ na kṣamante, evameva yāvat triṣvapi adhvasu sarvajñajñānaṃ dharmadhātuviṣayamavabhāsayati / atrāntare yāni kāni cit sarvadevamanuṣyasarvasattvasarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakuśalamūlāni sāsravānāsravāṇi sarvāṇi tāni bodhicittotpādavaśirājamahāmaṇiratnasya mūlyaṃ na kṣamante / [gaṇḍavyūhasūtra-500] iti //
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O son of good family, the radiance of the orbs of the sun and moon illuminates [the world] — whatever wealth, grain, jewels, gold, silver, flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, and enjoyments exist within that [illuminated] extent — all of them are not equal to the price of the great jewel of the <s>Vaśirāja</s> (Sovereign Lord) gem — even so, for as long as the omniscient knowledge illuminates the domain of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) across all three times — whatever wholesome roots there are of all gods, humans, all beings, all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, whether with outflows or without outflows — all of them are not equal to the price of the great jewel of the <s>Vaśirāja</s> gem of the arising of the awakening mind.' [<s>Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra</s>]

body.text: idamaparamasādhāraṇamatiśayavat kalpataroriva māhātmyamasya upadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing that this [<s>bodhicitta</s>] has yet another supremely extraordinary greatness, like that of a wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpataru</s>), [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.text: kadalīva phalaṃ vihāya yāti kṣayamanyat kuśalaṃ hi sarvameva /
children.translated_text: 'Like a plantain tree, all other virtue perishes after yielding its fruit;

children.text: satataṃ phalati kṣayaṃ na yāti prasavatyeva tu bodhicittavṛkṣaḥ // Bca_1.12 //
children.translated_text: but the tree of <s>bodhicitta</s> constantly bears fruit, does not perish, and continually produces [more]. // <s>Bca</s> 1.12 //

body.text: kadalī yathā palamekavāraṃ datvā na punaḥ phalati, tathā bodhicittādanyadapi kuśalaṃ sarvameva kiṃcideva vipāke paripakve na punaḥ phaladānasamarthaṃ bhavati / tāvataivāsya parikṣayāt, vipākasya ca avyākṛtatayā punaḥ phalānubandhābhāvāt / bodhicittasya punarayaṃ viśeṣaḥ ityāha- satatamityādi / sarvakālaṃ phalati devamanuṣyopapattiṣu sukhasaṃpattipradānāt kṣayaṃ na yāti tadanyakuśalavat, sthirasvabhāvatvāt / pratikṣaṇamanekaprakāraiḥ śubhameghapravāhairāpūryamāṇatvācca prasavatyeva tu bodhicittavṛkṣaḥ, avicchinnasukhasaṃpattiphalaprasavanāt, uttarottaramaparā paraguṇaviśeṣajananācca / bodhicittaṃ vṛkśa iva / upamitaṃ vyāghrādibhiḥ iti samāsaḥ / yasmādevam, tasmādanuparatamatiśayavatsarvasukhasaṃpadaḥ prāptukāmaiḥ prekṣāvadbhiridameva grāhyam / kathitaṃ caitadāryākṣayamatinirdeśe-
body.translated_text: Just as a plantain (<s>kadalī</s>), having given fruit once, does not bear fruit again, so too all other virtue apart from <s>bodhicitta</s> — whatever it may be — when its result has ripened, is not capable of giving fruit again. This is because of its exhaustion at just that point, and because the result, being morally indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>), has no further connection with fruit. But <s>bodhicitta</s> has this distinction, [as] he says: 'constantly' and so forth. At all times it bears fruit — through the bestowal of the prosperity of happiness in divine and human rebirths — and does not perish like other virtue, because of its stable nature. And because it is being filled at every moment by streams of clouds of merit of many kinds, the tree of <s>bodhicitta</s> continually produces — through the uninterrupted production of the fruit of the prosperity of happiness, and through the generation of ever-higher, unsurpassed qualities. <s>Bodhicitta</s> is like a tree — a compound [formed] like 'compared to tigers and so forth.' Since this is so, those of discernment who wish to attain the incessantly surpassing prosperity of all happiness should grasp this very [<s>bodhicitta</s>]. And this is stated in the Noble <s>Akṣayamatinirdeśa</s>:

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhadanta śāradvatīputra mahāsamudrapatitasyodakabindornāstyantarā parikṣayaḥ paryādānaṃ yāvanna kalpaparyantaḥ iti, evameva bodhipariṇāmitasya kuśalamūlasya nāstyantarā parikṣayaḥ paryādānaṃ yāvanna bodhimaṇḍaniṣadanam // iti //
body.translated_text: 'Just as, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a drop of water that has fallen into the great ocean has no intermediate exhaustion or consumption until the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, even so, a wholesome root dedicated toward awakening has no intermediate exhaustion or consumption until the sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>).'

body.text: na kevalaṃ sarvaśubhasaṃcayakāraṇam, akuśalapakṣakṣayaheturapi bodhicittamiti sārdhaślokenāha-
body.translated_text: [<s>Śāntideva</s> says] in a verse and a half that <s>bodhicitta</s> is not only the cause of the accumulation of all good, but also the cause of the destruction of the side of the unwholesome:

children.translated_text: 'Even having committed terrible sins, one who relies on it crosses over in an instant,
as [one crosses over] great dangers by relying on a hero — why is it not resorted to by ignorant beings?' // <s>Bca</s> 1.13 //

body.text: bodhicittagrahaṇātpūrvaṃ kṛtvāpi pāpāni akuśalakarmāṇi narakādiṣu duḥsahaduḥkhadāyakatvāt sudāruṇāni atibhayaṃkarāṇi mahānti vā yasya bodhicittasyāśrayādāśrayaṇāt tadutpādanarakṣaṇavardhanasevanalakṣaṇāt uttarati nistarati / tatsāmarthyābhibhavena atikrāmatītyarthaḥ / kṣaṇena ekasminneva kṣaṇe mahataḥ puṇyarāśeḥ samupārjanāt / tadutpādanamātreṇa / kathamivottarati? śūrāśrayeṇeva mahābhayāni balavatpuruṣāśrayeṇa yathā mahāparādhaṃ kṛtvāpi kaściduttarati tadaparādhaphalānnirbhayo bhavati, tathā prakṛte 'pi / tadevaṃbhūtaṃ bodhicittaṃ kathaṃ kimiti nāśrīyate na sevyate? ajñasattvaiḥ prajñāvikalairmūḍhajanairityarthaḥ / āśrayaṇīyameva tadbhavediti bhāvaḥ / idamapi tatraivoktam-
body.translated_text: Even having committed sins (<s>pāpāni</s>), unwholesome actions — which are exceedingly terrible (<s>sudāruṇāni</s>), extremely frightful and great, because they give unbearable suffering in hells and so forth — prior to grasping <s>bodhicitta</s>, one crosses over, one escapes, by relying on (<s>āśrayāt</s>), that is, by taking refuge in that <s>bodhicitta</s>, characterized by its generation, protection, increase, and practice. The meaning is: one transcends by the overpowering force of its power. 'In an instant' (<s>kṣaṇena</s>) — in a single moment, through the accumulation of a great mass of merit. Merely by its generation. How does one cross over? 'As great dangers by relying on a hero' — just as someone, even having committed a great offense, crosses over by relying on a powerful person, becoming free from fear of the fruit of that offense, so too in the present case. Such being the nature of <s>bodhicitta</s>, why is it not resorted to (<s>nāśrīyate</s>), not cultivated? 'By ignorant beings' — by those deficient in wisdom, by deluded people — this is the meaning. The sense is that it should indeed be resorted to. This too is stated in that very [text]:

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra śūrasaṃniśritaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvaśatrubhyo na bibheti, evameva bodhicittotpādaśūrasaṃniśrito bodhisattvaḥ sarvaduścaritaśatrubhyo na bibhetīti //
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O son of good family, one who relies on a hero does not fear any enemy, even so, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who relies on the hero of the arising of the awakening mind does not fear any enemy of misconduct.'

body.text: aparamapi bodhicittātpāpakṣayadṛṣṭāntamāha-
body.translated_text: He states yet another example of the destruction of sin through <s>bodhicitta</s>:

body.text: yugāntakālānalavanmahānti pāpāni yannirdahati kṣaṇena /
body.translated_text: 'Like the fire at the end of an age, which burns up great sins in an instant —'

body.text: yugāntakāle pralayasamaye analo bahniḥ saptasūryodayasamudbhūtaḥ yathā sarvaṃ kāmādhātuṃ saprathamadhyānaṃ nirdahati, niḥśeṣaṃ dahati yathā bhasmāpi nāvaśiṣyate, tadvat pāpāni / kiṃbhūtāni? mahānti sumeruprakhyāni mahārauravādiduḥkhavipākāni yad bodhicittaṃ nirdahati tadvipākopaghātānnirmūlayati / kṣaṇena nacireṇa / nāśrīyate tatkathamajñasattvairiti saṃbandhaḥ kāryaḥ // etadapi tatraivoktam- kalpoddāhāgnibhūtaṃ sarvaduṣkṛtanirdahanatayā / pātālabhūtaṃ sarvākuśaladharmaparyādānakaraṇatayā iti //
body.translated_text: The fire (<s>anala</s>) at the end of an age (<s>yugānta</s>), at the time of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), born from the rising of seven suns, just as it burns the entire desire-realm together with the first <s>dhyāna</s> [heaven], burns completely so that not even ash remains — so too the sins. Of what kind? Great (<s>mahānti</s>) — enormous like <s>Sumeru</s>, productive of the suffering of <s>Mahāraurava</s> and other [hells] — which <s>bodhicitta</s> burns up, meaning eradicates through the destruction of their result. 'In an instant' (<s>kṣaṇena</s>) — in a short time. The connection should be made with 'Why is it not resorted to by ignorant beings?' This too is stated in that very [text]: 'It is like the fire at the destruction of a <s>kalpa</s>, through its burning up of all misdeeds; it is like the abyss, through its consuming all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: nanu kṛtakarmāvipraṇāśavādī bhagavān, tat kathamidamabhidhīyate? satyamucyate / bodhicittaprasūte pratikṣaṇamākāśadhātuvyāpake mahati puṇyaughe 'ntarbhūtatayā lavaṇapalopamanyāyena aprajñāyamānatvāt, balavatā pratipakṣeṇa abhībhūtatvācca, phaladānāsamarthaṃ dagdhameva tadityadoṣaḥ / yadi vā nirupāyābhisaṃdhinā taduktam- nābhuktaṃ kṣīyate karmeti / idaṃ tu sarvapāpanirmūlane
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But the Blessed One teaches the non-destruction of performed <s>karma</s> — how then can this be stated? Truly it is said: because in the great flood of merit arising from <s>bodhicitta</s> at every moment, pervading the entire space-element, [the evil karma] is included and thereby, by the principle of the salt-crystal analogy, becomes imperceptible; and because it is overpowered by a stronger antidote, it is incapable of giving its fruit — it is as though burned — hence there is no fault. Alternatively, the statement 'karma that has not been experienced does not perish' is said without reference to [salvific] means; but this [<s>bodhicitta</s>] is

body.text: mahānupāyaḥ / tathā hi- yadā bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvānākāśadhātuvyāpinaḥ sarvaduḥkhāt samuddhṛtya sarvasukhasaṃpannān kariṣyāmītyadhyāśayena vicintayati / pūrvakṛtaṃ ca pāpaṃ vidūṣaṇāsamudācārādibhiḥ kṣapayati, tadā bodhicittabalādeva tatsaṃtāne pāpasya kaḥ sadbhāvaḥ, yena codyasyāvakāśaḥ syāditi sarvaṃ nirākulam / etāvatā yaduktam- tajjīyate 'nyena śubhena kena iti, tadapi vispaṣṭīkṛtam / anye punaḥ- aniyatavipākāpekṣayā sarvametaducyate, niyatavipākasya tu karmaṇaḥ kenacitpratiṣeddhumaśakyatvādityāhuḥ //
body.translated_text: a great means for the eradication of all sin. For when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thinks with the intention 'I shall deliver all beings pervading the space-element from all suffering and endow them with all prosperity of happiness,' and when he eliminates previously committed sin through confession and other practices of remorse, then by the very power of <s>bodhicitta</s>, what real existence does sin have in his continuum, such that there could be an occasion for objection? Thus everything is resolved. By this, what was said — 'By what other virtue is that overcome?' — is also made clear. Others, however, say: all this is said with reference to <s>karma</s> of indeterminate result; but <s>karma</s> of determinate result cannot be prevented by anything.

body.text: itthamapi bodhicittamupādeyamityāha-
body.translated_text: [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says that in this way too, <s>bodhicitta</s> should be adopted:

body.text: yasyānuśaṃsānamitānuvāca maitreyanāthaḥ sudhanāya dhīmān // Bca_1.14 //
body.translated_text: 'Whose immeasurable benefits the wise Lord <s>Maitreya</s> declared to <s>Sudhana</s> —' // <s>Bca</s> 1.14 //

body.text: yasya bodhicittasya anuśaṃsān svābhāvikān guṇān amitān apramāṇān maitreyanāthaḥ bhagavānajitaḥ / kiṃbhūtaḥ? dhīmān bodhisattvaḥ / uvāca uktavān / sudhanāya sudhananāmne bodhisattvāya / tathā ca āryagaṇḍavyūhasūtre [varṇitam-
body.translated_text: 'Whose' — of <s>bodhicitta</s> — 'benefits' (<s>anuśaṃsān</s>), meaning natural virtues — 'immeasurable' (<s>amitān</s>), meaning without measure — Lord <s>Maitreya</s>, the Blessed <s>Ajita</s>. Of what kind? 'Wise' (<s>dhīmān</s>) — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. 'Declared' (<s>uvāca</s>), meaning spoke. 'To <s>Sudhana</s>' — to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Sudhana</s>. And thus in the Noble <s>Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra</s> [it is described:]

body.text: bodhicittaṃ hi kulaputra bījabhūtaṃ sarvabuddhadharmāṇām / kṣetrabhūtaṃ sarvajagacchukladharmavirohaṇatayā / dharaṇibhūtaṃ sarvalokapratiśaraṇatayā / yāvat pitṛbhūtaṃ sarvabodhisattvārakṣaṇatayā / pe......... / vaiśravaṇabhūtaṃ sarvadāridyasaṃchedanatayā / cintāmaṇirājabhūtaṃ sarvārthasaṃsādhanatayā / bhadraghaṭabhūtaṃ sarvābhiprāyaparipūraṇatayā / śaktibhūtaṃ kleśaśatruvijayāya // ityādi vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Bodhicitta</s>, O son of good family, is like a seed, for all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>; like a field, for the sprouting of all white <s>dharmas</s> of the world; like the earth, for the support of the entire world; [and so forth] up to: like a father, for the protection of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; [and continuing:] like <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, for the cutting off of all poverty; like the king of wish-fulfilling gems, for the accomplishment of all aims; like the auspicious vase (<s>bhadraghaṭa</s>), for the fulfillment of all aspirations; like a spear, for the conquest of the enemy of defilements.' And so forth in detail.

body.text: nāśrīyate tat kathamajñasattvaiḥ iti atrāpi yojanīyam //
body.translated_text: 'Why is it not resorted to by ignorant beings?' — this should be connected here too.

body.text: idānīṃ bodhicittasya prabhedaṃ darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, showing the classification of <s>bodhicitta</s>, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.translated_text: 'That <s>bodhicitta</s> should be known, in brief, as twofold:'
the mind of aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhipraṇidhicitta</s>) and the mind of setting forth for awakening (<s>bodhiprasthāna</s>). // Bca_1.15 //

body.text: tat samanantarapradarśitānuśaṃsaṃ bodhicittaṃ dvividhaṃ dviprakāraṃ vijñātavyaṃ veditavyam / gotrabhūmyādigatānekaprakārasaṃbhave 'pi kathaṃ dvividhamityāha- samāsataḥ / aparaprakārasaṃbhave 'pi saṃkṣepataḥ idaṃ dvividhamucyate / dvividhamapi katham? bodhipraṇidhicittamityekam, bodhiprasthānamiti dvitīyam / bodhau praṇidhiḥ, tadeva cittaṃ tatra vā cittam / yaccittaṃ praṇidhānādutpannaṃ bhavati dānādipravṛttivikalaṃ ca, tat praṇidhicittam / tadyathā- sarvajagatparitrāṇāya buddho bhaveyamiti prathamataraṃ prārthanākārā cetanā / prasthāne cittaṃ prasthānameva vā cittam / cittasya tatsvabhāvatvāt / pūrvakamanaskārapuraḥsarameva yataḥ prabhṛti saṃvaragrahaṇapūrvakaṃ saṃbhāreṣu pravartate, tat prasthānacittam / iti uktakrameṇa dvaividhyam / iyāneva bhedaḥ iti evakāreṇa pratipādayati / cakāradvayaṃ parasparasamuccaye / dvayorapi bodhicittatvaṃ darśayati / tena pūrvakaṃ bodhicittaṃ na bhavatīti śaṅkāṃ nirasyati / śūraṃgamasūtre ādyotpāditasyāpi bodhicittasya buddhatvahetutvābhidhānāt / tathā āryagaṇḍavyūhe coktam-
body.translated_text: That <s>bodhicitta</s>, whose benefits have just been shown, should be understood as twofold, of two kinds. How can it be [only] twofold when many kinds arise [at] the levels of lineage (<s>gotra</s>), stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), and so forth? He says: 'briefly' — even though other kinds are possible, in summary it is said to be twofold. And how is it twofold? The 'mind of aspiration for awakening' (<s>bodhipraṇidhicitta</s>) is one; 'setting forth for awakening' (<s>bodhiprasthāna</s>) is the second. An aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>) directed toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — that itself as a mental state, or a mental state directed toward that. Whatever mental state arises from the aspiration but lacks engagement in practices such as giving, etc. — that is the aspiration-mind. Namely: the volition (<s>cetanā</s>) having the form of a wish — "May I become a <s>Buddha</s> for the protection of the entire world" — this initial [impulse]. The mind directed toward setting forth, or [it is] the setting forth itself as mind — since the mind has that very nature. From the time when, preceded by the prior mental resolve, one engages in the accumulations [of merit and knowledge] with the prior undertaking of the discipline (<s>saṃvara</s>) — that is the setting-forth mind. Thus the twofoldness is according to the stated order. He indicates with the particle "eva" that this is the only division. The two uses of "ca" are for mutual conjunction. He shows that both are <s>bodhicitta</s>. By this he dispels the doubt that the former [aspiration] is not <s>bodhicitta</s>. Since in the <s>Śūraṃgamasūtra</s>, even the initially generated <s>bodhicitta</s> is stated to be a cause of Buddhahood. So too in the noble <s>Gaṇḍavyūha</s> it is said —

body.text: durlabhāḥ kulaputra te sattvāḥ sattvaloke ye anuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ praṇidadhati / tato 'pi durlabhatamāste sattvāḥ ye anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimanuprasthitāḥ // iti //
body.translated_text: "Rare, O son of good family, are those beings in the world of beings who generate the mind directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. Even rarer than those are the beings who have set forth toward unsurpassed perfect awakening." Thus. //

body.text: idānīmuktameva prabhedamudāharaṇena vyaktīkurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, making clear the very division just stated by means of an illustration, he says —

children.translated_text: Just as the distinction between one who wishes to go and one who is [actually] going is recognized,
so the distinction between these two should be known by the wise in respective order. // Bca_1.16 //

body.text: yathā kaścit puruṣaḥ abhimatadeśaprāptaye gantukāmaḥ gamanābhiprāyaḥ, na tu punargacchatyeva, anyaḥ punastatprāptaye prasthito gacchatyeva / yadvadyathā / tayorbhedo viśeṣaḥ pratīyate avagamyate, tadvattathā bhedo nānātvamanayorbodhipraṇidhiprasthānacetasorjñeyaḥ avaboddhavyaḥ paṇḍitairvicakṣaṇaiḥ / katham? yāthāsaṃkhyena / svārthe 'pyaṇ / prāktanaṃ praṇidhicittasya nidarśanaṃ paścāttanaṃ prasthānacetasaḥ iti saṃkhyārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as a certain person, wishing to reach a desired destination, has the intention of going but does not actually go, while another, having set out to reach that [destination], is actually going — just so, the distinction between them is recognized, is understood. Even so, the distinction, the difference, between these two — the aspiration-mind and the setting-forth mind — should be known, should be understood, by the wise, the discerning. How? 'In respective order' (<s>yāthāsaṃkhyena</s>) — the [suffix] aṇ is in its own sense. The former illustration corresponds to the aspiration-mind, the latter to the setting-forth mind — this is the meaning of the enumeration. //

body.text: tadetat praṇidhicittaṃ pratipattivikalamapi saṃsāre mahāphalaṃ bhagavatā varṇitamityāha-
body.translated_text: Saying that even this aspiration-mind, though lacking in practice, has been praised by the Blessed One as bearing great fruit in <s>saṃsāra</s>, he states —

body.text: bodhipraṇidhicittasya saṃsāre 'pi phalaṃ mahat /
body.translated_text: Even in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the fruit of the aspiration-mind for awakening is great.

body.text: yadi nāma tat pratipattivikalam, tathāpi tasya āstāṃ tāvad buddhatvam, saṃsāre 'pi devamanuṣyopapattisvabhāvaṃ sukhasaṃpattilakṣaṇaṃ phalaṃ mahat, anyasmāt kuśalād bṛhat / satataṃ phalatītyādiviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭatvāt / tathā coktamāryamaitreyavimokṣe [=gaṇḍavyūhasūtra-508]-
body.translated_text: Even if it lacks practice, still — let alone Buddhahood — its fruit even in <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose nature is rebirth among gods and humans, characterized by the attainment of happiness, is great — greater than other [forms of] merit. Because it is distinguished by the special qualifiers 'it bears fruit continuously,' and so on. As stated in the liberation [section] of the noble <s>Maitreya</s> [= <s>Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra</s> 508] —

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra bhinnamapi vajraratnaṃ sarvaprativiśiṣṭaṃ suvarṇālaṃkāramabhibhavati, vajraratnanāma ca na vijahāti, sarvadāridyaṃ ca vinivartayati, evameva kulaputra pratipattibhinnamapi sarvajñatācittotpādavajraratnaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaguṇasuvarṇālaṃkāramabhibhavati, bodhicittanāma ca na vijahāti, saṃsāradāridyaṃ ca vinivartayatīti //
body.translated_text: "Just as, O son of good family, even a broken diamond-jewel surpasses all the finest golden ornaments, does not lose the name 'diamond-jewel,' and removes all poverty — even so, O son of good family, even the diamond-jewel of the generation of the mind of omniscience, when broken by lack of practice, surpasses the golden ornaments of all the qualities of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, does not lose the name '<s>bodhicitta</s>,' and removes the poverty of <s>saṃsāra</s>." //

body.text: tasmād yo 'pi pāramitāsu sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā śikṣitumasamarthaḥ, tenāpi bodhicittamutpādanīyam / evamupāyaparigraheṇa mahāphalatvāt / yathoktamāryāpararājāvavādakasūtre-
body.translated_text: Therefore, even one who is entirely unable to train in the <s>pāramitās</s> in every way should still generate <s>bodhicitta</s> — because, through the adoption of this skillful means, it bears great fruit. As stated in the noble <s>Apararājāvavādakasūtra</s> —

body.text: yasmāt tvaṃ mahārāja bahukṛtyo bahukaraṇīyaḥ, asahaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvadā dānapāramitāyāṃ śikṣitum, yāvat prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitum / tasmāttarhi tvaṃ mahārāja evameva saṃbodhicchandaṃ śraddhāṃ prārthanāṃ praṇidhiṃ ca, gacchannapi tiṣṭhannapi niṣaṇṇo 'pi śayāno 'pi jāgradapi bhuñjāno 'pi pibannapi, satatamamitamanusmara, manasi kuru, bhāvaya / sarvabuddhabodhisattvapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakapṛthagjanānāmātmanaśca atītānāgatapratyutpannāni kuśalamūlānipiṇḍayitvā tulayitvā anumodayasva agrayā anumodanayā / anumodya ca sarvabuddhabodhisattvapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakāṇāṃ pūjākarmāṇi niryātaya / niryātya ca sarvasattvasādhāraṇāni kuru / tataḥ sarvasattvānāṃ yāvat sarvajñatāpratilambhāya sarvabuddhadharmaparipūraṇāya dine dine traikālyamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmaya / evaṃ khalu tvaṃ mahārāja pratipannaḥ san rājyaṃ ca kārayiṣyasi, rājyakṛtyāni ca na hāpayiṣyasi, bodhisaṃbhārāṃśca paripūrayiṣyasi // ityādikamuktvāha-
body.translated_text: "Since you, great king, have many duties and many obligations, and are unable to train completely and in every way at all times in the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), up to the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) — therefore, great king, whether going, standing, sitting, lying down, waking, eating, or drinking, constantly remember, attend to, and cultivate without limit this aspiration, faith, wish, and vow for awakening. Accumulating and weighing the wholesome roots of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, ordinary persons, and yourself — past, future, and present — rejoice with the supreme rejoicing. Having rejoiced, offer the worship-deeds to all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>. Having offered, make [them] common to all beings. Then, for the attainment of omniscience by all beings, and for the fulfillment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, dedicate [them] daily, three times a day, to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Indeed, great king, being thus engaged, you will carry out your kingship, you will not neglect the duties of kingship, and you will fulfill the accumulations for awakening." Having said this and more, he says —

body.text: sa khalu punastvaṃ mahārāja samyaksaṃbodhicittakuśalamūlavipākena anekakṛtvo deveṣu upapanno 'bhūḥ / anekakṛtvo manuṣyeṣu upapanno 'bhūḥ / sarvāsu ca devamanuṣyopapattiṣu ādhipatyaṃ kārayiṣyasi / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover, great king, through the ripening of the wholesome roots of the mind of perfect awakening, you have been reborn many times among the gods, and reborn many times among humans. And in all those rebirths among gods and humans, you will exercise sovereignty." Thus in detail. //

body.text: iti caryāvikale 'pi bodhicitte nāvamanyanā kāryā / tasyāpi anantasaṃsāre sukhaprasavanāt / yat punaḥ pratipattisāraṃ bodhicittaṃ tadatitarāṃ vipulaphalameveti siddhamityāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, even <s>bodhicitta</s> that lacks [full] practice should not be disparaged — since it produces happiness throughout infinite <s>saṃsāra</s>. But that <s>bodhicitta</s> whose essence is practice bears fruit all the more abundantly — this being established, he says —

body.text: na tvavicchinnapuṇyatvaṃ yathā prasthānacetasaḥ // Bca_1.17 //
body.translated_text: But [the aspiration-mind] does not have the uninterrupted merit that the setting-forth mind has. // Bca_1.17 //

body.text: na tu na punaḥ / yathā prasthānacittasya avicchinnapuṇyatvaṃ nirantaraśubhapravāha vāhitvam, na tathā asyeti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: "But not" — "not indeed." Just as the setting-forth mind has uninterrupted merit — a continuous flow of wholesomeness — the [aspiration-mind] does not have that — this is the meaning. //

body.text: idameva avicchinnapuṇyatvaṃ vṛttadvayena prasādhayannāha-
body.translated_text: He establishes this very uninterrupted merit with two verses, saying —

children.translated_text: From the time when, for the liberation of the boundless realm of beings,
he takes up that mind with an irreversible intention, // Bca_1.18 //
from then on, even for one who is sleeping or heedless, many times over,
uninterrupted streams of merit flow forth, equal to the sky. // Bca_1.19 //

body.text: yataḥprabhṛtiḥ yasmādārabhya / na vidyate paryantaḥ iyattā asyeti aparyantasya ākāśadhātuvyāpinaḥ sattvadhātoḥ / pramokṣaṇe pramokṣe sarvaduḥkhopaśamanimitte / samādadāti taccittam, samyaksaṃbodhicittaṃ samādāya vartate / katham? anivartyena cetasā apravṛttibhraṣṭena manasā / tataḥprabhṛti tadādiṃ kṛtvā / suptasya middhākrāntacittasya pramattasya vikṣiptacittasyāpi / ubhayatrāpi saṃbadhyate / upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat / gacchato 'pi tiṣṭhato 'pi niṣaṇṇasyāpi bhuñjānasyāpi mūrcchādyavasthāyāmapītyādi draṣṭavyam / anekaśa iti / pratikṣaṇamanekavāram / avicchinnāḥ puṇyadhārāḥ nirantarasaṃtatayaḥ śubhavegāḥ pravartante / nabhaḥsamāḥ pratikṣaṇamākāśadhātupramāṇāḥ / tasmāt pratipattisāreṇa bodhisattvena bhavitavyam / āryasamādhirāje coktam-
body.translated_text: "From the time when" means from [the time] beginning with which. The realm of beings is "boundless" — having no limit, no measure — pervading the expanse of space. "For the liberation" — for the purpose of liberation, the cause of the cessation of all suffering. "He takes up that mind" — he takes up and abides in the mind of perfect awakening. How? "With an irreversible intention" — with a mind that does not lapse from engagement. "From then on" — making that the starting point. "Even for one who is sleeping" — whose mind is overcome by torpor — "or heedless" — whose mind is distracted. Both [qualifiers] connect with both [verses]. And this is an illustrative [list]: one should understand [that it applies] also to one who is walking, standing, sitting, eating, or even in a state of fainting, etc. "Many times" means many times at every moment. "Uninterrupted streams of merit" — continuous successions of wholesome impulses — "flow forth." "Equal to the sky" — at every moment equal in measure to the expanse of space. Therefore, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be one whose essence is practice. As stated in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s> —

body.text: tasmāt pratipattisāro bhaviṣyāmi, ityevaṃ kumāra śikṣitavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ? pratipattisārasya kumāra na durlabhā bhavati anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti [samādhi-10] //
body.translated_text: "Therefore, 'I shall be one whose essence is practice' — thus, O Prince, one should train. For what reason? For one whose essence is practice, O Prince, unsurpassed perfect awakening is not difficult to attain." [<s>Samādhi</s> 10] //

body.text: avicchinnapuṇyaṃtvamasya bhagavataivoktamityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing that this uninterrupted merit was stated by the Blessed One himself, he says —

children.translated_text: "This was stated with reasoning, in the <s>Subāhupṛcchā</s>,
by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, for the sake of beings of inferior inclination. // Bca_1.20 //
