body.text: idameva aprameyapuṇyatvaṃ svayameva ātmanaiva tathāgato buddho bhagavānuktavān kathitavān / kva? subāhupṛcchāyāṃ subāhupṛcchānāmni sūtre / katham? sopapattikaṃ sayuktikam / kimartham? hīnādhimuktisattvārtham / hīne śrāvakapratyekabuddhayāne adhimuktiḥ śraddhā chando vā
body.translated_text: This very immeasurable merit was stated, was declared, by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — himself, by his own [authority]. Where? In the <s>Subāhupṛcchā</s> — in the <s>sūtra</s> named <s>Subāhupṛcchā</s>. How? 'With reasoning' — with logical support. For what purpose? 'For the sake of beings of inferior inclination.' Those who have inclination (<s>adhimukti</s>) — faith or desire — toward the inferior — the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles —

body.text: yeṣāṃ te / te sattvāśca / tebhya idaṃ tadartham / tat prayojanamuddiśyetyarthaḥ / tathā hi- ye aniyatagotrāściratarakālena bahutarasaṃbhāropārjanabhītā mahāyānāccittaṃ vyāvartya laghutarakālena alpatarasaṃbhārasādhye śrāvakapratyekabuddhayāne cittamutpādayanti, tadvayāvartanārthaṃ bhagavānupapattimāha //
body.translated_text: those are the beings, and it is for their sake. The meaning is: with that [specific] purpose in view. Namely: those of indeterminate lineage (<s>aniyatagotra</s>) who, frightened by the longer time and greater accumulations [required], turn their minds away from the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and generate the mind toward the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, which are achievable in a shorter time with lesser accumulations — for the purpose of turning them back [to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>], the Blessed One stated the reasoning. //

body.text: tāmevopapattiṃ vṛttadvayena kathayannāha-
body.translated_text: Stating that very reasoning in two verses, he says —

children.translated_text: "Thinking 'I shall cure the headaches of beings' —

children.text: aprameyeṇa puṇyena gṛhyate sma hitāśayaḥ // Bca_1.21 //
children.translated_text: one possessed of a beneficial intention is seized by immeasurable merit. // Bca_1.21 //
How much more so one who wishes to remove the incomparable suffering of each and every [being],
and who wishes to create immeasurable virtue in each and every being! // Bca_1.22 //

body.text: katipayajanānāṃ mastakapīḍāṃ nāśayāmi mantreṇa agadena vā, ityevaṃ manasi kurvan apramāṇena sukṛtena asau kalyāṇābhiprāyo gṛhīto draṣṭavyaḥ / kiṃ punarapramāṇaṃ saṃsāraduḥkhaṃ pratisattvamapramāṇasya jagato hartumicchataḥ / api ca tacchūlamapanīya sarvasattvān sarvaguṇasamaṅginaḥ kartumicchataḥ kimaprameyaṃ puṇyaṃ na bhavati? iti vibhaktivipariṇāmena yojanīyam / avicchinnāḥ puṇyadhārāḥ kimuta tasya na pravartante nabhaḥsamā iti / tasmād yathā saṃbhārabāhulyasādhyaṃ buddhatvam, yathā saṃbhāravaipulye 'pi pratikṣaṇamiti hetuviśeṣādatraiva mahāyāne mahānlābhaḥ / ato nāsmaccittamabhayasthāne kātaratayā vinivartanīyamityupadarśitaṃ bhavati / yadvakṣyati-
body.translated_text: Thinking in his mind, 'I shall cure the head-pain of a few people through a spell or a remedy' — that one of benevolent intention is to be seen as seized, [that is,] characterized, by incalculable good merit. How much more so for one who wishes to remove the immeasurable suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> for each and every being of the immeasurable world! And moreover, for one who, having removed that suffering, wishes to make all beings complete with all virtues — would the merit not be immeasurable? This should be construed with an inversion of cases [i.e., rhetorically]. Would not uninterrupted streams of merit, equal to the sky, flow for such a one? Therefore, just as Buddhahood is achievable through abundant accumulations, and just as even amidst the vastness of accumulations there is [merit] at every moment — through this special cause, the great gain is in this very <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Hence it is shown that one should not turn one's mind away from the safe ground out of timidity. As he will say —

children.translated_text: "Exhausting former sins and receiving oceans of merit,
through the power of <s>bodhicitta</s> alone, he is swifter even than the <s>Śrāvakas</s>."

body.text: iti // [bodhi. 7.29]
body.translated_text: [<s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> 7.29]

body.text: yaścaivaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ hitasukhārthamudyujyate, sa devādibhyo 'pyasādhāraṇaguṇātvāt praśasya ityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: And showing that one who thus exerts himself for the welfare and happiness of all beings is praiseworthy even beyond the gods and others, due to his uncommon qualities, he says —

children.translated_text: "Whose mother or father has such a wish for benefit?

children.text: devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ vā brahmaṇāṃ vā bhaviṣyati // Bca_1.23 //
children.translated_text: Which gods, which <s>ṛṣis</s>, which <s>Brahmās</s> would possess it? // Bca_1.23 //

body.text: kasya sattvasya / māturjananyāḥ / kasya piturvā janakasya / devatānāṃ somavaruṇādīnām / ṛṣīṇāṃ vā vasiṣṭhagotamādīnām / brahmaṇāṃ vā vedhasām / iyamīdṛśī hītāśaṃsā hitopasaṃhāramatiḥ yādṛśī samanantaraṃ pratipāditā bodhisattvasya bhaviṣyati iti / āstāṃ tāvat bhūtā bhavati vā, bhaviṣyatyapi naiva kasyacidbodhisattvamantareṇānyasya //
body.translated_text: "Whose" — of which being. "Mother" — the one who gave birth. "Or whose father" — the begetter. "Of the gods" — of <s>Soma</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and others. "Or of the <s>ṛṣis</s>" — of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gotama</s>, and others. "Or of the <s>Brahmās</s>" — of the Creators. "This" — such — "wish for benefit" — the intention of conferring welfare — "of such a kind" as has just been demonstrated of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — "would exist?" — would it exist? Let alone whether it has existed or exists — it will never exist for anyone else apart from a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: kutaḥ punaretadityāha-
body.translated_text: "Why is this so?" he says —

children.translated_text: "For those very beings, even in their own interest, such a wish

children.text: notpannapūrvaḥ svapne 'pi parārthe saṃbhavaḥ kutaḥ // Bca_1.24 //
children.translated_text: has never arisen even in a dream — how could it arise for the sake of others? // Bca_1.24 //

body.text: teṣāṃ mātrādīnāṃ svārthe 'pi ātmanaḥ kṛte 'pi eṣa manorathaḥ sarvaduḥkhamapahartum, apramāṇaguṇānādhātuṃ notpannapūrvaḥ abhūtapūrvaḥ svapne 'pi / āstāṃ tāvajjāgradavasthāyāṃ buddhipūrvakamutpannaḥ / parārthe kadācidutpadyeta ityāha- parārthe saṃbhavaḥ kutaḥ / ātmā hi vallabho lokasya parasmāt / tatraiva cennāsti, parārthe saṃbhāvanāpi kutaḥ? athavā / svapne 'pi parārthe saṃbhavaḥ kutaḥ iti yojyam //
body.translated_text: For those mothers and others, even for their own sake — this aspiration to remove all suffering and to establish [beings in] immeasurable qualities — has never arisen before, was unprecedented even in a dream. Let alone [the question of whether it] has arisen intentionally in the waking state. He says that it might sometimes arise for the sake of others — 'how could it come about for others' sake?' The self is indeed dear to the world, dearer than others. If even there [in one's own case] it does not exist, how could there even be a possibility for others' sake? Or alternatively, it should be construed as: 'how could it come about for others' sake, even in a dream?'

body.text: tadevamasādhāraṇatvaṃ bodhisattvasya pratipādya upasaṃharannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the extraordinary nature of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, summing up he says —

children.translated_text: This extraordinary jewel among beings — how does it arise as something unprecedented,
since this intention for others' benefit does not arise in others even for their own sake? // Bca_1.25 //

body.text: evamatyadbhutakarmakāritayā durlabhotpādāt sattva eva ratnaviśeṣaḥ apūrvaḥ anupalabdhapūrvaḥ / ayamiti yādṛśaguṇo 'tra kathitaḥ / jāyate katham / kathamityadbhute / kasmāt punarevamucyate? āha- yatparārtheti / yasya mahātmanaḥ parārthāśayaḥ anyeṣāṃ sattvānāmuktakrameṇa na svārthe 'pyupajāyate ityasmāt //
body.translated_text: 'Jewel among beings' — because of performing such wondrous deeds and being of rare arising, it is a special jewel among beings. 'Unprecedented' — not previously found. 'This' — one of such qualities as described here. 'How does it arise?' — 'how' [expresses] wonder. 'Why is this said?' He says 'since for others' benefit' etc. — because the intention for others' benefit of this great being does not arise even for their own sake in other beings, in the manner described.

body.text: atra ca anye 'pi bodhicittotpādakasya guṇā vaktavyāḥ / yathā āryagaṇḍavyūhe bhagavatā āryamaitreyeṇa sudhanamadhikṛtya udbhāvitāḥ / te ca ativistareṇa śāstrakṛtā śikṣāsamuccaye darśitāśca, tatraiva avadhārayitavyā //
body.translated_text: And here, other qualities of the one who generates <s>bodhicitta</s> should also be stated — as they were extolled by the Blessed <s>Āryamaitreya</s> with reference to <s>Sudhana</s> in the <s>Āryagaṇḍavyūha</s>. These have been shown at great length by the author of the treatise in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, and should be ascertained there.

body.text: punarapi bodhicittānuśaṃsādvāreṇa bodhisattvasyāprameyapuṇyatvamāha-
body.translated_text: Again, through the door of the benefits of <s>bodhicitta</s>, he states the immeasurable merit of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> —

children.translated_text: Of the jewel-mind that is the seed of the world's joy and the medicine for the world's suffering —

children.text: cittaratnasya yatpuṇyaṃ tatkathaṃ hi pramīyatām // Bca_1.26 //
children.translated_text: how could its merit be measured? // Bca_1.26 //

body.text: sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaprāmodyakāraṇasya devādisarvasaṃpattinidānabhūtatvāt / cittaratnasya bodhicittasya yat puṇyaṃ tat kathaṃ hi pramīyatām, kena prakāreṇa nāma saṃkhyeyatām / ativipulatayā pramātumaśakyatvāt / etaduktamāryavīradattaparipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: Because it is the source of all the attainments of gods and others, the cause of all delight for all beings. The merit of the jewel-mind — of <s>bodhicitta</s> — 'how could it be measured?' — in what manner could it be enumerated? Because of its extreme vastness, it is impossible to measure. As stated in the <s>Āryavīradattaparipṛcchā</s> —

children.translated_text: If the merit arising from <s>bodhicitta</s> were to have physical form,
filling the entire space-element, it would be even more than that.

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: yadi nāma sāmānyena nirdeśaḥ, tathāpi prasthānacittasyeti draṣṭavyam, tasyaiva prakṛtatvāt / punarapi tasyaiva viśeṣaṇamāha- jagadduḥkhauṣadhasya ceti / sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ kāyikacaitasikasarvaduḥkhanivartanatayā sarvavyādhiharaṇamahāgadasvabhāvatvāt / tadanena abhyudayaniḥśreyasahetutvaṃ bodhicittasya pratipāditaṃ bhavati / ato yuktameva asya asaṃkhyeyapuṇyatvamityuktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: Although the instruction is given in general terms, it should still be understood as referring to the aspiration-mind (<s>prasthānacittasya</s>), since that is the topic at hand. Again he states a further qualification of that very [mind] — 'and the medicine for the world's suffering' — because it has the nature of a great remedy that removes all disease, through eliminating all physical and mental suffering of all living beings. By this, it is demonstrated that <s>bodhicitta</s> is the cause of both worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). Hence it is rightly said that its merit is immeasurable.

body.text: kathaṃ punaretadyuktamityāśaṅkaya pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Anticipating the objection 'how is this justified?' and demonstrating [it], he says —

children.translated_text: By the mere aspiration for benefit, [the merit] surpasses the worship of <s>Buddhas</s>;
how much more so from the exertion for the complete happiness of all beings? // Bca_1.27 //

body.text: sarvajagatparitrāṇāya buddho bhaveyamityadhyāśayena āśaṃsanāt prārthanāt kevalāt pratipattivikalādbodhicittādityarthaḥ / yatpuṇyaṃ bhavati tadbuddhapūjāmatiśete ityāgamādbhavatyeva puṇyaskandhaprasavahetuḥ / iti prathamasya bodhicittasya māhātmyamuktam / etadapi tatraivoktam-
body.translated_text: The meaning is: from <s>bodhicitta</s> that consists merely of aspiration — prayer — 'May I become a <s>Buddha</s> for the protection of all the world,' lacking in actual practice — whatever merit arises, that surpasses the worship of <s>Buddhas</s>. From scripture, it is indeed a cause for producing an accumulation of merit. Thus the greatness of the first [aspiration] <s>bodhicitta</s> has been stated. This too is stated there [in the same text] —

children.translated_text: He who would give <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
all filled with precious jewels, to the Lords of the World —
and one who, merely with palms joined, would incline the mind toward awakening —

children.text: iyaṃ viśiṣyate pūjā yasyānto 'pi na vidyate //
children.translated_text: this [latter] worship is superior; its end cannot be found.

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ sarvaduḥkhitajanānāṃ sarvaduḥkhamapanīya sarvasukhasaṃpannān kariṣyāmītyudyogakaraṇādatiśayavat puṇyaṃ na bhavati //
body.translated_text: How much more so — would there not be extraordinary merit from exerting oneself [thinking] 'I shall remove all suffering of all suffering beings and make them endowed with all happiness'?

body.text: nanu hitāhitaprāptiparihārayoḥ svayameva sattvā vicakṣaṇāḥ / tat kutrodyamasyopayoga iti vṛttatritayena pariharannāha-
body.translated_text: Objection: 'Beings themselves are discerning regarding the obtaining and avoidance of the beneficial and harmful. So where is the use of exertion?' He answers this with a set of three [verses] —

children.translated_text: They run toward suffering itself, though wishing to escape from suffering;

children.text: sukhecchayaiva saṃmohāt svasukhaṃ ghnanti śatruvat // Bca_1.28 //
children.translated_text: out of delusion, with the very desire for happiness, they destroy their own happiness, as if it were an enemy. // Bca_1.28 //
He who would give satisfaction with all happinesses to those who crave happiness and are afflicted in manifold ways,

children.text: tṛptiṃ sarvasukhaiḥ kuryātsarvāḥ pīḍāścchinatti ca // Bca_1.29 //
children.translated_text: and who cuts off all their afflictions, // Bca_1.29 //
and who also destroys their delusion — where is a good person equal to him?

children.text: kuto vā tādṛśaṃ mitraṃ puṇyaṃ vā tādṛśaṃ kutaḥ // Bca_1.30 //
children.translated_text: Where is such a friend? And where is such merit? // Bca_1.30 //

body.text: duḥkhānniḥsaraṇābhiprāyāḥ prāṇātipātādibhirakuśalaiḥ karmabhiḥ kṣudhādiduḥkhapratīkāramicchantaḥ / duḥkhameva narakādiprapātavedanāsvabhāvam / abhidhāvanti tadabhimukhāḥ pravartante / duḥkhameva praviśantītyarthaḥ / śalabhā iva dīpaśikhāmiti / ata eva sukhecchayaiva sukhābhilāṣeṇaiva svasukhaṃ ghnanti śatruvat / ātmasukhaghātāya kathamātmanaiva śatravo bhavantīti cet, saṃmohād viparyāsavaśāt hitāhitaprāptiparihārayoḥ parijñānābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: Those whose intention is to escape from suffering, desiring a remedy for sufferings such as hunger through unwholesome actions like taking life — they run toward suffering itself, toward what has the nature of the sensation of falling into hell-realms and the like. They rush toward it, proceed toward it — meaning they enter into suffering itself. Like moths toward a lamp-flame. And therefore, with the very desire for happiness — through the longing for happiness alone — they destroy their own happiness 'as if it were an enemy.' If [one asks] 'how do they become enemies to themselves for the destruction of their own happiness?' — [the answer is:] through delusion, through the power of wrong perception, through the absence of understanding regarding obtaining and avoiding the beneficial and harmful.

body.text: ato yaḥ puṇyātmā akāraṇavatsalaḥ teṣāṃ viparyastānāṃ sukharaṅkāṇāṃ sukhabhilāṣukāṇāṃ sarvaśo 'labdhasukhānāṃ pīḍitānāṃ duḥkhitānām / anekaśa iti anekairduḥkhaśatairbahudhā bādhitānāṃ tṛptimāpyāyanaṃ sarvasukhaiḥ kuryāt kāyikacaitasikaiḥ / yadi vā / anekaśaḥ anekaprakāraṃ tṛptiṃ sarvasukhaiḥ kuryāt iti yojanīyam / na sukhatṛptimātraṃ janayati, kiṃ tarhi sarvāḥ pīḍāḥ samastā duḥkhā vedanāścchinatti ca śamayati ca //
body.translated_text: Therefore, he who is of meritorious nature, compassionate without cause — for those who are deluded, who crave happiness, who have everywhere failed to obtain happiness, who are afflicted, suffering — 'in manifold ways' means tormented in many ways by hundreds of sufferings — he 'would give satisfaction,' that is, refreshment, 'with all happinesses,' both physical and mental. Or alternatively, it should be construed: 'in manifold ways' — in many different manners — 'he would give satisfaction with all happinesses.' He does not merely produce satisfaction of happiness, but rather 'he cuts off' — pacifies — 'all afflictions,' all painful sensations.

body.text: na kevalaṃ duḥkhapraśāntiṃ sukhatṛptiṃ ca karoti, nāśayatyapi saṃmoham, aparijñānamapi nivartayati /
body.translated_text: Not only does he bring about the pacification of suffering and satisfaction of happiness — 'he also destroys delusion' — he also removes non-understanding —

body.text: apathamidameṣa panthā bhayamata ita eta gāta māsādam /
body.translated_text: 'This is not the path; this is the path. Here is danger; go this way. Do not approach that!'

body.text: iti heyopādeyamārgaprakāśanāt / yaścaivaṃ paravyasananivartanaparatanno hitasukhavidhānatatparaśca
body.translated_text: — through illuminating the path of what is to be avoided and what is to be adopted. And he who thus is intent upon removing the misfortunes of others and devoted to providing welfare and happiness

body.text: sarvabhūtānām / sādhustena samaḥ kutaḥ, tena mahātmanā tulyaḥ sādhuḥ kutaḥ? naiva kutaścidvidyate akāraṇaparamavatsalasvabhāvatvāt / kuto vā tādṛśaṃ mitram, hitasukhopasaṃhārapravaṇamānasaṃ paramaviśvāsasthānaṃ tādṛśaṃ tatsamaṃ mitram, suhṛt kutaḥ? naiva saṃbhavati / puṇyaṃ vā tādṛśaṃ kutaḥ? evaṃ viharato bodhisattvasya yat puṇyamupajāyate, tadapi na kenacitpuṇyena samānam //
body.translated_text: for all beings — 'where is a good person equal to him?' — where is a good person equal to that great being? There is absolutely none, because his nature is one of supreme compassion without cause. 'Where is such a friend?' — a friend equally trustworthy, with a mind inclined toward conveying welfare and happiness, a supreme object of confidence — where is such a friend, such an equal companion? It is simply impossible. 'And where is such merit?' — whatever merit arises for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelling thus, that too is not equaled by any [other] merit.

children.translated_text: He who would make a return for what was done — even he is praiseworthy;
but what need be said of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who is good without being asked? // Bca_1.31 //

body.text: pūrvaṃ bhayasaṃkaṭavyasaneṣu upakṛtamanena ityupakṛte sati pratyupakāraṃ karoti yaḥ, so 'pi tāvat praśasyate lokena stūyate sādhurayamiti / yaḥ punaravyāpāritasādhuḥ anabhyarthitakalyāṇopanetā bodhisattvaḥ, kimucyatāṃ kimaparamabhidhīyatām? tasya praśaṃsā kartumaśakyetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: When one has previously been benefited in times of danger, distress, or calamity, he who makes a return — even he is praiseworthy, celebrated by the world as 'this is a good person.' But what should be said — what else needs to be stated — about the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who is 'good without being asked' — who brings goodness without being requested? The meaning is that praise of him is impossible [to fully express].

body.text: dṛṣṭavyavahāramapekṣyāpi bodhisattvasya puṇyamāhātmyamudbhāvayannāha-
body.translated_text: Highlighting the greatness of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s merit even with reference to observed convention, he says —

children.translated_text: One who gives a meal to a few people is honored by the world as a doer of good,
though [it is] momentary, from giving only a morsel of food, contemptuously, for the sustenance of half a day. // Bca_1.32 //

body.text: parimitasattvānāmāhārapānamātradānasamādānamādiśan puṇyakarmā ayamiti pūjyate satkriyate janaiḥ satkarmaratairlokaiḥ / tadapi dānaṃ kṣaṇam, na sakalamahaḥ, tadardhaṃ vā, api tu muhūrtamekam / aśanakamātradānata iti / kutsitamaśanamaśanakam, apraṇītaṃ bhojanam, tadeva kevalaṃ tanmātram, tathāvidhavyañjanarahitam / tasya dānataḥ parityāgataḥ / katham? saparibhavam / kriyāviśeṣaṇametat / satiraskāraṃ namaskārāpuraḥsaram / haṭhātsatrāgāraṃ praviśataḥ khaṭacapeṭādinā prahṛtyeti yāvat / punaḥ kiṃbhūtāt? divasārdhayāpanāt praharadvayopastambhanāt / madhyānhe bhuktvā sāyaṃ punarāhārānveṣaṇāt //
body.translated_text: One who undertakes the giving of mere food and drink to a limited number of beings is worshipped, honored by people — by worldly folk who delight in good deeds — [thinking] 'this is a doer of meritorious deeds.' And that giving [is] momentary — not for an entire day, or even half of one — but rather for a single moment. 'From giving only a morsel of food' — <s>aśanaka</s> means inferior food, unrefined nourishment, merely that alone, devoid of such relishes. 'From giving' — from the relinquishment of that. How? 'Contemptuously' — this qualifies the action — with disrespect, without a preceding salutation. As when one who forcibly enters the alms-hall is struck with a slap and so forth. Furthermore, of what kind? 'For the sustenance of half a day' — for support through two watches [of the day]. Having eaten at midday, one must again seek food in the evening.

body.text: bodhisattvasya punaretadviparītaṃ dānamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s giving is the opposite of this, he says —

children.translated_text: How much more so for one who gives for unlimited time, to an unlimited number of beings,
inexhaustibly until the exhaustion of sky and beings, the complete fulfillment of all desires? // Bca_1.33 //

body.text: na vidyate avadhiriyattā / iyadbhayaḥ śatasahasralakṣakoṭisaṃkhyebhyo dāsyāmi, tataḥ paraṃ neti na sattvānāṃ gaṇanayā dadāti, kiṃ tu niravadhisattvasaṃkhyayā / nāpi niyatakālam,
body.translated_text: There is no limit (<s>avadhi</s>), no fixed extent. He does not give with a number [in mind, thinking] 'I shall give to this many — a hundred thousand, a <s>lakṣa</s>, a <s>koṭi</s> — and beyond that, no' — he does not give with a count of beings, but rather to an unlimited number of beings. Nor for a fixed time

body.text: api tu niravadhikālam / kalpaśatasahasralakṣakoṭiśataṃ yāvaddāsyāmi, tataḥ paraṃ neti sāvadhikaṃ na dadāti / gaganeti / gaganamiva janāḥ gaganajanāḥ / yathā ākāśamaparyantaṃ tathā jano 'pītyarthaḥ / yadi vā / gaganaṃ ca janāśca te gaganajanāḥ / teṣāṃ parikṣayaḥ paryavadānam / yāvadākāśadhāturyāvacca sattvā na parinirvṛtāḥ tāvadavadhikam / yadvakṣyati-
body.translated_text: — but rather for unlimited time. He does not give with a limit [thinking] 'I shall give for a hundred thousand <s>lakṣa</s> <s>koṭi</s> hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, and beyond that, no.' 'Gagana' — beings like space (<s>gagana</s>) are 'sky-beings' (<s>gaganajana</s>). Just as space is boundless, so too are beings — that is the meaning. Or alternatively, 'gagana' (sky) and 'jana' (beings) — those are 'gaganajana.' Their 'exhaustion' (<s>parikṣaya</s>) means complete purification. Until the space-element [exists] and until beings have not entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — with such a limit. As will be stated —

body.text: ākāśasya sthitiryāvadyāvacca jagataḥ sthitiḥ /

children.translated_text: so long may my existence endure. [<s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> 10.55]

body.translated_text: As long as space endures and as long as the world endures,

body.text: tasmādakṣayam, na vidyate kṣayaḥ paryanto 'syeti kṛtvā / ayamabhiprāyaḥ- gaganajanaparikṣayāvadhi yaddānaṃ tadvastuto 'kṣayameva, teṣāṃ parikṣayābhāvāt / nāpi pratiniyataṃ vastu, api tu sakalamanorathasaṃprapūraṇam / yadyasyābhimataṃ tat sarvamanavadyamabhiprāyālhādanakaraṃ paramapremagauravasatkārapriyavacanapuraḥsaraṃ pramuditamanasā anuprayacchato bodhisattvasya kiṃ punaḥ pūjā na yujyate? tasya sutarāṃ yujyate iti yojyam / yaduktaṃ nārāyaṇaparipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: Therefore 'inexhaustible' — because there is no end, no boundary, to it. The intent is this: the giving that has the exhaustion of sky-and-beings as its limit is in reality inexhaustible, because their exhaustion is impossible. Nor is it a fixed object [that is given], but rather 'the complete fulfillment of all desires.' Whatever is wished for by whomever — all of that, blameless, causing delight of intention, preceded by supreme love, respect, honor, and kind words — for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who gives with a delighted mind, how much more is worship not fitting? For him it is supremely fitting — thus it should be construed. As stated in the <s>Nārāyaṇaparipṛcchā</s> —

body.text: na tadvastu upādātavyaṃ yasmin vastuni nāsya tyāgacittamutpadyate / na tyāgabuddhiḥ krameta / yāvat ayaṃ mamātmabhāvaḥ sarvasattvebhya utsṛṣṭaḥ parityaktaḥ, prāgeva bāhyāni vastūni / yasya yasya sattvasya yena yena yadyat kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati, tasmai tasmai tattaddāsyāmi / tatsaṃvidyamānaṃ hastaṃ hastārthikebhyo dāsyāmi, yāvat śiraḥ śirorthikebhyaḥ parityakṣyāmi, kaḥ punarvādo bāhyeṣu vastuṣu / yaduta dhanadhānyajātaruparajataratnābharaṇahayarathagajavāhanagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarājyarāṣṭrarājadhānīpattanadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaputraduhitṛparivāreṣu / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'There is no object to be grasped at regarding which no thought of relinquishment arises in him. No thought of renunciation would occur [to one not so inclined]. As far as: "This self-existence of mine is released, abandoned to all beings; how much more external things!" For whatever being, by whatever means, whatever may need to be done — to each of them I shall give that. I shall give my available hand to those who need a hand; I shall relinquish my head to those who need a head — what need be said regarding external things? That is: wealth, grain, gold, silver, jewels, ornaments, horses, chariots, elephants, vehicles, villages, cities, market-towns, populaces, kingdoms, dominions, royal capitals, garments, slaves male and female, workers, servants, sons, daughters, and retinue.' Thus in detail.

body.text: evaṃ ca guṇaratnasamuccayasthāne parahitasukhavidhānaikaparamamahāvrate bodhisattve svātmahitakāmaiḥ svacittaṃ rakṣitavyaṃ prayatnataḥ ityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating that those who desire their own welfare should protect their own mind with effort regarding the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who is a repository of the jewels of qualities and is established in the supreme great vow of providing welfare and happiness to others, he says —

children.text: iti sattrapatau jinasya putre kaluṣaṃ sve hṛdaye karoti yaśca /
children.translated_text: Thus, he who produces impurity in his own heart toward the son of the <s>Jina</s>, who is a patron of feasts —

children.text: kaluṣodayasaṃkhyayā sa kalpān narakeṣvāvasatīti nātha āha // Bca_1.34 //
children.translated_text: He dwells in the hells for as many <s>kalpas</s> as the number of moments of polluted [thought] that arose — thus the Protector has said. // Bca_1.34 //

body.text: ityevamuktakrameṇa sattrapattau sarvadā sukhadānapatau jinasya putre sugatasya sute / bodhisattve ityarthaḥ / kaluṣaṃ pāpacittaṃ sve hṛdaye ātmacittasaṃtāne karoti utpādayati durātmā yaḥ, sa narakeṣvāvasati iti nātho buddho bhagavānāha brūte / upānvadhyāḍvasaḥ iti karmatve prāpte adhikaraṇavivakṣā / kiyad yāvat kaluṣodayasaṃkhyayā kalpān / yāvataḥ kṣaṇāṃstatsaṃtāne kaluṣacittamutpadyate, tāvataḥ kalpān kaluṣacittakṣaṇasaṃkhyān narakeṣu tiṣṭhatīti bhāvaḥ / yaduktaṃ praśāntaviniścayaprātihāryasūtre-
body.translated_text: Thus, in the manner stated — in the <s>sattrapatti</s> (a son of the <s>Jina</s>), who is always a bestower of happiness, a son of the <s>Sugata</s> — that is, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — 'he generates a polluted [thought]' means: whoever, being evil-natured, produces — generates — a polluted, evil thought in his own heart — in his own mental continuum — 'he dwells in the hells' — thus the Protector, the <s>Buddha</s> Blessed One, has said — declared. The locative (<s>upānvadhyāḍvasaḥ</s>) indicates the sense of the locus of action. For how long? 'For as many <s>kalpas</s> as the number of moments of polluted [thought] that arose.' For as many moments as a polluted thought arises in that [being's] continuum, for that many <s>kalpas</s> — <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the moments of polluted thought — he remains in the hells: this is the meaning. As stated in the <s>Praśāntaviniścayaprātihāryasūtra</s> —

body.text: yāvanti mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo bodhisattvasyāntike pratighacittānyutpādayati avamanyanācittāni vā, tāvataḥ kalpāṃstena saṃnāhaḥ saṃnaddhavyaḥ- vastavyaṃ mayā mahānarakeṣu iti //
body.translated_text: 'For as many thoughts of hostility or contempt as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> generates toward a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for that many <s>kalpas</s> must he don the armor [again] — [thinking:] "I must dwell in the great hells."'

body.text: nanu tathāgatasya duṣṭacittena rudhiramutpādayato nāvīcau cittotpādanakṣaṇasaṃkhyayā kalpān avasthitiruktā / na tathāgatāt kaścidadhikataraḥ saṃbhavati trailokye / tat kathamidamatidurghaṭaṃ nīyate? satyam / na khalu yathābhūtamasmin naye vastutattvavyavasthā / sarvasya pravacanasya neyanītārthatayā vyavasthāpanāt / na hi kaścit tathāgate sadevako 'pi loko duṣṭacittamutpādayituṃ kṣamate / analpakalpasaṃkhyayā abhyāsena sarvasattveṣu maitracittasya sātmībhāvāt, nāsya kāye śastraṃ kramatīti maitracittasyānuśaṃsakathanāt / na ca karmaplutiriha vastuto darśitā / karmāvaraṇasya buddhānāṃ prahīṇatvāt / tasmādvaineyajanābhisaṃdhinā tadupadarśitaṃ na paramārthataḥ / bodhisattvāpakāre tu buddhatvameva samūlopaghātamupahataṃ bhavet / tathā ca sadevakasya lokasya arthaḥ upahato bhavet / yathāgamamidamuktam / paramārthamiha bhagavāneva jānāti / idamuktaṃ ca śraddhābalādhānāvatāramudrāsūtre-
body.translated_text: Objection: 'But it is not stated that one who, with hostile intent toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, draws [his] blood dwells [in hell] for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the number of moments of hostile thought-generation. No one superior to the <s>Tathāgata</s> is possible in the three worlds. So how is this extremely difficult [proposition] maintained?' True. Indeed, in this system, the establishment of the real nature of things is not according to the literal [sense]. Because all of the [<s>Buddha</s>'s] word is established as requiring interpretation (<s>neyārtha</s>) and definitive in meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>). For no one, even in the world including gods, is able to generate a hostile thought toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> — because through practice over no few <s>kalpas</s>, the mind of loving-kindness toward all beings has become his very nature, and therefore weapons do not reach his body — this being stated as a benefit of the mind of loving-kindness. Nor is the maturation of <s>karma</s> shown here as real. Because <s>karma</s>-obscuration has been abandoned by <s>Buddhas</s>. Therefore, that was shown with the intention [of training] those to be disciplined, not ultimately. But in the case of harming a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Buddhahood</s> itself — the very root — would be destroyed. And thus the welfare of the world including gods would be destroyed. This was stated according to scripture. The ultimate [meaning] here is known by the Blessed One alone. This is stated in the <s>Śraddhābalādhānāvatāramudrāsūtra</s> —

body.text: yaḥ kaścinmañjuśrīḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā gaṅgānadīvālukāsamān stūpān vinipātayeddahedvā, yaścānyaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā mahāyānādhimuktasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya vyāpādakhilakrodhacittamutpādya ākrośayet paribhāṣayet, ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ pāpaṃ praviśati / tat kasmāddhetoḥ? bodhisattvanirjātā hi buddhā bhagavantaḥ, buddhanirjātāśca stūpāḥ sarvasukhopadhānāni ca sarvadevanikāyāśca / bodhisattvamasatkṛtya sarvabuddhā asatkṛtā bhavanti / bodhisattvaṃ satkṛtya sarvabuddhāḥ satkṛtā bhavanti / ityādi //
body.translated_text: 'If, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, any son or daughter of good family were to cause the collapse or burn <s>stūpas</s> equal in number to the grains of sand in the river Ganges, and another son or daughter of good family were to generate a mind of hostility, rancor, and anger toward a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who aspires to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and were to revile and abuse [him] — this latter accumulates incomparably greater evil than the former. For what reason? Because the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> arise from <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>stūpas</s> arise from <s>Buddhas</s>, as do all bases of happiness and all assemblies of gods. By disrespecting a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, all <s>Buddhas</s> are disrespected. By honoring a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, all <s>Buddhas</s> are honored.' And so forth.

body.text: yasya punastatra prasannaṃ cittamutpadyate, tasya kiyat puṇyaphalamupajāyate, ityāha-
body.translated_text: Now, for one in whom a faithful mind arises toward them, how much merit-fruit is produced? He says —

children.text: atha yasya manaḥ prasādameti prasavettasya tato 'dhikaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: But for one whose mind reaches faith [in them], the fruit produced thereby is even greater;

children.text: mahatā hi balena pāpakaṃ jinaputreṣu śubhaṃ tvayatnataḥ // Bca_1.35 //
children.translated_text: for evil toward the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> [requires] great force, while good [arises] effortlessly. // Bca_1.35 //

body.text: yasya punaḥ puṇyātmano manaḥ prasādamupayāti bodhisattve, prasavettasya tato 'dhikaṃ phalam, tasya prasannacittasya prasavedupajāyeta tato 'dhikaṃ phalaṃ tasmātpūrvakapāpaphalād bahutaraṃ puṇyakarmaphalaṃ vipākaviśeṣāt prasavedutpadyeta / yadi vā / tatsamadhikavipākaphalādhāyakaṃ karmaiva phalamucyate / adhikataraphalajanakaṃ karma upajāyate iti yāvat / uktaṃ ca niyatāniyatāvatāramudrāsūtre-
body.translated_text: 'But for one whose mind reaches faith' — for one of meritorious nature whose mind attains faith, confidence, in a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — 'the fruit produced thereby is even greater': for that one of faithful mind, a fruit would be produced — would arise — even greater than that, greater than the former evil fruit, [namely] a fruit of meritorious action, due to the distinction in its maturation. Or alternatively: that very <s>karma</s> which is productive of a superior maturation-fruit is called 'the fruit' — meaning: a <s>karma</s> generating an even greater fruit arises. As stated in the <s>Niyatāniyatāvatāramudrāsūtra</s> —

body.text: sacenmañjuśrīḥ daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvā utpāṭitākṣā bhaveyuḥ parikalpamupādāya /
body.translated_text: 'If, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all beings in all world-systems in the ten directions had their eyes plucked out — through supposition —

body.text: atha kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā teṣāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ maitracittastānyakṣīṇi janayet parikalpamupādāya / yo 'nyo vā mañjuśrīḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā mahāyānādhimuktaṃ bodhisattvaṃ prasannacittaḥ paśyet, ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati / iti //
body.translated_text: and some son or daughter of good family were, with a mind of loving-kindness toward all those beings, to generate those eyes [for them] — through supposition — and if another, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, son or daughter of good family were with faithful mind to behold a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who aspires to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — this latter generates incomparably more merit than the former.'

body.text: tasmādasmin mahati puṇyakṣetre śubhacittameva karaṇīyamātmajñaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, in this great field of merit, only a wholesome mind should be cultivated by those who know themselves.

body.text: api ca / ito 'pi śubhacittameva kartumucitam / yasmānmahatā balena paramakṛcchreṇa pāpakaṃ pāpameva pāpakaṃ kutsitatvādvā duṣkṛtaṃ karma bodhisattveṣu kriyate, teṣāṃ sakalakāyavāṅyanaḥpracārasya prasādajanakatvāt / bodhicittaprabhāvācca na bodhisattveṣu kasyacidapakāracittamutpadyate / etaduktamāryamañjuśrīvimokṣe-
body.translated_text: Moreover, it is fitting to cultivate only a wholesome mind for this further reason: because evil — evil <s>karma</s>, or base <s>karma</s> since it is contemptible — 'with great force,' with supreme difficulty, is done toward <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; because their entire conduct of body, speech, and mind is productive of faith. And through the power of <s>bodhicitta</s>, no one's mind of hostility arises toward <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. This was stated in the <s>Āryamañjuśrīvimokṣa</s> —

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra cintāmaṇiratnarājamukuṭāvabaddhānāṃ mahānāgarājñāṃ nāsti paropakramabhayam, evameva bodhicittamahākaruṇācintāmaṇiratnarājamukuṭāvabaddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ nāsti durgatyapāyaparopakramabhayam / iti //
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O son of good family, for great <s>Nāga</s> kings who have a wish-fulfilling jewel-king bound in their diadems, there is no fear of attack from others — even so, for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have the wish-fulfilling jewel-king of <s>bodhicitta</s> and great compassion bound in their diadems, there is no fear of lower rebirths, evil destinies, or attack from others.'

body.text: ataḥ kimarthamanarthopārjanaṃ kaṭukaphalaṃ teṣu prayatnataḥ prārabhyate? ata eva śubhaṃ tvayatnataḥ, saṃgrahavastvādibhiḥ sarvasattvahitasukhakarmakāritvāt pariśuddhakarmakāritayā, kvacidapi skhalitābhāvācca / aprayatnata eva prītiprasādaprāmodyamupajāyate teṣu / ataḥ kuśalaṃ punarayatnata eva prasūyate //
body.translated_text: Hence, why is the acquisition of misfortune — whose fruit is bitter — undertaken with effort toward them? Therefore 'good [arises] effortlessly' — because through the bases of gathering (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) and such, [Bodhisattvas] always perform actions for the welfare and happiness of all beings; because of their acting with purified <s>karma</s>; and because there is never any stumbling anywhere. Without any effort at all, delight, faith, and joy arise toward them. Therefore, wholesome [merit] is produced again entirely without effort.

body.text: sāṃpratamutpāditabodhicitteṣu atiśayavatā ātmanā manaḥprasādamāviṣkurvan śāstrakārastān namasyannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, manifesting his mind's faith with a surpassing nature toward those who have generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, the author, paying homage to them, says —

children.translated_text: I bow to the bodies of those in whom that precious jewel-mind has arisen;

children.text: yatrāpakāro 'pi sukhānubandhī sukhākarāṃstān śaraṇaṃ prayāmi // Bca_1.36 //
children.translated_text: even harm toward whom is followed by happiness — I go for refuge to those sources of bliss. // Bca_1.36 //

body.text: teṣāṃ puruṣakuñjarāṇāṃ śarīrāṇi ātmabhāvān namaskaromi praṇipatya vande / yatra yeṣu (yeṣāṃ?) saṃtāneṣu uditamutpannaṃ taduktānuśaṃsaṃ varacittaratnam / cittameva ratnaṃ cintāmaṇisadṛśam / varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvadāridyaduḥkhāpahāritvāt / tacca tadvaracittaratnaṃ ceti vigrahaḥ / taditi bhinnaṃ vā / iyaṃ ca adhikaguṇādhārasya satkṛtiḥ / aparamapi tadviśeṣaṇamāha- yatrāpakāro 'pīti / yeṣu paramakalyāṇahṛdayeṣu bodhisattveṣu apakāro 'pi parābhavo 'pi kṛtaḥ tatkartuḥ sukhānubandhī paraṃparayā sukhamāvahatīti / ayamabhiprāyaḥ- tatrāpakāraḥ kartumaśakyaḥ / saṃbhave vā kathaṃcit tadapakārameva nimittaṃ kṛtvā pravṛttānāṃ duṣṭābhiprāyāṇāṃ punaḥ kenacinnimittena tatprasādasamutpādanāt / tatra apakāro nirvāṇe sukhamanubandhāti / tadyathā maitrībalajātake [jātakamālā-8] pañcakānadhikṛtyoktam / bodhisattvapraṇidhānādvā apakāro 'pi sukhānubandhītyucyate / yadvakṣyati-
body.translated_text: 'I bow to the bodies' — the personal existences — 'of those' bull-among-men — I prostrate and venerate. 'In whom' — in whose continua — has 'arisen' — been born — 'that precious jewel-mind' with the benefits stated [above]. The mind itself is a jewel — like a wish-fulfilling gem. 'Precious' — supreme — because it removes all poverty and suffering. And 'that precious jewel-mind' — this is the compound resolution. Or 'that' may be separate. This is the honoring of one who is the basis of superior qualities. He states yet another qualifier — 'even harm toward whom' etc. 'In whom' — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of supremely good hearts — 'even harm' — even injury — done [to them], 'is followed by happiness' — brings happiness in succession for the doer. The meaning is this: harm toward them is impossible to accomplish. Or should it somehow occur, then — making that very harm the occasion — for those who acted with corrupt intentions, by some other occasion, through the generation of faith in them [the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>], that harm 'is followed by happiness' [leading to] <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For example, as stated in the <s>Maitrībalajātaka</s> [<s>Jātakamālā</s> 8] concerning the five [hunters]. Or, through the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vow, 'even harm is followed by happiness' is said. As will be stated —

body.text:
abhyākhyāsyanti māṃ ye ca ye cānye 'pyapakāriṇaḥ /
utprāsakāstathānye 'pi sarve syurbodhibhāginaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Those who slander me, and others too who cause harm,

body.text: iti // [bodhi. 3.16]
body.translated_text: and likewise others who mock — may all become sharers in awakening!'

body.text: athavā / yatrāpakāro 'pi yeṣāmapakāro 'pi mahākaruṇādhyāśayāt priyaputreṇa kṛta iva duḥkhaheturapi sukhameva janayati, yathā kṣāntiparicchede kathayiṣyāmaḥ / evaṃ sarvathā sukhahetutvāt sukhārthināṃ ratnākara iva ratnārthināmāśryaṇīyā bodhisattvā ityupadarśayati / sukhākarāṃstān śaraṇaṃ prayāmi / sukhasya ākarāḥ sarvasukhaikaprabhavatvāt / tān uktakrameṇa apakāre 'pi sukhahetūn / śaraṇaṃ prayāmi / te mama trāṇaṃ bhavantu iti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: [<s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> 3.16] Or alternatively: 'even harm toward whom' — even harm toward whom, because of [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s] disposition of great compassion, like [harm] done by a dear son, even though it causes suffering, generates only happiness — as we shall explain in the chapter on patience. Thus, since they are in every way a cause of happiness, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be resorted to by those desiring happiness, like a jewel-mine by those seeking jewels — this he demonstrates. 'I go for refuge to those sources of bliss.' 'Sources of bliss' — because they are the single origin of all happiness. 'Those' — in the manner stated, causes of happiness even when harmed. 'I go for refuge' — may they be my protectors: this is the meaning.

body.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ bodhicittānuśaṃsāvivaraṇaṃ nāma prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>, the exposition named 'The Benefits of <s>Bodhicitta</s>.'

body.text: 2. pāpadeśanā nāma dvitīyaḥ paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: 2. The second chapter, named '<s>Pāpadeśanā</s>' (Confession of Evil).

body.text: sāṃpratamevaṃ kṣaṇasaṃpatsamāgamaṃ durlabhamadhigamya viditabodhicittānuśaṃsaḥ bodhicittagrahaṇārthaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāmukhīkṛtya vandanapūjanaśaraṇagamanapāpadeśanāpuṇyānumodanabuddhādhyeṣaṇāyācanābodhipariṇāmanāṃ ca kurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, having obtained this rare conjunction of the moment of opportunity — having understood the benefits of <s>bodhicitta</s> — for the purpose of taking <s>bodhicitta</s>, facing the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, [the author] performs homage, worship, going for refuge, confession of evil, rejoicing in merit, requesting [the <s>Buddhas</s> to teach], supplication [not to pass into <s>nirvāṇa</s>], and dedication to awakening, saying —

children.translated_text: For the proper taking of that jewel-mind, I make worship to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

children.text: saddharmaratnasya ca nirmalasya buddhātmajānāṃ ca guṇodadhīnām // Bca_2.1 //
children.translated_text: and to the stainless jewel of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and to the sons of the <s>Buddhas</s>, oceans of good qualities. // Bca_2.1 //

body.text: tasya samanantarapratipāditānuśaṃsasya cittaratnasya grahaṇāya svīkārāya / tadutpādayitumityarthaḥ / tathāgatānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjāṃ karomi / eṣo 'hamiti bodhicittagrāhako 'yamātmānaṃ nidarśayati / ayaṃ buddharatnasya nirdeśaḥ / saddharmaratnasya ceti āgamādhigamalakṣaṇasya / nirmalasyeti trikalyāṇatayā trikoṭiśuddhasya prakṛtiprabhāsvarasya ca / sarvadā sarvamalānāmasthānatvāt, kleśānāmāgantukatvāt, samastamalāpaharaṇapaṭutvācca / ayaṃ ca dharmaratnasya nirdeśaḥ / tadātmajānāṃ ca buddhasutānām / guṇodadhīnāṃ guṇaratnasamudrāṇām āryāvalokitamañjughoṣaprabhṛtīnām / ayaṃ tu saṃgharatnasya nirdeśaḥ / ityādau ratnatrayapūjāvidhiḥ / pūjāṃ karomīti sarvatra saṃbandhanīyam / samyagiti pūjāyā eva viśeṣaṇam / samyagaviparītaṃ yathā bhavati / tīvracittaprasādena vā grahaṇasya vā viśeṣaṇam / samyaggrahaṇāya atiśayaprasannacittena na parānurodhādinā / yathā gṛhītaṃ na punarbhraśyati iti //
body.translated_text: 'For the taking' — for the acceptance — 'of that jewel-mind' whose benefits have been demonstrated immediately before; that is, for producing it. 'I make worship to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' — the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. 'This' [<s>eṣa</s>] — he points to himself, the one who would take <s>bodhicitta</s>. This is the exposition of the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel. 'And to the jewel of the true <s>Dharma</s>' — that which is characterized by scripture and realization. 'Stainless' — pure in three aspects (<s>trikalyāṇa</s>), pure at the three points (<s>trikoṭiśuddha</s>), and luminous by nature; because at all times it is not the abode of any stain; because defilements are adventitious; and because it is effective in removing all stains. This is the exposition of the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel. 'And to the sons of that [<s>Buddha</s>]' — the children of the <s>Buddha</s>. 'Oceans of good qualities' — oceans of quality-jewels — such as noble <s>Avalokita</s> and <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> and the rest. This is the exposition of the <s>Saṃgha</s>-jewel. Thus, at the outset, the method of worship to the Three Jewels. 'I make worship' should be connected everywhere [in what follows]. '<s>Samyak</s>' (properly) is a qualifier of the worship itself — so that the worship may be proper, not mistaken; or [it qualifies] with intensely faithful mind; or it is a qualifier of 'taking' — for proper taking, with a supremely faithful mind, not through compliance with others and such; so that once taken, it is never lost.

body.text: pūjāmeva kathayannāha-
body.translated_text: Describing the worship itself, he says —

children.text: yāvanti puṣpāṇi phalāni caiva bhaiṣajyajātāni ca yāni santi /
children.translated_text: Whatever flowers and fruits there are, and whatever kinds of medicines there are,

children.text: ratnāni yāvanti ca santi loke jalāni ca svacchamanoramāṇi // Bca_2.2 //
children.translated_text: and whatever jewels there are in the world, and waters that are clear and delightful — // Bca_2.2 //

body.text: yat parimāṇameṣāmiti yāvanti niravaśeṣāṇi / puṣpāṇi phalāni caiva / ākāśadhātuprasarāvadhīni sarvāṇyapīmāni aparigrahāṇi / ādāya buddhayā munipuṃgavebhyo niryātayāmyeṣa saputrakebhyaḥ iti sarvatra pūrveṣu yojanīyam / bhaiṣajyajātāni auṣadhaprakārāḥ / svacchamanoramāṇīti ratnānāmapi viśeṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: 'Whatever' — meaning all without remainder. 'Flowers and fruits.' [These extend] to the limit of the expanse of space — all these that are unowned. 'Taking [them] with [the power of] <s>Buddha</s>-mind, I offer [them] to the best of sages, together with their sons' — this should be connected with all the [previous verses]. 'Kinds of medicines' — varieties of medicinal herbs. 'Clear and delightful' is also a qualifier of 'jewels.'

children.translated_text: Mountains made of jewels, and other forest regions lovely with seclusion,

children.text: latāḥ sapuṣpābharaṇojjvalāśca drumāśca ye satphalanamraśākhāḥ // Bca_2.3 //
children.translated_text: and creepers brilliant with flower-ornaments, and trees whose branches bow with fine fruits — // Bca_2.3 //

body.text: devādilokeṣu ca gandhadhūpāḥ kalpadrumā ratnamayāśca vṛkṣāḥ /
body.translated_text: And in the worlds of gods and others, fragrant incenses, wish-fulfilling trees, and trees made of jewels,

body.text: sarāṃsi cāmbhoruhabhūṣaṇāni haṃsasvanātyantamanoharāṇi // Bca_2.4 //
body.translated_text: and lakes adorned with lotuses, supremely enchanting with the cries of swans — // Bca_2.4 //

body.text: mahīdharāḥ parvatāḥ / ratnamayā ratnasvabhāvāḥ / vivekaramyā iti vivekoparamyā manoharāḥ / vivekānukūlā iti yāvat / supuṣpābharaṇojjvalāśceti śobhanapuṣpāṇyevābharaṇāni maṇḍanāni tairujjvalā atibhrājiṣṇavaḥ / satphalanamraśākhā iti santi ca śobhanāni varṇagandharasasaṃpannāni tāni phalāni ceti tairnamrā avanatā bhūmilagnā iva śākhā yeṣāṃ te kalpadrumāḥ kalpavṛkṣāḥ / ambhoruhabhūṣaṇāni padmānyeva bhūṣaṇāni yeṣāṃ tāni tathā / haṃsasvanātyantamanoharāṇi haṃsānāṃ svanai rūtairatyantamanoharāṇi ramaṇīyāni tāni tathā //
body.translated_text: 'Mountains' (<s>mahīdharāḥ</s>) means mountains. 'Made of jewels' means whose nature is that of jewels. 'Delightful in solitude' (<s>vivekaramyā</s>) means beautiful, charming by virtue of solitude — that is, conducive to solitude. 'Ablaze with ornaments of beautiful flowers' — the beautiful flowers themselves are the ornaments, the adornments; ablaze, that is, exceedingly radiant, with them. 'With branches bowed by excellent fruits' — there exist beautiful fruits, endowed with color, fragrance, and taste, and by those fruits the branches are bowed, bent down, as if touching the ground — these are wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpadruma</s>), wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>). 'Adorned with lotuses' — lotuses themselves are the adornments of those [lakes]; thus [they are described]. 'Exceedingly charming with the sounds of geese' — exceedingly charming, delightful, with the sounds, the calls, of geese; thus [they are described].

children.translated_text: 'And crops that grow unsown, and other adornments worthy of worship,
extending to the limits of the expanse of the space-element — all these too are without ownership.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.5 //

body.text: akṛṣṭānyeva halavilekhanamantareṇaiva jātāni prādurbhūtāni / śasyajātāni vrīhiviśeṣāḥ / anyāni vā pūjyavibhūṣaṇāni pūjyānāmārādhyānāṃ vibhūṣaṇāni śobhākarāṇi / anyāni aparāṇi ākāśadhātuprasarāvadhīni ākāśadhātoḥ prasaro 'vakāśaḥ vistāro vā, tāvadavadhīni tatparyantāni / sarvāṇyapīmāni uktāni uktasadṛśāni aparigrahāṇi amamāni na kenacit svīkṛtānītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Unsown' means arisen, appeared, without even the plowing of the soil. 'Crops' means varieties of rice. 'Other adornments worthy of worship' means things that are embellishments, beautifiers, of those worthy of worship, those to be honored. 'Others' means yet others. 'Extending to the limits of the expanse of the space-element' — the expanse (<s>prasara</s>) of the space-element is its extent or breadth; [things] having that as their limit, bounded by that. 'All these too' — all these mentioned, and those similar to what has been mentioned — 'without ownership' — without 'mine-ness,' not claimed by anyone — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: 'Taking these with my mind, I offer them to the bulls among sages, together with their sons;

children.text: gṛhṇantu tanme varadakṣiṇīyā mahākṛpā māmanukampamānāḥ // Bca_2.6 //
children.translated_text: may the supreme worthy ones, of great compassion, accept these from me, having mercy on me.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.6 //

body.text: ādāya buddhayā gṛhītvā manovijñānena / munipuṃgavebhyo munivṛṣabhebhyo niryātayāmi prayacchāmi / saputrakebhyaḥ sabodhisattvagaṇebhyaḥ / gṛhṇantu tanme svīkurvantu tadetat sarvaṃ mama pūjopahāravastu / varadakṣiṇīyā anuttaradakṣiṇāpātrāṇi buddhabodhisattvāḥ / mahākṛpāḥ sarvasattvahitasukhavidhānaikamanasaḥ / māṃ dīnaduḥkhitasattvamanukampamānāḥ karuṇāyamānāḥ / mamānugrahāyeti yāvat //
body.translated_text: 'Taking with the mind' (<s>buddhyā</s>) means having grasped with the mind-consciousness. 'To the bulls among sages' means to the foremost among sages. 'I offer' means I present. 'Together with their sons' means together with the assemblies of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. 'May they accept this from me' — may they take possession of all this, my offering-gift. 'The supreme worthy ones' — the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who are supreme vessels for offerings. 'Of great compassion' — whose minds are single-pointedly devoted to providing welfare and happiness for all beings. 'Having mercy on me' — showing compassion toward me, a miserable, suffering being. The meaning extends to: for my benefit.

body.text: syādetat- kiṃ punarevaṃ manomayapūjāmātraṃ vidhīyate yāvatā tattadvastu manoharaṃ sākṣādeva kasmānnopanīyate ityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: One might think: 'But why is merely a mind-made worship prescribed here? Why are such-and-such charming objects not actually brought and offered?' Anticipating this objection, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

body.text: apuṇyavānasmi mahādaridraḥ pūjārthamanyanmama nāsti kiṃcit /
body.translated_text: 'I am without merit, extremely poor; I have nothing else for the purpose of worship.

body.text: ato mamārthāya parārthacittā gṛhṇantu nāthā idamātmaśaktyā // Bca_2.7 //
body.translated_text: Therefore, for my sake, may the Protectors, whose minds are devoted to the welfare of others, accept this through their own power.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.7 //

body.text: akṛtapuṇyo 'smi, ata eva mahādaridraḥ / puṇye sarvopakaraṇasaṃpattibhirbhavati / tadabhāvāt pūjārthamanyadupakaraṇaṃ mama nāsti kiṃcit / ato mamārthāya mama puṇyakāmatayā bhagavantaśca parārthacittāḥ parahitasukhābhilāṣiṇo mahākāruṇikatvāt / ato gṛhṇantu nāthā idamuktaṃ pūjopakaraṇaṃ mayā niryātitam / ātmaśaktyeti svasāmarthyena //
body.translated_text: 'I am without accumulated merit, and therefore I am extremely poor.' Through merit, one possesses all requisites and prosperities; because of its absence, 'I have nothing else' — no other requisite — 'for the purpose of worship.' 'Therefore, for my sake' — because of my desire for merit — 'and the Blessed Ones are those whose minds are devoted to the welfare of others' — who desire the benefit and happiness of others, because of their great compassion. 'Therefore, may the Protectors accept this' — this offering-requisite presented by me. 'Through their own power' — by their own capacity.

body.text: ayaṃ punarātmabhāvo mamāyatto 'sti / taṃ niryātayāmītyāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover: 'This person, this self, is at my disposal — I offer that.' He says:

children.text: dadāmi cātmānamahaṃ jinebhyaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ ca tadātmajebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I give myself entirely to the Conquerors, and entirely to their sons;

children.text: parigrahaṃ me kurutāgrasattvā yuṣmāsu dāsatvamupaimi bhaktyā // Bca_2.8 //
children.translated_text: accept me, O supreme beings! With devotion I submit to servitude to you.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.8 //

body.text: ātmānaṃ ca prayacchāmi jinebhyaḥ / sarveṇa sarvaṃ ca sarvaprakāreṇa / ātmasvīkāraṃ parityajya tadātmajebhyo 'pi / māṃ pratigṛhṇīta naravṛṣabhāḥ / yuṣmāsu dāsatvaṃ dāsabhāvaṃ svīkaromi / na jīvikādilobhāt, api tu bhaktyā paramagauraveṇa / śraddhāvilena cetasetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'And I give myself' — and I offer my own self — 'to the Conquerors.' 'Entirely' (<s>sarveṇa sarvaṃ</s>) — in every way. Having relinquished self-ownership, [I give myself] 'to their sons also' — to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as well. 'Accept me, O bulls among men!' 'I submit to servitude to you' — I accept the state of being a servant. Not from greed for livelihood and such, but rather 'with devotion' — with supreme reverence. The meaning is: with a mind steeped in faith.

body.text: nanu kaḥ punaratra guṇo 'stītyāha-
body.translated_text: 'But what benefit is there in this?' he says:

children.translated_text: 'By your acceptance of me, I become fearless in existence and work for the benefit of beings;

children.text: pūrvaṃ ca pāpaṃ samatikramāmi nānyacca pāpaṃ prakaromi bhūyaḥ // Bca_2.9 //
children.translated_text: I transcend my former sin and commit no further sin hereafter.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.9 //

body.text: bhavatkṛtena yuṣmadīyena mahadāśrayeṇa vigatabhayaḥ saṃsāre lokānāṃ hitamarthaṃ saṃpādayāmi / mahadāśraye 'pi nākuśalakarmāvṛtasya svahitakaraṇe 'pi sāmarthyamastītyāha- pūrvaṃ cetyādi / pūrvamaparijñānāt kṛtamakuśalakarma samatikramāmi, vidūṣaṇāsamudācārādibhirnirharāmi / samatikrāmatītyukte samatikramāmītyuktaṃ śābdavyavahāreṣvanādarāt, arthapratiśaraṇatādhātupradhānatvācca / aparaṃ ca pāpaṃ na punaḥ karomi / āyatyāṃ punarakaraṇasaṃvaraṃ vidadhe //
body.translated_text: 'By your acceptance' means: by the great refuge that is yours; 'fearless' — free from fear — 'in <s>saṃsāra</s>, I accomplish the benefit, the welfare, of beings.' [But] even with a great refuge, one who is enveloped by unwholesome <s>karma</s> has no capacity even for accomplishing one's own benefit — [to address this] he says 'And the former' etc. 'The former' — previously, through ignorance — unwholesome <s>karma</s> that was committed, 'I transcend' — I remove through confession and practices of remorse and the like. Though 'samatikrāmati' [third person] is expected, 'samatikramāmi' [first person] is used because of disregard for [strict] grammatical usage, and because of the primacy of taking refuge in meaning over verbal roots. 'And I commit no further sin hereafter' — for the future I undertake the restraint of non-repetition.

body.text: iti sarvamātmaniryātanāprabhṛtipūjopahāraṃ niryātya punarviśeṣeṇa pūjāṃ vidhātumāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus offered the entire offering-gift beginning with the offering of self, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says, wishing to perform worship in a special way:

children.translated_text: 'In those bathing houses — charming with pillars ablaze with jewels,
with canopies radiant with pearls,

body.text: ratnairindranīlādibhirujjvalāḥ prabhāsvarā ye stambhāḥ tairmanoharāḥ kamanīyāḥ / teṣu snānagṛheṣu snānaṃ karomīti yojyam / punaḥ kiṃbhūteṣu? muktāmayā mauktikaracanākhacitā udbhāsinaḥ udbhāsvarāḥ vitānā iva vitānakāḥ yeṣu te tathā, teṣu / svacchāḥ sunirmalāḥ , ujjvalā dīptimantaḥ, sphaṭikasyeme sphāṭikāḥ, kuṭṭimāḥ bhūmiracanāviśeṣā yeṣu, teṣu / sugandhiṣu kṛṣṇāgurucandanādidhūpitavāsiteṣu / snānāya gṛhāḥ teṣu //
body.translated_text: 'ablaze' means resplendent with jewels such as sapphires and the like — the pillars are thus; 'charming' means beautiful, lovely — in such bathing houses, 'I bathe' — this should be construed. Furthermore, of what kind? 'With canopies radiant with pearls' — made of pearls, studded with pearl settings, 'radiant' means resplendent — the canopies are like that; in those [having such canopies]. 'Clear' means very spotless; 'brilliant' means lustrous; 'of crystal' — these belong to crystal, hence 'crystalline'; 'floors' — particular kinds of floor-paving — in those [having such floors]. 'Fragrant' — perfumed with the incense of black aloe, sandalwood, and the like. Houses for bathing — in those.

children.translated_text: 'With numerous great jewel-bedecked vessels filled with pleasantly fragrant water and flowers —

children.text: snānaṃ karomyeṣa tathāgatānāṃ tadātmajānāṃ ca sagītivādyam // Bca_2.11 //
children.translated_text: I bathe the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and their sons, accompanied by songs and music.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.11 //

body.text: udakaṃ ca puṣpāṇi ca manojñagandhāni ca tāni / taiḥ pūrṇāḥ kumbhā ghaṭāḥ, taiḥ / mahāratnamayaiḥ mahānti vaidūryā(dī)ni ca ratnāni ca tāni, tatsvabhāvaiḥ / anekaiḥ śatasahasrakoṭibhiḥ / sagītavādyaṃ saha manoharagītanṛttamurajādivādyaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Water, flowers, and pleasant fragrances — with those. Filled vessels, pots — with those. Made of great jewels — great [gems] such as <s>vaidūrya</s> and the like, and jewels — of that nature. 'Numerous' means hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s>. 'With songs and music' means together with charming songs, dances, and music of drums (<s>muraja</s>) and the like.

children.translated_text: 'With cloths that are perfumed, washed clean, incomparable, I dry their bodies;

children.text: tataḥ suraktāni sudhūpitāni dadāmi tebhyo varacīvarāṇi // Bca_2.12 //
children.translated_text: then I give those [<s>Buddhas</s>] well-dyed, well-perfumed, excellent robes.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.12 //

body.text: pradhūpitairaguruprabhṛtidhūpaiḥ / dhautamalaiḥ prakṣālitakalmaṣaiḥ / nirmalairityarthaḥ / atulyairapratisamaiḥ / vastrairdukūlaiḥ / teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ tadātmajānāṃ ca / tanuṃ śarīram / unmṛṣāmi saṃmārjayāmi / tatastasmādunmarṣaṇānantaram / suraktāni śobhanarāgaiḥ suṣṭhu vā raktāni / śobhanadhūpena dhūpitāni / dadāmi tebhyo jinebhyaḥ / varacīvarāṇi anuttarāṇyācchādanāni //
body.translated_text: 'Perfumed' — with incense of aloe and the like. 'Washed clean' — whose stains have been washed away. 'Spotless' — this is the meaning. 'Incomparable' — without equal. 'Cloths' — fine fabrics. 'Of those' — of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and their sons. 'The body' — the physical form. 'I dry' — I wipe. 'Then' — immediately after the drying. 'Well-dyed' — with beautiful dyes, well-colored. 'Perfumed with fine incense.' 'I give to them' — to the Conquerors. 'Excellent robes' — unsurpassed garments.

children.translated_text: 'With divine, soft, fine, variously beautiful garments, and with various choice ornaments,
I adorn <s>Samantabhadra</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, <s>Lokeśvara</s>, and the others too.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.13 //

body.text: divyairdivibhavairdevārhaiḥ / mṛdūni ca sukumārasparśāni, ślakṣṇāni ca sūkśmāṇi / vicitrā nānāvarṇakṛtā śobhā yeṣāṃ tairvastraiḥ / alaṃkāravaraiśca vibhūṣaṇapradhānaiḥ / taistairiti mukuṭakaṭakakeyūrahāranūpurādibhiḥ / samantabhadrājitamañjughoṣalokeśvarādīnapi bodhisattvān maṇḍayāmi alaṃkaromi //
body.translated_text: 'Divine' — heavenly, fit for gods. 'Soft' means delicate to the touch; 'fine' means subtle. 'Variously beautiful' — those whose beauty is made of many colors — with such garments. 'Choice ornaments' means foremost among adornments. 'Various' — meaning crowns, bracelets, armlets, necklaces, anklets, and the like. 'I adorn' — I ornament — '<s>Samantabhadra</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, <s>Lokeśvara</s>, and the other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> too.'

children.translated_text: 'With the finest fragrances whose scent pervades the entire trichiliocosm, I anoint them —
all the bodies of the Lords of Sages, blazing with the luster of well-smelted, well-polished, well-refined gold.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.14 //

body.text: sahasraṃ caturdvīpikānāṃ tathā candrasūryamerūṇāṃ pratyekaṃ kāmadevānāṃ brahmalokānāṃ ca / sāhasraścūliko mataḥ / sa eva sahasraguṇite dvisāhasra / tatsahasraṃ trisāhasraḥ / śatakoṭiḥ cāturdvīpikānāmityarthaḥ / evaṃ sarvāsu dikṣu lokadhāturananto 'paryantaśca / sarvatrisāhastrāṇi / visartuṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathā / tathāvidhā gandhāḥ parimalā yeṣāṃ te tathā / tairgandhottamairyakṣakardamaharicandanādibhiḥ / tān munīndrakāyānanulepayāmi samālabhe / kiṃbhūtān? sūttaptaṃ puṭapākādinā pariśodhitāntarmalam / sūnmṛṣṭaṃ roṣāṇādimaṇisaṃmārjitam / sudhautaṃ kṣārāmlalavaṇādiprakṣālitabahirmalam / tathābhūtaṃ ca taddhema ceti / tasya prabhā, dyutirityarthaḥ / tadvadujjvalān dyutimataḥ / etacca yathālokaprasiddhitaḥ kathitam / na tu tathāgatakāyaśobhāyā laukikaṃ kiṃcidupamānamasti //
body.translated_text: 'A thousand' refers to [a thousand] four-continent [world-systems], and likewise of suns, moons, <s>Merus</s>, desire-realm gods, and <s>Brahmā</s>-worlds individually. 'A first-thousand is considered' [a <s>sāhasracūlika</s>]. That same, multiplied by a thousand, is the two-thousand [<s>dvisāhasra</s>]. A thousand of that is the three-thousand [<s>trisāhasra</s>] — meaning a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of four-continent worlds. Thus in all directions the world-systems are infinite and boundless. 'Of the entire trichiliocosm' — those whose nature it is to spread throughout [are called <s>visārin</s>]. The fragrances, the perfumes, of that kind [are described] thus. 'With the finest fragrances' — such as <s>yakṣakardama</s>, <s>haricandana</s>, and the like. 'I anoint them' — I apply to — 'the bodies of the Lords of Sages.' Of what kind? '<s>Sūttapta</s>' — whose inner impurities have been purified through cupellation and the like. '<s>Sūnmṛṣṭa</s>' — polished with gems such as <s>roṣāṇā</s>. '<s>Sudhautam</s>' — whose outer impurities have been washed away with alkaline solutions, acids, salt, and the like. Such gold — its luster, meaning radiance. Similarly blazing, meaning lustrous. This is spoken according to worldly convention. But no worldly thing is an [adequate] comparison for the beauty of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body.

children.translated_text: Now he introduces the worship with garlands:
'With <s>māndārava</s> flowers, blue lotuses, jasmine, and all other pleasant and fragrant blossoms,
I worship the Lords of Sages, the most worthy of worship, and with garlands of beautiful arrangement.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.15 //

body.text: māndāravaṃ deveṣu puṣpaviśeṣaḥ / indīvaramutpalam / mallikā vārṣikī / etatpramukhaiḥ sarvaiḥ śobhanagandhaiḥ puṣpairmanohāribhiḥ pūjyatamān munīndrān pūjayāmi / stragbhiśca mālābhiśca grathanaracanāviśeṣakamanīyābhiḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Māndārava</s>' is a particular flower among the gods. '<s>Indīvara</s>' is the blue lotus. '<s>Mallikā</s>' is the <s>vārṣikī</s> (jasmine). With these foremost [among flowers], with all blossoms of fine fragrance, charming — 'I worship the Lords of Sages, the most worthy of worship.' 'And with garlands' — with chaplets beautiful in their stringing and arrangement.

body.text: dhūpapūjāmāha-
body.translated_text: He speaks of worship with incense:

body.text: sphītasphuradgandhamanoramaiśca tān dhūpameghairupadhūpayāmi /
body.translated_text: 'And with clouds of incense — rich, effusing, and of delightful fragrance — I perfume them.'

body.text: sphītā māṃsalāḥ / sphurantaśca digantavyāpinaḥ bahulagandhodgāriṇo vā / tādṛśā gandhā yeṣāṃ dhūpameghānāṃ te tathā, taiḥ / dhūpā meghā iva ambaratalāvalambibimbāḥ / upamitaṃ vyāghrādibhiḥ iti samāsaḥ / dhūpānāṃ vā meghāḥ, taiḥ, meghavadudgacchadbhirityarthaḥ / tāniti munīndrān upadhūpayāmi //
body.translated_text: 'Rich' (<s>sphīta</s>) means full-bodied. 'Effusing' means pervading the horizons, or copiously emitting fragrance. The incense-clouds have fragrances of that kind; with those. 'Incense-clouds' — clouds of incense, hanging like masses in the vault of the sky. [This is] a compound like 'compared with tigers and the like.' Or: clouds, that is, masses, of incense; with those — meaning: rising up like clouds — this is the meaning. 'I perfume them' — the Lords of Sages.

body.text: naivedyapūjāmāha-
body.translated_text: He speaks of the worship with food-offerings:

body.text: bhojyaiśca khādyairvividhaiśca peyaistebhyo nivedyaṃ ca nivedayāmi // Bca_2.16 //
body.translated_text: 'With various foods to eat, to chew, and to drink, I present the offering to them.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.16 //

body.text: bhojyaṃ yanmukhamāpūrya bhujyate / khādyaṃ yat kavalaśaḥ / chedyaṃ dhṛtapūrādi / peyaṃ yat pīyate eva pānakādi / ebhirvividhairnānāprakāropasaṃskṛtaiḥ / tebhyo munīndrebhyo nivedyaṃ ca nivedayāmi //
body.translated_text: 'Food' (<s>bhojya</s>) is that which is eaten by filling the mouth. 'To chew' (<s>khādya</s>) is that [eaten] morsel by morsel — things to cut, such as sweets filled with ghee and the like. 'To drink' (<s>peya</s>) is that which is simply drunk — beverages and the like. 'Various' means prepared with many kinds of seasoning. 'To them' — to the Lords of Sages — 'I present the offering.'

body.text: dīpapūjāmāha-
body.translated_text: He speaks of the worship with lamps:

body.text: ratnapradīpāṃśca nivedayāmi suvarṇapadmeṣu niviṣṭapaṅktin /
body.translated_text: 'And I offer lamps of jewels, with rows set upon golden lotuses;

body.text: gandhopalipteṣu ca kuṭṭimeṣu kirāmi puṣpaprakarān manojñān // Bca_2.17 //
body.translated_text: and on floors anointed with fragrance, I scatter delightful heaps of flowers.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.17 //

body.text: ratnamayāḥ pradīpāḥ tān / niviṣṭā paṅktirmālā yeṣāṃ te tathā / kveti? suvarṇapadmeṣu / sāpekṣatve 'pi gamakatvāt samāsaḥ / gandhopalipteṣu candanakuṅkumādigandhaiścarciteṣu //
body.translated_text: 'Made of jewels' — the lamps are thus. 'With set rows' means those in which rows, garlands [of lamps], are arranged. Where? 'Upon golden lotuses.' Though [the compound is] dependent, it is [still valid] because it conveys the meaning. 'Anointed with fragrance' means anointed, smeared, with the fragrances of sandalwood, saffron, and the like.

children.translated_text: 'Those [palaces] adorned at the entrances of the directions, radiant with the beauty of pendant strings of pearls and gems —
those cloud-like palaces, delightful with songs of praise, I offer to those who are made of loving-kindness.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.18 //

body.text: pralambairmuktāmaṇihāraiḥ śobhā yeṣāṃ tān vimānameghān vimānasamūhān ālokakāriṇaḥ sarvadikūśobhākarān //
body.translated_text: 'With pendant strings of pearls and gems,' whose beauty is [enhanced by them] — 'cloud-like palaces,' meaning assemblages of palaces — light-making, beautifying all the directions.

children.translated_text: 'With golden handles, of beautiful form, strung with pearls, raised aloft —
I hold up jeweled parasols, supremely beautiful, for these great sages.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.19 //

body.text: kanakamayadaṇḍaiḥ kāntimatsaṃsthānaiḥ / muktākhacitāni ratnamayāni chatrāṇi / samucchritānīti uddaṇḍitāni //
body.translated_text: 'With handles made of gold, of beautiful shape. 'Studded with pearls' — jeweled parasols. 'Raised aloft' means held up high on their handles.

body.text: idānīṃ pūjopahāramupasaṃharannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, summarizing the offering-gift, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.translated_text: Henceforth, may delightful clouds of worship be established,
and clouds of music and concerts that delight all beings. // Bca_2.20 //

body.text: itaḥ prabhṛti ete pūjāmeghā mayā niryātitāḥ, anye vā devādibhirupanītāḥ kalpaṃ vā kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā pratiṣṭhantām prakarṣavṛttisthitā bhavantu / tūryasaṃgītimeghāśca tūryāṇi murajādivādyāni / saṃgītayaḥ sametya gītayaḥ / samudāyagītānītyarthaḥ / athavā / saṃgītakāni nuttagītavāditāni samuditānyucyante / teṣāṃ meghāḥ anekasamudāyāḥ / te ca sarvasattvapraharṣaṇāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ pramodakāriṇaḥ, na punaraśakyaśravaṇāḥ / pratiṣṭhantāmiti saṃbandhaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'From this point on,' may these clouds of worship that I have offered, or that have been presented by gods and others, 'be established' — may they abide in a state of excellence — for a <s>kalpa</s> or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>. 'And clouds of music and concerts' — 'music' (<s>tūrya</s>) means instruments such as drums; 'concerts' (<s>saṃgīti</s>) means singing together — meaning collective songs. Or alternatively, performances of dance, song, and instrumental music together are called <s>saṃgītaka</s>. Their 'clouds' means their numerous assemblies. And they are 'delighting all beings' — causing the joy of all beings, not unlistenable. 'May they be established' is the syntactical connection.

body.text: sāmānyenābhisaṃkṣipya saddharmādiṣu pūjāmāha-
body.translated_text: Summarizing worship of the true <s>Dharma</s> and so forth in general, he says —

children.translated_text: Upon all the jewels of the true <s>Dharma</s>, upon <s>caityas</s>, and upon images,
may showers of flowers, jewels, and the like rain down continuously. // Bca_2.21 //

body.text: dvādaśāṅgapravacanātmakeṣu sarvasaddharmaratneṣu / ratnamiva ratnaṃ vastutattvālokakāritvāt, paramanirvṛtihetutvācca / stūpeṣu bhagavaccaityeṣu / pratimāsu ceti buddhabodhisattvavigrahapratikṛtiṣu / puṣpavṛṣṭayo ratnavṛṣṭayaśca / ādiśabdāccandanacūrṇavastrādivarṣāḥ / nirantaramiti āsaṃsāramanavacchinnam //
body.translated_text: 'Upon all the jewels of the true <s>Dharma</s>' — whose nature is the twelvefold word of the <s>Buddha</s>. A jewel like a jewel — because it illuminates the true nature of things and because it is the cause of supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Upon <s>caityas</s>' — the <s>stūpas</s> of the Blessed One. 'And upon images' — replicas of the physical forms of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Showers of flowers and showers of jewels. Through the word 'and so forth,' showers of sandalwood powder, garments, and the like. 'Continuously' means uninterrupted throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: anuttarapūjāmatidiśannāha-
body.translated_text: Dedicating the supreme worship, he says —

children.translated_text: Just as <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> and others worship the <s>Jinas</s>,
so too I worship the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the Protectors, together with their sons. // Bca_2.22 //

body.text: mañjughoṣasamantabhadrājitalokanāthapramukhā daśabhūmīśvarā bodhisattvāḥ yathā yena adhyāśayena tathāgatān pūjayanti, tathā tena adhimokṣeṇa ahamapi tathāgatān saha putraiḥ bodhisattvagaṇaiḥ pūjayāmi //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are lords of the ten stages, led by <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, and <s>Ajitalokanātha</s> — in whatever manner, with whatever aspiration they worship the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, so too, with that same resolve, I also worship the <s>Tathāgatas</s> together with their sons, the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: stutipūjāmāha-
body.translated_text: He states the worship of praise —

children.translated_text: With hymns that are oceans of musical tones, I too praise those oceans of qualities;
and may clouds of songs of praise arise for them, without fail. // Bca_2.23 //

body.text: svarāḥ sapta gāndhārādayaḥ / teṣāmaṅgāni prabhedāḥ kāmodādayaḥ / teṣāṃ sāgaravadatibāhulyāt sāgarāḥ, taiḥ stotraiḥ / stutaya eva saṃgītayaḥ, stutīnāṃ vā saṃgītayaḥ samudāyāḥ / tāsāṃ meghāḥ saṃbhavantu upatiṣṭhantām / eṣu buddhabodhisattveṣu / ananyathā aviparītā yathā mayopakalpitāstathaivetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The 'notes' (<s>svara</s>) are the seven — <s>Gāndhāra</s> and the rest. Their 'limbs' are their subdivisions — <s>Kāmoda</s> and the rest. Their 'oceans' — because of their extreme abundance, like oceans — with such hymns. 'Songs of praise' — praises that are concerts, or concerts of praises — their assemblies. Their 'clouds' — may they 'arise,' be established. 'For them' — for these <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. 'Without fail' — not otherwise than as I have imagined — that is the meaning.

body.text: buddhadharmasaṃgharatneṣu praṇāmapūjāmāha-
body.translated_text: He states the worship of prostration to the jewels of <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> —

children.translated_text: With prostrations equal in number to the atoms of all fields, I bow
to all <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times, together with the <s>Dharma</s> and the supreme assembly. // Bca_2.24 //

body.text: yāvanti daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetrāṇi, teṣu yāvanto 'ṇavaḥ, tatsaṃkhyaiḥ praṇāmaiḥ / sarvatryadhvagatāniti atītapratyutpannānāgatān tathāgatān / kiṃbhūtān? sahadharmagaṇottamān gaṇānāmuttamo 'grabhūto bodhisattvagaṇaḥ / dharmaśca gaṇottamaśca tābhyāṃ saha //
body.translated_text: As many <s>Buddha</s>-fields as there are in the ten directions, and as many atoms as there are in them — with prostrations equal to that number. 'Of all three times' — past, present, and future <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Of what sort? 'Together with the <s>Dharma</s> and the supreme assembly' — the supreme among assemblies, the foremost, is the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> and the supreme assembly — together with those two.

body.text: tathāgatastūpeṣu praṇāmamāha-
body.translated_text: He states prostration at the <s>stūpas</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> —

children.translated_text: I venerate all <s>caityas</s>, and likewise the abodes of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;
I make homage to preceptors and likewise to venerable ascetics worthy of reverence. // Bca_2.25 //

body.text: ūrdhvatiryagadhastanāsu diśāsu vidiśāsu ca / saśarīrāśarīreṣu stūpeṣu praṇamāmyahamityarthaḥ / bodhisattvāśrayānapīti jātakāvadānajanmādisthānāni / abhivandyāniti vṛddhān vandanārhān / tadanena pūjāvandanāvidhiruktaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the directions above, across, and below, and in the intermediate directions — to <s>stūpas</s> both with relics and without relics — 'I bow': this is the meaning. 'And the abodes of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' — the places of <s>Jātakas</s>, <s>Avadānas</s>, births, and the like. 'Worthy of reverence' — the elders, those deserving of veneration. By this, the method of worship and veneration has been stated.

body.text: ayaṃ ca pūjāvidhistrisamayarāje kathitaḥ / yathoktam- sthalajā ratnaparvatāḥ / jalajā ratnaparvatāḥ / sthalajajalajāni ratnāni daśadigavasthitāni / amamānyaparigrahāṇi / deyānītyuktam / anayā ca diśā sarvabhaiṣajyāni sarvarasāyanāni sarvasalilāni / anavadyāni āmaṇḍalāni (?) sarvakāñcanamaṇḍalāni / vivṛtteṣu vā lokadhātuṣu paramarasasparśasaṃpannā bhūparpaṭakā amṛtalatā / akṛṣṭoptāḥ śālayaḥ / sarvottarakurudvīpeṣu ca pariśuddheṣu ca lokadhātuṣu ye ramaṇīyāḥ paribhogāḥ /
body.translated_text: And this method of worship is described in the <s>Trisamayarāja</s>. As stated: 'Land-born jewel-mountains. Water-born jewel-mountains. Land-born and water-born jewels situated in the ten directions — ownerless, unpossessed — are to be given.' And in this manner, all medicines, all elixirs, all waters; unblemished complete (?) golden discs; or in open world-realms, bark-sheets of earth endowed with the touch of supreme essence, immortal creepers; unharvested <s>śāli</s> rice; and in all <s>Uttarakuru</s> continents and in purified world-realms, whatever delightful objects of enjoyment [there are].

body.text: yathā āryaratnameghe cāha-
body.translated_text: As also stated in the <s>Āryaratnamegha</s> —

body.text: sa yānīmāni sūtrānteṣu udārāṇi pūjopasthānāni śṛṇoti, tānyāśayatastīvreṇādhyāśayena
body.translated_text: 'Whatever grand modes of worship and attendance he hears of in the <s>sūtras</s>, those he dedicates with aspiration, with intense resolution

body.text: buddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ pariṇāmayati / tathā sa vividhāni pūjopasthānānyanuvicintayati iti //
body.translated_text: to the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Thus he contemplates various modes of worship and attendance.'

body.text: sāṃprataṃ ratnatrayaśaraṇagamanapūrvakaṃ pāpadeśanāmāha-
body.translated_text: Now he states the confession of evil preceded by going for refuge to the Three Jewels —

children.translated_text: I go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s> until the seat of awakening;

children.text: dharmaṃ gacchāmi śaraṇaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ tathā // Bca_2.26 //
children.translated_text: I go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s>, and likewise to the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // Bca_2.26 //

body.text: trāṇārthaṃ śaraṇārtham / gamanaṃ tadājñāparipālanam / yo hi yaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati, sa tadājñāṃ nātikramatīti bhāvaḥ / bodhimaṇḍata iti / maṇḍaśabdo 'yaṃ sāravacanam, ghṛtamaṇḍa iti yathā / tathā ca sati bodhipradhānaṃ yāvat / yāvat samyaksaṃbodhiṃ nādhigacchāmi ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'For the purpose of protection' — for the purpose of refuge. 'Going' is the observance of his commands. For he who goes for refuge to someone does not transgress that one's command — this is the sense. 'Until the seat of awakening' — the word <s>maṇḍa</s> here means 'essence,' as in '<s>ghṛtamaṇḍa</s>' (the essence of ghee). This being so, it means 'until the supreme [essence] of awakening' — meaning: until I attain perfect awakening.

children.translated_text: I make known to the Perfectly Awakened Ones established in all directions,
and to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great compassion, with palms joined — // Bca_2.27 //
