body.text: vijñāpayāmītyanena buddhabodhisattvānāmagragatamātmānaṃ dhyātvā adhyāśayenaitadvaktavyamityupadarśitam / kṛtāñjaliriti kāyavijñaptiruktā / añjaliḥ karadvayena saṃpuṭaṃ kṛtvetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: By 'I make known,' it is shown that one should meditate upon oneself as being in the presence of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and should state this with aspiration. 'With palms joined' expresses bodily expression. '<s>Añjali</s>' means having formed a cupped [gesture] with both hands.

children.translated_text: In beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, in this birth or in others,

children.text: yanmayā paśunā pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ kāritameva vā // Bca_2.28 //
children.translated_text: whatever evil has been done by me, a fool, or caused to be done, // Bca_2.28 //
and whatever has been rejoiced at, to my own destruction, out of delusion —
that transgression I confess, tormented by remorse. // Bca_2.29 //

body.text: anādimatīti pūrvajanmaparaṃparāsu / janmanyatraiveti asminnapi janmani, na kevalaṃ pūrvatra / paśuneti mohabahulatāmātmano darśayati / trividhaṃ karma kāyavāṅmanobhistatra kṛtam / tribhirapi kāritamiti / vāṅmanobhyāmanumoditamityapi / ātmaghātāyeti tatpāpakarmaphalasya mama ātmanyeva vipākāt / tadatyayamiti tadāpattim / deśayāmi prakāśayāmi uttānīkaromi, na pracchādayāmi / paścāttāpeneti akuśalakarmaṇo narakādau duḥkhavipākaśravaṇāt //
body.translated_text: 'In beginningless' — in the succession of former births. 'In this birth' — in this present life too, not only formerly. 'A fool' — shows his own prevalence of delusion. The threefold <s>karma</s> of body, speech, and mind — therein, 'done' [by oneself]. 'Caused to be done' — through all three [doors of body, speech, and mind]. 'Rejoiced at' — through speech and mind. 'To my own destruction' — because the fruit of that evil <s>karma</s> matures upon my own self. 'That transgression' — that offense. 'I confess' — I reveal, I make manifest, I do not conceal. 'By remorse' — from hearing of the painful maturation of unwholesome <s>karma</s> in hell and elsewhere.

body.text: adhunā yathāpradhānamatyayadeśanāmāha-
body.translated_text: Now he states the confession of transgressions in order of priority —

children.translated_text: Whatever offense has been committed by me against the Three Jewels, or against mother and father,

children.text: guruṣvanyeṣu vā kṣepāt kāyavāgbuddhibhiḥ kṛtaḥ // Bca_2.30 //
children.translated_text: or against teachers and others, through contempt, by body, speech, and mind — // Bca_2.30 //

body.text: ratnatraye iti anuttaraguṇakṣetre / mātetyādinā upakārikṣetre / tatrāpakārasya vistaratīvraduḥkhavipākatvāt //
body.translated_text: 'Against the Three Jewels' — in this unsurpassed field of qualities. 'Against mother' etc. — in the field of benefactors. Because offenses against these [fields] have extensively intense painful maturation.

children.translated_text: Whatever terrible evil has been done by me, a sinner defiled with many faults —

children.text: yatkṛtaṃ dāruṇaṃ pāpaṃ tatsarvaṃ deśayāmyaham // Bca_2.31 //
children.translated_text: all of that I confess, O Guides! // Bca_2.31 //

body.text: anekadoṣaduṣṭeneti rāgādikleśadūṣitena, na svatantreṇetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Defiled with many faults' — polluted by the defilements of passion and the rest — meaning: not acting freely.

children.translated_text: How shall I escape from this? I am always anxious, O Guides!

children.text: mā bhūnme mṛtyuracirād akṣīṇe pāpasaṃcaye // Bca_2.32 //
children.translated_text: May death not come to me while my heap of evil is unexhausted! // Bca_2.32 //

body.text: pāpakarmaṇi saṃvegamāha-
body.translated_text: He expresses alarm at evil <s>karma</s> —

body.text: kathaṃ ca niḥsarāmyasmāt paritrāyata satvaram /
body.translated_text: 'How shall I escape from this? Rescue me quickly!'

body.text: kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa / asmādaśubhāt / satvaraṃ śīghram / keyaṃ tvarā bhavata ityāha-
body.translated_text: 'How' — in what manner. 'From this' — from this evil. 'Quickly' — swiftly. 'What is this haste of yours?' he says —

body.text: mā mamākṣīṇapāpasya maraṇaṃ śīghrameṣyati // Bca_2.33 //
body.translated_text: May death not come swiftly to me while my evil is unexhausted! // Bca_2.33 //

body.text: yāvat pāpakṣayaṃ na karomi, tāvanmama mṛtyurbhaviṣyati na / anyathā durgati gamanabhayāt //
body.translated_text: As long as I have not brought about the exhaustion of evil, until then may death not come to me; otherwise, from fear of going to a lower rebirth.

body.text: nanu ca akṛtapāpaparikṣayasya bhavato mṛtyoḥ ko 'vakāśa ityāha-
body.translated_text: 'But what occasion has death for one like you who has not exhausted his evil?' he says —

children.translated_text: This death, which does not examine what is done and what is undone, is a treacherous killer;
not to be trusted by the healthy or the sick — a sudden great thunderbolt. // Bca_2.34 //

body.text: idaṃ kṛtamidamakṛtaṃ tāvaditi na parīkṣate mṛtyuḥ / viśrambho viśvāsaḥ / tena ghātakaḥ / nāpi nīrogo 'haṃ yuvā balavatkāyo veti viśvasanīyam / kutaḥ? ākasmikamahāśaniriti acintitavajrapātasadṛśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Death does not examine — 'this is done, this is undone, so wait.' 'Treacherous' (<s>viśrambha</s>) — trust; 'killer by means of trust' (<s>viśrambhaghātaka</s>). Nor is it to be trusted [thinking] 'I am healthy, young, of strong body.' Why? 'A sudden great thunderbolt' — resembling an unforeseen lightning-strike.

body.text: yadyevaṃ pāpād bhayam, kimarthaṃ tarhi tat kṛtamityāha-
body.translated_text: 'If there is fear of evil, then why was it committed?' he says —

children.translated_text: Evil has been committed in manifold ways on account of the loved and the unloved;
that all must be abandoned and one must go — this was not understood to be so. // Bca_2.35 //

body.text: priya ātmā ātmīyaśca, apriyastadapakārī / priyasya hitasukhamapriyasya ca tadviparītamicchatā kṛtaṃ pāpamanekadhā prāṇātipātādattādānādibhedenānekaprakāram / nanu sarvametannacireṇa parityajya gantavyam, tat kimiti nirarthakaṃ pāpakamupacīyate ityāha- sarvamityādi / sarvaṃ priyamapriyaṃ vā utsṛjya vihāya gantavyam / etattu na mayā mugdhena paribhāvitam //
body.translated_text: The 'loved' is oneself and what belongs to oneself; the 'unloved' is one who harms them. Desiring welfare and happiness for the loved, and the opposite for the unloved, evil has been committed in manifold ways — in many forms such as killing, stealing, and the rest. 'But surely all this must before long be abandoned and one must go — then why is pointless evil accumulated?' he says 'all must be abandoned' etc. All — whether loved or unloved — 'having abandoned,' leaving behind, 'one must go.' But this was not considered by me, the deluded one.

children.text: apriyā na bhaviṣyanti priyo me na bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: The unloved will not exist, and the loved will not exist for me;

children.text: ahaṃ ca na bhaviṣyāmi sarvaṃ ca na bhaviṣyati // Bca_2.36 //
children.translated_text: I too will not exist, and all will not exist. // Bca_2.36 //

body.text: kimidānīṃ pariśiṣṭamavasthitamityāha-
body.translated_text: 'What then remains established?' he says —

children.translated_text: Whatever objects are experienced — each and every one turns into a mere memory;
like something experienced in a dream, all has gone and is not seen again. // Bca_2.37 //

body.text: yadyadvastviti sukhaheturduḥkhaheturvā / anubhūyate saṃvedyate / kathaṃ punarevamityāhasvapnānubhūtavaditi / yathā svapnāvasthāyāmupalabdhaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ na punarīkṣyate, tatra smaraṇamātrameva avaśiṣyate //
body.translated_text: 'Whatever objects' — whether causes of happiness or causes of suffering — 'are experienced,' that is, felt. 'How is this so?' he says 'like something experienced in a dream' — just as what was perceived in the dream state, having perished, is not seen again; there, only a mere memory remains.

body.text: tathā anyadapi sarvaṃ priyādisaṃgatamasthiramasminneva janmanītyupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Further demonstrating that all else too — association with loved ones and the like — is impermanent in this very life, he says —

children.translated_text: Even while standing right here, many loved and unloved ones have passed away;

children.text: tannimittaṃ tu yatpāpaṃ tatsthitaṃ ghoramagrataḥ // Bca_2.38 //
children.translated_text: but the terrible evil committed on their account stands before me. // Bca_2.38 //

body.text: tiṣṭhataḥ āsīnasyaiva mama paśyataḥ / gatā anityatayā grasitāḥ / yadyevaṃ tarhi tadarthaṃ kṛtaṃ pāpamapi taiḥ saha yāsyatītyāha- tannimittamityādi / teṣāṃ priyādīnāṃ nimittaṃ tadarthaṃ yatkṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatpunaragrata eva sthitaṃ me / tanmayā saha yāsyatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'While standing right here' — while I myself am sitting, looking on. 'Have passed away' — devoured by impermanence. 'If so, then the evil committed for their sake should also depart with them,' he says 'on their account' etc. The evil committed 'on their account' — for the sake of those loved ones and the rest, as the occasion — 'that stands before me' again. It will go with me — that is the meaning.

body.text: nanvevaṃ paśyannapi kathaṃ mūrcchito 'sītyāha-
body.translated_text: 'But even while seeing thus, how are you dazed?' he says —

children.translated_text: 'I am a transient [visitor]' — this was not reflected upon by me;
through delusion, attachment, and hatred, evil was committed in manifold ways. // Bca_2.39 //

body.text: nāhaṃ kasyacit paritaḥ, na me kaścit, ityevaṃ na mayā pratyavekṣitaṃ vicāritam / tena kāraṇena / anunaya āsaṅgaḥ ātmani ātmīye ca / vidveṣaḥ pratighaḥ / tat pratikūlamācarati //
body.translated_text: 'I do not belong to anyone and no one belongs to me' — thus it was not reflected upon, not examined, by me. For that reason — attachment (<s>anunaya</s>) is clinging to oneself and what belongs to oneself; hatred (<s>vidveṣa</s>) is hostility — 'that one acts contrary to me.'

body.text: cirataramatidīrghāyuṣo bhavataḥ kā maraṇāśaṅkā? tat kimevaṃ bibheṣītyāha-
body.translated_text: 'For one of very long life like you, what fear of death? So why do you fear thus?' he says —

children.translated_text: Night and day, without rest, the expenditure of life increases;

children.text: āyasya cāgamo nāsti na mariṣyāmi kiṃ nvaham // Bca_2.40 //
children.translated_text: and there is no arrival of the [life-]stock — shall I indeed not die? // Bca_2.40 //

body.text: aharniśam / āyuṣo vardhate vyayaḥ, āyuḥsaṃskārāḥ kṣīyante / aviśrāmamiti kṣaṇamapi na vyayavicchittirasti / āgamanamāgamaḥ anupraveśaḥ / sa ca āyasya upacayasya leśato 'pi na saṃvidyate tadahamevaṃ kiṃ nu na mariṣyāmi? api tu ciramapi sthitvā jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānamiti //
body.translated_text: Day and night. 'The expenditure of life increases' — the formations of the lifespan are being depleted. 'Without rest' — there is no interruption of expenditure even for an instant. 'Arrival' (<s>āgama</s>) — the inflow — 'of the stock' — of increase — does not exist even in the slightest. Then, being like this, shall I indeed not die? On the contrary — even having lived long, life ends in death.

body.text: syādetat / yannimittaṃ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ te 'pi na narakādiṣu tatphaladuḥkhānubhavakāle saṃvibhāgino bhaviṣyanti / tat kimiti kātarabhāvamavalambase ityatrāha / āstāṃ tāvatparaloke-
body.translated_text: One might say: 'Those on whose account evil was done — they too will not be sharers of the suffering-fruit in the hells and so forth at the time of experiencing it. So why do you cling to a state of fear?' To this he says — 'Setting aside the next world for now' —

children.translated_text: Even while lying on one's bed, even standing in the midst of relatives,
the agony of having one's vital parts cut must be endured by me alone. // Bca_2.41 //

body.text: iha asminneva bhave maraṇāntikādiduḥkhabādhāyāṃ svajanaparijanamadhyagatenāpi / marmacchedādivedaneti pipāsāgātrasaṃtāpādiduḥkhaṃ mayaivaikena soḍhavyam / na tatra alpīyānapi bhāgo 'nyasya saṃbhavati //
body.translated_text: 'Here' — in this very existence — the affliction of death and so forth — even while surrounded by one's own people and retinue. 'The agony of having one's vital parts cut' — the suffering of thirst, bodily burning, and so forth — 'must be endured by me alone.' Not even the slightest share of it is possible for another.

body.text: kiṃ punarnarakādāvityāha-
body.translated_text: How much more in the hells and so forth — he says —

children.translated_text: When seized by the messengers of <s>Yama</s>, what use is a relative? What use is a friend?

children.text: puṇyamekaṃ tadā trāṇaṃ mayā tacca na sevitam // Bca_2.42 //
children.translated_text: Merit alone is then a protection — and that has not been cultivated by me. // Bca_2.42 //

body.text: kāladūtairgṛhītasya adhiṣṭhitasya galapāśena baddhasya mudgarairākoṭyamānasya aṭavīkāntāragahanakaṇṭakaviṣamaśilāśakalairvitudyamānacaraṇasya asahāyasya karmānubhavabhūmiṃ nīyamānasya / kuto bandhuḥ kutaḥ suhṛt iti na tatra kecit sahāyāsrāṇaṃ saṃbhavanti / puṇyamevaikaṃ tadā trāṇaṃ syāt / mayā tacca na sevitam, tacca puṇyaṃ trāṇabhūtaṃ mayā nopārjitam //
body.translated_text: 'When seized' — overpowered — by the messengers of Death, bound by a noose around the neck, being pounded with clubs, with feet pierced by the thorns, rough stones, and fragments of wilderness, desolate paths, and thickets — helpless, being led to the realm of <s>karma</s>-experience. 'What use is a relative? What use is a friend?' — no companions or protectors are possible there. 'Merit alone' is then a protection. 'And that has not been cultivated by me' — and that merit which would be a protection has not been accumulated by me.

body.text: punarapi pāpāt saṃvegamāha-
body.translated_text: Again expressing alarm at evil, he says —

children.translated_text: Not knowing this terror, through clinging to impermanent life,

children.text: pramattena mayā nāthā bahu pāpamupārjitam // Bca_2.43 //
children.translated_text: much evil has been accumulated by me, heedless, O Protectors. // Bca_2.43 //

body.text: asthāyini jīvite / āsaṅgādāgrahāt / idamāgāmi narakādiduḥkhabhayamajānatā apaśyata / pramatteneti yauvanarūpadhanādhipatyādimadamattena //
body.translated_text: 'In life that does not last.' 'Through clinging' — through grasping. 'Not knowing' — not seeing — this terror of future suffering in hells and so forth. 'Heedless' — intoxicated with the pride of youth, beauty, wealth, power, and so forth.

body.text: kiṃ punarevaṃ saṃvegabahulo bhavānityāha-
body.translated_text: Why then are you so filled with alarm? He says —

children.translated_text: Even one being led today for the cutting of a limb withers away;
parched, with dejected gaze, he sees the world differently. // Bca_2.44 //

body.text: atyalpamidaṃ karacaraṇādicchedanaṃ duḥkhaṃ narakaduḥkhāt / tathāpi tatreyamavasthā bhavati / viśuṣyati sarvātmanā śoṣamupayāti / pipāsitastṛṣṇārtaḥ / dīnadṛṣṭiriti kṛpaṇadṛṣṭiḥ / anyadeveti viparītam //
body.translated_text: This suffering of having hands, feet, and so forth cut off is extremely small compared to the suffering of hell. Yet even there, this condition arises: 'he withers away' — dries up completely. 'Parched' — tormented by thirst. 'With dejected gaze' — with pitiable look. 'Differently' — meaning the reverse [of how it normally appears].

body.text: narakaduḥkhasyātiśayamāha-
body.translated_text: He states the extreme [nature] of hell-suffering —

children.translated_text: How much more when overpowered by the terrifying forms of <s>Yama</s>'s messengers,
seized by the great fever of terror, covered in one's own excrement — // Bca_2.45 //

body.text: kātarairdṛṣṭipātaiśca trāṇānveṣī caturdiśam /
body.translated_text: with fearful glances seeking protection in the four directions!

body.text: bhairavākārairiti bhayaṃkararūpaiḥ / adhiṣṭhitaḥ ātmasātkṛtaḥ / mahātrāsanajvarastena grasto gṛhītaḥ / purīṣamuccāraḥ, tasyotsargo vinirgamaḥ, tena veṣṭito viliptaḥ / kātarairiti dīnaiḥ / caturdiśaṃ trāṇānveṣī / kathamityāha-
body.translated_text: 'Terrifying forms' — of frightening appearance. 'Overpowered' — taken possession of. 'Seized by the great fever of terror' — grasped by [that condition]. 'Excrement' means feces; its 'discharge' means emission; 'covered' — smeared — by it. 'Fearful' — dejected. 'Seeking protection in the four directions.' How? He says —

body.text: ko me mahābhayādasmātsādhustrāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati // Bca_2.46 //
body.translated_text: 'Who will be a good protector for me from this great terror?' // Bca_2.46 //

body.text: sādhurakāraṇavatsalaḥ / trāṇaṃ paritrātā //
body.translated_text: 'Good' — spontaneously compassionate. 'Protector' — a rescuer.

children.translated_text: Having seen the directions empty of protection, he again falls into stupor;

children.text: tadāhaṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmi tasmin sthāne mahābhaye // Bca_2.47 //
children.translated_text: then what shall I do in that place of great terror? // Bca_2.47 //

body.text: evamapi yadā kutracidapi trāṇaṃ na paśyati, tadā trāṇābhāvāt punaḥ saṃmohamāgataḥ / tadā tasmin kāle kiṃ kariṣyāmi? sarvakriyāsu asamarthaḥ san / tasmin sthāne pratāpanādinarakabhūmau //
body.translated_text: Thus also, when one does not see protection anywhere at all, then — because of the absence of protection — 'he again falls into stupor.' 'Then' — at that time — 'what shall I do?' — being incapable of all actions. 'In that place' — in the hell-realm of <s>Pratāpana</s> and others.

body.text: tasmādidānīmeva pratīkārānuṣṭhānaṃ yuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is proper to undertake the remedy right now — he says —

children.translated_text: This very day I go for refuge to the mighty Lords of the World,
who are engaged in protecting the world, the <s>Jinas</s> who remove all terror. // Bca_2.48 //

body.text: jagatāṃ nāthān sarvāśvāsanirvṛtisthānabhūtān nāyakān / mahābalāniti sarvatrāpratihatasāmarthyān / jagadrakṣārthamudyuktāniti sarvasattvaparitrāṇārthamudyuktān / evamapi
body.translated_text: 'Lords of the World' — protectors who are the locus of all solace, peace, and leadership. 'Mighty' — of power unobstructed everywhere. 'Engaged in protecting the world' — engaged in rescuing all beings. Even so

body.text: trāṇānāśritya bhayopaśamo na syāt, tadā kiṃ śaraṇagamanenetyatrāha- sarvatrāsaharāniti sarvavyasanāpahartṝn //
body.translated_text: 'if, despite taking refuge in protectors, fear is not pacified, then what use is going for refuge?' — to this he says 'who remove all terror' — who destroy all calamities.

body.text: dharmasaṃghaśaraṇagamanamāha-
body.translated_text: He states going for refuge to <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Saṃgha</s> —

children.translated_text: And to the <s>Dharma</s> realized by them, which destroys the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: śaraṇaṃ yāmi bhāvena bodhisattvagaṇaṃ tathā // Bca_2.49 //
children.translated_text: I go for refuge sincerely, and likewise to the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // Bca_2.49 //

body.text: tairbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ / adhigataṃ sākṣātkṛtam / dharmaṃ nirvāṇamityarthaḥ / saṃsārabhayanāśanaṃ sarvakleśapratipakṣatvāt / bhāveneti paramaprasādena na māyāśāṭhyena vicikitsayā vā / bodhisattvagaṇamiti saṃgham / tatheti bhāvena //
body.translated_text: 'By them' — by the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. 'Realized' — directly experienced. '<s>Dharma</s>' — meaning <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Which destroys the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>' — because it is the antidote to all defilements. 'Sincerely' — with supreme faith, not through pretense, deceit, or doubt. 'The assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' — [that is,] the <s>Saṃgha</s>. 'Likewise' — sincerely.

body.text: idānīṃ yathāpradhānaṃ bodhisattvebhya ātmaniryātanaṃ kurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, surrendering himself primarily to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, he says —

children.translated_text: To <s>Samantabhadra</s> I give myself, overwhelmed by fear;
and again to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> I give myself, of my own [will]. // Bca_2.50 //

body.text: samantabhadrāya bodhisattvāya / ātmānaṃ dadāmi niryātayāmi / bhayavihvalo narakādibhayavyākulaḥ / punaśca mañjughoṣāya mañjunāthāya / ātmaneti na parapreraṇayā / svayameva prasannacitta ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'To <s>Samantabhadra</s>' — to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [of that name]. 'I give myself' — I surrender myself. 'Overwhelmed by fear' — agitated by the fear of hells and so forth. 'And again to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>' — to <s>Mañjunātha</s>. 'Of my own [will]' — not through the urging of another. Of his own accord, with a faithful mind — that is the meaning.

children.translated_text: And to that Protector <s>Avalokita</s>, whose conduct is pervaded by compassion,

children.text: viraumyārtaravaṃ bhītaḥ sa māṃ rakṣatu pāpinam // Bca_2.51 //
children.translated_text: I cry out a piteous cry, afraid — may he protect me, a sinner! // Bca_2.51 //

body.text: āryāvalokiteśvaram / kṛpayā vyākulaṃ caritaṃ śīlamasyeti kṛpāvyākulacāriṇamiti tasyaiva viśeṣaṇam / viraumi āravaṃ karomi / ārtaravamiti kriyāviśeṣaṇam / duḥkhadīnakātarasvaram / bhītaḥ trastaḥ pāpakarmaphalāt / sa bhagavānavalokitaḥ māṃ rakṣatu pāpinaṃ kṛtapāpaṃ māṃ trāyatām //
body.translated_text: To noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. 'Whose conduct is pervaded by compassion' — whose conduct, whose character, is pervaded by compassion: this is his qualifier. 'I cry out' — I make a cry. 'A piteous cry' — this qualifies the action: with a voice that is suffering, dejected, and fearful. 'Afraid' — terrified — of the fruit of evil <s>karma</s>. 'May he' — may that Blessed <s>Avalokita</s> — 'protect me, a sinner' — may he rescue me who have done evil.

children.translated_text: And noble <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, and <s>Kṣitigarbha</s> too, sincerely,
and all the greatly compassionate ones — seeking protection, I cry out. // Bca_2.52 //

body.text: āryamākāśagarbhaṃ ca bodhisattvam / kṣitigarbhaṃ ca bodhisattvam / viraumīti pareṇa saṃbandhaḥ / sarvān mahākṛpāṃścāpi, ye 'pi na nāmagrahaṇenodāhṛtāḥ, tānapi paramakāruṇikān paraduḥkhaduḥkhinaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Noble <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>' — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. 'And <s>Kṣitigarbha</s>' — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. 'I cry out' connects with the previous [verse]. 'And all the greatly compassionate ones' — even those not mentioned by name — those supremely compassionate ones who suffer at others' suffering.

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva ca saṃtrastāḥ palāyante caturdiśam /
children.translated_text: Upon merely seeing whom, the terrifying <s>Yama</s>'s messengers and others flee in the four directions,
frightened — to him, the Vajra-holder, I pay homage. // Bca_2.53 //

body.text: yasya darśanamātreṇa yamadūtādayaḥ / ādiśabdādanye 'pi yakṣarākṣasādayo duṣṭā bhītāḥ santaḥ palāyante, dūramapagacchanti / taṃ namasyāmi namaskaromi / vajriṇamiti vajramasyāstīti vajrapāṇiṃ bodhisattvam / tadanena śaraṇagamanādinā pāpakṣayārthamāśrayabalamupadarśitam / yaduktaṃ caturdharmakasūtre-
body.translated_text: 'Upon the mere sight of whom,' <s>Yama</s>'s messengers and others — the word 'and others' [includes] <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and so forth — malevolent, being frightened, 'flee' — go far away. 'To him I pay homage' — I bow. 'The Vajra-holder' — he who has a <s>vajra</s>, thus <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. By this, the power of reliance through going for refuge and so forth has been shown for the purpose of destroying evil. As stated in the <s>Caturdharmasūtra</s> —

body.text: tatrāśrayabalaṃ buddhadharmasaṃghaśaraṇagamanamanutsṛṣṭabodhicittatā ca / sa balavatsaṃniśrayeṇa na śakyate pāpenābhibhavitum / iti //
body.translated_text: 'Therein, the power of reliance is going for refuge to <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, and not abandoning <s>bodhicitta</s>. He who has the power of reliance cannot be overpowered by evil.'

body.text: punaranyathātvaśaṃkāṃ nirākartumāha-
body.translated_text: To remove the suspicion of change [in their attitude toward him], he says —

children.translated_text: Having transgressed your words, now from seeing [this] terror,

children.text: śaraṇaṃ yāmi vo bhīto bhayaṃ nāśayata drutam // Bca_2.54 //
children.translated_text: I go to you for refuge, frightened — destroy [this] fear quickly! // Bca_2.54 //

body.text: atikramya yuṣmadājñām / sāṃpratamidānīm / bhayadarśanāt, tadatikrame yasmādaniṣṭaphalasaṃbhavadarśanāt, vo yuṣmān śaraṇaṃ yāmi bhītaḥ aniṣṭaphalāduttrastaḥ / tasmātpunaranyathāśaṅkā na kartavyā / ato bhayaṃ nāśavata, pūrvakṛtapāpād bhayamapanayata / drutaṃ śīghram / mametyadhyāhāryam //
body.translated_text: 'Having transgressed' — violated — your command. 'Now' — at this time. 'From seeing [this] terror' — because of seeing that from that transgression, an unpleasant fruit is possible. 'To you I go for refuge, frightened' — terrified of the unpleasant fruit. Therefore no suspicion of change should be entertained. Hence 'destroy [this] fear' — remove the fear from formerly-done evil. 'Quickly' — swiftly. 'My' should be supplied.

body.text: nanu evamapi kaḥ pratyeṣyati / tvadvacanādityāśaṅkaya punaratrārthe dṛḍhatāmāha-
body.translated_text: Objection: 'Even so, who will believe [it]? [Only] because of your word!' — countering this doubt, he further establishes firmness in this matter —

children.translated_text: Even one frightened by a transient illness would not transgress the physician's word;
how much more one seized by four hundred and four diseases! // Bca_2.55 //

body.text: itvaro gatvaro naśvaro 'cirasthāyītyarthaḥ / laghurvā / sa cāsau vyādhiśceti, tasmād bhayena / vaidyavākyaṃ na laṅghayet vaidyopadeśaṃ nātikramet / mā ayaṃ vyādhirmama vṛddhimupagacchet / kimu kiṃ punaḥ / vyādhiśatairgrasto laṅghayet / caturbhiścaturuttarairiti caturadhikaiścaturbhiḥ śatairityarthaḥ / śatamakālamṛtyūnām, ekaṃ kālamaraṇamityekottaraṃ śataṃ mṛtyūnām / te ca pratyekaṃ vātapittaśleṣmakṛtāḥ tatsaṃnipātakṛtāśceti caturuttarāṇi catvāri śatāni bhavanti / iti kāraṇabhedātkāryabhedaḥ, kāryabhedācca kāraṇabhedavyavasthā //
body.translated_text: 'Transient' (<s>itvara</s>) — fleeting, perishable, not long-lasting in meaning; or minor. That which is such an illness — [frightened] by it. 'Would not transgress the physician's word' — would not violate the physician's instruction — [thinking] 'lest this illness grow worse for me.' 'How much more' — all the more — 'one seized by hundreds of diseases would not transgress.' 'Four hundred and four' — meaning four hundred with four additional, that is, four sets of a hundred plus four. One hundred types of untimely death; one type of timely death — thus one hundred and one types of death. These are each caused by wind, bile, phlegm, and by their combination — thus four sets of four hundred arise. Thus from the differentiation of causes, the differentiation of effects [is established], and from the differentiation of effects, the arrangement of differentiated causes.

body.text: nanu tathāpi kimatra bhayakāraṇaṃ yannāstītyāha-
body.translated_text: Objection: 'Even so, what cause for fear is there here that does not exist [for others]?' — he says —

children.translated_text: Since by even a single one [of these diseases], all humans dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>

children.text: naśyanti yeṣāṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ sarvadikṣu na labhyate // Bca_2.56 //
children.translated_text: perish — [diseases] whose medicine cannot be found in any direction — // Bca_2.56 //

body.text: ekenāpi vyādhinā kupitena yasmātsarve jambudvīpagatā narāḥ prāṇino naśyanti mriyante / anyacca / yeṣāṃ vyādhīnāṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ auṣadhaṃ cikitsārthaṃ kvacidapi na prāpyate / atra kāśirājapadmakajātakamupaneyam / tadyathānuśrūyate- bodhicaryāṃ carannayameva bhagavānatīte 'dhvani padmo nāma kāśirājo babhūva / tasmin samaye sarve jambudvīpakā manuṣyā mahatā rogeṇa vikalībhūtā mriyante ca / tairidamālocitam- ayameva asmākaṃ svāmī rājā paramakāruṇikaḥ pratīkāraṃ vidhāsyatīti asyaiva ātmaduḥkhaṃ nivedayāmaḥ / te ca evamavadhārya militvā, bho mahārāja, bhavati svāmini paramahitaiṣiṇi saṃvidyamāne 'pi iyamasmākamavasthā, iti tasmin rājani duḥkhamāviṣkṛtavantaḥ / sa ca rājā karuṇāparavaśahṛdayaḥ teṣāṃ duḥkhamasahamānaḥ śīghramamīṣāṃ rogapīḍāmapanayata iti vaidyānājñāpayāmāsa / te 'pi tatheti pratiśrutya
body.translated_text: 'By even a single disease, when aggravated, all humans dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>' — all living beings — 'perish' — die. 'And moreover, [diseases] whose medicine' — remedy, for the purpose of treatment — 'cannot be found' — cannot be obtained — anywhere at all. Here the <s>Jātaka</s> of King <s>Padmaka</s> of <s>Kāśī</s> should be adduced. As tradition has it: this very Blessed One, while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct in a past era, was a king of <s>Kāśī</s> named <s>Padmaka</s>. At that time, all the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> became disabled by a great disease and were dying. They reflected: 'This very king, our lord, is supremely compassionate — he will provide a remedy. Let us report our suffering to him.' Having resolved thus, gathering together, [they said:] 'O great king, even while you, our lord, who are supremely desirous of our welfare, exist, this is our condition!' — thus they disclosed their suffering to that king. And that king, his heart overcome by compassion, unable to bear their suffering, commanded the physicians: 'Quickly remove the disease-affliction of these [people]!' They, having assented 'Very well!'

body.text: cikitsāśāstrāṇi vyavalokya sadyorohitamatsyamāṃsādanyad bhaiṣajyamalabhamānāḥ tathaiva rājñaḥ pratyuktavantaḥ / iti vistaraḥ / idameva jātakaṃ bhavopalakṣaṇaṃ darśitam //
body.translated_text: having consulted the medical treatises, not finding any other medicine than fresh <s>Rohita</s>-fish flesh, reported back to the king just so. Thus the full account. This very <s>Jātaka</s> is shown as illustrative of [cyclic] existence.

children.translated_text: And in that [regard:] 'I transgress the word of the omniscient physician who removes all darts' —
shame on me, the supremely deluded! // Bca_2.57 //

body.text: kāyikamānasikānekaśalyoddhāriṇaḥ / ātmānaṃ jugupsate / dhiṅ māmatyantamohitamiti / evaṃ jānannapi yadi tathāgatājñāyā vaimukhyamāseve, tadā mama mohasya paryanto nāsti / kutsanīyo 'smītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Who removes many physical and mental darts.' He feels disgust at himself: 'Shame on me, the supremely deluded!' — even knowing thus, if I still turn away from the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s command, then there is no end to my delusion — 'I am contemptible': that is the meaning.

body.text: kiṃ punarevamityāha-
body.translated_text: Why is [this alarm so great]? He says —

children.translated_text: Even at other, [lesser] precipices, I stand with extreme caution;
how much more at a precipice a thousand <s>yojanas</s> [deep], lasting for a long time! // Bca_2.58 //

body.text: parvatādiprapāteṣu alpatareṣu yatrāsthibhaṅgamātraṃ maraṇamātraṃ vā duḥkhaṃ syāt / kimu yojanasāhasra iti / yojanasahasraṃ parimāṇamasya ityaṇ / anekayojanasahasraparimāṇe avīcyādikaprapāte ityarthaḥ / dīrghakālika iti / yatrāntarakalpādibhirāyuṣaḥ kṣayaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'At precipices' of mountains and so forth — at minor ones — where one might suffer merely broken bones or death. 'How much more at one a thousand <s>yojanas</s> [deep]' — 'whose measure is a thousand <s>yojanas</s>' [with the taddhita suffix]; meaning: at a precipice of many thousands of <s>yojanas</s> in extent, such as <s>Avīci</s> and others. 'Lasting for a long time' — where the lifespan expires only through intermediate <s>kalpas</s> and so forth.

body.text: sadyo maraṇamadṛṣṭvaiva kimakāṇḍe kātaratayā sukhāsikāṃ jahāsītyāha-
body.translated_text: 'Not having seen immediate death, why do you groundlessly give up your comfortable seat out of fear?' — he says —

children.text: adyaiva maraṇaṃ naiti na yuktā me sukhāsikā /
children.translated_text: Death does not come only today — my comfortable seat is not fitting;

children.text: avaśyameti sā velā na bhaviṣyāmyahaṃ yadā // Bca_2.59 //
children.translated_text: that time will certainly come when I shall be no more. // Bca_2.59 //

body.text: avaśyamiti niścitametat //
body.translated_text: 'Certainly' — this is established beyond doubt.

body.text: tathāpi bhayamayuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: Yet still, fear is unjustified — he says —

children.text: abhayaṃ kena me dattaṃ niḥsariṣyāmi vā katham /
children.translated_text: By whom was fearlessness given to me? Or how shall I escape?

children.text: avaśyaṃ na bhaviṣyāmi kasmānme susthitaṃ manaḥ // Bca_2.60 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall certainly cease to be — why is my mind at ease?' // <s>Bca</s> 2.60 //

body.text: abhayaṃ mā bhairiti kena satpuruṣeṇa mama dattaṃ yena nirbhayo vihariṣyāmīti bhāvaḥ / yadi vā niḥsaraṇopāyo 'pi yadi bhavet, tathāpi bhayamayuktam / tadapi nāsti / niḥsariṣyāmi vā kathaṃ tato duḥkhāt / avaśyaṃ na bhaviṣyāmīti / sarvajīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānamityuktaṃ bhagavatā //
body.translated_text: 'Fearlessness' — 'Do not fear!' — by what good person was this given to me, that I should live without fear? — this is the sense. Or even if there were a means of escape, even then fear would be unjustified. But even that does not exist. 'Or how shall I escape from that suffering?' 'I shall certainly cease to be' — for the Blessed One has said: 'All life has death as its conclusion.'

children.translated_text: 'Thus ease is not fitting for me' — he says:
'From things formerly experienced, now perished — what essence remains for me?

children.text: yeṣu me 'bhiniviṣṭena gurūṇāṃ laṅghitaṃ vacaḥ // Bca_2.61 //
children.translated_text: Attached to which, I have transgressed the words of my teachers.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.61 //

body.text: abhiniviṣṭeneti āsaktena / gurūṇāmiti buddhabodhisattvakalyāṇamitrāṇām //
body.translated_text: 'Attached' (<s>abhiniviṣṭena</s>) means clinging. 'Teachers' (<s>gurūṇām</s>) means <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and spiritual friends.

body.text: tasmādidamaharniśaṃ mama manasi kartumucitamityāha-
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, this should be the constant focus of my mind, day and night' — he says:

children.translated_text: 'Having left this world of the living, and likewise relatives and acquaintances,

children.text: ekākī kvāpi yāsyāmi kiṃ me sarvaiḥ priyāpriyaiḥ // Bca_2.62 //
children.translated_text: I shall go alone to some place — what use to me are all friends and foes?' // <s>Bca</s> 2.62 //

body.text: jīvalokaṃ sattvalokam, imaṃ manuṣyādiasabhāgatālakṣaṇam / ekākītyasahāyaḥ / kvāpītyaniścitasthānam //
body.translated_text: 'The world of the living' means the world of beings — 'this' one, characterized by the common class of humans and so forth. 'Alone' means without a companion. 'To some place' means to an uncertain destination.

children.text: iyameva tu me cintā yuktā rātriṃdivaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: 'But this alone is the proper reflection for me, day and night:"

children.text: aśubhānniyataṃ duḥkhaṃ niḥsareyaṃ tataḥ katham // Bca_2.63 //
children.translated_text: "From the unwholesome, suffering is certain — how may I escape from that?"' // <s>Bca</s> 2.63 //

body.text: aśubhāditi akuśalāt karmaṇaḥ / tata ityaśubhāt //
body.translated_text: 'From the unwholesome' means from unwholesome <s>karma</s>. 'From that' means from the unwholesome.

body.text: sāṃprataṃ kṛtakarmaphalasaṃbandhaniścayo mahatābhiniveśena punaratyayadeśanāmārabhata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Now, having ascertained the connection between performed actions and their fruits, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] undertakes the confession of transgressions again with great earnestness — [the commentator] says:

children.translated_text: 'Whatever sin has been accumulated by me, a fool, a deluded one —

children.text: prakṛtyā yacca sāvadyaṃ prajñaptyāvadyameva ca // Bca_2.64 //
children.translated_text: both that which is faulty by nature and that which is faulty by designation — // <s>Bca</s> 2.64 //
all of that I confess, standing before the Protectors,
with joined palms, fearful of suffering, bowing down again and again. // <s>Bca</s> 2.65 //

body.text: atyayamatyayatvena pratigṛhṇantu nāyakāḥ /
body.translated_text: May the Guides accept my transgression as a transgression!'

body.text: bāleneti ajānatā / mūḍheneti mohāndhena / yatkiṃciditi kāyena vācā manasā vā / prakṛtisāvadyaṃ prāṇātipātādidaśākuśalasvabhāvam / prajñaptisāvadyaṃ yad bhagavatā gṛhītasaṃvarāṇāmeva prajñaptamakālabhojanādirūpam / deśayāmīti vāgvijñaptimutthāpayati / kṛtāñjaliriti kāyavijñaptiḥ / praṇipatya punaḥpunariti atiśayavaccittasaṃvegamupadarśayati / ati yatatyanena narakādiṣu iti atyayaḥ, aśubhaṃ karma / tamatyayatvena doṣatvena pratigṛhṇantu jānantu paśyantu vidantu vyaktīkṛtaṃ mayā / anāvaraṇacittena, pracchādanā atra mamāstīti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Fool' (<s>bālena</s>) means one who does not know. 'Deluded' (<s>mūḍhena</s>) means blinded by delusion. 'Whatever' means by body, speech, or mind. 'Faulty by nature' (<s>prakṛtisāvadya</s>) means whose nature is the ten unwholesome [courses of action] such as killing and the rest. 'Faulty by designation' (<s>prajñaptisāvadya</s>) means what has been designated by the Blessed One for those who have taken the [monastic] restraint only, such as eating at improper times and the like. 'I confess' (<s>deśayāmi</s>) — he produces vocal expression. 'With joined palms' — this is bodily expression. 'Bowing down again and again' — this displays the extraordinary agitation of mind. 'Transgression' (<s>atyaya</s>) — by which one 'goes beyond' (<s>ati-yatati</s>) into hells and the like — unwholesome <s>karma</s>. [May the Guides] 'accept that transgression as a transgression' — as a fault — may they know, see, understand that it has been made manifest by me, with an unobstructed mind. The sense is: 'I have no concealment here.'

body.text: punaḥ skhalitaśaṅkāmapākartuṃ punarakaraṇasaṃvaraṃ kurvannāha- na bhadrakamityādi /
body.translated_text: In order to remove the apprehension of future lapse, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] undertakes the restraint of non-repetition, saying 'This is not good' and so forth:

body.text: na bhadrakamidaṃ nāthā na kartavyaṃ punarmayā // Bca_2.66 //
body.translated_text: 'This is not good, O Protectors; it shall not be done again by me.' // <s>Bca</s> 2.66 //

body.text: yadāryakāntaṃ vijñapraśastaṃ na bhavati tadabhadrakaṃ garhitam anāryaṃ karmetyucyate / tadadyaprabhṛti jānatā paśyatā buddhipūrvakaṃ saṃcintya punarmayā na kartavyam / āyatyāṃ punarakaraṇasaṃvaramāpatsye ityarthaḥ / etacca triskandhapravartanaprastāve [bodhe, 5.98-99] vyaktīkariṣyate //
body.translated_text: That which is not pleasing to the noble ones, not praised by the wise — that is called 'not good' (<s>abhadraka</s>), blameworthy, ignoble action. That, from today onward, by one who knows, who sees, who deliberates — shall not be done again by me. The meaning is: 'I shall undertake the restraint of non-repetition for the future.' And this will be made explicit in the context of the turning of the three heaps [<s>triskandha</s>] [in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s>, 5.98-99].

body.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ pāpadeśanā nāma dvitīyaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the second chapter, called 'The Confession of Sins' (<s>Pāpadeśanā</s>), in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.

body.text: 3. bodhicittaparigraho nāma tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter 3: The Chapter Called 'The Embracing of <s>Bodhicitta</s>' (<s>Bodhicittaparigraha</s>).

body.text: adhunā pāpadeśanānantaraṃ puṇyānumodanāmāha-
body.translated_text: Now, immediately after the confession of sins, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] speaks of the rejoicing in merit:

children.translated_text: 'I rejoice with delight in the good done by all beings,

children.text: anumode pramodena sukhaṃ tiṣṭhantu duḥkhitāḥ // Bca_3.1 //
children.translated_text: which grants respite from the sufferings of the lower realms — may the suffering ones abide in happiness!' // <s>Bca</s> 3.1 //

body.text: narakādigatau duḥkhamanubhavanto hi pariśrāntāḥ sukṛtavipākamadhigamya pratilabdhasukhā viśrāmyanti kiyatkālam / anumode prasādena iti saṃpraharṣayāmi prasannacittaḥ / anumodanāpi trividhāmanasā kāyena vācā ca / tatra prasannacittaḥ saṃpraharṣayati manasā, kāyena romaharṣaśrupātagātrakampādikamanubhavan, vācā ca saṃprahṛṣṭacetanaḥ tathāvidhāmeva vācamuccārayan, sādhu kṛtaṃ bhadrakaṃ kṛtamiti / sukhaṃ tiṣṭhantu duḥkhitā iti yadarthaṃ taistatkarma kṛtam, tadapi teṣāṃ samṛdhyatu iti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: For those who are experiencing suffering in the destinies such as hell, who are weary, rest for a time having attained happiness through reaching the ripening of good deeds. 'I rejoice with delight' — I gladden with a clear mind. Rejoicing (<s>anumodanā</s>) is also threefold: by mind, body, and speech. Therein, with a clear mind one gladdens by mind; by body, experiencing goose-bumps, tears, bodily trembling, and the like; and by speech, with a gladdened mind, uttering such words as 'Well done! Good has been done!' 'May the suffering ones abide in happiness' — may that for whose sake they performed those actions also be fulfilled for them — this is the sense.

body.text: laukikaṃ karmānumodya lokottaramanumodamānaḥ prāha-
body.translated_text: Having rejoiced at worldly <s>karma</s>, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] now rejoices at the supramundane, saying:

children.translated_text: 'I rejoice in the liberation of embodied beings from the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
I rejoice in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-hood and <s>Buddha</s>-hood of the Protectors.' // <s>Bca</s> 3.2 //

body.text: duḥkhanirmokṣamiti śrāvakabodhiḥ pratyekabuddhabodhirvā / cittaṃ vā tadarthamutpāditaṃ tathocyate / tadā bodhitrayamapi tadgāhaḥ / śarīriṇāmiti prāṇinām / bodhisattvatvabuddhatvamiti bodhisattvatvaṃ bhagavatāṃ hetvavasthām, buddhatvaṃ phalāvasthāmiti / tāyināmiti svādhigatamārgadeśakānām / yaduktam- tāyaḥ svadṛṣṭamārgoktiḥ iti / tadvidyate yeṣāmiti / athavā- tāyaḥ saṃtānārthaḥ āsaṃsāramapratiṣṭhitanirvāṇatayāvasthāyinām //
body.translated_text: 'Liberation from suffering' means the awakening of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> or the awakening of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>; or the mind generated for that purpose is referred to thus. Then all three types of awakening are included. 'Of embodied beings' means of living creatures. '<s>Bodhisattva</s>-hood and <s>Buddha</s>-hood' — <s>Bodhisattva</s>-hood is the causal stage of the Blessed Ones; <s>Buddha</s>-hood is the resultant stage. 'Of the Protectors' (<s>tāyinām</s>) means of those who teach the path they have themselves realized. As it is said: '<s>Tāya</s> means the declaration of the path one has seen.' Those who possess that. Or alternatively: '<s>tāya</s>' means continuity — of those who abide [in the world] for all time through non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: bodhisattvānāṃ puṇyānumodanāṃ kurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Performing the rejoicing in merit of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.translated_text: 'I rejoice in the oceans of the arising of the mind [of awakening], which bring happiness to all beings,
and which establish the welfare of all beings — [the minds] of the Teachers.' // <s>Bca</s> 3.3 //

body.text: cittotpādāḥ pratikṣaṇabhāvino 'paryantāgādhatayā samudrā iva samudrāḥ tān / kiṃbhūtān? sarvasattvasukhāvahān sarvasattvānāṃ sukhamāvahantīti tadrasaikanimnasvabhāvānityarthaḥ / sarvasattvahitādhānāniti hitavidhāyakān / śāsināmiti śāsanaṃ śāsaḥ buddhatvopāyābhyāsaḥ, tadarthatvādupacārāt / tadvidyate yeṣāmiti śāsino bodhisattvāḥ / taduktam-
body.translated_text: 'The arisings of mind' — occurring at every moment, like oceans in being boundless and unfathomable — those. Of what kind? 'Which bring happiness to all beings' — which convey happiness to all beings, meaning whose nature inclines entirely toward that essence — this is the meaning. 'Which establish the welfare of all beings' — which provide welfare. 'Of the Teachers' (<s>śāsinām</s>) — 'teaching' (<s>śāsana</s>) means the practice of the means to <s>Buddha</s>-hood; by figurative extension, because [<s>Bodhisattvas</s>] exist for that purpose. Those who possess that are '<s>śāsins</s>' — the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. As it is said:

children.translated_text: 'This very practice of means is considered to be "teaching" (<s>śāsana</s>), because of being for that purpose [of <s>Buddha</s>-hood].'
Thus.

body.text: athavā- śāsituṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāmiti śāsinaḥ / bodhisattvā hi dānādibhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ sattvān saṃgṛhya sanmārge 'vatārayanti //
body.translated_text: Or alternatively: those whose nature (<s>śīla</s>) is to teach (<s>śāsitum</s>) are '<s>śāsins</s>.' For the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having drawn beings near through the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) such as giving and the like, guide them onto the right path.

body.text: etāvatā anumodanā kathitā / adhyeṣaṇāṃ kathayannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus far, the rejoicing has been described. [<s>Śāntideva</s>] speaks of the entreaty (<s>adhyeṣaṇā</s>), saying:

children.translated_text: 'With joined palms I beseech the <s>Buddhas</s> in all directions:
may they light the lamp of <s>Dharma</s> for those who are falling into suffering through delusion!' // <s>Bca</s> 3.4 //

body.text: dharmapradīpaṃ kurvantviti ajñānatamovṛtānāṃ sattvānāṃ mārgāmārgaviśeṣaparijñānavikalānāṃ dharmadeśanātmakamālokaṃ kurvantu //
body.translated_text: 'May they light the lamp of <s>Dharma</s>' — may they create the light that consists of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching for beings who are covered by the darkness of ignorance, who lack the discrimination between the right path and the wrong path.

body.text: etāvatā adhyeṣaṇā kathitā / yācanāmupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus far the entreaty has been described. Showing the supplication (<s>yācanā</s>), [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.translated_text: 'With joined palms I supplicate the Conquerors who wish to enter <s>nirvāṇa</s>:
may they remain for infinite <s>kalpas</s>, lest this world become blind!' // <s>Bca</s> 3.5 //

body.text: kṛtakṛtyatayā parinirvāṇaṃ gantumanasaḥ / aparyantakalpān sthitaye yācayāmi / mā bhūdandhamiti pūrvavanmārgājñānaniścetanaṃ mā bhūt / anenāpi yācanā proktā //
body.translated_text: 'Those whose minds [intend] to pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having accomplished their task.' 'I supplicate them to remain for boundless <s>kalpas</s>.' 'Lest [the world] become blind' — may it not become, as before, without consciousness of the path, ignorant of the way. By this too, the supplication is declared.

body.text: yācanānāntaramidānīṃ pariṇāmanāmāha-
body.translated_text: Now, immediately after the supplication, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] speaks of the dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>):

children.translated_text: 'Having done all this thus, whatever good has been obtained by me —
by that, may I become the one who pacifies all the suffering of all beings.' // <s>Bca</s> 3.6 //

body.text: evamuktakrameṇa sarvamidaṃ pūjāpāpadeśanāpuṇyānumodanādi kṛtvā vidhāya yanmayā āsāditaṃ prāptaṃ śubhaṃ sukṛtaṃ tena śubhena syāṃ bhaveyaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ samastaprāṇabhṛtāṃ sarvaduḥkhapraśāntikṛditi niḥśeṣavyasanapraśamanasamartho bhaveyam //
body.translated_text: 'In the manner described' — having done all this — worship, confession of sins, rejoicing in merit, and the rest — having performed [it], 'whatever good' — whatever merit — 'has been obtained' — gained — 'by me,' 'by that good, may I become' — may I be — 'the pacifier of all the suffering of all beings' — of all living creatures — meaning: may I become capable of pacifying all misfortune without remainder.

body.text: iti sāmānyena pariṇamayya punarviśeṣeṇāha-
body.translated_text: Having dedicated in general terms, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] speaks further in specific terms:

children.text: glānānāmasmi bhaiṣajyaṃ bhaveyaṃ vaidya eva ca /
children.translated_text: 'May I be the medicine for the sick, and the physician too,
and their attendant, until the non-recurrence of disease.' // <s>Bca</s> 3.7 //

body.text: teneti sarvatra yathāyogaṃ saṃbandhanīyam / glānānāmiti vyādhipīḍitānām / bhaiṣajyamiti auṣadham / vaidyaścikitsakaḥ / tadupasthāyakaḥ tasya glānasya paricārakaḥ / rogāpunarbhava iti yāvad vyādhinivṛttiḥ syāt //
body.translated_text: 'By that' should be connected everywhere as appropriate. 'For the sick' means those afflicted by illness. 'Medicine' means remedies. 'Physician' means healer. 'Their attendant' means the caretaker of that sick person. 'Until the non-recurrence of disease' means until the cessation of illness.

children.translated_text: 'May I destroy the torment of hunger and thirst through showers of food and drink;
in the intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of famine, may I become drink and food.' // <s>Bca</s> 3.8 //

body.text: kṣud bubhukṣā / pipāsā tṛṣṇā / tayorvyathā, tābhyāṃ vā vyathā / tāṃ hanyāṃ nivarteyam / annapānapravarṣaṇaiḥ prabandhāhārapānasaṃpādanaiḥ / durbhikṣāntarakalpeṣviti-
body.translated_text: 'Hunger' (<s>kṣud</s>) means craving for food. 'Thirst' (<s>pipāsā</s>) means craving [for drink]. 'The torment of these two,' or 'torment caused by these two.' 'May I destroy' — may I eliminate. 'Through showers of food and drink' — through the continuous provision of nourishment and beverages. 'In the intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of famine' —

body.text: kalpasya śastrarogābhyāṃ durbhikṣeṇa ca nirgamaḥ / iti //
body.translated_text: 'The <s>kalpa</s> ends through weapons, disease, and famine.' Thus.

body.text: tatra daśavarṣāyuṣi prajāyāmantarakalpaparyante durbhikṣeṇa saṃvartaḥ prādurbhavati varṣān sapta, māsān sapta, divasānapi saptaiva / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: Therein, at the end of an intermediate <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people is ten years, destruction by famine arises — for seven years, seven months, and seven days. As it is said:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>kalpa</s> ends through weapons, disease, and famine —
for [seven] days, [seven] months, and [seven] years, respectively.'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tatra annapānābhāvādanyonyamāṃsāsthibhakṣaṇameva āhāraḥ / tadapi kecidalabhamānā āhāravaikalyācca mriyante / tatra bhaveyaṃ pānabhojanam //
body.translated_text: Therein, due to the absence of food and drink, eating each other's flesh and bones is the only nourishment. And some, unable to obtain even that, die from lack of food. 'There may I become drink and food.'

children.translated_text: 'And for poor beings, may I be an inexhaustible treasure;
may I stand before them in the forms of various requisites.' // <s>Bca</s> 3.9 //

body.text: daridrāṇāmiti dhanavikalānām / akṣaya iti ākṛṣyamāṇadhano 'pi yo na kṣīyate / nānopakaraṇākārairiti śayanāsanavasanabhojanābharaṇavilepanaprabhṛti yadyadabhilaṣanti sattvāḥ, taistairupakaraṇaviśeṣākāraiḥ ahameva upatiṣṭheyaṃ pratyupasthito bhaveyam / teṣāṃ daridrāṇāṃ sattvānāmagrataḥ purataḥ / idaṃ ca pariṇāmanamāryavajradhvajasūtre vistareṇa pratipāditam / tatredamuktam-
body.translated_text: 'For the poor' means for those lacking wealth. 'Inexhaustible' means one whose wealth, even when drawn upon, is not depleted. 'In the forms of various requisites' — whatever beings desire, such as bedding, seating, clothing, food, ornaments, ointments, and the rest — in the forms of those various particular requisites, 'may I myself stand' — may I be present — 'before them' — before those poor beings. And this dedication is taught in detail in the Noble <s>Vajradhvajasūtra</s>. Therein it is said:

body.text: sa tāni kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayan evaṃ pariṇāmayati- anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena sarvasattvānāṃ layanaṃ bhaveyaṃ sarvaduḥkhaskandhavinivartanatayā / sarvasattvānāṃ trāṇaṃ bhaveyaṃ sarvakleśaparimocanatayā / sarvasattvānāṃ śaraṇaṃ bhaveyaṃ sarvabhayārakṣaṇatayā / sarvasattvānāṃ gatirbhaveyaṃ sarvabhūmyanugamanatayā / sarvasattvānāṃ parāyaṇaṃ bhaveyamatyantayogakṣemapratilambhanatayā / sarvasattvānāmāloko bhaveyaṃ vitimirajñānasaṃdarśanatayā / sarvasattvānāmulkā bhaveyamavidyātamondhakāravinivartanatayā / ityādi vistaraḥ / idamuktvā punaridamāha- tatrādhyāśayataḥ pariṇamayatio na vacanamātreṇa / taccodagracittaḥ pariṇamayati / hṛṣṭacittaḥ pariṇamayati / prasannacittaḥ pariṇamayati / pramuditacittaḥ strigdhacittaḥ pariṇamayati / maitracittaḥ premacitto 'nugrahacitto hitacittaḥ sukhacittaḥ pariṇamayati / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Dedicating those wholesome roots, he dedicates thus: "By these wholesome roots, may I become a refuge for all beings, through the turning away of the entire mass of suffering. May I become a protection for all beings, through the deliverance from all defilements. May I become a shelter for all beings, through the guarding from all fears. May I become a destination for all beings, through the accompanying to all stages. May I become a final resort for all beings, through the attainment of ultimate security. May I become a light for all beings, through the showing forth of knowledge free from darkness. May I become a torch for all beings, through the turning away of the darkness of the blindness of ignorance."' And so forth in detail. Having said this, [the sūtra] says further: 'Therein, he dedicates from [right] intention, not by mere words. And he dedicates with an elated mind. He dedicates with a joyful mind. He dedicates with a clear mind. He dedicates with a gladdened mind, an affectionate mind. He dedicates with a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of love, a mind of beneficence, a mind of benevolence, a mind of happiness.' And so forth in detail.

body.text: idānīmātmabhāvādiparityāgaṃ kurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] speaks of the relinquishing of self and the rest:

children.translated_text: 'My selves, my enjoyments, and the good of all three times —
I relinquish without reservation, for the accomplishment of the welfare of all beings.' // <s>Bca</s> 3.10 //

body.text: ātmabhāvāniti sarvagaticyutyupapattiṣu sarvakāyān / nirapekṣaḥ sarvaprakāreṇa nirāsaṅga ityarthaḥ / tyajāmi utsṛjāmi / dadāmītyarthaḥ / bhogāniti upabhogyavastūni hayagajarathaprāsādādyāśrayastrakcandanavastrābharaṇakanyādīni / sarvatryadhvagataṃ śubhamiti sarvatraidhātukasaṃgṛhītaṃ puṇyāneñjayasvabhāvam / yadi vā dānaśīlādiprasūtaṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ ca / tryadhvagatam atītānāgatapratyutpannam / syādetat- anāgatasya asatsvabhāvasya ko 'yamutsargo nāma? satyam / kiṃ tu tatsaṃbhavakāle tatrāsaṅganivāraṇārthamevamucyate, idānīmeva tatparityāgāt, āśayasya viśuddhivardhanārthaṃ ca / etadevāha- nirapekṣa iti / tadvipākasya svārthe 'napekṣaḥ / kimarthamevamanuṣṭhīyate ityāha- sarvasattvārthasiddhaye iti / sarvasattvānāṃ traidhātukavartināmabhyudayaniḥśreyasalakṣaṇārthaniṣpattaye / atītānāgataśubhotsargastu āryākṣayamatisūtre 'bhihitaḥ / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: 'Personal existences' — all bodies in all rebirths and transmigrations through the destinies. 'Without concern' — utterly unattached in every way: that is the meaning. 'I relinquish' — I release, I give. 'Enjoyments' — objects to be enjoyed: horses, elephants, chariots, palaces and such dwellings, garlands, sandalwood, garments, ornaments, maidens, and so forth. 'All the merit of the three times' — included within the entire triple realm, of the nature of merit and imperturbable [karma]; or alternatively, born from giving, morality, and so forth, and also born of meditation. 'Of the three times' — past, future, and present. One might object: 'What kind of relinquishment is this of the future, which is of non-existent nature?' True. But this is said in order to prevent attachment at the time of its arising — through relinquishing it now — and for the purpose of increasing the purity of one's aspiration. This is what [the word] 'without concern' states: he has no concern for the result in his own interest. 'For what purpose is this practiced?' He says 'for the accomplishment of the welfare of all beings' — for the attainment of the welfare characterized by worldly prosperity and supreme good for all beings abiding in the triple realm. The relinquishment of past and future merit is stated in the <s>Āryākṣayamatisūtra</s>. As stated there —

body.text: kuśalānāṃ ca cittacaitasikānāmanusmṛtiḥ, anusmṛtya ca bodhipariṇāmanā, ida matītakauśalyam / yā anāgatānāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ nidhyaptirbodherāmukhīkarmasamanvāhāraḥ, ye ye utpatsyante kuśalāścittotpādāḥ, tānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayiṣyāmi / idamanāgatakauśalyam / iti vistaraḥ / sarvatyāgādhimuktiṃ paripūrye parityāgacittavegāt tena kāyaprayogeṇa utsṛṣṭasarvaparigrahaḥ / sarvaparigrahamūlādbhavaduḥkhādvimukto mukta ityucyate / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'The recollection of wholesome mental and mental-factor states, and having recollected, dedicating [them] to awakening — this is skill in the past. Whatever acceptance of future roots of merit, the directing toward awakening as application [of the thought] "whatever wholesome thought-moments will arise, I shall dedicate them to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening" — this is skill in the future.' Thus in detail. 'Having fulfilled the resolve of the renunciation of all things, through the force of the thought of renunciation, by that bodily action he has relinquished all possessions. Freed from the suffering of existence whose root is all possessions — [he] is called "liberated."' Thus in detail.

body.text: nanu ca ātmārthamapi kiṃcidrakṣitumucitamiti mātsaryaṃ nirākurvannāha-
body.translated_text: 'But surely it is fitting to keep something back even for one's own sake' — refuting this miserliness, he says —

children.text: sarvatyāgaśca nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇārthi ca me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The complete renunciation of all is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and my mind seeks <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: tyaktavyaṃ cenmayā sarva varaṃ sattveṣu dīyatām // Bca_3.11 //
children.translated_text: if all must be relinquished by me, better it be given to beings. // Bca_3.11 //

body.text: sarveṣāṃ sāsravātmabhāvādīnāṃ nirvāṇaṃ mokṣaḥ / tadarthi ca me manaḥ, tadarthi ca mama cittam / tyaktavyaṃ cediti / nirvāṇasamaye yadi sarvamātmabhāvādi avaśyaṃ parityajya yātavyaṃ mayā, tadā varaṃ sattveṣu dīyatām, kimanena mātsaryahetunā vidhṛteneti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Nirvāṇa</s>' — liberation — of all [things] including one's personal existence that involve outflows. 'And my mind seeks that' — and my mind is intent on that. 'If all must be relinquished' — if at the time of <s>nirvāṇa</s> everything including one's personal existence must necessarily be given up by me and departed from, then 'better it be given to beings' — what use in holding on to it through a motive of miserliness? This is the purport.

body.text: tasmādidamihānurūpamityāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, this is appropriate here — he says —

body.text: yaścāsukhīkṛtaścātmā mayāyaṃ sarvadehinām /
body.translated_text: 'And this self has been placed by me at the disposal of all embodied beings;

body.text: yathākāmaṃgamakāritāyāṃ niyukto mayāyamātmā kāyaḥ / sarvadehināṃ sarvasattvānāṃ kṛte / etadeva darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: this self — this body — has been engaged by me, made to go as [others] wish, for the sake of all beings — all sentient beings.' He demonstrates this very point saying —

body.text: ghrantu nindantu vā nityamākirantu ca pāṃsubhiḥ // Bca_3.12 //
body.translated_text: let them strike, let them revile constantly, and let them scatter me with dust! // Bca_3.12 //

children.text: krīḍantu mama kāyena hasantu vilasantu ca /
children.translated_text: Let them play with my body, let them laugh and amuse themselves;

children.text: dattastebhyo mayā kāyaścintayā kiṃ mamānayā // Bca_3.13 //
children.translated_text: my body has been given to them — why should I have this concern? // Bca_3.13 //

body.text: kārayantu ca karmāṇi yāni teṣāṃ sukhāvaham /
body.translated_text: And let them make [me] do actions that bring them happiness.

body.text: daṇḍādibhistāḍayantu vā, avarṇavādairjugupsantu, ākirantu ca pāṃsubhiḥ, dhūlibhiravakirantu / dattastebhyo mayā kāya iti, sarvaḥ sarveṇa mayā teṣāṃ parityaktaḥ, kiṃ mama samaviṣamacintayā? kārayantu karmāṇīti anavadyāni / etadevāha-
body.translated_text: Let them strike with sticks and such, let them revile with blame-speech, let them scatter — cast — dust upon [me]. 'My body has been given to them' — it has been entirely given up by me to them. What concern have I with fairness or unfairness? 'Let them make [me] do actions' — blameless ones. He says this very thing —

body.text: anarthaḥ kasyacinmā bhūnmāmālambya kadācana // Bca_3.14 //
body.translated_text: Let no harm ever come to anyone on account of me! // Bca_3.14 //

body.text: aniṣṭaṃ kasyacitprāṇino mā bhūt, māmāśritya kadācana, iha paratra vā //
body.translated_text: Let nothing unwanted come to any living being ever, on account of me — in this life or the next.

children.translated_text: For those whose angry or displeased mind arises on account of me,

children.text: teṣāṃ sa eva hetuḥ syānnityaṃ sarvārthasiddhaye // Bca_3.15 //
children.translated_text: may that very [attitude] always be a cause for the accomplishment of all aims! // Bca_3.15 //

body.text: yeṣāṃ kruddhā yeṣāmaprasannā vā matiścittaṃ bhavet, teṣāṃ kruddhāprasannamatīnāṃ sa eva hetuḥ syāt, kruddhā aprasannā matireva / puṃstvaṃ tu tacchabdasya hetusamānādhikaraṇatayā / sarvārthasiddhaya iti ātmaparābhyudayaniḥśreyasaniṣpattaye //
body.translated_text: 'For those whose angry' — for those whose displeased mind arises — for those of angry or displeased minds — 'may that very [attitude] be a cause': may the angry or displeased mind itself [be a cause]. The masculine gender [of <s>sa</s>] is because of co-referentiality with the word 'cause' (<s>hetu</s>). 'For the accomplishment of all aims' — for the attainment of worldly prosperity and supreme good for oneself and others.

children.text: abhyākhyāsyanti māṃ ye ca ye cānye 'pyapakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who will slander me, and others too who cause harm,
and likewise others who mock — may all become sharers in awakening! // Bca_3.16 //

body.text: abhyākhyāsyanti iti mithyāropitadoṣeṇa dūṣayiṣyanti / anye 'pi ye kāyikaṃ mānasikaṃ vā apakāraṃ kariṣyanti / utprāsakā iti upahāsakāḥ, viḍambakāriṇo vā / tathā anye 'pi udāsīnāḥ prasannāśca / sarve bhaveyurbuddhatvalābhinaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Will slander' — will accuse with falsely attributed faults. 'Others too' — those who will do physical or mental harm. 'Mockers' — those who ridicule, or who caricature. 'Likewise others' — the indifferent and the faithful too. May all become attainers of <s>Buddhahood</s>.

children.translated_text: May I be a protector of the protectorless, a caravan-leader for travelers,

children.text: pārepsūnāṃ ca naubhūtaḥ setuḥ saṃkrama eva ca // Bca_3.17 //
children.translated_text: and for those wishing to cross, may I be a boat, a bridge, and a causeway! // Bca_3.17 //

body.text: anāthānāmiti sāṃnāyyānveṣiṇām / sārthavāhaśca yāyināmiti sārthamukhyo mārgaprapannānām / pārepsūnāmiti nadyādīnāṃ pārimakūlaṃ gantukāmānām //
body.translated_text: 'Of the protectorless' — of those seeking a protector. 'A caravan-leader for travelers' — the chief of a caravan for those set upon the road. 'For those wishing to cross' — for those wishing to go to the far bank of rivers and such.

children.translated_text: May I be a lamp for those seeking a lamp, a bed for those seeking a bed,
and may I be a servant for those seeking a servant — for all embodied beings! // Bca_3.18 //

body.text: dīpārthināmiti andhakārāvasthitānām / śayyārthināmiti śayanābhilāṣiṇām / dāsārthināmiti upasthānārthaṃ ye bhṛtyakarmakarādīnicchanti //
body.translated_text: 'For those seeking a lamp' — for those situated in darkness. 'For those seeking a bed' — for those desiring a place to sleep. 'For those seeking a servant' — for those who desire attendants, hired workers, and so forth for service.

children.translated_text: May I be a wish-fulfilling jewel, an auspicious vase, a perfected <s>vidyā</s>, a great medicine,
and may I be a wish-fulfilling tree and a wish-granting cow for embodied beings! // Bca_3.19 //

body.text: cintāmaṇiriti cintitaphaladātā ratnaviśeṣaḥ / bhadraghaṭa iti yadyadvastu abhilaṣitamabhisaṃdhāya asmin hastaṃ prakṣipet, tatsarvaṃ saṃpadyate / siddhavidyeti siddhamantraḥ yadyatkarma tayā kriyate, tatsarvaṃ sidhyati / mahauṣadhiriti yadekaiva sarvopadravapīḍāpraśamanahetuḥ / kalpavṛkṣaśceti kalpitārthasaṃpādako vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ / kāmadhenuśceti yā vāñchitadohaṃ duhyate //
body.translated_text: 'Wish-fulfilling jewel' — a special kind of jewel that grants the fruit of whatever is thought. 'Auspicious vase' — into which, having intended whatever object is desired, if one thrusts one's hand, all of it materializes. 'Perfected <s>vidyā</s>' — a perfected <s>mantra</s>; whatever action is performed by it, all of it succeeds. 'Great medicine' — that which alone is the cause of pacifying all calamities and afflictions. 'Wish-fulfilling tree' — a special kind of tree that produces whatever is wished for. 'Wish-granting cow' — [a cow] that is milked for whatever [milk] is desired.

children.translated_text: Just as earth and the other elements serve in many ways
as enjoyments for the measureless beings dwelling throughout all space — // Bca_3.20 //
so may I become a source of livelihood in many ways
for the realm of beings extending to the limit of space, until all are liberated! // Bca_3.21 //

body.text: pṛthivyādīnīti pṛthivī vasaṃdharā / ādiśabdādāpastejo vāyuriti catvāri mahābhūtāni / tāni yathā śayanāśanasasyaphalamūlādyādhāratayā , tathā yānāvagāhanādihetutayā / evamanyatrāpi yojyam / anantākāśadhatuvyāpināmasaṃkhyānāṃ sattvānāṃ paribhogamupayānti, evameva ahamapi sarvasattvānāmanekaprakāreṇa upabhogyo bhaveyam / yāvatsarve na nirvṛtā iti yāvat sarve na saṃsāraduḥkhavinirmuktāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Earth and the other elements' — earth, the ground-supporter. 'The other' [elements] by the word 'and so forth' — water, fire, and wind: the four great elements. They provide enjoyment to innumerable beings pervading the infinite space-realm, as the support of beds, food, crops, fruits, and roots, and as the cause of conveyances, bathing, and so forth. Similarly in other [cases] also it should be construed. Even so, 'may I too become enjoyable by all beings in many ways.' 'Until all are liberated' — until all are freed from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: tasmādeṣāmātmabhāvādīnāmutsargaḥ kāryo bodhyarthinā / etacca dānamativistareṇa śikṣāsamuccaye pradarśitam / tadyathā tatraiva bodhisattvaprātimokṣe kathitam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, this relinquishment of one's personal existence and so forth should be done by the aspirant to awakening. This giving has been shown at great length in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>. As stated there in the Bodhisattva-<s>prātimokṣa</s> —

body.text: punaraparaṃ śāriputra bodhisattvaḥ sarvadharmeṣu parakīyasaṃjñāmutpādayati, na kaṃcidbhāvamupādatte / tatkasya hetoḥ? upādānaṃ hi bhayamiti /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> generates the perception of [all things as] belonging to others regarding all <s>dharmas</s>; he does not appropriate any thing. For what reason? Because appropriation is fear.'

body.text: idamuktvā tatraiva punaridamuktam-
body.translated_text: Having said this, it was further said there —

body.text: tathā cittaśūrāḥ khalu punaḥ śāriputra bodhisattvā bhavanti / yāvat svahastaparityāgī bhavati, pādaparityāgī nāsāparityāgī śīrṣaparityāgī aṅgapratyaṅgaparityāgī, yāvat sarvasvaparityāgīti //
body.translated_text: 'Such indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, are <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are heroes of mind: one who gives up his own hands, one who gives up feet, one who gives up nose, one who gives up head, one who gives up [all] limbs and sub-limbs — even one who gives up all his possessions.'

body.text: evaṃ nārāyaṇaparipṛcchāyāmapyabhihitam-
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated in the <s>Nārāyaṇaparipṛcchā</s> as well —

body.text: na taddhastu upādātavyaṃ yasmin vastuni nāsya tyāgacittamutpadyeta, na tyāgabuddhiḥ krameta,
body.translated_text: 'There is no object to be appropriated regarding which no thought of relinquishment arises in him, [regarding which] no disposition toward renunciation would proceed

body.text: iti yāvat, api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam- ayaṃ mamātmabhāvaḥ sarvasattvebhya utsṛṣṭaḥ parityaktaḥ, prāgeva bāhyāni vastūni / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: ' — and so forth. 'Rather, O son of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should generate this thought: "This personal existence of mine has been released and given up to all beings — how much more external things!"' Thus in detail.

body.text: tathā āryākṣayamatisūtre 'pi deśitam-
body.translated_text: Likewise it is taught in the <s>Āryākṣayamatisūtra</s> —

body.text: ayaṃ mayā kāyaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ kiṃkaraṇīyeṣu kṣapitavyaḥ / tadyathā imāni catvāri mahābhūtāni pṛthivīdhāturabdhātustejodhāturvāyudhātuśca nānāsukhaiḥ nānāparyāyaiḥ nānārambaṇaiḥ nānopakaraṇaiḥ nānāparibhogaiḥ sattvānāmupabhogaṃ gacchanti, evameva ahamimaṃ caturmahābhūtasamucchrayaṃ kāyaṃ nānāsukhaiḥ nānāparyāyaiḥ nānārambaṇaiḥ nānopakaraṇaiḥ nānāparibhogairvistareṇa sarvasattvānāmupajīvyaṃ kariṣyāmīti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'This body of mine should be spent in service to all beings. Just as these four great elements — the earth element, water element, fire element, and wind element — provide enjoyment for beings through various happinesses, various methods, various supports, various implements, and various uses, even so I shall make this body — a composite of the four great elements — extensively available as a source of livelihood for all beings through various happinesses, various methods, various supports, various implements, and various uses.' Thus in detail.

body.text: taccittaratnentyārabhya sarvamidaṃ pūrvakaṃ bodhicittasaṃvaragrahaṇāya prayogo veditavyaḥ / tadevaṃ pūjādi vidhāya ātmabhāvādidānamutsṛjya pratipannabodhicittānuśaṃsaḥ kṣaṇasaṃpadaṃ paramadurlabhāmavetya śraddhāmūlaṃ dṛḍhamupasthāpya sattvānatrāṇānaparāyaṇān karuṇāyamānaḥ svasukhanirapekṣaḥ paraduḥkhaduḥkhī tatsamuddharaṇāśayābhiprāyo buddhatvameva tadupāyaṃ samutpaśyan tatra baddhasaṃnāhaḥ-
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'for that jewel-mind' [Bca 2.1], all this preceding [material] should be understood as a preparation for taking the <s>bodhicitta</s> vow. Thus, having performed worship and so forth, having relinquished the gift of one's personal existence and so forth, having understood the benefits of <s>bodhicitta</s> realized [through practice], having recognized the moment of opportunity as supremely rare, having firmly established the root of faith, generating compassion for beings who are without a protector and without a refuge, without concern for one's own happiness, suffering at others' suffering, with the intention and aim of rescuing them, seeing <s>Buddhahood</s> itself as the means for that, having bound on the armor for that purpose —

children.text: yadātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ ca bhayaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca na priyam /
children.translated_text: 'Since fear and suffering are not dear to myself or to others,

children.text: tadātmanaḥ ko viśeṣo yattaṃ rakṣāmi netaram //
children.translated_text: what distinction is there in myself that I protect it and not the other?'

body.text: iti / [śikṣa.sa.kārikā-1]
body.translated_text: [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 1]

body.text: tena ātmanaḥ sattvadhātośca-
body.translated_text: Therefore, for oneself and for the realm of beings —

children.translated_text: 'By one who wishes to put an end to suffering, by one who wishes to attain happiness,
having made the root of faith firm, one should make the mind firm toward awakening.'

body.text: iti // [śikṣa.sa.kārikā-2]
body.translated_text: [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 2]

body.text: samyaksaṃbodhicittamutpādayitumupakramate-
body.translated_text: He undertakes to generate the mind of perfect, complete awakening —

children.translated_text: Just as <s>bodhicitta</s> was taken by the <s>Sugatas</s> of old,
and just as they dwelt in succession in the training of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — // Bca_3.22 //

body.text: yenāśayena sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhaprahāṇārtham / yadi vā yathā gṛhītaṃ tadeva bhagavanto jānanti / bodhicittamiti bodhirbuddhatvaṃ sarvāvaraṇaprahāṇāt sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatādhigamaḥ / etacca sapracayaṃ prajñāparicchede vakṣyāmaḥ / tatra cittamadhyāśayena tatprāptaye manasikāraḥ buddho bhaveyaṃ sarvasattvahitasukhasaṃpādanāyetyarthaḥ // iti pūrvārdhena bodhicittotpādaṃ pratipādya śikṣāsaṃvaragrahaṇaṃ pratipādayannāha- te bodhisattvetyādi / bodhisattvaśikṣā yadutpāditabodhicittena bodhisattvena sadā karaṇīyam, tatretyarthaḥ / ānupūrvīti anu..........
body.translated_text: With the aspiration for the purpose of removing all suffering of all beings. Or alternatively, 'just as it was taken' — that itself is known by the Blessed Ones. '<s>Bodhicitta</s>' — <s>Bodhi</s> is <s>Buddhahood</s>: the realization of the non-inherent-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> through the abandonment of all obscurations. This we shall explain with elaboration in the chapter on wisdom. 'Mind' (<s>citta</s>) there [means] mental attention through aspiration for attaining that: 'may I become a <s>Buddha</s> for the purpose of accomplishing the welfare and happiness of all beings' — that is the meaning. Having presented the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> through the first half [of the verse], he presents the taking of the training-vow saying 'they, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' etc. '<s>Bodhisattva</s> training' — that which one who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, should always do — in that: this is the meaning. 'In succession' — in order...

body.text: tadvadutpādayāmyeṣa bodhicittaṃ jagaddhite /
body.translated_text: So likewise I generate <s>bodhicitta</s> for the welfare of the world;

body.text: tadvadeva ca tāḥ śikṣāḥ śikṣiṣyāmi yathākramam // Bca_3.23 //
body.translated_text: and so likewise I shall train in those trainings in due order. // Bca_3.23 //

children.translated_text: Having wisely taken <s>bodhicitta</s> thus, out of faith,

children.text: punaḥ puṣṭasya puṣṭayarthaṃ cittamevaṃ praharṣayet // Bca_3.24 //
children.translated_text: one should, for the purpose of further nourishing it, gladden the mind in this way: // Bca_3.24 //

children.text: adya me saphalaṃ janma sulabdho mānuṣo bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Today my birth is fruitful; well-obtained is [this] human existence!

children.text: adya buddhakule jāto buddhaputro 'smi sāṃpratam // Bca_3.25 //
children.translated_text: Today I am born in the family of <s>Buddhas</s>; I am now a son of the <s>Buddha</s>! // Bca_3.25 //
Henceforth I must act in a manner befitting those who act worthily of their family,

children.text: nirmalasya kulasyāsya kalaṅko na bhavedyathā // Bca_3.26 //
children.translated_text: so that no stain may come upon this stainless family. // Bca_3.26 //
Just as a blind man might find a jewel in a heap of refuse,
so too, somehow, this <s>bodhicitta</s> has arisen in me. // Bca_3.27 //
'This elixir has arisen for the destruction of the death of the world;
this is the inexhaustible treasure that pacifies the poverty of the world. // <s>Bca</s> 3.28 //
This is the supreme medicine that pacifies the diseases of the world;
it is the wish-fulfilling tree of rest for the world, weary from wandering on the road of existence. // <s>Bca</s> 3.29 //
It is the bridge common to all travelers for crossing over from the lower realms;
the moon of the mind has risen, pacifying the defilements of the world. // <s>Bca</s> 3.30 //
It is the great sun that dispels the darkness of the world's ignorance;
the fresh butter arisen from the churning of the milk of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 3.31 //
For the caravan of people journeying on the road of existence, hungry for the enjoyment of happiness,
this resting-house of happiness is prepared, satisfying all beings who have arrived. // <s>Bca</s> 3.32 //

children.text: jagadadya nimantritaṃ mayā sugatatvena sukhena cāntarā /
children.translated_text: Today I invite the world to the state of a <s>Sugata</s> and, in the meantime, to happiness;
before all the Protectors, may the gods, <s>asuras</s>, and others rejoice!' // <s>Bca</s> 3.33 //

body.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ bodhicittaparigraho nāma tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the third chapter, called 'The Embracing of <s>Bodhicitta</s>' (<s>Bodhicittaparigraha</s>), in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.

body.text: 4. bodhicittāpramādo nāma caturthaḥ paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter 4: The Chapter Called 'Heedfulness Regarding <s>Bodhicitta</s>' (<s>Bodhicittāpramāda</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Having thus firmly grasped <s>bodhicitta</s>, a son of the Conquerors
should always make effort, unwearied, not to transgress the trainings. // <s>Bca</s> 4.1 //
That which was hastily undertaken, not properly considered —

children.text: tatra kuryānna vetyevaṃ pratijñāyāpi yujyate // Bca_4.2 //
children.translated_text: regarding that, it is fitting even to deliberate: "Shall I do it or not?" // <s>Bca</s> 4.2 //
But that which has been examined by the <s>Buddhas</s>, by their sons of great wisdom,

children.text: mayāpi ca yathāśakti tatra kiṃ parilambyate // Bca_4.3 //
children.translated_text: and by me too according to my ability — why would one delay in that? // <s>Bca</s> 4.3 //

children.text: yadi caivaṃ pratijñāya sādhayeyaṃ na karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: If, having pledged thus, I should not accomplish it in action,

children.text: etāṃ sarvāṃ visaṃvādya kā gatirme bhaviṣyati // Bca_4.4 //
children.translated_text: having deceived all these [beings], what will be my destiny? // <s>Bca</s> 4.4 //
A person who, having merely thought in his mind, does not then give —
he becomes a hungry ghost (<s>preta</s>), it is said, even regarding a small thing. // <s>Bca</s> 4.5 //
How much more so [for one who], having loudly proclaimed the unsurpassed happiness with genuine [intent],

children.text: jagatsarvaṃ visaṃvādya kā gatirme bhaviṣyati // Bca_4.6 //
children.translated_text: deceives the entire world — what will be my destiny? // <s>Bca</s> 4.6 //
Only the Omniscient One knows this inconceivable course of <s>karma</s> —
that even one who abandons <s>bodhicitta</s>, he still liberates those people. // <s>Bca</s> 4.7 //
Therefore, for a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, every transgression is thus most serious,
since, by transgressing, he works harm to the welfare of all beings. // <s>Bca</s> 4.8 //
And whoever else obstructs his merit even for an instant —
for that destroyer of the welfare of beings, there is no end to lower rebirths. // <s>Bca</s> 4.9 //

children.text: ekasyāpi hi sattvasya hitaṃ hatvā hato bhavet /
children.translated_text: For one who destroys the welfare of even a single being would be destroyed;
how much more so [for destroying the welfare] of all embodied beings dwelling to the limits of space! // <s>Bca</s> 4.10 //
Thus, tossed about in <s>saṃsāra</s> by the force of transgression and the force of <s>bodhicitta</s>,
one delays long in the attainment of the stages. // <s>Bca</s> 4.11 //
Therefore, I should accomplish with care what I have pledged;

children.text: nādya cetkriyate yatnastalenāsmi talaṃ gataḥ // Bca_4.12 //
children.translated_text: if effort is not made today, I have gone from lower to lower [depths]. // <s>Bca</s> 4.12 //
Innumerable <s>Buddhas</s> have passed, who sought out all beings;
through my own faults, I did not come within the range of their healing. // <s>Bca</s> 4.13 //

children.text: adyāpi cettathaiva syāṃ yathaivāhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: If even now I should remain as I have been, again and again
