I would obtain lower rebirths, disease, death, cutting, and splitting. // <s>Bca</s> 4.14 //
When shall I obtain [these], so exceedingly rare — the arising of a <s>Tathāgata</s>,
faith, human birth, and fitness for the practice of virtue? // <s>Bca</s> 4.15 //

body.text: ārogyaṃ divasaṃ cedaṃ sabhaktaṃ nirupadravam /
body.translated_text: 'This day of health, with food, without misfortune —

body.text: āyuḥkṣaṇaṃ visaṃvādi kāyopācitakopamaḥ // Bca_4.16 //
body.translated_text: life is momentary and deceptive, the body is like a thing on loan. // <s>Bca</s> 4.16 //

children.translated_text: Through such conduct of mine, human birth will not be obtained again;

children.text: alabhyamāne mānuṣye pāpameva kutaḥ śubham // Bca_4.17 //
children.translated_text: and if human birth is not obtained, there is only sin — whence any good? // <s>Bca</s> 4.17 //
When, even though fit for virtue, I do not perform virtue,

children.text: apāyaduḥkhaiḥ saṃmūḍhaḥ kiṃ kariṣyāmyahaṃ tadā // Bca_4.18 //
children.translated_text: what shall I do then, when I am stupefied by the sufferings of the lower realms? // <s>Bca</s> 4.18 //
For one who does not perform virtue and accumulates sin —
even the word "happy destiny" is destroyed for hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 4.19 //
Therefore the Blessed One has said that human birth is exceedingly rare,
like the [chance of] a turtle's neck entering a hole in a yoke floating in a great ocean. // <s>Bca</s> 4.20 //
From sin committed in a single instant, one dwells in <s>Avīci</s> for a <s>kalpa</s>;

children.text: anādikālopacitāt pāpāt kā sugatau kathā // Bca_4.21 //
children.translated_text: from sin accumulated since beginningless time, what need to speak of a happy destiny? // <s>Bca</s> 4.21 //
And having experienced that alone, one is not freed;
for while experiencing that, yet other sin is produced. // <s>Bca</s> 4.22 //

children.text: nātaḥ parā vañcanāsti na ca moho 'styataḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no greater self-deception than this, and no greater delusion than this —

children.text: yadīdṛśaṃ kṣaṇaṃ prāpya nābhyastaṃ kuśalaṃ mayā // Bca_4.23 //
children.translated_text: that having obtained such a [rare] moment, I have not practiced virtue! // <s>Bca</s> 4.23 //

children.text: yadi caivaṃ vimṛṣyāmi punaḥ sīdāmi mohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if, having reflected thus, I again sink down, deluded,

children.text: śociṣyāmi ciraṃ bhūyo yamadūtaiḥ pracoditaḥ // Bca_4.24 //
children.translated_text: I shall grieve for a long time, urged on by the messengers of <s>Yama</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 4.24 //

children.text: ciraṃ dhakṣyati me kāyaṃ nārakāgniḥ suduḥsahaḥ /
children.translated_text: The unbearable fire of hell will burn my body for a long time;
and the fire of remorse will burn my untrained mind for a long time. // <s>Bca</s> 4.25 //
Having somehow obtained this beneficial ground, so hard to find —

children.text: jānannapi ca nīye 'haṃ tāneva narakān punaḥ // Bca_4.26 //
children.translated_text: even knowing this, I am led again to those very hells! // <s>Bca</s> 4.26 //

children.text: atra me cetanā nāsti mantrairiva vimohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Herein I have no intention — as if bewildered by spells;

children.text: na jāne kena muhyāmi ko 'trāntarmama tiṣṭhati // Bca_4.27 //
children.translated_text: I do not know by what I am deluded — who is it that dwells within me? // <s>Bca</s> 4.27 //
The enemies of craving, hatred, and the rest have no hands, feet, or the like;

children.text: na śūrā na ca te prājñāḥ kathaṃ dāsīkṛto 'smi taiḥ // Bca_4.28 //
children.translated_text: they are neither brave nor wise — how have I been made their slave? // <s>Bca</s> 4.28 //
Dwelling within my very mind, they kill me at their ease;
yet even at this I do not become angry — shame on such misplaced forbearance! // <s>Bca</s> 4.29 //

children.text: sarve devā manuṣyāśca yadi syurmama śatravaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all gods and humans were my enemies,

children.text: te 'pi nāvīcikaṃ banhiṃ samudānayituṃ kṣamāḥ // Bca_4.30 //
children.translated_text: even they would be unable to drag me into the fire of <s>Avīci</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 4.30 //

body.text: merorapi yadāsaṅgānna bhasmāpyupalabhyate /
body.translated_text: [A fire] at whose contact not even ash is found of [Mount] <s>Meru</s> —

body.text: kṣaṇāt kṣipanti māṃ tatra balinaḥ kleśaśatravaḥ // Bca_4.31 //
body.translated_text: these powerful defilement-enemies cast me there in an instant. // <s>Bca</s> 4.31 //

children.translated_text: For the lifespan of no other enemies is this long —
the long, great, beginningless and endless [lifespan] of my defilement-enemies. // <s>Bca</s> 4.32 //
All [others], when served agreeably, act for one's benefit;
but these defilements, when served, only cause more suffering. // <s>Bca</s> 4.33 //
While such constant, long-standing enemies, the sole cause of floods of misfortune,

children.text: hṛdaye nivasatsu nirbhayaṃ mama saṃsāraratiḥ kathaṃ bhavet // Bca_4.34 //
children.translated_text: dwell in my heart, how can I be fearlessly happy in <s>saṃsāra</s>? // <s>Bca</s> 4.34 //
These prison-keepers of the existence-cycle, these executioners even in hells —

children.text: mativeśmani lobhapañjare yadi tiṣṭhanti kutaḥ sukhaṃ mama // Bca_4.35 //
children.translated_text: if they remain in the cage of greed in the house of my mind, how can there be happiness for me? // <s>Bca</s> 4.35 //

children.text: tasmānna tāvadahamatra dhuraṃ kṣipāmi yāvanna śatrava ime nihatāḥ samakṣam /
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall not lay down this burden until these enemies are slain before my eyes;

children.text: svalpe 'pi tāvadapakāriṇi baddharoṣā mānonnatāstamanihatya na yānti nidrām // Bca_4.36 //
children.translated_text: those puffed up with pride, enraged even at a small offender, do not sleep without destroying him. // <s>Bca</s> 4.36 //

body.text: prakṛtimaraṇaduḥkhitāndhakārān / raṇaśirasi prasabhaṃ nihantumugrāḥ /

children.translated_text: heedless of the pain of arrows and spear-blows, do not turn back without accomplishing [their aim]. // <s>Bca</s> 4.37 //

body.translated_text: Those fierce ones, [eager] to slay in the front line of battle those who will die of natural death anyway,

children.translated_text: How much more so for one who undertakes to destroy the natural enemies, the constant cause of all suffering —

children.text: bhavati mama viṣādadainyamadya vyasanaśatairapi kena hetunā vai // Bca_4.38 //
children.translated_text: for what reason should I today have depression and dejection, even from hundreds of adversities? // <s>Bca</s> 4.38 //
Without any [real] purpose, people display the scars of enemies on their bodies like ornaments;

children.text: mahārthasiddhyai tu samudyatasya duḥkhāni kasmānmama bādhakāni // Bca_4.39 //
children.translated_text: when I have undertaken the great purpose, why should sufferings afflict me? // <s>Bca</s> 4.39 //
Fishermen, outcasts, farmers, and the like, their minds fixed on mere livelihood,

children.text: śītātapādivyasanaṃ sahante jagaddhitārthaṃ na kathaṃ sahe 'ham // Bca_4.40 //
children.translated_text: endure the miseries of cold, heat, and the rest — shall I not endure for the welfare of the world? // <s>Bca</s> 4.40 //
Having pledged to liberate the world from defilements, throughout all ten directions to the ends of space,

children.text: pratijñāya madātmāpi na kleśebhyo vimocitaḥ // Bca_4.41 //
children.translated_text: even my own self has not been freed from defilements. // <s>Bca</s> 4.41 //
Not knowing my own measure, I was then speaking as a madman;
therefore I shall be one who never turns back from the slaying of defilements. // <s>Bca</s> 4.42 //
Herein I shall be tenacious, hostile and combative,
except against that kind of defilement which accompanies the slaying of defilements. // <s>Bca</s> 4.43 //

children.text: galantvantrāṇi me kāmaṃ śiraḥ patatu nāma me /
children.translated_text: Let my entrails spill out! Let my head fall off!

children.text: na tvevāvanatiṃ yāmi sarvathā kleśavairiṇām // Bca_4.44 //
children.translated_text: But I shall never bow down to the defilement-enemies in any way. // <s>Bca</s> 4.44 //

children.text: nirvāsitasyāpi tu nāma śatrordeśāntare sthānaparigrahaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Even an exiled enemy might find a foothold in another land,

children.text: yataḥ punaḥ saṃbhṛtaśaktireti na kleśaśatrorgatirīdṛśī tu // Bca_4.45 //
children.translated_text: from which, having gathered strength, he might return — but the defilement-enemy has no such course. // <s>Bca</s> 4.45 //

body.text: nāya, na tu kleśaśatroḥ / na tasya itaraśatruvatsamācāro dṛśyate / kutaḥ punarevamicchayā labhyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: 'No,' [means] the defilement-enemy has not [such a course]. The conduct of other enemies is not seen in it. 'How then is it obtained merely by will?' he says:

children.text: kvāsau yāyānmanmanaḥstho nirastaḥ sthitvā yasmin madvadhārthaṃ yateta /
children.translated_text: 'Where would he go, that one expelled, dwelling in my mind? Where would he stand and strive to kill me?

children.text: nodyogo me kevalaṃ mandabuddheḥ kleśāḥ prajñādṛṣṭisādhyā varākāḥ // Bca_4.46 //
children.translated_text: It is only my dull-wittedness that [prevents] effort — the wretched defilements are to be overcome by the eye of wisdom!' // <s>Bca</s> 4.46 //

body.text: mama cittānnirvāsitaḥ asau kleśaripuḥ kutra gatvā avasthānaṃ kuryāt, yatrāvasthitiṃ kṛtvā mama vadhāya yateta? naiva tatsthānamutpaśyāmi, nirmūlitasya punarutthānāyogāditi bhāvaḥ / ahameva tu kevalamanutsāhī, apaṭubuddhipracāratvāt / kleśāḥ punarime nirmūlatvāt paramārthatattvadarśanamātrapraheyāstapasvinaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Where would this defilement-enemy, expelled from my mind, go? Where would he take up his stand and strive to kill me? I do not see such a place — since, once eradicated, it has no basis for arising again' — this is the sense. 'It is only I who lack enthusiasm, because my mental activity is dull. But these defilements are wretched things — they are to be abandoned merely by the seeing of ultimate reality, since they have no root.'

body.text: etadeva prasādhayannāha-
body.translated_text: Establishing this very point, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

body.text:
na kleśā viṣayeṣu nendriyagaṇe nāpyantarāle sthitā
nāto 'nyatra kuha sthitāḥ punaramī mathnanti kṛtsnaṃ jagat /
body.translated_text: 'The defilements do not dwell in sense-objects, nor in the collection of sense-faculties, nor in the interval between [them] — not dwelling anywhere else either, these [defilements] crush the entire world.' // <s>Bca</s> 4.47a-c //

body.text: manojñādiviṣayadarśane 'pi keṣāṃcitsaṃvṛtendriyāṇāṃ kleśānutpatteḥ paramāṇuśo vicāre 'pi tatrādarśanāt / na viṣayeṣu, nāpi cakṣurādīndriyagaṇe pūrvavat, dharmacintādyavasthāyāmindriyasadbhāve 'pyanupalabdheḥ / nāpi viṣayendriyayorantarāle madhye tiṣṭhanti, dṛśyānāmanupalabdhereva / na ca etebhyo 'nyasmin sthāne kvacidavasthitā niścitāḥ / ato nirmūlatayā tattvaśūnyā āgantukā eva, abhūtaparikalpamātraprasūtatvāt / tathābhūtā api jagadaśeṣaṃ mathnanti / tathā ca kimatra samucitamasti? āha-
body.translated_text: Because, even when encountering pleasant sense-objects and the like, defilements do not arise for some whose senses are restrained, and because upon atomic analysis they are not found therein — [they do] not [dwell] in sense-objects. Nor in the collection of sense-faculties such as the eye — as before, because even when the sense-faculties are present in states of <s>Dharma</s>-contemplation, [defilements] are not apprehended. Nor do they dwell in the interval, the middle, between sense-objects and sense-faculties — simply because visible things are not apprehended [there]. Nor are they ascertained to dwell in any other place beyond these. Therefore, being without root, empty of reality, adventitious only, produced merely from false conceptualization — yet such as they are, they crush the entire world. Then what is fitting here? He says:

body.text: māyaiveyamato vimuñca hṛdayaṃ trāsaṃ bhajasvodyamaṃ

children.translated_text: for the sake of wisdom! Why do you torment yourself needlessly in the hells?' // <s>Bca</s> 4.47d //

body.translated_text: 'This is nothing but an illusion — therefore release your heart [from fear], embrace effort

body.text: yathā hi māyā hastyākāratayā tadākāraśūnyāpi mantrauṣadhaprabhāvādidaṃpratyayatayā mantreṇa tattvarahitāpi pratibhāsate, tathā amī api kleśā viparyāsanimittā ayoniśomanasikārasamudbhūtā idaṃpratītyatāmātrato nistattvā eva prakāśante / ato vijahīhi hṛdaya trāsaṃ kleśebhyaḥ / ke nāma amī varākāḥ paramārthato vicāryamāṇāḥ? ato bhajasva udyamam, utsāhaṃ kuruṣva prajñārthaṃ tattvapravicayādhigamāya / kimakāṇḍa eva niṣprayojanameva narakeṣu saṃghātādiṣu kleśavaśagatayā ātmānamābādhase, pīḍayasi?
body.translated_text: Just as an illusion, in the form of an elephant, though empty of that form, appears through the power of mantras and herbs as having that appearance — reality-less yet appearing through dependent conditions — so too these defilements, caused by error, arisen from improper mental activity, appear through mere dependent conditionality, without any essence. Therefore, abandon the fear of defilements, O heart! What are these wretched things when examined from the ultimate standpoint? Therefore, embrace effort, exert enthusiasm for the sake of wisdom — for the attainment of the discernment of reality! Why do you needlessly, without purpose, torment yourself in the hells such as <s>Saṃghāta</s> and the like, under the power of defilements?

body.text: idānīṃ prāktanamarthamaśeṣamupasaṃharannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, summarizing the entire preceding meaning, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.translated_text: 'Having thus resolved, I shall make effort for the practice of the trainings as taught;
how can one who is curable by medicine have health, if one departs from the physician's instructions?' // <s>Bca</s> 4.48 //

body.text: evaṃ samanantarasakalaparicchedapratipāditamarthaṃ viniścitya dṛḍhīkṛtya anantaramāyāsvabhāvatāṃ vā, karomi yatnam / kimartham? yathoktaśikṣāpratipattihetoḥ, yathoktaśikṣā bodhisattvasya teṣu teṣu sūtrānteṣu yāḥ karaṇīyatayā pratipāditāḥ, ihaiva vā śāstre saṃkṣepeṇa tatra tatropadarśitāḥ, tāsāṃ śikṣaṇārtham //
body.translated_text: Thus, having ascertained and made firm the meaning presented in the immediately preceding complete chapter — or alternatively, the illusory nature [of all things] — 'I make effort.' For what purpose? 'For the practice of the training as stated' — the training of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> that has been presented in various <s>sūtras</s> as what must be done, and here also in this treatise has been indicated briefly in various places — for the purpose of training in those.

body.text: uktāni ca bhagavatā sūtrānteṣu bodhisattvaśikṣāpadāni / yathoktamāryaratnameghe-
body.translated_text: And the training-rules of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> have been stated by the Blessed One in the <s>sūtras</s>. As stated in the <s>Āryaratnamegha</s> —

body.text: kathaṃ ca kulaputra bodhisattvo bodhisattvaśikṣāsaṃvarasaṃvṛto bhavati? iha bodhisattva evaṃ vicārayati- na prātimokṣasaṃvaramātrakeṇa mayā śakyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum / kiṃ tarhi yānīmāni tathāgatena teṣu teṣu sūtrānteṣu bodhisattvasamudācārā bodhisattvaśikṣāpadāni prajñaptāni, teṣu mayā śikṣitavyam / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'And how, O son of good family, is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> restrained by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training-vow? Here a <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflects thus: "By the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> vow alone I am not able to awaken to unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening. Rather, whatever <s>Bodhisattva</s> conducts and <s>Bodhisattva</s> training-rules have been prescribed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the various <s>sūtras</s> — in those I must train."' Thus in detail.

body.text: tasmādasmādvidhena mandabuddhinā
body.translated_text: Therefore, for one of dull intellect such as myself —

body.text:
durvijñeyo vistaroktatvād bodhisattvasya saṃvaraḥ /
tataḥ kiṃ yuktam? marmasthānānyato vidyādyenānāpattiko bhavet /
[śikśā. sa. kārikā-3]
body.translated_text: 'The vow of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being hard to know because stated at length — what then is appropriate? One should know the vital points, by which one would be free from transgression.' [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 3]

body.text: katamāni ca tāni marmasthānāni? yaduta-
body.translated_text: And what are those vital points? Namely —

children.translated_text: 'The relinquishment of one's personal existence, enjoyments,
and merit of the three times to all beings — its protection, purification, and increase.'

body.text: śikśā. sa. kārikā-4
body.translated_text: <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 4

body.text: ityuktam / eṣa bodhisattvasaṃgraho yatra bodhisattvānāmabhyāsaviśrāme 'pi āpattayo vyavasthāpyante / yathoktaṃ bodhisattvaprātimokśasūtre-
body.translated_text: Thus it is said. This is the summary of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [vow], wherein transgressions are determined even in the pause from practice for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. As stated in the <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣasūtra</s> —

body.text: yo bodhisattvena mārgaḥ parigṛhītaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ kṛte duḥkhakṣayagāmī, sacedbodhisattvasya taṃ mārgaṃ parigṛhyāvasthitasya api kalpakoṭeratyayena ekaṃ sukhacittamutpadyeta, antaśo niṣadyācittamapi, tatra bodhisattvena evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam- sarvasattvānāmātyayikaṃ parigṛhya etadapi me bahu yanniṣīdāmīti //
body.translated_text: 'Whatever path has been taken up by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> leading to the destruction of suffering for all beings — if, for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has taken up and is established in that path, even after the passing of a <s>koṭi</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, a single thought of comfort arises, even so much as a thought of sitting down, then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should generate this thought: "Having taken upon myself the urgent [needs] of all beings, even this much — that I sit down — is a great deal for me."'

body.text: ata evāha- vaidyopadeśāditi / yathā vaidyopadeśamakurvāṇasya bhaiṣajyasādhyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ yasya bhaiṣajyena vā sādhyasya rogiṇaḥ kuto 'sti nirāmayatvaṃ nīrogatā? tathā sarvajñamahāvaidyopadiṣṭaśikṣāpratipattimakurvataḥ kuto nirāmayatvaṃ karmakleśopajanitajātyādiduḥdukhamahābhayādvimuktiḥ?
body.translated_text: For this reason he says 'because of the physician's instruction.' Just as for one who does not follow the physician's instruction, how can there be freedom from disease for one whose ailment is treatable by medicine? Similarly, for one who does not practice the training instructed by the great physician who is omniscient, how can there be freedom from disease — liberation from the great terror of suffering [consisting of] birth and so forth, produced by <s>karma</s> and defilements?

body.text: tadevaṃ samāttasaṃvarasya sāmānyamāpattilakṣaṇamucyate yena āpattilakṣaṇena yuktaṃ vastu svayamapyutprekṣya pariharet / na ca āpattipratirūpakeṣu anāpattipratirūpakeṣu ca saṃmuhyet / bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ vartamānānāgatasarvaduḥkhadaurmanasyopaśamāya vartamānānāgatasarvasukhasaumanasyotpādāya ca niḥśāṭhyataḥ kāyavāṅmanaḥparākramaiḥ prayatnaṃ na karoti, tatpratyayasāmagrīṃ
body.translated_text: Thus, for one who has taken the vow, the general characteristic of transgression is stated, by which characteristic of transgression, when the relevant situation [arises], one should oneself examine and avoid [the transgression]; and should not be confused regarding what resembles transgression but is not, and what resembles non-transgression [but is]. [If] a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the purpose of pacifying all present and future suffering and dejection of all beings, and for the purpose of producing all present and future happiness and cheerfulness, does not make effort sincerely through exertions of body, speech, and mind;

body.text: nānveṣate, tadantarāyapratīkārāya na ghaṭate, alpaduḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ bahuduḥkhadaurmanasyapratīkārabhūtaṃ notpādayati, mahārthasiddhayarthaṃ vā alpahāniṃ na karoti, kṣaṇamapyupekṣate, sāpattiko bhavati / saṃkṣepato 'nāpattiḥ svaśaktyaviṣayeṣu kāryeṣu, tatra niṣphalatayā śikṣāprajñaptyabhāvāt / prakṛtisāvadyatayā vā anyad gṛhyat eva / yatra tu svaśaktyagocare 'pi yogasāmarthyādāpattiḥ syāt, tanna cintyam, sāmānyapāpadeśanāntarbhāvāttato muktiḥ / etat samāsato bodhisattvaśikṣāśarīram / vistaratastu aprameyakalpaparyavasānanirdeśyam //
body.translated_text: does not seek the assemblage of conditions for that; does not endeavor to counteract obstacles to that; does not produce a small amount of suffering and dejection that would serve as a remedy for great suffering and dejection; or does not incur a small loss for the accomplishment of a great purpose; or is indifferent even for a moment — he incurs a transgression. In brief, there is no transgression in matters beyond one's own capacity, since there is no prescription of training for what would be fruitless in that case. Or, what is naturally blameworthy is to be understood separately. But where there might be a transgression even within the scope of one's own capacity through the power of [meditative] application — that should not be worried about, since liberation from it comes through inclusion in the general confession of evil. This is, in summary, the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training. In detail, however, it would require description extending over immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>.

body.text: athavā saṃkṣepato dve bodhisattvasyāpattī / yathāśaktyā yuktāyuktamasamīkṣyārabhate, na nivartate upekṣate vā, sāpattiko bhavati / nirūpya yathārhamatikrāmati antaśaścaṇḍāladāsenāpi coditaḥ, sāpattiko bhavati / yaḥ punaretadabhyāsārthaṃ vyutpādamicchati, tena śikṣāsamuccaye tāvaccaryāmukhamātraśikṣaṇārthamabhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ, śikṣaṇārambhasyaiva mahāphalatvāt / yathopavarṇitaṃ praśāntaviniścayaprātihāryasūtre-
body.translated_text: Or alternatively, in brief, there are two transgressions for a <s>Bodhisattva</s>: [1] without examining what is appropriate and inappropriate according to one's capacity, one undertakes [an action], or one does not desist, or one is indifferent — one incurs a transgression; [2] having examined, one transgresses what is proper — even when prompted by a <s>caṇḍāla</s> servant — one incurs a transgression. Now, one who desires proficiency for the purpose of practicing this should first make effort in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> for the purpose of training in at least the entrance to conduct, since even the mere beginning of training is of great fruit. As described in the <s>Praśāntaviniścayaprātihāryasūtra</s> —

body.text: iti bodhisattvaśikṣā samāsato yathopadeśataḥ kathiteti //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training has been stated in summary according to the instruction.

body.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ bodhicittāpramādaścaturthaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>, [named] '<s>Bodhicittāpramāda</s>' (Heedfulness regarding <s>Bodhicitta</s>).

body.text: 5. saṃprajanyarakṣaṇaṃ nāma pañcamaḥ paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: 5. The fifth chapter, named '<s>Saṃprajanyarakṣaṇa</s>' (Guarding Introspective Awareness).

body.text: evamātmabhāvādīnāmutsargaṃ rakṣāṃ ca pratipādya punarvistareṇa rakṣāśodhanavardhanāni pratipādayitumupakramate / utpāditabodhicittena hi bodhisattvena utsṛṣṭasyāpi cātmabhāvasya rakṣāśodhanavardhanāni kāryāṇi / yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Having thus presented the relinquishment of one's personal existence and so forth, and its protection, he now undertakes to present at length the protection, purification, and increase [thereof]. For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s> must perform the protection, purification, and increase even of the personal existence that has been relinquished. Because —

children.translated_text: 'One's personal existence and so forth are given for the enjoyment of beings;

children.text: arakṣite kuto bhogaḥ kiṃ dattaṃ yanna bhujyate //
children.translated_text: if unprotected, how can there be enjoyment? What is given that is not consumed?'
'Therefore, for the purpose of beings' enjoyment, one should protect one's personal existence and so forth,
through non-abandonment of spiritual friends and constant study of <s>sūtras</s>.'

body.text: śikśā. sa. kārikā 5-6
body.translated_text: <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verses 5-6

body.text: tacca ātmabhāvādiparipālanādi śikṣārakṣaṇādeva syāt / anyathā narakādivinipātagamanāt tanna syāt / ata idamabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: And that protection of one's personal existence and so forth would come from guarding the training alone. Otherwise, through falling into hells and so forth, it would not be [possible]. Therefore this is stated —

children.translated_text: By one who wishes to guard the training, the mind should be guarded with effort;

children.text: na śikṣā rakṣituṃ śakyā calaṃ cittamarakṣatā // Bca_5.1 //
children.translated_text: the training cannot be guarded by one who does not guard the unsteady mind. // Bca_5.1 //

body.text: śikṣyate upādīyate gṛhītasaṃvaraṇeneti vihiteṣu karaṇīyatā, pratiṣiddheṣvakaraṇaṃ śikṣā, tāṃ rakṣituṃ paripālayituṃ kāmena icchatā bodhisattvena ātmacittaṃ rakṣitavyaṃ prayatnata iti kathayiṣyamāṇāt / atha śikṣārakṣaṇādhikāre kimiti cittaṃ rakṣyata ityāha- na śikṣeti / anyathā śikṣaiva rakṣitumaśakyā calamanāyattaṃ cittamarakṣatā / cittasya calatāyāṃ śikṣāyāḥ sthairyāyogāt //
body.translated_text: 'Training' (<s>śikṣā</s>) — doing what is prescribed by one who has taken the vow, and not doing what is prohibited. By one 'who wishes to guard' — to protect — [this training], namely, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, one's own mind should be guarded 'with effort' — as will be explained. 'But in the topic of guarding the training, why is it the mind that is to be guarded?' He says 'the training cannot' etc. Otherwise, the training itself cannot be guarded by one who does not guard the unsteady, uncontrolled mind — because when the mind is unsteady, the training has no stability.

body.text: ito 'pi cittameva rakṣaṇīyamityāha-
body.translated_text: For this further reason too, it is the mind alone that should be guarded — he says —

children.text: adāntā mattamātaṅgā na kurvantīha tāṃ vyathām /
children.translated_text: Untamed, maddened elephants do not cause as much harm here
as a released elephant of the mind causes in <s>Avīci</s> and elsewhere. // Bca_5.2 //

body.text: aparikarmitā mattavaravāraṇā na janayanti tāṃ pīḍāmihaloke / paraloke avīcyādau yāṃ karoti svacchandatayāvasthitaṃ cittameva mataṅgaja eva / tathāgatājñāṅkuśena kathaṃcid vaśīkriyamāṇatvāt /
body.translated_text: Untrained, maddened excellent elephants do not produce as much affliction in this world as the mind alone — an elephant indeed — causes in the next world, in <s>Avīci</s> and elsewhere, when it stands according to its own whim. Because it is somehow brought under control only by the goad of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s command.

body.text: tasyāyattīkaraṇe guṇamāha-
body.translated_text: He states the benefit of bringing it under control —

children.translated_text: But if the elephant of the mind is bound on all sides by the rope of mindfulness,
all fear has set, and complete well-being has arrived. // Bca_5.3 //

body.text: yadi baddhaḥ kathaṃcid bhavet / smṛtirvakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇā / saiva rajjurbandhanopāyatvāt / samantataḥ sarvathā asatpakṣe pracāranirodhāt / tadā bhayamastaṃgataṃ pratyastamitaṃ sarvamaśeṣam / sarvaṃ kalyāṇamabhyudayaniḥśreyasalakṣaṇam / āgataṃ saṃprāptam / devaśced vṛṣṭo niṣpannāḥ śālaya iti yathā //
body.translated_text: 'If bound' — if somehow restrained. 'Mindfulness' — whose characteristics will be described. It itself is the 'rope' — because it is the means of binding. 'On all sides' — in every way, through preventing movement toward the unwholesome side. Then 'all fear has set' — has completely set, without remainder. 'All well-being' — characterized by worldly prosperity and supreme good. 'Has arrived' — has been attained. Just as [one says] 'if the god has rained, the rice has ripened.'

body.text: nanu bahavaśca mṛgavyālādayo 'pyupadravakāriṇaḥ santi, tebhyaḥ kathaṃ cittasya vaśīkaraṇād bhayaṃ na bhaviṣyatītyāha-
body.translated_text: Objection: 'But there are many harmful creatures such as deer, wild beasts, and so forth; how will there be no fear from them through the mastery of the mind?' He says —

children.text: vyāghrāḥ siṃhā gajā ṛkṣāḥ sarpāḥ sarve ca śatravaḥ /
children.translated_text: Tigers, lions, elephants, bears, serpents, and all enemies,
all guardians of hell, <s>Ḍākinīs</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s> likewise — // Bca_5.4 //
all these become bound by the binding of the one mind alone;

children.text: cittasyaikasya damanāt sarve dāntā bhavanti ca // Bca_5.5 //
children.translated_text: by the taming of the one mind alone, all become tamed. // Bca_5.5 //

body.text: subodham //
body.translated_text: This is easily understood.

body.text: kutaḥ punarevamityāha-
body.translated_text: From what [basis] is this so? He says —

children.translated_text: Because all fears and immeasurable sufferings
arise from the mind alone — thus it has been declared by the speaker of truth. // Bca_5.6 //

body.text: sarve hyete karmākṣepavaśādaniṣṭadāyakā bhavanti / karma ca cittameva / cetanā karmeti vacanāt / vākkāyakarmaṇorapi cittameva samutthāpakam / tadantareṇa tayoranutpatteḥ / cetayitvā karmeti vacanāt / tasmāt sarvamiha karmanirmitameva / tacca cittānnānyat / tadāha-
body.translated_text: For all these become givers of the unwanted through the force of <s>karma</s>-projection. And <s>karma</s> is the mind itself — because of the statement 'volition is <s>karma</s>.' Even of verbal and bodily <s>karma</s>, the mind alone is the instigator, since without it those two do not arise — because of the statement 'having willed, [one performs] <s>karma</s>.' Therefore, everything here is constructed by <s>karma</s> alone. And that is nothing other than mind. Thus it is said —

body.text:
karmajaṃ lokavaicitryaṃ cetanā tatkṛtaṃ ca tat /
cetanā mānasaṃ karma tajje vākkāyakarmaṇī /
iti /
[abhi. koṣa-4.1]
body.translated_text: 'The variety of the world is born from <s>karma</s>; volition is that, and what is done by it; volition is mental <s>karma</s>; verbal and bodily <s>karma</s>s are born from that.' [<s>Abhidharmakośa</s> 4.1]

body.text: na ca anapakāracittasya kecidapakāriṇo nāma / yasmāt-
body.translated_text: And for one whose mind is free from harm, there are no harmers at all. Because —

children.translated_text: 'For one whose evil mind has ceased, there is no fear of an enemy in the world;

children.text: sukhahānirna tasyāsti yasya cittaṃ vaśe sthitam //
children.translated_text: there is no loss of happiness for one whose mind is under control.'

body.text: ata idamuktam-
body.translated_text: Therefore this was said —

body.text:
cittasya damanaṃ sādhu cittaṃ dāntaṃ sukhāvaham /
iti /
[=dhammapada-25]
body.translated_text: 'The taming of the mind is good; a tamed mind brings happiness.' [= <s>Dhammapada</s> 25]

body.text: tattvavādī bhagavān vastutattvakathanaśīlatvāt / tenedaṃ tattvaṃ kathitaṃ prakāśitam- sarvaṃ cittaprasūtamiti / ataḥ sarvatra cittameva pradhānam //
body.translated_text: 'The speaker of truth' — the Blessed One, because his nature is to speak the truth of things. By him this truth was declared, illuminated — that all is born from mind. Therefore, in all [matters], the mind alone is primary.

body.text: itthamevaitannānyathā iti prasādhayannāha-
body.translated_text: Establishing that 'it is just so, not otherwise,' he says —

children.translated_text: By whom in hell were weapons fashioned with effort?

children.text: taptāyaḥkuṭṭimaṃ kena kuto jātāśca tāḥ striyaḥ // Bca_5.7 //
children.translated_text: By whom was the floor of heated iron [made]? And from where did those women arise? // Bca_5.7 //

body.text: narakapālānāṃ kuntāsimusalādīni, asipatravanasamudbhūtāni vā kena kṛtāni? na tatra kaścit kartāsti īśvarādiḥ, tatkartṛtvasya anyatra niṣiddhatvāt, ihāpi niṣetsyamānatvāt /
body.translated_text: The spears, swords, pestles, and such of the hell-guardians, or those arising from the <s>Asipattravana</s> (sword-leaf forest) — by whom were they made? There is no maker there such as <s>Īśvara</s> and so forth, since their being the maker has been refuted elsewhere, and will be refuted here also.

body.text: taptalohamayī ca bhūmiḥ kena ghaṭitā? tāśca striyaḥ kutaḥ kāraṇasāmagrīto jātāḥ, yāḥ pāradārikaiḥ śālmalīvṛkṣasya adhastādupari ca dṛśyante? sa ca śālmalirvā ? ato nānyat kāraṇamatra cittādupakalpanīyam / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: And by whom was the floor made of heated iron fashioned? And from what assemblage of causes did those women arise, who are seen below and above the <s>Śālmalī</s> tree by adulterers? And that <s>Śālmalī</s> tree [itself]? Therefore, no other cause should be imagined here than the mind. As stated —

children.translated_text: 'The mind alone constructs the world of beings and the container world, supremely marvelous;

children.text: karmajaṃ hi jagaduktamaśeṣaṃ karma cittamavadhūya ca nāsti //
children.translated_text: for the world has been declared to be entirely born from <s>karma</s>, and <s>karma</s> does not exist apart from mind.'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: madhyamakāvatāra-6.89
body.translated_text: <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> 6.89

body.text: tasmāccittamevātra kāraṇaṃ nānyadityata āha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, the mind alone is the cause here, nothing else — thus he says —

children.translated_text: All that is born from the evil mind — thus the Sage declared;

children.text: tasmānna kaścit trailokye cittādanyo bhayānakaḥ // Bca_5.8 //
children.translated_text: therefore, there is no one more frightening in the three worlds than the mind. // Bca_5.8 //

body.text: pāpakarmopaskṛtaṃ cittameva teṣāṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavān kathitavāt / nāparaṃ kiṃcit / yata evam, tasmānna trijagati pāpacittādaparaḥ kaścid bhayaheturasti / tasmāccittameva vaśīkartavyam / yaduktamāryaratnameghe-
body.translated_text: Because the Blessed One has declared that the mind conditioned by evil <s>karma</s> is the cause of those [hell-phenomena]; nothing else. Since it is so, therefore in the three worlds there is no other cause of fear than the evil mind. Therefore, the mind alone should be brought under control. As stated in the <s>Āryaratnamegha</s> —

body.text: cittapūrvagamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / citte parijñāte sarvadharmāḥ parijñātā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are preceded by the mind. When the mind is fully known, all <s>dharmas</s> are fully known.'

body.text: api ca-
body.translated_text: And further —

children.text: cittena nīyate lokaścittaṃ cittaṃ na paśyati /
children.translated_text: 'The world is led by the mind; the mind does not see [its own] mind;

children.text: cittena cīyate karma śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham //
children.translated_text: by the mind is <s>karma</s> accumulated — whether wholesome or unwholesome.'

body.text: cittaṃ bhramate alātavat / cittaṃ vibhramate taraṃgavat / cittaṃ dahate davāgnivat / cittaṃ rohayate (harate) mahāmbuvat / iti ca //
body.translated_text: 'The mind whirls like a firebrand; the mind surges like a wave; the mind burns like a forest fire; the mind carries away like a great flood.' Thus also.

body.text: evaṃ byupaparīkṣamāṇaścitte sūpasthitasmṛtirviharati, na ca cittasya vaśaṃ gacchati / api tu cittamevāsya vaśaṃ gacchati / cittenāsya vaśībhūtena sarve dharmā vaśībhavantīti //
body.translated_text: 'One who examines thus abides with mindfulness well-established regarding the mind, and does not come under the power of the mind; rather, the mind itself comes under his power. When the mind has come under his power, all <s>dharmas</s> come under his power.'

body.text: syādetat- dānapāramitādiṣu kathamiva cittaṃ pradhānam? sā hi sarvasattvānāṃ dāridyāpanayanalakṣaṇetyāha-
body.translated_text: One might ask: 'How is the mind primary in the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) and the rest? For that [perfection] is characterized by the removal of the poverty of all beings.' [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.translated_text: 'If the perfection of giving consists in making the world free from poverty,
since the world is still poor today, how did the former Protectors [attain] it? // <s>Bca</s> 5.9 //

body.text: dāridyaṃ hi nāma sāsravasukhabhogabubhukṣayā cittakārpaṇyam upakaraṇavaikalyaṃ vā / tadapanīya jagato yadi dānapāramitāparipūrirbhavatītyucyate, tadā sā katham? na kathaṃcidapi pūrvatāyināṃ pūrvamabhisaṃbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yujyate / kutaḥ? jagaddaridramadyāpi, nādyāpi yāvajjagaddāridyamupaśāmyati //
body.translated_text: For poverty means either the mental miserliness [produced by] craving for enjoyment of pleasures with outflows, or the deficiency of requisites. If the completion of the perfection of giving is said to consist in removing that from the world, then how [could it have been attained]? In no way at all does it apply to the former Protectors — the Blessed Ones who formerly attained awakening. Why? 'Because the world is still poor today' — because the poverty of the world has not been pacified even now.

body.text: yadyevaṃ neṣyate, kathaṃ sā bhavatītyāha-
body.translated_text: 'If it is not accepted thus, how does it [the perfection] come about?' he says:

children.translated_text: 'The perfection of giving is said to be the mind of relinquishing all possessions, together with the fruit, to all people;

children.text: dānapāramitā proktā tasmātsā cittameva tu // Bca_5.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore it is mind alone.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.10 //

body.text: sarvasvaṃ bāhyādhyātmikaṃ sarvaṃ vastu dānaṃ dānaphalaṃ ca sarvasattvebhyaḥ parityajato 'bhyāsena prakarṣagamanād yadā apagatamātsaryamalaṃ nirāsaṅgatayā cittamutpadyate, tadā dānapāramitāniṣpannetyucyate / tasmāt sā cittameva nānyā dānapāramitā //
body.translated_text: All possessions — all internal and external things — giving, and the fruit of giving too — [relinquishing these] to all beings: through the practice of relinquishing, when, by advancing to the highest degree, a mind free from the stain of miserliness arises through non-attachment — then the perfection of giving is said to be accomplished. Therefore, it is mind alone — there is no other perfection of giving.

body.text: śīlapāramitā tu sutarāṃ cittamevetyata āha-
body.translated_text: 'The perfection of morality is even more obviously mind alone' — therefore he says:

children.text: matsyādayaḥ kva nīyantāṃ mārayeyaṃ yato na tān /
children.translated_text: 'Where could fish and the rest be taken, so that I would not kill them?

children.text: labdhe viraticitte tu śīlapāramitā matā // Bca_5.11 //
children.translated_text: When the mind of abstention is obtained — that is considered the perfection of morality.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.11 //

body.text: prāṇātipātādisarvāvadyaviraticittameva hi śīlam, na punastadāśrayabhūtabāhyaviṣayanivṛttisvabhāvam / yadi punarvadhādiviṣayavastvabhāvena tadvadhādyabhāvācchīlaṃ syāt, tadā te matsyādayaḥ kva nīyantāṃ yatra teṣāṃ darśanaṃ na syāt? anyathā tadvadhādyupakrame śīlaṃ na syāt / na caivam / tasmātteṣu vidyamāneṣvapi labdhe viraticitte nivṛttimanasikāre śīlapāramitā matā saṃmatā tatsvabhāvavidām / tasmāt sā cittameva //
body.translated_text: For morality is the mind of abstaining from all faults such as killing and the rest — not [something whose] nature is the cessation of external objects that serve as the basis [for such acts]. If morality consisted in the absence of killing and such, due to the non-existence of the objects of killing and the like, then where would those fish and other [beings] be taken, where they would not be seen? Otherwise, when there is an occasion for their killing and such, morality would not exist. But this is not so. Therefore, even when they exist, when the mind of abstention is obtained — [that is,] when the mental disposition of renunciation [is present] — the perfection of morality is considered, agreed upon by those who know its nature. Therefore, it is mind alone.

body.text: kṣāntipāramitāpi na cittādbhinnetyāha-
body.translated_text: 'The perfection of patience, too, is not different from mind' — he says:

children.translated_text: 'How many evildoers, limitless as the sky, could I kill?

children.text: mārite krodhacitte tu māritāḥ sarvaśatravaḥ // Bca_5.12 //
children.translated_text: When the mind of anger is killed, all enemies are killed.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.12 //

body.text: parāpakārādisaṃbhave 'pi cittasyākopanatā kṣāntiḥ / anyathā yadi sarvaśatrūṇāṃ tadvinipātanena vairaniryātanaṃ kṛtavataḥ kenacidvairābhāvādupaśāntavairasya na kaścidapakārī syāt / iti marṣaṇaṃ kṣāntiḥ / tadā etadaśakyānuṣṭhānam / śatravo hi gaganasamatvādaparyantāḥ / teṣāṃ māraṇamaśakyam / tasmāt krodhādinivṛtticittameva teṣāmupāyena māraṇamiva, tatkṛtāpakārasyāgaṇanāt, janmāntaravairāsaṃbhavācca māritaprāyāste //
body.translated_text: Patience is the non-agitation of the mind even when harm from others and the like occurs. Otherwise, if through the destruction of all enemies, the repayment of enmity having been accomplished by someone, there would be no one to do harm — [since] the enmity is pacified by the absence of enemies — [and] if that patience, that forbearance, [were defined thus,] then this would be impossible to practice. For the enemies are infinite, being like the sky. Their killing is impossible. Therefore, the mind of cessation from anger and the like is, as it were, the killing of them through skillful means, because the harm done by them is not reckoned, and because enmity in future lives does not occur — thus they are as good as killed.

body.text: atra aśakyatāyāmapyupāyena pravṛttau dṛṣṭāntopadarśanena śakyatāmāha-
body.translated_text: Showing the possibility through a simile, even where [direct action] is impossible, when one proceeds by skillful means, he says:

children.translated_text: 'Where would there be enough leather to cover the entire earth?
With the leather of [one's] sandals alone, the earth is covered. // <s>Bca</s> 5.13 //

body.text: kaṇṭakādyupaghātarakṣaṇārthaṃ pṛthvī chādayitumucitā / na caitacchakyam, tāvataścarmaṇo 'bhāvāt, bhāve 'pi chādanasyāśakyatvāt / upāyena punaḥ śakyam / upānahaścarmaṇā kevalena sarvā bhūmiśchāditā bhavati //
body.translated_text: For the purpose of protection from the harm of thorns and the like, it would be fitting to cover the earth. But this is impossible — because of the non-existence of that much leather, and even if it existed, because the covering would be impossible. But through skillful means it is possible: with the leather of sandals alone, the entire earth becomes covered.

body.text: dṛṣṭāntoktamarthaṃ prakṛte yojayannāha-
body.translated_text: Applying the meaning stated through the simile to the subject at hand, he says:

children.text: bāhyā bhāvā mayā tadvacchakyā vārayituṃ na hi /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise, external phenomena cannot be restrained by me;
I shall restrain my own mind — what use are other things restrained? // <s>Bca</s> 5.14 //

body.text: śatruprabhṛtayo bhāvā mayā vārayitumaśakyāḥ / tadvat medinīcarmacchādanavat apakārakriyāyāḥ / ataḥ svacittameva śakyaṃ vārayiṣyāmi / anyavāraṇasyāpārthakatvāt, svacittavāraṇādeva tatsiddheḥ / tasmāt sā cittameva //
body.translated_text: External phenomena, beginning with enemies, cannot be restrained by me — like covering the earth with leather, [to prevent] the doing of harm. Therefore, I shall restrain my own mind alone, which can be [restrained]. Because restraining other things is purposeless, since from the restraint of one's own mind alone, that [purpose] is accomplished. Therefore, it [the perfection] is mind alone.

children.translated_text: 'The perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), whose nature is enthusiasm for the wholesome, is very clearly mind alone' — he says:
'Even together with speech and body, a mind of sluggish activity does not produce that fruit
which [is produced by] a keen mind alone — the attainment of <s>Brahmā</s>-hood and the like. // <s>Bca</s> 5.15 //

body.text: vacanakāyasahitasyāpi cittasya kuśalapakṣe mandapracārasya na tādṛśaṃ phalamupajāyate, yādṛśaṃ dhyānādiviṣaye paṭupravṛtterekākino 'pi cittasya phalaṃ brahmabhūyādikam / tasmāt sā cittameva //
body.translated_text: Even for a mind accompanied by vocal and bodily [activities], if its activity in the direction of the wholesome is sluggish, such a fruit does not arise as [that which arises] for a mind alone that is keenly engaged in the domain of <s>dhyāna</s> and the like — the fruit of attaining <s>Brahmā</s>-existence and the like. Therefore, it [the perfection] is mind alone.

body.text: dhyānaṃ tu cittaikāgratālakṣaṇaṃ cittādanyathā vaktumaśakyamityāha-
body.translated_text: '<s>Dhyāna</s>, whose characteristic is one-pointedness of mind, is impossible to describe as other than mind' — he says:

children.translated_text: 'Recitations and all austerities, even performed for a long time,
are in vain when the mind is distracted and sluggish — so says the Omniscient One.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.16 //

body.text: mantrādyāvartanalakṣaṇā vacanavyāpārā japāḥ / tapāṃsi ca indriyadamanalakṣaṇāḥ kāyikāḥ / tāni atibahukālamabhyastānyapi anyatra saktacittena middhādyupahatacittena vā / samānapāṭavavikalenetyarthaḥ / vṛthaiva niṣphalameva, atyarthakṛśaphalatvāt, abhimatārthe 'nupayogādvā / putro 'pyaputra eva, putrakāryākaraṇādyathā / ityāha bhagavān sarvajñaḥ / tasmād dhyānapāramitāpi cittameva //
body.translated_text: Recitations (<s>japāḥ</s>) are vocal activities characterized by the repetition of <s>mantras</s> and the like. And austerities (<s>tapas</s>) are bodily [practices] characterized by the restraint of the senses. Even when those are practiced for a very long time, with a mind attached to other things or impaired by torpor and the like — meaning, lacking equal keenness — they are in vain, that is, fruitless, because of yielding only meager fruit, or because of being useless for the intended purpose. Just as a son [who does not fulfill his duties] is as good as no son, because he does not do what a son should do. So says the Blessed One, the Omniscient One. Therefore, the perfection of <s>dhyāna</s>, too, is mind alone.

body.text: prajñā tu nirvivādā cittamevetyāha-
body.translated_text: '<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) is indisputably mind alone' — he says:

children.text: duḥkhaṃ hantuṃ sukhaṃ prāptuṃ te bhramanti mudhāmbare /
children.translated_text: 'Those who have not cultivated this secret mind, the essence of all <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: yairetaddharmasarvasvaṃ cittaṃ guhyaṃ na bhāvitam // Bca_5.17 //
children.translated_text: wander uselessly in the sky, seeking to destroy suffering and attain happiness. // <s>Bca</s> 5.17 //

body.text: pañcagatisaṃsārajātyādiduḥkhaṃ prahātuṃ tatprahāṇe nirvāṇasukhamadhigantuṃ te sattvā mudhā nirarthakā eva bhramanti ambare kāsīpuṣpamiva niṣphalaṃ saṃsāre / yadanuṣṭhitaṃ kvacidapi na lagnamiti tadevamamidhīyate pañcāgnisevāśiroluñcanādivratam / ke punarevaṃ bhramanti? yaiḥ saṃsārabhayabhīrubhiḥ sukhārthibhiśca dharmasarvasvaṃ sarvalaukikalokottarakarmanidānabhūtaṃ cittaṃ bālānāmagocarasvabhāvatayā guhyaṃ na bhāvitaṃ tattvacittatayā punaḥ punaḥ sthirīkṛtam / tasmādiyamatitarāṃ cittameva / yathopavarṇitamāryagaṇḍabyūhe-
body.translated_text: To abandon the suffering of birth and the like in <s>saṃsāra</s> through the five destinies, and to attain the happiness of <s>nirvāṇa</s> through that abandonment — those beings wander uselessly, fruitlessly in the sky, in <s>saṃsāra</s>, like a flower of the sky [i.e., something non-existent]. Whatever is practiced bears no fruit anywhere — thus it is called this way: the observance of the five fires, shaving the head, pulling out hair, and the like. Who then wander thus? Those who, fearful of the dangers of <s>saṃsāra</s> and desirous of happiness, have not cultivated the 'mind that is the essence of all <s>Dharma</s>' — the cause of all worldly and supramundane activities — 'secret' because it is beyond the domain of the ignorant — that is, have not repeatedly stabilized it through the mind [that contemplates] reality. Therefore, this is most especially mind alone. As described in the Noble <s>Gaṇḍavyūha</s>:

body.text: svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryā / svacittādhiṣṭhānaṃ sarvasattvaparipākavinayaḥ / peyālaṃ / tasya mama kulaputra evaṃ bhavati- svacittamevopastambhayitavyaṃ sarvakuśalamūlaiḥ / svacittameva parisyandayitavyaṃ dharmameghaiḥ / svacittameva pariśodhayitavyamāvaraṇīyadharmebhyaḥ / svacittameva dṛḍhīkartavyaṃ vīryeṇa / ityādi //
body.translated_text: 'The practice of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> depends on one's own mind. The ripening and discipline of all beings depends on one's own mind. [Abbreviated.] This thought occurs to me, O son of good family: One's own mind should be supported by all wholesome roots. One's own mind should be made to flow with the clouds of <s>Dharma</s>. One's own mind should be purified from obstructive <s>dharmas</s>. One's own mind should be strengthened by vigor.' And so forth.

body.text: iti cittasvabhāvatāṃ sarvatra pratipādya upasaṃharannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, having demonstrated the mind-nature [of all <s>pāramitās</s>] throughout, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] summarizes, saying:

children.translated_text: 'Therefore, my mind should be well-established and well-guarded;

children.text: cittarakṣāvrataṃ mukttvā bahubhiḥ kiṃ mama vrataiḥ // Bca_5.18 //
children.translated_text: apart from the vow of guarding the mind, what use are many vows to me? // <s>Bca</s> 5.18 //

body.text: evamutpāditabodhicittena śikṣārakṣaṇe yatnavatā manasi kartavyam- svadhiṣṭhitaṃ smṛtyā surakṣitaṃ saṃprajanyena vakṣyamāṇarītyā mayā svacittaṃ kartavyaṃ tadekāgramānasena / atraiva sarveṣāmantarbhāvāt / ataścittarakṣaṇameva pradhānaṃ vratam / tadvihāya kimanyairvratairbahubhirapi mama prayojanam? na kiṃcit / tadrahitasya niṣphalatvāt / etāvatī ceyaṃ bodhisattvaśikṣā yaduta cittaparikarma / etanmūlatvāt sarvasattvārthānām / tadyathā dharmasaṃgītisūtre kīrtitam-
body.translated_text: Thus, by one who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s> and is making effort in guarding the trainings, this should be kept in mind: 'My own mind should be well-established' — through mindfulness — 'and well-guarded' — through introspective awareness, in the manner that will be described — 'by me' — with a mind focused on this alone. Because all [trainings] are included within this very [practice]. Therefore, guarding the mind is the primary vow. Apart from that, what use are many other vows to me? None. Because without it, [they are] fruitless. And this entire <s>Bodhisattva</s>-training is nothing but the cultivation of the mind — because all aims for beings are rooted in it. As it is proclaimed in the <s>Dharmasaṃgītisūtra</s>:

body.text: mativikramabodhisattva āha- yo 'yaṃ dharmo dharma ityucyate, nāyaṃ dharmo deśastho na pradeśastho 'nyatra svacittādhīno dharmaḥ / tasmānmayā svacittaṃ svārādhitaṃ svadhiṣṭhitaṃ suparijitaṃ susamārabdhaṃ sunigṛhītaṃ kartavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ? yatra cittaṃ tatra guṇadoṣāḥ / tadbodhisattvo doṣebhyaścittaṃ nivārya guṇeṣu pravartayati / taducyate- cittādhīno dharmaḥ, dharmādhīnā bodhiriti //
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mativikrama</s> said: "This <s>Dharma</s> that is called '<s>Dharma</s>' — this <s>Dharma</s> does not abide in a place or a region; the <s>Dharma</s> depends on one's own mind alone. Therefore, my own mind should be well-propitiated, well-established, well-mastered, well-undertaken, and well-restrained. For what reason? Where the mind is, there are virtues and faults. Therefore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having turned the mind away from faults, directs it toward virtues. Hence it is said: the <s>Dharma</s> depends on the mind; awakening depends on the <s>Dharma</s>."'

body.text: evaṃ cittāyattatāṃ sarvatra niścitya cittadṛḍhatāyāmudāharaṇamāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus ascertained the dependence [of everything] on the mind in all respects, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] gives a simile for the firmness of [guarding] the mind:

children.translated_text: 'Just as one in the midst of a rough crowd carefully guards a wound,
so, in the midst of evil people, one should always guard the wound of the mind.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.19 //

body.text: asamāhitajanamadhye punarupaghātabhayāttadgatamanasā yathā vraṇaṃ rakṣati kaścidapramattaḥ, evaṃ tathā śikṣārakṣaṇakāmaḥ akāraṇavairibālajanamadhye saṃvasan tatparaścittaṃ vraṇamiva rakṣet sarvakālam //
body.translated_text: Just as, in the midst of unsteady people, someone, vigilant, with his mind focused thereon, guards a wound out of fear of harm — so too, one who wishes to guard the trainings, living among evil people who are enemies without cause, with his [mind] devoted to that, should guard the mind like a wound, at all times.

body.text: yathāprasiddhita idamudāharaṇam / na tu punarmanāgapi sādṛśyamastītyāha-
body.translated_text: 'This simile is given as a commonly known [illustration]. But it does not have even the slightest true similarity [to the case at hand]' — he says:

children.translated_text: 'Fearing the slight pain of a wound, I guard the wound with care;
fearing the blow of the crushing mountains [of <s>Saṃghāta</s> hell], should I not [guard] the wound of the mind? // <s>Bca</s> 5.20 //

body.text: īṣanmātraṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhalavo vraṇakṛtaḥ / tasmādbhīto rakṣāmi vraṇam / prakṛtānurodhe rakṣatīti pāṭho yuktaḥ / ādarāt tātparyeṇa / saṃghātanarakaprabhavādanekavarṣasahasrānubhūyamānaduḥkhāt parvatāghātātsarvato vyāptiprahārāt bhītaḥ cittavraṇaṃ na kiṃ rakṣediti prakṛtena saṃbandhaḥ / yadi vā / ahaṃ tu kiṃ na rakṣāmīti pariṇāmena yojanīyam / athavā / evamutpāditabodhicittena manasā cintayitavyamityavatāryate / tadā rakṣāmīti //
body.translated_text: A 'slight pain' means the small suffering caused by a wound — fearing that, 'I guard the wound.' The reading 'he guards' (<s>rakṣati</s>), conforming to the subject, is fitting. 'With care' means with diligence. 'Fearing the blow of the crushing mountains' — the suffering arising in <s>Saṃghāta</s> hell, experienced for many thousands of years, the blow of mountains that strike from all sides — fearing this, 'should one not [guard] the wound of the mind?' — this is the connection with the subject. Alternatively: 'But should I not guard it?' — this should be construed through a change [of person]. Or alternatively: 'Thus, by one who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, it should be reflected upon in the mind' — this introduces [the passage]. Then 'I guard' is [correct].

body.text: kaḥ punarevaṃ sati guṇaḥ syādityāha-
body.translated_text: 'What benefit would there be in doing so?' he says:

children.translated_text: 'For one who lives with this conduct, even among evil people,
even in the midst of attractive women, the steadfast ascetic does not break [his vow].' // <s>Bca</s> 5.21 //

body.text: yasmādevaṃmanasikāreṇa vicaran vanitājanamadhye 'pi prāsādapṛṣṭhe ayamanivāryo 'tiśayena kāmarāgeṣu / tenedamuktaṃ yatirdhīra iti / asmin manasikāre nidhyaptacittaḥ / na khaṇḍayate śikṣārakṣaṇamanasikārānna skhalati //
body.translated_text: Because, with such mental attention, even living among attractive women on the upper floor of a palace — this one, who is irresistible, exceedingly [firm] in matters of sensual desire. Therefore it is said: 'the steadfast ascetic' — that is, one whose mind is absorbed in this mental attention. 'Does not break' — does not slip from the mental attention of guarding the trainings.

body.text: punarevaṃ karaṇīyamityatrārthe dṛḍhamabhiniveśaṃ darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing firm conviction in the meaning that this should indeed be done, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.text: lābhā naśyantu me kāmaṃ satkāraḥ kāyajīvitam /
children.translated_text: 'Let my gains perish! Let my honor, body, and life [perish]!

children.text: naśyatvanyacca kuśalaṃ mā tu cittaṃ kadācana // Bca_5.22 //
children.translated_text: Let other virtue perish too — but never my mind!' // <s>Bca</s> 5.22 //

body.text: civarapiṇḍapātādayo naśyantu, vilayaṃ yāntu mama kāmaṃ yatheṣṭam / satkāro gauraveṇa āsanadānapādavandanādipūjā / kāyo jīvitaṃ ca sarvametannaśyatu / anyadapi yatkiṃcit sukhasaumanasyanimittaṃ tadapi naśyatu / kuśalaṃ punarmama cittaṃ mā kasmiṃścidapi kāle naṅkṣīditi //
body.translated_text: Robes, alms-food, and the like — let them perish, let them be destroyed, as they please. 'Honor' means worship through respectful offering of seats, bowing at the feet, and the like. Body and life — let all of this perish. And whatever else is a cause of happiness and mental pleasure — let that too perish. But my wholesome mind — let it never be destroyed at any time!

body.text: atra punarādaramutpādayituṃ śāstrakāra āha-
body.translated_text: Here again, in order to generate earnestness, the author of the treatise says:

children.translated_text: 'To those who wish to guard the mind, I make this entreaty with joined palms:

children.text: smṛtiṃ ca saṃprajanyaṃ ca sarvayatnena rakṣata // Bca_5.23 //
children.translated_text: guard mindfulness and introspective awareness with all effort!' // <s>Bca</s> 5.23 //

body.text: añjaliṃ kṛtvā prārthayāmi / kimartham? smṛtiṃ ca saṃprajanyaṃ ca / na kevalāṃ smṛtim, nāpi kevalaṃ saṃprajanyamiti parasparāpekṣayā cakāradvayam / tatra smṛtirāryaratnacūḍasūtre 'bhihitā-
body.translated_text: 'With joined palms, I entreat' — for what purpose? 'Mindfulness and introspective awareness.' Not mindfulness alone, nor introspective awareness alone — the two uses of 'and' (<s>ca</s>) indicate their mutual dependence. Therein, mindfulness is described in the Noble <s>Ratnacūḍasūtra</s> —

body.text: yayā smṛtyā sarvakleśānāṃ prādurbhāvo na bhavati / yayā smṛtyā sarvamārakarmaṇāmavatāraṃ na dadāti / yayā smṛtyā utpathe kumārge vā na patati / yayā smṛtyā dauvārikabhūtayā sarveṣāmakuśalānāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāmavakāśaṃ na dadāti, iyamucyate samyaksmṛtiriti //
body.translated_text: 'That mindfulness by which the manifestation of all defilements does not occur; that mindfulness by which one does not give entry to all the works of <s>Māra</s>; that mindfulness by which one does not fall onto a wrong path or a bad road; that mindfulness which, acting as a doorkeeper, does not give occasion to any unwholesome mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> — this is called right mindfulness.'

body.text: saṃkṣepataḥ punariyaṃ smṛtirucyate- vihitapratiṣiddhayoryathāyogaṃ smaraṇaṃ smṛtiḥ / yaccāhasmṛtirālambanāsaṃpramoṣa iti //
body.translated_text: In brief, again, this mindfulness is stated [thus]: 'The recollection, as appropriate, of what is prescribed and what is prohibited is mindfulness.' And it is said: 'Mindfulness is non-loss of the object.'

body.text: saṃprajanyaṃ tu prajñāpāramitāyāmuktam-
body.translated_text: Introspective awareness (<s>saṃprajanya</s>), however, is stated in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> —

body.text: caraṃścarāmīti prajānāti / sthitaḥ sthito 'smīti prajānāti / niṣaṇṇo niṣaṇṇo 'smīti prajānāti / śayānaḥ śayito 'smīti prajānāti / yathā yathāsya kāyaḥ sthito bhavati tathā tathainaṃ prajānāti / peyālaṃ / so 'tikrāman vā pratikrāman vā saṃprajānacārī bhavati / ālokite vilokite saṃmiñjite prasārite saṃghāṭīpaṭapātracīvaradhāraṇe aśite pīte khādite nidrāklamaprativinodane āgate gate sthite niṣaṇṇe supte jāgarite bhāṣite tūṣṇībhāve pratisaṃlayane saṃprajānacārī bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: 'Walking, he knows "I am walking." Standing, he knows "I am standing." Sitting, he knows "I am sitting." Lying down, he knows "I am lying down." In whatever manner his body is positioned, he knows it accordingly.' In abbreviated form. 'Going forward or returning, he acts with introspective awareness. In looking and gazing, in bending and stretching, in wearing the saṃghāṭī, upper robe, and bowl, in eating, drinking, chewing, in countering sleepiness and fatigue, in going, coming, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, being silent, and in meditation — he acts with introspective awareness.'

body.text: idameva vakṣyati-
body.translated_text: This very [point] will be stated —

children.translated_text: 'This alone, in brief, is the characteristic of introspective awareness:
the repeated examination of the state of body and mind.'

body.text: iti // [bodhi. 5.108]
body.translated_text: [<s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> 5.108]

body.text: kaḥ punaranayorvyatireke doṣaḥ, yenaite yatnena rakṣaṇīye kathite ityāha-
body.translated_text: 'But what is the fault in the absence of these two, such that they are said to require guarding with effort?' He says —

children.translated_text: Just as a man afflicted by illness is incapable of all actions,

children.text: tathābhyāṃ vikalaṃ cittaṃ na kṣamaṃ sarvakarmasu // Bca_5.24 //
children.translated_text: so a mind deprived of these two is incapable of all actions. // Bca_5.24 //

body.text: rogopahatasāmarthyo yathā puruṣaḥ sarvakarmasu gamanabhojanādiṣu akarmaṇyo bhavati, tathā smṛtisaṃprajanyābhyāṃ vikalaṃ cittaṃ sarvakarmasu dhyānādhyayanādilakṣaṇeṣu //
body.translated_text: Just as a person whose capacity is impaired by illness becomes incapable of all actions such as walking, eating, and so forth, so too a mind deprived of mindfulness and introspective awareness [is incapable] of all actions characterized by meditation, study, and so forth.

body.text: anayoḥ samudāyābhāve doṣamuktvā pratyekamabhāve kathayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Having stated the fault in the absence of their combination, he speaks of [the fault in] the absence of each individually —

children.translated_text: For one whose mind lacks introspective awareness, what has been heard, reflected upon, and cultivated
does not remain in memory — like water in a pot with holes. // Bca_5.25 //

body.text: na vidyate saṃprajanyaṃ yasmiṃstadasaṃprajanyam / taccittaṃ yasya tasya / śrutacintābhāvanāmayaprajñāpariniṣṭhitaṃ vastu na smaraṇamadhivasati / tanmūlaṃ ca sarvaṃ kalyāṇam / kimiva? yathā sacchidrakumbhe mukhanikśiptamudakamadhastādgacchati nāvatiṣṭhate //
body.translated_text: 'Lacking introspective awareness' — that in which introspective awareness does not exist. 'Whose mind is such' — for one of such a mind. What has been perfected through wisdom born of hearing, reflection, and meditation does not abide in recollection. And all that is good has that [recollection] as its root. Like what? Just as water poured into the mouth of a pot with holes goes down through the bottom and does not remain.

body.text: idamaparaṃ tadvayatireke dūṣaṇamāha-
body.translated_text: He states this further fault in the absence of those two —

children.translated_text: Many who are learned, even those with faith and devoted to effort,
become stained with transgressions through the fault of lacking introspective awareness. // Bca_5.26 //

body.text: bahavo 'pi bahuśrutāḥ tathā śraddhāvanto yatnaparāḥ śikṣāyāmādarakāriṇaḥ asaṃprajanyadoṣeṇa āpattikaluṣitā bhavanti kāyacittapracārāpratyavekṣaṇāt //
body.translated_text: Even those of much learning, likewise those of faith, devoted to effort, diligent in the training — through the fault of lacking introspective awareness, they become tainted with transgressions, because of not examining the conduct of body and mind.

body.text: aparamapi tadabhāve dūṣaṇamāha-
body.translated_text: He states yet another fault in its absence —

children.translated_text: By the thief of non-introspective-awareness, who follows the robbery of mindfulness,

children.text: upacityāpi puṇyāni muṣitā yānti durgatim // Bca_5.27 //
children.translated_text: even those who have accumulated merit go to lower rebirths, robbed. // Bca_5.27 //

body.text: asaṃprajanyameva saṃprajanyābhāvaḥ kleśasvabhāvaścauraḥ kuśaladhanāpaharaṇāt / tena smṛtimoṣānusāriṇā rakṣapālabhūtāyāḥ smṛteḥ pramoṣamabhāvamanusṛtya muṣitā viluptakuśaladhanāḥ santaḥ upacityāpi puṇyāni, kuśaladhanānāṃ saṃcayaṃ kṛtvāpi, durgatiparāyaṇā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Non-introspective-awareness itself — the absence of introspective awareness — being of the nature of defilements, is a 'thief,' because it steals the wealth of wholesome [qualities]. By it, 'following the robbery of mindfulness' — following upon, [that is,] after the loss of mindfulness which serves as the guardian — 'robbed' — those whose wealth of wholesome [qualities] has been plundered — 'even those who have accumulated merit' — even having made an accumulation of the wealth of wholesome [qualities] — become destined for lower rebirths.

body.text: kutaḥ punarevamiti uktamevārthaṃ spaṣṭayannāha-
body.translated_text: How is this so? Clarifying the meaning already stated, he says —

children.translated_text: This band of defilement-thieves seeks an entry;
having found an entry, it robs and kills the life of happy destinies. // Bca_5.28 //

body.text: taskarāścaurāḥ teṣāṃ saṃghātaḥ avatāragaveṣakaḥ piśācavadavatāramārgaprekṣī / chidrānveṣaṇatatpara ityarthaḥ / prāpyāvatāraṃ praveśamārgamāsādya muṣṇāti / tato hanti śobhanagataye jīvitapratilambhaṃ kuśalapātheyābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: 'Thieves' — robbers; their 'band' — assemblage. 'Seeking an entry' — watching for an entry-path like a demon. Intent upon seeking an opening — that is the meaning. 'Having found an entry' — having obtained a way in — 'it robs.' Thereby 'it kills the life' — the obtaining of life for a good destiny — because of the absence of merit-provisions.

body.text: smṛtimadhikṛtyādhunā prāha-
body.translated_text: Now he speaks with reference to mindfulness —

children.translated_text: Therefore, mindfulness should never be removed from the door of the mind;
even if gone, it should be re-established, recalling the suffering of lower rebirths. // Bca_5.29 //

body.text: yataḥ smṛterabhāve dūṣaṇamevaṃ syāt, tasmādidamatra doṣaṃ paśyatā smṛtirālabamnāsaṃpramoṣalakṣaṇā manodvārāt manogṛhapraveśamārgāt nāpaneyā nāpasāryā / sadā avasthāpayitavyetyarthaḥ / atha kadācit pramādatastato 'pagacchet, tadā gatāpi punarnirvartyopasthāpyā tatraivāropayitavyā / katham? saṃsmṛtya manasi nidhāya āpāyikīṃ narakādidurgativyathām //
body.translated_text: Since in the absence of mindfulness such a fault would arise, therefore — seeing this fault here — mindfulness, whose characteristic is non-loss of the object, should not be removed, not displaced, from the door of the mind — from the entrance to the house of the mind. It should always be stationed [there] — that is the meaning. But should it sometimes depart from there through heedlessness, then even when gone, it should be brought back and re-established, placed there again. How? By recollecting — placing in the mind — the suffering of lower rebirths such as hells.

body.text: tatra dvādaśemāḥ smṛtayo niṣphalaspandavarjanārthaṃ tathāgatājñānatikramānupālanavipākagauravasmṛtiprabhṛtayaḥ śikṣāsamuccaye pradarśitāḥ, tata eva vivekenāvadhāryāḥ //
body.translated_text: On this [topic], these twelve kinds of mindfulness — mindfulness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s command, mindfulness of non-transgression, mindfulness of the gravity of ripening, and so forth — have been shown in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>; they should be ascertained from there with discernment.

body.text: sāpi smṛtistībrādarātsamutpadyate / ādaro 'pi śamathamāhātmyamavagamya ātāpena jāyate / etacca yathāvasaraṃ vakṣyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: And that mindfulness arises from intense diligence. Diligence too arises through exertion, having understood the greatness of calm. This we shall state as occasion arises.

body.text: keṣāṃcit punaranyathāpi smṛtirutpadyate / tadupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: But for some, mindfulness arises in yet another way. Showing this, he says —

children.translated_text: Through the instruction of preceptors, and for those who act with diligence out of fear,
for the fortunate ones, from dwelling with a teacher, mindfulness easily arises. // Bca_5.30 //

body.text: ācāryopādhyāyasaṃnidhau tadanyatamārādhyabrahmacārisaṃnidhau vā saṃvasatāṃ tadanuśāsanyā, bhītya tadbhayenāpi ādaraḥ kāryeṣu sarvabhāvenābhimukhyam, avajñāpratipakṣo dharmaḥ / tatkāriṇāṃ yatnavatāṃ sukṛtināṃ tadanuśāsanīṃ hitāhitavidhipratiṣedhaniyamamanugṛhṇatāmakṛcchreṇaiva smṛtirutpadyate //
body.translated_text: In the presence of an <s>ācārya</s> or <s>upādhyāya</s>, or while dwelling in the presence of some other venerable fellow-practitioner, through their instruction — or even through fear of them — 'diligence' [means] complete engagement in duties, a quality that is the antidote to disregard. For those who do that — for the diligent, the meritorious ones — for those who accept that instruction, the regulation of what is beneficial and harmful, prescribed and prohibited — mindfulness arises without difficulty.

body.text: itthamapi viharan smṛtimanasikārabahulavihārī bhavatīti kārikādvayena darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing by means of two verses that one who dwells thus also dwells abundantly in the mental application of mindfulness, he says —

children.translated_text: <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> possess unobstructed vision everywhere;
everything is before them — I stand in their presence. // Bca_5.31 //
Reflecting thus, one should stand possessed of modesty, diligence, and fear;
recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> too will thus arise in him repeatedly. // Bca_5.32 //

body.text: sarvadā buddhabodhisattvānāṃ samastavastuviṣayāpratihatajñānacakṣuṣāṃ sarvameva vastujātaṃ purato 'vasthitameva / ahamapi teṣāṃ puro 'vasthita eva, sarvavastuvat / iti manasi nidhāya tathaiva saṃyatātmā tiṣṭhet / trapādarabhayānvitaḥ / apratirūpe karmaṇi trapā lajjā / śikṣāyāmādaraḥ, tadatikrame bhayam / buddhabodhisattveṣveva vā trapādayaḥ / evaṃ sati aparo 'pi viśeṣaḥ syādityāha- buddhetyādi / tadevaṃ viharatastasya pratikṣaṇamakāmata eva buddhānusmṛtiḥ syāt //
body.translated_text: At all times, the entire range of things stands before the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> whose wisdom-eye is unobstructed regarding all objects; and I too stand in their presence, like all things. Placing this in mind, one should stand self-controlled just so. 'Possessed of modesty, diligence, and fear' — 'modesty' (<s>trapā</s>) is shame at improper action; 'diligence' is care in the training; 'fear' is [fear] of transgressing it. Or modesty and so forth [may be directed] toward the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> themselves. 'If so, there would be yet another special quality' — he says '<s>Buddha</s>' etc. For one thus dwelling, recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> would arise at every moment, effortlessly.

body.text: saṃprajanyasya utpattisthairyayoḥ smṛtireva kāraṇamiti kathayannāha-
body.translated_text: Stating that mindfulness alone is the cause for the arising and stability of introspective awareness, he says —

children.text: saṃprajanyaṃ tadāyāti na ca yātyāgataṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Introspective awareness then comes and, once come, does not depart again,
when mindfulness stands at the door of the mind for the purpose of guarding. // Bca_5.33 //

body.text: yadā smṛtirmanogṛhadvāri kleśataskarasaṃghātānupraveśanivāriṇī dauvārikavadavasthitā bhavati, tadā saṃprajanyamayatnata evotpadyate, utpannaṃ ca sat sthirībhavati //
body.translated_text: When mindfulness stands stationed at the door of the mind's house — like a doorkeeper preventing the entry of the band of defilement-thieves — then introspective awareness arises effortlessly, and once arisen, becomes stable.

body.text: evaṃ tāvadanayoranvayavyatirekābhyāṃ guṇadoṣāvabhidhāya anarthavivarjanārthaṃ niṣphalaspandavarjanamāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, having stated the virtues and faults of these two through positive and negative concomitance, he speaks of avoiding fruitless agitation for the purpose of avoiding harm —

body.text: pūrvaṃ tāvadidaṃ cittaṃ sadopasthāpyamīdṛśam /
body.translated_text: First, then, the mind should always be instructed thus:

body.text: nirindriyeṇeva mayā sthātavyaṃ kāṣṭhavatsadā // Bca_5.34 //
body.translated_text: 'I should always stand as if without sense-faculties — like a block of wood.' // Bca_5.34 //

body.text: prathamaṃ tāvat idaṃ cittamityadhyātmani cintayati- sarvakālamīdṛśamuktakramayuktamupasthāpayitavyam / tataḥ paraṃ niṣphalaspandavarjanārthamapagatakaraṇagrāmeṇeva niṣphalarūpādiviṣayagrahaṇasarvavikalpopasaṃhārāt mayā sthātavyam / kimiva? kāṣṭhavat, cakṣurādivyāpāraśūnyatvāt //
body.translated_text: First of all, this mind — reflecting inwardly — should be instructed at all times in the manner stated in the proper sequence. Then, for the purpose of avoiding fruitless agitation — as if lacking the group of sense-organs — through the withdrawal of all conceptual proliferation regarding fruitless grasping of forms and other sense-objects — 'I should stand.' Like what? 'Like a block of wood' — because of the absence of the functioning of the eye and so forth.

body.text: idameva vyanakti-
body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very [point] —

children.translated_text: Fruitless glances of the eyes should never be made;
the gaze should always be directed downward, as if meditating. // Bca_5.35 //

body.text: īṣanmukulitapakṣmayugalā nāsāgraviniveśitā yugamātravyavalokinī vā kāryā dṛṣṭiḥ //
body.translated_text: The gaze should be made with eyelids slightly closed, fixed on the tip of the nose, or looking ahead only a yoke's length.

body.text: prathamārambhiṇaḥ saṃtatābhyāsena kleśasya parihārārthamāha-
body.translated_text: For a beginner, in order to remove defilements through sustained practice, he says —

children.translated_text: But for the purpose of resting the gaze, one may sometimes look at the directions;

children.text: ābhāsamātraṃ dṛṣṭvā ca svāgatārthaṃ vilokayet // Bca_5.36 //
children.translated_text: and having seen merely an appearance, one may look for the purpose of greeting. // Bca_5.36 //

body.text: dṛṣṭicittaparikhedaparityāgāya kadācit karhicit diśo vyavalokayet / atha kadācit kaścit tatsamīpamāgacchet, tadā tasya praticchāyāmātraṃ viditvā svāgatavādena saṃtoṣaṇārthaṃ vilokayet / anyathā tatra tasya avadhyānena akuśalaṃ prasavet //
body.translated_text: For the purpose of removing the fatigue of the gaze and mind, one may sometimes look at the directions. But if at some time someone approaches nearby, then having noticed merely their shadow, one may look for the purpose of satisfying [them] with a greeting. Otherwise, through inattention to them, an unwholesome [state] might arise.

body.text: mārge 'pi tathādṛṣṭergacchata upaghātaparihārārthamāha-
body.translated_text: He speaks of avoiding harm even for one walking with such a gaze on the road —

children.translated_text: For awareness of danger on the road and so forth, one should repeatedly look in the four directions;

children.text: diśo viśramya vīkṣeta parāvṛtyaiva pṛṣṭhataḥ // Bca_5.37 //
children.translated_text: having rested, one should survey the directions, and look behind by turning around. // Bca_5.37 //

body.text: bhayahetucaurādipratipattyarthaṃ caturdiśamiti krameṇa / anyathā ātmabhāvasya rakṣā kṛtā na syāt / sarvadigvyavalokanaṃ tu kriyamāṇamauddhatyopaghātaparihārārthaṃ sthitvā kartavyam / pṛṣṭhato vyavalokanaṃ parāvṛtya paścānmukhībhūya //
body.translated_text: 'For the purpose of recognizing' the causes of danger such as thieves and so forth — 'in the four directions' — in succession. Otherwise, the protection of one's personal existence would not be accomplished. But the surveying of all directions — being done — should be done while standing still, for the purpose of avoiding the harm of agitation. Looking behind [should be done] 'by turning around' — by facing backward.

body.text: asamādhānasya ca rakṣaṇāmāha-
body.translated_text: He states the guarding of [one who is] not in meditative equipoise —

children.translated_text: Having examined what lies ahead and behind, one should go forward or retreat;

children.text: evaṃ sarvāsvavasthāsu kāryaṃ buddhvā samācaret // Bca_5.38 //
children.translated_text: thus in all situations, having understood what is to be done, one should act. // Bca_5.38 //

body.text: saretpuraḥ apasaretpaścāt / prapātādyupaghātaṃ nirīkṣya ca / evamityuktakramadiśā svaparahitaprayojanamavagamya pratipattisāro bhavet //
body.translated_text: 'Go forward' — ahead; 'retreat' — backward. Having examined the harm from precipices and so forth. 'Thus' — in the manner stated, understanding the purpose for one's own and others' welfare — one should be of the essence of practice.

body.text: idānīṃ saṃprajanyakāritāṃ śikṣayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Now, in order to teach the function of introspective awareness, he says —

children.translated_text: 'The body should be positioned thus' — having initiated the action,

children.text: kathaṃ kāyaḥ sthita iti draṣṭavyaṃ punarantarā // Bca_5.39 //
children.translated_text: one should again examine in the meantime: 'how is the body positioned?' // Bca_5.39 //

body.text: caturṇāmīryāpathānāmanyatamasminnīryāpathe / kāyenaivamiti sthitena niṣaṇṇena vā avastheyamiti / tadanantaraṃ svādhyāyādikriyāmārabhya punarantarāle vyavalokitavyaṃ kathaṃ kāyaḥ sthita iti tasminneveryāpathe, uta bhinne īryāpathe / bhinne punaḥ pūrvavadavasthāpyaḥ //
body.translated_text: In whichever of the four deportments [one is situated]. 'The body thus' — 'I should remain standing or sitting.' Then immediately, having begun the activity of recitation and so forth, one should examine again in the intervals: 'how is the body positioned?' — whether in that very deportment, or in a changed deportment. If changed, one should again establish it as before.

body.text: kāyapratyavekṣāmabhidhāya cittapratyavekṣaṇāmāha-
body.translated_text: Having spoken of examining the body, he speaks of examining the mind —

children.translated_text: The maddened elephant of the mind should be examined with all effort,

children.text: dharmacintāmahāstambhe yathā vaddho na mucyate // Bca_5.40 //
children.translated_text: [to see] that, bound to the great post of <s>Dharma</s>-contemplation, it does not get free. // Bca_5.40 //

body.text: dharmasya svaparahitalakṣaṇasya cintaiva mahāstambho vandhanāyattīkaraṇahetutvāt //
body.translated_text: The contemplation of the <s>Dharma</s> characterized by one's own and others' welfare is itself the 'great post' — because it is the cause of binding and bringing [the mind] under control.

body.text: tasmin baddho 'pi punaḥ punarnirūpaṇīya ityāha-
body.translated_text: Even when bound to it, it should be examined again and again — he says —

children.text: kutra me vartata iti pratyavekṣyaṃ tathā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where is my [mind] engaged?' — thus the mind should be examined,
so that one should never abandon, even for a moment, the burden of concentration. // Bca_5.41 //

body.text: kva punaridaṃ mano mama vartate, pūrvasminnālambane anyatra vā gatam / gatamavagamya tato nirvatya tatraiva yojayitavyam / svarasavāhitāyāmupekṣaṇīyam / iti śamathadhuramekamapi kṣaṇaṃ yathā na parityajati tathā dhārayitavyam / etāvatā śīlaṃ hi samādhisaṃvartanīmamityuktaṃ bhavati / yathoktaṃ candrapradīpasūtre-
body.translated_text: 'Where is my mind now dwelling? Has it gone to the former object or elsewhere?' Having ascertained that it has gone, one should withdraw it from there and apply it to that very [meditation object]. When [the mind] is carried along by its own momentum, one should observe equanimity. Thus, one should hold [the practice] so that one does not abandon the task of tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) even for a single moment. To this extent, it is said that 'morality conduces to <s>samādhi</s>.' As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s>:

body.text:
kṣipraṃ samādhiṃ labhate niraṅgaṇaṃ
