viśuddhaśīlasyimi ānuśaṃsāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'One of purified morality quickly obtains <s>samādhi</s> without stain — these are the benefits.'

body.text:
iti /
[samādhi. 27.6]
body.translated_text: [<s>Samādhi</s>. 27.6]

body.text: ato 'vagamyate- ye kecit samādhihetavaḥ prayogāḥ, te śīle 'nugatā iti / tasmāt samādhyarthinā smṛtisaṃprajanyaśīlena bhavitavyam / tathā śīlārthināpi samādhau yatnaḥ kārya iti //
body.translated_text: From this it is understood: whatever practices are causes of <s>samādhi</s>, they follow upon morality. Therefore, one who desires <s>samādhi</s> should be endowed with the morality of mindfulness and introspective awareness. Likewise, even one who desires morality should make effort in <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: samādhānaparityāgāvakāśamāha-
body.translated_text: [<s>Śāntideva</s>] states the occasion for not abandoning concentration:

children.translated_text: 'In situations involving danger or celebration, one may act as one likes if unable [to maintain concentration];
for at the time of giving, the relaxation of morality has been stated.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.42 //

body.text: agnidāhādi bhayam / tathā ratnatrayapūjādikṛta utsavaḥ / samadhikataraḥ sattvārthādirvā / tatsaṃbhave yadi sthātumaśaktaḥ, tadā kāmacāra ityanujñātam / sāpattiko na bhavatītyarthaḥ / kutaḥ punarayamaniyamo labhyata ityāha- dānetyādi / śīlaṃ yadyapi dānātprakṛṣṭam, tathāpi avaraśikṣāyāṃ śikṣamāṇasya tadanantarameva uttaraśikṣāvasthitasya abhyāsapāṭavābhāvāt kathaṃcit tāvatkālaṃ tato nivartamānasyāpi nāpattiḥ / dānasyāsau kālo na śīlasya / ata evoktam- yadyaśakta iti / etāvanmātreṇedamudāharaṇam / yathoktam- tatraikasyāṃ śikṣāyāṃ niṣpādyamānāyāmaśaktasya itaraśikṣānabhyāsādanāpattiḥ / āryākṣayamatisūtre 'pyevamavocat-
body.translated_text: 'Danger' is [threat from] fire, and the like. 'Celebration' is a festival occasioned by worship of the Three Jewels and the like, or a greater welfare of beings and such. When that occurs, if one is unable to remain [in concentration], then free conduct is permitted — meaning: one does not incur a fault. 'How is this rule obtained?' he says: 'At the time of giving' etc. Though morality is superior to giving, nevertheless, for one who is training in a lower training and who is stationed in the next higher training — because of the absence of proficiency through practice — for a time, even though temporarily withdrawing from it, there is no fault. That is the time of giving, not of morality. Hence it is said 'if unable.' This much is the illustration. As stated: 'When one training is being accomplished, for one unable [to maintain another], there is no fault from non-practice of the other training.' And in the Noble <s>Akṣayamatisūtra</s> too, it is said thus:

body.text: dānakāle śīlopasaṃhārasyopekṣā / iti / na cātaḥ śithilena bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: 'At the time of giving, there is relaxation of the application of morality.' But one should not become lax because of this.

body.text: yatra kuśalapakṣasaṃcāre 'pi kvacit samādhānavighātaḥ syāt, tannopādeyamityāha-
body.translated_text: 'Where even wholesome activity would cause obstruction to concentration — that should not be taken up' — he says:

children.translated_text: 'What one has deliberately undertaken to do — one should not think of anything else;
that very thing should first be brought to completion, with one's inner self absorbed in it.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.43 //

body.text: svayameva tu yuktyāgamābhyāṃ kalyāṇamitravacanādvā yathābalamavadhārya yatkiṃcitkarma kartumārabdhaṃ dhyānādhyayanādikam, prathamatastadeva tāvanniṣpattiṃ neyaṃ tannimnena cetasā, na punastadaniṣpannameva parityajya paramārambhaṇīyam //
body.translated_text: Having ascertained by one's own reasoning and scripture, or by the words of a spiritual friend, according to one's ability — whatever activity one has undertaken, such as meditation or study — that very thing should first be brought to completion, with a mind inclined toward it. One should not abandon it incomplete and take up something else.

body.text: kiṃ punarevaṃ syādyadi na syādityāha-
body.translated_text: 'What would happen if this were not so?' he says:

children.text: evaṃ hi sukṛtaṃ sarvamanyathā nobhayaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'For thus everything is well done; otherwise, neither [task] would be [accomplished];
and the defilement of non-awareness will increase in this way.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.44 //

body.text: yasmādevamanutiṣṭhataḥ sarvaṃ suśliṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ syāt / tadviparyaye punarduḥśliṣṭamubhayaṃ pūrvaṃ cāttaṃ paścāt svīkṛtaṃ ca syāt / calapravṛtterasaṃprajanyaṃ syāt / praveśe vṛddhiḥ syāt //
body.translated_text: Because for one who practices thus, everything would be well-joined, well-done. In the contrary case, both would be ill-joined — what was previously taken up and what was later adopted. For one of unsteady activity, there would be non-awareness (<s>asaṃprajanya</s>). Upon entry [of non-awareness], there would be increase.

body.text: itthamapi niṣphalaṃ varjayedityāha-
body.translated_text: 'In this way too, one should avoid what is fruitless' — he says:

children.translated_text: 'When various kinds of idle chatter arise in manifold ways,
and in all [objects of] curiosity — one should destroy the eagerness that has arisen.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.45 //

body.text: anekaprakāre 'saṃbaddhābhidhāne 'paropādhike pravartamāne āścaryavastuṣu ca samasteṣu svayamapi tatkriyāyāṃ darśanaśravaṇāya vākūcittasya tāratamyaṃ nivārayet //
body.translated_text: When pointless speech of many kinds, irrelevant and concerning others' affairs, is going on, and regarding all wondrous things — one should gradually restrain the eagerness of speech and mind for participation therein, for seeing and hearing.

body.text: aparamapi niṣphalavarjanāya prātimokṣoddiṣṭamācaret ityāha-
body.translated_text: 'For another [purpose of] avoiding the fruitless, one should practice what is set forth in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>' — he says:

children.translated_text: 'When the urge arises to purposelessly knead earth, cut grass, draw lines, and the like,
remembering the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s training, one should immediately desist, in fear.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.46 //

body.text: bhūmiphalakādiṣu nakhadaṇḍādinā rekhākarṣaṇalekhanādi niṣprayojanamāgatamāpatitaṃ vivarjayet bhagavatā atra nivṛttirājñapteti saṃsmṛtya, tadatikramavipākaphalabhayāt / tatkṣaṇamiti na tatra kālaparilambhaṃ kuryāt //
body.translated_text: Drawing lines with nails, sticks, and the like on floors and boards — [when] the purposeless [urge] has arisen, has occurred — one should avoid it, remembering that the Blessed One has enjoined abstention here, out of fear of the ripening-fruit of transgressing that [rule]. 'Immediately' means one should not delay in that.

body.text: saṃkleśasamudācāre saṃprajanyakāritāṃ yadetyādibhiḥ saptabhiḥ ślokaiḥ śikṣayitumāha-
body.translated_text: [<s>Śāntideva</s>] teaches through seven verses, beginning with 'When,' what introspective awareness should do when a defiled state arises:

children.translated_text: 'When one desires to move or desires to speak,
one should first examine one's own mind and then act firmly and fittingly.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.47 //

body.text: prathamata eva svacittaṃ nirūpya / uktam (?) asaṃkliṣṭāvasthāyāṃ karaṇīyamuktam //
body.translated_text: First of all, having examined one's own mind — the stated [instruction] indicates what should be done when [the mind is] in an undefiled state.

body.text: etadeva darśayati-
body.translated_text: He shows this very [point]:

children.translated_text: 'When one sees one's own mind to be attracted or repelled,

children.text: na kartavyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ sthātavyaṃ kāṣṭhavattadā // Bca_5.48 //
children.translated_text: one should neither act nor speak; one should remain then like a block of wood.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.48 //

body.text: raktaṃ dviṣṭaṃ vā svacittaṃ yadā paśyet, tadā hastapādādicalanamātramapi na kartavyam, nāpi vacanodīraṇam / anyathā tadutthāpite kāyavāgvijñaptī api saṃkliṣṭe syātām / ato bahirindriyavyāpāravikalpāvupasaṃhṛtya sthātavyaṃ kāṣṭhavattadā / sarvavyāpāravirahānnirvyāpārāḥ sarvadharmā iti manasi nidhāya //
body.translated_text: When one sees one's own mind as attached or hostile — then one should not perform even the slightest movement of hands, feet, and the like, nor utter any speech. Otherwise, the bodily and vocal expressions produced by that [defiled mind] would also become defiled. Therefore, having withdrawn both the activity of the external senses and conceptualization, 'one should remain like a block of wood' — keeping in mind that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are inactive due to the absence of all activity.'

body.text: aparamāha-
body.translated_text: He says further:

children.translated_text: 'When [the mind] is excited, mocking, or imbued with pride and arrogance,

children.text: sotprāsātiśayaṃ vakraṃ vañcakaṃ ca mano bhavet // Bca_5.49 //
children.translated_text: when it is insolent, or excessively [so], crooked, or deceitful — // <s>Bca</s> 5.49 //

body.text: uddhatamiti / saddharmādiśravaṇapramādādapi uddhatam / vikṣepabahulamityarthaḥ / sopahāsaṃ vāgviheṭhanārambhakam, tayā yuktaṃ vā / mānaścittasyonnatiḥ / madaḥ svadharme (?) cittasyābhiniveśaḥ / tābhyāmanvitaṃ tatsaṃprayuktam / utprāsaḥ kāyikī viheṭhanā, tena sahotkaṭam / vakraṃ kuṭilaṃ śaṭhaṃ vā / vañcakaṃ pratārakaṃ māyāvi vā / yadi mano bhavet, sthātavyaṃ kāṣṭhavattadeti saṃbandhaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Excited' — even through heedlessness regarding hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> and the like — excited, meaning full of distraction. 'Mocking' — initiating verbal harassment, or [a mind] conjoined with it. 'Pride' is the mind's elevation; 'arrogance' is the mind's fixation on its own qualities (?). 'Imbued with them' means conjoined with them. 'Insolence' (<s>utprāsa</s>) is physical harassment — with it, [the mind is] aggressive. 'Crooked' means bent, dishonest. 'Deceitful' means a cheat, or hypocritical. 'If the mind should be [thus]' — the connection is: 'one should remain like a block of wood.'

children.translated_text: 'When [the mind shows] the semblance of self-exaltation, or the disparagement of others,
with reproach and with quarrelsomeness — one should remain then like a block of wood.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.50 //

body.text: ātmotkarṣaṇaṃ svaguṇātiśayaprakāśanam / tadābhāsaṃ tatpratibhāsaṃ tadvikalpanāt / parapaṃsanaṃ paravigrahaḥ doṣāviṣkaraṇaṃ vā, tadyuktam / adhikṣepaḥ parasya vacanatiraskāraḥ / saṃrambhaḥ sadākalivivādanimittacittapradoṣaḥ / ubhayatra saha tena vartata iti vigrahaḥ / evaṃ yadā paśyetsvakaṃ manaḥ, sthātavyaṃ kāṣṭhavat tadeti sāmānyoktamabhisaṃbadhyate //
body.translated_text: 'Self-exaltation' is the display of the superiority of one's own qualities. 'Its semblance' means its appearance — through conceptualizing it. 'Disparagement of others' is attacking others, or revealing [their] faults — with that. 'Reproach' (<s>adhikṣepa</s>) is verbal insult of others. 'Quarrelsomeness' (<s>saṃrambha</s>) is constant mental hostility that is the cause of dispute. Both [phrases] are compounds meaning '[possessing] that together with [the other].' When one sees one's own mind thus — the general statement 'one should remain like a block of wood' connects here.

children.translated_text: 'When my mind desires gain, honor, fame, a retinue,

children.text: upasthānārthi me cittaṃ tasmāttiṣṭhāmi kāṣṭhavat // Bca_5.51 //
children.translated_text: or personal service — therefore I shall stand like a block of wood.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.51 //

body.text: kīrtiryaśaḥ / parivāraḥ dāsīdāsakarmakarādiḥ / upasthānaṃ pādadhāvanamardanādi / ebhirarthi tadabhilāṣaṃ mama cittam / tasmāttiṣṭhāmi kāṣṭhavat //
body.translated_text: 'Fame' (<s>kīrti</s>) means renown. 'Retinue' means servants, male and female, workers, and the like. 'Service' (<s>upasthāna</s>) means foot-washing, massage, and the like. 'Desiring these' — my mind has craving for these. 'Therefore I shall stand like a block of wood.'

children.translated_text: 'When [my mind] is hostile to the welfare of others, interested in my own welfare, or desirous of an audience,

children.text: vaktumicchati me cittaṃ tasmāttiṣṭhāmi kāṣṭhavat // Bca_5.52 //
children.translated_text: and wishes to speak — therefore I shall stand like a block of wood.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.52 //

body.text: parārtharūkṣaṃ parārthavimukham / svārthārthi svārthābhiniviṣṭam / pariṣat śiṣyāntevāsiprabhṛtijanasamājaḥ / tadabhilāṣi tatparivārārthi //
body.translated_text: 'Hostile to the welfare of others' means averse to the welfare of others. 'Interested in my own welfare' means fixated on my own benefit. 'Audience' (<s>pariṣat</s>) is an assembly of people such as students and attendants. 'Desirous of that' means desiring that retinue.

children.translated_text: 'Impatient, lazy, fearful, brazen, garrulous,
and attached to one's own faction — therefore I shall stand like a block of wood.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.53 //

body.text: asahiṣṇu asahanaśīlam / alasaṃ kriyāsu akarmaṇyam / kusīdamityarthaḥ / bhītaṃ kāyajīvitabhīru bhayahetubhyo vā / pragalbhaṃ dhṛṣṭam / mukharaṃ durvacaskam, yuktāyuktamanapekṣya abhidhāyakaṃ vā / svapakṣeḥ śiṣyāntevāsijñātisālohitādau abhiniviṣṭaṃ pakṣapātātiśayavat //
body.translated_text: 'Impatient' means intolerant by nature. 'Lazy' means unfit for activities — meaning indolent. 'Fearful' means afraid for body and life, or afraid of the causes of fear. 'Brazen' (<s>pragalbha</s>) means bold, impudent. 'Garrulous' (<s>mukhara</s>) means abusive, or speaking without considering what is appropriate and inappropriate. 'Attached to one's own faction' — having excessive partiality toward students, attendants, relatives, blood-relations, and the like.

body.text: sāṃprataṃ pratikāranirdeśamāha-
body.translated_text: Now [<s>Śāntideva</s>] states the instruction on the antidote:

children.translated_text: 'Having observed the mind thus defiled, or engaged in fruitless endeavors,

children.text: nigṛhṇīyād dṛḍhaṃ śūraḥ pratipakṣeṇa tatsadā // Bca_5.54 //
children.translated_text: the hero should always firmly subdue it with the antidote.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.54 //

body.text: upadarśitakrameṇa saṃkliṣṭaṃ saṃkleśasaṃprayuktaṃ niṣphalavyāpāraṃ vā jñātvā svacittaṃ sarvapravṛttinigedhena prabhāvamandatāṃ vidhāya nigṛhṇīyādabhibhavet / dṛḍhaṃ yathā punarapi samudācāradharmakaṃ
body.translated_text: Having known one's own mind to be defiled — conjoined with defilement — or engaged in fruitless activity, in the manner described, one should subdue it, overpower it, by restraining all its tendencies and reducing its power. 'Firmly' — so that it does not again acquire the tendency to arise

body.text: na bhavati / kleśādisaṃgrāme vijayāya kṛtaparikaraḥ śuro bodhisattvaḥ / pratipakṣeṇa yo yasmin pratipakṣa uktaḥ yathā rāgādāvaśubhādi, tena tadviparītavidhānenetyarthaḥ / sadā sarvakālam, yadā yadā saṃkliṣṭaṃ pratīyate / ugraparipṛcchāyāṃ gṛhiṇaṃ bodhisattvamadhikṛtyoktam-
body.translated_text: . A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has prepared himself for victory in the battle against defilements and the like is a 'hero.' 'With the antidote' — whatever antidote has been prescribed for whatever [defilement], such as the meditation on the unattractive for passion and the like — by means of applying the opposite — this is the meaning. 'Always' — at all times, whenever defilement is detected. In the <s>Ugraparipcchā</s>, it is stated with reference to the lay <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

body.text: tena surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānāt prativiratena bhavitavyam, amattena anunmattena acapalena acañcalena abhrāntena amukhareṇa anunnatena upasthitasmṛtināsasaṃprajanyena / iti //
body.translated_text: 'He should abstain from the occasion of heedlessness [consisting of] liquor, spirits, and intoxicants; he should be sober, not crazed, not fickle, not restless, not confused, not garrulous, not haughty, with established mindfulness and introspective awareness.'

body.text: atraiva ca pravrajitaṃ bodhisattvamadhikṛtyoktam- smṛti saṃprajanyasyāvikṣepaḥ / iti //
body.translated_text: And there, with reference to the ordained <s>Bodhisattva</s>, it is said: 'Mindfulness is the non-distraction of introspective awareness.'

body.text: tathā āryatathāgataguhyasūtre darśitam-
body.translated_text: Likewise, it is shown in the Noble <s>Tathāgataguhyasūtra</s>:

body.text: na khalu punaḥ kulaputra bodhisattvasya vāg raktā vā duṣṭā vā mūḍhā vā kliṣṭā vā kṣaṇavyākaraṇī vā svapakṣotkarṣaṇavacanā vā parapakṣanigrahavacanā vā ātmavarṇānunayavacanā vā paravarṇapratighātavacanā vā pratijñottāraṇavacanā vā ābhimānikavyākaraṇavacanā veti //
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O son of good family, the speech of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not passionate, not hateful, not deluded, not defiled, not given to answering questions maliciously, not given to words that exalt one's own faction, not given to words that suppress the other's faction, not given to words that court favor for one's own reputation, not given to words that attack the other's reputation, not given to words that fulfill a [mere] pledge, not given to answers spoken from pride.'

body.text: evaṃ niṣphalaspandavarjanena anarthādātmabhāvasya rakṣā pratipāditā bhavati / tasmānmayā śīlasusthitena aprakampena aśithilena bhavitavyamiti //
body.translated_text: Thus, through the avoidance of fruitless movement, the protection of the self from harm has been demonstrated. Therefore, 'I should be well-established in morality, unshaken, not lax.'

body.text: etacca samāhitacittasya sidhyati / ata idaṃ śamathamāhātmyamavagamya tātparyeṇa bhāvayitavyam / anena tīvra ādaro bhavati śikśāsu / tenāpi smṛtirupatiṣṭhate / upasthitasmṛtirniṣphalaṃ varjayati / tasya anarthā na saṃbhavanti / tasmādātmabhāvaṃ rakṣitukāmena smṛtimūlamanviṣya nityamupasthitasmṛtinā bhavitavyam / etadevāha-
body.translated_text: And this is accomplished for one whose mind is concentrated. Therefore, having understood this greatness of tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>), one should cultivate [it] with diligence. Through this, there arises intense care in the trainings. Through that, mindfulness is established. One whose mindfulness is established avoids what is fruitless. For such a one, harms do not arise. Therefore, one who wishes to protect the self, having sought out the root [which is] mindfulness, should always be one whose mindfulness is established. This very [point] he states:

children.translated_text: 'What is the protection of the self therein? It is the avoidance of harm.
By what is all that obtained? Through the avoidance of fruitless movement.
That succeeds through constant mindfulness; mindfulness arises from intense care;
care arises from exertion, knowing the greatness of tranquility.'

body.text:
iti /
[śikṣā. sa. kārikā-7-8]
body.translated_text: [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, Verse 7-8]

body.text: śamathamāhātmyaṃ tu yathāvasaramihaiva kathayiṣyate //
body.translated_text: The greatness of tranquility will be described here as occasion arises.

body.text: ayamatra piṇḍārthaḥ anarthavivarjanārthamavadhārayitavya iti vṛttatritayenopadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: The essential meaning here is: 'One should hold firm for the purpose of avoiding harm' — showing this through three verses, [<s>Śāntideva</s>] says:

children.translated_text: 'Well-resolved, clear, steadfast, with care and reverence,
with modesty, with fear [of wrongdoing], calm, devoted to pleasing others — // <s>Bca</s> 5.55 //
unwearied by the mutually contradictory wishes of childish people,
knowing that these arise from defilement — with compassion — // <s>Bca</s> 5.56 //
always under the control of self and beings, in blameless matters,
free from pride, like a magical creation — thus shall I maintain my mind.' // <s>Bca</s> 5.57 //

body.text: suniścitaṃ saṃdehaviparyāsarahitam / suprasannaṃ sadā prītisaumanasyabahulam / dhīramacañcalam / ādaraḥ kathita eva / gauravaṃ ārādhyeṣu cittasya namratā / tābhyāṃ saha vartate / salajjaṃ pūrvavat / sabhayaṃ skhalita[mālokya] bhītam / śāntaṃ saṃyatendriyam / sattvārādhanayatnavat //
body.translated_text: 'Firmly resolved' — free from doubt and error. 'Well-pleased' — always abundant in joy and cheerfulness. 'Steadfast' — unagitated. 'Diligence' has been explained already. 'Reverence' is the humility of mind toward those worthy of respect. [The mind] abides with these two. 'Modest' — as before. 'Fearful' — frightened upon seeing a misstep. 'Calm' — with restrained senses. 'Striving to please beings' —

body.text: yadekasya rucijanakaṃ tadanyasya viparītam / anyonyaviruddhābhiḥ pṛthagjanecchābhirakheditamavipratisāri / katham? dayānvitam / hetupadametat / kutaḥ? yasmāt kleśotpādānna svātantryādidametat parasparaviruddhacaritameṣāṃ bālānāmiti matvā //
body.translated_text: What produces delight in one is the opposite in another. Not wearied by the mutually contradictory desires of ordinary persons, and without regret. How? 'Endowed with compassion' — this is the causal ground. Why? Because, knowing that this mutually contradictory behavior of these childish beings is due to the arising of defilements, not from their own free will —

body.text: ātmasattvavaśaṃ svaparāyattaṃ sarvakālam / kiṃ sarvatra? na / anavadyeṣu vastuṣu ubhayasāvadyaśūnyeṣu / kiṃvat? nirmāṇamiva nirmitavat / vigatamānaṃ mānasaṃ dhārayāmi / eṣo 'hamiti bodhisattvo manasi niveśayet //
body.translated_text: 'Subject to oneself and beings' — dependent on oneself and others, at all times. In everything? No — 'in blameless matters,' those free from fault on both sides. Like what? 'Like an emanation' — like something magically created. 'Free from pride' — I shall maintain a mind [free from pride]. 'This is I' — thus should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> establish in the mind.

body.text: asmādapi saṃvegamanasikārāccittasyānarthavivarjanena rakṣā vidhātavyetyāha-
body.translated_text: From this sense of urgency too, the mind should be guarded by averting harm — he says —

children.translated_text: Remembering again and again the excellent moment obtained after a long time,
I shall hold the mind thus — immovable like <s>Sumeru</s>. // Bca_5.58 //

body.text: aticireṇa kālena labdham uktaṃ kṣaṇavaraṃ smaraṇena cetasi kṛtvā punaḥ punarantaraṃ sthirīkaromi īdṛśamuktasvabhāvam / aprakampyaṃ kampayitumaśakyaṃ kāmādivitarkapavanaiḥ parvatarājavat //
body.translated_text: 'Obtained after a very long time' — the excellent moment that has been described, placing it in the mind through recollection again and again at intervals, 'I shall make firm' — of the nature described. 'Immovable' — unable to be shaken by the winds of thoughts such as desire and so forth — like the king of mountains.

body.text: evametābhyāṃ śīlasamādhibhyāmanyonyasaṃvardhakābhyāṃ cittakarmapariniṣpattiḥ / tasmādavasthitametat- cittaparikarmaiva bodhisattvaśikṣā iti / tena yaduktam-
body.translated_text: Thus, through these two — morality and concentration — which mutually reinforce each other, the refinement of the mind's action is accomplished. Therefore this is established: the refinement of the mind alone is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training. Hence what was said —

body.text:
cittarakṣāvrataṃ muktvā bahubhiḥ kiṃ mama vrataiḥ /
[bodhi. 5.18]
body.translated_text: 'Apart from the vow of guarding the mind, what use to me are many vows?' [<s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> 5.18]

body.text: iti, tat pariniṣṭhitam //
body.translated_text: — that is fully established.

body.text: punastadekāntamavadhārayituṃ kāyapratyavekṣāmāha-
body.translated_text: Further, in order to ascertain that definitively, he speaks of examination of the body (<s>kāyapratyavekṣā</s>) —

children.translated_text: Being dragged here and there by vultures greedy for flesh,

children.text: na karotyanyathā kāyaḥ kasmādatra pratikriyām // Bca_5.59 //
children.translated_text: the body does nothing otherwise — why then does it offer resistance here? // Bca_5.59 //

body.text: kāyasya sarvathā kvacidapi vyāpāro nāsti, svātmanyapi sāmarthyābhāvāt / anyathā cittarahito mṛtasya kāyaḥ / gṛdhrādibhirvipralujyamāna itastataḥ pratikāramātmarakṣaṇārthaṃ kimiti na karotīti pṛcchati sarvasāmarthyavikalatvāt / ata eva cittaparikarmaiva sādhyam / tasmin parikarmite kāyasya ayatnata eva parikarmasiddheḥ, tatparatantratvāttasyetyuktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: The body has absolutely no activity anywhere, even regarding itself, due to the absence of any capacity. Otherwise — the body of a dead person, devoid of mind — being torn apart here and there by vultures and such, he asks why it does not make any countermeasure for the purpose of self-protection, since it is devoid of all capacity. Therefore, it is the refinement of the mind alone that should be accomplished. When that is refined, the refinement of the body is accomplished effortlessly, because it is dependent on that [mind] — this is what is stated.

body.text: evaṃ sarvathānupayogini kāye sāpekṣatāṃ nirasyannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, rejecting attachment to the body which is entirely useless [in itself], he says —

children.translated_text: O mind, why do you protect this heap, having appropriated it as your own?

children.text: tvattaścetpṛthagevāyaṃ tenātra tava ko vyayaḥ // Bca_5.60 //
children.translated_text: If indeed it is separate from you, then what loss is there to you in this? // Bca_5.60 //

body.text: he manaḥ, anātmakameva ātmatvena svīkṛtya māṃsāsthipuñjaṃ kāyasaṃjñakaṃ kasmātkāraṇāt tvaṃ rakṣasi? kimevamiti cet, bhavato yadi bhinna evāyaṃ kāyaḥ, tena asyāpacaye tava kimapacīyate?
body.translated_text: O mind, having appropriated as self — as one's own — what is in reality without self, this heap of flesh and bones called 'body,' for what reason do you protect it? If you ask 'why so?' — if this body is indeed distinct from you, then what is diminished of yours by its decline?

body.text: pūrvameva ciraṃ svīkṛta iti cedāha-
body.translated_text: 'But it has long been appropriated from before' — to this he says —

children.text: na svīkaroṣi he mūḍha kāṣṭhaputtalakaṃ śucim /
children.translated_text: O fool, you do not appropriate a clean wooden doll;
why do you protect this putrid machine fashioned of impurities? // Bca_5.61 //

body.text: he mūḍha, mohavijṛmbhitametad bhavataḥ / śuciṃ pavitram / ayaṃ ca aśuciḥ / idamevāha- amedhyeti / pūtikaṃ śatanadharmakam //
body.translated_text: O fool — this is the sport of your delusion. 'Clean' — pure. But this [body] is impure. He states just this — 'fashioned of impurities.' 'Putrid' — of the nature of decay.

body.text: syādetat- kimanyasminnasannapi doṣa ucyate ityatrāha-
body.translated_text: 'But what fault is there even if there is none in something else?' — to this he says —

children.translated_text: First, with your own intellect, separate this skin-covering;
with the sword of wisdom, release the flesh from the cage of bones. // Bca_5.62 //
Having separated the bones too, look finally at the marrow;
'Is there any essence here?' — investigate this yourself. // Bca_5.63 //

body.text: carmamayaṃ puṭam / svamativiśeṣeṇa pṛthak kuru svakāyādapasāraya / asthighaṭitapañjarād yantrāt prajñātmakena śastreṇa māṃsakartanena / tadanantaramasthīnyapi khaṇḍaśaḥ pṛthag bhinnāni kṛtvā majjānaṃ paśya avalokaya / yadi antaraṃ kāyaḥ caturmahābhūtikaḥ mātapitraśucikalalasaṃbhūtaḥ duḥkhamayaḥ kṛtaghnaśceti vistareṇa pratipādayiṣyatīti kimatra sāramasti vijñapraśastaṃ nyāyyaṃ vā, ityātmanaiva vicāraya //
body.translated_text: A covering made of skin. 'With your own special intellect, separate' — remove from your own body. 'From the cage' — the framework — 'fashioned of bones,' with a 'sword that is wisdom,' a cutter of flesh. Then, after that, having also separated the bones into pieces, 'look at the marrow' — observe it. 'If the interior — the body — is composed of the four great elements, born from the impure embryo of father and mother, full of suffering, ungrateful' — thus he will demonstrate at length — 'is there any essence here,' anything worthy of the wise, anything proper? — 'investigate with your own [mind].'

children.text: evamanviṣya yatnena na dṛṣṭaṃ sāramatra te /
children.translated_text: Having searched thus with effort, no essence has been seen here by you;

children.text: adhunā vada kasmāttvaṃ kāyamadyāpi rakṣasi // Bca_5.64 //
children.translated_text: now say — why do you still protect the body even now? // Bca_5.64 //

body.text: evaṃ kathitanayena / sādhūktamiti cet, adhunā vada kasmāt tvamadyāpi sarvaguṇavikalamapi kāyaṃ rakṣasi? evaṃ vidvānapi //
body.translated_text: 'Thus' — in the manner described. 'Well said' — if so, now say why you still protect the body even now, though it is devoid of all good qualities. 'Even one who knows thus' —

body.text: tathāpi asti kiṃcidatropādeyamiti cedāha-
body.translated_text: 'Even so, there is something here worth taking up' — to this he says —

children.text: na khāditavyamaśuci tvayā peyaṃ na śoṇitam /
children.translated_text: The impure is not to be eaten by you, blood is not to be drunk,

children.text: nāntrāṇi cūṣitavyāni kiṃ kāyena kariṣyasi // Bca_5.65 //
children.translated_text: the entrails are not to be sucked — what will you do with the body? // Bca_5.65 //

body.text: yadasti, na tadupayuktamiti saṃkṣepārthaḥ / ataḥ kimanupayoginā kāyena kariṣyasi? atra āsaṅgo na yukta ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: What exists is not fit for use — this is the summary meaning. Therefore, what will you do with the useless body? Attachment to it is not appropriate — that is the meaning.

body.text: anyaprayojanābhāvādidamevocitamutpaśyāmaḥ ityāha-
body.translated_text: 'In the absence of any other purpose, we see this alone as fitting' — to this he says —

children.translated_text: It is fitting to protect it for the food of vultures and jackals;
but this body of human beings is an instrument of action. // Bca_5.66 //

body.text: yasmāt karmaṇi kenacit sahakāribhāvenopayujyate iti rakṣyate //
body.translated_text: Since it is used in some auxiliary capacity in action, it is protected.

body.text: tathāpi nātrābhiniveśaḥ kārya ityāha-
body.translated_text: Even so, one should not cling to it — he says —

children.translated_text: Even as you thus protect it, merciless death will seize

children.text: kāyaṃ dāsyati gṛdhrebhyastadā tvaṃ kiṃ kariṣyasi // Bca_5.67 //
children.translated_text: the body and give it to the vultures — what then will you do? // Bca_5.67 //

body.text: ācchidyeti balāt / bhavato gṛhītvā niṣkṛpo mṛtyustava kāyaṃ gṛdhrebhyo dāsyati, tadāpi na kaścitpratikāro bhaviṣyati ityabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Seizing' — by force. Without compassion, death will take your body and give it to the vultures; even then there will be no countermeasure — that is the purport.

body.text: syādetat- yadyapi evam, tathāpi bhaktācchādanamātreṇāpi paripālanīya ityatrāha- na
body.translated_text: 'But even so, it should be maintained with at least food and clothing' — to this he says — 'Not

children.translated_text: going to stay' — to a servant [who will not stay], clothing and such are not given;

children.text: kāyo yāsyati khāditvā kasmāttvaṃ kuruṣe vyayam // Bca_5.68 //
children.translated_text: the body will depart having consumed — why do you incur this expense? // Bca_5.68 //

body.text: yadi nāma bhṛtyakarmakaraṇaṃ tathāpi tatrānavasthāyisvabhāve vicakṣaṇo jñātvaiva pravartate, evaṃ prakṛte 'pi taddharmiṇi kenābhiprāyeṇa he manaḥ, tvaṃ kuruṣe vyayamupakaraṇopakṣayam?
body.translated_text: Even if indeed it performs the work of a servant, still, a discerning person acts knowing that its nature is impermanent; so too in the present case, regarding what shares that same nature — with what intention, O mind, do you incur expense, the depletion of resources?

body.text: tat kiṃ sarvathaiva niravakāśo 'yaṃ kartavyaḥ? netyāha-
body.translated_text: 'Then should it be made entirely neglected?' — 'No,' he says —

children.translated_text: Therefore, having given it wages, now pursue your own purpose, O mind;

children.text: na hi vaitanikopāttaṃ sarvaṃ tasmai pradīyate // Bca_5.69 //
children.translated_text: for not everything earned by a hired worker is given to him. // Bca_5.69 //

body.text: vetanaṃ karmamūlyam / tāvanmātraṃ datvā asmai gatvaraśarīrāya, karmopakaraṇatvāt, svaprayojanamanuvidheyaṃ he manaḥ / anenaivopārjitaṃ kasmādasmai na dīyate iti cet, na hi yasmāt yatkiṃcit karmakareṇopāttaṃ sarvaṃ tasmai karmakarāya pradīyate iti nyāyo 'sti //
body.translated_text: 'Wages' — the price of labor. Having given just that much to this transient body — because it is an instrument of action — one's own purpose should be pursued, O mind. 'What is earned by this very [body], why is it not given to it?' — if so [one asks], because there is no rule that whatever is earned by a hired worker, all of it is given to that worker.

body.text: tasmādevamupastambhamātraṃ datvā-
body.translated_text: Therefore, having given merely this much support —

children.translated_text: Placing upon the body the notion of a boat, on account of its being the basis for going and coming,
make the body go as you wish, for the accomplishment of the welfare of beings. // Bca_5.70 //

body.text: kāye naubuddhiṃ kṛtvā pravṛttinivṛttihetoḥ icchāyattaṃ kāyaṃ kuru sattvārthānuṣṭhānāya niṣpattaye vā / he manaḥ iti prakṛtamabhisaṃbadhyate //
body.translated_text: Having placed upon the body the notion of a boat, for the purpose of activity and cessation, make the body subject to your will for the performance — or accomplishment — of the welfare of beings. 'O mind' — this is connected with what precedes.

body.text: iti kāyapratyavekṣayā tatsvabhāvamupayogaṃ ca vicārya pariniścitakāyaprayojanamupasaṃharannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, having examined through body-examination its nature and its utility, and having ascertained the purpose of the body, he concludes —

children.translated_text: One who has thus brought oneself under control should always have a smiling face;
one should abandon frowning, be the first to speak, and be a friend to the world. // Bca_5.71 //

body.text: uktanītyā āyattīkṛtaḥ ātmā cittakāyalakṣaṇaḥ / sarvadā prasannavadano bhavet / bhrūlalāṭasaṃkocaṃ ca prasādahānikaraṃ tyajet / pūrvameva asaṃcodita eva pareṇa svāgatādivādaiḥ saṃtoṣaṇaśīlo bhavet / sarvasattvānāmakāraṇabāndhavaśca //
body.translated_text: 'The self' — characterized by mind and body — 'brought under control' in the manner described. One should always have a serene countenance. And one should abandon the contraction of the brow and forehead, which destroys serenity. Without being prompted first by another, one should be disposed to please with words of welcome and such. And one should be an uncaused kinsman to all beings.

body.text: ityapi śikṣā anarthavarjanāya kāryetyāha-
body.translated_text: This too is a training to be practiced for the avoidance of harm — he says —

children.translated_text: One should not throw down seats and such hastily with a crash;
one should not bang doors; one should always delight in silence. // Bca_5.72 //

body.text: sahasā tvaritameva niṣprayojanaṃ hastadaṇḍādinā kapāṭaṃ ca nākoṭayet / saṃkṣepataḥ niḥśabdābhiratirbhavet //
body.translated_text: Hastily — quickly, without purpose — one should not strike a door with a staff or such. In brief, one should delight in silence.

body.text: kaḥ evaṃ sati guṇaḥ syādityāha-
body.translated_text: What virtue would there be in this? — he says —

children.translated_text: The crane, the cat, and the thief — moving silently and stealthily —
obtain their desired objective; the ascetic should always move likewise. // Bca_5.73 //

body.text: ete sarve niḥśabdā anuddhatāśca viharanto vivakṣitamarthaṃ labhante / vratināpi tathaiva samādhānakaṇṭakaparihāreṇa vihartavyam //
body.translated_text: All these, dwelling silently and without agitation, obtain their intended purpose. The one under vows too should live likewise, avoiding the thorns to concentration.

body.text: ityapi śikṣitavyamityāha-
body.translated_text: This too should be trained in — he says —

children.translated_text: One should accept with bowed head the words of those skilled in exhortation,

children.text: pratīcchecchirasā vākyaṃ sarvaśiṣyaḥ sadā bhavet // Bca_5.74 //
children.translated_text: of those who render assistance unasked — one should always be a student of all. // Bca_5.74 //

body.text: kaukṛtyavinodanāvavādānuśāsanīsamarthānāṃ vinayādikovidānām aprārthitahitaiṣiṇāṃ hitavidhāyakaṃ vacanaṃ mūrdhnā gṛhṇīyāt / na teṣu svacittaṃ dūṣayitavyam, nāpyavamānanā kāryeti bhāvaḥ / sarvasattveṣu gurugauravadhiyā samācaritavyamiti sarvaṃ sarvebhyaḥ śikṣet //
body.translated_text: Of those competent in admonition and instruction for dispelling remorse, of those skilled in the <s>Vinaya</s> and such, of those who wish well without being asked — one should accept upon one's head their beneficial words. One should not corrupt one's own mind toward them, nor should disrespect be shown — that is the purport. One should act with the attitude of reverence toward a teacher regarding all beings — thus one should learn everything from everyone.

body.text: īrṣyāmalaprakṣālanāmāha-
body.translated_text: He speaks of washing away the stain of envy —

children.translated_text: One should utter 'well done!' to all good words;
seeing one who performs meritorious acts, one should delight them with praises. // Bca_5.75 //

body.text: parakīyaguṇavardhanavacaneṣu tatparitoṣaṇāya sādhu sādhu, bhadrakamidam, iti śabdamadhyāśayenoccārayet / kuśalakarmakāriṇamapi dṛṣṭvā sādhu kṛtam, dhanyo bhavān sukṛtakarmakārī, ityādibhiḥ stutivacanaiḥ protsāhayet //
body.translated_text: Regarding others' statements that enhance virtues, for the purpose of pleasing them, one should sincerely utter the word 'Well done! Well done! This is excellent!' And seeing one who performs wholesome actions, one should encourage them with words of praise such as 'Well done! Fortunate are you, performer of good deeds!'

body.text: lapanāśaṅkāṃ nirasyannāha-
body.translated_text: Dispelling the suspicion of flattery, he says —

children.translated_text: One should speak of [others'] virtues behind their back, and should repeat [them] with delight;
and when one's own praises are spoken, one should cultivate appreciation of the other's virtue-discernment. // Bca_5.76 //

body.text: paraguṇān sadbhūtānapi parokṣaṃ brūyānna samakṣam / anyathā lapanāṃ kaścinmanyeta / pareṇa tu tatsamakṣamanyasya guṇe bhāṣyamāṇe tadanuvādakatayā samakṣamapi brūyāt / anyathā nāsya rūciratreti matvā svacittaṃ pradūṣayet paraḥ / svaguṇe punaḥ kenacid guṇapakṣapātinā prasannena samakṣaṃ parokṣaṃ ca kīrtyamāne cittasyonnatiṃ nivārayaṃstasyaiva guṇābhidhāyakasya guṇānurāgitāṃ manasi kuryāt //
body.translated_text: One should speak of others' genuine virtues behind their back, not face to face. Otherwise, someone might consider it flattery. But when another speaks of someone's virtue in their presence, as a re-stater of that, one may speak even face to face. Otherwise, [the person] might think 'this one does not approve' and corrupt their own mind. When one's own virtue is proclaimed face to face or behind one's back by someone who is partial to virtues and well-disposed, one should — restraining the mind's inflation — consider in mind the virtue-appreciation of that very person who praises virtues.

body.text: paraguṇāmarṣaṇaṃ vārayannāha-
body.translated_text: Preventing impatience at others' virtues, he says —

children.text: sarvārambhā hi tuṣṭayarthāḥ sā vittairapi durlabhā /
children.translated_text: All undertakings are indeed for the sake of satisfaction, and that is hard to obtain even with wealth;
therefore I shall enjoy the happiness of satisfaction through virtues produced by others' effort. // Bca_5.77 //

body.text: sarveṣāṃ hīnamadhyotkṛṣṭānāṃ sattvānām / sarve vā upakramāḥ duḥkhaparihāreṇa tuṣṭayarthāḥ / sarvārambhapariśrameṇa tuṣṭirevotpādayitavyetyarthaḥ / sā ca tuṣṭirdhanavisargairapi durlabhā, syādvā na veti / iha punarayatnasiddhopasthitā kasmātparihīyata iti matvā bhokṣye anubhaviṣyāmi saṃtoṣasukham anyayatnaniṣpāditairguṇairupanāmitam / na hi priyaputraguṇairakṣamāyuktā / iti bhāvanayā paraguṇaśravaṇāccittakārkaśyamapakuryāt //
body.translated_text: Of all beings — inferior, middling, and superior. Or: all endeavors, through the elimination of suffering, are for the sake of satisfaction. The meaning is: through the toil of all endeavors, satisfaction alone is to be produced. And that satisfaction is hard to obtain even through expenditure of wealth — or it may not be [obtained at all]. But here it is at hand, accomplished without effort — why should it be forsaken? Thinking thus, 'I shall experience' — I shall enjoy — the happiness of contentment brought by virtues accomplished through others' effort. For impatience is not appropriate regarding the virtues of a dear son. Thus, through this contemplation, one should remove the harshness of mind upon hearing of others' virtues.

body.text: atraivopacayamāha-
body.translated_text: He speaks of the benefit in this very [practice] —

children.text: na cātra me vyayaḥ kaścitparatra ca mahatsukham /
children.translated_text: There is no loss to me in this, and in the hereafter, great happiness;

children.text: aprītiduḥkhaṃ dveṣaistu mahadduḥkhaṃ paratra ca // Bca_5.78 //
children.translated_text: but through hatred, there is the suffering of displeasure, and great suffering in the hereafter. // Bca_5.78 //

body.text: naiva asminnarthe pravṛttimato mama ihaloke vā upakṣayaleśo 'pi saṃbhavati / upacayaḥ punarvidyata eveti darśayati- paratra mahatsukhaṃ paraguṇābhinandanāt / evamakriyamāṇe punarapacayo dṛśyate, ubhayaloke 'pi duḥkhaṃ paraguṇāsahanāt //
body.translated_text: For one engaged in this matter, not even the slightest diminishment occurs in this world. But there is indeed an increase — he shows: 'in the hereafter, great happiness' — from rejoicing in others' virtues. When this is not done, however, a decline is seen — suffering in both worlds from intolerance of others' virtues.

body.text: tasmāt sarvakalmaṣaparityāgena iyamucitā karmakāritā śiksaṇīyetyāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, through the abandonment of all defilements, this is the proper course of action to be trained in — he says —

children.translated_text: One should speak words that are trustworthy, with well-placed syllables, clear in meaning, pleasing,
delightful to hear, rooted in compassion, soft and gentle in tone. // Bca_5.79 //

body.text: sarvāvadyavinirmuktatvādviścastam / ānupūrvyā vyavasthitapadam / asaṃdigdhārtham / manaḥprahlādanakaram / śravaṇāpyāyakam / karuṇārasaniṣyandabhūtaṃ na rāgādinidānam / mṛdusvaramakarkaśavacanam / mandasvaraṃ yāvatā dhvaninā pratipādyasya pratītiḥ syāt, na tato nyūnaṃ nātiriktamudīrayan /
body.translated_text: 'Trustworthy' — because of being free from all fault. 'With well-placed syllables' — words arranged in proper sequence. 'Clear in meaning' — unambiguous. 'Pleasing' — producing delight in the mind. 'Delightful to hear' — nourishing to the ear. 'Rooted in compassion' — flowing from the essence of compassion, not caused by desire and such. 'Soft in tone' — not harsh in speech. 'Gentle in tone' — uttering with just enough sound for the listener's comprehension, neither less nor more than that.

children.translated_text: One should always look at beings directly, with eyes as if drinking them in;

children.text: etāneva samāśritya buddhatvaṃ me bhaviṣyati // Bca_5.80 //
children.translated_text: 'Depending on these very [beings], my <s>Buddhahood</s> will come about.' // Bca_5.80 //

body.text: avakramakuṭilaṃ paramaprītirasabharāvanatena cakṣuṣā tṛṣita iva śītalajala paramāhlādakaraṃ saṃpivanniva sattvān vyavalokayan / na raktena na duṣṭena mugdhena / paramopakārakā hyete / kutaḥ? yasmādetān sattvān samāsādya durlabhalābhaṃ buddhatvaṃ me bhaviṣyati utpatsyate / evaṃ ca viharan adyatve 'pi sattvārthasamartho bhavatyeva / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: 'Directly' — not crookedly or obliquely, with eyes bowed from the fullness of supreme affection, as if drinking in, like one thirsting [drinks] cool water supremely refreshing — thus gazing at beings. Not with desire, not with hostility, not with delusion. For these are supremely beneficial. Why? Because, 'depending on these beings,' my <s>Buddhahood</s> — hard to obtain — 'will come about,' will arise. And one dwelling thus becomes capable of accomplishing the welfare of beings even in this present life. As stated —

children.translated_text: 'One who is unagitated everywhere, through measured, gentle, and affectionate speech,
attracts worthy people, and becomes one whose [words] are accepted.'

body.text:
iti /
[śikṣā. sa. kārikā-10]
body.translated_text: [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 10]

body.text: etadeva ca bodhisattvasya kṛtyaṃ yaduta sattvāvarjanaṃ nāma / yathā dharmasaṃgītisūtre āryāpriyadarśanena bodhisattvena paridīpitam-
body.translated_text: And this alone is the duty of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — namely, the attracting of beings. As illustrated by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Āryāpriyadarśana</s> in the <s>Dharmasaṃgītisūtra</s> —

body.text: tathā tathā bhagavan bodhisattvena pratipattavyaṃ yatsahadarśanena sattvāḥ prasīdeyuḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na bhagavan bodhisattvasyānyat karaṇīyamasti anyatra sattvāvarjanāt / sattvaparipāka eveyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya dharmasaṃgītiriti //
body.translated_text: 'A <s>Bodhisattva</s> should conduct himself in such a way, O Blessed One, that beings are pleased at the mere sight of him. For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has no other task apart from attracting beings. This attracting of beings is itself, O Blessed One, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s recitation of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: evamakriyamāṇe ko doṣa iti cet-
body.translated_text: 'What fault is there if this is not done?' —

children.text: anādeyaṃ tu taṃ lokaḥ paribhūya jināṅkuram /
children.translated_text: 'But the world, despising one who is unacceptable — a sprout of the <s>Jina</s> —
would be burned as by a fire covered with ashes, in the hells and such.'

body.text:
iti /
[śikṣā. sa. kārikā-11]
body.translated_text: [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 11]

body.text: tasmāt sattvārādhanameva bodhisattvasya karma upakārikṣetramasādhāraṇaṃ puṇyaprasūtiheturiti //
body.translated_text: Therefore, pleasing beings alone is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s action — an extraordinary field of benefit, the cause of the production of merit.

body.text: tatprasaṅgena anyadapi darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: In this connection, showing something further, he says —

children.translated_text: That which arises from sustained commitment, that which arises from its antidote,

children.text: guṇopakārikṣetre ca duḥkhite ca mahacchubham // Bca_5.81 //
children.translated_text: [merit] in fields of virtue and of benefit, and toward the afflicted — great is the merit. // Bca_5.81 //

body.text: samādānena kriyamāṇam / abhiniveśotthaṃ tīvraprasādajanitam / pratipakṣotthaṃ kleśapratipakṣaśūnyatādibhāvanāprasūtam / guṇakṣetraṃ buddhabodhisattvādi / upakārikṣetraṃ mātāpitādi / duḥkhitā glānādayaḥ / eteṣu svalpamati kṛtamaprameyaśubhaheturupajāyate //
body.translated_text: 'From sustained commitment' — performed through formal undertaking. 'Arising from intense devotion' — born from intense faith. 'Arising from the antidote' — produced by meditation on emptiness and such, which are antidotes to defilements. 'Field of virtue' — <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and such. 'Field of benefit' — mother, father, and such. 'The afflicted' — the sick and so forth. Even a small [act] done in these [contexts] becomes a cause of immeasurable merit.

body.text: idamapi bodhisattvenābhyasanīyamityāha-
body.translated_text: This too should be practiced by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — he says —

children.translated_text: One should be skillful, endowed with diligence, and always act by oneself;
no opportunity should be yielded to anyone in any task. // Bca_5.82 //

body.text: dakṣaḥ sarvatra paṭupracāraḥ / utthānasaṃpannaḥ kausīdyāpanayanād vīryasamanvāgataḥ / ata eva svayameva sarvaṃ karaṇīyam, na parāpekṣā kvacidapi karmaṇi kāryā / idameva nāvakāśa ityādinā darśayati //
body.translated_text: 'Skillful' — having sharp conduct everywhere. 'Endowed with diligence' — possessed of vigor through the removal of laziness. Therefore, everything should be done by oneself; dependence on others should not be made in any task whatsoever. He shows this very point with 'no opportunity' and so forth.

body.text: pāramitābhyāse 'narthavivarjanāyānupūrvakāritāmāha-
body.translated_text: He speaks of the proper sequence in the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>, for the avoidance of harm —

children.translated_text: The <s>pāramitās</s> of generosity and so forth are progressively superior;
one should not abandon a superior one for the sake of an inferior, except on account of the bridge of conduct. // Bca_5.83 //

body.text: uparyuparitaḥ / dānācchīlaṃ śreṣṭham, śīlāt kṣāntirityādayaḥ / ato 'varapāramitāhetoruttaraṃ na tyajet / tadvirodhena na seveteti bhāvaḥ / kiṃ sarvathā? netyāha- anyatreti / bodhiattvānāṃ ya ācāraḥ śikṣāsaṃvaralakṣaṇaḥ sa eva kuśalajalarakṣaṇāya setubandho vihitaḥ, tasmādanyatra taṃ vihāya / sa yathā na bhidyate ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Progressively' — each higher than the previous. Morality is superior to generosity; patience to morality — and so forth. Therefore, one should not abandon a superior <s>pāramitā</s> for the sake of an inferior one. The purport is that one should not practice [the inferior] in conflict with [the superior]. In all cases? 'No' — he says 'except.' The conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, characterized by the training-vow, has been established as a bridge for the protection of wholesome waters — except for that, setting it aside. The meaning is: so that it [the bridge of conduct] is not broken.

body.text: tasmātsaṃbhāramupāditsunā karuṇāparatantreṇa sarvaṃ karaṇīyamuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, for one who desires to accumulate the provisions [for awakening], being governed by compassion, all that should be done has been stated — he says —

children.translated_text: Having understood thus, one should always be engaged in the welfare of others;
even what is prohibited is permitted for the compassionate one who sees the [greater] purpose. // Bca_5.84 //

body.text: evamanuttaraṃ jñātvā sattvānāṃ hitasukhavidhānāya nityamārabdhavīryo bhavet / pratiṣiddhārthe pravṛttau kathaṃ na sāpattika iti cet, na / kvacinniṣiddhamapi sattvārthaviśeṣaṃ prajñācakṣuṣā
body.translated_text: Having understood this supreme [teaching] thus, one should always be engaged with vigor for the provision of benefit and happiness to beings. 'But how is there no transgression when engaging in what is prohibited?' — Not so. In some cases, even what is prohibited, when a special welfare of beings is seen with the eye of wisdom —

body.text: paśyataḥ karaṇīyatayā anujñātaṃ bhagavatā / saniḥsaraṇaṃ ca bhagavataḥ śāsanam / taccāpi na sarvasya, api tu kṛpāloḥ karuṇāprakarṣapravṛttitayā tatparatantrasya parārthaikarasasya svaprayojanavimukhasya / iti prajñākaruṇābhyāmudbhūtaparārthavṛtterupāyakuśalasya pravartamānasya nāpattiḥ / atra ca upāliparipṛcchāyāmāpattyanāpattivibhāgo veditavyaḥ / tathā upāyakauśalyasūtre jyotiṣkamāṇavakādhikāre //
body.translated_text: — is permitted by the Blessed One as what should be done. And the teaching of the Blessed One has an escape [clause]. But this is not for everyone; rather, it is for the compassionate one — one whose activity proceeds from the excellence of compassion, who is governed by that [compassion], who is wholly devoted to others' welfare, indifferent to his own purposes. Thus, for one whose activity for others' welfare arises from wisdom and compassion, who is skilled in means and acts accordingly — there is no transgression. And here, the distinction between transgression and non-transgression should be understood from the <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s>. Likewise in the <s>Upāyakauśalyasūtra</s>, in the section on the youth <s>Jyotiṣka</s>.

body.text:
eṣā rakṣātmabhāvasya bhaiṣajyavasanādibhiḥ /
[śikṣā. sa. kārikā-13]
body.translated_text: 'This is the protection of one's personal existence through medicine, clothing, and so forth' [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 13] —

body.text: ityetat pratipādayitumāha-
body.translated_text: in order to demonstrate this, he says —

children.translated_text: Having shared with those who have fallen into lower states, the protectorless, and those observing vows,
one should eat a moderate amount; one should give away [everything] beyond the three robes. // Bca_5.85 //

body.text: bhaiṣajyavasanādibhirātmabhāvo hi paripālanīyaḥ parārthopayogitvāt / yathoktaṃ prākūtatra dvividhaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ satatabhaiṣajyaṃ glānapratyayabhaiṣajyaṃ ca / tatra satatabhaiṣajyamodanādi / tadarthaṃ piṇḍāya gocare caratā grāmapraveśe yathoktaśikṣāyāṃ smṛtimādhāya caritavyam / tato labdhāt piṇḍapātāt caturthabhāgavibhaktāt vinipātagatānanāthavratasthān saṃvibhāginaḥ kuryāt / ekaṃ pratyaṅgaṃ vinipātinām / dvitīyamanāthānām / tṛtīyaṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ datvā caturthamātmanā paribhuñjīta / sa paribhuñjāno na raktaḥ paribhuṅkte asaktaḥ, agṛddhaḥ, anadhyavasitaḥ, anyatra yāvadevāsya kāyasya sthitaye yāpanāyai / madhyamāṃ mātrām / tathā ca paribhuṅkte yathā nātisaṃlikhito bhavati, nātigurukāyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? ati saṃlikhito hi kuśalapakṣaparāṅmukho bhavati, atigurukāyo middhāvaṣṭabdho bhavati / tena taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhujya kuśalapakṣābhimukhena bhavitavyam / iti āryaratnameghe 'bhihitam / āryaratnarāśāvapi-
body.translated_text: For one's personal existence should be maintained through medicine, clothing, and so forth, because it is useful for others' welfare. As stated earlier — here, medicine is of two kinds: regular medicine and medicine for illness. The regular medicine is food and such. For this purpose, while going for alms on one's begging round, one should walk into the village maintaining mindfulness in the prescribed training. Then, from the alms obtained, divided into four portions: one should share with those who have fallen into lower states, the protectorless, and those observing vows. One portion for those who have fallen into misfortune; a second for the protectorless; a third given to fellow practitioners; and one should eat the fourth oneself. And eating thus, one eats without attachment, without clinging, without greed, without fixation — only for the maintenance and sustenance of this body. One should eat a moderate amount. And one eats in such a way that one is neither too emaciated nor too heavy of body. For what reason? Because one who is too emaciated turns away from wholesome endeavors, and one who is too heavy of body is overcome by torpor. Therefore, having eaten that alms food, one should be inclined toward wholesome endeavors. Thus it is stated in the <s>Āryaratnamegha</s>. And in the <s>Āryaratnarāśi</s> also —

body.text: paribhuñjatā ca evaṃ manasikāra utpādayitavyaḥ- santi asmin kāye aśītikṛmikulasahasrāṇi, tāni anenaivojasā sukhaṃ viharantu / idānīṃ caiṣāmāmiṣeṇa saṃgrahaṃ kariṣyāmi / bodhiprāptaśca punardharmeṇa saṃgrahaṃ kariṣyāmi / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'And while eating, one should generate this mental attention: "There are eighty thousand families of worms in this body; may they live happily through this very nourishment. Now I shall gather them through material [food]; and having attained awakening, I shall gather them through the <s>Dharma</s>."' Thus in detail.

body.text: punaratraivoktam-
body.translated_text: And it is further stated there —

body.text: dvayorahaṃ kāśyapa śraddhādeayamanujānāmi / katamayordvayoḥ? yuktasya muktasya ca / iti //
body.translated_text: 'I permit two [kinds of] faith, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. Which two? Of one who is disciplined and of one who is liberated.'

body.text: anayā diśā sarvaparibhogāḥ sattvārthamadhiṣṭhātavyāḥ / anyathā-
body.translated_text: In this manner, all enjoyments should be consecrated for the welfare of beings. Otherwise —

body.text: ātmatṛṣṇopabhogāttu kliṣṭāpattiḥ prajāyate //
body.translated_text: 'But from enjoyment motivated by craving for self, a defiled transgression arises.'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: śikṣā. sa. kārikā-13
body.translated_text: <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 13

body.text: yathoktaṃ candrapradīpasūtre-
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s> —

children.text: te bhojanaṃ svādurasaṃ praṇītaṃ labdhvā ca bhuñjanti ayuktayogāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having obtained delicious, flavorful, and excellent food, they eat while unyoked from discipline;

children.text: teṣāṃ sa āhāru vadhāya bhoti yatha hastipotāna bisā adhautakāḥ //
children.translated_text: that food becomes their destruction, like unwashed lotus-roots for young elephants.'

body.text: =samādhi. 9. 29
body.translated_text: = <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> 9.29

body.text: vistareṇa caitacchikṣāsamuccaye draṣṭavyam //
body.translated_text: And this should be seen at length in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>.

body.text: glānabhaiṣajyaṃ tu yāmikaṃ sāptāhikaṃ yāvajjīvikamiti trividham / etacca bhikṣuvinaye pratipāditaṃ tatraivāvadhāryam //
body.translated_text: Medicine for illness, however, is of three kinds: for one day, for seven days, and for a lifetime. This has been explained in the <s>Bhikṣuvinaya</s>; it should be ascertained from there.

body.text: vasanādibhirātmarakṣāmāha- tricīvarabahistyajet / iti / sacedāgatya kaścid bodhisattvaṃ pātracīvaraṃ yāceta, tena atityāgo na kartavyaḥ / kiṃ tu yattadanujñātaṃ bhagavatā- tricīvaraṃ śramaṇakalpaḥ, tato 'tiriktaṃ ca yadbhavet, tyaktavyamarthine, nānyathā / uktaṃ ca bodhisattvapratimokṣe- sacetpunaḥ kaścidāgatya pātraṃ vā cīvaraṃ vā yāceta, sacettasyātiriktaṃ bhaved buddhānujñātāttricīvarāt, yathāparityaktaṃ dātavyam / sacetpunastasya ūnaṃ tricīvaraṃ bhavet yanniśritya brahmacaryāvāsaḥ, tanna parityaktavyam / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? avisarjanīyaṃ hi tricīvaramuktaṃ tathāgatena / sacecchāriputra bodhisattvastricīvaraṃ parityajya yācanaguruko bhavet, na tena alpecchatā āsevitā bhavet / iti //
body.translated_text: He speaks of protecting oneself through clothing and so forth: 'one should give away beyond the three robes.' If someone were to come and ask the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for his bowl and robes, he should not make an excessive gift. Rather, what has been permitted by the Blessed One — the three robes are the ascetic's standard (<s>śramaṇakalpa</s>) — whatever is beyond that should be given to the petitioner, not otherwise. And it is stated in the <s>Bodhisattvapratimokṣa</s>: 'If someone were to come and ask for bowl or robe, if he has any surplus beyond the three robes permitted by the <s>Buddha</s>, it should be given as completely as possible. But if his three robes — on which the celibate life depends — are deficient, those should not be given up. For what reason? Because the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared the three robes not to be relinquished. If, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to give up the three robes and become one who panders to begging, he would not have cultivated contentment with little.'

body.text: atityāgaṃ niṣedhayan punarātmarakṣāmupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Prohibiting excessive giving, he further shows the protection of oneself — he says —

children.translated_text: One should not torment the body, which serves the true <s>Dharma</s>, for a trifling purpose;
for precisely thus will one swiftly fulfill the hopes of beings. // Bca_5.86 //

body.text: satāṃ satpuruṣāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dharmaḥ / laukikalokottaraparahitasukhavidhānam / tatsevakaṃ kāyam alpārthanimittaṃ na pīḍayet / anyathā mahato 'rtharāśerhāniḥ syāt / ata eva pūrvasmin hetupadametat / kutaḥ punarevam? yasmādanenaiva sukumāropakrameṇa saṃvardhamānaḥ śīghrameva sattvānāṃ hitasukhasaṃpādanasamartho bhavati //
body.translated_text: 'True' — of good persons, of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Their '<s>Dharma</s>' — the provision of benefit and happiness to others, both worldly and supramundane. The body that 'serves' that should not be tormented 'for a trifling purpose.' Otherwise, there would be loss of a great mass of purpose. Therefore, this [statement] is a causal ground for the preceding [verse]. Why is this so? Because, through this very gentle approach, one who grows [in practice] quickly becomes capable of accomplishing the benefit and happiness of beings.

body.text: yata evaṃ tasmāt-
body.translated_text: Since it is thus, therefore —

children.translated_text: One should not sacrifice one's life when the compassionate intention is impure;

children.text: tulyāśaye tu tattyājyamitthaṃ na parihīyate // Bca_5.87 //
children.translated_text: but when the intention is equal [or superior], it should be sacrificed — thus one is not diminished. // Bca_5.87 //

body.text: svaśarīraśirodānādi na kartavyamiti niṣiddham / kadā? aśuddhe mitrāmitretarasarvavyasanijanasādhāraṇapravṛtte kṛpācitte / atyārabdhena hi vīryeṇa svaparahitārthasya bādhā syāt / samapravṛtte punarāśaye svaparātmano 'tirikte vā na niṣidhyate / yaduktam- tathā svaparabodhipakṣaśrutādyantarāyakarau tyāgātyāgau na kāryau / adhikasattvārthaśaktestulyaśaktervā
body.translated_text: The giving of one's own body, head, and so forth should not be done — it is prohibited. When? When the compassionate mind is impure — operating commonly toward friend, enemy, and neutral, [and toward] all persons in calamity. For through overly strenuous vigor, harm would come to the purpose of one's own and others' welfare. But when the intention operates equally [toward all], or exceeds [that standard] regarding oneself and others, it is not prohibited. As stated: 'Thus, the giving up or not giving up [of the body] should not be done when it would create obstacles to the factors of awakening, learning, and so forth, for oneself and others. For one whose power to benefit beings is superior or equal —'

body.text: bodhisattvasya adhikatulyakuśalāntarāyakarau tyāgātyāgau na kāryāviti siddhaṃ bhavati / idameva ca saṃdhāya bodhisattvaprātimokṣe 'bhihitam- yastu khalu punaḥ śāriputra abhiniṣkrāntagṛhāvāso bodhisattvo bodhyaṅgairabhiyuktaḥ, tena kathaṃ dānaṃ dātavyam, kataraṃ dānaṃ dātavyam, kiyadrūpaṃ dānaṃ dātavyam / peyālaṃ / dharmadāyakena bhavitavyam / yaśca śāriputra gṛhī bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇi saptaratnaparipūrṇāni tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, yaśca śāriputra pravrajyāparyāpanno bodhisattvaḥ ekāṃ catuṣpadikāṃ gāthāṃ prakāśayet, ayameva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati / na śāriputra tathāgatena pravrajitasya āmiṣadānamanujñātam / peyālaṃ / yasya punaḥ śāriputra pātrāgataḥ pātraparyāpanno lābho bhaveddhārmiko dharmalabdhaḥ, tena sādhāraṇabhājinā bhavitavyaṃ sārdhaṃ sabrahmacāribhiriti //
body.translated_text: the giving up and not giving up that would obstruct superior or equal wholesome [factors] — for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — should not be done: this is established. And with reference to this very [point], it is stated in the <s>Bodhisattvapratimokṣa</s>: 'But, <s>Śāriputra</s>, what of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth from the household life and is engaged with the factors of awakening? By him, how should giving be practiced, what kind of giving should be practiced, how much giving should be practiced? In abbreviated form: he should be a giver of <s>Dharma</s>. And if, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a householder <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to give to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, filled with the seven precious substances — and if, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has gone forth were to illuminate a single four-line verse — this latter would generate far more merit. <s>Śāriputra</s>, material giving has not been permitted by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for one who has gone forth. In abbreviated form: But if, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a gain has come to one's bowl, an appropriate gain, a righteous gain obtained in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, one should share it in common with one's fellow practitioners.'

body.text: tatraivāha- yastu khalu punaḥ śāriputra anabhiniṣkrāntagṛhāvāso bodhisattvaḥ, tena dharma āsevitavyaḥ / tatra tenābhiyuktena bhavitavyamiti / anyathā hi ekasattvārthasaṃgrahārthaṃ mahataḥ sattvarāśestasya ca sattvasya bodhisattvāśayaparikarmāntarāyānmahato 'rthasya hāniḥ kṛtā syāditi //
body.translated_text: And there it is further stated: 'But, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has not gone forth from the household life — by him the <s>Dharma</s> should be cultivated; therein he should be diligent.' Otherwise, for the sake of gathering a single being, through creating an obstacle to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mental refinement [directed toward] a great mass of beings and that [single] being — there would be loss of a great purpose.

body.text: anenopāyakauśalena viharan na bodhimārgātparibhraśyate / ayamabhiprāyaḥ- dattaḥ pūrvameva anena ātmabhāvaḥ sarvasattvebhyaḥ / kevalamakālaparibhogātparirakṣaṇīyaḥ / ato na mātsaryasyāvakāśaḥ / nāpi pratijñātārthahāniriti / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: Dwelling with this skill in means, one does not fall from the path to awakening. This is the intent: one's personal existence has already been given previously to all beings. It is merely to be protected from untimely consumption. Therefore, there is no occasion for miserliness. Nor is there any loss of what was promised. As stated —

children.translated_text: 'Just as the seed of the medicinal tree <s>Sudarśana</s>, whose roots and such are for enjoyment,
[should be protected] — having given, it should be guarded from untimely consumption — so too the medicinal tree of the Perfectly Awakened One.'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: sattvāśayarakṣaṇādapyātmā rakṣitavya ityāha-
body.translated_text: From the [need for] protecting the aspirations of beings, too, oneself should be protected — he says —

children.text: dharmaṃ nirgaurave svasthe na śiroveṣṭite vadet /
children.translated_text: One should not teach the <s>Dharma</s> to one who is disrespectful, to one who is healthy [but wears] a head-covering,
nor to one with an umbrella, staff, or weapon, nor to one whose head is veiled. // Bca_5.88 //

body.text: devamanuṣyapūjito hi bhagavato dharmaḥ / tato 'vadhyāyanti devatādayo gauravamakurvato dharmaprakāśanāt / niṣiddhaṃ caitadbhagavatā iti tadājñātikrame sāpattiko bhavet / na vastrādibaddhaśirasi / sahaśabdena triṣvapi saṃbandhaḥ / tathottarīyādinā pihitaśīrṣe / pratyekaṃ svastha iti saṃbandhanīyam / glāne punaranāpattiḥ / upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat / na sthitena suptāya niṣaṇṇāya vā, na niṣaṇṇena suptāya, na cānāsanena niṣaṇṇāya / notpathayāyinā mārgayāyine, nāgragāmine pṛṣṭhagāminā, nāpyalaṃkārayuktāya / ityādayo 'pi draṣṭavyā iti //
body.translated_text: For the <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed One is honored by gods and humans. Therefore, deities and others censure one who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> without showing reverence. And this has been prohibited by the Blessed One; hence one who transgresses his command incurs a fault. Not to one with head bound by cloth and such. The word 'with' (<s>sa</s>) connects with all three [items]. Likewise, not to one whose head is covered by an upper garment and such. 'Healthy' should be connected with each separately. But there is no fault in the case of one who is ill. And this is merely illustrative: [one should not teach] while standing to one who is asleep or seated; not while seated to one who is asleep; not while without a seat to one who is seated; not while going by a side-path to one on the main road; not to one in front while [one is] behind; nor to one adorned [while one is not]. These and such [cases] should also be observed.

body.text: idamapyanarthavivarjanāya mūlāpattikāraṇamakaraṇīyamityāha-
body.translated_text: This too, for the avoidance of harm — what constitutes a root transgression should not be done — he says —

body.text: gambhīrodāramalpeṣu na strīṣu puruṣaṃ vinā /
body.translated_text: One should not [teach] the profound and exalted to those of small [capacity], nor to women without a man [present];

body.text: gambhīro durmedhasāmagādhatvāt / udāraśca prakarṣaparyantatvāt / tādṛśaṃ ca dharmamalpeṣu asaṃskṛtabuddhiṣu hīnādhimuktiṣu vā na vadediti prakṛtena saṃbandhaḥ / na mātṛgrāmasya ekākī rahogato dharmaṃ vadet / vadan sāpattiko bhavati / na doṣaḥ puruṣo yadi syāt //
body.translated_text: 'Profound' — because of being unfathomable to those of dull intellect. 'Exalted' — because of being at the extreme of excellence. Such <s>Dharma</s> one should not teach 'to those of small [capacity]' — to those of uncultivated intellect or of inferior aspiration: this connects with the main [subject]. One should not teach the <s>Dharma</s> to women alone, in private without others. One who does so incurs a fault. There is no fault if a man is present.

body.text: hīnotkṛṣṭeṣu dharmeṣu samaṃ gauravamācaret // Bca_5.89 //
body.translated_text: One should maintain equal reverence toward inferior and superior <s>Dharmas</s>. // Bca_5.89 //

body.text: śrāvakayānabhāṣiteṣu vā mahāyānabhāṣiteṣu vā dharmeṣu tulyaṃ cittaprasādādikaṃ kuryāt / anyathā saddharmapratikṣepaḥ syāt //
body.translated_text: Toward <s>Dharmas</s> taught in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> or taught in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, one should maintain equal faith and reverence of mind. Otherwise, there would be rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s>.

children.translated_text: One should not direct a vessel of the exalted <s>Dharma</s> toward an inferior <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: na cācāraṃ parityajya sūtramantraiḥ pralobhayet // Bca_5.90 //
children.translated_text: and one should not, abandoning conduct, entice with <s>sūtras</s> and <s>mantras</s>. // Bca_5.90 //

body.text: gambhīrodāradharmabhājanaṃ ca sattvaṃ nimittajñairjñātvā na śrāvakayānādidharmeṣvavatārayet / na ca ācāraṃ śikṣāsaṃvarakaraṇīyatāṃ muktvā sūtrāntādipāṭhenaiva tava śuddhirbhaviṣyati iti dharmakāmaṃ prabhāvayet / āha cātra- punaraparo 'nartho ratnakūṭe dṛṣṭaḥ- aparipāciteṣu sattveṣu viśvāso bodhisattvaskhalitam / abhājanībhūteṣu udārabuddhadharmaprakāśanā bodhisattvaskhalitam / udārādhimuktikeṣu sattveṣu hīnayānaprakāśanā bodhisattvaskhalitamiti //
body.translated_text: A being who is a vessel for the profound and exalted <s>Dharma</s>, having been recognized by those skilled in signs, should not be introduced into <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> and similar <s>Dharmas</s>. And one should not, abandoning conduct — the duties of the training-vow — deceive one desirous of <s>Dharma</s> by saying 'through mere recitation of <s>sūtras</s> and such, your purification will come about.' And it is stated here: 'Yet another harm is seen in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: trust in beings who have not been matured is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s stumbling. Teaching the exalted <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharma</s> to those who have not become vessels is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s stumbling. Teaching the inferior vehicle to beings of exalted aspiration is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s stumbling.'

body.text: āryasarvadharmavaipulyasaṃgrahe sūkṣmo 'pyanartha uktaḥ- sūkṣmaṃ hi mañjuśrīḥ saddharmapratikṣepakarmāvaraṇam / yo hi kaścinmañjuśrīḥ tathāgatabhāṣite dharme kasmiṃścit śobhanasaṃjñāṃ karoti, kvacidaśobhanasaṃjñām, sa saddharmaṃ pratikṣipati / tena saddharmapratikṣeptrā tathāgato 'bhyākhyāto bhavati, saṃgho 'pavādito bhavati, ya evaṃ vadati- idaṃ yuktamidamayuktam / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryasarvadharmavaipulyasaṃgraha</s>, even a subtle harm is stated: 'Subtle indeed, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the karmic obstruction of rejecting the true <s>Dharma</s>. If anyone, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, regarding <s>Dharma</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, forms the notion "beautiful" regarding some [of it] and the notion "not beautiful" regarding other [parts], he rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. By that rejecter of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is falsely accused, and the <s>Saṃgha</s> is disparaged — [by] one who says: "This is proper; this is improper."' Thus in detail.

body.text: āryākāśagarbhasūtre ca mūlāpattiprastāve coktam- punaraparamādikarmiko bodhisattvaḥ keṣāṃcidevaṃ vakṣyati- kiṃ bhoḥ prātimokṣavinayena? śīlena surakṣitena śīghraṃ tvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayasva / mahāyānaṃ paṭha / yatte kiṃcit kāyavāṅmanobhiḥ kleśapratyayādakuśalaṃ karma samudānītam, tena te śuddhirbhaviṣyatyavipākam, yāvadyathā pūrvoktam / iyamādikarmikasya bodhisattvasya tṛtīyā mūlāpattiriti //
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Āryākāśagarbhasūtra</s>, in the context of root transgressions, it is also stated: 'Furthermore, a beginner <s>Bodhisattva</s> will say to some: "What use is the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> discipline to you? Rather, with morality well-guarded, quickly generate the mind toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening! Study the <s>Mahāyāna</s>! Whatever unwholesome <s>karma</s> you have accumulated through body, speech, and mind due to defilements — through this your purification will come about, it will be without ripening" — and so forth as stated earlier. This is the third root transgression of a beginner <s>Bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: ataḥ idamapi prātimokṣaniṣiddhaṃ nācaraṇīyamityāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, this too, which is prohibited by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, should not be done — he says —

children.translated_text: The discarding of tooth-sticks and spittle uncovered

children.text: neṣṭaṃ jale sthale bhogye mūtrādeścāpi garhitam // Bca_5.91 //
children.translated_text: is not wished; urination and such in water, on usable ground, is also censured. // Bca_5.91 //

body.text: kheṭasya śleṣmaṇo visarjanamapāvṛtaṃ na kuryāt / jale sthale bhogye upabhogye mūtrapurīṣāderapi kutsitam / atrāpi devatādyavadhyānādapuṇyaṃ prasavet //
body.translated_text: The discarding of spittle — of phlegm — 'uncovered' — one should not do. In water, on usable ground, urination, defecation, and such are also condemned. Even in this, from the censure of deities and such, demerit would be produced.

children.translated_text: One should not eat with mouth overfull, noisily, or with mouth wide open;

children.text: pralambapādaṃ nāsīta na bāhū mardayetsamam // Bca_5.92 //
children.translated_text: one should not sit with legs dangling, nor should one rub both arms simultaneously. // Bca_5.92 //

body.text: mukhaṃ pūritaṃ kṛtvā mahatkavalagrahaṇāt / saśabdaṃ sukasunikādiśabdena / [prasṛtānanaṃ] dūraṃ vidāritamukham / pralambapādaṃ bhūmyādyalagnapādaṃ khaṭvādyārohaṇe sati nāsīta / dvāvapi bāhū samamekasmin kāle na mardayet / kramamardane na doṣaḥ / sati pratyaye //
body.translated_text: 'Mouth overfull' — from taking excessively large mouthfuls. 'Noisily' — with slurping and smacking sounds. '[With mouth wide open]' — mouth opened far apart. 'With legs dangling' — with legs touching the floor and such while climbing onto a bed and such, one should not sit. Both arms should not be rubbed simultaneously at the same time. In sequential rubbing, there is no fault — when there is occasion.

body.text: naikayānyastriyā kuryādyānaṃ śayanamāsanam /
body.translated_text: One should not travel, sleep, or sit alone with another's wife;

body.text: ekayā advitīyayā anyastriyā / gṛhipravrajitayoridamiha sādhāraṇamityanyagrahaṇam / na kuryādyānādi / saṃkṣepeṇa saṃkalayya darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: 'Alone' — without a second — with another woman. The word 'another' [indicates] this applies in common to both householders and renunciants. One should not travel and such. He shows [the principle] in summary, condensing —

body.text: lokāprasādakaṃ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭvā ca varjayet // Bca_5.93 //
body.translated_text: having seen and having asked, one should avoid everything that produces displeasure in people. // Bca_5.93 //

body.text: lokānāṃ yat prasādajanakaṃ na bhavati, tat sarva dṛṣṭvā śāstre vyavahāre vā / pṛṣṭvā vijñān / varjayet / anenaitaddarśitaṃ bhavati- dṛṣṭe 'pi yadbādhākaramevaṃvidhaṃ tadvarjayet āpattirbhavatīti / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: Whatever does not produce faith in people — all that, having seen in the scriptures or in actual practice, or having asked the wise, one should avoid. By this the following is shown: even regarding what is seen [to be permissible], if it causes harm of this kind, one should avoid it, [since] a transgression occurs. As stated —

children.translated_text: 'The summary restraint taught by the <s>Jina</s> in the <s>Ratnamegha</s>:
that which causes displeasure in beings, one should abandon with effort.'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: śikṣā. sa. kārikā-12
body.translated_text: <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 12

body.text: yathāha- katame ca te bodhisattvasamudācārāḥ? yāvadiha bodhisattvo nāghaḥsthāne viharati, nākāle / nākāle bhāṇī bhavati / nākālajño bhavati / nādeśajño bhavati / yatonidānamasyāntike sattvā aprasādaṃ pratisaṃvedayeyuḥ / sa sarvasattvānurakṣayā ātmanaśca bodhisaṃbhāraparipūraṇārthaṃ samyagīryāpatho bhavati, mṛdubhāṇī mandabhāṇī asaṃsargabahulaḥ pravivekābhimukhaḥ suprasannamukhaḥ iti //
body.translated_text: As stated: 'And what are those <s>Bodhisattva</s> modes of conduct? Insofar as here a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not dwell in a place of harm, not at an improper time; he is not one who speaks at an improper time; he is not ignorant of proper time; he is not ignorant of proper place — so that beings in his presence might not experience displeasure. He, for the sake of protecting all beings and fulfilling his own accumulation of awakening, has proper deportment: he is gentle in speech, moderate in speech, mostly free from association, inclined toward solitude, with a well-pleased countenance.' Thus.

body.text: na bodhisattvena avamanyanā kvacidapi kartavyetyāha-
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> should never show contempt anywhere — he says —

children.translated_text: One should not indicate anything with a [pointed] finger, but respectfully, with the right [hand],
with the entire palm — one should point out even the road thus. // Bca_5.94 //

body.text: ekayā aṅgulyā tarjanyādikayā na kiṃcidupadarśayet, api tu samastenaiva samagreṇaiva hastena / dakṣiṇena na vāmena / mārgamapi kathayet / āstāṃ tāvatsagauravaṃ vastu //
body.translated_text: With a single finger — the index finger and such — one should not point out anything; rather, with the entire — the complete — palm. With the right [hand], not the left. One should indicate even the road [thus]. How much more, then, something worthy of respect!

body.text: lokāprasādanivāraṇāyāha-
body.translated_text: For the prevention of producing displeasure in people, he says —

children.translated_text: One should not call anyone with an upflung arm when the matter is slight;
rather, one should snap the fingers and such; otherwise one would be unrestrained. // Bca_5.95 //

body.text: na bhujamutkṣipya kaṃcidāhvayet, alpaprayojanatāratamye / mahati punaradoṣaḥ / acchaṭādiśabdaṃ tu kuryāt / tadakaraṇe 'samāhitacāritāyāmasaṃvṛtaḥ syāt / etāvatā auddhatyaparihāro 'pi darśito bhavati //
body.translated_text: One should not summon anyone by raising the arm, in a matter of lesser importance. But in a great [matter], there is no fault. Rather, one should make a snapping sound of the fingers and such. If one does not do so, one would be unrestrained, in undisciplined conduct. By this, the avoidance of agitation is also shown.

body.text: sa hi śayyāṃ parikalpayannevaṃ parikalpayedityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: He shows how one preparing a bed should prepare it — he says —

children.translated_text: One should lie down in the desired direction, in the manner of the Lord's <s>nirvāṇa</s>-posture,
with introspective awareness, rising quickly — beforehand, determinedly, by resolution. // Bca_5.96 //

body.text: bhagavato mahānirvāṇaśayyāmiva śayyāṃ parikalpayet / abhimatayā diśā śiro vidhāya, dakṣiṇena pārśvena, pādasyopari pādamādhāya, dakṣiṇaṃ bāhumupadhānaṃ kṛtvā, vāmaṃ ca
