body.translated_text: One should prepare one's bed like the posture of the Blessed One's great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>: placing the head in the desired direction, [lying] on the right side, placing foot upon foot, making the right arm the pillow, and

body.text: prasārya jaṅghopari niveśya, cīvaraiḥ susaṃvṛtakāyaḥ, smṛtaḥ, saṃprajānānaḥ, utthānasaṃjñī, ālokasaṃjñī, śayitaḥ, nācittakamiddhāvaṣṭabdhaḥ / na ca nidrāsukhamākhādayet, na ca pārśvasukham anyatra yāvadevaiṣāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ sthitaye yāpanāyai iti / laghutthānaḥ śīghramevottiṣṭhet / na tu jṛmbhikāṃ gātramoṭanaṃ kurvannālasyopahitaścireṇa / etebhya eva sarvebhyaḥ pūrvameva //
body.translated_text: extending the left [arm] and placing it upon the thigh; with body well-covered by robes; mindful; with introspective awareness; with the perception of rising; with the perception of light; one should sleep — not sunk in torpor without [mental] intention. And one should not indulge in the pleasure of sleep, nor in the pleasure of lying on one's side — only for the maintenance and sustenance of these great elements. 'Rising quickly' — one should rise promptly; not slowly, overcome by laziness while yawning and stretching the limbs. [One should arise] before all these very [indulgences].

body.text: idamaparamabhisaṃkṣipya kathayannāha-
body.translated_text: He states this further, summarizing —

children.translated_text: The conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> has been declared to be immeasurable;
one should definitely practice at least the conduct that purifies the mind. // Bca_5.97 //

body.text: ācāraḥ śikṣaṇīyam / aprameyaḥ asaṃkhyeyaḥ bodhisattvaprātimokśādiṣu pradarśitaḥ / tatsaṃgraharūpaṃ prathamataḥ cittaśodhanameva ācāramācaret / niyatamavaśyaṃtayā //
body.translated_text: 'Conduct' — what should be trained in. 'Immeasurable' — innumerable, as shown in the <s>Bodhisattvapratimokṣa</s> and such. In the form of a summary of that, primarily, one should practice the conduct that is the purification of the mind alone. 'Definitely' — necessarily.

body.text: sāmānyāpattiśodhanāyāha-
body.translated_text: For the purification of general transgressions, he says —

children.text: rātriṃdivaṃ ca triskandhaṃ triṣkālaṃ ca pravartayet /
children.translated_text: Day and night, one should perform the three-section [confession] three times;
the remaining transgressions are pacified by this, through reliance on <s>bodhicitta</s> and the <s>Jinas</s>. // Bca_5.98 //

body.text: triṣkṛtvo rātreḥ / triṣkṛtvo divasasya / triskandhaḥ trayāṇāṃ skandhānāṃ pāpadeśanāpuṇyānumodanābodhipariṇāmanānāṃ samāhāraḥ / triskandhaṃ pravartayet / śeṣā mūlāyā anyāḥ / athavā, saṃcitya kṛtā yāḥ pratikṛtāḥ tābhyo 'nyāḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣeṇa asaṃprajānatā vā kṛtāḥ / tāsāṃ praśamaḥ pratikaraṇaṃ tena triskandhaparivartanena bodhicittasya jinānāṃ ca bhagavatāṃ samāśrayaṇācca //
body.translated_text: Three times during the night; three times during the day. '<s>Triskandha</s>' — the collection of the three sections: confession of evil, rejoicing in merit, and dedication to awakening. One should perform the <s>triskandha</s>. 'The remaining' — those other than root [transgressions]. Or alternatively, those other than deliberately committed and counteracted [transgressions] — those done through lapse of mindfulness or without introspective awareness. Their 'pacification' — their remedy — is through that performance of the <s>triskandha</s>, and through reliance on <s>bodhicitta</s> and the <s>Jinas</s>, the Blessed Ones.

body.text: etena vidūṣaṇāsamudācārādayo darśitā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: By this, misconduct and such [modes of behavior] are [also] shown.

body.text: tatra pāpaśodhanaṃ caturdharmakasūtre deśitam-
body.translated_text: There, the purification of evil has been taught in the <s>Caturdharmasūtra</s> —

body.text: caturbhirmaitreya dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṛtopacitaṃ pāpamabhibhavati / katamaiścaturbhiḥ? yaduta vidūṣaṇāsamudācāreṇa, pratipakṣasamudācāreṇa, pratyāpattibalena, āśrayabalena ca / tatra vidūṣaṇāsamudācāraḥ akuśalaṃ karma kṛtvā vipratisārarūpātsavigarhaṇā pāpadeśanā, tadanuṣṭhānaṃ tatsamudācāraḥ / tatra pratipakṣasamudācāraḥ akuśalapratipakṣaḥ kuśalam, tatsamudācāraḥ, kṛtvāpyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale karmaṇyatyantamabhiyogaḥ / tatra pratyāpattibalaṃ saṃvarasamādānādakaraṇasaṃvaralābhaḥ / tatrāśrayabalaṃ buddhadharmasaṃghaśaraṇagamanam, anutsṛṣṭabodhicittatā ca / sa balavatsaṃniśrayeṇa na śakyate pāpenābhibhavitum / ebhirmaitreya caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṛtopacitaṃ pāpamabhibhavatīti //
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> overcomes accumulated evil. Which four? Namely: by the practice of censure, by the practice of the antidote, by the power of restraint, and by the power of reliance. There, the practice of censure is: having performed unwholesome <s>karma</s>, the confession of evil with self-reproach in the form of remorse — that is its observance, that is its practice. There, the practice of the antidote is: the wholesome, which is the antidote to the unwholesome — that is its practice; even after performing unwholesome <s>karma</s>, one applies oneself intensely to wholesome action. There, the power of restraint is: the obtaining of restraint through non-commission by undertaking the precepts. There, the power of reliance is: taking refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, and not abandoning <s>bodhicitta</s>. One who has a strong foundation cannot be overcome by evil. <s>Maitreya</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> endowed with these four <s>dharmas</s> overcomes accumulated evil.

body.text: viśeṣatastu bodhisattvāpattīnāṃ gurvīṇāṃ ladhvīnāṃ ca deśanā āryopāliparipṛcchāyāmuktāḥ / tāḥ śikṣāsamuccaye draṣṭavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: In particular, the confession of <s>Bodhisattva</s> transgressions, both grave and light, has been stated in the <s>Āryopāliparipṛcchā</s>. Those should be seen in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>.

body.text: sarvāpattayo bodhisattvena pañcatriṃśatāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmantike rātriṃdivamekākinā deśayitavyāḥ / tatreyaṃ deśanā- ahamevaṃnāmā buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmītyārabhya yāvat saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi, namaḥ śākyamunaye tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya / namo vajrapramardine ityārabhya yāvat-
body.translated_text: All transgressions should be confessed by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone, day and night, in the presence of the thirty-five Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. There, this is the confession: 'I, named so-and-so, take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>' — beginning thus, up to 'I take refuge in the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' 'Homage to <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Homage to <s>Vajrapramardin</s>' — beginning thus, up to —

body.text: upaimi sarvān śaraṇaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ /
body.translated_text: 'I approach all for refuge, with palms joined.'

body.text: iti vistaramuktvāha- iti hi śāriputra bodhisattvena imān pañcatriṃśato buddhān pramukhān kṛtvā sarvatathāgatānugatairmanasikāraiḥ pāpaviśuddhiḥ kāryā / tasyaivaṃ pāpaviśuddhasya ta eva buddhā bhagavanto mukhānyupadarśayanti / peyālaṃ / na tat śakyaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhanikāyairāpattikaukṛtyasthānaṃ viśodhayituṃ yadbodhisattvasteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ nāmadheyadhāraṇaparikīrtanena rātriṃdivaṃ triskandhakadharmaparyāyapravartanena āpattikaukṛtyānniḥsarati, samādhiṃ ca pratilabhate //
body.translated_text: Thus, having spoken at length, he says: 'Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having placed these thirty-five <s>Buddhas</s> foremost, should accomplish the purification of evil through mental attentions following all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. When his evil is thus purified, those very Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> reveal their faces to him.' In abbreviated form. 'It is not possible for all the assemblies of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> to purify the place of remorse for transgression, from which a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by holding and proclaiming the names of those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, by performing the three-section <s>dharma</s>-discourse day and night, emerges from the remorse of transgression and also attains <s>samādhi</s>.'

body.text: etatsākalyena śikṣāsamuccaye veditavyam //
body.translated_text: This should be understood in its entirety from the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>.

body.text: ukto vidūṣaṇāsamudācāraḥ / pratipakṣasamudācārapratyāpattibale api vistareṇa śikṣāsamuccayādeva draṣṭavye / āryamaitreyavimokṣe tu bodhicittena pāpaviśuddhiruktā / taccoktameva prāk / jināśrayāt pāpaviśuddhau sūkarikāvadānamudāhāryam /
body.translated_text: The practice of censure has been stated. The practice of the antidote and the power of restraint should also be seen in detail from the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> itself. In the <s>Āryamaitreyavimokṣa</s>, however, the purification of evil through <s>bodhicitta</s> is stated — and that has already been stated before. Regarding purification of evil through reliance on the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Sūkarikāvadāna</s> (Parable of the Sow) should be cited.

children.text: ye buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ yānti na te gacchanti durgatim /
children.translated_text: Those who take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s> do not go to lower realms;

children.text: prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyāṃllabhanti te //
children.translated_text: having left behind human bodies, they obtain divine bodies.

body.text: evaṃ dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ cādhikṛtya pāṭhaḥ / anenāśrayabalamuktam //
body.translated_text: Likewise the reading applies with reference to the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>. By this, the power of reliance has been stated.

body.text: punaraniyamena darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Further, showing [the training] without restriction, he says —

children.text: yā avasthāḥ prapadyeta svayaṃ paravaśo 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever situations one may enter, whether by oneself or under the power of another,

children.text: tāsvavasthāsu yāḥ śikṣāḥ śikṣettā eva yatnataḥ // Bca_5.99 //
children.translated_text: in those situations, whatever trainings [apply], one should train in those very ones with effort. // Bca_5.99 //

body.text: svayamātmanā parāyatto vā sattvārthakriyāyāṃ pravṛttaḥ //
body.translated_text: By oneself — on one's own — or dependent on others, engaged in activity for the welfare of beings.

body.text: kiṃ punarevamaniyamenābhidhīyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Why then is it stated thus without restriction? He says —

children.text: na hi tadvidyate kiṃcidyanna śikṣyaṃ jinātmajaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For there is nothing whatsoever that the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> should not train in;

children.text: na tadasti na yatpuṇyamevaṃ viharataḥ sataḥ // Bca_5.100 //
children.translated_text: there is nothing that is not meritorious for such a one who abides thus. // Bca_5.100 //

body.text: yasmāt sarvākāraṃ sarvavastutattvamadhigamya sarveṣāṃ hitasukhavidhānārthamudyacchadbhirbuddhasutaiḥ na tadasti kiṃcit, yanna śikṣitavyam / anyathā sarvākāraḥ sarvasattvānāmarthaḥ kartumaśakyaḥ / puṇyasaṃbhāro 'pi evaṃ vicarato 'paryanta eva syāt //
body.translated_text: Since for the sons of the <s>Buddha</s> who exert themselves to provide benefit and happiness for all, having comprehended the reality of all things in all aspects, there is nothing whatsoever that should not be trained in — otherwise, the welfare of all beings in all aspects could not be accomplished. Even the accumulation of merit for one who conducts oneself thus would be limitless.

body.text: iyamapi śikṣāpadamudrā avadhārayitavyetyāha-
body.translated_text: This too is a seal of the training rules that should be retained — he says —

children.translated_text: One should not engage in anything other than the welfare of beings, whether directly or indirectly;

children.text: sattvānāmeva cārthāya sarvaṃ bodhāya nāmayet // Bca_5.101 //
children.translated_text: and for the welfare of beings alone, one should dedicate everything toward awakening. // Bca_5.101 //

body.text: antataḥ svayamāhārādikriyayā parapreraṇayā aparāparadūtapreraṇayā vā, sākṣāt svayameva āmiṣadānādinā vā, yat sattvānāṃ hitasukhaheturna bhavati, tanna kuryāt kārayedvā / na caitadeva kevalam / kiṃcit sattvānāmeva saṃsāraduḥkhapatitānāṃ tato niḥsaraṇāya sarvaṃ kuśalamūlamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayet //
body.translated_text: At the very least, through one's own activities such as eating, or through urging others, or through sending successive messengers, or directly by oneself through material gifts and such — whatever does not become a cause of benefit and happiness for beings, that one should not do nor cause to be done. And not only this: one should dedicate all roots of virtue toward unsurpassed perfect awakening for the sake of beings alone, who have fallen into the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, for their deliverance therefrom.

body.text: etāvatā ślokadvayena puṇyavṛddhirupadarśitā bhavati //
body.translated_text: By this much, through two verses, the increase of merit has been demonstrated.

body.text: yaduktaṃ kalyāṇamitrānutsargāditi [śikṣā. sa. kārikā-6] tadāha-
body.translated_text: As stated, 'from not abandoning the spiritual friend' [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 6] — regarding that, he says —

children.text: sadā kalyāṇamitraṃ ca jīvitārthe 'pi na tyajet /
children.translated_text: One should never abandon the spiritual friend, even at the cost of one's life —
one who upholds the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vow, who is skilled in the meaning of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. // Bca_5.102 //

body.text: kalyāṇakarmaṇi abhyudayaniḥśreyasaprāptilakṣaṇe mitramasādhāraṇo bandhuḥ, tat kāyajīvitavipraṇāśabhayabhīto 'pi na tyajet / kalyāṇamitrānuśaṃsāśca prajñāpāramitāyāmāryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ [aṣṭa. 30] sadāpraruditaparivartādveditavyāḥ / caturdharmakasūtre 'pyuktam- kalyāṇamitraṃ bhikṣavo bodhisattvena mahāsattvena yāvajjīvaṃ na tyaktavyamapi jīvitahetoriti / aparityājyasya kalyāṇamitrasya lakṣaṇamāha- bodhisattvaśikṣāsaṃvare vyavasthitam / mahāyānārthapaṇḍitam / etādṛśaṃ sudurlabham //
body.translated_text: A 'spiritual friend' — a friend in virtuous action characterized by the attainment of prosperity and highest good — an extraordinary companion: that one should not be abandoned even when frightened by danger to body and life. The benefits of a spiritual friend should be understood from the chapter on <s>Sadāprarudita</s> in the <s>Āryāṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>. In the <s>Caturdharmasūtra</s> also it is stated: 'Monks, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should not abandon the spiritual friend for as long as one lives, even for the sake of life.' He states the characteristics of the spiritual friend who should not be abandoned: one established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training-vow; learned in the meaning of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; such a one is extremely rare.

body.text: kalyāṇamitrasya paryupāsanaparijñānārthamāha-
body.translated_text: For the purpose of understanding the attendance upon a spiritual friend, he says —

body.text: śrīsaṃbhavavimokṣācca śikṣedyadguruvartanam /
body.translated_text: From the <s>Śrīsaṃbhavavimokṣa</s>, one should learn proper conduct toward the teacher.

body.text: śrīsaṃbhavavimokṣāt āryagaṇḍavyūhaparivartāt kalyāṇamitraparyupāsanaṃ śikṣet jānīyāt / yathoktamāryagaṇḍavyūhe āryaśrīsaṃbhavena- kalyāṇamitrasaṃdhāritāḥ kulaputra bodhisattvā na patanti durgatiṣu / yāvat- saṃcodakāḥ kalyāṇamitrā akaraṇīyānām / saṃnivārakāḥ pramādasthānāt / niṣkāsayitāraḥ saṃsārapurāt / tasmāttarhi kulaputra evaṃmanasikārāpratiprasrabdhena kalyāṇamitrāṇyupasaṃkramitavyāni / pṛthivīsamacittena sarvabhārodvahanāparitasanatayā / vajrasamacittena abhedyāśayatayā / cakravālasamacittena sarvaduḥkhāsaṃpravedhanatayā / lokadāsasamacittena sarvakarmasamādānāvijugupsanatayā / rajoharaṇasamacittena mānābhimānavivarjanatayā / yānasamacittena gurubhāranirvāhanatayā / aśvasamacittena akrudhyanatayā / nausamacittena gamanāgamanāparitasanatayā / suputrasadṛśena kalyāṇamitramukhavīkṣaṇatayā / ātmani ca te kulaputra āturasaṃjñotpādayitavyā kalyāṇamitreṣu ca vaidyasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu bhaiṣajyasaṃjñā, pratipattiṣu vyādhinirghātanasaṃjñā / ātmani ca te kulaputra bhīrusaṃjñotpādayitavyā, kalyāṇamitreṣu śūrasaṃjñā, anuśāsanīṣu praharaṇasaṃjñā, pratipattiṣu śatrunirghātanasaṃjñā //
body.translated_text: From the <s>Śrīsaṃbhavavimokṣa</s> — the chapter from the <s>Āryagaṇḍavyūha</s> — one should learn, should understand, attendance upon the spiritual friend. As stated in the <s>Āryagaṇḍavyūha</s> by the noble <s>Śrīsaṃbhava</s>: 'Son of good family, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are sustained by spiritual friends do not fall into lower realms.' Up to: 'Spiritual friends are exhorters away from what should not be done; restrainers from occasions of heedlessness; expellers from the city of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore, son of good family, with mental attention unrelaxed, one should approach spiritual friends: with a mind like the earth, through not being wearied by bearing all burdens; with a mind like a diamond, through indestructible intention; with a mind like the surrounding mountains, through not being shaken by all sufferings; with a mind like a worldly servant, through not feeling disgust at undertaking all tasks; with a mind like a dust-remover, through abandoning pride and conceit; with a mind like a vehicle, through carrying heavy loads; with a mind like a horse, through not becoming angry; with a mind like a boat, through not being wearied by coming and going; with a mind like a good son, through gazing at the face of the spiritual friend. And you, son of good family, should generate the perception of being sick toward yourself, and the perception of physician toward spiritual friends, the perception of medicine toward their instructions, and the perception of curing disease toward practice. And you, son of good family, should generate the perception of being timid toward yourself, the perception of hero toward spiritual friends, the perception of weapons toward their instructions, and the perception of slaying enemies toward practice.'

body.text: yaduktaṃ sūtrāṇāṃ ca sadekṣaṇāditi [śikṣā. sa. kā.-6], tadupadarśayitumāha-
body.translated_text: As stated, 'and from constant examination of the <s>sūtras</s>' [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 6] — to demonstrate that, he says —

body.text: etaccānyacca buddhoktaṃ jñeyaṃ sūtrāntavācanāt // Bca_5.103 //
body.translated_text: This and other things spoken by the <s>Buddha</s> should be known from the reading of <s>sūtras</s>. // Bca_5.103 //

body.text: etadiha śāstre pratipāditam, anyadyadiha noktam / buddhena bhagavatā bodhisattvānāṃ karaṇīyatayā nirdiṣṭam, tannānāsūtrāntārthaparicayād veditavyam //
body.translated_text: This which has been set forth in this treatise, and that other which has not been stated here — what has been taught by the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> as what should be done by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — that should be understood through familiarity with the meaning of the various <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: etadeva darśayati-
body.translated_text: He demonstrates this very point —

body.text: śikṣāḥ sūtreṣu dṛśyante tasmātsūtrāṇi vācayet /
body.translated_text: The trainings are seen in the <s>sūtras</s>; therefore one should recite the <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: śikṣā bodhisattvānāṃ heyopādeyalakṣaṇāḥ / sūtreṣu mahāyānasūtrānteṣu ratnameghādiṣu / yata evaṃ tasmāt / idaṃ tu viśeṣanirdeśamāha-
body.translated_text: The 'trainings' — for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, characterized by what is to be abandoned and what is to be adopted — are in the <s>sūtras</s>, in <s>Mahāyāna sūtras</s> such as the <s>Ratnamegha</s> and others. Since this is so, therefore — but he states this particular instruction —

body.text: ākāśagarbhasūtre ca mūlāpattīrnirūpayet // Bca_5.104 //
body.translated_text: One should examine the root transgressions in the <s>Ākāśagarbhasūtra</s>. // Bca_5.104 //

body.text: āryākāśagarbhasūtre kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pañca mūlāpattayo nirdiṣṭāḥ / tathā sāmānyena ekā mūlāpattiḥ / tathā ādikarmikasya bodhisattvasya aṣṭau mūlāpattaya iti / tathā ca tatroktam- pañca kulaputra kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya mūlāpattayaḥ yābhirmūlāpattibhiḥ kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ sarvāṇi pūrvāvaropitāni kuśalamūlāni jhoṣayati / vastupatitaḥ parājitaḥ sarvadevamanuṣyasukhebhyaḥ apāyagāmī bhavati / katamāḥ pañca? yaḥ kulaputra kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ staupikaṃ vastu apaharati sāṃghikaṃ vā cāturdiśasaṃghe niryātitaṃ vā, svayaṃ vā apaharati hārayati vā / iyaṃ prathamā mūlāpattiḥ / evaṃ triyānabhāṣitadharmapratikṣepāt dvitīyā / pravrajitasya śīlavato duḥśīlasya vā kāṣāyāpaharaṇāt, gṛhasthakaraṇāt, kāyaprahārāt, cārake prakṣepāt, jīvitaviyojanādvā tṛtīyā / pañcānantaryeṣvanyatamakaraṇāccaturthī / mithyādṛṣṭeḥ, daśākuśalakarmapathasamādānāt, parasamādāpanādvā pañcamīti //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryākāśagarbhasūtra</s>, five root transgressions have been taught for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> who has received royal consecration. Likewise, one root transgression in common for all. Likewise, eight root transgressions for a beginner <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And there it is stated: 'Son of good family, there are five root transgressions of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> who has received royal consecration, by which root transgressions the consecrated <s>Kṣatriya</s> burns up all previously planted roots of virtue, falls from his position, is defeated, becomes a goer to lower realms [deprived] of all happiness of gods and humans. What are the five? Son of good family, a consecrated <s>Kṣatriya</s> who seizes <s>stūpa</s> property or <s>Saṃgha</s> property dedicated to the community of the four directions — who seizes it himself or causes it to be seized — this is the first root transgression. Likewise, the second is from rejecting the <s>Dharma</s> taught for the three vehicles. The third is from stripping the robes of a renunciant, whether virtuous or immoral, from making [them] a householder, from striking [their] body, from throwing [them] into prison, or from taking [their] life. The fourth is from committing any of the five acts of immediate [retribution]. The fifth is from wrong views, from adopting the ten unwholesome courses of action, or from causing others to adopt [them].'

body.text: tathā grāmabhedādikaraṇāt sarveṣāṃ sādhāraṇī caikā / tatraivoktam-
body.translated_text: Likewise, one [transgression] common to all, from causing division in a village and such. There too it is stated —

body.text: ādikarmikāṇāṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṛṇāṃ ca aṣṭau mūlāpattayaḥ, yāmirmūlāpattibhiḥ skhalitā ādikarmikā mahāyānasaṃprasthitāḥ sarvāṇi pūrvāropitānītyādi pūrvavat / katamā aṣṭau? ye sattvāḥ pūrvaduścaritahetunā asmin kliṣṭe pañcakaṣāye loke utpannāḥ, te itvarakuśalamūlāḥ / yāvat, teṣāmidaṃ paramaṃ gambhīraṃ śūnyatāpratisaṃyuktaṃ sūtrāntaṃ yāvadvistareṇāgrataḥ smārayanti prakāśayanti / te hi akṛtaśramā bālapṛthagjanāḥ śṛṇvanta utrasyanti, yāvad vivartayanti anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheścittam, śrāvakayāne cittaṃ praṇidadhati / eṣā ādikarmikasya bodhisattvasya mūlāpattiḥ prathamā, yayā mūlāpattyā ityādi pūrvavat / tasmādbodhisattvena parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāmāśayānuśayaṃ prathamaṃ jñātvā yathāśayānāṃ sattvānāmanupūrveṇa dharmadeśanā kartavyeti / sopāyāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodhervinivartya hīnayāne parasya cittamutpādayato dvitīyā / prātimokṣaśikṣāsaṃvaraṃ vihāya mahāyāne cittotpādamātreṇa tatpaṭhanena cāsya śuddhiprakāśanāt tṛtīyā / śrāvakādiyānasya tatphalasya gopananindāprakāśanāt, mahāyāne sarvaśuddhiprakāśanāt, pareṣāṃ tadvacanakaraṇāccaturthī / kīrtilābhādihetoḥ mahāyānapaṭhanādinā, tathā tatpratyayāt pareṣāṃ kutsānindādibhāṣaṇāt, ātmotkarṣaṇāt, uttaramanuṣyadharmopagamāt pañcamī / pāṭhamātreṇa gambhīradharmādhigamaprakāśanāt, pareṣāṃ tathaiva samādāpanāt ṣaṣṭhī / kṣatriyasya purohitāmātyacaṇḍālairye bhikṣavo daṇḍitā arthadaṇḍena sāṃghikaṃ staupikaṃ vā cāturdiśasāṃghikaṃ vā dravyamapahṛtya tebhya evopanāmayanti / te ca kṣatriyā ubhaye 'pi mūlāpattimāpadyante / iyaṃ saptamī / dharmādharmavivādanāpūrvaṃ śikṣāpraṇayanāt, tanmūlācāravipannānāṃ satkārāt, prahāṇikānāmupabhogaparibhogāṇyanyatra pariṇāmanāt ubhaye 'pi mūlāpattimāpadyante / iyamaṣṭamī //
body.translated_text: For beginner <s>kulaputras</s> (sons of good family) and <s>kuladuhitṛs</s> (daughters of good family) who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, there are eight root transgressions. By these root transgressions, beginners who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [lose] all previously planted [roots of merit] — and so forth as before. What are the eight? Those beings who have been born in this afflicted world of the five degenerations due to previous misconduct — they have weak roots of merit. As far as: for them, this supremely profound <s>sūtrānta</s> connected with <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is recited and explained in detail before them. Those foolish ordinary persons, not having exerted effort [in practice], upon hearing become terrified, and so forth up to: they turn away their minds from unsurpassed perfect awakening and set their minds upon the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>. This is the first root transgression of a beginner <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by which root transgression — and so forth as before. Therefore, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should first ascertain the dispositions and latent tendencies of other beings and other individuals, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> gradually according to the dispositions of beings. The second is turning others away from the skillful means of perfect awakening and generating in them the mind toward the inferior vehicle. The third is from abandoning the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> training-restraint and proclaiming purification through mere generation of the mind toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and recitation of it. The fourth is from concealing, disparaging, and proclaiming [the faults of] the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> and other vehicles and their fruits, and from proclaiming complete purification in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> alone, and from causing others to speak thus. The fifth is from reciting <s>Mahāyāna</s> texts and such for the sake of fame, gain, and so forth, and from thereby causing others to speak words of contempt and disparagement, from self-aggrandizement, and from claiming attainment of superhuman states. The sixth is from proclaiming through mere recitation the attainment of the profound <s>Dharma</s>, and from inducing others to do the same. The seventh: when monks are punished by the <s>kṣatriya</s>'s ministers, priests, or <s>caṇḍālas</s> with monetary punishment, and <s>Saṃgha</s> property or <s>stūpa</s> property or property belonging to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions is seized and given to those very [punishers] — both those <s>kṣatriyas</s> and [the accomplices] incur a root transgression. This is the seventh. The eighth: from establishing a training preceded by disputes about <s>Dharma</s> and non-<s>Dharma</s>, from honoring those whose conduct has declined on account of that, and from diverting the requisites and belongings of those devoted to abandonment [of defilements] elsewhere — both [parties] incur a root transgression. This is the eighth.

body.text: āsāṃ ca mūlāpattīnāṃ sukhagrahaṇārthaṃ śāstrakāropadarśitāḥ saṃgrahakārikā ucyante-
body.translated_text: For easy comprehension of these root transgressions, the summary verses composed by the author of the treatise are stated —

children.translated_text: From stealing the property of the <s>Three Jewels</s>, a transgression amounting to defeat is considered [the first];
the second, declared by the <s>Muni</s>, is rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
duḥśīlasyāpi vā bhikṣoḥ kāṣāyastainyatāḍanāt /
cārake vā vinikṣepādapapravrājanena ca //
body.translated_text: From stealing the saffron [robe] of a monk, even one of poor conduct, from beating him, from casting [him] into prison, or from causing [his] expulsion,

children.translated_text: from committing the five sins of immediate [retribution], from holding wrong views,
and from destroying villages and such — a root transgression is declared by the <s>Jina</s>.
From teaching <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) to beings whose minds are unprepared,
and from turning back from awakening those who have set out toward <s>Buddhahood</s>,
from abandoning the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> and enjoining [entry into] the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,
or from holding that the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> does not lead to the abandonment of desire and such,
or from causing others to hold [this], and again from displaying one's own virtues,
from disparaging others for the sake of gain, honor, and fame,
and again from falsely declaring 'I am one patient with the profound,'
or from causing ascetics to be punished, or from giving away [property] of the <s>Three Refuges</s>,
or from accepting what is being given [from such property], and again from abandoning <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility),
and from assigning the enjoyments of those in retreat to those engaged in recitation —
these are the root transgressions, causes of the great hells;
they should be confessed, standing before [the image of] the noble <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, in a dream.
From abandoning <s>bodhicitta</s>, from not giving to a petitioner,
from intense jealousy and greed, or from striking beings out of anger,
when earnestly entreated, one does not practice forbearance toward beings,
or from following others under the influence of defilements, or from proclaiming a semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s> —

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: tasminneva sūtre samuddharaṇamāsāmuktam //
body.translated_text: In that very <s>sūtra</s>, the remedy for these [transgressions] has been stated.

body.text: śikśāsamuccaye 'pi bodhisattvānāṃ karaṇīyamupadiṣṭamiti tadapi nirūpaṇīyamityāha-
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> also, the duties of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have been instructed, and that too should be examined — he says —

children.translated_text: The <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> must necessarily be consulted again and again,
since proper conduct is shown there in detail. // <s>Bca</s> 5.105 //

body.text: śikśāsamuccayo 'pi svayamebhireva kṛtaḥ / avaśyaṃ niyamena / draṣṭavyaḥ punaḥ punarasakṛt / abhyasanīya iti bhāvaḥ / kutaḥ? yasmāt satāṃ bodhisattvānām / ācaraṇamācāra itikartavyatā / tatra śikṣāsamuccaye / vistareṇa prabandhena / pradarśitaḥ vispaṣṭīkṛtya prakāśitaḥ, tasmāt //
body.translated_text: The <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> was also composed by this very [author] himself. 'Necessarily' — by rule. 'Must be consulted again and again' — not just once — the meaning is: it should be studied repeatedly. Why? Because the conduct — the duties — of the virtuous, of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, is shown in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> 'in detail' — in extenso — 'shown' — made clear and illuminated. Therefore.

body.text: yadi tasyābhyāse 'śaktiḥ, tadā-
body.translated_text: If one is incapable of studying that, then —

body.text: saṃkṣepeṇāthavā tāvatpaśyetsūtrasamuccayam /
body.translated_text: alternatively, one should at least briefly consult the <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s>;

body.text: nānāsūtraikadeśānāṃ vā samuccayamebhireva kṛtaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa paśyet vyavalokayet granthato 'rthato vā / atrāpi pūrvakameva prayojanam // yadi vā-
body.translated_text: The <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s>, a compilation of portions of various <s>sūtras</s>, also composed by this very [author], one should consult briefly — examine it in terms of text or meaning. Here too, the same purpose as before [applies]. Or alternatively —

body.text: āryanāgārjunābaddhaṃ dvitīyaṃ ca prayatnataḥ // Bca_5.106 //
body.translated_text: and the second [work], composed by the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, with effort. // <s>Bca</s> 5.106 //

body.text: āryanāgārjunapādairnibaddhaṃ dvitīyaṃ śikṣāsamuccayaṃ sūtrasamuccayaṃ ca paśyet prayatnataḥ ādarataḥ / yadiha na dṛśyate, tat tatra dṛśyate iti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: One should consult the second <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>, the <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s> composed by the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, 'with effort' — with diligence. The meaning is: what is not seen here [in the first] is seen there [in the second].

body.text: niyamena śikṣādarśane 'pi sākalyena sarveṣāmupayogamāha-
body.translated_text: Even in necessarily consulting the training, he states the usefulness for all in its completeness —

children.text: yato nivāryate yatra yadeva ca niyujyate /
children.translated_text: From what one is restrained, where, and what one is enjoined to do —
having consulted the training, one should practice that, for the sake of protecting the minds of people. // <s>Bca</s> 5.107 //

body.text: yato heyādakaraṇīyānnivāryate, na karaṇīyametaditi pratiṣidhyate / yatra śikśāsamuccaye sūtrasamuccaye vā / yadeva karma kartavyatayā niyujyate vidhīyate, tat prasiddhaṃ vihitaṃ vā / lokānāṃ cittamāśayaḥ tasya rakṣārtham, tadyathā vikopitaṃ na syāt / śikṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā śikṣāsamuccayādiṣu / pratipādaṃ samācaret, yatra yadyathā yujyate, tatra tathā vyavaharet / anyathā arthasaṃmūḍhavyavahārasya āpattikaśmalatā syāt //
body.translated_text: 'From what' — from the objectionable, from what should not be done — 'one is restrained' — one is prohibited, [told] 'this should not be done.' 'Where' — in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> or <s>Sūtrasamuccaya</s>. 'What' — whatever action 'is enjoined' — is prescribed as something to be done — that which is established or ordained. 'Of people' — their 'mind' is their disposition — 'for its protection' — so that it may not be disturbed. 'Having consulted the training' — in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> and such. 'One should practice' at every step — wherever and however it is appropriate, so should one conduct oneself. Otherwise, for one whose conduct is confused about the meaning, there would be the stain of transgression.

body.text: etāvatā ātmabhāvasya śuddhirākhyātā / yadāha-
body.translated_text: By this much, the purification of one's own person has been declared. As it is said —

children.translated_text: 'What is the purification of one's own person? The cleansing of evil and defilements,
in accordance with the word of the Perfectly Awakened One; in the absence of effort, one goes to the lower realms.'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: śikṣā. sa. kārikā-19
body.translated_text: <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 19

body.text: yaduktam- sadā smṛtisaṃprajanyacāriṇā bhavitavyamiti, tataḥ smṛteḥ svanāmnaiva svarūpaṃ pratītam / saṃprajanyasya tu na jñāyate kīdṛśamiti, tatsvarūpapratipattaye prāha-
body.translated_text: As was stated — 'one should always act with mindfulness and introspective awareness' — from that, the nature of mindfulness is understood by its very name. But the nature of introspective awareness (<s>saṃprajanya</s>) is not known — what is it like? To establish its nature, he says —

children.translated_text: This alone, in summary, is the characteristic of introspective awareness (<s>saṃprajanya</s>):
the repeated examination of the states of body and mind. // <s>Bca</s> 5.108 //

body.text: yatkāyāvasthāyāḥ cittāvasthāyāśca sarveryāpatheṣu pratyavekṣā nirūpaṇaṃ sarvavāraṃ yathā pratipāditaṃ prāk //
body.translated_text: The examination — the investigation — of the states of body and the states of mind, in all postures, at every turn, as has been explained before.

body.text: sarvametaduktaśikṣākauśalaṃ karmaṇā niṣpādayitavyaṃ na vacanamātreṇeti niyamayitumāha-
body.translated_text: All this instruction in skill regarding the training should be accomplished through action, not by mere words — to establish this, he says —

children.text: kāyenaiva paṭhiṣyāmi vākpāṭhena tu kiṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: I shall practice with the body itself; what will be accomplished by mere verbal recitation?
What will become of a sick person by merely reciting a medical treatise? // <s>Bca</s> 5.109 //

body.text: manaḥpūrvaṃgamatvāt kāyavyāpārasya, so 'pyanenaiva pratipāditaḥ / pratipattyā sarvaṃ saṃpādayiṣyāmi, na tu śabdamātraghoṣaṇayā niṣphalatvāditi bodhisattvena yatitavyam / kathamiva? vaidyakaśāstrādhyayanamātreṇa tatkriyāmakurvato vyādhigrastasya kiṃ phalaṃ niṣpatsyate? tāvanmātreṇa rogasya tasyāvinivṛtteḥ / na kiṃciditi bhāvaḥ / tasmāt sarvametat kriyānuṣṭhānena niṣpādayitavyamiti //
body.translated_text: Since the activity of the body is preceded by the mind, that too is established by this very [principle]. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> should strive [thinking]: 'I shall accomplish everything through practice, not through mere proclamation of words, since that is fruitless.' How so? For one who has merely studied the treatise on medicine but does not perform its procedures — what result will come about for one afflicted by disease? Since by that much alone the disease is not removed — the meaning is: nothing [comes of it]. Therefore, all this should be accomplished through the performance of action.

body.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ saṃprajanyarakṣaṇaṃ nāma pañcamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, named 'The Guarding of Introspective Awareness,' in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.

body.text: 6. kṣāntipāramitā nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: 6. The sixth chapter, named '<s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>' (The Perfection of Patience).

body.text: tadevaṃ bahudhā śīlaviśuddhiṃ pratipādya ātmabhāvādīnāṃ rakṣāṃ śuddhiṃ pratipādya śubhaviśuddhiṃ pratipādayitum, yaccoktam-
body.translated_text: Having thus taught the purification of morality in many ways, and having taught the protection and purification of one's own person and such, in order to teach the purification of virtue, and as was stated —

children.translated_text: 'One should be patient, one should listen, one should resort to the forest thereafter;
one should engage in meditative equipoise and cultivate contemplation of the impure and such.'

body.text: śikṣā. sa. kārikā-20
body.translated_text: <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 20

body.text: ityetacca abhidhātumupakramate sarvamityādinā-
body.translated_text: And to expound upon this, he begins with 'all this' and so forth —

children.translated_text: All this good conduct, generosity, worship of the <s>Sugatas</s>,
performed over thousands of <s>kalpas</s> — <s>pratigha</s> (hatred) destroys that. // <s>Bca</s> 6.1 //

body.text: sarvametaditi śīlasaṃvarasamādānaprasūtam / sucaritaṃ kuśalaṃ karma / dānaṃ trividham / sāmānyena sugatapūjanamapi trividham / kṛtam upārjitamanekaiḥ kalpasahasrairyat tat sarvaṃ pratighaḥ sattvavidveṣaḥ pratihanti nirdahati bahnilava iva tṛṇasaṃghātam //
body.translated_text: 'All this' — produced from undertaking the moral discipline. 'Good conduct' — wholesome <s>karma</s>. 'Generosity' — threefold. 'Worship of the <s>Sugatas</s>' — also threefold, in general. 'Performed' — accumulated over numerous 'thousands of <s>kalpas</s>' — all that, '<s>pratigha</s>' — hatred toward beings — 'destroys' — burns it up, like a great fire [consumes] a mass of straw.

body.text: āryamañjuśrīvikrīḍitasūtre cāha- pratighaḥ pratigha iti mañjuśrīḥ kalpaśatopacitaṃ kuśalaṃ pratihanti, tenocyate pratigha iti //
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Āryamañjuśrīvikrīḍitasūtra</s> it is said: '<s>Pratigha</s>, <s>pratigha</s>' — <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, it destroys merit accumulated over hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>; therefore it is called '<s>pratigha</s>.'

body.text: āryasarvāstivādinā paṭhyate- paśyatha bhikṣava etaṃ bhikṣuṃ keśanakhastūpe sarvāṅgena praṇipatya cittamabhiprasādayantam? evaṃ bhadanta / anena bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇā yāvatī bhūmirākrāntā, adhaścaturaśītiyojanasahasrāṇi, yāvat kāñcanavajramaṇḍalāntare yāvantyo vālikāḥ, tāvantyanena bhikṣuṇā cakravartirājyasahasrāṇi paribhoktavyāni / yāvat / athāyuṣmānupāliryena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat- yaduktaṃ bhagavatā asya bhikṣorevaṃ mahānti kuśalamūlāni / kutremāni bhagavan kuśalāni tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti? nāhamupāle evaṃ kṣatimupahatiṃ ca samanupaśyāmi yathā sabrahmacārī sabrahmacāriṇo 'ntike duṣṭacittamutpādayati / tatropāle imāni mahānti kuśalamūlāni tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti / tasmāttarhi upāle evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yaddagdhasthūṇāyāmapi cittaṃ na pradūṣayiṣyāmaḥ, prāgeva savijñānake kāye iti //
body.translated_text: According to the <s>Āryasarvāstivādins</s>, it is recited: 'Do you see, monks, this monk prostrating with his entire body before the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s> and generating faith in his mind? Yes, Venerable One. Monks, as much ground as this monk has covered, downward for eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s>, as far as the golden <s>vajra</s>-platform — as many grains of sand as there are — that many thousands of <s>Cakravartin</s> kingships shall this monk enjoy. And so forth. Then the venerable <s>Upāli</s>, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, said to the Blessed One: The Blessed One has declared that this monk has such great roots of merit. Where, O Blessed One, do these wholesome [roots] diminish, decline, and become exhausted? I do not see, <s>Upāli</s>, such destruction and harm as when a fellow practitioner generates a hostile mind toward a fellow practitioner. There, <s>Upāli</s>, these great roots of merit diminish, decline, and become exhausted. Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, one should train thus: "We shall not corrupt our minds even toward a burnt post, how much less toward a body endowed with consciousness."'

body.text: ata evāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore he says —

children.text: na ca dveṣasamaṃ pāpaṃ na ca kṣāntisamaṃ tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no evil equal to hatred, and no austerity equal to patience;
therefore one should cultivate patience with effort, by various methods. // <s>Bca</s> 6.2 //

body.text: na ca dveṣeṇa samaṃ pāpamaśubhaṃ puṇyābhibhavaheturasti / na ca kṣāntyā titikṣayā samaṃ tulyaṃ tapaḥ / sumahatpariśramasādhyatvāt sukṛtam / yata evam, tasmāt kṣāntiṃ kṣamāṃ sarvatātparyeṇa bhavayedabhyaset / vividhairnānāprakārairupāyairvakṣyamāṇaiḥ //
body.translated_text: There is no evil — no unwholesome [karma] — equal to hatred that is a cause of overpowering merit. And there is no austerity equal to — the same as — patience, forbearance. Since it is accomplished through very great exertion, it is a meritorious deed. Since this is so, therefore one should cultivate — practice — patience, forbearance, with complete devotion, by various — manifold — methods that will be explained.

body.text: dṛṣṭadharma eva dveṣasya doṣān vṛttatrayeṇopadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing the faults of hatred in this very life, through a triad of verses, he says —

children.text: manaḥ śamaṃ na gṛhṇāti na prītisukhamaśrute /
children.translated_text: The mind does not find peace, nor does it experience joy and happiness,

children.text: na nidrāṃ na dhṛtiṃ yāti dveṣaśalye hṛdi sthite // Bca_6.3 //
children.translated_text: nor does it find sleep or steadiness, when the thorn of hatred is lodged in the heart. // <s>Bca</s> 6.3 //
Even those dependents who are honored with wealth and respect,
even they wish to kill that master made wretched by hatred. // <s>Bca</s> 6.4 //
Even friends recoil from him; he gives but is not served;

children.text: saṃkṣepānnāsti tatkiṃcit krodhano yena susthitaḥ // Bca_6.5 //
children.translated_text: in short, there is nothing by which an angry person can be well-situated. // <s>Bca</s> 6.5 //

body.text: śamaṃ praśamaṃ na gṛhṇāti nāśrayate / anupaśānta eva sadā dveṣānalaprajvalitatvāt na prītisukhaṃ saumanasyasukhamaśnute āpnoti, tenaivākrāntatvāt / na nidrāṃ na dhṛtiṃ cittasukhaṃ labhate kāyacittasaṃtāpakāriṇi dveṣaśalye hṛdayanivāsini / pūjayati satkaroti lābhasatkārairyān / ye 'pi cānujīvinaḥ, evaṃ dveṣiṇaṃ svāminamapakartumicchanti / kimiti? dveṣadurbhagam apriyamiti hetupadametat / suhṛdo bhitrāṇyapi udvijante uttrasanti asmād dveṣiṇaḥ / dānonmukho 'pi bhṛtyavargairna sevyate nopagamyate / kiṃ bahunā? idamiha saṃkṣepeṇāvadhāryatām- nāsti tadupaśamakāraṇaṃ kiṃcidyena kopanaḥ sukhaṃ labheta //
body.translated_text: He does not grasp or resort to <s>śama</s> (tranquility) or <s>praśama</s> (deep peace). Being always unpeaceful, since he is ablaze with the fire of hatred, he does not experience or attain <s>prītisukha</s> (the pleasure of joy) or <s>saumanasyasukha</s> (the pleasure of gladness), being overwhelmed by that very [hatred]. He obtains neither sleep nor <s>dhṛti</s> (steadiness) — mental ease — when the thorn of hatred, which causes torment to body and mind, dwells in the heart. Even those whom he honors and treats with respect through gifts and honors — even those dependents [of his] — wish to harm such a hateful master. Why? 'Ill-fortuned through hatred, disagreeable' — this is the causal statement. Even intimate friends recoil and are frightened of this hateful person. Even when inclined to give, he is not served or approached by his retinue. In brief, let this be determined here in summary: there is no cause for its alleviation — nothing by which an angry person could obtain happiness.

body.text: cittasya karkaśāvasthā dveṣaḥ / tasyodbhūtavṛttistu krodhaḥ, yadvaśāt daṇḍādigrahaṇaṃ kriyate / iti anayorbhede 'pi dvayorapi parihartavyatayā abhedenaiva nirdeśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Hatred is the harsh state of mind. Its actively manifest form is anger (<s>krodha</s>), under whose power one resorts to seizing a stick and such. Thus, although these two are distinct, since both are to be abandoned, the instruction treats them as identical.

body.text: evamiha dṛṣṭadharme 'pi dveṣadoṣānavagamya tatparityāgāya yatnavatā bhavitavyamityāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus recognized the faults of hatred even in this present life, one should exert effort to abandon it — he says:

children.translated_text: Since [hatred], designated as 'the enemy,' produces such sufferings as these,

children.text: yaḥ krodhaṃ hanti nirbandhāt sa sukhīha paratra ca // Bca_6.6 //
children.translated_text: one who destroys anger with perseverance is happy here and hereafter. // Bca_6.6 //

body.text: evaṃ yathoktaprakāreṇa duḥkhāni janayati yasmāt, tasmād yaḥ sukṛtātmā nirbandhāt, gāḍhābhiniveśāt / ārabdhavīrya ityarthaḥ / sa sukhī ihaloke paraloke ca //
body.translated_text: Since it produces sufferings in the manner described, therefore one of virtuous nature who [destroys anger] 'with perseverance' — with firm determination — meaning one of aroused vigor — that one is happy in this world and in the next.

body.text: idānīṃ dveṣopaghātāya tatkāraṇamupahantuṃ vyavasthāṃ kurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, in order to strike at hatred, establishing the method for destroying its cause, he says:

children.translated_text: Born from the occurrence of the undesired and from the obstruction of the desired,

children.text: daurmanasyāśanaṃ prāpya dveṣo dṛpto nihanti mām // Bca_6.7 //
children.translated_text: having obtained the fuel of mental distress, hatred, emboldened, slays me. // Bca_6.7 //

body.text: tasmādvighātayiṣyāmi tasyāśanamahaṃ ripoḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore I shall destroy the fuel of that enemy.

body.text: ātmātmīyagrahaprasūte iṣṭāniṣṭe / ātmātmīyayoḥ sukhasādhanamiṣṭam, tadviparītamaniṣṭam, iti kalpanākṛtamevaitat / na tu paramārthataḥ kiṃcidiṣṭamaniṣṭaṃ vā saṃbhavati / tasmānmithyābhiniveśavāsanāvaśāt aniṣṭasya karaṇāt, iṣṭasya copahananād daurmanasyaṃ mānasaṃ duḥkhamupajāyate, tasmāt tatkāriṇi tadvirodhini vā dveṣa utpadyate / iti daurmanasyameva balabadbhojanaṃ
body.translated_text: The desired and undesired arise from grasping at self and what belongs to self. What serves as a means of happiness for self and what belongs to self is 'desired'; its opposite is 'undesired' — this is merely a product of conceptual construction. In ultimate reality, nothing desired or undesired whatsoever exists. Therefore, from the force of habitual tendencies of false attachment, from the occurrence of the undesired and from the obstruction of the desired, mental distress — mental suffering — arises; from that, toward what causes it or what opposes it, hatred arises. Thus, mental distress itself is [hatred's] powerful nourishment

body.text: labdhasāmarthyaḥ san dveṣo nihanti mām iti niścitya tatpuṣṭikāraṇaṃ ca haniṣyāmi prathamataḥ / tasmin hate sukhameva / tasya hananāt, samūlaghātaṃ hatasya punarutthānāyogācca //
body.translated_text: ; having gained strength, hatred slays me — having determined this, I shall first destroy the cause of its nourishment. When that is destroyed, there is only happiness. Because of its destruction, and because what is destroyed root and all cannot rise again.

body.text: nanu ko 'yamatyarthamabhiniveśo bhavata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Is not this excessive fixation of yours [unwarranted]? — he says:

body.text: yasmānna madvadhādanyatkṛtyamasyāsti vairiṇaḥ // Bca_6.8 //
body.translated_text: Since this enemy has no other task than my destruction. // Bca_6.8 //

body.text: yasmāt mama vadhaṃ vihāya rātriṃdivamaparaṃ na kiṃcid dveṣasya vairiṇaḥ karaṇīyamasti //
body.translated_text: Since, apart from my destruction, hatred — the enemy — has no other business to perform, day and night.

body.text: evaṃ dveṣadoṣān vibhāvya sarvopāyena tadvipakśabhūtāṃ kṣāntimutpādayet / tatra kṣāntistrividhā dharmasaṃgītisūtre 'bhihitā / tadyathā- duḥkhādhivāsanākṣāntiḥ, dharmanidhyānakṣāntiḥ, parāpakāramarṣaṇakṣāntiśca / tatra tāvadduḥkhādhivāsanākṣāntimadhikṛtyāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus discerned the faults of hatred, one should generate <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), which is its antidote, by every means. Therein, patience is threefold, as stated in the <s>Dharmasaṃgītisūtra</s>: namely, <s>duḥkhādhivāsanākṣānti</s> (patient endurance of suffering), <s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s> (patient contemplation of dharmas), and <s>parāpakāramarṣaṇakṣānti</s> (patient forbearance of others' harm). Regarding the first of these, <s>duḥkhādhivāsanākṣānti</s>, he says:

children.translated_text: Even upon the arrival of the extremely undesired, my cheerfulness should not be disturbed;
for even in mental distress there is nothing desired [gained], while wholesome [merit] is indeed diminished. // Bca_6.9 //

body.text: duḥkhādhivāsanākṣāntivipakṣaḥ aniṣṭāgamaprāptaduḥkhabhīrutā, iṣṭavighātaprāptaśca sukhābhiṣvaṅgaḥ / tābhyāṃ daurmanasyam / tato dveṣo līnacittatā vā / ata evāha candrapradīpasūtresukhe 'nabhiṣvaṅgaḥ, duḥkhe 'vaimukhyam / iti / ratnameghasūtre 'pyuktam- ya ime ādhyātmikāḥ śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ, tān kṣamate adhivāsayatīti //
body.translated_text: The adversary of <s>duḥkhādhivāsanākṣānti</s> (patient endurance of suffering) is timidity toward suffering arising from the occurrence of the undesired, and attachment to pleasure arising from the obstruction of the desired. From these two arises mental distress; from that, hatred or mental depression. Therefore it is stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s>: 'Non-attachment to pleasure, non-aversion to suffering.' It is also said in the <s>Ratnameghasūtra</s>: 'Whatever internal sorrows, lamentations, sufferings, mental distresses, and despairs there are — these one endures, these one patiently bears.'

body.text: ato yadi nāma mama śiraśchidyate, tathāpi na kṣobhyā na vikopayitavyā muditā mayā / muditā hi daurmanasyapratipakṣaḥ / duḥkhāgame 'pi pramuditacittasya daurmanasyānavakāśāt, iti daurmanasyanirāsāya muditā yatnena rakṣitavyā / kutaḥ? daurmanasye 'pi kṛte iṣṭavighāte sati nāstīṣṭaṃ nābhilaṣitaṃ setsyati / ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ syāt- kuśalaṃ punarupahanyate //
body.translated_text: Therefore, even if my head is cut off, my cheerfulness should not be disturbed or agitated. For cheerfulness is the antidote to mental distress. Even upon the arrival of suffering, for one whose mind is cheerful there is no occasion for mental distress; thus, to dispel mental distress, cheerfulness should be diligently guarded. Why? Even when mental distress arises — when the desired is obstructed — what is desired will not come to pass. But this distinction would exist: wholesome [merit] is further destroyed.

body.text: muditā ca āryākśayamatisūtre varṇitā- tatra katamā muditā? yā buddhadharmāṇāmanusmaraṇāt prītiḥ prasādaḥ prāmodyaṃ cittasyānavalīnatā anavamṛdyatā aparitarṣaṇatā, sarvakāmaratīnāmapakarṣaṇāt sarvadharmaratīnāṃ pratiṣṭhānam, cittasya prāmodyam, kāyasyaudvilyam, buddheḥ saṃpraharṣaṇam, manasa utpalavaḥ, tathāgatakāyābhinandanaratiḥ / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Muditā</s> (joy) is described in the <s>Āryākṣayamatisūtra</s>: 'What therein is <s>muditā</s>? That which is delight, serenity, gladness from recollecting the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>; non-depression of mind, non-crushing, non-craving; the uprooting of all sensual pleasures and the establishment of all pleasures in the <s>Dharma</s>; gladness of mind, exhilaration of body, jubilation of the intellect, blossoming of the mind, delight and pleasure in the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Thus in detail.

body.text: kiṃ cedamavicārayato daurmanasyamutpadyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: What if mental distress arises without deliberation? — he says:

children.translated_text: If there is indeed a remedy, then what is the use of mental distress?

children.text: atha nāsti pratīkāro daurmanasyena tatra kim // Bca_6.10 //
children.translated_text: And if there is no remedy, then what is the use of mental distress? // Bca_6.10 //

body.text: yadi ca iṣṭavighātanivartanāya aniṣṭopanipātapratiṣedhāya ca pratīkāraḥ upāyāntaramasti, tadā daurmanasyena tatra kim? tadeva anuṣṭhīyatām / atha nāsti, tadāpi daurmanasyena tatra kim? na kiṃcit prayojanam / upāyābhāvāt sarvathā gatametat / iti vicārya daurmanasyanivartanameva varam //
body.translated_text: If there is a remedy — an alternative means — for averting the obstruction of the desired and for preventing the onset of the undesired, then what is the use of mental distress? Let that very [remedy] be undertaken. And if there is none, then too what is the use of mental distress? There is no purpose whatsoever, since there is no means [available]. It has gone beyond [help] in every way. Having reflected thus, the cessation of mental distress alone is preferable.

body.text: abhyāsād duḥkhamabādhakaṃ bhavatīti prasādhayitumupakramate-
body.translated_text: He begins to establish that through habituation, suffering becomes non-afflicting:

children.translated_text: Suffering, humiliation, harsh words, disrepute — these are undesired
for one's dear ones and oneself, and for one's enemy it is the reverse. // Bca_6.11 //

body.text: duḥkhaṃ kāyikaṃ mānasikaṃ ceti dvividham / tatra kāyikaṃ daṇḍādighātajam / mānasikaṃ nyakkārādinimittam / tatra nyakkāro dhikkāraḥ / pārūṣyaṃ marmaghaṭṭanāvacanam / ayaśaśca akīrtiḥ vaiguṇyaprakāśanam / ityetatsarvamanabhilaṣitam / yadi pareṣāṃ śivaṃ nanu? tadarthamāha- priyāṇām / ātmīyatvena ye svīkṛtāḥ, premasthānaṃ teṣāmātmanaśca / duḥkhādikārakasya punaḥ śatroretadviparyayāt / tasya duḥkhādikamabhīṣṭameva //
body.translated_text: Suffering is twofold: physical and mental. Among these, physical [suffering] arises from blows with sticks and such. Mental [suffering] has humiliation and such as its causes. Among these, 'humiliation' is disparagement. '<s>Pāruṣya</s>' (harshness) is speech that strikes at vital points. And 'disrepute' is the disclosure of faults. All this is unwished for. But if it is beneficial for others? To address that he says: 'for one's dear ones' — those accepted as one's own through affection, those who are the objects of love — and for oneself. But for the enemy — for the one who causes suffering and such — it is the reverse: suffering and such for him are indeed desired.

body.text: tatra duḥkhasahiṣṇutāṃ tāvannirākartumāha-
body.translated_text: Regarding endurance of suffering, in order to refute [the objection against] it, he says:

children.translated_text: Happiness is obtained only with difficulty; suffering remains effortlessly.

children.text: duḥkhenaiva ca niḥsāraḥ cetastasmād dṛḍhībhava // Bca_6.12 //
children.translated_text: Only through suffering is there liberation; therefore, O mind, be firm! // Bca_6.12 //

body.text: mahatā prāyatnena kuśalapakṣamupasevya kadācit karhicit sudurlabhaṃ saṃsāre sāsravaṃ sukhaṃ labhyate / duḥkhaṃ tu sarvadā sulabham, ayatnasiddhatvāt, iti tadabhyāso na duṣkaraḥ, sarvadā paricitatvāt / kiṃ ca / saṃsāraniḥsaraṇopāyo 'pi duḥkhameva / tathāpi pātheyarūpatayā tatparigraho yukta eva / yata evam, tasmāt he citta, duḥkhānubhavanāya dṛḍhībhava, mā kātaratāmāśrayasva //
body.translated_text: Through great effort, by cultivating the wholesome side, sometimes, on rare occasions, the extremely difficult to obtain conditioned happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s> is obtained. But suffering is always easily available, being accomplished without effort; therefore its habituation is not difficult, since it is always familiar. Moreover, the very means of escape from <s>saṃsāra</s> is suffering itself. Even so, its acceptance as provisions [for the journey] is entirely appropriate. Since this is so, therefore, O mind, be firm for the experience of suffering — do not resort to timidity!

body.text: api ca / idaṃ duḥkhaṃ mahārthasādhakatvāt soḍhumucitam, iti manasi kartavyam, ityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, this suffering should be borne because it accomplishes a great purpose — thus it should be held in mind, he says:

children.translated_text: The sons of <s>Durgā</s> and the <s>Karṇāṭas</s> endure the pain of burning, cutting, and such

children.text: vṛthā sahante muktyarthamahaṃ kasmāttu kātaraḥ // Bca_6.13 //
children.translated_text: in vain; for the sake of liberation, why then am I timid? // Bca_6.13 //

body.text: durgāputrakāḥ caṇḍīsutāḥ / mahānavamīsamayādiṣu trirātramekāhaṃ vā upoṣya gātradāhacchedanabhedanaṃ kurvanto duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ niṣphalamevānubhavanti / tathā karṇāṭadeśādisamudbhūtā dākṣiṇātyā uparināmalikhanamātrābhimānataḥ parasparaṃ spardhamānā anekābhiḥ kāraṇābhirduḥkhamanubhavanto jīvitamapyutsṛjanti / ahaṃ tu svaparātmanoḥ paramadurlabhabuddhatvasādhanāya kṛtotsāhaḥ duḥkhaiḥ kasmāt kāraṇāt kātarībhavāmi?
body.translated_text: The 'sons of <s>Durgā</s>' are the devotees of <s>Caṇḍī</s>. During the great <s>Navamī</s> festival and such occasions, having fasted for three nights or one day, they perform burning, cutting, and piercing of their limbs, experiencing painful sensations entirely without fruit. Likewise, those born in the <s>Karṇāṭa</s> region and such — southerners — out of pride in mere scarification on the upper body, competing with one another, experience suffering through numerous tortures and even abandon their lives. But I, who have aroused determination for the attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s>, supremely difficult to obtain, for myself and others — why should I become timid on account of sufferings?

body.text: syādetat- atyalpaduḥkhaṃ kathaṃcitsoḍhuṃ śakyate / karacaraṇaśiraśchedanādiduḥkhaṃ narakādiduḥkhaṃ vā muktayarthaṃ kathaṃ nu soḍhavyamityatrāha-
body.translated_text: It might be said: extremely slight suffering can somehow be endured, but how can the suffering of having hands, feet, and head cut off, or the suffering of the hells and such, be endured for the sake of liberation? To this he says:

children.translated_text: There is nothing whatsoever that remains difficult through practice;
therefore, through practice of mild pain, even great pain should be endured. // Bca_6.14 //

body.text: śāstrābhyāsakalādi kauśalādi mṛdumadhyātimātraduḥkhānubhavanādi vā vastu na tadvidyate kiṃcit yadabhyāsagocaro na bhavati / sarvameva abhyāsādātmasātkartuṃ śakyata iti bhāvaḥ / yasmāt tasmāt atyalpatarādivyathābhyāsānnarakādimahāvyathāpi soḍhuṃ [śakyate] / yathoktam- tatra alpaduḥkhābhyāsapūrvakaṃ kaṣṭakaṣṭatarābhyāsaḥ sidhyati / yathā ca abhyāsavaśāt
body.translated_text: Whether it be the study of scriptures, mastery of arts, or the experience of mild, moderate, and intense suffering — there exists nothing whatsoever that does not come within the scope of practice. Everything can indeed be made one's own through practice — this is the meaning. Since this is so, therefore, through practice of extremely slight pain, even the great pain of the hells and such can be endured. As it is said: 'Therein, through prior practice of slight suffering, practice of increasingly difficult [levels] is accomplished.' And just as through the power of practice

body.text: sattvānāṃ duḥkhasukhasaṃjñā, tathā sarvaduḥkhotpādeṣu sukhasaṃjñāpratyupasthānābhyāsāt sukhasaṃjñaiva pratyupatiṣṭhate / evaṃ niṣpandaphalaṃ ca sarvadharmasukhākrāntaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate / uktaṃ hi pitāputrasamāgame-
body.translated_text: beings develop the perception of pleasure [even] in suffering, so through practice of establishing the perception of pleasure in all arising of suffering, the perception of pleasure alone comes to be established. Thus one attains the <s>samādhi</s> called 'overwhelmed by the happiness of all dharmas,' which yields the fruit of complete stillness. For it is stated in the <s>Pitāputrasamāgama</s>:

body.text: asti bhagavan sarvadharmasukhākrānto nāma samādhiḥ, yasya samādheḥ pratilambhād bodhisattvaḥ sarvārambaṇavastuṣu sukhāmeva vedanāṃ vedayate na duḥkhām, nāduḥkhasukhām / tasya nairayikāmapi vedanāṃ kāryamāṇasya sukhasaṃjñaiva pratyupasthitā bhavati / mānuṣīmapi kāraṇāṃ kāryamāṇasya, hasteṣvapi chidyamāneṣu pādeṣvapi karṇeṣvapi nāsāsvapi, sukhasaṃjñaiva pratyupasthitā bhavati / vetrairapi tāḍyamānasya ardhavetrairapi kaśābhirapi tāḍayamānasya sukhasaṃjñā pravartate / bandhanāgāreṣvapi prakṣiptasya, tailapācikāṃ vā kriyamāṇasya, ikṣukuṭṭitikaṃ vā kuṭyamānasya, naḍacippitikaṃ vā cipyamānasya, tailapradyotikaṃ vā ādīpyamānasya yāvat kārṣāpaṇacchedikāṃ chidyamānasya piṣṭapācanikāṃ vā pācyamānasya, hastibhirvā mardyamānasya sukhasaṃjñaiva pravartate // iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'There is, Blessed One, a <s>samādhi</s> called "overwhelmed by the happiness of all dharmas." Upon attaining that <s>samādhi</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> experiences only pleasant feeling regarding all objects and bases — not painful, not neutral. Even when experiencing the sensation of hell-beings, the perception of pleasure alone is present. Even when experiencing human tortures — even when hands are being cut off, feet, ears, or noses — the perception of pleasure alone is present. Even when being beaten with canes, half-canes, or whips, the perception of pleasure operates. Even when thrown into prison, or when the oil-cooking [torture] is being performed, or when being crushed in the sugarcane-press, or when being split in the reed-splitter, or when being burned in the oil-lamp [torture], or even when being cut with the coin-cutter, or when being cooked in the flour-cooker, or when being trampled by elephants — the perception of pleasure alone operates.' Thus in detail.

body.text: syādevaitad yadi prathamata eva mṛduvyathābhyasaḥ syāt / yāvatā sa eva nāstīti / atrāha-
body.translated_text: It might be [objected]: this would apply if one had prior practice of mild pain; but that very [practice] does not exist. To this he says:

children.translated_text: The sensations of gadflies, biting flies, mosquitoes, hunger, thirst, and such,

children.text: mahatkaṇḍvādiduḥkhaṃ ca kimanarthaṃ na paśyasi // Bca_6.15 //
children.translated_text: and great suffering of itching and the like — why do you not see [these as] purposeful? // Bca_6.15 //

body.text: uddaṃśādikṛtaduḥkhamanarthaṃ kiṃ na paśyasi? tadayatnasiddhaṃ mṛduvyathābhyāsanimittamastyeva iti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: The suffering caused by gadflies and such — why do you not see [it as] purposeful? The meaning is: that very [practice of] mild pain, effortlessly obtained, which serves as the basis for habituation, does indeed exist.

body.text: punaranyathā svacittaṃ draḍhayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Again, to strengthen one's mind in another way, he says:

children.translated_text: Through cold, heat, rain, wind, travel, sickness, bondage, and beatings,

children.text: saukumāryaṃ na kartavyamanyathā vardhate vyathā // Bca_6.16 //
children.translated_text: one should not cultivate delicacy; otherwise, distress increases. // Bca_6.16 //

body.text: sukumārataracittasya hi duḥkhamatitarāṃ bādhakaṃ bhavati, duḥkhe 'pi dṛḍhacittasya viparyayaḥ //
body.translated_text: For one whose mind is excessively delicate, suffering becomes exceedingly afflicting; but for one whose mind is firm even in suffering, it is the opposite.

body.text: nanu dṛḍhīkaraṇe 'pi cittasya duḥkhamasahyameveti / atrāha-
body.translated_text: But even with a firmed mind, suffering is still unbearable — to this he says:

children.translated_text: Some, seeing their own blood, become especially valorous;

children.text: paraśoṇitamapyeke dṛṣṭvā mūrcchāṃ vrajanti yat // Bca_6.17 //
children.translated_text: while others, seeing even another's blood, faint. // Bca_6.17 //
This comes from the firmness or timidity of the mind.
One who is difficult to conquer by suffering would therefore overcome pain. // Bca_6.18 //

body.text: na khalu dṛḍhacittasya kiṃcidaśakyaṃ nāma / tathāhi- kecidvīrapuruṣāḥ saṃgrāmabhūmau svaśoṇitamapi paśyanto 'dhikataraṃ śauryamābhajante / kecitpunaḥ kātaracittasaṃtatayaḥ pararudhiradarśanādapi
body.translated_text: Indeed, for one of resolute mind nothing is impossible. For example — certain heroic men, seeing even their own blood on the battlefield, take on even greater valor. But others, of timid mental dispositions, even from seeing another's blood

body.text: maraṇāntikaṃ duḥkhamanubhavanti / etadubhayamapi cittasya itaretarābhyāsaviparyayāt iti matvā duḥkhaduryodhano nādhigamyo bhavet, duḥkhairapyakampyatvāt / tato 'bhibhaved vyathām, na punastayāmibhūyate //
body.translated_text: experience suffering unto death. Both of these are due to the reversal of respective habituations of the mind — knowing this, one should become '<s>duḥkha-duryodhana</s>' (difficult to conquer by suffering), being unshakable even by sufferings. Therefore one should overcome pain, and not be overwhelmed by it. //

body.text: itthamapyabhibhaved vyathāmityāha-
body.translated_text: Even so, one should overcome pain — he says —

children.text: duḥkhe 'pi naiva cittasya prasādaṃ kṣobhayed budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in suffering, a wise person should not disturb the serenity of the mind;

children.text: saṃgrāmo hi saha kleśairyuddhe ca sulabhā vyathā // Bca_6.19 //
children.translated_text: for the battle is with the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and in battle, pain is easily [encountered]. // Bca_6.19 //

body.text: prasādaṃ pūrvoktaṃ nāvasādayedvicakṣaṇaḥ / kutaḥ? yasmāt kleśaśatrubhiḥ saha saṃgrāmo 'yamārabdhaḥ / saṃgrāme ca vyathā nāma na bhavediti durlabham, vyathā tu sulamaiva //
body.translated_text: 'Serenity' — as described before — the discerning one should not allow to decline. Why? Because this battle has been undertaken with the enemies that are the <s>kleśas</s>. And in battle, that there would be no pain is rare — rather, pain is easy indeed. //

body.text: nanu tathāpi duṣkaramidamatīva dṛśyata iti / atrāha-
body.translated_text: But even so, this appears to be extremely difficult — to this he says —

children.translated_text: Those who, receiving the blows of enemies upon the chest, conquer their foes —

children.text: te te vijayinaḥ śūrāḥ śeṣāstu mṛtamārakāḥ // Bca_6.20 //
children.translated_text: they indeed are the victorious heroes; the rest are merely slayers of the dead. // Bca_6.20 //

body.text: abhimukhamabhibhavantaḥ śatrum / tatprahārān vakṣaḥsthalena pratīcchanto ye jayanti samare ripūn, te te śūrapuruṣāḥ pararipuvijayādiha labdhavijayāḥ praśasyante / ye punaranye chalaprahārādibhirabhibhavanti śatrum, te ca akiṃcitkaratayā mṛtamārakā jugupsanīyā eva śūraiḥ //
body.translated_text: Confronting the enemy face to face — those who, receiving their blows upon the chest, conquer foes in battle — they indeed, those heroic men, having obtained victory here through conquest of the opposing enemy, are praised. But others who overcome the enemy through deceptive strikes and such — they, being of no consequence, are 'slayers of the dead,' despicable to the truly brave. //

body.text: ito 'pi guṇadarśanādduḥkhamadhivāsayitavyamityāha-
body.translated_text: From this further perception of virtue, suffering should be endured — he says —

children.translated_text: Another virtue of suffering is that through <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency), pride falls away;

children.text: saṃsāriṣu ca kāruṇyaṃ pāpadbhītirjine spṛhā // Bca_6.21 //
children.translated_text: compassion [arises] toward beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>, fear of evil, and longing for the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). // Bca_6.21 //

body.text: ayamaparaḥ śubhaheturguṇo duḥkhasyāsya saṃbodhimārgānukūlaḥ, yadduḥkhasya samāveśe manasi saṃvega upajāyate / tasmācca yauvanadhanādikṛtasya madasya cyutirbhaṅgo jāyate, saṃsāriṣu ca saṃsāraduḥkhapīḍitesu karuṇācittam, pāpasya phalamidamiti matvā pāpād bhayamakaraṇacittaṃ ca, buddhe ca bhagavati spṛhā bhaktiḥ śraddhā cittaprasādaśca / bhagavāneva hi duḥkhakṣayagāminaṃ mārgamupadiṣṭavāniti //
body.translated_text: This is another virtue of suffering that is a wholesome cause conducive to the path of awakening: that when suffering pervades the mind, <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency) arises. From that, the fall — the destruction — of pride produced by youth, wealth, and such occurs; and compassion of mind toward those in <s>saṃsāra</s> who are afflicted by the suffering of cyclic existence; and fear of evil — the thought of non-commission — knowing 'this is the fruit of sin'; and toward the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, longing, devotion, faith, and mental serenity. For it is the Blessed One alone who has taught the path leading to the cessation of suffering. //

body.text: parapratyayotpannaduḥkhādhivāsanāya parāmṛśannāha-
body.translated_text: For the endurance of suffering arising from the actions of others, he reflects and says —

children.translated_text: I do not become angry at <s>pitta</s> (bile) and such, even though they cause great suffering;

children.text: sacetaneṣu kiṃ kopaḥ te 'pi pratyayakopitāḥ // Bca_6.22 //
children.translated_text: why then anger at sentient beings? They too are provoked by conditions. // Bca_6.22 //

body.text: pittādidoṣatrayātmakameva śarīram / te ca tathāvidhāhāravihāravaiguṇyād viṣamāvasthāṃ prāptā vyādhīn janayantaḥ sarvaduḥkhahetavo bhavanti / tathāpi na teṣu mama kopaḥ, acetanatvāt / na te saṃcintya duḥkhadāyakāḥ, kiṃ tarhi svakāraṇasāmagrībalena prakopamupāgatāḥ / yadyevam, sacetaneṣu kiṃ kopaḥ? kiṃ na syāditi cet, te 'pi pūrvakarmāparādhāt svakāraṇasāmagrīprakopitā duḥkhadāyakā bhavanti / iti pittādivat teṣvapi na yujyate mama krodhaḥ //
body.translated_text: The body itself is constituted of the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors) — <s>pitta</s> (bile) and such. These, having reached a disordered state through deficiency of proper diet and behavior, generate diseases and become causes of all suffering. Yet I do not become angry at them, because they are non-sentient. They do not deliberately cause suffering; rather, they become agitated by the force of their own causal conditions. If this is so, why then anger at sentient beings? If one objects that there should be — they too, through the fault of prior <s>karma</s>, are provoked by the assemblage of their own causal conditions and become inflicters of suffering. Therefore, just as with <s>pitta</s> and such, anger toward them too is not justified. //

body.text: ubhayatrāpi samānaṃ kāraṇādhīnatvamityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: That the dependence on causes is the same in both cases — showing this, he says —

children.translated_text: Just as a thorn arises even though unwished for,
so too anger arises forcibly even though unwished for. // Bca_6.23 //

body.text: svapratyayopajanitasāmarthyebhyaḥ pittādibhyo 'nabhipretamapi śūlamavaśyamutpadyate yathā, tathā svahetumapariṇāmādhigataśaktibhyo daurmanasyādibhyaḥ krodha utpadyate, iti sādhāraṇamanayorhetupratyayādhīnatvam //
body.translated_text: Just as from <s>pitta</s> and such, which possess power generated by their own conditions, a thorn [of pain] inevitably arises even though unintended, so too from mental distress and such, which have acquired power through the maturation of their own causes, anger arises — thus the dependence on causes and conditions is common to both. //

body.text: atha syāt- uktamatra sacetanāḥ saṃcintya tathāvidhāniṣṭakāriṇaḥ, na tu punaritare tathetyāha-
body.translated_text: Now one might say — sentient beings intentionally perform such unwished-for actions, but the others do not act thus — to this he says —

children.text: kupyāmīti na saṃcintya kupyati svecchayā janaḥ /
children.translated_text: A person does not become angry having deliberately thought 'I shall be angry';

children.text: utpatsya ityabhipretya krodha utpadyate na ca // Bca_6.24 //
children.translated_text: nor does anger arise having intended 'I shall arise.' // Bca_6.24 //

body.text: tatpratyayasāmagrīmantareṇa kupyāmītyevaṃ buddhipūrvakaṃ saṃcintya na janaḥ svairaṃ prakupyati / krodho 'pi utpatsya ityabhisaṃghāya svātantryeṇa naivotpadyate //
body.translated_text: Without the assemblage of conditions for anger, a person does not deliberately, having thought 'I shall be angry,' become angry of their own will. Anger too does not arise independently, having planned 'I shall arise.' //

body.text: tasmādidamevātra pramāṇasiddhamityāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore this alone is established by valid cognition — he says —

children.translated_text: Whatever offenses there are, and whatever various sins,

children.text: sarva tatpratyayabalāt svatantraṃ tu na vidyate // Bca_6.25 //
children.translated_text: all arise through the force of conditions; nothing independent exists. // Bca_6.25 //

body.text: idaṃpratyayatāmātrasamupasthitasvabhāvaṃ sarvamidam / na tu svātantryapravṛttaṃ kiṃcidapi vidyate //
body.translated_text: All this is of such a nature as to exist merely through the condition of being dependent on this [or that cause]. But nothing whatsoever exists that operates through independence. //

children.translated_text: The assemblage of conditions does not have the intention 'I shall produce';

children.text: na cāpi janitasyāsti janito 'smīti cetanā // Bca_6.26 //
children.translated_text: nor does what is produced have the thought 'I have been produced.' // Bca_6.26 //

body.text: pratyayasāmagryapi na svakāryaṃ janayantī saṃcintya janayati / sā hi svahetupariṇāmopanidhidharmatayā tathāvidhaṃ kāryaṃ janayati na tu saṃcintya / na cāpi janitasya kāryasyāpi anayā sāmagryā janito 'smīti cetanā manasikāro 'sti / tasmānnirvyāpāratayā sarvadharmāṇām, asmin sati idaṃ bhavati, asyotpādādidamutpadyate, iti idaṃpratyayatāmātramidaṃ jagat, nātra kaścitsvatantraḥ saṃbhavati / hetupratyayādhīnatvātsarvadharmāṇām //
body.translated_text: The assemblage of conditions too, when producing its own effect, does not produce it deliberately. For it produces such an effect by the nature of the conditions arising from the maturation of its own causes — not deliberately. Nor does the produced effect have the intention, the mental engagement, 'I have been produced by this assemblage.' Therefore, since all <s>dharmas</s> are without agency — when this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises — this world is merely dependent on conditions, and no one independent is possible here. [This is] because all <s>dharmas</s> are dependent on causes and conditions. //

body.text: syādetat- astyeva svatantraṃ yathā sāṃkhyānāṃ pradhānamātmā ca, naiyāyikānāmākāśādayaḥ / tat kimucyate na kiṃcitsvatantramiha vidyate, ityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: One might object: something independent does indeed exist — such as <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Nature) and <s>Ātman</s> (Self) of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, and space and such of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>. Why then is it said 'nothing independent exists here'? — anticipating this, he says —

children.translated_text: What is supposedly accepted as <s>Pradhāna</s>, and what is imagined as <s>Ātman</s>,

children.text: tadeva hi bhavābhīti na saṃcintyopajāyate // Bca_6.27 //
children.translated_text: even that does not arise having deliberated 'I shall come into being.' // Bca_6.27 //

body.text: yattadbhavatāṃ sattvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthā prakṛtiḥ pradhānamityabhimatam / kileti pramāṇāsaṃgatametadityaruciṃ prakāśayati / yadapi tadvastu kiṃcidātmeti kalpitamadhyavasitaṃ pramāṇāsaṃgatameva / āha- yasmāttadeva svayameva tadaparakāraṇābhāvād bhavāmi samutpadya iti nābhisaṃdhāya jāyate /
body.translated_text: What you accept as <s>Prakṛti</s> (Primal Nature) — the equilibrium state of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — called <s>Pradhāna</s>. The word '<s>kila</s>' (supposedly) reveals disfavor, [indicating] this is unsupported by valid cognition. And whatever entity is imagined — determined — as <s>Ātman</s> — that too is equally unsupported by valid cognition. He says: since that very thing does not arise having resolved 'I shall come into being, having arisen,' because there is no other cause [for it to do so].

body.text: kutaḥ? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Why? Because —

body.text: anutpannaṃ hi tannāsti ka icchedbhavituṃ tadā /
body.translated_text: For when that has not arisen, it does not exist — who then would wish to come into being?

body.text: tat pradhānādi prāgasadeva / asataśca vandhyāsutāderiva kā bhavitumutpattumicchā bhavet? atha nāsadutpadyate kiṃcit, kevalamavyaktāvasthāto vyaktāvasthāyāṃ pariṇāmamātram / yadyevam, pariṇāmo 'pi kathamasannutpaṃdyate vyaktāvasthā vā? pariṇāmasya vyaktāvasthāyāśca tatsvabhāvatve tasyāpyutpattiprasaṅgaḥ / vyatireke saṃbandhābhāvaḥ / saṃbandhakalpanāyāṃ ca anavasthā / parato vistareṇa pradhānaṃ nirākariṣyate [9.127-138] //
body.translated_text: That — <s>Pradhāna</s> and such — is prior [to creation] simply non-existent. And for something non-existent, like the son of a barren woman, what wish to come into being — to arise — could there be? If one says nothing non-existent arises, [and that there is] merely a transformation from the unmanifest state to the manifest state — if so, how does the transformation arise as non-existent, or the manifest state? If the transformation and the manifest state are of the nature of that [Pradhāna], then the absurd consequence arises that it too would have origination. If they are different, there is no connection. And in the supposition of a connection, there is an infinite regress. <s>Pradhāna</s> will be refuted at length later [9.127-138]. //

body.text: syādetat- ātmanyayamadoṣa eva / na hi tasya vayamutpādamicchāmaḥ / sarvadā nityasvabhāvatayā anutpanna evāsau / bhavatu nāma evam / tathāpi sarvathā kharaviṣāṇakalpa evāsau, utpādābhāvāt / tato nātrāpi nivartate-
body.translated_text: One might say: with regard to <s>Ātman</s>, this is no fault at all. For we do not accept its origination. Being always of eternal nature, it is simply unoriginated. Let it be so! Even then, it is in every respect like the horn of a donkey, due to the absence of origination. Therefore, even here the [criticism] does not turn back —

body.text:
anutpannaṃ hi tannāsti ka icchedbhavituṃ tadā /
iti /
body.translated_text:
'For when that has not arisen, it does not exist — who then would wish to come into being?'
Thus.

body.text: bhāve 'pi vā nāsya svātmanyapi prabhutvamasti / prakṛtyupanāmitameva hi viṣayamapi sa bhuṅkte / tadā ca viṣayopabhogātprāk tadbhoktṛtvamasya nāsīt, paścādutpannaṃ ca tatsvabhāvameva / anyathā tasya bhoktṛtvāyogāt / tadutpāde ca tasyāpyutpāda iti kathaṃ nātmana utpāda iṣyata iti / tadevaṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: Or even if it exists, it has no sovereignty even over its own self. For it enjoys even sense-objects only as presented by <s>Prakṛti</s>. And then, prior to the enjoyment of sense-objects, its nature as experiencer did not exist — it arose afterward and is of that very nature. Otherwise, its being an experiencer would be impossible.
