children.text: puṣṇāti yastvayā poṣyaṃ tubhyameva dadāti saḥ /
children.translated_text: One who nourishes what should be nourished by you — he gives to you alone;

children.text: kuṭumbajīvinaṃ labdhvā na hṛṣyasi prakupyasi // Bca_6.82 //
children.translated_text: having found one who sustains your household, do you not rejoice but rather become angry? // <s>Bca</s> 6.82 //

body.text: tvayā poṣaṇīyaṃ priyaputrakādikaṃ tvadīyaṃ yaḥ puṣṇāti, sa tubhyameva dadāti / tavaiva tenopacayaḥ kṛto bhavet / ataḥ tvatkuṭumbajīvinaṃ tvadīyaṃ kuṭumbaṃ jīvayati yaḥ, taṃ tathāvidhaṃ puruṣaṃ labdhvā prāpya prahṛṣyasi na? kākvā pṛcchati- prakupyasi, na prahṛṣyase cetyarthaḥ / tathā prakṛte 'pi yena sarvasattvā ātmīyatvena gṛhītāḥ, tasya tatsukhaiḥ sukhamevocitamiti //
body.translated_text: One who nourishes what should be nourished by you — your dear children and such — he gives to you alone; by him alone has your prosperity been produced. Therefore, having found — having obtained — such a person who sustains your household — who keeps alive your dependents — do you not rejoice? He asks with irony: you become angry, meaning you do not rejoice. Likewise in the present context too: for one who has adopted all beings as one's own, happiness alone is fitting through their happiness.

body.text: syādetat- buddhatvameva tvayā teṣāṃ pratijñātam, na tu punaranyasukhamityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: [Objection:] It is <s>Buddhahood</s> alone that you have promised for them, not other forms of happiness. Anticipating this objection, he says —

body.text: sa kiṃ necchasi sattvānāṃ yasteṣāṃ bodhimicchati /
body.translated_text: Does he who wishes awakening for them not wish [this] for beings?

body.text: nanu etadapi na samyak / yasmāt-
body.translated_text: But this too is not correct, since —

body.text: jagadadya nimantritaṃ mayā sugatatvena sukhena cāntarā //
body.translated_text: 'I have today invited the world to <s>Sugata</s>-hood and to happiness in the interim.'

body.text: bodhi. 3.33
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>. 3.33

body.text: iti pratijñātam / bhavatu nāma evam, tathāpi yaḥ samutpāditabodhicittaḥ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhiṃ buddhatvamicchati, sa kimanyalaukikalokottaramarthajātaṃ necchati? atha naivamiṣyate, tadā bodhicittamapi hīyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: — thus it was promised. Granted it is so; nevertheless, does one who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s> and wishes awakening, <s>Buddhahood</s>, for those beings — does he not wish for them every other kind of worldly and supramundane benefit? If this is not accepted, then even <s>bodhicitta</s> itself is impaired. He says —

body.text: bodhicittaṃ kutastasya yo 'nyasaṃpadi kupyati // Bca_6.83 //
body.translated_text: How can there be <s>bodhicitta</s> in one who is angered by another's prosperity? // <s>Bca</s> 6.83 //

body.text: bodhicittaṃ kutastasya? mithyaiva bodhicittapratijñasya / kasya? yo 'nyasaṃpadi kupyati / itaravibhūtau lābhasatkāraprasūtāyām, iti marmacodanā bodhisattvasya kuśalakarmanivṛttihetuḥ //
body.translated_text: How can there be <s>bodhicitta</s> in such a one? — it is merely a false profession of <s>bodhicitta</s>. In whom? In one who is angered by another's prosperity — by another's wealth arising from gain and honor. This is a piercing rebuke to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, serving as a cause for the cessation of wholesome action [being obstructed].

body.text: api ca / aparasya lābhasatkārasaṃpadabhāve 'pi na bhavatastadbhāvasaṃbhavaḥ / tatkimakāraṇameva tadvidveṣiṇā ātmaghātāya yatnaḥ kriyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, even in the absence of another's attainment of gain and honor, there would be no such attainment for you. So why does one who harbors enmity toward that make effort toward self-destruction without cause? — showing this, he says —

children.text: yadi tena na tallabdhaṃ sthitaṃ dānapatergṛhe /
children.translated_text: If he had not obtained that, it would remain in the donor's house;

children.text: sarvathāpi na tatte 'sti dattādattena tena kim // Bca_6.84 //
children.translated_text: in any case it is not yours — whether given or not given, what is it to you? // <s>Bca</s> 6.84 //

body.text: yadi nāma tena tava akṣamāviṣayeṇa sattvena taddīyamānaṃ vastu na labdham, tathāpi sthitaṃ dānapatergṛhe / bhavatastu kiṃ tasmājjātam? sarvathāpi tena labdhena gṛhāvasthitena vā na tadvastu tavāsti / iti dattādattena te kim? na kiṃcit prayojanaṃ bhavataḥ / atastatra upekṣaiva yuktā viduṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Even if that being — the object of your intolerance — had not obtained the thing being given, still it would remain in the donor's house. And what has arisen from that for you? In any case, whether obtained by him or remaining in the house, that thing is not yours. So whether given or not given, what is it to you? Nothing whatsoever is your concern. Therefore, equanimity alone is fitting here for the wise.

body.text: kiṃ ca / idamapi tāvat paribhāvyatāmityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, showing that even this should be reflected upon, he says —

children.translated_text: Should he obstruct his merits, those who are favorably disposed, or his own virtues?

children.text: labhamāno na gṛhṇātu vada kena na kupyasi // Bca_6.85 //
children.translated_text: Should he, when receiving, not accept? Tell me — toward whom are you not angry? // <s>Bca</s> 6.85 //

body.text: yo 'sau atiprasannairdāyakadānapatiobhirlābhasatkāraiḥ pūjyate, sa kiṃ vārayatu puṇyāni pūrvajanmakṛtāni vipākonmukhāni, yadvaśāttasya lābhasatkārāḥ / uta prasannān dāyakadānapatīn vārayatu, atha svaguṇān vārayatu, yānāśritya eṣāṃ prasādo jātaḥ / mā prasādamapyeṣāṃ janayiṣyatheti / athavā / labhamāno 'pi tebhyo na svīkarotu / brūhi kena prakāreṇa atra na bhavato 'paritoṣaḥ syāt / tatra puṇyādīnāṃ vārayitumaśakyatvāt labhyamānāgrahaṇe 'pi sarvathāpi na tatte 'stītyādinā bādhakasyoktatvāditi na kiṃcit paritoṣakāraṇamasti //
body.translated_text: That person who is honored with gain and honor by exceedingly devoted donors and patrons — should he obstruct his merits, accumulated in previous lives and facing their ripening, by whose power he receives gain and honor? Or should he obstruct those who are favorably disposed — the devoted donors and patrons? Or should he obstruct his own virtues, relying upon which their faith arose — [saying] 'may you not even generate faith'? Or alternatively, even when receiving from them, should he not accept? Tell me, in what manner could there be no dissatisfaction for you? Since merits and such cannot be obstructed, and since even non-acceptance of what is received has been refuted by 'in any case it is not yours' and so forth — there is no ground for satisfaction at all.

body.text: athāpi syāt- parasyaiva lābhasatkārasaṃpattirasti, na mama / atha mama nāsti, tadā parasyāpi mā bhūt, ityetanmamāsaṃtuṣṭinibandhanamityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Another has the attainment of gain and honor, and I do not; since I do not have it, may the other not have it either — this is the basis of my dissatisfaction. Anticipating this, he says —

children.text: na kevalaṃ tvamātmānaṃ kṛtapāpaṃ na śocasi /
children.translated_text: Not only do you not grieve for yourself, who have committed evil,
but you wish to compete with others who have performed merit! // <s>Bca</s> 6.86 //

body.text: subodham / "yat kiṃcidduḥkhaṃ tatsarvaṃ pāpasamudbhūtam / abhilāṣavighāto 'pi duḥkham / yadapi paryeṣamāṇo na labhate, tadapi duḥkham" iti vacanāt // yadvakṣyati-
body.translated_text: This is easily understood. 'Whatever suffering there is, all of it has arisen from evil; the frustration of desire is also suffering; even what one does not obtain while seeking is suffering' — thus it is stated. As will be said [later] —

body.text:
abhilāṣavighātāśca jāyante pāpakāriṇām /
iti /
[bodhi . 7.41]
body.translated_text: 'Frustrations of desires arise for those who commit evil.' Thus. [<s>Bodhi</s>. 7.41]

body.text: yat kiṃcit sukhaṃ tat sarvaṃ puṇyaprasūtam / iti sukhābhilāṣiṇā śubhe karmaṇi udyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / yadvakṣyati-
body.translated_text: 'Whatever happiness there is, all of it is born from merit.' Therefore, one who desires happiness should make effort in wholesome action. As will be said —

body.text:
puṇyakārisukhecchā tu............ ityādi /
[bodhi. 7.42-43]
body.translated_text: 'The desire for happiness of one who performs merit...' and so forth. [<s>Bodhi</s>. 7.42-43]

body.text: iti kathaṃ kṛtapuṇyaiḥ saha spardhā yujyate? sukṛtakriyāyāmeva tatsukhābhilāṣiṇāṃ spardhā yuktetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, how is competition with those who have performed merit justified? The meaning is: for those who desire such happiness, competition in performing good deeds alone is appropriate.

body.text: api ca / idamapi praṣṭavyo 'si-
body.translated_text: Moreover, you should also be asked this —

body.text: jātaṃ cedapriyaṃ śatrostvattuṣṭayā kiṃ punarbhavet /
body.translated_text: Even if something unpleasant has occurred for your enemy, what more will come of your satisfaction?

body.text: tava śatrordveṣaviṣayasya tvadabhilāṣamātreṇa apriyamaniṣṭaṃ jātamutpannaṃ ced yadi, etāvatā bhavataḥ kiṃ punarbhavet? bhavatu tāvat tasyāniṣṭam, anyasya tu bhavatu, mā vā / mama kiṃcideva tāvanmātreṇa prayojanamiti parābhiprāyamāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: If something unpleasant — something unwished — has arisen for your enemy, the object of your hatred, merely through your wish, what more would come of it for you? Granted, let there be something unpleasant for him; but whether it happens to another or not — what concern of mine is there in that alone? — anticipating this thought of the other, he says —

body.text: tvadāśaṃsanamātreṇa na cāheturbhaviṣyati // Bca_6.87 //
body.translated_text: By your mere wishing alone, it will not become a cause [of his misfortune]. // <s>Bca</s> 6.87 //

body.text: tavāśaṃsanam icchā / abhilāṣa iti yāvat / tāvanmātreṇa na cāhetuḥ, na vidyate heturasya, ityaheturartho bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: Your 'wish' — desire, that is, longing — by that much alone, it is not without cause; 'there is no cause for this' — this is the meaning of 'causeless.' //

body.text: apriyasya bhavatu nāma evamityabhyupagamyocyate-
body.translated_text: Granting that unpleasant [consequences] may indeed be so, he says by way of concession —

body.text: atha tvadicchayā siddhaṃ tadduḥkhe kiṃ sukhaṃ tava /
body.translated_text: Even if it were accomplished by your wish, what pleasure is there for you in his suffering?

body.text: yadi nāma tavecchayā siddhaṃ niṣpannamapriyaṃ śatroḥ, tathāpi tasya duḥkhe samutpanne kiṃ sukhaṃ tava? na kiṃcit / niṣprayojanamidamabhipretamiti yāvat / nanu idameva prayojanaṃ yat tadduḥkhe mama saṃtuṣṭirityata āha-
body.translated_text: Even if the enemy's misfortune were accomplished — brought about — by your wish, still, when his suffering has arisen, what pleasure is there for you? None whatsoever. The meaning is that this aim is purposeless. But surely this itself is the purpose — that his suffering brings me satisfaction — to this he says —

body.text: athāpyartho bhavedevamanarthaḥ ko nvataḥ paraḥ // Bca_6.88 //
body.translated_text: Even if there were such a purpose, what greater calamity could there be than this? // Bca_6.88 //

body.text: evamapi paraduḥkhaparitoṣe yadi arthaḥ prayojanaṃ bhavet, tadā ataḥ paraḥ anarthaḥ ko nu? nurityatiśaye / ayamevānartho mahānityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Even so, if there were purpose — benefit — in satisfaction at another's suffering, then what greater calamity could there be than this? 'None' — [used] for emphasis. The meaning is: this itself is a great calamity. //

body.text: kathaṃ punarayamanartha ityāha-
body.translated_text: How then is this a calamity? — he says —

children.translated_text: For this is a terrible hook cast by the fishermen that are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

children.text: yato narakapālāstvāṃ krītvā pakṣyanti kumbhiṣu // Bca_6.89 //
children.translated_text: from which the guardians of hell, having purchased you, will cook you in cauldrons. // Bca_6.89 //

body.text: yasmādetadidamevaṃvidhaṃ parānarthacittaṃ baḍiśaṃ ghoraṃ mahābhayaṃkaram / kiṃbhūtam? kleśabāḍiśikārpitam / kleśā eva baḍiśena carantīti bāḍiśikāḥ tairarpitamādattam / yataḥ kleśabāḍiśikāt / bāḍiśikādiva matsyam / narakapālā yamapuruṣāḥ tvāṃ krītvā pakṣyanti pakṣyante / kvacinnītveti pāṭhaḥ / kumbhiṣu narakaviśeṣeṣu / tasmādatrābhilāṣaṃ mā kārṣīriti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because this very mind of taking pleasure in another's misfortune is a 'hook' — terrifying, causing great fear. Of what kind? Cast by the fishermen that are the <s>kleśas</s> — the <s>kleśas</s> themselves move about like fishermen; 'cast' means seized by them. From which — from the hook of the <s>kleśas</s>, like a fish from a fisherman — the guardians of hell, the servants of <s>Yama</s>, having purchased you, will cook you. In some readings: 'having taken you.' In <s>Kumbhī</s> hells — particular hells. Therefore, the purport is: do not harbor such desire! //

body.text: yadapi stutyādivighāte duḥkhamutpadyate, tadapi avivecayata evetyupadeśayannāha-
body.translated_text: As for the suffering that arises from the obstruction of praise and such — that too arises only from lack of discernment — instructing thus, he says —

children.text: stutiryaśo 'tha satkāro na puṇyāya na cāyuṣe /
children.translated_text: Praise, fame, and honor are not for the sake of merit, nor for longevity,

children.text: na balārthaṃ na cārogye na ca kāyasukhāya me // Bca_6.90 //
children.translated_text: nor for the purpose of strength, nor for health, nor for my bodily pleasure. // Bca_6.90 //

body.text: etāvāṃśca bhavetsvārtho dhīmataḥ svārthavedinaḥ /
body.translated_text: This much would be the self-interest of a wise person who knows [true] self-interest:

body.text: pañcaprakāra evārthaḥ puruṣārthatvenābhimato viduṣām / tadyathā- puṇyam, āyurvṛddhiḥ, balavṛddhiḥ, ārogyalābhaḥ, kāyasukhaṃ ceti / na caiteṣu kvacidupayujyante stutyādayaḥ / iyāneva hi svārtho bhavato bhavet prajñāvataḥ svārthavedinaḥ / anyasya punaranyathāpi bhavet, iti ātmani parāmṛśati / jānantu yadyapi svārtham, tathāpi svārthavedinaḥ anupāyatvāt pṛthagupadarśitaḥ / dhīmata ityanena tadasaṅgatayā tadapi kathitam //
body.translated_text: The purposes regarded by the wise as constituting human aims are fivefold only: merit, increase of longevity, increase of strength, attainment of health, and bodily pleasure. And praise and such are not useful for any of these. 'This much indeed would be the self-interest of one who is wise, who knows self-interest.' For another, however, it might be otherwise — thus he reflects upon himself. Even those who know their self-interest are shown separately because of the inadequacy of their means. By 'wise' that [inadequacy] too is indicated. //

body.text: nanu mānasamapi sukhamasti, tena avadhāraṇamayuktamityatrāha-
body.translated_text: But surely there is also mental pleasure — therefore the exclusion is not justified — to this he says —

body.text: madyadyūtādi sevyaṃ syānmānasaṃ sukhamicchatā // Bca_6.91 //
body.translated_text: If one desires mental pleasure, one should resort to liquor, gambling, and such. // Bca_6.91 //

body.text: mānasaṃ sukhaṃ saumanasyam / tadicchatā madyaṃ dyūtaṃ gaṇikā pāradārikaṃ sevanīyaṃ syāt / yatpunaḥ saddharmaśravaṇāt saumanasyam, tat puṇyagrahaṇena saṃgṛhītamityadoṣaḥ / tasmāt saumanasya heturbhavato 'pi stutyādayo bālajanānandakāriṇo 'nupādeyā eva //
body.translated_text: 'Mental pleasure' — gladness. One desiring that should resort to liquor, gambling, courtesans, and adultery. But the gladness that comes from hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> is included under the heading of merit — so there is no fault. Therefore, even though praise and such are causes of gladness, being delighters of the childish, they are not to be valued. //

body.text: itthamapi bālajanollāpakāriṇaḥ stutyādaya ityāha-
body.translated_text: That praise and such are indeed delighters of the childish — he says —

body.text: yaśorthaṃ hārayantyarthamātmānaṃ mārayantyapi /
body.translated_text: For the sake of fame, some give away wealth and even destroy themselves.

body.text: kecinmohapuruṣāḥ tādṛśaguṇāt svayamatisudūre vartamānā api śakrādiguṇaiḥ stūyamānā bandijanairanyaiśca protphullanayanavadanā yaśorthino hastyaśvādidhanaṃ tṛṇavat tebhyaḥ prayacchanti / tathā taireva guṇaiḥ saṃbhāvitātmanāmapi śakravat śatruvijayasamudbhūtaṃ yaśo mama jagati vipulatāṃ gamiṣyati, ityabhiniveśādduḥsahasaṃgrāmārohaṇānmārayanti /
body.translated_text: Certain deluded persons, though themselves far removed from such qualities, being praised by bards and others with the qualities of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and such, with eyes and faces beaming, desirous of fame, give away wealth such as horses and elephants as if it were straw. Likewise, those who esteem themselves as endowed with qualities like <s>Śakra</s>'s, thinking 'My fame, born from victory over enemies, will become widespread in the world' — from attachment, they kill themselves by ascending into difficult, dangerous battles.

body.text: na cātra paramārthataḥ kiṃcit prayojanam, anyatra mithyāvikalpāditi pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And in this there is no ultimate purpose, apart from false conceptualization — demonstrating this, he says —

body.text: kimakṣarāṇi bhakṣyāṇi mṛte kasya ca tatsukham // Bca_6.92 //
body.translated_text: Are [mere] syllables edible? And when one is dead, whose is that pleasure? // Bca_6.92 //

body.text: stutyādyabhidhāyakāni akṣarāṇi varṇāḥ kiṃ bhakṣyāṇi carvitavyāni? yaśorthaṃ mṛte sati kasya ca tat sukhaṃ yaśaḥśravaṇasamuttham?
body.translated_text: The syllables — the letters — that express praise and such, are they edible, to be chewed? And when one has died for the sake of fame, whose is that pleasure arising from hearing [one's] fame?

body.text: tasmādbālakrīḍāsamānametadityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, showing that this is equivalent to children's play, he says —

body.text: yathā pāṃśugṛhe bhinne rodityārtaravaṃ śiśuḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as a child cries out piteously when its sand-castle is broken,

body.text: yathā kaścid bālo dhūlimayagṛheṇa paramaparitoṣeṇa parikrīḍamānaḥ kenacit tasmin bhagne mahadduḥkhena parigṛhītaḥ paramārtipīḍita iva madgṛhaṃ bhagnamiti karuṇasvaraṃ krandati, saivopamā atrāpi ityāha-
body.translated_text: Just as some child, playing with utmost delight with a house made of dust, when it is broken by someone, seized by great suffering, as if afflicted by supreme anguish, cries out in a pitiful voice 'My house is broken!' — that same analogy applies here as well — he says —

body.text: tathā stutiyaśohānau svacittaṃ pratibhāti me // Bca_6.93 //
body.translated_text: so too, when praise and fame are destroyed, my mind appears [to behave]. // Bca_6.93 //

body.text: tathaiva stutiyaśohānau vighāte svacittaṃ duḥkhamāviśat pratibhāsate vicārayato mama / atrāpi na vastusatā kenacid vipralambha iti parāmarṣṭavyam //
body.translated_text: Just so, when praise and fame are destroyed — obstructed — my own mind appears, upon reflection, to be pervaded by suffering. Here too, one should consider: there is no deception by anything real. //

body.text: punaranyathā vicāreṇa bāladharma evāyamiti caturbhiḥ ślokaiḥ parāmṛśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through yet another analysis, this is merely a quality of the childish — reflecting through four verses, he says —

body.text: śabdastāvadacittatvāt sa māṃ stautītyasaṃbhavaḥ /
body.translated_text: Sound, being non-conscious — the possibility that 'it praises me' does not exist.

body.text: śabdo varṇātmako bāhyārthatayā acittaḥ acetanaḥ / tasya bhāvaḥ tasmāt / sa śabdo māṃ stauti madīyaṃ varṇamudīrayati / asaṃbhavaḥ na saṃbhavatyetat / tat kathaṃ saumanasyaṃ jāyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: Sound, consisting of phonemes, being an external object, is non-conscious — without mind. Its nature is such. That sound praises me — utters my qualities — this is impossible; it does not occur. Then how does gladness arise? — he says —

body.text: paraḥ kila mayi prīta ityetatprītikāraṇam // Bca_6.94 //
body.translated_text: 'The other is pleased with me' — this is the cause of delight. // Bca_6.94 //

body.text: anyaḥ puruṣaścetanātmakaḥ / kileti nirarthakametadapītyarucipratipādakam / mayi prītaḥ abhiprasannaḥ ityetadabhisaṃdhānaṃ prītikāraṇam /
body.translated_text: 'The other' — a person, of conscious nature. '<s>Kila</s>' (supposedly) indicates disfavor, [suggesting] that this too is pointless. 'Pleased with me' — favorably disposed — this intention is the cause of delight.

body.text:
tatrāpyevamasaṃbandhātkevalaṃ śiśuceṣṭitam /
[bodhi. 6.97]
body.translated_text:
Even in that case, due to lack of connection, it is merely the behavior of a child.
[Bodhi. 6.97]

body.text: iti saṃbandhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus is the connection. //

body.text: asaṃbandhameva kalpayannāha-
body.translated_text: Elaborating on the very lack of connection, he says —

children.text: anyatra mayi vā prītyā kiṃ hi me parakīyayā /
children.translated_text: Whether the delight is in another or in me — what benefit is there to me from another's [delight]?

children.text: tasyaiva tatprītisukhaṃ bhāgo nālpo 'pi me tataḥ // Bca_6.95 //
children.translated_text: That pleasure of delight belongs to him alone; not even a small share of it is mine. // Bca_6.95 //

body.text: yasmādanyasmin mayi vā prītyā parasaṃtānavartinyā kimāyātaṃ mama? na kiṃcit / kutaḥ? tasyaiva tato ya eva prītaḥ stutikartā, tat prītisukhaṃ nānyasya / ato bhāgo nālpo 'pi īṣadapi mama tataḥ parasaṃtānavartinaḥ prītisukhāt //
body.translated_text: Since from the delight — existing in the mental continuum of another — whether in another or in me, what has come to me? Nothing whatsoever. Why? Because that pleasure of delight belongs to him alone who is pleased, the giver of praise — not to another. Therefore not even the slightest share of it is mine, from the pleasure of delight existing in another's mental continuum. //

body.text: syādetat- parasukhenaiva sukhitvaṃ bodhisattvānām / tat kimiti tato bhāgo nāstīti? atrāha-
body.translated_text: One might say: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are happy through the happiness of others itself. So why is there no share from it? To this he says —

children.translated_text: If there is happiness through his happiness, then let it be so in all cases for me;

children.text: kasmādanyaprasādena sukhiteṣu na me sukham // Bca_6.96 //
children.translated_text: why then, when [people] are happy through the favor of another, is there no happiness for me? // Bca_6.96 //

body.text: yadi parasukhena sukhitvam / tadā tasminnanyatra prasādena sukhite 'pi mamāstu tatsukhitvam / kimātmanyabhiprasādena prīte parasmin prītiḥ? na tvanyasmin prasādena sukhiteṣu mama sukham //
body.translated_text: If there is happiness through another's happiness, then let that happiness of mine exist even when another is made happy elsewhere by [someone else's] favor. Why is there delight when another is pleased with my own self? But there is no happiness for me when others are happy through another's favor. //

body.text: tasmādvacanamātramevaitat, na paramārtha iti darśayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, showing that this is merely verbal — not ultimate — he says —

children.translated_text: Therefore the delight that arises in oneself [thinking] 'I am praised' —
even in that case, due to lack of connection, it is merely the behavior of a child. // Bca_6.97 //

body.text: tadanyanimittābhāvāt ahaṃ stuta ityevaṃ vikalpanāt prītirātmabni jāyate, na punaḥ parasukhena sukhitvāt / tatrāpi na kevalamanyaprasādena sukhite sati / ātmanyapi evamuktakrameṇa asaṃbandhādapratyāsatteḥ kāraṇāt kevalaṃ bālavilasitametat //
body.translated_text: Due to the absence of any other cause, from the conceptualization 'I am praised,' delight arises in oneself — not from happiness through another's happiness. Even in that case — not only when another is made happy through [someone else's] favor — even with regard to oneself, in the manner stated, due to lack of connection — from the cause of non-proximity — this is merely the playfulness of the childish. //

body.text: api ca / stutyādayo mama apacayameva dadhatītyupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, showing that praise and such actually bring me loss, he says —

children.translated_text: Praise and such destroy my well-being and <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency);

children.text: guṇavatsu ca mātsaryaṃ saṃpatkopaṃ ca kurvate // Bca_6.98 //
children.translated_text: they produce jealousy toward the virtuous and anger at [others'] prosperity. // Bca_6.98 //

body.text: amī stutyādayaḥ mama kṣemaṃ kalyāṇam / atha kṣemaṃ kuśalapakṣaparipālanam / tathā saṃvegaṃ saṃsāraduḥkhanirvedanam / nāśayanti ghnanti / na tāvanmātrameva, kiṃ tu guṇavatsu ca mātsaryam / ātmani guṇādhikamānena paraguṇapracchādanāt / tadguṇāsahanatayā vā saṃpadi lābhasatkārādisvabhāvāyāṃ kopaṃ ca amarṣaṃ kurvate teṣveva / ahameva guṇādhikaḥ, mamaiva sarvā saṃpattirucitā nānyeṣāmiti matvā //
body.translated_text: These praise and such [destroy] my well-being — welfare. Or 'well-being' [means] the safeguarding of the side of virtue. And <s>saṃvega</s> — world-weariness regarding the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> — they destroy, they kill. Not only that, but also jealousy toward the virtuous — through the pride of considering oneself superior in qualities, one conceals others' qualities; or through inability to tolerate their qualities. And they produce anger — resentment — toward prosperity consisting of gain, honor, and such — toward those very [persons]. [One thinks:] 'I alone am superior in qualities; all prosperity is befitting me alone, not others.' //

body.text: yata ete doṣāḥ stutyādiṣu saṃbhavinaḥ,
body.translated_text: Since these faults are inherent in praise and such —

children.translated_text: therefore, those who are present to destroy my praise and such

children.text: apāyapātarakṣārthaṃ pravṛttā nanu te mama // Bca_6.99 //
children.translated_text: are they not engaged in protecting me from falling into the lower realms? // Bca_6.99 //

body.text: tasmāt kāraṇāt / stutyādighātāya virodhāya ye sattvā mama pratyupasthitā udyatāḥ / apāyapāto narakādipatanam / tato rakṣārthaṃ trāṇārthaṃ rakṣaṇanimittaṃ pravṛttā udyuktā nanu te mama / ataḥ kalyāṇamitrāṇi te, nāpakāriṇa iti //
body.translated_text: Therefore — for this reason — those beings who are present, who have risen up for the destruction — the obstruction — of my praise and such, are they not engaged — exerting themselves — for the purpose of protecting me from falling into the lower realms — from descent into hells and such? Therefore they are spiritual friends, not harmful beings. //

body.text: lābhādivirodhini sarvathā pratighacittamayuktaṃ mama ityupadarśayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Showing that the mind of aversion toward those who obstruct gain and such is entirely unjustified for me, he says —

children.translated_text: For one seeking liberation, the bondage of gain and honor is unfitting;

children.text: ye mocayanti māṃ bandhādveṣasteṣu kathaṃ mama // Bca_6.100 //
children.translated_text: those who free me from bondage — how can I hate them? // Bca_6.100 //

body.text: vimuktikāmasya lābhasatkārau bandhanamiva, saṅgasthānatvāt, ayuktaṃ nocitaṃ mumukṣorbandhanam / kalyāṇamitrakṛtyakāriṇaḥ śatrutvenābhimatā vimocayanti viyojayanti māṃ bandhāt saṃsāraduḥkhalakṣaṇāt lābhādisvabhāvādvā / dveṣasteṣu paramopakāriṣu prītisthāneṣu kathaṃ mama? na yukta ityabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: For one desiring liberation, gain and honor are like bondage, because they are grounds for attachment — bondage is unfitting for one seeking freedom. Those who, performing the function of spiritual friends, though regarded as enemies, free — separate — me from bondage characterized by the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, or from the nature of gain and such — how can I harbor hatred toward them, who are supreme benefactors, who should be objects of delight? The intent is: it is not justified. //

body.text: kathaṃ na yuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: How is it not justified? — he says —

children.translated_text: For one wishing to enter [the house of] suffering, those who have become like a door-bolt —

children.text: buddhādhiṣṭhānata iva dveṣasteṣu kathaṃ mama // Bca_6.101 //
children.translated_text: as if by the blessing of the <s>Buddhas</s> — how can I hate them? // Bca_6.101 //

body.text: lābhasatkārābhiṣvaṅgaprasaṅgāt saṃsāraduḥkhairvimoktukāmasya ye satpuruṣaviśeṣāḥ kapāṭatvamapadvāratvamāgatāḥ / kutaḥ? buddhānāmadhiṣṭhānato 'nubhāvādiva / dveṣasteṣu kathaṃ mama?
body.translated_text: For one wishing to be freed from the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, consequent upon attachment to gain and honor, those excellent persons who have become like a door-bolt — a barrier at the gate of calamity. How so? As if by the blessing — the power — of the <s>Buddhas</s>. How can I hate them?

body.text: kuśalāpaghātakāriṇyapi dveṣaṃ nivārayannāha-
body.translated_text: Restraining hatred even toward one who obstructs wholesome [actions], he says —

children.translated_text: 'He has created an obstacle to my merit' — anger here is not justified;

children.text: kṣāntyā samaṃ tapo nāsti nanvetattadupasthitam // Bca_6.102 //
children.translated_text: there is no austerity equal to patience — and is not this [very situation] that [occasion for patience]? // Bca_6.102 //

body.text: kuśalavighātaḥ kṛto 'nena ityevaṃ manasi nidhāya atra puṇyavighātakāriṇi dveṣo na yujyate / kasmāt? yataḥ kṣāntyā titikṣayā samaṃ tulyaṃ tapaḥ sukṛtaṃ nāsti sarvaśubhakarmahetutvāt / "na ca kṣāntisamaṃ tapaḥ" (bodhi. 6.2) iti vacanāt / nanu tadevedamayatnata eva upasthitamupanatam / puṇyavighnakāricchalena puṇyahetusaṃnidheḥ //
body.translated_text: Keeping in mind 'He has created an obstacle to my virtue' — anger here, toward one who obstructs merit, is not justified. Why? Because there is no austerity — no wholesome practice — equal to <s>kṣānti</s> (patience, forbearance), since it is the cause of all meritorious actions. As stated: 'There is no austerity equal to patience' (<s>Bodhi</s>. 6.2). And is not this very [situation] that [occasion for patience], which has presented itself — arrived — without any effort on one's part? Through the pretext of one who obstructs merit, there is the presence of a cause of merit! //

body.text: tatra pradveṣe tu ātmanaiva puṇyavighātaḥ kṛto bhavedityāha-
body.translated_text: But if one gives in to hatred, the obstacle to merit would be created by oneself alone — he says —

children.translated_text: If through my own fault I do not practice patience here,
then the obstacle is created by me alone, when a cause of merit has presented itself. // Bca_6.103 //

body.text: atha yadi ātmana eva doṣeṇa asahiṣṇutātmakena na karomi kṣamāṃ kṣāntimiha vighnakāriṇi, tadā mayaiva na punaranyena atra puṇye kṛto vighnaḥ / kutaḥ? puṇyahetau puṇyavighātakāritvenābhimate upasthite saṃnihitībhūte / atretyasmin puṇyahetāviti vā saṃbhāvyate //
body.translated_text: If through my own fault — one characterized by intolerance — I do not practice patience — <s>kṣānti</s> — here toward one who creates obstacles, then the obstacle to merit is created by me alone, not by another. Why? When a cause of merit — one regarded as creating an obstacle to merit — has presented itself, has become proximate. 'Here' may also be construed as 'in this cause of merit.' //

body.text: yadi puṇyavighātakārī, kathamasau puṇyahetuḥ? yāvat sa eva vighna ityāha-
body.translated_text: If he creates obstacles to merit, how is he a cause of merit? As long as he is only an obstacle — he says —

children.text: yo hi yena vinā nāsti yasmiṃśca sati vidyate /
children.translated_text: That without which something does not exist, and in the presence of which it does exist —

children.text: sa eva kāraṇaṃ tasya sa kathaṃ vighna ucyate // Bca_6.104 //
children.translated_text: that alone is its cause; how can it be called an obstacle? // Bca_6.104 //

body.text: yo bhāvaḥ kāryābhimataḥ yena kāraṇābhimatena vinā nāsti, tadvayatireke na bhavati, sa eva yadbhāvena bhavati, nānyaḥ kāraṇaṃ janakaḥ tasya kāryābhimatasya, tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānāt / evaṃ prakṛte 'pi sa janaka eva kathaṃ tasya janyasya vighna ucyate vighātaheturabhidhīyate? tathāvidhe 'pi tathā vyavahāraṃ kurvato nāsti vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: That effect which does not exist without what is considered its cause — which does not occur in the absence of both [cause and effect] — that very [effect] comes into being through the existence of that [cause], and no other is the generator, the producer, of that considered effect, since it conforms to the positive and negative concomitance of that [cause]. Thus, in the present case too, that very [enemy] is indeed the generator — how can he be called an obstacle, a cause of obstruction, for that which he generates? Even when one speaks thus regarding such a [case], there is no contradiction in such conventional usage.

body.text: uktamevārthaṃ dṛṣṭāntopadarśanena vyaktaṃ kurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Making clear the meaning already stated by showing an illustration, he says —

children.translated_text: For a beggar who arrives at the right time does not create an obstacle to giving;

children.text: na ca pravrājake prāpte pravrajyāvighna ucyate // Bca_6.105 //
children.translated_text: nor when a preceptor arrives is it called an obstacle to ordination. // <s>Bca</s> 6.105 //

body.text: na yasmāt kasyaciddānapaterditsākāle eva saṃprāptenārthinā yācanakena dānavighnaḥ kṛtaḥ ityucyate, yataḥ sa kāraṇameva dānasya / tathā kasyacit pravrajitukāmasya pravrājakasamavadhānaṃ pravrajyā saṃvarādigrahaṇasvabhāvā, na ca tasyā vighna ucyate, api tu kāraṇameva sa tasyāḥ / tamantareṇa tasyā asaṃbhavāt / evaṃ prakṛte 'pi draṣṭavyam /
body.translated_text: For it is not said that a beggar — a petitioner — who has arrived at the very moment of a donor's wish to give has created an obstacle to giving, since he is the very cause of giving. Likewise, for one who wishes to go forth, the presence of a preceptor — ordination being by nature the taking of vows and such — is not called an obstacle to ordination; rather, he is the very cause of it, since without him it is impossible. Thus it should be seen in the present case as well.

body.text: api ca / kṣāntiheturatidurlabha iti tatsamāgame prītireva yujyate ityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, showing that since the cause of patience is exceedingly rare, joy alone is appropriate upon encountering it, he says —

body.text: sulabhā yācakā loke durlabhāstvapakāriṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: Beggars are easily found in the world, but those who cause harm are rare;

body.text: atipracuraprāptikā yācanakā loke sarvatra sarveṣāṃ dīyamānagrahaṇāvaimukhyāt, na tu punarapakāriṇaḥ / ataste durlabhāḥ śatasahasreṣu, yadi kathaṃcit kaścit syādvā na veti / kutaḥ punaretadevamityāha-
body.translated_text: Beggars — those who request abundantly — are found everywhere in the world, among all [people], because they do not turn away from accepting what is given. But those who cause harm are not [easily found]. Therefore they are rare — perhaps one among hundreds of thousands, if there is even one at all. Why is this so? He says —

body.text: yato me 'naparādhasya na kaścidaparādhyati // Bca_6.106 //
body.translated_text: since no one wrongs me when I have done no wrong. // <s>Bca</s> 6.106 //

body.text: yasmādanaparādhasya nivṛttaparāpakārasya mama nirnimittaṃ na kaścideko 'pi aparādhyati, nāpakaroti / karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī //
body.translated_text: Because when I have done no wrong — when I have ceased harming others — no one, not even a single person, wrongs me, does me harm, without cause. The sixth case-ending is used in the sense of the object [of the action].

body.text: evamatidurlabhatayā paramopakāritvācca abhinandanīya eva apakārītyāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, showing that because of being exceedingly rare and supremely beneficial, one who harms should indeed be welcomed, he says —

children.translated_text: Therefore, like a treasure that has appeared in one's house, obtained without effort,
my enemy should be cherished, being a companion in the practice of awakening. // <s>Bca</s> 6.107 //

body.text: yasmāt kathaṃcit prāpyante apakāriṇaḥ, tasmād gṛhe prādurbhūto nidhiriva śramamantareṇaivādhigato ripurabhilaṣaṇīya eva mayā syāt, bodhicaryāyāṃ buddhatvasaṃbhāropārjane sahakāritvācca //
body.translated_text: Since those who cause harm are obtained only with difficulty, therefore, like a treasure that has manifested in one's house — obtained without any effort — the enemy should indeed be desired by me, because he is a helper in the practice of awakening, in accumulating the provisions for <s>Buddhahood</s>.

body.text: evaṃvidhe paramapuruṣārthe sāhāyyaṃ bhajamānasya pratyupakārakaraṇameva kṛtajñatayā mama yuktamityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing that for one who renders such assistance in the supreme human goal, making a return of kindness is indeed appropriate for me out of gratitude, he says —

children.translated_text: Since this fruit of patience has been produced by both me and him,

children.text: etasmai prathamaṃ deyametatpūrvā kṣamā yataḥ // Bca_6.108 //
children.translated_text: it should first be given to him, since patience has him as its prior [cause]. // <s>Bca</s> 6.108 //

body.text: yasmādasau tatra sāhāyyaṃ kurvan kāraṇameva na vighnaḥ tasmānmayā kṣamāmabhyastatā, anena cāpakāraṃ kurvatā, iti dvābhyāmevopārjitam / etaditi yasya sādhanāya sāhāyyaṃ bhajate / kṣamāphalaṃ dharmādhigamalakṣaṇam etasmai dharmasahāyāya prathamamagrato dātavyaṃ mayā iti praṇidhātavyam / yathā maitrībalena bodhisattvena praṇihitaṃ pañcakānuddiśya / tatra kāraṇamāha- yasmādetatpūrvā, eṣa eva pūrvaṃ kāraṇaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā / na hi apakāriṇamantareṇa anyat kṣāntikāraṇamasti //
body.translated_text: Since he, rendering assistance there, is indeed the cause and not an obstacle — therefore, by me practicing patience, and by him doing harm — it has been produced by both. 'This' refers to that for the attainment of which he renders assistance. The fruit of patience — characterized by the attainment of <s>Dharma</s> — should first, before all else, be given by me to this companion in <s>Dharma</s> — thus should one resolve. Just as a <s>Bodhisattva</s> through the power of loving-kindness made a dedication for five [beings]. There he states the reason: 'since patience has him as its prior [cause]' — he alone is the prior cause of which, and so it is called thus. For apart from one who does harm, there is no other cause of patience.

body.text: yuktamevaitad yadi tenaivābhiprāyeṇa asau pravartate, kevalamapakārāśaya evāyamityāśaṅkayannāha-
body.translated_text: Anticipating the objection — 'this is justified only if he acts with that very intention; but this [enemy] has only the intention to harm,' he says —

children.text: kṣamāsiddhayāśayo nāsya tena pūjyo na cedariḥ /
children.translated_text: If the enemy is not to be honored because he has no intention [to bring about] the accomplishment of patience,
then how is the true <s>Dharma</s>, which is a cause of accomplishment yet without intention, honored? // <s>Bca</s> 6.109 //

body.text: kṣamā asya bodhisattvasya niṣpadyatām, ityāśayo nāsya apakārodyatasya / tena kāraṇena kuśalaheturapi yadi śatruḥ pūjanīyo na bhavati, evaṃ tarhi kuśalaniṣpattihetuḥ nirabhiprāyo 'pi saddharmaḥ pravacanalakṣaṇaḥ kathaṃ pūjyate? so 'pi tadāśayaśūnyatvāt pūjanīyo na syāt, iti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'May this <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s patience be accomplished' — such is not the intention of this one intent on harm. If for that reason even an enemy who is a cause of wholesome [qualities] is not to be honored, then the true <s>Dharma</s>, characterized as the teaching, which is a cause of the accomplishment of wholesome [qualities] yet is without intention — how is it honored? It too, being devoid of such intention, should not be worthy of honor — this is the meaning.

body.text: atha saddharmasya nirabhiprāyatayā apakārāśayo 'pi nāsti, asya punastadviparyayo dṛśyate, ityāha-
body.translated_text: But the true <s>Dharma</s>, being without intention, has no intention to harm either, whereas in this [enemy] the opposite is seen — to this he says —

children.translated_text: If the enemy is not to be honored because 'his intention is to harm,'

children.text: anyathā me kathaṃ kṣāntirbhiṣajīva hitodyate // Bca_6.110 //
children.translated_text: then how would I [practice] patience otherwise? — [one does not get angry] at a physician who is intent on benefit. // <s>Bca</s> 6.110 //

body.text: apakāraḥ āśayaḥ asya śatroḥ, ityevamabhisaṃdhāya śatruryadi na pūjyate dānamānairna satkriyate / anyatheti apakāriṇi dveṣacittamanivārayataḥ kathaṃ mama kṣāntiḥ? tadapakāramasahamānasya
body.translated_text: 'Harm is the intention of this enemy' — holding this view, if the enemy is not honored, not respected with gifts and honors — 'otherwise' means: how would I [practice] patience when, toward one who harms, I do not restrain my mind of hatred? The meaning is: for one who cannot endure that harm

body.text: pratyapakāraṃ vā kurvato naiva yuktetyarthaḥ / anyatrapi kathaṃ kṣāntiḥ? bhiṣajīva hitodyate, suvaidyavad hitasukhavidhāyake yatra premagauravameva sadā, dveṣanibandhanasya gandho 'pi na vidyate //
body.translated_text: or who retaliates, it is simply not justified. And how else [would there be] patience? [The enemy is] like a physician intent on benefit — toward a good doctor who arranges what is beneficial and pleasant, there is always love and respect alone; not even a trace of the basis for hatred exists.

body.text: dveṣacittanivaertanācca kṣāntirucyate / tasmādapakāriṇyeva pratighacittaṃ nivartayataḥ kṣāntiriti / etadeva darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: And patience is defined as the turning back of a mind of hatred. Therefore, patience is the restraining of a hostile mind specifically toward one who does harm. Showing this very point, he says —

children.translated_text: Therefore, patience arises dependent upon his hostile intention alone;

children.text: sa evātaḥ kṣamāhetuḥ pūjyaḥ saddharmavanmayā // Bca_6.111 //
children.translated_text: he alone, therefore, is the cause of patience and should be honored by me, like the true <s>Dharma</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 6.111 //

body.text: yato bhiṣajīva hitodyate kṣāntirna yuktā, ataḥ asmāddhetoḥ tasya duṣṭāśayameva pratītya nimittīkṛtya samupajāyate kṣamā / na punaḥ kasyacicchubhāśayam / ataḥ asmāt sa eva yasyāśayaṃ pratītyotpadyate kṣamā kṣamāhetuḥ, na tu punaryo vaidyavadaduṣṭāśayaḥ / iti pūjyaḥ kṣamāsiddhyāśayarahito 'pi saddharmavadasau mayā / etaduktaṃ bhavati- kiṃ mamānena āśayavicāreṇa prayojanam? abhimatasādhyasiddhau cedupayujyate, tāvataiva mamopādeyaḥ syāt / viguṇāśayaphalaṃ tu tasyaiva, yasyāsau viguṇāśayaḥ / mama tu śubhodayaheturevāyam, iti kathamiva pūjanīyo na bhavediti / tasmāt saṃbhāropayogini hetau kiṃ svarūpanirūpaṇena?
body.translated_text: Since, like a physician intent on benefit, patience [toward a well-intentioned person] is not justified — therefore, for this reason, it is dependent upon, taking as its condition, his hostile intention alone that patience arises. Not, however, dependent on anyone's benevolent intention. Therefore, from this it follows that he alone, upon whose intention patience arises, is the cause of patience — not one who, like a physician, has a non-hostile intention. Thus he should be honored by me like the true <s>Dharma</s>, even though devoid of the intention to accomplish patience. What is stated here is this: what use is this investigation of intention to me? If it serves the accomplishment of the desired goal, that alone is sufficient for me to accept it. The fruit of a defective intention is his alone, whose intention is defective. For me, however, this is the very cause of the arising of good; so how indeed could he not be worthy of honor? Therefore, what is the point of examining the intrinsic nature of a cause that serves the accumulation [of merit]?

body.text: etadeva saṃbhārahetutvamasya āgamataḥ prasādhayannāha-
body.translated_text: Establishing this very point — that he is a cause of the accumulation [of merit] — from scripture, he says —

children.translated_text: 'The field of beings is the field of the <s>Jinas</s>' — thus was it declared by the <s>Muni</s>,

children.text: etānārādhya bahavaḥ saṃpatpāraṃ yato gatāḥ // Bca_6.112 //
children.translated_text: since, by gratifying these, many have gone to the far shore of attainment. // <s>Bca</s> 6.112 //

body.text: saṃbhāraprasūtipravṛttihetutvāt sattvāḥ kṣetram / buddhā bhagavantastathaiva kṣetram / iti evam / ato buddhatvakāraṇahetutvāt anekaprakāraṃ bhagavatā varṇitam / kutaḥ? yato yasmādetān sattvān jināṃśca ārādhya ānukūlyānuṣṭhānena bahavo buddhatvamadhigamya sarvalaukikalokottarasarvasaṃpattiparyantaṃ prāptāḥ //
body.translated_text: Beings are a field because they are the cause of the arising and activity of the accumulations. The Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> are likewise a field. 'Thus' — in this way. Therefore, because they are the causes of <s>Buddhahood</s>, this has been praised in many ways by the Blessed One. Why? Because, by gratifying — by acting in accordance with — these beings and the <s>Jinas</s>, many have attained <s>Buddhahood</s> and reached the culmination of all mundane and supramundane attainments.

body.text: syādetat- yadi nāma sattvā api sarvasaṃpattihetavaḥ, tathāpi tathāgataiḥ saha sādhāraṇatā na yukteti / atrāha-
body.translated_text: One might say: even if beings too are causes of all attainments, still equality with the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is not justified. To this he says —

children.translated_text: When the attainment of the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities is equal from both beings and <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: jineṣu gauravaṃ yadvanna sattveṣviti kaḥ kramaḥ // Bca_6.113 //
children.translated_text: what kind of logic is it that there is reverence toward the <s>Jinas</s> but not toward beings? // <s>Bca</s> 6.113 //

body.text: ubhayebhyo 'pi buddhadharmāṇāṃ balavaiśāradyādīnāmāgame pratilambhe tulye aviśiṣṭe / ubhayamapi tat prati hetutvamaviśiṣṭamiti bhāvaḥ / ataḥ sādhāraṇe 'pi hetubhāve jineṣu gauravaṃ yadvat, tadvanna sattveṣu / ityevaṃ kaḥkramaḥ paripāṭiḥ prekṣāvatām? naiva yuktetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: From both, the attainment — the acquisition — of the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the powers, the fearlessnesses, and so forth is equal, undifferentiated. The meaning is: the causal status of both with respect to that [attainment] is undifferentiated. Therefore, when the causal status is common [to both], what kind of logic — what order — is it for discerning people that there is reverence toward the <s>Jinas</s> just as [there should be], but not toward beings? The meaning is: it is simply not justified.

body.text: nanu ca sattvānāṃ rāgādimalairhīnāśayatvāt kāraṇatve 'pi kathaṃ bhagavatsamānatā yujyate ityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: But since beings have inferior dispositions due to stains of desire and such, how can equality with the Blessed Ones be justified even in [their] causal status? — anticipating this, he says —

children.text: āśayasya ca māhātmyaṃ na svataḥ kiṃ tu kāryataḥ /
children.translated_text: The greatness of an intention is [measured] not by itself but by its effect;

children.text: samaṃ ca tena māhātmyaṃ sattvānāṃ tena te samāḥ // Bca_6.114 //
children.translated_text: and the greatness [of the effect] is equal — therefore they are equal. // <s>Bca</s> 6.114 //

body.text: yadyapi bhagavatāmaparimitapuṇyajñānopajanitamanuttaramiha māhātmyam, tathāpi upayuktopayogitvena hetubhāvasya tulyatvāt samaṃ māhātmyamucyate / tena hetunā te sattvāḥ samāḥ jinaistulyā ucyante iti nātra viśeṣaḥ kriyate //
body.translated_text: Although the Blessed Ones possess unsurpassed greatness here, produced by immeasurable merit and wisdom, nevertheless, since their causal status is equal in terms of being applicable and useful, their greatness is said to be equal. For that reason, those beings are said to be equal — the same as — the <s>Jinas</s>; no distinction is made here.

body.text: yatra punaḥ pratiniyatātmagato viśeṣaḥ, tamupadarśayitumāha-
body.translated_text: To show the distinction that pertains to each individually, he says —

children.translated_text: That one is honored due to a disposition of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) — that is the greatness of the being;
that merit [arises] from faith in the <s>Buddha</s> — that is the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 6.115 //

body.text: sattveṣu maitracittavihārī punaryatpūjyate janaiḥ, tattasyaiva maitryāśayasya pratyātmagataṃ māhātmyaṃ nānyasya / tathā tathāgatamāhātmyamālambya svacittaṃ prasādayato yatpuṇyamutpadyate, tadbhagavata eva māhātmyamasādhāraṇam, anyasya tathāvidhaguṇābhāvāt //
body.translated_text: When one who dwells in a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward beings is honored by people, that is the greatness pertaining to that very disposition of loving-kindness alone, not of another. Likewise, the merit that arises when one generates faith in one's own mind based on the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — that is the uncommon greatness of the Blessed One alone, since such qualities are absent in others.

body.text: ityasādhāraṇaṃ guṇamabhidhāya prakṛtamupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Having stated the uncommon quality, and showing the topic at hand, he says —

children.translated_text: Therefore, in the aspect of [being a cause for] the attainment of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, beings are equal to the <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: na tu buddhaiḥ samāḥ kecidanantāṃśairguṇārṇavaiḥ // Bca_6.116 //
children.translated_text: but none are equal to the <s>Buddhas</s>, who are oceans of qualities with infinite aspects. // <s>Bca</s> 6.116 //

body.text: idamatra bījaṃ samatopādāne ityarthaḥ / paramārthatastu na buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ samāḥ kecit sattvāḥ santi / yadi bhaveyustathāvidhāḥ, tadā te 'pi buddhā eva syuḥ / kiṃbhūtaiḥ? guṇārṇavaiḥ / guṇānāmarṇavā guṇaratnākarāḥ, agādhāpāratvāt, taiḥ / punarapi teṣāmaparameva viśeṣaṇamāha- anantāṃśaiḥ / anantaḥ aparyantaḥ aṃśaḥ, ekadeśo 'pi yeṣāṃ guṇārṇavānām, te tathā, taiḥ //
body.translated_text: This here is the seed — the basis — for [asserting] equality: this is the meaning. But in the ultimate sense, no beings are equal to the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. If there were such [beings], then they too would simply be <s>Buddhas</s>. Of what kind? 'Oceans of qualities' — treasure mines of qualities, by virtue of being fathomless and boundless — with those. And again, he states yet another qualifier of those [Buddhas]: 'with infinite aspects' — those oceans of qualities whose even a single aspect — a single part — is infinite, boundless; they are such; with those.

body.text: uktamevārthaṃ vyaktīkurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Making clear the meaning already stated, he says —

children.translated_text: If even a minute quality of those who are the sole repositories of the essence of qualities

children.text: dṛśyate tasya pūjārthaṃ trailokyamapi na kṣamam // Bca_6.117 //
children.translated_text: is seen in anyone, even the triple world is not sufficient for honoring him. // <s>Bca</s> 6.117 //

body.text: guṇeṣu pradhānānāmekarāśayo ye bhagavantaḥ, teṣāṃ guṇaḥ aṇurapi paramāṇumātro 'pi / guṇakaṇikāpīti yāvat / yadi kvacit sattvaviśeṣe dṛśyate pratīyate, tasya tadguṇādhārasya pūjānimittaṃ trailokyamapi na kṣamam / trailokyajātāni ratnādīni na pratirūpāṇīti yāvat //
body.translated_text: The Blessed Ones who are the sole repositories of the foremost qualities — even a minute quality of theirs, even the size of an atom — even a particle of a quality, as it were — if it is seen, perceived in any particular being, for the sake of honoring that bearer of that quality, even the triple world is not sufficient. That is to say, the jewels and such produced in the triple world are not adequate [as offerings].

body.text: yadyevam, kathaṃ tarhi sattvārādhanamuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: If this is so, how then was the gratification of beings spoken of? He says —

children.translated_text: The supreme aspect — that of giving rise to <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — exists in beings;
in proportion to that aspect, let honor to beings be rendered. // <s>Bca</s> 6.118 //

body.text: vyākhyātametat pūrvam //
body.translated_text: This has been explained previously.

body.text: ito 'pi sattvārādhanamucitamityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, showing that the gratification of beings is fitting, he says —

children.translated_text: Furthermore, besides the gratification of beings, what other recompense could there be

children.text: sattvārādhanamutsṛjya niṣkṛtiḥ kā parā bhavet // Bca_6.119 //
children.translated_text: to the sincere friends of immeasurable beneficence? // <s>Bca</s> 6.119 //

body.text: niśchadmabandhūnāmakṛtrimasuhṛdāṃ buddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ ca / aparyantopakāriṇāṃ niṣkṛtiḥ tatkṛtāpakārasya niṣkrayaṇaṃ pariśodhanamiti yāvat / kimaparaṃ bhavet sattvārādhanamantareṇa / etadeva paraṃ niṣkrayaṇamityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Sincere friends' — genuine, unfeigned companions — the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. 'Of immeasurable beneficence' — recompense — means the repayment, the purification, of the wrong done to them. What else could there be apart from the gratification of beings? The meaning is: this alone is the supreme recompense.

body.text: prabhucittānukūlavartina eva bhṛtyasya vāñchitaṃ sidhyatītyavagamya sattvārādhanamevopādeyamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Understanding that a servant who acts in accordance with his master's wishes achieves what he desires, and showing that the gratification of beings alone should be adopted, he says —

children.text: bhindanti dehaṃ praviśantyavīciṃ yeṣāṃ kṛte tatra kṛte kṛtaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Those for whose sake they tear apart their bodies and enter <s>Avīci</s> — by serving them, it would be done;
therefore, toward these [beings], even those who cause great harm, one should practice only what is good. // <s>Bca</s> 6.120 //

body.text: karacaraṇaśironayanasvamāṃsāni chittvā chittvā pradattāni yeṣāṃ hitasukhavidhānāya, tathā avīcīmapi paraduḥkhaduḥkhino yeṣāṃ kṛte praviśanti tatsamuddharaṇāya / prakṛtatvād buddhā bodhisattvāḥ / tatra teṣu sattveṣu kṛte kṛtaṃ syāt / anyathā tu kṛtamapi na kṛtaṃ bhavet / kṛtaśabdo 'yamiha prakṛtādhikārāt sādhukaraṇe vartate / yenaivam, tena paramāpakāriṣvapi na cittaṃ dūṣayitavyam / kiṃ tu sarvamanekaprakāraṃ kāyavāṅmanobhirvā kalyāṇameva hitasukhameva vidhātavyameteṣu //
body.translated_text: Having repeatedly cut off and given away their own hands, feet, heads, eyes, and flesh for the sake of providing benefit and happiness to those [beings], and even entering <s>Avīci</s> [hell] for the sake of rescuing those [beings], suffering from the suffering of others — the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> being the subject. For those beings, what has been done would be [truly] done; otherwise, even what has been done would not be [truly] done. The word 'done' here, given the subject under discussion, is used in the sense of 'well done.' Since this is so, one should not corrupt one's mind even toward the greatest harmers; rather, one should provide only what is good, only benefit and happiness, to these [beings] in many ways, through body, speech, and mind.

body.text: uktameva prasādhayannāha-
body.translated_text: Establishing what has already been stated, he says —

children.text: svayaṃ mama svāmina eva tāvad yadarthamātmanyapi nirvyapeikṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: My masters themselves — for whose sake they are indifferent even toward their own selves —

children.text: ahaṃ kathaṃ svāmiṣu teṣu teṣu karomi mānaṃ na tu dāsabhāvam // Bca_6.121 //
children.translated_text: how is it that I show arrogance, rather than servitude, toward those very masters? // Bca_6.121 //

body.text: mama svāmina eva buddhādayaḥ svayameva ātmanaiva / tāvaditi parāmarśe / yadarthaṃ yeṣāṃ nimittam / ātmanyapi svakāyajīvite 'pi / uktakrameṇa nirapekṣā nirabhiṣvaṅgāḥ tṛṇavat parityajanti, tadahaṃ punaḥ teṣāṃ bhṛtyaḥ teṣu sattveṣu prabhuputreṣvatyantapriyeṣu kathaṃ karomi mānam, kimiti jānanneva tān pratikūlayāmi? na tu dāsabhāvam, na punardāsībhūyārādhayāmi?
body.translated_text: 'My masters' — the <s>Buddhas</s> and such — 'themselves,' by themselves. 'Tāvat' indicates reference [to what follows]. 'For whose sake' — on whose account. 'Even toward themselves' — even toward their own body and life. In the manner stated, they are 'indifferent' — without attachment, discarding [these] like straw. Then I, who am their servant, toward those beings who are like the beloved children of my lords — how is it that I show arrogance? Why, knowing this full well, do I act contrary to them? 'Rather than servitude' — why do I not, having become a servant, please them?

body.text: ito 'pi ca sattvāpakāraṃ parityajya tadārādhanameva kartavyamityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, one should abandon harm to beings and devote oneself to pleasing them — he says —

children.text: yeṣāṃ sukhe yānti mudaṃ munīndrāḥ yeṣāṃ vyathāyāṃ praviśanti manyum /
children.translated_text: Those in whose happiness the <s>Munīndras</s> (Lords of Sages) rejoice, and at whose suffering they become displeased —
from pleasing them comes the satisfaction of all <s>Munīndras</s>; in harming them, an offense is committed against the <s>Munis</s>. // Bca_6.122 //

body.text: yeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ priyaputrāṇāmiva pitaro munīndrā buddhā bhagavantaḥ sukhe kāyamanojanmani mudaṃ harṣaṃ yānti, yeṣāṃ ca duḥkhe manyuṃ praviśanti aparitoṣamāsādayanti / etacca
body.translated_text: Those beings — like beloved children, of whom their fathers, the <s>Munīndras</s>, the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, experience joy, delight, at their happiness arising from body and mind, and at whose suffering they become displeased, experiencing dissatisfaction. And this

body.text: anabhimatatvād bhagavatāmitthamabhidhīyate, na tu vāṇī (sī?) candanakalyāṇā(lpava?)t(?) tacchrāvakāṇāmapi pratighānunayāsaṃbhavaḥ(?) / anyat subodham //
body.translated_text: is stated thus because it is undesirable to the Blessed Ones, not as if [they experienced] anger and attachment like <s>Śrāvakas</s> — for the arising of hostility and partiality is impossible [in them]. The rest is easily understood.

body.text: kathaṃ punastatrāpakāre munīnāmapakṛtaṃ syādityatrāha-
body.translated_text: How then would harming them constitute an offense against the <s>Munis</s>? To this he says —

children.translated_text: Just as for one whose body is ablaze on all sides, there is no delight even from all objects of desire,

children.text: sattvavyathāyāmapi tadvadeva na prītyupāyo 'sti dayāmayānām // Bca_6.123 //
children.translated_text: so too, when beings suffer, there is no means of joy for those who are made of compassion. // Bca_6.123 //

body.text: samantāt sarvāvayavānabhivyāpya vahninā prajvalitaśarīrasya yathā pañcakāmaguṇairna saumanasyam, kāyikamapi sukhaṃ nāsti, tasya prajvalitatvādeva duḥkhenākrāntatvāt, tadvat tathaiva sattvānāṃ vyathāyāṃ duḥkhavedanāyāṃ na prīteḥ saumanasyasya upāyo heturasti kṛpātmakānāṃ bhagavatām //
body.translated_text: Just as for one whose body is blazing, pervaded by fire throughout all limbs, there is no delight from the five strands of sensual pleasure, nor even physical pleasure, since the body being ablaze is overcome by suffering — so too, when beings experience suffering, painful sensation, there is no means, no cause, of joy, of delight, for the Blessed Ones who are of the nature of compassion.

body.text: tasmādaparijñānena kleśagrahāveśavaśena vā sattvāpakārakarmaṇā yadakuśalamupacitam, tadapi idānīmupasaṃhāradvāreṇa vāntīkurvannāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, whatever unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] has been accumulated through the act of harming beings, whether through ignorance or under the possession of the grip of defilements — now confessing that through a summation, he says —

children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever suffering I have caused to the greatly compassionate ones by inflicting pain on beings,

children.text: tadadya pāpaṃ pratideśayāmi yatkheditāstanmunayaḥ kṣamantām // Bca_6.124 //
children.translated_text: that evil I confess today; may the <s>Munis</s> who have been aggrieved forgive me. // Bca_6.124 //

body.text: yasmādevaṃ sattvāpakāre munīnāmapakṛtaṃ syāt, tasmāt pāpam adya idānīṃ pratideśayāmi, saṃvegabahulasteṣāmeva mahākṛpāṇāmagrataḥ prakāśayāmi / punarevaṃ saṃprajānanna kariṣyāmi, iti āyatyāṃ saṃvaramāpadye / yadi pratirūpamācaritaṃ tatra me kṣāntiṃ kurvantu anukampāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: Since thus an offense against the <s>Munis</s> would result from harming beings, therefore I confess — I openly declare — my evil today, now, before those very greatly compassionate ones, with abundant urgency. 'I shall never do so again, knowing thus' — in this way I undertake restraint for the future. If my conduct has been appropriate, may they grant me forgiveness, out of compassion.

body.text: kṣamayitvā sāṃpratamārādhanāyetyādinā tadekaparāyaṇatāmātmano darśayati-
body.translated_text: Having asked forgiveness, he now shows his single-minded devotion to pleasing [them], with 'for the sake of pleasing' and so forth —

children.translated_text: For the sake of pleasing the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, today I enter into servitude to the world with my entire being;

children.text: kurvantu me mūrdhni padaṃ janaughā vighnantu vā tuṣyatu lokanāthaḥ // Bca_6.125 //
children.translated_text: let the throngs of people trample upon my head, or strike me — may the Protector of the World be pleased! // Bca_6.125 //

body.text: tathāgatānāmabhipretasaṃpādanāya loke lokaviṣaye sarvātmanā kāyena vācā manasā vā dāsībhāvaṃ svīkaromi / te 'pi me prasādaṃ kurvanto mastake pādaṃ nidadhatu / teṣāṃ pādaṃ pramuditacittaḥ śirasā dhārayāmi / anena mayi purvāparādhamapāsya jagatāṃ patirbhagavān saṃtuṣṭamānaso bhavatu //
body.translated_text: For the accomplishment of what is desired by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in the world, in the worldly domain, with my entire being — through body, speech, and mind — I accept the state of servitude. Let them too, showing me grace, place their feet upon my head. With a joyful mind I shall bear their feet upon my head. By this, having set aside my former offenses, may the Blessed One, the Lord of beings, become pleased in mind.

body.text: bhagavatsu ca gauravakāribhiḥ sattveṣvanādaro na kartavya iti prasādhayannāha-
body.translated_text: And he establishes that those who show reverence to the Blessed Ones should not show disrespect to beings —

children.text: ātmīkṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ jagattaiḥ kṛpātmabhirnaiva hi saṃśayo 'sti /
children.translated_text: All this world has been made their own by those of compassionate nature — of this there is indeed no doubt;

children.text: dṛśyanta ete nanu sattvarūpāsta eva nāthāḥ kimanādaro 'tra // Bca_6.126 //
children.translated_text: are not these [beings] seen in the form of living creatures those very Protectors themselves? Why then this disrespect? // Bca_6.126 //

body.text: sarvatragadharmadhātuprativedhāt sarvasattvasamatāpādanaparātmaparivartanādinā vā ātmīkṛtaṃ svīkṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ jagat, na kiyadeva / tairbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ karuṇāmayacittasaṃtānaiḥ / suniścitamevaitat / anyathā buddhatvāyogāt / tasmāt sattvarūpeṇa buddhā bhagavanta evaite sattvā dṛśyante / tena kimanādaro 'tra mūḍhacetasām? naiva yukta iti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Through penetrating the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) present everywhere, or through the exchange of self and other producing equality with all beings, all this world has been made their own — adopted — not just a part. By those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, whose mental continua are made of compassion. This is well established; otherwise, <s>Buddhahood</s> would be untenable. Therefore, the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> themselves are seen in the form of beings — these very beings. Why then this disrespect on the part of the deluded? It is not at all justified — this is the meaning.

body.text: anekārthatvādapi sattvārādhanasya tatraiva yatitavyamityāha-
body.translated_text: Since the service of beings serves many purposes, one should strive in that very [endeavor] — he says —

children.translated_text: This alone is the pleasing of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; this alone is the accomplishment of one's own purpose;
this alone is the removal of the world's suffering — therefore let this alone be my vow. // Bca_6.127 //

body.text: svārthasya buddhatvasaṃbhāralakṣaṇasyaiva / lokasya duḥkhāpahaṃ taddhetutvāt / etadeveti / sarvatra sattvārādhanamiti yojyam //
body.translated_text: 'One's own purpose' — characterized by the accumulation [of merit] for <s>Buddhahood</s> itself. 'The removal of the world's suffering' — because it is its cause. 'This alone' — everywhere this should be construed as 'the service of beings.'

body.text: āgāmibhayadarśanādapi ca parāpakāravaimukhyameva abhyasanīyamityudāharaṇenopadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, aversion to harming others should be cultivated even from seeing future dangers — he illustrates with an example —

children.translated_text: Just as a single king's officer oppresses a great multitude,

children.text: vikartuṃ naiva śaknoti dīrghadarśī mahājanaḥ // Bca_6.128 //
children.translated_text: the far-sighted multitude is unable to retaliate. // Bca_6.128 //

body.text: yasya rājño deśanivāsinaṃ tasyāsau rājapuruṣaḥ / mahājanaṃ nagaranigamagrāmakarvaṭādivāstavyam / pramathnāti vimardayati / sa ca āgāmirājadaṇḍabhayadarśitayā mahājano vacanamātreṇāpi yāvadvikāramupagantumasamarthaḥ / tena tāḍito 'pi saṃkucitavṛttirevāsti //
body.translated_text: The king's officer belongs to the king in whose territory [the people] reside. The 'great multitude' — the inhabitants of cities, market towns, villages, hamlets, and such. He 'oppresses' — harasses them. And that great multitude, having been shown the danger of future royal punishment, is unable to resort to even the slightest retaliation by a mere word. Thus, even when struck, one remains with constrained conduct.

body.text: kasmāt?
body.translated_text: Why?

body.text: yasmānnaiva sa ekākī tasya rājabalaṃ balam /
body.translated_text: Because he is not alone — the king's power is his power.

body.text: naiva sa rājapuruṣo 'sahāya eva draṣṭavyaḥ / kathaṃ punarayamasahāyo na bhavatītyāha- tasyeti / rājño balameva tasya balam, tatpakṣagrahaṇāt /
body.translated_text: That king's officer should not be regarded as being without support. How then is he not without support? He says 'his' — the king's power alone is his power, because of his being on the king's side.

body.text: tathā na durbalaṃ kaṃcidaparāddhaṃ vimānayet // Bca_6.129 //
body.translated_text: Likewise, one should not disrespect anyone who is weak and has not offended. // Bca_6.129 //

body.text: tasmāt kṛśaśaktimapi kṛtāparādhaṃ nāpakuryāt / so 'pi na yasmādekākī //
body.translated_text: Therefore, one should not harm even one of feeble power who has committed an offense. He too is not alone —

children.translated_text: because the guardians of hell and the compassionate ones are his strength.
Therefore one should please beings, as a servant [pleases] a wrathful king. // Bca_6.130 //

body.text: tasmādārādhayet sattvān / kutaḥ? yasmānnarakapālāśca tadapakāramiva pratyapakāriṇo 'nvācarantaḥ (?) kṛpāvantaśca jinādayaḥ tatpakṣapātino balam / kathamivārādhayet? adhṛṣyaṃ rājānaṃ sarvānuvṛttikaraṇānujīvino yathā, tathā //
body.translated_text: Therefore one should please beings. Why? Because the guardians of hell — who pursue retaliators as if [punishing] harm done to them — and the compassionate ones, the <s>Jinas</s> and such, who take their side, are [their] strength. How should one please them? Just as one who lives by serving an unapproachable king by doing everything in conformity [with his wishes] — so likewise.

body.text: kiṃ ca / lokaprasiddhita idamevamihoktam, na tu punaḥ sattvāprasaktiphalasya rājāparādhaphalena samānatā samastītyāha-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, this has been stated here according to worldly convention, but the consequence of displeasing beings is not comparable to the consequence of offending a king — he says —

children.translated_text: What could an angry king do that would equal the suffering of hell
that is experienced as a result of causing mental distress to beings? // Bca_6.131 //

body.text: kimiti kākvā pṛcchati / kiṃ tadduḥkhajātamutpādayituṃ nṛpatiḥ samartho bhavet? naiveti bhāvaḥ / kiṃbhūtam? yena duḥkhajātena nārakī vedanā anubhūyate //
body.translated_text: 'What' — he asks with a tone of reproach. Could a king be capable of producing that kind of suffering? Not at all — this is the meaning. Of what kind? The kind of suffering by which hellish pain is experienced.

children.translated_text: What could a pleased king give that would equal <s>Buddhahood</s>,
which is experienced as a result of causing mental happiness to beings? // Bca_6.132 //
Setting aside the future <s>Buddhahood</s> that arises from pleasing beings,

children.text: ihaiva saubhāgyayaśaḥsausthityaṃ kiṃ na paśyasi // Bca_6.133 //
children.translated_text: do you not see even here [the fruits of] good fortune, fame, and well-being? // Bca_6.133 //
Gracefulness, health, joy, and long life —

children.text: cakravartisukhaṃ sphītaṃ kṣamī prāpnoti saṃsaran // Bca_6.134 //
children.translated_text: the patient one obtains the abundant happiness of a <s>Cakravartin</s> while wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Bca_6.134 //

body.text: iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitā nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the sixth chapter, called 'The Perfection of Patience,' in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.

body.text: 7. vīryapāramitā nāma saptamaḥ paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: 7. The seventh chapter, called 'The Perfection of Effort.'

body.text: tadevaṃ vipakṣapratiṣedhena tridhā kṣāntiṃ pratipādya vīryaṃ pratipādayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus established patience in three aspects through the negation of its opposite, he says, in order to set forth effort —

children.text: evaṃ kṣamo bhajedvīryaṃ vīrye bodhiryataḥ sthitā /
children.translated_text: Thus patient, one should undertake effort, for awakening is established in effort;

children.text: na hi vīryaṃ vinā puṇyaṃ yathā vāyuṃ vināgatiḥ // Bca_7.1 //
children.translated_text: for without effort there is no merit, just as without wind there is no motion. // Bca_7.1 //

body.text: evamuktakrameṇa kṣamāyuktaḥ kṣamaḥ svayamabhyastakṣāntiḥ / bhajedvīryaṃ vīryamārabheta / anyathā duḥkhāsahiṣṇutayā vīryasya prasrabdhirna syāt / kasmāt punarvīryamupādīyata ityāha / vīryaṃ ityādi- yasmādvīrye buddhatvamavasthitam / taddhetukatayā tadāyattatvādbuddhatvasya / etadapi kutaḥ? yasmānna vīryamantareṇa puṇyaṃ puṇyasaṃbhāro 'sti / upalakṣaṇametat / jñānamapi draṣṭavyam, vīryasyobhayahetutvāt / tadanena vīryāt puṇyajñānasaṃbhārau, tābhyāṃ ca buddhatvamityuktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: 'Patient' — endowed with patience in the manner stated, one who has personally cultivated patience. 'Should undertake effort' — should commence effort. Otherwise, through intolerance of suffering, effort would slacken and would not [be maintained]. Why then should effort be undertaken? He says 'effort' and so forth: because <s>Buddhahood</s> is established in effort — because it depends on effort as its cause. And why is this? Because without effort there is no merit, no accumulation of merit. This is illustrative; knowledge too should be understood [as included], since effort is the cause of both. Thus by this it is stated that from effort come the accumulations of merit and knowledge, and from those, <s>Buddhahood</s>.

body.text: vīryasvarūpāparijñānāt pṛcchati-
body.translated_text: Due to not fully understanding the nature of effort, he asks —

children.translated_text: What is effort? Zeal in what is wholesome. What is said to be its opposite?
Laziness, attachment to the despicable, despondency, and self-deprecation. // Bca_7.2 //

body.text: kimetadvīryaṃ nāma? atrāha- kuśalotsāhaḥ / yo 'yaṃ kuśalakarmaṇi dānādau śrutādau ca samudyamaḥ, tadvīryamabhidhīyate / akuśale tu kausīdyameva / vipakṣeṇopahataṃ vīryamanaṅgamevābhimatasiddhaye iti tadvipakṣamapanayanāya darśayitumāha- tadvipakṣa ityādi / tasya vīryasya viruddho vināśāya pakṣo vipakṣaḥ ka ucyate? uttaramāha- ālasyamityādi / ālasyaṃ kausīdyaṃ kāyamanasorakarmaṇyatā / kutsite jugupsanīye hāsyalāsyādau āsaṅgaḥ / viṣādo viṣaṇṇatā / duṣkare karmaṇi cittasya vinivṛttiḥ / anadhyavasānamityarthaḥ / tena ātmano 'vamanyanā avajñā / ayaṃ tadvipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is this thing called effort? To this he says: 'zeal in what is wholesome' — the exertion in wholesome action, in giving and such, in learning and such — that is called effort. In the unwholesome, however, it is merely idleness. Since effort impaired by its opposite becomes ineffectual for the accomplishment of what is desired, he shows the opposite in order to remove it: 'its opposite' and so forth. What is called the opposite of effort, the faction that is hostile, [aimed at] its destruction? He answers: 'laziness' and so forth. 'Laziness' — sloth, the unworkability of body and mind. 'Attachment to the despicable' — clinging to what is contemptible, such as laughter and frivolous play. 'Despondency' — dejection, the mind's turning away from what is difficult to do; the meaning is lack of resolve. 'Self-deprecation' — contempt for oneself, because of that. This is its opposite.

body.text: tadālasyaniṣedhāya tatkāraṇaṃ tāvadupadarśayitumāha-
body.translated_text: In order to prohibit that laziness, he first shows its cause —

children.translated_text: Through the craving that takes as its refuge the relishing of the pleasure of inactivity and sleep,
through lack of alarm at the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, laziness arises. // Bca_7.3 //

body.text: saṃsāraduḥkhānudvegādasaṃvegāt, yo 'yamavyāpāro nirvyāpāratā, tatra tena vā sukhāsvādaḥ sukhābhirāmaḥ / sa ca nidrā ca middhākramaṇam / tābhyāṃ middhākramaṇamapāśrayatṛṣṇā avaṣṭambhanābhilāṣaḥ, tayā / ālasyamupajāyate iti yojanīyam / yadi vā / saṃsāraduḥkhānudvegādavyāpāraḥ, kvacidapi kuśalakarmaṇi na pravṛttiḥ, tasmāt sukhāsvādaḥ, tato nidrā, tasyāśca apāśrayatṛṣṇā, tayā //
body.translated_text: Through lack of alarm — lack of urgency — at the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is inactivity — the state of having nothing to do — and in that, or by that, the 'relishing of pleasure,' the delight in comfort. And that, together with sleep — the onset of drowsiness — the craving that takes these as its refuge, the desire for dependence [on them] — by that, laziness arises: this is how it should be construed. Alternatively: from lack of alarm at the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s> comes inactivity — no engagement in any wholesome action whatsoever; from that comes the relishing of pleasure; from that comes sleep; and the craving that takes it as refuge — by that [laziness arises].

body.text: ataḥ saṃsāraduḥkhānudveganivartanārthamiyamatra saṃvegabhāvanā āmukhīkartavyetyāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, for the purpose of removing the lack of alarm at the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>, this cultivation of urgency should be taken up as a preliminary — he says —

children.translated_text: Caught by the snare of the trap of defilements, having entered the trap of birth —
do you even now not realize that you have come into the mouth of Death? // Bca_7.4 //

body.text: vāgurikā matsyādivadhikā jālikā ucyante kaivartādayaḥ (dibhiḥ?) / kleśā eva vāgurikāḥ , tairāghrāta āyattīkṛtaḥ / kathamiti cet, praviṣṭo janmavāgurām, nikāyasabhāgatotpattireva vāgurikā jālam, tat praviṣṭaḥ, tadantargata ityarthaḥ / idamiha tadātmasātkaraṇe kāraṇam / adyāpi etāṃ daśāṃ prāpto 'pi mṛtyormukhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ san kimiti na vetsi? jātaścenmaraṇamavaśyaṃbhāvītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Trappers' (<s>vāgurikā</s>) — those who kill fish and such with nets — are called fishermen and such. The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) themselves are the trappers; by them one is ensnared — made subject [to them]. How so? One has entered the net of birth; the arising of a particular class of existence is itself the trapper's net — one has entered it, meaning one is caught within it. This is the reason for its appropriation. Even now, having reached this state, having entered the mouth of death — why do you not understand? The meaning is: if born, death is inevitable.

body.text: idamaparaṃ saṃvegakāraṇamāha-
body.translated_text: He states another cause for <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency):

children.translated_text: Do you not see your companions being slain one after another?

children.text: tathāpi nidrāṃ yāsyeva caṇḍālamahiṣo yathā // Bca_7.5 //
children.translated_text: Yet you still go to sleep, like a buffalo among <s>caṇḍālas</s>. // Bca_7.5 //

body.text: yūthaṃ vargaḥ, tatra bhavā yūthyāḥ, yaiḥ saha bālyādyavasthāyāṃ krīḍitahasitādinā vicaritam / tān svavargyān / caṇḍālānāmavaśyaṃmāraṇīyamahiṣavat / na paśyasi mamāpi iyamavasthitiḥ syāditi //
body.translated_text: 'Herd' (<s>yūtha</s>) is a group; 'herd-fellows' are those belonging to it — those with whom one has wandered, playing and laughing since childhood and other stages of life. Those of one's own group — like a buffalo of the <s>caṇḍālas</s> that is inevitably to be slaughtered. Do you not see [that] this same fate could befall me?

body.text: avaśyamiha kiyatkālaṃ parilambya mṛtyurāgamiṣyati / tena tāvatkālaṃ sukhānubhavanameva mama yuktamityatrāha- yadi nāmaivam, tathāpi nāvaśyaṃbhāvini maraṇe viśvāso yuktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Surely death will come after some time here; therefore it is appropriate for me to enjoy pleasures for that long — to this he says: even if that is so, still, trust in the certainty of death is not justified.

children.translated_text: When <s>Yama</s> is watching, and your path is blocked on all sides,

children.text: kathaṃ te rocate bhoktuṃ kathaṃ nidrā kathaṃ ratiḥ // Bca_7.6 //
children.translated_text: how can you delight in eating, how in sleep, how in pleasure? // Bca_7.6 //

body.text: iti vadhyapuruṣasyeva sarvato vadhyaghātakairadhiṣṭhitasya vadhyabhūmiṃ nīyamānasya niḥsaraṇamapaśyataḥ sukhāsikāvalambanamanucitameva bhavataḥ / tasmātsaṃvegato bhāvanayā anayā hetunivartanādālasyamapāsya kuśalapakṣotsāhavardhanamanuṣṭheyam //
body.translated_text: Just like a man condemned to death — surrounded on all sides by executioners, being led to the execution ground, seeing no escape — clinging to comfort is truly unbecoming for you. Therefore, through <s>saṃvega</s>, by this meditation, having averted the cause [of laziness], one should cast aside laziness and cultivate the strengthening of enthusiasm for the wholesome side.

body.text: athāpi syāt- yadi nāma avaśyaṃbhāvitā mṛtyoḥ, tathāpi tatsaṃnidhānamavagamya ālasyamapahāsyāmi ityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: One might think: even if death is certain, still, I will cast off laziness upon perceiving its approach. Anticipating this, he says:

children.translated_text: Death will come swiftly, having assembled its provisions;
even if you cast off laziness then, at that untimely [moment], what will you do? // Bca_7.7 //

body.text: saṃbhṛtaḥ sajjīkṛtaḥ saṃbhāraḥ sāmagrī vadhāya vyādhijarālakṣaṇo yena / yāvaditi lokoktam / śīghraṃ tvaritamanabhisaṃdhānāt / tadā mṛtyumukhāntargataḥ asamaye ālasyaṃ tyaktvāpi kiṃ kariṣyasi? na tadā kiṃcit prayojanamiti bhāvaḥ //
