body.translated_text: 'Assembled' means prepared; the 'provisions' — the assemblage for slaying, characterized by disease and old age — by which [death is equipped]. '<s>Yāvat</s>' is a colloquial expression [meaning 'quickly']. 'Swiftly' means hastily, without deliberation. Then, having entered the mouth of death, even if you cast off laziness at that improper time, what will you do? The meaning is: there will be no use then.

body.text: akālatāmevāsya samarthayituṃ vṛttatrayeṇāha-
body.translated_text: To establish why that time is indeed untimely, he says in three verses:

children.translated_text: 'This has not been attained; this has been started; this remains half-done' —
thinking 'Death has come suddenly — alas, I am slain!' // Bca_7.8 //

body.text: śokavegasamucchūnasāśruraktekṣaṇānanān /
body.translated_text: Gazing upon the faces of relatives swollen with the surge of grief, with tearful, bloodshot eyes,

body.text: bandhūnnirāśān saṃpaśyan yamadūtamukhāni ca // Bca_7.9 //
body.translated_text: now hopeless, and [seeing] the faces of <s>Yama</s>'s messengers, // Bca_7.9 //

children.translated_text: tormented by the memory of your own sins, hearing the cries of the hell-beings,
with limbs smeared by excrement [released] from terror, distressed — what will you do? // Bca_7.10 //

body.text: idaṃ yadanāgate kartavyatayā manasikṛtaṃ tanna prāptam / idamārabdhaṃ yatkāryamādita eva kartumiṣṭam / idamardhakṛtaṃ sthitam, yat kiyanniṣpannaṃ kiyadaniṣpannam / iti kāryaparyantamagatasyaiva akasmānmṛtyurāgato mama / aho bata atikaṣṭam, hato 'smīti vicintayan vihvalaḥ kiṃ kariṣyasītyanāgatena saṃbandhaḥ / śokaḥ priyaviprayogakṛtaścittaparitāpaḥ / tasya vego 'nivāryapravṛttiḥ / tena samucchūnāni samunnatāni sāśrūṇi sabāṣpāṇi raktāni tāmravarṇāni locanāni yeṣu ānaneṣu tāni tathā / tathābhūtāni ānanāni mukhāni yeṣāṃ bandhūnāṃ te tathā / tān saṃpaśyan vilokayan / tatrākarmakādhikārāt parasmaipadaṃ dṛśaḥ / kiṃbhūtān? nirāśān / kva? pratyujjīvanaṃ prati tyaktāśān, tatsānāthyavikalān vā / maraṇasamayopasthitakṛtāntānucaramukhāni ca saroṣaparuṣabhṛkuṭīni saṃpaśyan vihvalaḥ kiṃ kariṣyasi? svayaṃkṛtapāpakarmasmaraṇena maraṇasamaye kimityevaṃ mayā kṛtamiti paścāttāpena tāpitaḥ / naitāvanmātrameva, kiṃ tu śṛṇvannādāṃśca nārakān tīvrakāraṇānubhavanadukhanirmuktān vikrośitaśabdān narakasamudbhūtān arthāntarakopāṇāmeva (?) / tacchrutvā mamāpyevamevāvasthā iti saṃtrāsena yaḥ purīṣotsargo viṭpravṛttiḥ, tenopaliptagātraḥ / vihvalaḥ anāyattakāyavākcittapracāraḥ / kiṃ kariṣyasi sarvakriyāsu nivṛttavyāpāraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'This' — what was contemplated as something to be done in the future — has not been attained. 'This has been started' — what was intended to be done from the very beginning. 'This remains half-done' — what has been partly completed and partly not. Thus, for one who has not reached the end of [his] tasks, death has come suddenly — 'Alas, how terrible! I am slain!' — thinking thus, distressed, what will you do? — this connects with what follows. 'Grief' is the mental torment caused by separation from the beloved. Its 'surge' is its unstoppable flow. 'Swollen' by that means raised up; faces with tearful — with tear-filled — and reddened — copper-colored — eyes; those whose faces are such — those relatives — gazing upon them, beholding them. The verb '<s>dṛś</s>' takes <s>parasmaipada</s> because the action is intransitive. Of what kind? Hopeless — having abandoned hope regarding what? Regarding revival — bereft of hope for it, or deprived of its protection. And seeing the faces of the attendants of the Lord of Death who appear at the time of dying — fierce, harsh, with furrowed brows — distressed, what will you do? Tormented at the time of death by the recollection of one's own evil <s>karma</s> — 'Why did I act thus?' — scorched by remorse. Not only this much, but also hearing the cries of the hell-beings — the sounds of screaming emitted from experiencing intense torments in the hells, or [cries] of other kinds (?). Having heard that, [thinking] 'this same state awaits me too,' with limbs smeared — the body soiled — by the voiding of excrement due to terror; distressed — with uncontrolled activity of body, speech, and mind; what will you do — having ceased from all functions?

body.text: iti matvā svasthāvasthāyāmeva yatitavyam iti śikṣayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Reflecting thus, one should exert oneself while still in a state of health — teaching this, he says:

children.translated_text: 'I am like a live fish' — this fear is justified for you even now;
how much more for one who has committed evil, from the intense sufferings of the hells! // Bca_7.11 //

body.text: jīvanta eva matsyāḥ krameṇa bhakṣaṇārthaṃ prāyaḥ prāgdiṅanivāsibhireva janai rakṣyante / jīvanopalakṣitā matsyā jīvamatsyā iti teṣāmeva samayaḥ / śākapārthivāditvānmadhyamapadalopī samāsaḥ / tadvadahamapi adya śvo vā niyatameva mariṣyāmi iti manasi kṛtvā yuktaṃ bhayamihaiva te / ihaiva saṃprajānadavasthāyāmeva tavāsaṃprāptamaraṇasya maraṇataḥ, kiṃ punaḥ kṛtapāpasya bhavato bhayaṃ yuktaṃ na bhavati, ityapi āhāryam / atiduḥsahānnarakaduḥkhataḥ //
body.translated_text: Fish that are still alive are usually kept by people dwelling in the eastern regions for the purpose of gradual consumption. Live fish are marked by being alive — this is their designation. It is a compound with elision of the middle member, like '<s>śākapārthiva</s>' and such. Likewise I too — having kept in mind that 'I will certainly die today or tomorrow' — this fear is justified for you even now. Even now, while you are in a state of full awareness, not yet having met death — [this fear] from death [is justified]. How much more should fear not be justified for you who have committed evil? — this too should be understood. From the extremely unbearable sufferings of the hells.

body.text: nirvyāpārasukhāsvādābhiratamadhikṛtyāha-
body.translated_text: Addressing one who is absorbed in the enjoyment of effortless pleasures, he says:

children.translated_text: O delicate one, you are scorched even when touched by hot water;

children.text: kṛtvā ca nārakaṃ karma kimevaṃ svasthamāsyate // Bca_7.12 //
children.translated_text: having performed <s>karma</s> [leading to] the hells, how can you remain so at ease? // Bca_7.12 //

body.text: taptavāriṇāpi saṃspṛṣṭaḥ / sukumāreti saṃbodhanam / atimṛduśarīratayā soḍhumaśakto 'si / yadyevam, tadā kṛtvā cetyādi subodham //
body.translated_text: Touched even by hot water. 'O delicate one' — this is a form of address. Due to your extremely tender body, you are unable to endure. If so, then 'having performed' and so forth is easily understood.

body.text: aparamapi taṃ pratyāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, he says to that [mind]:

children.translated_text: O effortless one who desires results, O delicate one of much distress,
seized by death yet acting like an immortal — alas, O wretched one, you are being destroyed! // Bca_7.13 //

body.text: sukhahetūtpādanāya vyāpāraśūnyo 'si / atha ca tasya phalaṃ sukhamabhilaṣasi / duḥkhāsahiṣṇurasi, atha ca bahuvyatho 'si sarvaduḥkhākaratvāt / mṛtyunā ca vaśīkṛto 'si, atha ca amaraṇadharmāṇamātmānaṃ manyase / evaṃ ca viparyastaṃ caritamasya vipaśyan karuṇāyamānaḥ sakhedamenamāha- hā duḥkhita vihanyase / saṃmohabahulatayā kaṣṭāṃ daśāṃ praviṣṭo 'si / ātmagatameva vā vimṛśati / evamanyatrāpi yathāsaṃbhavaṃ draṣṭavyam / nirudyamādīni cāmantritapadāni //
body.translated_text: You are devoid of effort for producing the cause of happiness, yet you desire its fruit — happiness. You are unable to endure suffering, yet you are one of much distress — because of [your karma] producing every kind of suffering. You are under the power of death, yet you consider yourself to be of deathless nature. Seeing such perverted conduct of this [mind], speaking with compassion and sorrow, he says: 'Alas, O wretched one, you are being destroyed! Through the predominance of delusion, you have entered a terrible state.' Or he is reflecting upon his own [condition] alone. Elsewhere too, this should be understood as appropriate. '<s>Nirudyama</s>' and the others are vocative forms.

body.text: nidrāparatantraṃ pratyāha-
body.translated_text: Addressing one who is enslaved to sleep, he says:

children.translated_text: Having obtained the human [birth] as a boat, cross the great river of suffering!

children.text: mūḍha kālo na nidrāyā iyaṃ naurdurlabhā punaḥ // Bca_7.14 //
children.translated_text: O fool, this is no time for sleep — this boat will be hard to find again! // Bca_7.14 //

body.text: aṣṭākṣaṇavinirmuktaṃ manuṣyabhāvapratilambhaṃ nāvamiva abhyudayādipāragamanāya prāpya tara plavasva duḥkhamayīṃ mahānadīm / sarvaduḥkhāni pṛṣṭhīkuruṣva / vīryāvalambaneneti yāvat / he mohaparavaśa, nāyaṃ kālo nidrāyāḥ, yāvadiyaṃ nauḥ saṃnihitā / yadi nedānīmeva yatnaḥ kriyate, tadā punariyaṃ durgatigatasya naurdurlabhā bhaviṣyati / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: Having obtained the attainment of human existence, free from the eight unfavorable conditions, like a boat for crossing to the far shore of higher rebirth and such — cross, swim across the great river that is full of suffering! Turn your back on all sufferings — meaning through reliance on vigor. O you who are subject to delusion, this is no time for sleep, while this boat is at hand. If effort is not made right now, then for one who has fallen into lower states of existence, this boat will be hard to find again. As it is said:

children.translated_text: 'Where again will there be such a conjunction?'
Thus.

body.text: bodhi. 1.4
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>. 1.4

body.text: evamālasyaṃ nivārya kutsitāsaktiṃ nivārayannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus warded off laziness, averting attachment to base things, he says:

children.translated_text: Having abandoned the supreme delight in the <s>Dharma</s>, a continuous stream of infinite joy,
how can you find pleasure in agitation, laughter, and such — causes of suffering? // Bca_7.15 //

body.text: śubhakarmaṇāṃ ratiṃ śreṣṭhāmuttamām / kiṃbhūtām? anantaratisaṃtatim / sugatiparaṃparāsaṃjananādanantā aparyavasānā ratisaṃtatiḥ sukhapravāho yasyāḥ sā tathā / ata eva uttame tyuktam / tāmapahāya ratirabhirāmaḥ, auddhatyamunnatatā / kāyacittayoḥ krīḍanaśīlateti yāvat / hāso vāgauddhatyam / sarabhasasya vāgvikāra iti yāvat / ādiśabdādgītādiparigrahaḥ / tatra kathaṃ ratistava? na yuktetyabhiprāyaḥ / kiṃbhūte? duḥkhahetau / narakādidurgatyupanayanādduḥkhasya heturbhavati //
body.translated_text: The supreme, the highest delight in wholesome actions. Of what kind? A continuous stream of infinite joy — because it generates an unbroken succession of favorable rebirths, the stream of happiness that characterizes it is endless and without limit. For this very reason it is called 'supreme.' Having abandoned that, [one finds] pleasure — delight; '<s>auddhatya</s>' — agitation, restlessness of body and mind; meaning a disposition toward frivolity. '<s>Hāsa</s>' (laughter) is verbal agitation — meaning a vocal disturbance of the impetuous. The word '<s>ādi</s>' ('and such') includes singing and similar activities. How can you have pleasure in that? The intent is: it is not justified. Of what kind? A cause of suffering — because it leads to lower states of rebirth such as the hells, it becomes a cause of suffering.

body.text: evaṃ kutsitāsaktimapi nirākṛtya viṣādātmāvamanyanāṃ vīryavipakṣaṃ nirākartum, aparamapi ca tadvipakṣanirasanāya pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus also refuted attachment to base things, in order to refute despondency and self-deprecation — the adversaries of vigor — and to present yet another [argument] for the removal of its adversary, he says:

children.translated_text: Non-despondency, the array of forces, earnestness, self-mastery,
equality of self and other, and the exchange of self and other — // Bca_7.16 //

body.text: viṣādaviparīto 'viṣādaḥ / balānāṃ vyūhaḥ samūho vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaḥ / tātparyaṃ nipuṇatā / ātmavidheyatā ātmavaśavartitā / etāḥ sarvāḥ kṛtadvandvasamāsāḥ / yadi vā /
body.translated_text: The opposite of despondency is non-despondency. The 'array' — assemblage — of forces has the characteristics to be described. 'Earnestness' is diligence. 'Self-mastery' is bringing oneself under one's own control. All of these are <s>dvandva</s> compounds. Or alternatively:

body.text: ebhiḥ sahitā ātmavidheyatā / parātmasamatāparātmaparivartane dhyānaparicchede [bodhi.8] vakṣyamāṇe / idamapi samastaṃ kausīdyaprahāṇāya vīryasamṛddhaye prabhavatītyuddeśaḥ //
body.translated_text: self-mastery combined with these. The equality of self and other, and the exchange of self and other, will be discussed in the chapter on meditation [Chapter 8]. All of this together serves for the abandonment of laziness and the accomplishment of vigor — this is the summary statement.

body.text: uddiṣṭamevārthaṃ krameṇa nirdiśannāha-
body.translated_text: Expounding in order the very topic that has been outlined, he says:

body.text: naivāvasādaḥ kartavyaḥ kuto me bodhirityataḥ /
body.translated_text: One should not become despondent, [thinking] 'How can awakening be mine?'

body.text: kuto me bodhiriti, kathamahaṃ varākaḥ samyaksaṃbodhibhājanam? buddhatvaṃ hi tīkṣṇendriyasya ārabdhavīryasya aparimitapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraiḥ atiduṣkarakarmānuṣṭhānaiḥ anekaiśca kalpāsaṃkhyeyaiḥ kasyacit puruṣaviśeṣasya sādhyaṃ bhavati / ahaṃ tu na tādṛśa iti kathaṃ madvidhānāṃ tathāvidhaṃ buddhatvaṃ saṃbhāvyeta, ityevamākāramanasikārādavasādo viṣādo na kartavyaḥ, mahārthabhraṃśasya hetutvāt / yathoktam- avasādo 'pyanartha iti [śi. sa. 34] // kasmāt?
body.translated_text: 'How can awakening be mine?' — 'How can a wretch like me be a vessel for perfect awakening? For <s>Buddhahood</s> is achieved only by someone of sharp faculties, of aroused vigor, through immeasurable accumulations of merit and wisdom, through the performance of exceedingly difficult deeds, and through innumerable <s>kalpa</s>-<s>asaṃkhyeyas</s> (incalculable aeons). But I am not of such [capacity]' — 'so how could <s>Buddhahood</s> of that kind be possible for the likes of me?' — from such mental reflection, despondency and depression should not be entertained, because it is the cause of losing the great purpose. As it is stated: 'Despondency too is a harm' [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> 34]. Why?

body.text: yasmāttathāgataḥ satyaṃ satyavādīdamuktavān // Bca_7.17 //
body.translated_text: Because the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the truthful speaker, has spoken this truth: // Bca_7.17 //

body.text: yasmāt tathāgataḥ idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ satyamavitathamuktavān kathitavān / kathaṃ jñāyate ityāha- satyavādīti / jñānakriyāsaṃbhavādaviparītavādī / ataḥ satyābhidhānahetupadametat //
body.translated_text: Because the <s>Tathāgata</s> has spoken — declared — this, which is about to be stated, as truth, as not false. How is this known? He says: 'the truthful speaker.' Because of the possibility of [his] knowledge and action, he is one who speaks without error. Therefore, this is the evidential statement for the truth of his declaration.

body.text: kiṃ tatsatyamuktavān?
body.translated_text: What is that truth he has spoken?

children.translated_text: Even they were once gadflies, mosquitoes, flies, and worms,
who, through the power of perseverance, attained the supreme, hard-to-reach awakening. // Bca_7.18 //

body.text: ityāha / te 'pi buddhā bhagavantaḥ purvaṃ śākyamuniratnaśikhidīpaṃkaraprabhṛtayaḥ saṃsārasāgarāvartāntargatāḥ pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ paribhramanta evaṃbhūtā evāsan babhūvuḥ, yairutsāhabalāt vīryotkarṣasāmarthyāt saṃbhārān saṃbhṛtya prāptā adhigatā durāpā durlabhapratilambhā bodhiruttamā anuttarā / ārabdhavīryasya na kiṃcidduṣkaramiti bhāvaḥ / idaṃ tat satyam //
body.translated_text: — he says. Even those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> — <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, and others — previously, while caught in the whirlpool of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, wandering in the state of ordinary beings, were indeed of just such a nature — they were [once gadflies and such]. They who, through the power of perseverance — through the strength and capacity of supreme vigor — having accumulated the requisites, attained — realized — the supreme, the unsurpassed awakening, which is hard to attain — hard to obtain. The meaning is: for one of aroused vigor, nothing is difficult. This is that truth.

body.text: ato mama punaratitarāṃ na durlabhā bodhirityāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, for me even more so, awakening is not hard to obtain — he says:

children.text: kimutāhaṃ naro jātyā śakto jñātuṃ hitāhitam /
children.translated_text: How much more so I, born as a human, capable of knowing benefit and harm —
if I do not abandon the way of the Omniscient Ones, why should I not attain awakening? // Bca_7.19 //

body.text: kiṃ punarahaṃ manuṣyabhūto janmanā / śakto jñātuṃ hitāhitamiti / idaṃ hitamidamahitam, śubhamaśubhaṃ ca karmetyupadiṣṭam, jñātumavaboddhuṃ samartho 'smi, iti vicintya sarvajñasya sarvavastutattvavedinaḥ nītirnayaḥ upādeyatattvapratipādanam / tasya anutsargādaparityāgāt / tasya ādānopādānasevanādityarthaḥ / buddhatvaṃ nāpnuyāmaham / kākvā paṭhanād āpnuyāmeveti / etadbhagavatā ratnameghe darśitam / yathoktam-
body.translated_text: Moreover, I, born as a human being, am capable of knowing what is beneficial and harmful — 'this is beneficial, this is harmful; this is wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>' — as taught, I am able to understand and comprehend. Reflecting thus, the instruction of the Omniscient One — the knower of the true nature of all things — his teaching, which conveys the truth to be adopted — by not abandoning it, by not relinquishing it, and by taking it up, adopting, and practicing it — this is the meaning — would I not attain <s>Buddhahood</s>? Reading with rhetorical force: I would indeed attain it. This has been shown by the Blessed One in the <s>Ratnamegha</s>. As stated —

body.text: iha bodhisattvo naivaṃ cittamutpādayati- duṣprāpyā bodhirmanuṣyabhūtena satā / idaṃ ca me vīryaṃ parīttaṃ ca hīnaṃ ca / kusīdo 'ham / bodhiśca ādīptaśiraścailopamena bahūn kalpān bahūni kalpaśatāni bahūni kalpasahasrāṇi samudācaratā samudānetavyā / tannāhamutsahe
body.translated_text: 'Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not generate such a thought: "Awakening is hard to attain for one who is a human being; and this effort of mine is meager and inferior; I am lazy; and awakening must be pursued for many <s>kalpas</s>, many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, with the urgency of one whose turban is on fire; I am not able

body.text: īdṛśaṃ bhāramudvoḍhum / kiṃ tarhi bodhisattvenaivaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam- ye 'pi te 'bhisaṃbuddhāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, ye 'pi vā abhisaṃbhotsyante, te 'pi īdṛśenaiva nayena, īdṛśyā pratipadā, īdṛśenaiva vīryeṇābhisaṃbuddhāḥ, yāvanna ca te tathāgatabhūtā evābhisaṃbuddhāḥ / ahamapi tathā tathā ghaṭiṣye, tathā tathā vyāyaṃsye sarvasattvasādhāraṇena vīryeṇa sarvasattvārambaṇena vīryeṇa yathāhamapyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsye iti //
body.translated_text: to bear such a burden." Rather, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should generate this thought: "Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones who have attained awakening, and those who will attain it — they too have attained awakening by just this method, by just this practice, by just this effort, and they were not already <s>Tathāgatas</s> when they attained awakening. I too shall strive thus and thus, I shall exert myself thus and thus, with effort common to all beings, with effort directed toward all beings, so that I too may attain unsurpassed perfect awakening."'

body.text: yuktamevaitat, kevalamatiduṣkarakarmaśravaṇādanadhyavasāyo vinivartayitumaśakya iti vikalpayannāha-
body.translated_text: This is indeed justified; but if one entertains the doubt that the resolve cannot be turned back from hearing of exceedingly difficult deeds, he says —

body.text: athāpi hastapādādi dātavyamiti me bhayam /
body.translated_text: But if I am afraid that hands, feet, and such must be given —

body.text: karacaraṇaśiraḥ prabhṛtidānamantareṇa buddhatvaṃ na prāpyate, iti atiduṣkarakarmasu pravṛttibhayādutsāho nivartata eva / iti cenmanyase svacittamevamāha-
body.translated_text: Without the giving of hands, feet, head, and so on, <s>Buddhahood</s> is not attained — thus, if enthusiasm is turned back out of fear of engaging in exceedingly difficult deeds, and if you think thus, he addresses his own mind —

body.text: gurulāghavamūḍhatvaṃ tanme syādavicārataḥ // Bca_7.20 //
body.translated_text: That would be my confusion about what is heavy and light, through lack of discernment. // <s>Bca</s> 7.20 //

body.text: tadetad gurulāghavamūḍhatvameva me / alpe bahutaraṃ bahutare cālpataramiti mohavaśena avicārato 'vivekānmama syāt, na tu paramārthavicārataḥ //
body.translated_text: That is indeed confusion about what is heavy and what is light on my part — [thinking] that the lesser is greater and the greater is lesser — through the power of delusion, through lack of discernment, through lack of discrimination, it would be mine; but not from ultimate discernment.

body.text: paramārthavicāreṇa gurulāghavaviparyāsa evāyamityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing through ultimate analysis that this is indeed a reversal of heavy and light, he says —

children.translated_text: I would have to be cut, split, burned, and torn apart, many times over,
for countless <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, and still awakening would not come about. // <s>Bca</s> 7.21 //

body.text: saṃsāracārake nivasaṃstathāvidhakarmavaśācchettavyaścāsmi karacaraṇādyaṅgapratyaṅgacchedanānnarakādiṣu / tathā bhettavyo 'smi śaktikuntādibhiḥ / dāhyo narakadahanādinā / pāṭyo jvalitakrakacādinā / anekaśaḥ anekavārān / narakādiṣu kāraṇāmanubhavan aparyantapathi saṃsāre / kalpānāṃ koṭīrasaṃkhyeyāḥ saṃkhyātumaśakyāḥ iti / akāmasyāpi duḥkhamaparyantamanekaprakāramāpatiṣyati, na ca buddhatvasaṃbhārāya tat saṃpatsyate //
body.translated_text: While dwelling in the wandering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, through the force of such <s>karma</s>, I would have to be cut — through the cutting of limbs and sub-limbs such as hands and feet in the hells and such. Likewise I would have to be split — by spears, lances, and such. Burned — by the fires of hell and such. Torn apart — by blazing saws and such. Many times over — on many occasions. While experiencing torments in the hells and such, on the endless path of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Countless <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — impossible to enumerate. Even unwillingly, immeasurable suffering of many kinds would befall me, and yet it would not contribute to the accumulation for <s>Buddhahood</s>.

body.text: idaṃ saṃsārāparyantatayā duḥkhaṃ bahutaraṃ niṣphalaṃ ca / buddhatvaprasādhakaṃ punaralpataraṃ saphalaṃ cetyupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing that this suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, being endless, is greater and fruitless, while the suffering that accomplishes <s>Buddhahood</s> is lesser and fruitful, he says —

children.text: idaṃ tu me parimitaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃbodhisādhanam /
children.translated_text: But this suffering of mine for accomplishing awakening is limited,
like the pain of extracting a thorn to remove [chronic] agony. // <s>Bca</s> 7.22 //

body.text: yad buddhatvaprasādhakaṃ tadidaṃ duḥkhaṃ parimitaṃ mama pratiniyatakālabhāvitayā, duḥkha [praśamana]hetuśca / tattathābhūtaṃ śalyaṃ tena vyathā, tasyā apoho nivṛttiḥ / tannimittaṃ tadvayudāsāya / yāvajjīvaṃ tatkṛtaduḥkhaprahāṇāyetyarthaḥ / tasya naṣṭaśalyasyotpāṭanaṃ śarīrāduddharaṇam / apakarṣaṇamiti yāvat / tena yadduḥkhaṃ pratiniyatakālamalpataram / dīrghakālikaduḥkhopaśamanimittam / tadvat soḍhumucitamidamapi duḥkham //
body.translated_text: That suffering which accomplishes <s>Buddhahood</s> — this suffering of mine is limited, because it is cultivated over a definite period of time, and it is a cause of the cessation of suffering. That thorn — the agony caused by it — the removal of that, its elimination — for the sake of removing it. For the sake of removing the suffering caused by it for a lifetime — this is the meaning. The extraction of that thorn — the drawing out from the body, the pulling out — that is what is meant. The pain caused by that is of a definite, brief duration, and is for the sake of pacifying long-term suffering. Like that, this suffering too is fitting to be endured.

body.text: ato 'pi samucitamidamityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, this is appropriate — he says —

children.translated_text: All physicians produce health through the pain of treatment;
therefore, to destroy many sufferings, a small [amount of suffering] should be endured. // <s>Bca</s> 7.23 //

body.text: sarve 'pi na kecideva / laṅghanapācanādikṛtairyatheṣṭāhāravihārapratiṣedhajanitaiśca kriyāduḥkhaiḥ rogapīḍitānāmārogyaṃ vidadhāti / anyathā tatkartumaśakyam / yata evam, tasmādatiśayena alpamalpakaṃ duḥkhaṃ soḍhavyam / kimartham? bahūni duḥkhāni hantum / sarvasattvānāmātmanaśca dīrghakālikasarvaduḥkhapraśamanāyetyarthaḥ / evaṃ tāvat svīkartuṃ yuktaṃ dhīmataḥ //
body.translated_text: 'All' — not just some. Through the pain of treatment — caused by fasting, digestive remedies, and the prohibition of food and activities as desired — they bring about health for those afflicted by disease. Otherwise it is impossible to do so. Since this is so, therefore a very small, slight amount of suffering should be endured. For what purpose? To destroy many sufferings — for the pacification of all long-term suffering for all beings and for oneself. This is the meaning. Thus, the wise person should accept this.

body.text: na cedaṃ yuktamapi duṣkaraṃ karma ādikarmikasya prathamanujñātaṃ bhagavateti darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing that this treatment, though appropriate, was not prescribed as difficult action for the beginner by the Blessed One, he says —

body.text: kriyāmimāmapyucitāṃ varavaidyo na dattavān /
body.translated_text: But the supreme physician has not administered even this appropriate treatment;

body.text: kriyāmimāṃ samanantarapratipāditāṃ duḥkhotpādanīm / ucitāmapi sevanīyāmapi / varavaidyo bhagavān sarvathā sarvāvyadhicikitsakaḥ / prathamaṃ na dattavān, na kartavyatayā pratipāditavānādikarmikasya / kathaṃ tarhi rāgādivyādhīnapanayati? āha-
body.translated_text: This treatment, just described, which produces pain — even though appropriate, even though worth pursuing — the supreme physician, the Blessed One, the healer of all diseases in every way — did not administer it initially, did not prescribe it as something to be done for the beginner. How then does he remove the diseases of desire and such? He says —

body.text: madhureṇopacāreṇa cikitsati mahāturān // Bca_7.24 //
body.translated_text: He treats the gravely afflicted with gentle methods. // <s>Bca</s> 7.24 //

body.text: sukumāratareṇopacāreṇa upakrameṇa / yathākṣamaṃ cikitsāpraṇayanenetyarthaḥ / cikitsati rogamuktān karoti / mahāturān dīrgharogiṇo rāgādimahāvyādhigrastān //
body.translated_text: With a most gentle method — with a gradual approach. With treatment administered according to [the patient's] capacity — this is the meaning. 'He treats' — he makes free from disease. 'The gravely afflicted' — those suffering from chronic illness, those seized by the great diseases of desire and such.

body.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ madhuropacāra ityāha-
body.translated_text: What then is this gentle method? He says —

children.translated_text: At first, the Guide enjoins [the practitioner] to the giving of vegetables and such;
he arranges it so that later one would give away even one's own flesh. // <s>Bca</s> 7.25 //

body.text: mātsaryamalāpanayanārthaṃ sukhasukhena saṃbhārasaṃvardhanārthaṃ ca śakyaparityāge śākasaktupiṇḍikādidānena prathamataraṃ pravartayati nāyako bhagavān / punastathopāyaviśeṣeṇa niyojanaṃ karoti / taditi lokoktau vā / yadyathā dātā mṛdudānābhyāsakrameṇa adhimātrādhimātradānābhyāsaprakarṣamāsādayan paścāduttarakālamakṛcchreṇaiva svamāṃsarudhirādikamapi prasanna eva prayacchet //
body.translated_text: For the purpose of removing the stain of miserliness and for the easy, comfortable augmentation of the accumulations, the Guide, the Blessed One, first sets [the practitioner] in motion with giving that is easy to relinquish — giving of vegetables, balls of barley flour, and such. Then, through such special skillful means, he directs [the practitioner further]. 'That' — or [it means] as is commonly said. In such a way that the giver, through the gradual practice of gentle giving, reaching the highest degree of practice of the most intense generosity, would later, in due course, give away even one's own flesh, blood, and such, cheerfully and without difficulty.

body.text: kathaṃ punaretadevamityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: How is this possible? — anticipating the question, he says —

children.translated_text: When an understanding like that toward vegetables arises even toward one's own flesh,

children.text: māṃsāsthi tyajatastasya tadā kiṃ nāma duṣkaram // Bca_7.26 //
children.translated_text: then for one who gives away flesh and bones, what is difficult? // <s>Bca</s> 7.26 //

body.text: yasmin kāle dānābhyāsāt paramaprakarṣagamanāt sarvathāpagatamātsaryatayā śākeṣviva svamāṃse 'pi nirāsaṅgā buddhirupajāyate, tadā svamāṃsādidāne 'pi nāśakyānuṣṭhānabuddhiriti tasmin kāle kiṃ nāma duṣkaram? naiva kiṃcidityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: At the time when, through the practice of giving reaching the ultimate degree, through complete freedom from miserliness in every respect, an unattached understanding arises toward one's own flesh just as toward vegetables — then, even in giving away one's own flesh and such, there is no thought of being unable to practice it. At that time, what indeed is difficult? Nothing at all — this is the meaning.

body.text: athāpi syāt- atidīrghakālaṃ parārthe saṃsaratā tadduḥkhaṃ kathamiva parihartuṃ śakyamityatrāha-
body.translated_text: One might say: how can the suffering of one who wanders for an exceedingly long time for the sake of others be avoided? To this he says —

body.text: na duḥkhī tyaktapāpatvātpaṇḍitatvānna durmanāḥ /
body.translated_text: He does not suffer because evil has been abandoned; he is not despondent because of his wisdom;

body.text: mithyākalpanayā citte pāpātkāye yato vyathā // Bca_7.27 //
body.translated_text: since suffering of the mind is due to false conceptualization, and of the body due to evil. // <s>Bca</s> 7.27 //

body.text: dvividhameva hi duḥkhaṃ bādhakamupajāyate kāyikaṃ mānasikaṃ ceti / tadetad dvayamapi bodhisattvasya na saṃbhavati / kāyavacanamanobhiḥ sarvāvadyavirateḥ kāyikaṃ duḥkhamasya na jāyate / yuktyāgamābhyāmubhayanairātmyasya ca niścayanānmānasamapi kutaḥ? yato mithyākalpanayā asadvikalpena ātmātmīyagrahapravṛttena bhāvādyabhiniveśakṛtena vā citte duḥkham, pāpāt prāṇātipātādeḥ kāye / evaṃ tāvadduḥkhahetuparihārādduḥkhamasya na jāyate iti pratipāditam //
body.translated_text: For only two kinds of obstructive suffering arise: physical and mental. And both of these do not occur for a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Physical suffering does not arise for one who has completely abstained from all wrongdoing through body, speech, and mind. And mental [suffering] — from where? Since through reasoning and scripture, the selflessness of both [person and phenomena] has been ascertained. For suffering of the mind is due to false conceptualization — false imagination proceeding from the grasping of self and what belongs to self, or caused by clinging to existence and so on. And [suffering] of the body is due to evil — killing and such. Thus, through the avoidance of the causes of suffering, suffering does not arise for this one — this has been demonstrated.

body.text: idānīṃ sukhameva kevalamasyāstīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, showing that only happiness exists for this one, he says —

children.text: puṇyena kāyaḥ sukhitaḥ pāṇḍityena manaḥ sukhi /
children.translated_text: The body is made happy by merit, the mind is happy through wisdom;

children.text: tiṣṭhan parārthaṃ saṃsāre kṛpāluḥ kena khidyate // Bca_7.28 //
children.translated_text: remaining in <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of others, the compassionate one — by what would he be wearied? // <s>Bca</s> 7.28 //

body.text: sukhaṃ jātamasya kāyasyeti sukhitaḥ / sukhaṃ vidyate 'sya manasa iti sukhi / evamubhayasukhasamanvāgatatvāt kṛpāvān parārthaṃ saṃsāre saṃsaran kena duḥkhena khidyate, khedaṃ manyate? yadi vā / kena khidyate? khedahetorabhāvānna kenaciditi bhāvaḥ / tat kimidamakāraṇabhīrutayā vaimukhyamupādīyate?
body.translated_text: 'Made happy' — happiness has arisen for this body. 'Happy' — happiness exists for this mind. Thus, being endowed with happiness of both kinds, the compassionate one, wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of others — by what suffering would he be wearied, would he consider it wearisome? Or alternatively: by what would he be wearied? Because there is no cause of weariness — by nothing at all. This is the meaning. So why is aversion adopted through groundless fear?

body.text: syādetat- dīrghakālamāsevitabhāvitabahulīkṛtena mahatā puṇyasaṃbhāreṇa samyaksaṃbodhiradhigamyate / tadvaraṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ śīghrakālatayā śrāvakayānamevāśrayaṇīyaṃ syādityāśaṅkayāha-
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Perfect awakening is attained through a great accumulation of merit cultivated and developed over a long time. In that case, it would be better for those seeking liberation to take refuge in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, since it is quicker. Anticipating this, he says —

children.translated_text: Destroying previous evil and gathering oceans of merit,
by the power of <s>bodhicitta</s> alone, he is swifter even than the <s>Śrāvakas</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 7.29 //

body.text: pūrvakṛtāni yāni pāpāni tāni bodhicittabalādeva kṣayīṇi kurvan / yathoktaṃ prāk-
body.translated_text: Destroying — making exhausted — the evil previously committed, by the power of <s>bodhicitta</s> alone. As stated before —

body.text:
yugāntakālānalavanmahānti pāpāni yannirdahati kṣaṇena /
iti /
[bodhi. 1.14]
body.translated_text: 'Like the fire at the end of an age, it burns up great evils in an instant.' Thus. [<s>Bodhi</s>. 1.14]

body.text: tathā bodhicittabalādeva pratīcchan ādadānaḥ puṇyasāgarān /
body.translated_text: Likewise, by the power of <s>bodhicitta</s> alone, gathering — receiving — oceans of merit.

body.text: yaduktam-
body.translated_text: As stated —

body.text:
avicchinnāḥ puṇyadhārāḥ pravartante nabhaḥsamāḥ /
iti /
[bodhi .1.19]
body.translated_text: 'Unbroken streams of merit flow forth, equal to space.' Thus. [<s>Bodhi</s>. 1.19]

body.text: evaṃvidhopāyabalajavena mahāyānamārūḍho bodhisattvaḥ śrāvakebhyo 'pi śīghragaḥ tvaritagāmī //
body.translated_text: By such swiftness of the force of skillful means, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has mounted the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is swifter even than the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, faster in progress.

children.translated_text: Thus, going from happiness to happiness, what discerning person would despair,
having obtained the chariot of <s>bodhicitta</s>, which removes all weariness and fatigue? // <s>Bca</s> 7.30 //

body.text: pratipāditamevārthaṃ piṇḍīkṛtya darśayati / evamuktakrameṇa sarvāvadyavirateḥ purākṛtapāpakṣayācca svapne 'pi durgatigamanābhāvāt tīvrābhiprāyeṇa anekasukhena aharniśamākāśadhātuvyāpinaḥ
body.translated_text: He shows the meaning already established, in summary. Thus, in the manner described, because one who has completely abstained from all wrongdoing and whose previously committed evil has been exhausted would not go to lower realms even in dreams, and because of intense aspiration, and because of the daily augmentation of an ocean of merit pervading the expanse of space

body.text: puṇyasāgarasyābhivardhanācca sugatiparaṃparāsanmārgāvataraṇabodhicittaṃ rathamiva āsādya / āruhyeti yāvat / sarvakhedaiḥ parikleśaiḥ śrama āyāsaḥ, tamapahantīti pratipāditanayena, sarvakhedaśramaṃ vā apahantīti tam / sukhādekasmādaparamuttarottaramadhikādhikaṃ sukhaṃ devamanuṣyasaṃpattilakṣaṇaṃ gacchan anuprāpnuvan ko nāma prekṣāvān viṣādamāpadyeta?
body.translated_text: — having reached, that is, having mounted, <s>bodhicitta</s> like a chariot, [which leads to] the succession of happy destinies and entry onto the noble path — [the chariot] which removes all weariness and fatigue, or which removes all afflictive weariness and fatigue, as demonstrated by the method [described] — going from one happiness to another, obtaining ever higher and greater happiness consisting of the attainments of gods and humans — what discerning person would fall into despair?

body.text: tadevamanekavidhaviṣādanimittapratiṣedhena aviṣādaṃ pratipādya balavyūhaṃ pratipādayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus established freedom from despair through the refutation of the many grounds for despair, in order to teach the array of powers, he says —

children.translated_text: The power of aspiration, steadfastness, joy, and release, for the accomplishment of beings' welfare;
one should generate aspiration out of fear of suffering and by contemplating the benefits. // <s>Bca</s> 7.31 //

body.text: idamapyuddeśavākyameva / chanda iha kuśalābhilāṣaḥ / sthāma ārabdhadṛḍhatā / ratiḥ satkarmāsaktiḥ muktirasāmarthye tāvatkālamutsargaḥ / etaccaturaṅgabalam, anekāvayavasamudāyātmakatvāt, hastyādibalavat / sattvārthasiddhaye vīryahetutvāt, asya vīryasya ca sarvābhimatasādhanatvāditi bhāvaḥ / tatra chandabalasya bahukaratvāt, chandamityādinā asyotpattinimittamāha- duḥkhabhayāditi / aśubhakarmaṇo duḥkhaṃ jāyata iti trāsācchandaṃ kuryāt / anuśaṃsāṃśca bhāvayan / anuśaṃsāḥ phaladvāreṇa guṇaviśeṣāḥ / te ca arthāt kuśalakarmaṇa eva / tān bhāvayan / śubhakarmaṇo 'nekaprakāreṇa madhuraphalotpattiṃ punaḥ punaḥ saṃcintayannityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: This too is merely a statement of the topic. '<s>Chanda</s>' (desire) here means aspiration for the wholesome. '<s>Sthāma</s>' (steadfastness) is firmness once begun. '<s>Rati</s>' (delight) is attachment to good deeds. '<s>Mukti</s>' (letting go) is temporary release when there is lack of capacity. This four-limbed force, being of the nature of a composite of many parts, is like the force of elephants and such. Because it is the cause of <s>vīrya</s> (diligence) for accomplishing the welfare of beings, and because this <s>vīrya</s> is the means for accomplishing all that is desired — this is the purport. Therein, since the power of <s>chanda</s> is of great efficacy, he states the cause of its generation beginning with '<s>chanda</s>' — 'from fear of suffering': knowing that suffering arises from unwholesome action, one should generate <s>chanda</s> out of dread. 'And by contemplating the benefits': the benefits are particular qualities in terms of their fruits. And these are only of wholesome action. Contemplating them — the meaning is: reflecting again and again on the arising of manifold sweet fruits from meritorious action. //

body.text: sāṃprataṃ balasya vyāpāramupadarśayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Now, to show the operation of the power, he says —

children.translated_text: Having thus uprooted the adversary, one should strive for the increase of enthusiasm,
through the powers of <s>chanda</s> (desire), <s>māna</s> (pride), <s>rati</s> (delight), and <s>mukti</s> (letting go). // Bca_7.32 //

body.text: evamuktaprabandhenetyādi / vipakṣamālasyādi / unmūlya pratipakṣabhāvanā vidhinā apasārya / vīryapravardhanāya yatnaṃ kuryāt / kenopāyenetyādi(ha?)- mānaścittasyonnatiḥ / ayaṃ sthāmabalasyopabṛṃhaṇam, sthāmabalameva vā / teṣāṃ balaiḥ sāmarthyaiḥ / sāmarthyaparyāyo 'tra balaśabdaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Thus in the manner stated' and so forth. 'The adversary' — laziness and such. 'Uprooting' — removing by the method of cultivating the antidote. One should make effort for the increase of <s>vīrya</s> (diligence). By what means? — and so forth: '<s>māna</s>' is the uplift of the mind. This is the nourishment of the power of <s>sthāma</s> (steadfastness), or it is the power of <s>sthāma</s> itself. 'Through their powers' — through their capacities. The word 'power' (<s>bala</s>) here is a synonym for capacity. //

body.text: tatra tāvacchandotpādanāya prathamamāha-
body.translated_text: Therein, for the generation of <s>chanda</s>, he first says —

children.translated_text: Immeasurable are the faults of self and others that I must destroy,

children.text: ekaikasyāpi doṣasya yatra kalpārṇavaiḥ kṣayaḥ // Bca_7.33 //
children.translated_text: where the elimination of even a single fault [requires] oceans of <s>kalpas</s>. // Bca_7.33 //
Yet in the endeavor to eliminate those faults, not even a trace is seen in me;

children.text: aprameyavyathābhājye noraḥ sphuṭati me katham // Bca_7.34 //
children.translated_text: how does my heart not burst, [I who am] the vessel of immeasurable suffering? // Bca_7.34 //
Many too are the qualities of self and others that I must cultivate,
where the practice of even a single quality may or may not [be accomplished] in oceans of <s>kalpas</s>. // Bca_7.35 //

body.text: guṇaleśe 'pi nābhyāso mama jātaḥ kadācana /
body.translated_text: Yet practice of not even a fraction of a quality has ever arisen in me.

body.text: sarvasattvānāmupakaraṇatayā ātmanaśca samastakleśaprahāṇāya niḥśeṣaguṇotpādanāya ca mayā bodhicittamutpāditam / tacca na śithilavyāpārasādhyamityavagamyāpi yadi anārabdhavīryatayā
body.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings and for the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in myself and for the production of all qualities without exception, I have generated <s>bodhicitta</s>. And understanding that this cannot be accomplished by slack effort, if

body.text: mandasamārambha eva tiṣṭhāmi, tadā durgativinipātamantareṇa nānyā gatirasti mameti vicintya saṃvegamāmukhīkurvan chandamutpādayediti samudāyārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: I remain with merely feeble undertaking through failure to exert <s>vīrya</s>, then there is no other destiny for me than falling into the lower realms — reflecting thus, making spiritual urgency one's guide, one should generate <s>chanda</s>: this is the combined meaning. //

body.text: avayavārthastu ucyate- aprameyāḥ pramātumaśakyāḥ / doṣāḥ kāyavākcittasamāśritāḥ / hantavyāḥ prahantavyāḥ / svaparātmanoḥ svātmanaḥ parātmanaśca / ekaikasyāpīti / āstāṃ tāvadvahūnām / yatra yeṣu / mandavīryeṇa kalpārṇavaiḥ anekaiḥ kalpaśatasahasraiḥ kṣayaḥ prahāṇaṃ kriyate / tatra teṣu doṣakṣayārambhe doṣaprahāṇotsāhe / leśo 'pi svalpamātramapi mama nekṣyate na dṛśyate / ataḥ aprameyavyathābhājye aparimitaduḥkhabhājanasya mama noraḥ sphuṭati hṛdayaṃ vidīryate / kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa / guṇā mayetyādi subodham / iti vicintya saṃvegamupadarśayati-
body.translated_text: The meaning of the individual parts is stated: 'immeasurable' — impossible to measure. 'Faults' — those pertaining to body, speech, and mind. 'Must be destroyed' — must be abandoned. 'Of self and others' — of one's own self and of others. 'Even a single one' — let alone many. 'Where' — in which [faults]. 'Oceans of <s>kalpas</s>' — by one of feeble diligence, through many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, the elimination — the abandonment — is accomplished. 'In the endeavor to eliminate those faults' — in the effort to abandon those faults. 'Not even a trace' — not even the slightest amount — 'is seen in me' — is not perceived. 'Therefore' — 'the vessel of immeasurable suffering' — for me, the container of limitless suffering — 'my heart bursts' — my heart is rent asunder. 'How' — by what means. 'Qualities that I must [cultivate]' and so forth is easy to understand. Thus, showing the spiritual urgency produced by this reflection —

body.text: vṛthā nītaṃ mayā janma kathaṃcillabdhamadbhutam // Bca_7.36 //
body.translated_text: I have led in vain this birth, which was somehow wondrously obtained. // Bca_7.36 //

body.text: vṛthā viphalameva mayā janma akṣaṇavinirmuktaṃ nītaṃ preritam / vṛthīkṛtamiti yāvat / kathaṃcillabdhaṃ mahārṇavayugacchidrakūrmagrīvārpaṇavat sucireṇa prāptam / ata eva āścaryasthānatvādadbhutam //
body.translated_text: 'In vain' — fruitlessly — by me, this birth, free from the inopportune states, has been 'led' — propelled. That is to say, it has been rendered futile. 'Somehow obtained' — acquired after a very long time, like the placing of a turtle's neck through the hole [in a yoke floating on] the great ocean. For that very reason, 'wondrous' — because it is a cause for amazement. //

body.text: ito 'pi viphalamityāha-
body.translated_text: For this further reason it has been fruitless — he says —

children.translated_text: I have not attained the happiness of the great festival of worshipping the Blessed Ones;

children.text: na kṛtā śāsane kārā daridrāśā na pūritā // Bca_7.37 //
children.translated_text: I have not rendered service to the Teaching; the hopes of the destitute I have not fulfilled. // Bca_7.37 //

children.text: bhītebhyo nābhayaṃ dattamārtā na sukhinaḥ kṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: I have not given fearlessness to the frightened, nor have I made the afflicted happy;
I have merely become a dart in my mother's womb, for [her] suffering alone. // Bca_7.38 //

body.text: tathāgatānāṃ satkriyābhirmahotsavamatiśayavadabhinandanam / tena sukhaṃ saumanasyaṃ na prāptaṃ nādhigataṃ mayā / nāpi śāsane pratimāstūpasaddharmādisatkāraiḥ vihārārāmaśayanādivastupradānaiśca kārā pūjā kṛtā / nāpi daridrāṇāṃ dhanahīnānāmāśā abhilāṣaḥ sarvopakaraṇasaṃpattisaṃpādanena pūritā / nāpi bhītebhyaḥ sapatnādibhayasamākulitebhyo mā bhaiṣīrityabhayaṃ dattam / nāpi kāyamanoduḥkhairārtāḥ pīḍitāḥ tadapanīya sukhinaḥ kṛtāḥ / iti sarvaiḥ satpuruṣadharmairvirahitatvādāha / duḥkhāyetyādi subodham //
body.translated_text: The great festival of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — the supreme celebration through acts of veneration. The happiness from that — the gladness — has not been attained, not realized by me. Nor has service — worship — to the Teaching been rendered through veneration of images, <s>stūpas</s>, the true <s>Dharma</s>, and such, and through offering material gifts such as monasteries, gardens, bedding, and such. Nor have the hopes — the desires — of the destitute, those lacking wealth, been fulfilled by providing all material necessities. Nor has fearlessness been given to the frightened — those agitated by fear of enemies and such — [saying] 'Do not fear!' Nor have those afflicted — tormented — by physical and mental suffering been made happy by removing that [suffering]. Thus, being devoid of all the qualities of a good person, he says: 'For suffering alone' and so forth is easy to understand. //

body.text: kathaṃ punaretāṃ dharmadaśāṃ prāpto bhavānityāha-
body.translated_text: How then have you arrived at this state of affairs? — he says —

children.translated_text: Through separation from desire for the <s>Dharma</s> in former [lives], now for me

children.text: vipattirīdṛśī jātā ko dharme chandamutsṛjet // Bca_7.39 //
children.translated_text: such a calamity has arisen — who would abandon desire for the <s>Dharma</s>? // Bca_7.39 //

body.text: dharmābhilāṣasyābhāvena prāktanajanmopacitena mama adhunā asmin janmani vipattirīdṛśī jātā / sarvasāmarthyavaikalyasvabhāvā samanantarakathitā samutpannā / evaṃ jñātvā ko dharme chandamutsṛjet parityajet? ko nāma nopādadīta vicakṣaṇa iti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Through the absence of aspiration for the <s>Dharma</s>, accumulated in former births, for me now, in this birth, such a calamity has arisen — of the nature of deficiency in all capacities, as described just now. Knowing this, who would abandon desire for the <s>Dharma</s> — who would give it up? Who indeed would not take it up, if they are discerning? — this is the purport. //

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kuśalārthināṃ chandotpādane yatna ityāśaṅkaya yaccoktaṃ chandaṃ duḥkhabhayāt kuryāt ityādi, tadvayaktīkartuṃ cāha-
body.translated_text: What then is the effort in generating desire for those who seek the wholesome? — anticipating this, and in order to make explicit what was said — 'one should generate desire from fear of suffering' and so forth — he says —

body.text: kuśalānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ chandaṃ mūlaṃ munirjagau /
body.translated_text: The <s>Muni</s> declared that desire is the root of all wholesome [qualities];

body.text: tasyāpi mūlaṃ satataṃ vipākaphalabhāvanā // Bca_7.40 //
body.translated_text: and the root of that [desire] is the constant contemplation of ripening fruits. // Bca_7.40 //

body.text: na kevalaṃ vipattiparihārārtham, śukladharmopacayārthamapi cchandotpādane yatitavyamiti cakārārthaḥ / sarveṣāmiti na keṣāṃcideva / chandaṃ mūlaṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavānuktavān, na tu svayamutprekṣya ucyate ityarthaḥ / tasyāpi cchandasyāpi mūlaṃ satataṃ sarvakālaṃ vipākaphalabhāvanā / śubhāśubhakarmaṇo vipākaphalaṃ paraloke iṣṭāniṣṭaprāptilakṣaṇam, tasya bhāvanā punaḥpunarāmukhīkaraṇam //
body.translated_text: Not merely for the avoidance of calamity, but also for the accumulation of bright <s>dharmas</s> one should strive to generate desire — this is the meaning of the word 'and.' 'Of all' — not of some only. The Blessed One declared that desire is the root — the cause; it is not said by personal conjecture — this is the meaning. And the root of that desire too is the constant — at all times — contemplation of ripening fruits. The ripening fruit of wholesome and unwholesome action is characterized by the attainment of the desired and the undesired in the next world; its contemplation is bringing it to mind again and again. //

body.text: tatra aśubhakarmaṇo vipākaphalamupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Therein, showing the ripening fruit of unwholesome action, he says —

children.translated_text: Sufferings, mental anguish, and manifold fears,
and the frustration of desires — these arise for those who do evil. // Bca_7.41 //

body.text: yāvanti kāyikamānasikāni narakādigatau duḥkhāni vividhāni nānāprakārāṇi jāyante bhavanti sarvāṇi pāpakāriṇāmeva / bhayāni badhabandhanatāḍanādibhyaḥ / paryeṣamāṇasya lābhavighātena abhilāṣavighātāśca //
body.translated_text: All the various physical and mental sufferings that arise in the states of hell and such — all belong to those who do evil. Fears — from execution, imprisonment, beating, and such. And the frustration of desires — through the obstruction of gains for one who seeks. //

body.text: sukṛtakarmaṇo vipākaphalamāha-
body.translated_text: He states the ripening fruit of meritorious action —

children.translated_text: Wherever the heart's desire of the doer of good goes,
there, in that very place, they are honored with the tribute of fruits by that merit. // Bca_7.42 //

body.text: iṣṭāśaṃsanavikalpo manorathaḥ, yasya loke manorājyamiti prasiddhiḥ śubhakṛtāṃ puṇyakāriṇām / yatra yatraiveti vīpsāyāṃ na kvacideva / gacchati prasarati / phalārgheṇeti / abhivāñchitaphalopanāmanameva argha ivārghaḥ pūjā //
body.translated_text: The conceptualization of a wished-for desire is '<s>manoratha</s>' (heart's desire), which is popularly known in the world as 'daydreaming' — [this belongs to] the doers of good, the performers of merit. 'Wherever' — in the sense of distribution, [meaning] everywhere without exception. 'Goes' — extends. 'With the tribute of fruits' — the presentation of the desired fruit is like an offering (<s>argha</s>), hence '<s>argha</s>' — worship. //

body.text: tena punaraśubhasya phalamāha-
body.translated_text: In contrast, he states the fruit of the unwholesome —

children.translated_text: Wherever the desire for happiness of the evil-doer goes,
there, in that very place, they are struck by the weapons of suffering through those sins. // Bca_7.43 //

body.text: sukhecchā sukhābhilāṣaḥ / tatpāpairiti kartari tṛtīyā / duḥkhaśastrairiti karaṇaiḥ / duḥkhānyeva śastrāṇīva tadicchāvicchedahetutvāt //
body.translated_text: 'Desire for happiness' — longing for happiness. 'Through those sins' — the instrumental is in the sense of agent. 'With weapons of suffering' — the instruments; sufferings themselves are like weapons, because they are the cause of cutting off that desire. //

body.text: pṛthagjanāsādhāraṇaśubhakarmavipākaphalamasādhāraṇamāha-
body.translated_text: He states the uncommon ripening fruit of uncommon meritorious action [performed] by ordinary beings —

children.translated_text: Dwelling within the hearts of vast, fragrant, cool lotuses,
their splendor nourished by feeding on the sweet voice of the <s>Jina</s>,
with excellent bodies emerging from lotuses opened by the rays of the <s>Muni</s>,

children.text: sugatasutā bhavanti sugatasya puraḥ kuśalaiḥ // Bca_7.44 //
children.translated_text: through wholesome [deeds], they become children of the <s>Sugata</s> in the presence of the <s>Sugata</s>. // Bca_7.44 //

body.text: pratilabdhamuditādibhūmayo hi bodhisattvā anicchanto mātṛkukṣau notpadyante, kiṃ tarhi sukhāvatyāṃ viśvadalakamalakośeṣu jāyante / teṣāṃ sukhavibhūtimanena kathayati- vipulāni
body.translated_text: For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the grounds beginning with <s>Muditā</s> (Joy) and beyond do not take birth in a mother's womb against their will; rather, they are born in the calyx of universal-petaled lotuses in <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. He describes their blissful splendor: 'vast'

body.text: vistīrṇāni sugandhīni manojñagandhāni śītalāni śītasukhasparśāni tāni ca saroruhāṇi paṅkajāni ceti, teṣāṃ garbhāṇi / saroruhagarbhāṇāṃ vā viśeṣaṇānyetāni / teṣu gatāḥ saṃsthitāḥ prajñopāyamahākaruṇāniryātapuṇyajñānakalalasaṃvalitasaṃbodhicittāḥ sugatasutā bhavanti kuśalairiti saṃbandhaḥ / kathaṃ punaḥ padmagarbheṣu puṣṭiṃ labhanta ityāha- madhuretyādi / madhuraiḥ sarvasvarāṅgopetatayā paramasaumanasyakāribhiḥ saṃbaddhadharmaghoṣāśanairāhāraiḥ kṛtā upacitā dyutayo vapūṃṣi yeṣāṃ te tathā / kathaṃ ca tato niryāntītyata āha- munikaretyādi / munikaraiḥ paripākakālamavagamya tathāgataraśmibhirbodhitāni vikāsitāni ca tānyambujāni ceti / tato vinirgatāni niryātāni santi lakṣaṇavyañjanālaṃkṛtatayā śobhanāni vapūṃṣi yeṣāṃ te tathā / tathābhūtāḥ santaḥ sugatasutā bodhisattvā bhavanti jāyante / sugatasya puraḥ sukhāvatyāmamitābhasya bhagavato 'grataḥ / kuśalairekāntaśuklaiḥ karmabhiḥ / tadanena mātṛkukṣau samutpadyamānānāmetadviśeṣaṇaviparyayeṇa duḥkhaṃ veditavyamityupadarśitaṃ bhavati / tathā hi tatra saṃkaṭe durgandhini jaṭharānalasaṃtapte ca utpannasya mātāpitraśucisaṃbhūtasya mātuḥ pītāśitairvāntakalpaiḥ saṃvardhamānasya garbhamalapaṅkanimagnasya paripākakāle kathaṃcit kaṇṭhagataprāṇasya yantraniṣpīḍitasyeva tato nirgamanamiti prāyeṇa manuṣyabhūtasya vyatimiśrakarmavipākaphalamuktam //
body.translated_text: — extensive; 'fragrant' — of delightful scent; 'cool' — of cool, pleasant touch; and these are lotuses; 'their hearts' — the interior of the lotus hearts. Or these are qualifiers of the lotus hearts themselves. Dwelling in them — established — with the awakening mind conjoined with the embryo of merit and wisdom produced through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and great compassion — they become children of the <s>Sugata</s> through wholesome [deeds]: this is the connection. How then do they receive nourishment within the lotus hearts? — he says: 'sweet' and so forth. Sweet — supremely gladness-producing through being endowed with all vocal parts — by feeding, by nourishment connected with the proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s>, their splendor — their bodies — are nourished: of whom this is so, they are such. And how do they emerge from there? — to this he says: 'by the rays of the <s>Muni</s>' and so forth. By the <s>Muni</s>'s rays — by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s light-rays, knowing the time of maturation, those lotuses are opened — made to blossom. From there, they have emerged — come forth — possessing bodies that are beautiful through being adorned with the [thirty-two] marks and [eighty] minor signs: of whom this is so, they are such. Being thus, they become — they are born as — children of the <s>Sugata</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. In the presence of the <s>Sugata</s> — before the Blessed <s>Amitābha</s> in <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. Through wholesome — exclusively bright — <s>karmas</s>. By this, the suffering of those who take birth in a mother's womb is shown by way of the reversal of these qualifiers. For there, in the cramped, foul-smelling [womb], heated by the fire of the belly, for one born there, produced from the impurities of mother and father, nourished by what the mother has eaten and drunk — which is like vomit — submerged in the mire of the womb's filth, when the time of maturation comes, with life-breath somehow reaching the throat, being squeezed out as if by a machine — thus the emergence. Hence, for the most part, the mixed karmic ripening fruit of a human birth has been stated. //

body.text: ekāntakṛṣṇasya tu vipākaphalamāha-
body.translated_text: But the ripening fruit of exclusively dark [karma], he states —

children.translated_text: Stripped of all skin by the servants of <s>Yama</s>, crying out in anguish,
the body drenched with molten copper melted by the heat of fire,
the flesh torn into pieces by hundreds of blows from blazing swords and spears —
through unwholesome [deeds], one falls upon the ground of burning iron, again and again. // Bca_7.45 //

body.text: yamapuruṣaiḥ kāladūtairapanītā viśleṣitā jvalitamudgarādiprahāraiḥ sakalā samastā chaviścarma prabhāvo vā yasya sa tathā / atiśayenārtaḥ san patati sutaptalohadharaṇīṣu / punarapi kiṃbhūtaḥ? tīvrānalatāpena dravībhūtaṃ yattāmraṃ tena niṣiktā snāpitā tanuḥ kāyo yasya / ato 'pyapanītasakalacchaviḥ / jvalantaḥ asayaḥ śaktayaśca śastraviśeṣāḥ, teṣāṃ ghātaśatairanekaiḥ prahāraiḥ śātitāni viccheditāni māṃsadalāni śakalāni yasya sa tathābhūtaḥ san patati / suṣṭhu taptāsu lohamayabhūmiṣu / aśubhairakuśalaiḥ karmabhiḥ / bahuśa iti bahūn vārān / dīrghakālena tatphalasya parikṣayāt //
body.translated_text: By the servants of <s>Yama</s> — the messengers of death — 'stripped' means separated; by strikes of blazing hammers and such, all — the entire — skin, or radiance, of whom has been [removed] — he is such. Being extremely afflicted, he falls upon the ground of burning iron. Furthermore, of what kind? His body — drenched, bathed with copper that has become liquid through the heat of intense fire. Hence [he is] 'stripped of all skin.' Blazing swords and spears — particular kinds of weapons; by hundreds of their blows — by numerous strikes — the flesh torn into pieces, into fragments: being in such a state, he falls. Upon the ground made of well-heated iron. Through unwholesome — through non-meritorious — <s>karmas</s>. 'Again and again' — many times; because of the long time [required for] the exhaustion of that fruit. //

body.text: tadevaṃ śubhāśubhakarmaṇorvipākaphalaṃ pratipādya cchandabalamupasaṃharannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the ripening fruits of wholesome and unwholesome action, concluding the power of <s>chanda</s>, he says —

body.text: tasmātkāryaḥ śubhacchando bhāvayitvaivamādarāt /
body.translated_text: Therefore, desire for the good should be cultivated, having thus reflected with care.

body.text: yata evaṃ śubhāśubhakarmaṇormadhurakaṭukaphalavipākaḥ, tasmādevaṃ paribhāvya śubhacchanda eva ādareṇāśubhakarma vihāya kāryaḥ / sāṃprataṃ sthāmabalaṃ pratipādayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Since thus the ripening of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> yields sweet and bitter fruits respectively, therefore, having reflected thus, one should earnestly cultivate desire for the wholesome alone, abandoning unwholesome action. Now, to teach the strength of firmness, he says —

body.text: vajradhvajasthavidhinā mānaṃ tvārabhya bhāvayet // Bca_7.46 //
body.translated_text: One should cultivate self-confidence, undertaking [action] according to the method stated in the <s>Vajradhvajasūtra</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 7.46 //

body.text: vajradhvajasūtrapratipāditavidhānena mānaṃ punaḥ sādhyaṃ karmārabhya bhāvayet / athavā / ārabhya bhāvayediti gāḍhasamārambheṇa bhāvayet, cetasi sthiraṃ kuryāt, na śithilopakrameṇetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: According to the method taught in the <s>Vajradhvajasūtra</s>, one should cultivate self-confidence, undertaking the task to be accomplished. Or alternatively, 'undertaking, one should cultivate' means: one should cultivate with firm resolve, should make it steady in the mind — the meaning is: not with a slack approach.

body.text: ārambhameva śikṣayitumāha-
body.translated_text: To teach the undertaking itself, he says —

body.text: pūrvaṃ nirūpya sāmagrīmārabhennārabheta vā /
body.translated_text: Having first examined the prerequisites, one should undertake [the task] or not undertake it.

body.text: pūrvaṃ prathamata eva abhimatakāryaniṣpādanāya sāmagrīṃ kāraṇasākalyaṃ nirūpya, tasyā balābalaṃ vicārya, ārabheta sati bale, nārabheta vā asati bale / kimevaṃvicāreṇa prayojanamiti cedāha-
body.translated_text: 'First' — at the very beginning — having examined the prerequisites, the totality of conditions, for accomplishing the intended task, having considered their strength or weakness, one should undertake it if there is strength, or not undertake it if there is no strength. If asked, 'What is the purpose of such examination?' he says —

body.text: anārambho varaṃ nāma na tvārabhya nivartanam // Bca_7.47 //
body.translated_text: Non-undertaking is better indeed than undertaking and then turning back. // <s>Bca</s> 7.47 //

body.text: anārambho varaṃ nāma prathamata eva, na tvārabhya nivartanamaśaktatve sati //
body.translated_text: Non-undertaking from the very beginning is better indeed than turning back from what has been undertaken when one proves incapable.

body.text: nanu kimatra dūṣaṇaṃ yenaiva neṣyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: But what fault is there in this, such that it is not desired? He says —

children.translated_text: In other lives too, that habit [of giving up] grows, and suffering from evil [increases];

children.text: anyacca kāryakālaṃ ca hīnaṃ tacca na sādhitam // Bca_7.48 //
children.translated_text: and another [task's] time is wasted, and that [original task] is not accomplished either. // <s>Bca</s> 7.48 //

body.text: tathā kriyamāṇaḥ anyasminnapi janmani so 'bhyāsa ityārabhya nivartanaṃ nāma / pratijñātamakurvataśca pāpaṃ tato duḥkhaṃ vardhate / anyacca hīnaṃ naṣṭaṃ yatparityajya tadārabdham, kāryakālaṃ ca hīnam / ārabdhaparityaktakāryasya kālo 'sya kāryasyeti / tasmin kāle yadanyat kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ tadityarthaḥ / tacca yadārabhya parityaktam, tadapi na sādhitaṃ na niṣpāditam / iti pañcaprakāramatra dūṣaṇam / tena neṣyata ityabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: When done thus, in another life too, 'that habit' — namely, undertaking and then turning back. And the evil of not fulfilling one's commitment — from that, suffering increases. 'Another' — what was abandoned in order to undertake that [task] — is 'wasted,' lost. 'And the time [for the task] is wasted' — the time spent on the undertaken-then-abandoned task — the time of this task — in that time, whatever other work should have been done, that [is lost] — this is the meaning. 'And that' — what was undertaken and then abandoned — 'is not accomplished either,' not completed. Thus there are five kinds of fault here. The intention is: therefore it is not desired.

body.text: atha kimayaṃ mānaḥ sarvatra na kartavyaḥ? netyāha-
body.translated_text: Now, is this self-confidence not to be applied in all [cases]? No, he says —

body.text: triṣu māno vidhātavyaḥ karmopakleśaśaktiṣu /
body.translated_text: Self-confidence should be applied in three [areas]: in action, against afflictions, and in ability.

body.text: keṣu triṣu? tadāha- karmasu upakleśeṣu śaktau ca / tatra upakleśāḥ kṣudravastukasaṃjñitāḥ krodhopanāhamrakṣapradāśādayaḥ sapta / pañcāśat kleśā eva vā rāgādaya upakleśā ucyante / tatra karmamānaṃ vyākhyātumāha-
body.translated_text: In which three? He states them: in actions, against <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions), and in ability. There, the <s>upakleśas</s> are the seven designated as minor afflictions — anger, resentment, concealment, spite, and so forth. Or alternatively, the fifty afflictions themselves — desire and such — are called <s>upakleśas</s>. There, to explain self-confidence in action, he says —

body.text: mayaivaikena kartavyamityeṣā karmamānitā // Bca_7.49 //
body.translated_text: 'I alone must do this' — this is self-confidence in action. // <s>Bca</s> 7.49 //

body.text: yatkiṃcidanavadyaṃ karma āpatitaṃ bhavati sattvānām, tat sarvaṃ mayaivaikena kartavyam / nānyasyāvakāśo dātavya ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Whatever blameless action arises [to be done] for beings, all that should be done by me alone. The meaning is: no opportunity should be given to another.

body.text: etadeva darśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing this very point, he says —

children.translated_text: This world, subject to <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), is incapable of accomplishing its own welfare;

children.text: tasmānmayaiṣāṃ kartavyaṃ nāśakto 'haṃ yathā janaḥ // Bca_7.50 //
children.translated_text: therefore I must act for them — I am not incapable like [ordinary] people. // <s>Bca</s> 7.50 //

body.text: kleśaiḥ parāyattīkṛtaḥ sarvo 'yaṃ janakāyaḥ kvacidapi svārthasādhane samartho na bhavati, iti eṣāṃ sarvasukhotpādanāya mayā bodhicittamutpāditam / yata evam, tasmānnāśakto 'hamīdṛśaṃ bhāramudboḍhuṃ yathā ayaṃ janaḥ / ato mayaivaiṣāṃ sarvaṃ kartavyam //
body.translated_text: This entire assembly of beings, made dependent by afflictions, is nowhere capable of accomplishing its own welfare. Thus I have generated <s>bodhicitta</s> for the production of all happiness for them. Since this is so, therefore I am not incapable of bearing such a burden like these people. Hence I alone must do everything for them.

body.text: dīne 'pi karmaṇi vaimukhyaṃ notpādayitavyamityāha-
body.translated_text: One should not develop aversion even toward lowly tasks — he says —

body.text: nīcaṃ karma karotyanyaḥ kathaṃ mayyapi tiṣṭhati /
body.translated_text: If another does menial work, how can it stand while I am here?

body.text: nīcamatigarhitaṃ loke bhārodvahanādikam / mayyapi sarvasattvānāṃ dāsabhūte 'pi tiṣṭati vidyamāne 'pi / matkaraṇīyaṃ kathamanyaḥ karoti? mayaiva kartumucitamiti bhāvaḥ / athāpratirūpam, mamaiva tat karmeti cittasyonnatiṃ nivārayitumāha-
body.translated_text: 'Menial' — greatly despised in the world, such as carrying burdens and so forth. 'While I am here' — even though I exist, being a servant of all beings. 'How does another do what should be done by me?' The meaning is: it is fitting that I alone should do it. But if it seems unsuitable — to restrain the mind's haughtiness [thinking] 'that is indeed my task,' he says —

body.text: mānāccenna karomyetanmāno naśyatu me varam // Bca_7.51 //
body.translated_text: If out of pride I do not do this, let my pride rather be destroyed. // <s>Bca</s> 7.51 //

body.text: ko 'muṣyaputraḥ, idaṃ ca karma atinihīnam, tadayuktaṃ mama kartumiti mānādyadi na karomi, tadā māno naśyatu me varam / kimanena mahārthabhraṃśakāriṇā mama, na tu nīcakarmapravṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Who is this so-and-so's son, and this task is extremely base — it is not fitting for me to do it' — if out of such pride I do not do it, then let my pride be destroyed, that is better. For what use is this [pride] to me, which causes the loss of great purpose? Rather than engaging in base work, [let pride perish].

body.text: iti karmasu mānamabhidhāya upakleśeṣu mānamupadarśayitumāha-
body.translated_text: Having stated self-confidence in action, to show self-confidence against <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions), he says —

children.translated_text: Having come upon a dead serpent, even a crow acts like a <s>Garuḍa</s>;

children.text: āpadābādhate 'lpāpi mano me yadi durbalam // Bca_7.52 //
children.translated_text: if my mind is weak, even a slight misfortune causes harm. // <s>Bca</s> 7.52 //

body.text: yadi upakleśeṣu nihatamānatayā durbalavṛtti mama cittaṃ syāt, tadā āpadāpattiḥ ābādhate ākrāmati yathā sāpattikaṃ syādityarthaḥ / alpāpi mṛdupracāropakleśajanitāpi / kathamivetyāha- mṛtamapagataprāṇaṃ duṇḍubhaṃ prāpya yathā kāko 'pi garuḍavadācarati //
body.translated_text: If, through having one's self-confidence destroyed by the secondary afflictions, my mind were of weak conduct, then even a slight misfortune — even one generated by secondary afflictions of mild operation — would cause harm, would overwhelm — the meaning is: there would be transgression. How so? He says: just as, having come upon a dead, lifeless serpent, even a crow acts like a <s>Garuḍa</s>.

body.text: kutaḥ punarevamityāha-
body.translated_text: Why is this so? He says —

children.translated_text: For one rendered inert by despondency, misfortunes are easy [to inflict], are they not?
But one who is aroused and striving is unconquerable even by great [adversities]. // <s>Bca</s> 7.53 //

body.text: cittonnativirahite viṣaṇṇatayā mandakāyacittapravṛttau ālasyopahate muṣitasmṛtau āpadaḥ sukarāḥ sulabhāḥ / utpadyanta eva svalpāpadāpi gamyatvāt / vyutthitaḥ samunnatacittatayā punarutsāhasaṃpannaḥ ceṣṭamānaḥ smṛtisaṃprajanyābhyāmupakleśānāmanavakāśaṃ dadānaḥ mahatāmapi durjayaḥ ajayyaḥ syāt //
body.translated_text: For one deprived of mental uplift, whose bodily and mental activity is sluggish due to dejection, who is overcome by laziness and whose mindfulness is impaired — misfortunes are easy, readily arise; even slight misfortunes [overwhelm one] because one is vulnerable. But one who is aroused — possessing energy through the elevation of mind — who is striving, who through mindfulness and introspective awareness gives no opportunity to the secondary afflictions — such a one would be unconquerable, invincible, even by great [adversities].

children.translated_text: Therefore, with a firm mind I shall make misfortune itself a misfortune;
it would be laughable for me, who aspires to conquer the triple world, to be defeated. // <s>Bca</s> 7.54 //

body.text: sthāmabalāvalambanaṃ nigamayan darśayati- yata evaṃ tasmāt dṛḍhena cittena mānasaṃnāhaḥ / āpada eva āpadamanarthaṃ karomi sarvathā tadanupraveśaṃ nivārayannunmūlitasaṃtānaṃ karomi / anyathā trijagadvijayārambho mama hāsyamupahasanīyam, āpadā āpadāyattatayā varākikayā jitasya gamiṣyati //
body.translated_text: Concluding [the discussion of] the strength of firmness, he shows: since this is so, therefore with a firm mind — donning the armor of self-confidence — I shall make misfortune itself a misfortune, an adversity — preventing its entry in every way, I shall uproot its continuity. Otherwise, my undertaking to conquer the three worlds would become laughable, ridiculous — for one defeated, one come under the power of the wretched misfortune.

body.text: kīdṛśametadityāha-
body.translated_text: What is this like? He says —

children.text: mayā hi sarvaṃ jetavyamahaṃ jeyo na kenacit /
children.translated_text: Everything must be conquered by me; I must not be conquered by anyone.

children.text: mayaiṣa māno voḍhavyo jinasiṃhasuto hyaham // Bca_7.55 //
children.translated_text: This self-confidence must be borne by me, for I am a son of the <s>Jina</s>-lions. // <s>Bca</s> 7.55 //

body.text: kutaḥ? yasmājjinā eva bhagavantaḥ siṃhāḥ sarvamāramṛgairanabhigamyatvāt / teṣāṃ sutaḥ ahamapi kathamanyaiḥ parājito nāma nāmadheyaṃ lapsye iti manasi nidhāya mayaiṣa māno boḍhavyaḥ / yathā hi siṃhakiśoraḥ pratilabdhavaiśāradyaḥ sarvānyamṛgairanabhibhūta eva vane vicarati, tathā mayā dṛḍhena bhavitavyamityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Why? Because the <s>Jinas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are lions — unapproachable by all the beasts of <s>Māra</s>. Keeping in mind 'I too am a son of those; how then shall I acquire the designation of being defeated by others?' — this self-confidence must be borne by me. For just as a young lion, having attained confidence, roams in the forest unconquered by all other animals, so must I be firm — this is the meaning.

body.text: syādetat- yadi yavam, tadā ye 'pi sapatnādivijayāya mānamudvahanti, te 'pi māninaḥ praśasyāḥ kathaṃ na bhaveyuḥ? ityatrāha-
body.translated_text: One might say: if this is so, then those who bear pride for the sake of conquering rivals and such — how would they too not be praiseworthy as proud ones? To this he says —

children.text: ye sattvā mānavijitā varakāste na māninaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those beings who are conquered by [worldly] pride are wretched; they are not the [truly] proud.

children.text: mānī śatruvaśaṃ naiti mānaśatruvaśāśca te // Bca_7.56 //
children.translated_text: The [truly] proud one does not come under the power of the enemy; but they are under the power of the enemy of pride. // <s>Bca</s> 7.56 //

body.text: mānavijitāḥ mānena abhibhūtāḥ varākāstapasvinaḥ te mānino bhavantyeva / kutaḥ? mānī śatruvaśaṃ naiti na gacchati / nāsau vairijanānuvṛttiṃ karotītyarthaḥ / ye bhavatābhimatā māninaḥ, te mānaśatruvaśāḥ tadāyattapravṛttayaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Conquered by pride' — overcome by [worldly] pride — they are indeed wretched, pitiable. How so? The [truly] proud one does not come under the power of the enemy — the meaning is: he does not follow the ways of adversaries. Those whom you consider proud — they are under the power of the enemy of pride, their activity is governed by that.

body.text: etadeva ślokadvayena samarthayitumāha-
body.translated_text: To establish this very point with two verses, he says —

children.translated_text: Led by [worldly] pride to the lower realms, even in human life they are bereft of joy,

children.text: parapiṇḍāśino dāsā mūrkhā durdarśanāḥ kṛśā // Bca_7.57 //
children.translated_text: eating the food of others, slaves, fools, ugly, and emaciated. // <s>Bca</s> 7.57 //
Despised by all, stiffened by pride, wretched —

children.text: te 'pi cenmānināṃ madhye dīnāstu vada kīdṛśāḥ // Bca_7.58 //
children.translated_text: if even they are counted among the proud, then say, what do the wretched look like? // <s>Bca</s> 7.58 //

body.text: saptavidhamāneṣu anyatamena mānena durgatiṃ nītā narakādiṣu pātitāḥ / atha kathaṃcinmanuṣyapratilambho bhavati teṣām, tadā tatrāpi tannindāphalena hatotsavā nirānandā bhavanti / hīnadīnamanasa ityarthaḥ / parapiṇḍāśinaḥ āhāravaikalyāt paradattabhikṣāhārabhujaḥ / dāsāḥ paratantravṛttayo bhṛtyāḥ / mūrkhāḥ sarvavikekaśūnyāḥ / durdarśanāḥ virūpātmabhāvā aprītijanakāśca / kṛśāḥ durbalaśarīrāḥ sāmarthyarahitāśca / sarvataḥ sarvebhyo 'kṛtāparādhā api kāyavacaḥparibhavalābhino bhavanti / ke punarevam? mānastabdhāstapasvinaḥ mānena stabdhāḥ anamrāḥ / tapasvino varākāḥ / te 'pi cet, evaṃbhūtā api yadi mānināṃ madhye gaṇyante, tarhi dīnāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ kṛpāpātramityarthaḥ / punaranye dīnāḥ kīdṛśā bhavantīti vada brūhi [iti] codakamāmantrayate //
body.translated_text: Led by one or another of the seven kinds of pride to the lower realms — cast into the hells and such. And if somehow they obtain a human birth, then even there, as a fruit of that censure, they are bereft of joy, devoid of happiness — the meaning is: of abject and lowly mind. 'Eating the food of others' — due to lack of food, eating alms-food given by others. 'Slaves' — servants dependent on others. 'Fools' — devoid of all discrimination. 'Ugly' — with disfigured bodies and producing displeasure in others. 'Emaciated' — with weak bodies and devoid of capacity. They receive contempt of body and speech from all, even having committed no offense. Who indeed are such? 'Stiffened by pride, wretched' — stiffened by pride, meaning unbending. Wretched, pitiable. If even they — even being of such a nature — are counted among the proud, then the wretched, the miserable — objects of pity, this is the meaning — what do other wretched ones look like? 'Say,' 'tell me' — he addresses the questioner.

body.text: yadi evaṃvidhā mānino nocyante, kīdṛśāstarhi te bhavantītyāha-
body.translated_text: If such persons are not called proud, then what kind [of persons] are [the truly proud]? He says —

children.text: te mānino vijayinaśca ta eva śūrā
children.translated_text: They are the [truly] proud, they the victorious, they the heroes,
who bear self-confidence for the conquest of the enemy of [worldly] pride;
who, having slain that swelling enemy of pride,
freely bestow the fruit of victory upon the world. // <s>Bca</s> 7.59 //

body.text: ta eva mānina ucyante ye bodhisattvāḥ taṃ sphurantamapi prabhavantamapi mānavairiṇaṃ nihatya vidhūya / kāmaṃ yatheṣṭam / uddāmeti yāvat / jane loke sadevakādike jayaphalaṃ prakāśayanti buddhatvāvasthāyām / etādṛśaṃ tanmānaśatruvijayaphalaṃ yādṛśamasmāsu dṛśyate ityabhiprāyaḥ / ta eva vijayinaśca labdhavijayāḥ / ta eva śūrāstejasvina iti padadvayaṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojyam //
body.translated_text: They alone are called the proud — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who, having slain, having dispelled, that swelling, that powerful enemy of pride — freely, as they wish — without restraint, as it were — bestow the fruit of victory upon the world including gods and others, in the state of <s>Buddhahood</s>. 'Such is the fruit of conquering the enemy of pride, as is seen in us' — this is the intention. They alone are the victorious — those who have won victory. They alone are the heroes, the valiant — the two words should be construed as contextually appropriate.

body.text: upakleśeṣu mānaṃ pratipādya śaktau mānamāha-
body.translated_text: Having taught self-confidence against secondary afflictions, he states self-confidence in ability —

body.text: saṃkleśapakṣamadhyastho bhavedduptaḥ sahasraśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Standing in the midst of the host of afflictions, one should be bold a thousandfold;

body.text: saṃkleśānāṃ pakṣo vargaḥ, tasya madhye tiṣṭhan sahasraguṇena dṛptataro bhavet, atiśayavacchauryabalamavalambeta / kiṃbhūtaḥ sannityāha-
body.translated_text: 'The host of afflictions' — their company; standing in their midst, one should be a thousand times bolder, should rely on supreme heroic strength. Of what kind? He says —

body.text: duryodhanaḥ kleśagaṇaiḥ siṃho mṛgagaṇairiva // Bca_7.60 //
body.translated_text: unconquerable by the hosts of afflictions, like a lion among herds of deer. // <s>Bca</s> 7.60 //

body.text: duḥkhena yodhyata iti duryodhanaḥ / kathaṃcidapi na parājīyate ityarthaḥ / kathamiva? yathā hi siṃho mṛgarājaḥ mṛgakulamadhye mahātejobalasamanvāgato viharan vane sarvamṛgānabhibhavati, na ca tairabhibhūyata iti, evaṃ bodhisattvo duryodhano bhavet //
body.translated_text: '<s>Duryodhana</s>' — one who is fought with difficulty, meaning: one who is not defeated in any way. How so? Just as a lion, the king of beasts, endowed with great splendor and strength, roaming in the midst of a herd of deer in the forest, overpowers all animals and is not overpowered by them — so should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> be unconquerable.

body.text: idamaparamapi nimittamudgahītavyamityāha-
body.translated_text: Yet another reason should be grasped — he says —

children.text: mahatsvapi hi kṛcchreṣu na rasaṃ cakṣurīkṣate /
children.translated_text: Even in great afflictions, the eye does not perceive taste;

children.text: evaṃ kṛcchramapi prāpya na kleśavaśago bhavet // Bca_7.61 //
children.translated_text: likewise, even when encountering difficulty, one should not come under the power of afflictions. // <s>Bca</s> 7.61 //

body.text: atiprakarṣavatsu api kṛcchreṣu duḥkheṣu satsu rasaṃ madhurādikaṃ jihvendriyagrāhyaṃ na cakṣurīkṣate na pratipadyate / na viṣayīkarotītyarthaḥ / tasyāviṣayatvāt / nāviṣaye pravartata iti bhāvaḥ / evamuktarasacakṣurnyāyena kaṣṭamapi prāpya na kleśavaśaṃ gacchet //
body.translated_text: Even when extremely intense afflictions — sufferings — are present, the eye does not perceive taste — sweet and such, which are objects of the tongue faculty — does not apprehend it, does not make it an object. The meaning is: because it is not its domain. The point is: it does not engage with what is not its object.
