body.text: yata eva utpādyameva tadduḥkhaṃ kṛpālunā svaparātmanoḥ ata eva supuṣpacandreṇa bodhisattvena / nṛpādāpadaṃ nṛpasya vā rājña āpadam / jānatāpi budhyamānenāpi / ātmaduḥkhaṃ na nihataṃ na nivartitam / upekṣitamiti yāvat / tathā rājño 'pi paralokaduḥkham / kimiti? bahūnāṃ duḥkhināṃ vyayāt / duḥkhasyeti prakṛtaṃ ṣaṣṭhayantatayā saṃbadhyate / yaduktaṃ supuṣpacandrasyetivṛttake [samādhi. 35]- tathā hi- atīte 'dhvani ratnapadmacandraviśuddhābhyudgatarājo nāma tathāgato 'bhūt / sa bhagavān buddhakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā ciratarakālamavasthāya parinirvṛtaḥ / tasmiṃśca parinirvṛte śāsanāntardhānasamaye rājā śūradatto nāma babhūva / tasya ratnāvatī nāma rājadhānī / tasmin kāle dṛṣṭivipannāḥ sattvāḥ / teṣāmanukampārthaṃ bahavo bodhisattvā utpannāḥ pravrajitāḥ / te ca tato rāṣṭrajanapadebhyo nirvāsitāḥ samantabhadraṃ nāma araṇyavanakhaṇḍamupasṛtya viharanti sma sārdhaṃ supuṣpacandreṇa dharmabhāṇakena / atha khalu supuṣpacandrasya bodhisattvasya sattvān karuṇāyamānasya rahogatasya cetasi vitarka udapādi- yannvahaṃ janapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīrgatvā sattvān kumārgaprapannān kalyāṇe vartmani pratiṣṭhāpayāmi / sa tamarthaṃ sabrahmacāribhyo nivedayāmāsa / tairnivāryamāṇo 'pi svayaṃ ca svāpadaṃ pratipadyamānaḥ tasya rājño 'pi tato vanakhaṇḍānnirjagāma /
body.translated_text: Precisely because that suffering should be generated by the compassionate one for the sake of both self and other — therefore by <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. 'The danger from the king' — or the calamity of the king. 'Even knowing' — even understanding. 'His own suffering was not destroyed' — was not averted — that is, it was disregarded. And also the suffering of the king in the next world. For what reason? 'For the sake of the many who suffered' — 'of suffering' is to be connected as an implied genitive of the word already at hand. As is stated in the <s>Supuṣpacandravṛttaka</s> [<s>Samādhirāja</s> 35]: Thus, in the past, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnapadmacandr-aviśuddhābhyudgatarāja</s>. That Blessed One, having performed the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, after abiding for a very long time, passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. After his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, at the time of the disappearance of his teaching, there was a king named <s>Śūradatta</s>. His capital was called <s>Ratnāvatī</s>. At that time, beings were of perverted views. For their sake, out of compassion, many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> arose and went forth [into renunciation]. They, having been expelled from that kingdom and its provinces, repaired to a forest grove called <s>Samantabhadra</s> and dwelt there together with the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>. Then a thought arose in the mind of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Supuṣpacandra</s>, who was feeling compassion for beings while in solitude: 'What if I were to go to the provinces, kingdoms, and capitals and establish beings who have entered the wrong path upon the good path?' He communicated this intention to his fellow practitioners. Though restrained by them, and himself recognizing the danger to himself, he nonetheless departed from that forest grove [to go before] that king.

body.text: sa krameṇa dharmaṃ deśayan tasya rājño rājadhānīmanuprāpto bahūn sattvān rājaputrāmātyapurohitaprabhṛtīn prakāraṃ vinīya satpathe vyavasthāpayan tena rājñā dṛṣṭaḥ / sahadarśanena prakuptaḥ sarva ca janakāyaṃ tadāvarjitaṃ pratipadya īrṣyādūṣitahṛdayaḥ / tadvadhārthaṃ svaputrānājñāpayāmāsa / tāṃśca tadvadhavimukhān pratipadya nandikaṃ vadhyaghātakamājñāpayāmāsa / tena tadājñāmanuvartamānena karacaraṇādicchedakrameṇa akṣīṇi ca saṃdaṃśikenoddhṛtya jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ / atha tasya bhikṣo rājamārgagatasya jīvitād vyaparopitasya śarīre anekānyadbhutāni babhūvuḥ / tāni pratipadya sa rājā niścitaṃ bodhisattva evāyaṃ bhikṣuriti paritāpagato bahutaraṃ paridevate sma / iti supuṣpacandrasyetivṛttakaṃ saṃkṣipya kathitam / vistareṇa punaḥ samādhirājasūtre [35] nirdiṣṭamiti tatraiva avadhāryam //
body.translated_text: Gradually teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, he arrived at that king's capital, and having skillfully disciplined many beings — princes, ministers, royal priests, and others — establishing them on the good path, he was seen by that king. Upon seeing him, the king became enraged, and perceiving that the entire populace had been won over by him, his heart was corrupted by jealousy. He commanded his own sons to kill him. Finding them averse to that killing, he then commanded <s>Nandika</s>, the executioner. He, carrying out that command, through the progressive cutting off of hands, feet, and such, and having gouged out the eyes with pincers, deprived him of life. Then, for that <s>bhikṣu</s> who had been deprived of life on the royal highway, many wondrous [signs] appeared upon his body. Perceiving these, that king [thought] 'This <s>bhikṣu</s> was certainly a <s>Bodhisattva</s>' — and overcome with remorse, lamented greatly. Thus the story of <s>Supuṣpacandra</s> has been told in brief. It is taught in full detail in the <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> [chapter 35], and should be examined there. //

body.text: na cāpi kṛpāvatāṃ paraduḥkhaduḥkhināṃ mahadapi duḥkhaṃ bādhakamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And demonstrating that for the compassionate, even great suffering from another's pain is not an affliction, he says —

children.translated_text: Those whose mental continua are thus cultivated, who hold another's suffering as dear as their own,
plunge into <s>Avīci</s> as swans [plunge] into a lotus pond. // Bca_8.107 //

body.text: evaṃ parātmasamatayā bhāvitasaṃtānāḥ anābhogapravṛttacittasaṃtatayaḥ / paraduḥkhena samaṃ tulyaṃ priyaṃ sukhaheturyeṣāṃ te tathā / ātmasukhamapi paraduḥkhena duḥkhameva yeṣāmityarthaḥ / te avīcimavagāhante paravyasanasamuddharaṇāya tadduḥkhaṃ sukhameva manyamānāḥ / idamevāha- haṃsāḥ padmavanaṃ yathā / āvīcikamapi duḥkhaṃ sukhameva parārthe yeṣāṃ te / kena duḥkhahetunā anyena duḥkhino bhaviṣyanti?
body.translated_text: 'Whose continua are thus cultivated' — through the equality of self and other — whose mental continua operate without deliberate effort. 'To whom another's suffering is equally dear' — equally a cause of happiness — they are such. The meaning is: those for whom even their own happiness is suffering when others suffer. They plunge into <s>Avīci</s> for the purpose of rescuing others from misfortune, regarding that suffering as happiness itself. This is exactly what is stated: 'as swans [plunge] into a lotus pond.' For those to whom even the suffering of <s>Avīci</s> is happiness when it is for others' sake — by what other cause of suffering could they be made to suffer?

body.text: api ca / sukhamapi teṣāmasādhāraṇamevopajāyate parasukhena, ityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, showing that an uncommon happiness indeed arises for them through the happiness of others, he says —

children.translated_text: When beings are being liberated, those oceans of joy that arise —

children.text: taireva nanu paryāptaṃ mokṣeṇārasikena kim // Bca_8.108 //
children.translated_text: are they not sufficient? What use is [that] flavorless liberation? // Bca_8.108 //

body.text: duḥkhabandhanādvisaṃyujyamāneṣu sattveṣu satsu / ye te iti / teṣāmeva anubhavasiddhatvādidaṃtayā kathayitumaśakyāḥ, ata eva prāmodyasāgarāḥ saṃtuṣṭisamudrāḥ kṛpāvatāṃ saṃtāneṣu prādurbhavanti / taireva prāmodyasāgaraiḥ paryāptaṃ tadanyasukhavaimukhyāt parisamāptam / *******
body.translated_text: When beings are being freed from the bondage of suffering. 'Those' — since they are established only through direct experience, they are inexpressible as 'this'; for that very reason 'oceans of joy' — seas of delight — arise in the continua of the compassionate. 'By those very oceans of joy, it is sufficient' — complete, due to aversion toward any other happiness. *******

children.text: ataḥ parārthaṃ kṛtvāpi na mado na ca vismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even having acted for the sake of others, there is no pride nor wonder,
nor expectation of ripening fruit — through the exclusive thirst for others' welfare alone. // Bca_8.109 //
Therefore, just as I protect myself from even slight blame,
so let me cultivate a mind of protection and a mind of compassion toward others as well. // Bca_8.110 //
Through habituation, the cognition 'I' arises with regard to the drops of semen and blood belonging to another,
even though no [such] entity exists. // Bca_8.111 //
Likewise, why should another's body not be apprehended as 'self'?

children.text: paratvaṃ tu svakāyasya sthitameva na duṣkaram // Bca_8.112 //
children.translated_text: The otherness of one's own body is already established — it is not difficult. // Bca_8.112 //
Having known oneself to be full of faults and others to be oceans of qualities,
one should meditate on the abandonment of self-cherishing and the adoption of others. // Bca_8.113 //
Just as the hands and such are cherished as parts of the body,
why are not embodied beings [cherished] as parts of the world? // Bca_8.114 //
Just as the notion of self arises through habituation in this selfless body,
why does the sense of self not arise in others too through habituation? // Bca_8.115 //

children.text: evaṃ parārthaṃ kṛtvāpi na mado na ca vismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus even having acted for the sake of others, there is no pride nor wonder;

children.text: ātmānaṃ bhojayitvaiva phalāśā na ca jāyate // Bca_8.116 //
children.translated_text: just as having fed oneself, no expectation of reward arises. // Bca_8.116 //
Therefore, just as you wish to protect yourself from suffering, grief, and such,
so let a mind of protection and a mind of compassion toward the world be practiced. // Bca_8.117 //
Therefore the Protector <s>Avalokita</s> blessed even his own name
to remove even the fear of timidity in assemblies from people. // Bca_8.118 //
One should not turn back from what is difficult, since through the power of habituation,

children.text: yasyaiva śravaṇātrāsastenaiva na vinā ratiḥ // Bca_8.119 //
children.translated_text: that whose mere hearing once caused fear — without it, there is no delight. // Bca_8.119 //
One who wishes to swiftly rescue oneself and others
should practice the supreme secret — the exchange of self and other. // Bca_8.120 //
Because of excessive attachment to this self, there is fear even from slight [danger];
who would not hate this self — a fear-bringing enemy? // Bca_8.121 //
One who, from the desire to remedy sluggishness, hunger, thirst, and such,

children.text: pakṣimatsyamṛgān hanti paripanthaṃ ca tiṣṭhati // Bca_8.122 //
children.translated_text: kills birds, fish, and deer, and stands in ambush on the road; // Bca_8.122 //
one who, for the sake of gain and honor, would kill even his own parents,
and would steal the property of the Three Jewels, by which he would become fuel for <s>Avīci</s>; // Bca_8.123 //

body.text: kaḥ paṇḍitastamātmānamicchedrakṣetprapūjayet //
body.translated_text: what wise person would desire that self, would protect it, would worship it?

body.text: na paśyecchatruvaccainaṃ kaścainaṃ pratimānayet // Bca_8.124 //
body.translated_text: Who would not regard it as an enemy? And who would honor it? // Bca_8.124 //

children.text: yadi dāsyāmi kiṃ bhokṣye ityātmārthe piśācatā /
children.translated_text: 'If I give, what shall I eat?' — this selfishness is the way of <s>piśācas</s> (demons);

children.text: yadi bhokṣye kiṃ dadāmīti parārthe devarājatā // Bca_8.125 //
children.translated_text: 'If I eat, what shall I give?' — this altruism is the way of the king of gods. // Bca_8.125 //
Having tormented another for one's own sake, one is cooked in the hells and such;

children.text: ātmānaṃ pīḍayitvā tu parārthaṃ sarvasaṃpadaḥ // Bca_8.126 //
children.translated_text: but having tormented oneself for the sake of others, all prosperity [follows]. // Bca_8.126 //
Lower rebirth, lowliness, and foolishness [result] from the very desire for self-exaltation;
transferring that same [desire] to others, favorable rebirth, honor, and wisdom [result]. // Bca_8.127 //
By commanding another for one's own sake, servitude and such are experienced;
but by commanding this [self] for the sake of others, lordship and such are experienced. // Bca_8.128 //

children.text: ye kecidduḥkhitā loke sarve te svasukhecchayā /
children.translated_text: All who are unhappy in the world are so from desiring their own happiness;

children.text: ye kecitsukhitā loke sarve te 'nyasukhecchayā // Bca_8.129 //
children.translated_text: all who are happy in the world are so from desiring the happiness of others. // Bca_8.129 //
But what need of saying more? Let this difference be observed:
between the childish one who seeks his own interest and the <s>Muni</s> who acts for others' benefit. // Bca_8.130 //

children.text: na nāma sādhyaṃ buddhatvaṃ saṃsāre 'pi kutaḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: Not to mention <s>Buddhahood</s> — even in <s>saṃsāra</s>, where is happiness
for one who does not exchange his own happiness for the suffering of others? // Bca_8.131 //

children.text: āstāṃ tāvatparo loke dṛṣṭo 'pyartho na sidhyati /
children.translated_text: Set aside the next world — even the visible purpose is not accomplished
when the servant does not do his work and the master does not give his wages. // Bca_8.132 //
Abandoning the mutual production of happiness — the festival of happiness seen and unseen —

children.text: anyonyaduḥkhānād ghoraṃ duḥkhaṃ gṛhṇanti mohitāḥ // Bca_8.133 //
children.translated_text: those who are deluded, through mutual infliction of suffering, seize upon terrible suffering. // Bca_8.133 //

children.text: upadravā ye ca bhavanti loke yāvanti duḥkhāni bhayāni caiva /
children.translated_text: Whatever calamities occur in the world, whatever sufferings and fears there are,

children.text: sarvāṇi tānyātmaparigraheṇa tatkiṃ mamānena parigraheṇa // Bca_8.134 //
children.translated_text: all of them arise from grasping at self — what then is the use of this grasping for me? // Bca_8.134 //
Without relinquishing the self, suffering cannot be abandoned,

children.text: yathāgnimaparityajya dāhaṃ tyaktuṃ na śakyate // Bca_8.135 //
children.translated_text: just as without relinquishing fire, burning cannot be abandoned. // Bca_8.135 //
Therefore, for the pacification of my own suffering and for the alleviation of others' suffering,

children.text: dadāmyanyebhya ātmānaṃ parān gṛhṇāmi cātmavat // Bca_8.136 //
children.translated_text: I give myself to others and adopt others as my own self. // Bca_8.136 //
'I am bound to another' — establish this determination, O mind!
Having relinquished [all] for the benefit of all beings, nothing else is to be considered by you now. // Bca_8.137 //
It is not right to see with those eyes, which belong to them, for one's own benefit;

children.text: na yuktaṃ syandituṃ svārthamanyadīyaiḥ karādibhiḥ // Bca_8.138 //
children.translated_text: it is not right to direct with those hands and such, which belong to others, for one's own benefit. // Bca_8.138 //
Therefore, having become devoted to beings, whatever you see in this body,
seize that very thing from it and practice what benefits others. // Bca_8.139 //
Having placed selfhood in the inferior and such, and otherness in oneself,

children.text: bhāvayerṣyāṃ ca mānaṃ ca nirvikalpena cetasā // Bca_8.140 //
children.translated_text: one should cultivate envy and pride with an undistracted mind. // Bca_8.140 //

children.text: eṣa satkriyate nāhaṃ lābhī nāhamayaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: 'This one is honored, not I; this one has gains, not I as he does;
this one is praised, I am blameworthy; I am in misery, this one is happy.' // Bca_8.141 //

children.text: ahaṃ karomi karmāṇi tiṣṭhatyeṣa tu susthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I do the work while this one remains at ease;

children.text: ayaṃ kila mahāṃlloke nīco 'haṃ kila nirguṇaḥ // Bca_8.142 //
children.translated_text: this one is apparently great in the world, while I am apparently low and without qualities.' // Bca_8.142 //
'What can one without qualities do? Everyone has a self endowed with qualities.',

children.text: santi te yeṣvahaṃ nīcaḥ santi te yeṣvahaṃ varaḥ // Bca_8.143 //
children.translated_text: 'There are those in comparison to whom I am inferior; there are those in comparison to whom I am superior.' // Bca_8.143 //
'The decline of morality and views, and such, is through the power of afflictions, not by my control;
I should be cured as far as possible — the suffering I accept as my own.' // Bca_8.144 //
'But if I am incurable by him, why does he look down on me?

children.text: kiṃ mamaitadguṇaiḥ kṛtyamātmā tu guṇavānayam // Bca_8.145 //
children.translated_text: What use are his qualities to me? — yet this one himself is endowed with qualities.' // Bca_8.145 //
'He has no compassion for people who dwell in the mouth of the wild beast of lower rebirth;
moreover, through pride in his qualities, he wishes to surpass the wise.' // Bca_8.146 //
'Seeing oneself as equal, in order to increase one's own superiority,
one should secure gain and honor for oneself, even through conflict.' // Bca_8.147 //

children.text: api sarvatra me loke bhaveyuḥ prakaṭā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'May my qualities become manifest everywhere in the world;

children.text: api nāma guṇā ye 'sya na śroṣyantyapi kecana // Bca_8.148 //
children.translated_text: may whatever qualities this one has not be heard of by anyone!' // Bca_8.148 //

children.text: chādyerannapi me doṣāḥ syānme pūjāsya no bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'May my faults be concealed; may there be worship for me, not for him;

children.text: sulabdhā adya me lābhāḥ pūjito 'hamayaṃ na tu // Bca_8.149 //
children.translated_text: my gains are now well-obtained; I am honored, but he is not.' // Bca_8.149 //
'Let us look on with delight as this one is finally humiliated,
the laughingstock of all people, criticized here and there.' // Bca_8.150 //

children.text: asyāpi hi varākasya spardhā kila mayā saha /
children.translated_text: 'For this wretch apparently has a rivalry with me!

children.text: kimasya śrutametāvat prajñā rūpaṃ kulaṃ dhanam // Bca_8.151 //
children.translated_text: Does he have the same learning, wisdom, beauty, lineage, or wealth?' // Bca_8.151 //
'Thus, hearing my own qualities being proclaimed here and there,
thrilled with horripilation, I shall enjoy the festival of happiness.' // Bca_8.152 //
'Even if this one should have gain, it should be seized by us forcibly;
if he works for us, let him be given just enough to sustain himself.' // Bca_8.153 //
'This one should be made to fall from happiness and should always be yoked to our suffering;

children.text: anena śataśaḥ sarve saṃsāravyathitā vayam // Bca_8.154 //
children.translated_text: for by this one, we have all been tortured in <s>saṃsāra</s> hundreds of times.' // Bca_8.154 //
Immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> have passed while you pursued your own interest;
through this great exertion, nothing but suffering has been earned by you. // Bca_8.155 //
Therefore, at my urging, engage in this without hesitation;

children.text: drakṣyasyetadguṇān paścādbhūtaṃ hi vacanaṃ muneḥ // Bca_8.156 //
children.translated_text: you will see its benefits later — for the word of the <s>Muni</s> is true. // Bca_8.156 //

children.text: abhaviṣyadidaṃ karma kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ yadi tvayā /
children.translated_text: If this practice had been performed by you before,

children.text: bauddhaṃ saṃpatsukhaṃ muktvā nābhaviṣyadiyaṃ daśā // Bca_8.157 //
children.translated_text: this state would not have arisen, setting aside the perfect happiness of a <s>Buddha</s>. // Bca_8.157 //
Therefore, just as you have produced the notion of 'I' in the drops of semen and blood belonging to others,
so too cultivate [this notion] in others. // Bca_8.158 //
Having become a spy for others, whatever you see in this body,
seize that very thing from it and practice what benefits others. // Bca_8.159 //
'This one is well, the other is unwell; this other is lowly, this one is exalted;

children.text: paraḥ karotyayaṃ neti kuruṣverṣyāṃ tvamātmani // Bca_8.160 //
children.translated_text: the other acts, but this one does not' — thus cultivate envy toward yourself. // Bca_8.160 //
Remove yourself from happiness and assign yourself to another's suffering;

children.text: kadāyaṃ kiṃ karotīti chala(phala)masya nirūpaya // Bca_8.161 //
children.translated_text: 'When does this one do what?' — examine the deception of this [self]. // Bca_8.161 //
Even a fault committed by another, cast it upon the head of this one;

children.text: alpamapyasya doṣaṃ ca prakāśaya mahāmuneḥ // Bca_8.162 //
children.translated_text: and even a small fault of this one, make it known before the great <s>Muni</s>. // Bca_8.162 //
Through talk of another's greater fame, make this one's fame faded;
and employ him in the service of beings, like the lowest slave. // Bca_8.163 //
He should not be praised for a mere fraction of adventitious qualities, for he is full of faults;

children.text: yathā kaścinna jānīyādguṇamasya tathā kuru // Bca_8.164 //
children.translated_text: act so that no one may know any quality of his. // Bca_8.164 //
In brief, whatever harm you have done to others for your own sake,
let that same harm fall upon yourself for the sake of beings. // Bca_8.165 //
He should not be given boldness by which he would become talkative;

children.text: sthāpyo navavadhūvṛttau hrīto bhīto 'tha saṃvṛtaḥ // Bca_8.166 //
children.translated_text: he should be kept in the manner of a new bride — modest, fearful, and restrained. // Bca_8.166 //

children.text: evaṃ kuruṣva tiṣṭhaivaṃ na kartavyamidaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: 'Do this! Stay thus! This should not be done by you!' —
thus he should be brought under control and restrained when he transgresses. // Bca_8.167 //
But if, even when told thus, O mind, you will not do this,
then I shall restrain you — for all faults depend on you. // Bca_8.168 //

children.text: kva yāsyasi mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sarvadarpānnihanmi te /
children.translated_text: Where will you go? I have you in my sight; I shall strike down all your pride.

children.text: anyo 'sau pūrvakaḥ kālastvayā yatrāsmi nāśitaḥ // Bca_8.169 //
children.translated_text: That former time is past — when you destroyed me. // Bca_8.169 //

children.text: adyāpyasti mama svārtha ityāśāṃ tyaja sāṃpratam /
children.translated_text: 'Even now I have self-interest' — abandon this hope now!
You have been sold by me to others — do not think of the many hardships [involved]. // Bca_8.170 //

children.text: tvāṃ sattveṣu na dāsyāmi yadi nāma pramodataḥ /
children.translated_text: If I do not joyfully give you to beings,

children.text: tvaṃ māṃ narakapāleṣu pradāsyasi na saṃśayaḥ // Bca_8.171 //
children.translated_text: you will certainly deliver me to the guardians of hell. // Bca_8.171 //
Thus having been given over by you many times, I have been tormented for a long time;

children.text: nihanmi svārthaceṭaṃ tvāṃ tāni vairāṇyanusmaran // Bca_8.172 //
children.translated_text: remembering those enmities, I shall destroy you, the servant of self-interest. // Bca_8.172 //
If you delight in yourself, you should not cherish yourself;

children.text: yadyātmā rakṣitavyo 'yaṃ rakṣitavyo na yujyate // Bca_8.173 //
children.translated_text: if the self is to be protected, this [self] should not be protected — this is not justified. // Bca_8.173 //
The more this body is pampered,

children.text: sukumārataro bhūtvā patatyeva tathā tathā // Bca_8.174 //
children.translated_text: the more delicate it becomes, and accordingly the more it falls. // Bca_8.174 //
And when it has fallen thus, even this entire earth

children.text: nālaṃ pūrayituṃ vāñchāṃ tatko 'syecchāṃ kariṣyati // Bca_8.175 //
children.translated_text: is not enough to fulfill its desires — who then can fulfill its wishes? // Bca_8.175 //
For one who desires the unattainable, affliction and the shattering of hopes arise;

children.text: nirāśo yastu sarvatra tasya saṃpadajīrṇikā // Bca_8.176 //
children.translated_text: but for one who is free from expectation in every respect, prosperity never decays. // Bca_8.176 //
Therefore, no scope should be given for the increase of the body's desires;

children.text: bhadrakaṃ nāma tadvastu yadiṣṭatvānna gṛhyate // Bca_8.177 //
children.translated_text: that thing is good indeed which is not grasped because of being desired. // Bca_8.177 //
This [body], whose end is ashes, is inert, moved by another;
this terrible image of impurity — why do I cling to it? // Bca_8.178 //

children.text: kiṃ mamānena yantreṇa jīvinā vā mṛtena vā /
children.translated_text: What use is this machine to me, whether alive or dead?

children.text: loṣṭādeḥ ko viśeṣo 'sya hāhaṃkāraṃ na naśyasi // Bca_8.179 //
children.translated_text: What difference between it and a clod of earth? Alas, why do you not perish, O ego-sense! // Bca_8.179 //
Through partiality to the body, suffering is needlessly earned;
what use is hatred or fondness toward this thing, which is like a log? // Bca_8.180 //
Whether thus protected by me or consumed by vultures and such,

children.text: na ca sneho na ca dveṣastatra snehaṃ karomi kim // Bca_8.181 //
children.translated_text: it has neither affection nor hatred — why then do I have affection for it? // Bca_8.181 //

children.text: roṣo yasya khalīkārāttoṣo yasya ca pūjayā /
children.translated_text: It is angered by contempt and pleased by worship —

children.text: sa eva cenna jānāti śramaḥ kasya kṛtena me // Bca_8.182 //
children.translated_text: yet if it itself does not know this, for whom is my labor? // Bca_8.182 //

children.text: imaṃ ye kāyamicchanti te 'pi me suhṛdaḥ kila /
children.translated_text: Those who desire this body are supposedly my friends;

children.text: sarve svakāyamicchanti te 'pi kasmānna me priyāḥ // Bca_8.183 //
children.translated_text: yet all desire their own bodies — why are they not equally dear to me? // Bca_8.183 //
Therefore, with indifference, this body has been relinquished by me for the benefit of the world;
hence, though it has many faults, it is maintained like a vessel for work. // Bca_8.184 //
Enough, then, with worldly conduct! I shall follow the wise,
recalling the discourse on heedfulness, warding off sloth and torpor. // Bca_8.185 //
Therefore, in order to destroy the obscurations, I shall apply concentration,
withdrawing the mind from false paths, constantly [fixing it] on its proper object. // Bca_8.186 //

body.text: bodhicaryāvatāre dhyānapāramitā nāma aṣṭamaḥ paricchedaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter, called the 'Perfection of Meditation,' in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s>.

body.text: 9. prajñāpāramitā nāma navamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: 9. The ninth chapter, called the 'Perfection of Wisdom.'

children.translated_text: That <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, which in its stainless nature is the unsurpassed state, free from all conceptual elaboration,
which is called 'undefiled' through conventional terms such as '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' and such,
having rightly realized which, those of pure intellect attain the supreme <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) —

children.text: tāṃ natvā vidhivat karomi vivṛtiṃ tasyāḥ prasannaiḥ padaiḥ // *1 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to her, I shall make a commentary upon her in lucid words. // *1 //
Where that teacher, that treasury of virtues, <s>Śāntideva</s>,
having reached the far shore of the great ocean of the [<s>Buddha</s>'s] discourses, was able to speak clearly,
how can I, of dull intellect, be capable of explaining his meaning? Nevertheless,
through the practice of wisdom, an incomparable meritorious deed — for this purpose I have set forth [this work]. // *2 //

children.text: na nāma kācidguṇaleśavāsanā materna me 'sti pratibhāguṇo 'rjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not even a trace of the impression of any virtue, indeed, has been earned by me from my mother;

children.text: tathāpi sanmitraniṣevaṇāphalaṃ yadeva me tādṛśi vāk prasarpati // *3 //
children.translated_text: yet, as the fruit of attending upon a good friend, my speech extends into such a [domain]. // *3 //

body.text: atha yo nāma kaścid gotraviśeṣāt paryupāsitakalyāṇamitratayā trijagatparyāpannasamastajanaduḥkhaduḥkhī sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ niḥśeṣaduḥkhasamuddharaṇāśayaḥ svasukhanirapekṣaḥ tatpraśamopāyabhūtaṃ buddhatvameva manyamānaḥ tatprāptivāñchayā samutpāditabodhicitto mahātmā saugatapadasādhanopāyabhūtasaṃbhāradvayaparipūraṇārthaṃ krameṇa dānādiṣu pravartate / tasya tathā pravartamānasya samyakpratipannaśamathasyāpi dānādayaḥ prajñāvikalatayā jagadarthasaṃpādananidānaṃ buddhatvaṃ nāvahantītyabhisaṃdhāya avaśyaṃ saṃsāraduḥkhanirmokśārthinā prajñotpādanāya yatitavyam / yathoktam-
body.translated_text: Now, a certain great being, by virtue of a special spiritual lineage and having attended upon spiritual friends, suffers at the suffering of all people within the three worlds, has the intention to rescue all living beings from suffering without remainder, is indifferent to his own happiness, considers <s>Buddhahood</s> itself to be the means for pacifying that [suffering], and having generated <s>bodhicitta</s> through the desire to attain it, progressively engages in generosity and such for the purpose of fulfilling the two accumulations that are the means for attaining the state of a <s>Sugata</s>. For one thus engaged, even when <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) has been properly attained, generosity and such — due to the lack of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — do not bring about <s>Buddhahood</s>, which is the cause of accomplishing the welfare of beings. With this intention, one who seeks liberation from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> must necessarily strive to generate <s>prajñā</s>. As stated —

body.text:
śamathena vipaśyanāsuyuktaḥ
[8.4]
body.translated_text: 'One endowed with <s>vipaśyanā</s> together with <s>śamatha</s>' [8.4]

body.text: ityādi / tatra śamathapratipādanaṃ kṛtam / idānīṃ tadanantaraprāptāṃ vipaśyanāṃ prajñāparanāmadheyāṃ pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: — and so forth. Therein, the exposition of <s>śamatha</s> has been completed. Now, to set forth <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) — which is another name for <s>prajñā</s> — which follows immediately after that, he says —

children.text: imaṃ parikaraṃ sarvaṃ prajñārthaṃ hi munirjagau /
children.translated_text: The <s>Muni</s> taught all this preparation for the sake of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom);
therefore, one should generate <s>prajñā</s>, with the desire for the cessation of suffering. // <s>Bca</s> 9.1 //

body.text: imamiti samanantaramiha śāstre lakṣaṇataḥ pratipāditaṃ dānādikamidaṃtayā pratyakṣatayā parāmṛśati / parikaramiti parivāraṃ paricchedam / saṃbhāramiti yāvat / sarvamuktaprakāramanyacca /
body.translated_text: 'This' — he refers as something immediately present and directly perceived to the generosity and such that have been described in terms of their characteristics in this treatise. 'Preparation' — retinue, section; 'accumulation' is the full meaning. 'All' — of the kind described and other [types] as well.

body.text: prajñārtha hi munirjagāviti saṃbandhaḥ / prajñā yathāvasthitapratītyasamutpannavastutattvapravicayalakṣaṇā, saiva arthaḥ prayojanaṃ saṃbodhihetubhāvopanāyakatayā yasya dānādilakṣaṇasya parikarasya sa tathā, tamiti / dānapāramitādiṣu dharmapravicayasvabhāvāyāḥ prajñāyāḥ pradhānatvāt / tathā hi dānaṃ saṃbuddhabodhiprāptaye prathamaṃ kāraṇam, puṇyasaṃbhārāntarbhūtatvāt / tacca śīlālaṃkṛtameva sugatiparaṃparāṃ sukhabhogopakaraṇasaṃpannāmāvahadanuttarajñānapratilambhahetuḥ / kṣāntirapi tadvipakṣabhūtapratighapratipakṣatayā dānaśīlasukṛtamayaṃ saṃbhāramanupālayantī sugatatvādhigataye saṃpravartate / etacca śubhaṃ dānāditritayasaṃbhūtaṃ puṇyasaṃbhārākhyaṃ vīryamantareṇa na bhavatīti tadapi ubhayasaṃbhārakāraṇatayā sarvāvaraṇaprahāṇāya samupajāyate / samāhitacittasya ca yathābhūtaparijñānamutpadyata iti dhyānapāramitāpi anuttarajñānaheturupapadyate / evamete dānādayaḥ satkṛtya saṃbhṛtā api prajñāmantareṇa saugatapadādhigamahetavo na bhavantīti nāpi pāramitāvyapadeśaṃ labhante / prajñākṛtapariśuddhibhājaḥ punaḥ avyāhatodārapravṛttitayā tadanukūlamanuvartamānāḥ taddhetubhāvamadhigacchanti, pāramitānāmadheyaṃ ca labhante / tathā dātṛdeyapratigrāhakāditritayānupalambhayogena prajñāpariśodhitāḥ sādaranirantaradīrghakālamabhyasyamānāḥ prakarṣaparyantamupagacchantaḥ avidyāpravartitasakalavikalpajālamalarahitaṃ kleśajñeyāvaraṇavinirmuktamubhayanairātmyādhigamasvabhāvaṃ sarvasvaparahitasaṃpadādhārabhūtaṃ paramārthatattvātmakaṃ tathāgatadharmakāyamabhinirvartayantīti prajñāpradhānā dānādayo guṇā ucyante //
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Muni</s> taught for the sake of <s>prajñā</s>' — this is the syntactic connection. <s>Prajñā</s> is characterized as the discernment of the true nature of dependently arisen things as they actually are; that very [<s>prajñā</s>] is the purpose — the aim — of this preparation characterized by generosity and such, in its capacity of bringing about the condition of being a cause of awakening. Because <s>prajñā</s>, whose nature is the discernment of <s>dharmas</s>, is primary among the perfections beginning with the perfection of generosity. For generosity is the first cause for attaining the awakening of a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, being included in the accumulation of merit. And that [generosity], adorned by moral discipline alone, brings about a succession of happy destinies endowed with the requisites for the enjoyment of happiness, and is a cause for the attainment of unsurpassed knowledge. Patience too, by serving as the antidote to hostility which opposes that [merit], guarding the accumulation composed of the meritorious deeds of generosity and moral discipline, contributes to the attainment of the state of a <s>Sugata</s>. And this wholesome [accumulation] produced by the triad of generosity and such, called the accumulation of merit, does not arise without <s>vīrya</s> (effort); therefore that too arises as the cause of both accumulations, for the abandonment of all obscurations. And since one whose mind is concentrated knows things as they truly are, the perfection of meditation too is established as a cause of unsurpassed knowledge. Thus, these [virtues] beginning with generosity, even when carefully accumulated, without <s>prajñā</s> do not become causes for the attainment of the <s>Sugata</s>'s state, nor do they obtain the designation of 'perfections.' But when purified by <s>prajñā</s>, through their unobstructed and noble activity, following in accordance with that [<s>prajñā</s>], they attain the status of being its causes and receive the name of perfections. Likewise, purified by <s>prajñā</s> through the yoga of non-apprehension of the triad of giver, gift, and recipient, being practiced with care, constantly, and for a long time, reaching the ultimate degree — they bring about the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s>, which is free from the web of all false conceptualizations set in motion by ignorance, liberated from the obscurations of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and the knowable, whose nature is the realization of the twofold selflessness, which is the basis of the attainment of all benefit for oneself and others, and whose essence is ultimate reality. Therefore, the qualities beginning with generosity are said to have <s>prajñā</s> as primary.

body.text: na caitadvaktavyam- yadi prajñā pradhānaṃ dānādīnām, saiva kevalā saṃbodhisādhanamastu, kimaparairdānādibhiriti / tadanyeṣāmupayogasya varṇitatvāt, kevalaṃ netravikalā iva dānādayaḥ prajñānetṛkā eva yathābhimatāṃ saugatīṃ bhūmimabhisarantīti prajñopanāyakā ucyante, na tu prajñaiva kevalā samyaksaṃbodhisādhanam / tasmāddānādiparikaraḥ prajñārthaḥ iti siddham //
body.translated_text: Nor should it be said: if <s>prajñā</s> is primary among generosity and such, let it alone be the means for awakening — what use are the others, generosity and such? Because the usefulness of the others has been described. Rather, generosity and such, like the blind without eyes, led by the guide of <s>prajñā</s>, proceed toward the desired <s>Sugata</s> ground. Thus they are said to have <s>prajñā</s> as their guide; but <s>prajñā</s> alone is not the means for perfect awakening. Therefore, 'the preparation of generosity and such is for the sake of <s>prajñā</s>' — this is established.

body.text: sarvakalpanāvirahāt samāropāpavādāntadvayamaunāt aśaikṣakāyavāṅmanaḥkarmalakṣaṇamaunatrayayogādvā munirbuddho bhagavān / triduḥkhatāduḥkhitasarvajagatparitrāṇādhyāśayo jagau jagāda / uktavānityarthaḥ / āryaprajñāpāramitādisūtrānteṣu prajñārthamuktavān krameṇa dānādiparikaram / yathoktamāryaśatasāhasrayāṃ prajñāpāramitāyām-
body.translated_text: '<s>Muni</s>' — a <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, because of being free from all conceptualization, because of the silence of [being free from] the two extremes of superimposition and denial, or because of the threefold silence characterized by the trainings of the body, speech, and mind of one beyond training. With the intention of rescuing all the world suffering from the three kinds of suffering, 'taught' — spoke, declared — this is the meaning. In the noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and other <s>sūtras</s>, he progressively taught the preparation of generosity and such for the sake of <s>prajñā</s>. As stated in the noble <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> —

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma subhūte sūryamaṇḍalaṃ candramaṇḍalaṃ ca caturṣu dvīpeṣu karma karoti, caturaśca dvīpānanugacchati anuparivartate, evameva subhūte prajñāpāramitā pañcasu pāramitāsu karma karoti, pañca pāramitā anugacchati, anuparivartate, prajñāpāramitāvirahitatvāt pañca pāramitāḥ pāramitānāmadheyaṃ na labhante / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte rājā cakravartī virahitaḥ saptabhī ratnai ścakravartināmadheyaṃ na labhate, evameva subhūte pañca pāramitāḥ prajñāpāramitāvirahitatvānna pāramitānāmadheyaṃ labhante / tadyathāpi nāma subhūte yāḥ kāścana kunadyaḥ, sarvāstā yena gaṅgā mahānadī tenānugacchanti / tā gaṅgayā mahānadyā sārdhaṃ mahāsamudramanugacchanti, evameva subhūte pañca pāramitāḥ prajñāpāramitāparigṛhītā yena sarvākārajñatā tenānugacchanti / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the disc of the sun and the disc of the moon perform their function in the four continents, and follow and accompany the four continents — just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the perfection of wisdom performs its function in the five perfections, follows and accompanies the five perfections. Without the perfection of wisdom, the five perfections do not obtain the designation of "perfections." Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a wheel-turning king, deprived of the seven jewels, does not obtain the designation of "wheel-turning [king]" — just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the five perfections, being deprived of the perfection of wisdom, do not obtain the designation of "perfections." Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, whatever small rivers there are, all of them follow the direction of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the great river; and they, together with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the great river, follow the great ocean — just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the five perfections, embraced by the perfection of wisdom, follow the direction of omniscience.' Thus in detail.

body.text: punaścoktam-
body.translated_text: And further it is stated —

body.text: iyaṃ kauśika prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ dānapāramitāmabhibhavati, śīlapāramitāmabhibhavati, kṣāntipāramitāmabhibhavati, [vīryapāramitāmabhibhavati,] dhyānapāramitāmabhibhavati / tadyathāpi nāma kauśika jātyandhānāṃ śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā apariṇāyakānāmabhavyaṃ mārgāvataraṇāya, kutaḥ punarnagarānupraveśāya, evameva kauśika acakṣuṣkāḥ pañca pāramitā jātyandhabhūtā bhavanti vinā prajñāpāramitayā apariṇāyakāḥ, vinā prajñāpāramitayā abhavyā bodhimārgāvataraṇāya, kuta eva sarvākārajñatānagarānupraveśāya / yadā punaḥ kauśika pañca pāramitāḥ prajñāpāramitāparigṛhītā bhavanti, tadā etāḥ pañca pāramitāḥ sacakṣuṣkā bhavanti / prajñāpāramitāparigṛhītāścaitāḥ pañca pāramitāḥ pāramitānāmadheyaṃ labhante // iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'This, <s>Kauśika</s>, the perfection of wisdom of <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, surpasses the perfection of generosity, surpasses the perfection of moral discipline, surpasses the perfection of patience, [surpasses the perfection of effort,] surpasses the perfection of meditation. Just as, <s>Kauśika</s>, a hundred or a thousand persons blind from birth, without a guide, would be incapable of entering a road — how much less of entering a city — just so, <s>Kauśika</s>, the five perfections become as if blind from birth, without eyes, without a guide, apart from the perfection of wisdom; without the perfection of wisdom they are incapable of entering the path to awakening — how much less of entering the city of omniscience. But when, <s>Kauśika</s>, the five perfections are embraced by the perfection of wisdom, then these five perfections become endowed with eyes. And these five perfections, embraced by the perfection of wisdom, obtain the designation of "perfections."' Thus in detail.

body.text: evamanyatrāpi yathāsūtramavagantavyam / uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Thus it should be understood from other [sūtras] as well, in accordance with the scriptures. And it is said —

children.translated_text: 'By all the perfections, spotless, O blameless one,
you are always followed, like a crescent moon by the stars.'

body.text: iti // [prajñāpāramitāstava-8]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Prajñāpāramitāstava</s> 8]

body.text: athavā- imamiti samanantaraprakrāntarūpaṃ śamathātmakaṃ prabandham / parikaramiti prajñāsamutthāpakatayā tatkāraṇasaṃdohaṃ pīṭhikābandhaṃ ca / prajñārthamiti prajñaiva pūrvoktā arthaḥ prayojanaṃ sādhyatayā yasya tam / śamathapariśodhitacittasaṃtāne prajñāyāḥ prādurbhāvāt supraśodhitakṣetre sasyaniṣpattivat / yathoktaṃ śikśāsamuccaye-
body.translated_text: Or alternatively: 'this' refers to the immediately preceding composition, which is of the nature of <s>śamatha</s>. 'Preparation' refers to the foundation and preliminary arrangement that serves to produce <s>prajñā</s>, as its causal collection. 'For the sake of <s>prajñā</s>' — <s>prajñā</s> itself, as described before, is the purpose, the goal to be accomplished, of that [preparation]. Because <s>prajñā</s> manifests in a mental continuum purified by <s>śamatha</s>, just as a crop matures in a well-prepared field. As stated in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> —

body.text:
kiṃ punarasya śamathasya māhātmyam? yathābhūtajñānajananaśaktiḥ /
yasmāt-
body.translated_text: 'What then is the greatness of this <s>śamatha</s>? The capacity to generate knowledge of things as they truly are. Since —'

children.translated_text: 'One who is concentrated knows things as they truly are — thus the <s>Muni</s> has spoken.'
Thus. [<s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s> verse 9]

body.text: etadapi dharmasaṃgītāvuktam-
body.translated_text: This is also stated in the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti</s> —

body.text: samāhitacetaso yathābhūtadarśanaṃ bhavati / yathābhūtadarśino bodhisattvasya sattveṣu mahākaruṇā pravartate / idaṃ mayā samādhimukhaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ niṣpādayitavyam / sa tayā mahākaruṇayā saṃcodyamāno 'dhiśīlamadhicittamadhiprajñaṃ ca śikṣāḥ paripūrya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'One whose mind is concentrated sees things as they truly are. For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who sees things as they truly are, great compassion toward beings arises. [He thinks:] "This <s>samādhi</s> gateway must be accomplished by me for the sake of all beings." He, being urged by that great compassion, having fulfilled the trainings in superior morality, superior mind, and superior wisdom, attains unsurpassed perfect awakening.' Thus in detail.

body.text: hiriti yasmāt prajñārthaṃ dānādiparikaraṃ śamathātmakaparikaraṃ vā munirjagau, tasmādutpādayet prajñāmiti yojanīyam / utpādayediti niṣpādayet sākṣātkuryāt bhāvayeta sevayet bahulīkuryādvā //
body.translated_text: The particle 'hi' (for) — since the <s>Muni</s> taught the preparation of generosity and such, or the preparation of the nature of <s>śamatha</s>, for the sake of <s>prajñā</s> — therefore one should generate <s>prajñā</s>: this is how it should be construed. 'Should generate' — should accomplish, should directly realize, should cultivate, should practice, should develop.

body.text: sā ca prajñā dvividhāhetubhūtā phalabhūtā ca / hetubhūtāpi dvividhā adhimukticaritasya ca bhūmipraviṣṭasya ca bodhisattvasya / phalabhūtā tu sarvākāravaropetā sarvadharmaśūnyatādhigamasvabhāvā
body.translated_text: And that <s>prajñā</s> is twofold: as cause and as fruit. As cause, it is again twofold: that of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> engaged in devoted conduct [before entering the grounds] and that of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has entered the grounds. As fruit, however, it is endowed with all supreme aspects, and its nature is the realization of the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: animittayogena / tatra prathamato hetubhūtā śrutacintābhāvanāmayī krameṇa abhyāsādbhūmipraviṣṭasya prajñāṃ nirvartayati / sā ca aparāparabhūmipratilambhayogena prakarṣamabhivardhayantī yāvadubhayāvaraṇavigamāt sakalakalpanājālavigatabuddhatvasvabhāvaprajñāṃ niṣpādayati / ata evāhaduḥkhanivṛttikāṅkṣayeti / duḥkhasya pañcagatisaṃgṛhītasattvarāśigatasya svātmagatasya ca sāṃsārikasya jātivyādhijarāmaraṇasvabhāvasya priyaviprayogāpriyasaṃprayogaparyeṣyamāṇalābhavighāta lakṣaṇasya, saṃkṣepataḥ pañcopādānaskandhātmakasya ca, nivṛttiḥ nirvāṇam upaśamaḥ / punaranutpattidharmakatayā ātyantikasamuccheda ityarthaḥ / tasyāḥ kāṅkṣayā abhilāṣeṇa / chandeneti yāvat / tathāhi viparyāsasaṃjñino 'satsattvasamāropābhiniveśavaśādātmātmīyagrahapravṛtterayoniśomanasikāraprasūto rāgādikleśagaṇaḥ samupajāyate, tasmāt karma, tato janma, tataśca vyādhijarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāśca prajāyante / evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati / tadevamanulomākāraṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ samyakprajñayā vyavalokayataḥ, punastameva nirātmakamasvāmikaṃ māyāmarīcigandharvanagarasvapnapratibimbādisamānākāratayā paramārthato niḥsvabhāvaṃ paśyato yathābhūtaparijñānāttadvipakṣātmakatayā mohasvabhāvamavidyābhavāṅgaṃ nivartate, avidyānirodhāttatpratyayāḥ saṃskārā nirudhyante / evaṃ pūrvapūrvasya kāraṇabhūtasya nirodhāduttarottarakāryabhūtasya nirodho veditavyaḥ / yāvajjātinirodhājjarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāśca nirudhyante / evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati / tatra avidyā tṛṣṇopādānaṃ ca kleśavartmano vyavacchedaḥ / saṃskārā bhavaśca karmavartmano vyavacchedaḥ / pariśiṣṭānyaṅgāni duḥkhavartmano vyavacchedaḥ / pūrvāntāparāntanirodho nirodhavartmano vyavacchedaḥ / evameva trivartma nirātmakam ātmātmīyarahitaṃ saṃbhavati ca saṃbhavayogena, vibhavati ca vibhavayogena, svabhāvānnaḍakalāpasadṛśa iti / etacca uttaratra vistareṇa yuktayāgamābhyāṃ pratipādayiṣyate //
body.translated_text: through the signless yoga. There, first, wisdom born of hearing, thinking, and meditation — which is the cause — progressively, through practice, brings about [the wisdom] of one who has entered the stages. And that [wisdom], increasingly developing through the attainment of successive stages, eventually — through the removal of both obscurations — produces the wisdom that is the nature of <s>Buddhahood</s>, free from the entire net of conceptual elaboration. For this very reason he says 'through the desire for the cessation of suffering.' The cessation of suffering — <s>nirvāṇa</s>, peace — is the [cessation] of the suffering that belongs to the mass of beings included in the five realms, and of one's own [suffering], which is of <s>saṃsāric</s> nature characterized by birth, disease, old age, and death, separation from the beloved, encounter with the unbeloved, and frustration in obtaining what is sought — in short, consisting of the five aggregates of clinging. 'Cessation' further means absolute elimination through the nature of non-arising again — this is the meaning. 'Through the desire' — with the wish, the longing — for that [cessation]. For thus, one whose cognition is perverted — through the force of superimposing and clinging to a truly existent being where there is none — gives rise to the host of afflictions such as desire and so forth, which are produced by improper mental attention (<s>ayoniśo manasikāra</s>) arising from grasping at self and mine. From that [arises] <s>karma</s>; from that, birth; and from that arise disease, old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and agitation. Thus there is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering. When one correctly discerns with wisdom this dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) in its forward order, and further sees that very [process] as selfless, ownerless, similar in nature to an illusion, a mirage, a city of <s>gandharvas</s>, a dream, a reflection, and such — as lacking intrinsic nature in the ultimate sense — then, through the correct understanding of things as they truly are, the ignorance that is the link of becoming, being of the nature of the opposing factor of delusion, ceases. Through the cessation of ignorance, the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) conditioned by it cease. Thus, through the cessation of each successive prior [link] that functions as a cause, the cessation of each successive subsequent [link] that functions as an effect should be understood — up to: through the cessation of birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and agitation cease. Thus there is the cessation of this entire great mass of suffering. There, ignorance, craving, and clinging constitute the severance of the path of afflictions. <s>Saṃskāras</s> and becoming constitute the severance of the path of <s>karma</s>. The remaining links constitute the severance of the path of suffering. The cessation of the prior and posterior limits constitutes the severance of the path of cessation. Thus this very triple path, being selfless — devoid of self and mine — arises through the process of arising, and ceases through the process of cessation; by nature it is like a sheaf of reeds. And this will be established in detail below, through reasoning and scripture.

body.text: tadevaṃ prajñayā svapnamāyādisvabhāvaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇasya sarvadharmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāvatayā pratipatteḥ paramārthādhigamāt savāsananiḥśeṣadoṣarāśivinivṛttirbhavatīti sarvaduḥkhopaśamahetuḥ prajñā upapadyate //
body.translated_text: Thus, for one who examines the conditioned as being of the nature of a dream, an illusion, and such through wisdom — through the realization that all <s>dharmas</s> lack intrinsic nature — the cessation of the entire mass of defects together with their latent impressions occurs through the attainment of ultimate [reality]. Thus wisdom is established as the cause of the cessation of all suffering.

body.text: yathā ca yuktyāgamābhyāṃ vicārayataḥ aviparītavastutattvapravicayaḥ samupajāyate, tadupadarśayituṃ satyadvayavyavasthāmāha saṃvṛtirityādi-
body.translated_text: To show how, through investigation by means of reasoning and scripture, the unerring discernment of the true nature of things arises, he presents the distinction of the two truths, with 'conventional' and so forth —

children.translated_text: <s>Saṃvṛti</s> (conventional [truth]) and <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate [truth]) — this pair of truths is accepted.
Reality is beyond the domain of the intellect; the intellect is said to be <s>saṃvṛti</s> (the conventional). // <s>Bca</s> 9.2 //

body.text: saṃvriyate āvriyate yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ svabhāvāvaraṇādāvṛtaprakāśanācca anayeti saṃvṛtiḥ / avidyā moho viparyāsa iti paryāyāḥ / avidyā hi asatpadārthasvarūpāropikā svabhāvadarśanāvaraṇātmikā ca satī saṃvṛtirupapadyate / yaduktamāryaśālistambasūtre-
body.translated_text: '<s>Saṃvṛti</s>' — it conceals, covers over, the correct understanding of things as they truly are; by its nature it obstructs [the perception of] intrinsic nature and covers and hides [reality] — thus it is <s>saṃvṛti</s>. <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>viparyāsa</s> (perversion) — these are synonyms. For ignorance, being one that superimposes the character of non-existent objects and being of the nature of obstructing the vision of [true] nature, is fittingly [called] <s>saṃvṛti</s>. As stated in the <s>Āryaśālistambasūtra</s> —

body.text:
punaraparam- tattve 'pratipattiḥ mithyāpratipattiḥ, ajñānamavidyā / iti /
uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Furthermore: 'Non-understanding of reality is wrong understanding; non-knowledge is ignorance.' Thus. And it is said —

children.translated_text: 'It manifests what is unreal and operates by concealing what is real —
ignorance, the very moment it arises, acts like the affliction of desire.'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tadupadarśitaṃ ca pratītyasamutpannaṃ vasturūpaṃ saṃvṛtirucyate / tadeva lokasaṃvṛtisatyamityamidhīyate lokasyaiva saṃvṛtyā tat satyamiti kṛtvā / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: And the dependently arisen form of things that is shown by that [ignorance] is called <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional). That very thing is called 'conventional truth' (<s>lokasaṃvṛtisatya</s>) — because it is true for the world by means of [its] concealment. As stated —

children.text: mohaḥ svabhāvāvaraṇādi saṃvṛtiḥ satyaṃ tayā khyāti yadeva kṛtrimam /
children.translated_text: 'Delusion, the concealment of intrinsic nature and such, is <s>saṃvṛti</s>; what appears as real through that, which is fabricated —

children.text: jagāda tatsaṃvṛtisatyamityasau muniḥ padārthaṃ kṛtakaṃ ca saṃvṛtim //
children.translated_text: that the <s>Muni</s> called conventional truth; and the fabricated entity [he called] <s>saṃvṛti</s>.'

body.text: iti / [ma. a. 6.28]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> 6.28]

body.text: sā ca saṃvṛtirdvividhā lokata eva, tathyasaṃvṛtirmithyāsaṃvṛtiśceti / tathā hi kiṃcit pratītyajātaṃ nīlādikaṃ vasturūpamadoṣavadindriyairūpalabdhaṃ lokata eva satyam, māyāmarīcipratibimbādviṣu pratītya samupajātamapi doṣavadindriyopalabdhaṃ yathāsvaṃ tīrthikasiddhāntaparikalpitaṃ ca lokata eva mithyā / taduktam-
body.translated_text: And that <s>saṃvṛti</s> is twofold, even from the worldly standpoint: correct conventional (<s>tathyasaṃvṛti</s>) and false conventional (<s>mithyāsaṃvṛti</s>). For some dependently arisen form of things such as blue and such, apprehended by sense-faculties free from defects, is true even from the worldly standpoint. But that which, though arising dependently — such as illusions, mirages, reflections, and so forth — is apprehended by defective sense-faculties, and that which is conceptually constructed by the doctrines of the <s>Tīrthikas</s>, is false even from the worldly standpoint. As stated —

children.translated_text: 'What the world cognizes as apprehensible by the six sense-faculties without impairment —

children.text: satyaṃ hi tallokata evaṃ śeṣaṃ vikalpitaṃ lokata eva mithyā //
children.translated_text: that is true from the worldly standpoint alone; the rest, being conceptually constructed, is false from the worldly standpoint alone.'

body.text: iti / [ma. a. 6.25]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> 6.25]

body.text: etattadubhayamapi samyagdṛśāmāryāṇāṃ mṛṣā, paramārthadaśāyāṃ saṃvṛtisatyālīkatvāt / etat samanantarameva upapattyā pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ / tasmādavidyāvatāṃ vastusvabhāvo na pratibhāsate iti //
body.translated_text: Both of these are false for the noble ones who see correctly, since in the perspective of ultimate [reality], conventional truth is unreal. We shall establish this with reasoning immediately following. Therefore, for those possessed of ignorance, the true nature of things does not appear.

body.text: paramaḥ uttamaḥ arthaḥ paramārthaḥ, akṛtrimaṃ vasturūpam, yadadhigamāt sarvāvṛtivāsanānu saṃdhikleśaprahāṇaṃ bhavati / sarvadharmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāvatā, śūnyatā, tathatā, bhūtakoṭiḥ, dharmadhāturityādiparyāyāḥ / sarvasya hi pratītyasamutpannasya padārthasya niḥsvabhāvatā pāramārthikaṃ rūpam, yathāpratibhāsaṃ sāṃvṛtasyānupapannatvāt / tathā hi- na tāvat yathāparidṛśyamānarūpeṇa satsvabhāvo bhāvaḥ, tasya uttarakālamanavasthānāt, svabhāvasya ca sarvadā anāgantukatayā avicalitarūpatvāt / yo hi yasya svabhāvaḥ, sa kathaṃ kadācidapi nivarteta? anyathā tasya svabhāvatāhāniprasaṅgānniḥsvabhāvataiva syāt / nāpi sa utpadyamānaḥ satsvabhāvarūpeṇa kutaścidāgacchati, nirudhyamāno vā kvacit saṃnicayaṃ gacchati, api tu hetupratyayasāmagrīṃ pratītya māyāvadutpadyate, tadvaikalyato nirudhyate ca / hetupratyayasāmagrīṃ pratītya jātasya parāyattātmalābhasyapratibimbasyeva
body.translated_text: The supreme (<s>parama</s>), the highest, meaning (<s>artha</s>) is <s>paramārtha</s> (the ultimate) — the unfabricated form of things, through the realization of which there occurs the abandonment of all the afflictions that are the connections of the latent impressions of all obscurations. The lack of intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s> — <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality), <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the expanse of <s>dharmas</s>) — these are synonyms. For the lack of intrinsic nature of every dependently arisen entity is its ultimate form, since the form as it appears [conventionally] is untenable. For a thing does not possess a real intrinsic nature in the form in which it is perceived, since it does not persist subsequently; and because intrinsic nature, being always non-adventitious, is of unshifting form. For what is the intrinsic nature of something — how could it ever cease? Otherwise, through the absurd consequence of the loss of its being intrinsic nature, it would simply be devoid of intrinsic nature. Nor does a thing, when arising, come from anywhere with a real intrinsic nature; nor, when ceasing, does it go to some repository. Rather, dependent on the assemblage of causes and conditions, it arises like an illusion; and through the deficiency of those [causes and conditions], it ceases. For something that has arisen dependent on the assemblage of causes and conditions — whose self-existence depends on others, like a reflection

body.text: kutaḥ satsvabhāvatā? na ca kasyacit padārthasya paramārthato hetupratyayasāmagrītaḥ samutpattiḥ saṃbhavati, tasyā api aparasāmagrījanitātmatayā parāyattātmalābhāyā niḥsvabhāvatvāt / evamanyasyāḥ pūrvapūrvāyāḥ svasvakāraṇasāmagrījanyatayā niḥsvabhāvatā draṣṭavyā / itthaṃ kāraṇānurūpaṃ kāryamicchatā kathaṃ niḥsvabhāvāt sasvabhāvasyotpattirabhyupetavyā? yadvakṣyati-
body.translated_text: — how could there be real intrinsic nature? Nor can there be, in the ultimate sense, the arising of any entity from the assemblage of causes and conditions, since that [assemblage] too — being itself generated by another assemblage, with its own existence depending on others — is devoid of intrinsic nature. Thus, every prior [assemblage] too should be seen as devoid of intrinsic nature, being produced by its own respective causal assemblage. For one who accepts the effect as conforming to the cause, how can the arising of something with intrinsic nature from something without intrinsic nature be accepted? As will be stated —

children.translated_text: 'That which is produced by an illusion and that which is produced by causes —

children.text: āyāti tatkutaḥ kutra yāti ceti nirūpyatām //
children.translated_text: from where does it come, and where does it go? Let this be examined.'
'That which is seen only in the proximity of something else, and not in its absence —
being like a reflection, being fabricated — how can it have reality?'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: And it is said —

children.text: yaḥ pratyayairjāyati sa hyajāto na tasya utpādu sabhāvato 'sti /
children.translated_text: 'What arises from conditions is indeed unborn; it does not have arising by its own nature.

children.text: yaḥ pratyayādhīnu sa śūnya ukto yaḥ śūnyatāṃ jānati so 'pramattaḥ //
children.translated_text: What is dependent on conditions is called empty; one who knows emptiness is heedful.'

body.text: iti / [anavataptahradāpasaṃkramaṇasūtram]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Anavataptahradāpasaṃkramaṇasūtra</s>]

body.text: iti śūnyebhya eva śūnyā dharmāḥ prabhavanti dharmebhya iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, from empty <s>dharmas</s> alone, empty <s>dharmas</s> arise.

body.text: na ca svaparobhayarūpahetunibandhanamahetunibandhanaṃ vā bhāvasya janma atipeśalamupapadyate / tathā hi ātmasvarūpaṃ bhāvānāṃ svajanmanimittaṃ bhavet, niṣpannamaniṣpannaṃ vā bhavet / na tāvanniṣpannasya sataḥ svātmani kāraṇatā, tasya sarvātmanā svayaṃ niṣpannatvāt kva punarasya vyāpāro 'stu? utpādyasya punarasyāniṣpannasyānyasya svabhāvasyābhāvāt, ekasya cāsya niraṃśatvāt / na ca paścādutpadyamānasyāparasya tatsvabhāvatā yuktā, tanniṣpattāvaniṣpannasya tatsvabhāvatvābhāvāt / iti na svātmano niṣpannāt kasyacidutpattirasti / na cāpi svatautpattipakṣe prāṅniṣpannaṃ svarūpamitaretarāśrayadoṣasaṅgāt kasyacit saṃbhavati / nāpi tadaniṣpannasvabhāvamākāśakuśeśayasaṃkāśamaśeṣasāmarthyaśūnyaṃ svaniṣpattau hetubhāvamupagantumarhati, anyathā kharaviṣāṇasyāpi svasvabhāvajanakatvaprasaṅgāt //
body.translated_text: Nor is the arising of a thing from a cause that is of the nature of self, other, both, or from no cause tenable even in the most subtle way. For the own-nature of things, if it were the cause of their own birth, would be either complete or incomplete. A complete, existent [thing] cannot be its own cause, since it is already fully complete in itself — where then would its activity be? And since the other — the incomplete [thing] to be produced — has no [own] nature, and since it [the cause] is unitary and without parts — nor is it justified that what arises subsequently as something different has the same nature as that [cause], since what is incomplete at the time of its [the cause's] completion does not have the nature of that [cause]. Thus, from nothing that is a complete self does anything arise. Nor, in the position of arising from self, does the own-nature exist as already complete prior [to the arising], due to the defect of mutual dependence. Nor can that, being of uncompleted nature — resembling a flower in the sky — devoid of all efficacy, be accepted as a cause of its own completion; otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence that a hare's horn too could produce its own nature.

body.text: nāpi parata iti pakṣaḥ, ādityādapi andhakārasya, sarvasmādvā sarvasya utpattiprasaṅgāt, janakājanakābhimatayorvivakṣitakāryāpekṣayā paratvāviśeṣāt / janyajanakaikatvaikasaṃtatipratiniyamo 'pi anutpanne kārye kālpanikatayā vastuto na saṃgacchate / na ca anāgatāvasthitadharmāpekṣayā kāryādivyavahāro vāstavaḥ, arthasvabhāvasadbhāvasya nirūpayiṣyamāṇatvāt / nāpi bījāvasthāsu vidyamānāṅkurāpekṣayā bījasya paratvamakālpanikamasti, kāraṇe kāryāstitvasya
body.translated_text: Nor is the position 'from another' [tenable] — since there would be the absurd consequence of darkness arising even from the sun, or of everything arising from everything, because with respect to the intended effect, there is no distinction in 'otherness' between what is accepted as a producer and what is not. The restriction [that] producer and product [must share] unity and belong to one continuum — this too, since the effect is unarisen, is merely conceptual and does not hold in reality. Nor is the conventional designation of 'effect' and such real with respect to a <s>dharma</s> existing in the future state, since the real existence of the nature of the thing will be refuted. Nor is the otherness of the seed with respect to the sprout existing in the seed-state non-conceptual, since the existence of the effect in the cause

body.text: niṣetsyamānatvāt / yatra paridṛśyamānameva rūpaṃ vicārato nāvatiṣṭhate, tatra anāgatādiṣu saṃbhāvitasya kā cintā?
body.translated_text: will be rejected. Where even the form that is directly perceived does not withstand examination, what concern is there for what is hypothesized in the future and such states?

body.text: nāpi ubhayata iti pakṣaḥ, pratyekapakṣoktasamuditadoṣaprasaṅgāt, kāryānutpatau ca ubhayarūpasya hetoḥ paramārthato 'bhāvāt / utpattau vā na kiṃcijjanayitavyamastīti kutra ubhayarūpasya hetorvyāpāraḥ syāt?
body.translated_text: Nor is the position 'from both' [tenable] — since there would be the absurd consequence of the combined defects stated for each position individually, and because in the non-arising of the effect, the cause of both natures has no existence in the ultimate sense. Or if it were to arise, since there would be nothing to be produced, where would the activity of the cause of both natures be?

body.text: nāpi ahetuta iti vikalpaḥ, yato nāyaṃ prasajyapratiṣedhātmatayā ahetuta iti yujyate / ahetukatve hi bhāvānāṃ deśakālaniyamābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ syāt, nityaṃ sattvāsattvaprasaṅgo vā / upeyārthināṃ pratiniyatopāyānuṣṭhānaṃ ca na syāt / pradhāneśvarādīnāṃ kāraṇasya pratiṣetsyamānatvāt / tanna ahetuto bhāvāḥ svabhāvaṃ pratilabhante //
body.translated_text: Nor is the alternative 'from no cause' [tenable] — since this is not justified as a mere negation in the form of a simple denial. For if things were causeless, there would be the absurd consequence of the absence of restriction by place and time, or the absurd consequence of permanent existence or permanent non-existence. And there would be no undertaking of specifically determined means by those who desire specific results. Since causes such as <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and others will be refuted — therefore things do not obtain their intrinsic nature from no cause.

body.text: tasmānna svaparobhayarūpahetubhya utpadyante satsvabhāvā bhāvāḥ / taduktam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, things possessing real intrinsic nature do not arise from causes of the nature of self, other, or both. As stated —

children.text: na svato nāpi parato na dvābhyāṃ nāpyahetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not from itself, not from another, not from both, and not from no cause —

children.text: utpannā jātu vidyante bhāvāḥ kvacana kecana //
children.translated_text: nowhere are any things found to have ever arisen.'

body.text: iti / [ma. śā.1.3]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Madhyamakaśāstra</s> 1.3]

body.text: ekānekasvabhāvavicāraṇayāpi sarvabhāvānāṃ svabhāvavikalatvānna satsvabhāvatvam / tasmāt svapnamāyāpratibimbādivat idaṃpratyayatāmātrameva avicāramanoharamastu / kimiha sarvaduḥkhahetunā bhāvābhiniveśena prayojanam? ataḥ idamarthasya tattvam-
body.translated_text: Through the analysis of unity and multiplicity too, since all things are devoid of intrinsic nature, there is no possession of real intrinsic nature. Therefore, like a dream, an illusion, a reflection, and such, let there be mere conditionality alone — charming to the unexamining [mind]. What use is there here of clinging to things, which is the cause of all suffering? Therefore, this is the reality of things —

children.translated_text: 'These things are devoid of intrinsic nature in reality, whether spoken of as self or other,
because of separation from a nature of unity or multiplicity — like a reflection.'

body.text: madhyamakālaṃkārakārikā-1
body.translated_text: <s>Madhyamakālaṃkārakārikā</s> 1

body.text: evaṃ niḥsvabhāvataiva sarvabhāvānāṃ nijaṃ pāramārthikaṃ rūpamavatiṣṭhate / tadeva pradhānapuruṣārthatayā paramārthaḥ utkṛṣṭaṃ prayojanamabhidhīyate //
body.translated_text: Thus, the absence of intrinsic nature is the own, ultimate form of all entities. That itself, as being the primary human purpose, is called '<s>paramārtha</s>' (ultimate reality) — the supreme purpose. //

body.text: atrāpi nābhiniveṣṭavyam / anyathā bhāvābhiniveśo vā śūnyatābhiniveśo veti na kaścidviśeṣaḥ, ubhayorapi kalpanātmakatayā sāṃvṛtatvāt / na ca abhāvasya kalpitasvabhāvatayā kiṃcit svarūpamasti / na ca bhāvanivṛttirūpo 'bhāvaḥ, nivṛtterniḥsvabhāvatvāt / yadi ca bhāvasyaiva kaścit svabhāvaḥ syāt, tadā tatpratiṣedhātmā abhāvo 'pi syāt / bhāvasya tu svabhāvo nāstīti pratipāditameva / ato na bhāvanivṛttirūpaḥ abhāvo nāma kaścit / na ca bhāvābhāvayoruktakrameṇa asattve pratipādite tadubhayasaṃkīrṇātmatā saṃbhavati ubhayapratiṣedhasvabhāvatā vā, bhāvavikalpasyaiva sakalavikalpanibandhanatvāt / tasminnirākṛte sarva eva amī ekaprahāreṇa nirastā bhavantīti / tasmāt-
body.translated_text: One should not cling even to this. Otherwise, there is no distinction between clinging to existence and clinging to emptiness, since both are of the nature of conceptualization and hence conventional. Nor does non-existence have any own form, being of fabricated nature. Nor is non-existence in the form of the negation of existence, since negation is without intrinsic nature. If existence itself had some intrinsic nature, then non-existence — being the negation of that — would also exist. But it has been demonstrated that existence has no intrinsic nature. Therefore, there is no such thing as non-existence in the form of the negation of existence. And when the non-existence of both existence and non-existence has been demonstrated in the manner stated, neither a nature that is a mixture of both nor a nature that is the negation of both is possible — because the conceptualization of existence is the basis of all conceptualization. Once that is eliminated, all of these are dispatched in a single stroke. Therefore —

body.text: na sannāsanna sadasanna cāpyanubhayātmakam /
body.translated_text: Neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent, nor of the nature of neither —

body.text: kiṃcidabhiniveśaviṣayatayā mantavyam / taduktamāryaprajñāpāramitāyām-
body.translated_text: nothing whatsoever should be conceived as an object of clinging. As stated in the <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitā</s> —

body.text: subhūtirāha- ihāyuṣman śāradvatīputra bodhisattvayānikaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anupāyakuśalo rūpaṃ śūnyamiti prajānāti, saṅgaḥ / vedanāṃ śūnyāmiti saṃjānāti, saṅgaḥ / saṃjñāṃ śūnyāmiti saṃjānāti, saṅgaḥ / saṃskārān śūnyāniti saṃjānāti, saṅgaḥ / vijñānaṃ śūnyamiti saṃjānāti, saṅgaḥ / evaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ jivhā kāyo manaḥ, yāvat sarvadharmaśūnyatāṃ śūnyāmiti saṃjānāti, saṅgaḥ / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, if a son or daughter of good family who follows the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, being unskilled in means, cognizes form as empty — that is attachment. Cognizes feeling as empty — that is attachment. Cognizes perception as empty — that is attachment. Cognizes formations as empty — that is attachment. Cognizes consciousness as empty — that is attachment. Likewise, [cognizes] eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind [as empty], up to: cognizes the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> as empty — that is attachment.' Thus in detail. //

body.text: uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: And it is said —

children.translated_text: 'The teaching of emptiness as nectar is for the abandonment of all conceptualization;
but one who grasps even at that has been declared by You to be incurable.'

body.text: iti / [catuḥstavanirupama-21]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Catuḥstava</s>, <s>Nirupama</s> 21]

children.translated_text: 'Neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent, nor of the nature of neither —
free from the four extremes: this is reality as the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> know it.'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: evaṃ catuṣkoṭivinirmuktamādiśāntamanutpannāniruddhānucchedāśāśvatādisvabhāvatayā niṣprapañcatvādākāśavadāsaṅgānāmanāspadamaśeṣaṃ viśvamutpaśyāma iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, we perceive the entirety of the universe as free from the four extremes, primordially quiescent, unborn, unceased, free from elaboration due to its nature of being neither annihilated nor eternal and such — unattached like space, without foundation. //

body.text: satyadvayamidaṃ matamiti / kiṃ tat? saṃvṛtiḥ paramārthaśceti paścādyojanīyam / bhūtamiyaṃ brāhmaṇī, āvapanamiyaṃ muṣṭiketi yathā / saṃvṛtirekaṃ satyamaviparītam, paramārthaśca aparaṃ satyamiti / cakāraḥ satyatāmātreṇa tulyabalatāṃ samuccinoti / tatra saṃvṛtisatyamavitathaṃ rūpaṃ lokasya, paramārthasatyaṃ ca satyamavisaṃvādakaṃ tattvamāryāṇāmiti viśeṣaḥ / itthaṃ viśeṣopadarśanārtho 'pi yuktaścakāraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'This pair of truths is accepted' — what is that? '<s>Saṃvṛti</s> (conventional) and <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate)' — this is to be connected afterward. Just as [one says]: 'this <s>brāhmaṇī</s> is a real one' or 'this <s>muṣṭikā</s> is for sowing.' <s>Saṃvṛti</s> is one truth — non-erroneous; and <s>paramārtha</s> is another truth. The particle 'and' (<s>ca</s>) indicates equal force merely in terms of [being called] 'truth.' Therein, the distinction is: <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth) is the non-false form of the world; <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth) is the truth that does not deceive — the reality of the <s>Āryas</s> (Noble Ones). The particle 'and' is also fitting for the purpose of showing this distinction. //

body.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati- sarva eva amī ādhyātmikā bāhyāśca bhāvāḥ svabhāvadvayamābibhrataḥ samupajāyante yaduta sāṃvṛtaṃ pāramārthikaṃ ca / tatraikamavidyātimirāvṛtabuddhilocanānāmabhūtārthadarśināṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ mṛṣādarśanaviṣayatayā samādarśitātmasattākam / anyat pravicayāñjanaśalākoddhātitāvidyāpaṭalasamyagjñānanayanānāṃ tattvavidāmāryāṇāṃ samyagdarśanaviṣayatayā upasthitasvarūpam / tadetat svabhāvadvayaṃ sarve padārthā dhārayanti / anayośca svabhāvayormṛṣādṛśāṃ bāliśānāṃ yo viṣayaḥ, tat saṃvṛtisatyam / yaśca samyagdṛśāmadhigatatattvānāṃ viṣayaḥ, tat paramārthasatyamiti vyavasthā śāstravidām / yadāha-
body.translated_text: What is stated is this: all these entities, both internal and external, arise bearing a twofold nature — namely, conventional and ultimate. Of these, one is the existence displayed through false seeing by ordinary beings whose eye of intelligence is veiled by the darkness of ignorance, who perceive what is unreal. The other is the own form presented through correct seeing — the domain of correct vision of the <s>Āryas</s>, the knowers of reality, whose eye of correct knowledge has had the film of ignorance removed by the collyrium-stick of discernment. All things bear this twofold nature. And of these two natures, that which is the domain of the childish who see falsely — that is <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth). That which is the domain of those who see correctly, who have realized reality — that is <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth): this is the determination of the knowers of the treatises. As is said —

children.translated_text: 'All entities bear a twofold form, obtained through correct and false seeing;

children.text: samyagdṛśāṃ yo viṣayaḥ sa tattvaṃ mṛṣādṛśāṃ saṃvṛtisatyamuktam //
children.translated_text: that which is the domain of those who see correctly is reality; that of those who see falsely is called <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth).'

body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> 6.23]

body.text: iti dvayoḥ samudāyo dvayamiti yujyate / matamiti saṃmatamabhimatam / keṣām? prahīṇāvaraṇadhiyāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatām, tanmārgānuyāyināmāryaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ ca / idameva satyadvayaṃ nānyat satyamastīti avadhāraṇārtho 'pi yujyate cakāraḥ / taduktam-
body.translated_text: 'The pair' — the collection of the two — is '<s>dvaya</s>' (pair): this is fitting. 'Accepted' — acknowledged, affirmed. By whom? By the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> whose intelligence has abandoned all obscurations, and by the <s>Ārya</s> <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who follow their path. The particle 'and' is also fitting in the sense of exclusion: this pair of truths alone and no other truth exists. As is said —

children.translated_text: 'The teaching of <s>Dharma</s> by the <s>Buddhas</s> relies upon two truths:
the truth of worldly convention and truth from the standpoint of ultimate reality.'

body.text: iti / [ma. śā.-24.8]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Madhyamakaśāstra</s> 24.8]

body.text: pitāputrasamāgame coktam-
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Pitāputrasamāgama</s> it is said —

children.text: satya ime duvi lokavidūnāṃ diṣṭa svayaṃ aśruṇitva pareṣām /
children.translated_text: 'These two truths of the knowers of the world were proclaimed by him, not heard from others:

children.text: saṃvṛti yā ca tathā paramārtho satyu na sidhyati kiṃ ca tṛtīyu //
children.translated_text: the conventional and likewise the ultimate — and no third truth is possible.'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: nanu catvāri āryasatyāni duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgalakṣaṇāni abhidharme kathitāni bhagavatā, tat kathaṃ dve eva satye iti? satyam, kiṃ tarhi vaineyajanāśayānuśayavaśādete dve eva catvāri kṛtvā kathitāni (kathite?), amīṣāṃ dvayorevāntarbhāvāt / tathā hi duḥkhasamudayamārgasatyāni saṃvṛtisvabhāvatayā saṃvṛtisatye 'ntarbhavanti, nirodhasatyaṃ tu paramārthasatye, iti na kaścidvirodhaḥ //
body.translated_text: But the Blessed One spoke of four <s>Āryasatyas</s> (Noble Truths) — characterized by suffering, origin, cessation, and path — in the <s>Abhidharma</s>. How then are there only two truths? True, but these two were taught as four in accordance with the dispositions and latent tendencies of those to be guided, since they are included within these two. For suffering, origin, and path — these truths are included within <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> because of being of conventional nature; but the truth of cessation is included within <s>paramārthasatya</s>. Thus there is no contradiction. //

body.text: syādetat- saṃvṛtiravidyopadarśitātmatayā abhūtasamāropasvarūpatvādvicārāt śataśo viśīryamāṇāpi kathaṃ satyamiti / etadapi satyam / kiṃ tu lokādhyavasāyataḥ saṃvṛtisatyamityucyate / loka eva hi saṃvṛtisatyamiha pratipannaḥ / tadanuvṛttyā bhagavadbhirapi tathaiva anapekṣitatattvārthibhiḥ saṃvṛtisatyamucyate / ata eva lokasaṃvṛtisatyaṃ ceti śāstre 'pi viśeṣa ukta ācāryapādaiḥ / vastutastu paramārtha eva ekaṃ satyam, ato na kācit kṣatiriti / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: One might object: <s>saṃvṛti</s>, being displayed by ignorance and being of the nature of false superimposition, disintegrates in a hundred ways under analysis — how can it be called 'truth'? This too is true. However, it is called '<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>' from the standpoint of worldly determination. For it is the world itself that has understood <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> here. In conformity with that, even the Blessed Ones, not themselves seeking the ultimate, speak of <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> in just the same way. For this very reason, the Master [<s>Nāgārjuna</s>] has specified the qualifier 'worldly' (<s>loka</s>) even in the treatise, [calling it] '<s>lokasaṃvṛtisatya</s>.' But in reality, the ultimate alone is the one truth — so there is no fault. As stated by the Blessed One —

body.text: ekameva bhikṣavaḥ paramaṃ satyaṃ yaduta apramoṣadharma nirvāṇam, sarvasaṃskārāśca mṛṣā moṣadharmāṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'There is, O monks, only one supreme truth — namely, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, which is of non-deceptive nature. All conditioned things are false, of deceptive nature.'

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: satyadvayamidamuktam / tatra avidyopaplutacetasāṃ tatsvabhāvatayā saṃvṛtisatyamiti pratītam / paramārthasatyaṃ tu na jñāyate kīdṛk kiṃsvabhāvaṃ kiṃlakṣaṇamiti / ato vaktavyaṃ tatsvarūpamityāha buddheragocarastattvamiti / buddheḥ sarvajñānānām, samatikrāntasarvajñānaviṣayatvādagocaraḥ aviṣayaḥ / kenacit prakāreṇa tat sarvabuddhiviṣayīkartuṃ na śakyate iti yāvat / iti kathaṃ tatsvarūpaṃ pratipādayituṃ śakyam? tathā hi sarvaprapañcavinirmuktasvabhāvaṃ paramārthasatyatattvam, ataḥ sarvopādhiśūnyatvāt kathaṃ kayācit kalpanayā paśyet? kalpanāsamatikrāntasvarūpaṃ ca śabdānāmaviṣayaḥ / vikalpajanmāno hi śabdā vikalpadhiyāmaviṣaye na pravartitumutsahante /
