The form <s>upaśāmayet</s> [with short vowel], while observing the Vedic convention, was not shortened in the <s>ṇic</s> causative after the prefix <s>upa</s> — because the rules preceded by designations are non-eternal; or [this can be explained otherwise].

body.text: evaṃ dṛṣṭāntamupapādya dārṣṭāntike yojayannāha bodhicaryeti-
body.translated_text: Having thus established the example, connecting it to the thing exemplified, he says 'the conduct for awakening' —

children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>Jina</s>-pillar too, empowered through conduct befitting awakening,
accomplishes all purposes even when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 9.38 //

body.text: yathāśabdastathetyākarṣayati / tathā bodhau bodhinimittaṃ buddhatvārthaṃ caryā [bodhicaryā] / bodhisattve 'pi nirvṛte iti, bodhiḥ buddhatvam, ekānekasvabhāvaviviktamanutpannāniruddhamanucchedamaśāśvataṃ sarvaprapañcavinirmuktamākāśapratisamaṃ dharmakāyākhyaṃ paramārthatattvamucyate / etadeva ca prajñāpāramitāśūnyatātathatābhūtakoṭidharmadhātvādiśabdena saṃvṛtimupādāya abhidhīyate / idameva ca abhisaṃdhāyoktam-
body.translated_text: The word 'just as' [from the previous verse] is carried forward as 'likewise.' Conduct for <s>bodhi</s> — conduct for the purpose of awakening, for <s>Buddhahood</s> — is the <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct for awakening). 'Even when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — here, <s>bodhi</s> means <s>Buddhahood</s>: free from the nature of unity or multiplicity, unarisen and unceased, neither annihilated nor eternal, liberated from all conceptual elaboration, equal to space — the ultimate reality called the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. And this very [reality] is designated conventionally by the terms <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality), <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the expanse of <s>dharmas</s>), and such. And it is with this very [reality] in mind that it is stated —

children.text: dharmato buddhā draṣṭavyā dharmakāyā hi nāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Buddhas</s> should be seen from [their] <s>Dharma</s> [nature], for the guides have the <s>Dharmakāya</s>;

children.text: dharmatā cāpyavijñeyā na sā śakyā vijānitum //
children.translated_text: and the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of things) is unknowable — it cannot be known.'

body.text: iti / [vajracchedikā-26]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Vajracchedikā</s> 26]

body.text: uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: And it is said —

children.translated_text: 'Without marks, unarisen, unconditioned, inexpressible —
space, <s>bodhicitta</s>, and <s>bodhi</s> have the characteristic of non-duality.'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tatra [bodhiḥ] sattvamabhiprāyo 'syeti bodhisattvaḥ / tasminnirvṛte 'pi / apiśabdo bhinnakramaḥ / apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇatvena paramāṃ śāntiṃ gate 'pi / hetvavasthānivṛttau phalāvasthāprāptau cetyarthaḥ / iti ubhayathāpi sarvathā kalpanāvirahe 'pi sattvārthasaṃpādanamavikalamupadarśitaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: There, [in 'Bodhisattva':] <s>bodhi</s> is that whose intention (<s>sattva</s>) is — thus a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Even when he has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The word 'even' is in a displaced sequence. Even when he has attained the supreme peace through non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The meaning is: when the state of the cause has ceased and the state of the fruit has been attained. Thus, in both ways, it has been shown that even with the complete absence of conceptualization in every respect, the accomplishment of the welfare of beings is unimpaired.

body.text: syādetat- yadi bhagavānuparatasakalavikalpālambanatayā nivṛttasarvacittacaittavyāpāraḥ, kathaṃ tarhi tathāgatapūjā mahāphalā varṇyate ityāśaṅkayannāha acittake ityādi-
body.translated_text: [Objection:] If the Blessed One has ceased all conceptual engagement and all operations of mind and mental factors, how then is the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> described as having great fruit? — anticipating this, he says 'toward one without mind' and so forth —

body.text: acittake kṛtā pūjā kathaṃ phalavatī bhavet /
body.translated_text: How could worship offered to one without mind be fruitful?

body.text: saṃvṛticittavivikte bhagavati kṛtā upahṛtā pūjā kārāviśeṣaḥ kathaṃ phalavatī bhavet, saphalā syāt? tatra asatyupabhoktari dāyakadānapatīnāṃ kathaṃ puṇyaṃ bhavet? atrottaramāha tulyaivetyādi-
body.translated_text: How could worship — a particular ritual act — offered to, presented before the Blessed One who is free from conventional mind be fruitful, bear fruit? When there is no one to enjoy [the offering], how would there be merit for the donors and patrons? The answer to this he states 'it is taught as equal' and so forth —

body.text: tulyaiva paṭhyate yasmāttiṣṭhato nirvṛtasya ca // Bca_9.39 //
body.translated_text: Because it is taught as equal, whether [the <s>Buddha</s>] is abiding or has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // <s>Bca</s> 9.39 //

body.text: tulyaiva samaiva / paṭhyate āgame pratipādyate / yasmāt tiṣṭhato nirvṛtasya ca tasmāt phalavatī bhavediti yojanīyam / tiṣṭhato 'parinirvṛtasya / nirvṛtasya nirupadhinirvāṇaṃ gatasya pūjāyā nāsti viśeṣaḥ / ayamabhiprāyaḥ- dvividhaṃ hi puṇyam- tyāgānvayaṃ ca, tyāgādeva yadutpadyate / paribhogānvayaṃ ca, deyadharmaparibhogād yadutpadyate / tatra yadi nāma nirvṛte bhagavati pratigrahīturabhāvāt paribhogānvayaṃ na bhaviṣyati puṇyam, parityāgānvayaṃ ca kena vāryate? apratigṛhṇati kasmiṃścit kathaṃ parityāgānvayamapi puṇyam? kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ sati pratigrahītari bhavitavyaṃ puṇyena, nāsati? kasyacidapyabhāvāditi cet, idamakāraṇameva / yadi hi puṇyaṃ parānugrahādeva syāt, maitryādyapramāṇasamyagdṛṣṭibhāvanāyāṃ na syāt / tasmāt draṣṭavyaṃ svacittaprabhavaṃ parānugrahamantareṇāpi puṇyam / tathā vyatīte 'pi guṇavati tadbhaktikṛtaṃ svacittādbhavat puṇyaṃ na virudhyate iti //
body.translated_text: 'Equal' — the same. 'Is taught' — is set forth in scripture. Because it is equal whether the [<s>Buddha</s>] is 'abiding' — not having passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — or 'has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — having gone to <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder — there is no distinction in the worship. Therefore it would be fruitful: this is how it should be construed. The intention is this: merit is twofold — that connected with renunciation, which arises from the act of giving itself; and that connected with enjoyment, which arises from the recipient's enjoyment of the gift. Among these, even if, when the Blessed One has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, there will be no merit connected with enjoyment due to the absence of a recipient — who prevents the merit connected with renunciation? [Objection:] When someone does not accept [the offering], how can there be merit connected with renunciation? What is the reason that merit must depend on the existence of a recipient and not [arise] in its absence? If [one says] because of the absence of anyone [to receive] — this is no reason at all. For if merit arose only from benefiting others, it would not arise from the cultivation of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the other immeasurables, or from the cultivation of right view. Therefore, it should be recognized that merit arises from one's own mind, even without benefiting another. Likewise, even regarding a virtuous one who has passed away, merit arising from devotion to him, produced from one's own mind, is not contradicted.

body.text:
api ca sarvapuṇyapāpasadbhāve sarveṣāmāgamaḥ sākṣītyāha āgamāccetyādi-
āgamācca phalaṃ tatra saṃvṛtyā tattvato 'pi vā /
body.translated_text: Moreover, scripture is witness to the real existence of all merit and demerit — he says 'from scripture too' and so forth — 'From scripture too, there is a fruit there — conventionally or ultimately.'

body.text:
kimatra upapattyantareṇa? āgamāt bhagavatpravacanāt phalaṃ bhagavatpūjākṛtaṃ mahābhogatādilakṣaṇamavagamyate / tatreti nirvṛtānirvṛte bhagavati pūjāyām / etāvāṃstu viśeṣaḥ- kasyacit tat phalaṃ sāṃvṛtam, kasyacit punaḥ pāramārthikamabhimatam / evamanantaravicāramanādṛtya viśeṣeṇocyate / saṃvṛtyā tattvato 'pi vā puṇyapāpakriyāyāḥ phalaṃ bhagavadāgamāt pratīyate, tatra ca āvayoravivāda eva tatra idamuktaṃ bhagavatā puṣpakūṭadhāraṇyām-
ye kecit siṃhavikrīḍita tathāgatasya pūjāṃ kariṣyanti tiṣṭhato vā parinirvṛtasya vā, sarve te triyānādekatareṇa yānena parinirvāsyanti / yaśca khalu siṃhavikrīḍita tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ prasādayet, prasannacittaḥ satkuryāt gurukuryāt mānayet pūjayet upacaret, lābhena cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvasukhopadhānairupatiṣṭhet / yaśca parinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya sarṣapaphalamātradhātau śarīrapūjāṃ kuryāt, samo vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ / tathā pūjāyai nāsti viśeṣo nānākaraṇaṃ ca / iti //
body.translated_text: What need here for a different justification? From scripture — from the Blessed One's teaching — the fruit of worship of the Blessed One is understood as characterized by great enjoyment and such. 'There' — in worship of the Blessed One whether he has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s> or not. But there is this much distinction: for some, that fruit is considered conventional; for others, ultimate. Thus, without regard to the immediately preceding investigation, it is stated with special emphasis. Conventionally or ultimately, the fruit of the activity of merit and demerit is understood from the Blessed One's scripture; and regarding that, there is simply no disagreement between us. Regarding this, the Blessed One stated in the <s>Puṣpakūṭadhāraṇī</s> — 'Whoever, <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s>, will worship the <s>Tathāgata</s>, whether abiding or having passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, all of them will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through one of the three vehicles. And indeed, <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s>, whoever, having seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, would generate faith in the mind, and with a faithful mind would honor, revere, respect, worship, and serve [him], and would attend to [him] with material offerings — robes, almsfood, bedding, and medicines for the sick — with all provisions of happiness; and whoever would perform worship of the relics, even of a mustard-seed-sized portion of the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — an equal ripening is to be expected. Likewise, in the worship, there is no distinction, no differentiation.'

body.text: uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: And it is said —

children.translated_text: 'Whoever would worship [the <s>Buddha</s>] while abiding, and whoever [would worship him having] passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,
with equal faith of mind, there is no distinction in merit.'

body.text: iti / [divyā]
body.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Divyāvadāna</s>]

body.text: punaridamuktam-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, this is stated —

body.text: yaśca khalu punaḥ siṃhavikrīḍita tathāgataṃ varṣaśataṃ vā varṣasahasraṃ vā sarvasukhopadhānenopatiṣṭhet, yaśca parinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya caitye bodhicittaparigṛhītaikapuṣpamāropayet, tathāgatapūjāyai jalāñjaliṃ copanāmayet, jalena copasiñcet, īṣikāpadaṃ vā dadyāt, nirmālyaṃ vā apanayet, upalepanapradānaṃ vā dīpapradānaṃ vā kuryāt, āttamanāḥ, ekakramapadavyatihāraṃ vā atikramya vācaṃ bhāṣeta- namastamai buddhāya bhagavate iti, mā te atra siṃhavikrīḍita kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā, yadasau kalpaṃ vā kalpaśataṃ vā kalpasahasraṃ vā durgativinipātaṃ gacchet, nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate // iti /
body.translated_text: 'And indeed, <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s>, whoever would attend to the <s>Tathāgata</s> for a hundred years or a thousand years with all provisions of happiness; and whoever would place upon a <s>caitya</s> (stūpa) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> a single flower accompanied by <s>bodhicitta</s>, or offer a handful of water for the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or sprinkle with water, or offer a blade of grass, or remove a withered [flower], or offer a smearing of plaster or a lamp offering — being delighted — or, taking a single step, cross over and speak the words: "Homage to that <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One" — do not, <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s>, have doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation about this: that such a one would go to a lower realm of misfortune for a <s>kalpa</s>, or a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, or a thousand <s>kalpas</s> — this situation does not exist.'

body.text: etadavaśyamabhyupeyamiti [āha] satyabuddhe ityādi-

children.text: satyabuddhe kṛtā pūjā saphaleti kathaṃ yathā // Bca_9.40 //
children.translated_text: How, in the same way, is worship offered to a real <s>Buddha</s> fruitful? // <s>Bca</s> 9.40 //

body.translated_text: This must necessarily be accepted — he says 'in a real <s>Buddha</s>' and so forth —

body.text: satyabuddhe paramārthasati bhagavati kṛtā pūjā saphaleti phalavatī, ityetadapi kathaṃ yatheti / kathamivetyudāharaṇamupadarśayati / nānyadatrodāharaṇamāgamāditi bhāvaḥ / tasmāt sarvathā bhagavatpūjāyāṃ phalasadbhāva āgamādavagamyate //
body.translated_text: 'In a real <s>Buddha</s>' — in the Blessed One who is real in the ultimate sense — how, in the same way, is worship offered fruitful, bearing fruit? 'How, in the same way' — he shows as if [asking for] an example. The meaning is: there is no other example here apart from scripture. Therefore, in every way, the real existence of the fruit of worship of the Blessed One is understood from scripture.

body.text: śūnyatāvāsanādhānādityādi yaduktam, tatra vaibhāṣikādayaḥ sarvadharmaśūnyatāyāḥ sarvāvaraṇaprahāṇamasahamānāḥ caturāryasatyadarśanabhāvanāṃ ca tadupāyamicchantaḥ prāhuḥ satyadarśanata ityādi-
body.translated_text: Regarding the statement 'through depositing the habitual tendencies of emptiness' and so forth — the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> and others, being unable to bear the abandonment of all obscurations through the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, and desiring the seeing and cultivation of the four noble truths as the means for that, say 'from seeing the truths' and so forth —

body.text: satyadarśanato muktiḥ śūnyatādarśanena kim /
body.translated_text: Liberation comes from seeing the truths — what use is seeing emptiness?

body.text: caturṇāmāryasatyānāṃ duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgalakṣaṇānāṃ darśanataḥ upalabdhitaḥ / sākṣātkaraṇādityarthaḥ / darśanata ityupalakṣaṇam / bhāvanāto 'pi draṣṭavyam / taduktam-
body.translated_text: From the seeing — the apprehension, the direct realization — of the four noble truths characterized by suffering, origination, cessation, and path. 'From seeing' is indicative; 'from cultivation' should also be understood. As stated —

body.text: kleśaprahāṇamākhyātaṃ satyadarśanabhāvanāt /

children.translated_text: Thus. [<s>Abhidharmakośa</s> 6.1]

body.translated_text: 'The abandonment of afflictions has been declared to be from the seeing and cultivation of the truths.'

body.text: tatra vṛttasthasya śrutacintāvato bhāvanāyāṃ pravṛttasya aśubhānāpānasmṛtismṛtyupasthānabhāvanā niṣpattikrameṇa anityato duḥkhata śūnyato 'nātmataśca ityetaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirākāraiḥ duḥkhādisatyaṃ paśyataḥ uṣmagatādicaturnirvedhabhāgīyadvāreṇa duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntyādipañcadaśakṣaṇalakṣaṇasya darśanamārgasya, tataḥ paraṃ bhāvanāmārgasyādhigamāt, darśanabhāvanāheyatraidhātukakleśopakleśarāśiprahāṇāt kṣayānutpādajñānotpattirityāryasatyeṣu saṃkṣepato 'bhisamayakramaḥ / itthamāryasatyadarśanato muktirucyate / tasmādata eva muktirastu, śūnyatādarśanena kim, śūnyatāyāḥ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāyā
body.translated_text: There, for one who is established in moral discipline, who possesses hearing and reflection, and has engaged in meditation — through the progressive accomplishment of the meditation on impurity, <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing), and the foundations of mindfulness — seeing the truth of suffering and such through these sixteen aspects: as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, and as non-self — through the gateway of the four aids to penetration beginning with heat and such, through the attainment of the path of seeing characterized by fifteen moments beginning with <s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>kṣānti</s> (patience for knowledge of <s>dharma</s>) regarding suffering, and thereafter through the attainment of the path of cultivation — through the abandonment of the mass of afflictions and secondary afflictions of the three realms that are to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation — the production of the knowledge of destruction and non-arising [occurs]. This, in brief, is the sequence of realization regarding the noble truths. In this way, liberation is said to come from seeing the noble truths. Therefore, let liberation be from this alone — what use is seeing emptiness, the lack of intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>

body.text: darśanena adhigamena / sākṣātkaraṇeneti yāvat / kim? na kiṃcit prayojanam / tadaparasya mukterupāyasya vidyamānatvāt / atrāha na vinetyādi-
body.translated_text: — from its attainment, from its direct realization? What use? No purpose whatsoever — because another means of liberation exists. To this he says 'not without this path' and so forth —

body.text: na vinānena mārgeṇa bodhirityāgamo yataḥ // Bca_9.41 //
body.translated_text: Because scripture declares that there is no awakening without this path. // <s>Bca</s> 9.41 //

body.text: na upāyāntaramasti, tasmādityarthaḥ / idaṃ mahārthasya tattvam / tathā hi- sarva eva hi bhāvā āropitamanāropitaṃ ceti rūpadvayamudvahanti / tatra yat tadavidyāpravāhitamāropitaṃ rūpam, tat sarvajanasādhāraṇamiti na tadupalabdheḥ saṃkleśaprahāṇamupapadyate / anyathā sarve bālajanāstathāgatāḥ syuriti prācīnaprasaṅgaḥ / iti anāropitameva tattvamanupalambhayogena adhigamyamānamajñānāsravakṣayāya sāmarthyavadupalabhyate / tacca prajñayā vivecyamānaṃ sarvadharmānupalambhalakṣaṇamavasitamiti sarvadharmaśūnyataiva sarvāvaraṇavibhramaprahāṇāya paṭīyasītyavagamyate / iti yuktito nirūpitaṃ prāk, nirupayiṣyate ca paścāt / iha punarāgamata eva enamarthamavagrāhayitum-
body.translated_text: There is no other means — therefore: this is the meaning. This is the truth of a great matter. For all things carry two forms — the superimposed and the non-superimposed. Of these, the superimposed form set in motion by ignorance, being common to all people — from its apprehension, the abandonment of affliction is not possible. Otherwise, all ordinary people would be <s>Tathāgatas</s> — this is the previously stated absurd consequence. Therefore, it is the non-superimposed reality alone — being realized through the yoga of non-apprehension — that is found to have the power to destroy the outflows of ignorance. And that, when analyzed by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), arrives at the characteristic of non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus it is understood that the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> alone is most effective for the abandonment of all obscurations and confusions. This has been established through reasoning previously and will be established afterward. But here, in order to make this point understood through scripture alone —

body.text: na vinānena mārgeṇa bodhirityāgamo yataḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Because scripture declares that there is no awakening without this path'

body.text: ityuktavān / yaduktaṃ prajñāpāramitāyām-
body.translated_text: — thus he has said. As stated in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> —

body.text: bhagavānāha- iha subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran rūpaṃ bhāva iti na bhāvayati / vedanāṃ bhāva iti na bhāvayati / saṃjñāṃ bhāva iti na bhāvayati / saṃskārān bhāva iti na bhāvayati / yāvat mārgākārajñatāṃ bhāva iti na bhāvayati / yāvat sarvākārajñatāṃ bhāva iti na bhāvayati / sarvavāsanānusaṃdhikleśaprahāṇaṃ bhāva iti na bhāvayati / tatkasya hetoḥ? nāsti bhāvasaṃjñinaḥ prajñāpāramitābhāvanā / yāvat nāsti bhāvasaṃjñino dānapāramitābhāvanā / nāsti bhāvasaṃjñino 'bhāvaśūnyatābhāvanā / nāsti bhāvasaṃjñinaḥ ṣaḍabhijñābhāvanā / yāvat nāsti sarvasamādhisarvadhāraṇīmukhatathāgatabalavaiśāradyapratisaṃvinmahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāveṇikabuddhadharmāṇāṃ bhāvanā / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi sa bhāvaḥ eṣo 'hamiti dvayorantayoḥ saktaḥ / dāne śīle kṣāntau vīrye dhyāne prajñāyām / eṣo 'hamiti dvayorantayoḥ saktaḥ / yaśca dvayorantayoḥ saktaḥ, tasya nāsti mokṣaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? nāsti subhūte bhāvasaṃjñino dānam, yāvat nāsti prajñā, nāsti mārgaḥ, nāsti jñānam, nāsti prāptiḥ, nāsti abhisamayaḥ, nāstyānulomikī kṣāntiḥ, nāsti rūpasya parijñā, nāsti vedanāyāḥ parijñā, yāvat nāsti pratītyasamutpādasya parijñā / nāsti ātmasattvajīvajantupoṣapudgalanujamānavakārakavedakajānakapaśyakasaṃjñāyāḥ parijñā / yāvat nāsti sarvavāsanānusaṃdhikleśaprahāṇasya parijñā / kutaḥ punarasya mokṣo bhaviṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not cultivate form as a real entity. He does not cultivate feeling as a real entity. He does not cultivate perception as a real entity. He does not cultivate formations as a real entity. Up to: he does not cultivate knowledge of the aspects of the path as a real entity. Up to: he does not cultivate knowledge of all aspects as a real entity. He does not cultivate the abandonment of all afflictions connected with latent impressions as a real entity. What is the reason? There is no cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for one who has the perception of a real entity. Up to: there is no cultivation of <s>Dānapāramitā</s> for one who has the perception of a real entity. There is no cultivation of emptiness of non-existence for one who has the perception of a real entity. There is no cultivation of the six superknowledges for one who has the perception of a real entity. Up to: there is no cultivation of all <s>samādhis</s>, all <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gateways, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, great <s>maitrī</s>, great <s>karuṇā</s>, and the distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. What is the reason? For that entity is attached to both extremes — [thinking] "this is I" — regarding generosity, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom — [thinking] "this is I" — attached to both extremes. And for one attached to both extremes, there is no liberation. What is the reason? <s>Subhūti</s>, for one who has the perception of a real entity, there is no generosity, up to: there is no wisdom, there is no path, there is no knowledge, there is no attainment, there is no realization, there is no <s>anulomikī kṣānti</s> (conformity patience), there is no full understanding of form, there is no full understanding of feeling, up to: there is no full understanding of dependent origination. There is no full understanding of the perception of self, being, living being, creature, nurturer, person, human, descendant of <s>Manu</s>, agent, experiencer, knower, and seer. Up to: there is no full understanding of the abandonment of all afflictions connected with latent impressions. From where then would his liberation come?'

body.text: ata eva punastatraivoktam-
body.translated_text: For this very reason, it is further stated there [in the same text] —

body.text: bhagavānāha- evametat kauśika, evametat / ye 'pi te 'bhūvannatīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, te 'pi imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Just so, <s>Kauśika</s>, just so! Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who existed in the past — they too, having relied upon this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

body.text: ye 'pi te bhaviṣyanti anāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, te 'pi imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / ye 'pi te etarhi daśadiglokadhātuṣu aprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāstiṣṭhanti, dhriyante yāpayanti dharmaṃ deśayanti, te 'pi imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ / ye 'pi te 'bhūvannatītānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ śrāvakāḥ, ye 'pi te bhaviṣyanti anāgatānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ śrāvakāḥ, ye 'pi te etarhi pratyutpannānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ śrāvakāḥ, te 'pi imāmeva prajñāpāramitāmāgamya pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ, prāpsyanti prāpnuvanti ca / tatkasya hetoḥ? atra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sarvāṇi trīṇi yānāni vistareṇopadiṣṭāni / tāni punaranimittayogena anupalambhayogena anutpādayogena asaṃkleśayogena avyavadānayogena, yāvat tatpunaḥ lokavyavahāreṇa aparamārthayogena / iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who will exist in the future — they too, having relied upon this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who now abide, sustain, maintain, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> in immeasurable, incalculable world-systems in the ten directions — they too, having relied upon this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Those who were disciples of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past; those who will be disciples of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the future; and those who are presently disciples of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the present — they too, having relied upon this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, have attained, will attain, and are attaining individual awakening (<s>Pratyekabodhi</s>). What is the reason? In this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all three vehicles are taught in detail. These [vehicles are taught], moreover, through the yoga of the signless, the yoga of non-apprehension, the yoga of non-arising, the yoga of non-affliction, the yoga of non-purification, and so forth — and again, through worldly convention, not through the yoga of the ultimate.' Thus in detail.

body.text: uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: And it is said —

children.translated_text: 'Practiced by the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>,
you are the one path to liberation; there is no other — this is certain.'

body.text: iti // [prajñāpāramitāstutiḥ]
body.translated_text: Thus. [Praise of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]

body.text: etanmahāyānavacanamasahamāna āha nanvasiddhamityādi-
body.translated_text: Unable to accept this <s>Mahāyāna</s> teaching, [the opponent] says with 'is not the <s>Mahāyāna</s> unestablished' and so forth —

body.text: nanvasiddhaṃ mahāyānaṃ
body.translated_text: Is not the <s>Mahāyāna</s> unestablished?

body.text: nanu bhoḥ śūnyatāvādin, mahāyānamāgamatvena mama asiddham, asaṃmatam, tadasyopanyāso na sādhanatayā sādhuḥ / atra parasya samānaparihāradūṣaṇamāha kathamityādinā-
body.translated_text: 'O proponent of emptiness, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, as scripture, is unestablished for me, not accepted — therefore its citation is not valid as proof.' To this, the proponent of the system states an equal counter-objection, saying with 'how' and so forth —

body.text: kathaṃ siddhastvadāgamaḥ /
body.translated_text: How is your scripture established?

body.text: yadi mahāyānamasiddham, kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa tvadīyāgamo bhagavadvacanamiti siddhaḥ? tatra na kiṃcidāgamatvaprasādhakaṃ pramāṇamutpaśyāmaḥ / paraḥ parihāramāha yasmāditi-
body.translated_text: If the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is unestablished, how — in what way — is your own scripture established as the word of the Blessed One? We do not see any valid cognition that could establish it as scripture. The opponent states a resolution, saying with 'because' and so forth —

body.text: yasmādubhayasiddho 'sau
body.translated_text: Because it is established by both.

body.text: yasmāt kāraṇāt ubhayasya tava mama ca siddhaḥ āgamatvena niścito 'sau mamāgamaḥ / na hi madāgame bhavato 'pi mahāyānānuyāyino buddhavacanatvena vipratipattirasti, tasmāt siddho 'sau / na tu mahāyāne mama saṃpratipattiḥ, yena idamevottaraṃ bhavato 'pi syāt / siddhāntavādī āha-
body.translated_text: 'Because' — for the reason that — it is established by both, by you and by me — 'that scripture of mine is determined as scripture.' For regarding my scripture, even you who follow the <s>Mahāyāna</s> have no disagreement that it is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>; therefore it is established. But I have no agreement regarding the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, such that this same answer would apply to you as well. The proponent of the system says —

body.text: na siddhau'sau tavāditaḥ // Bca_9.42 //
body.translated_text: It was not established for you from the beginning. // <s>Bca</s> 9.42 //

body.text: iti / yadyapi ubhayasiddhatvaṃ tvadāgamasya āgamasiddhau hetuḥ, tadāpi naitadvaktavyam, asiddhatvāt / yasmāt tavaiva tāvadasau tvadāgamaḥ na siddhaḥ / kadā? ādau tatsvīkārāt pūrvam / na hi abhyupagamāt prāk tava kathaṃcidapyasau siddhaḥ, iti ubhayasiddhatvamasiddhatvādasādhanam //
body.translated_text: Thus. Even though the mutual establishment of your scripture is a reason for establishing it as scripture, still this should not be said, because it is unestablished. Because that scripture of yours was simply not established for you. When? From the beginning — prior to accepting it. For prior to your acceptance, it was in no way established for you, and therefore the mutual establishment is unestablished as a proof, due to being unestablished [as a premise].

body.text: yadyapi ubhayasiddhatvamasiddham, idaṃ tarhi sādhanamastu- yad guruśiṣyaparaṃparayā āmrāyāyātaṃ buddhavacanatvena, yacca sūtre 'vatarati, vinaye saṃdṛśyate, dharmatāṃ [pratītyasamutpādaṃ] ca na vilomayati, tad buddhavacanaṃ nānyat / ityatrāha yatpratyayetyādi-
body.translated_text: Even if the mutual establishment is unestablished, let this then be the proof: what has come down through the succession of teacher and disciple as the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, and what accords with the <s>sūtras</s>, is consistent with the <s>Vinaya</s>, and does not contradict reality [i.e., dependent origination] — that is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, not otherwise. To this he says with 'whatever reason' and so forth —

body.text: yatpratyayā ca tatrāsthā mahāyāne 'pi tāṃ kuru /
body.translated_text: Whatever reason you have for confidence in that [scripture], apply it to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> as well.

body.text: yaḥ pratyayo nibandhanam asyā āsthāyāḥ, sā tathoktā / yatpratyayā yannibandhanā / āsthā ādeyatā ādaraḥ / tatra svāgame / tāṃ tatpratyayāmāsthām iha mahāyāne 'pi kuru vidhehi / mahāyāne 'pi uktasya āsthākāraṇasya vidyamānatvāt / idaṃ punaḥ sarvapravacanasādhāraṇamavyabhicāri lakṣaṇaṃ yaduktamadhyāśayasaṃcodanasūtre-
body.translated_text: The reason — the ground — for this confidence is such: thus it is so called. 'Whatever reason' — whatever ground. 'Confidence' — acceptance, respect. 'In that' — in your own scripture. 'Apply' — establish — that same confidence grounded in that reason, here in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> as well. Because the stated reason for confidence exists in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> as well. And this is the universal, unfailing criterion common to all teachings, as stated in the <s>Adhyāśayasaṃcodanasūtra</s> —

body.text: api tu maitreya caturbhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ pratibhānaṃ sarvabuddhabhāṣitaṃ veditavyam / katamaiścaturbhiḥ? iha maitreya pratibhānamarthopasaṃhitaṃ bhavati nānarthopasaṃhitam / dharmopasaṃhitaṃ bhavati nādharmopasaṃhitam / kleśaprahāyakaṃ bhavati na kleśavivardhakam / nirvāṇaguṇānuśaṃsasaṃdarśakaṃ bhavati na saṃsāraguṇānuśaṃsasaṃdarśakam / etaiścaturbhiḥ / peyālaṃ / yasya kasyacinmaitreya etaiścaturbhiḥ pratibhāti pratibhāsyati vā, tatra śrāddhaiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhirvā buddhasaṃjñā utpādayitavyā / śāstṛsaṃjñāṃ kṛtvā sa dharmaḥ śrotavyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yat kiṃcinmaitreya subhāṣitam, sarvaṃ tadbuddhabhāṣitam / tatra maitreya ya imāni pratibhānāni pratikṣipet- naitāni buddhabhāṣitānīti, teṣu ca agauravamutpādayet, pudgalavidveṣeṇa tena sarvaṃ buddhabhāṣitaṃ pratibhānaṃ pratikṣiptaṃ bhavati / dharmaṃ pratikṣipya dharmavyasanasaṃvartanīyena karmaṇā apāyagāmī bhavati //
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, <s>Maitreya</s>, by four reasons an utterance should be known as spoken by all <s>Buddhas</s>. By which four? Here, <s>Maitreya</s>, an utterance is connected with meaning, not connected with non-meaning. It is connected with <s>Dharma</s>, not connected with non-<s>Dharma</s>. It brings about the abandonment of afflictions, not the increase of afflictions. It shows the benefits and advantages of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, not the benefits and advantages of <s>saṃsāra</s>. By these four. [Abbreviation.] <s>Maitreya</s>, for whatever person these four [criteria] apply now or will apply, faithful <s>kulaputras</s> and <s>kuladuhitṛs</s> should generate the perception of the <s>Buddha</s> regarding that, and taking the perception of the Teacher, that <s>Dharma</s> should be listened to. What is the reason? <s>Maitreya</s>, whatever is well-spoken — all that is spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>. <s>Maitreya</s>, whoever rejects these utterances — [saying] "these are not spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>" — and generates disrespect toward them, out of personal hostility — by that, all utterances spoken by the <s>Buddha</s> are rejected. Having rejected the <s>Dharma</s>, by <s>karma</s> leading to the destruction of <s>Dharma</s>, one goes to the lower realms.'

body.text: tadatra dharmatāyā avilomanameva samyaglakṣaṇamuktam / uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Thus, non-contradiction with reality alone has been stated here as the correct criterion. And it is said —

children.translated_text: 'That speech which is meaningful, conducive to <s>Dharma</s>-phrases,
which eliminates the affliction of the three realms, and which shows the benefit of peace —

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: that is stated as spoken by the Sage; the opposite is otherwise.'

body.text: etanmahāyāne sarvamastīti kathamupādeyaṃ na syāt? yaduktam "na siddho 'sau tavāditaḥ" iti, tatra paro viśeṣamabhidhatte / na bravīmi yadāvayordvayoḥ siddhamubhayasiddhamiti, kiṃ tarhi āvābhyāmanyeṣāmubhayeṣāṃ madāgamaḥ siddha ityupādeyaḥ, na mahāyānam, etadviparītatvāt / tena nopādeyamityāha anyobhayeṣṭetyādi-
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: anyobhayeṣṭasatyatve vedāderapi satyatā // Bca_9.43 //
body.translated_text: If the truth [of a scripture] depends on others' and both parties' acceptance, then even the <s>Vedas</s> and such would be true. // <s>Bca</s> 9.43 //

body.text: yadi āvayorvivādārūḍhatvāt āvābhyāmanye ye kecidapratipannā ubhaye, teṣāmiṣṭaṃ abhimatam / saṃmatamiti yāvat / tasya satyatve yathārthatve abhyupagamyamāne sati vedāderapi satyatā vedavākyasya codanālakṣaṇasya / ādiśabdāt kaṇādādivacanasyāpi / satyatā
body.translated_text: If — since the two of us are in dispute — [the criterion is] that it is accepted by certain others who have not taken a position, and if that acceptance's being true — its being in accordance with fact — is granted, then even the <s>Vedas</s> and such would be true — the statements of the <s>Vedas</s>, which are of the nature of injunctions. By the word 'and such,' even the statements of <s>Kaṇāda</s> and others. Their truth —

body.text: amṛṣārthatā syāt / tatrāpi vādiprativādibhyāmanyonyobhayasaṃmatiḥ saṃbhāvyate, iti tadapyupādeyaṃ bhavataḥ syāt / tasmānnāyamapi viśeṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: their non-falsity — would follow. For even there, mutual acceptance between the disputant and respondent, by others who accept both, is conceivable. Thus that too would be acceptable for you. Therefore, this distinction too [fails].

body.text: athāpi syāt- madāgame buddhavacanatve 'vivādaḥ, na tu mahāyāne / tena sa upādeyo netaradityāśaṅkayannāha savivādaṃ mahāyānamityādi-
body.translated_text: But one might think: regarding my scripture, there is no dispute about its being the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, but there is regarding the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Therefore the former should be accepted and not the latter — anticipating this, he says with 'if the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is disputed' and so forth —

children.translated_text: If [you say] the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is disputed, then abandon your own scripture too,
since it is disputed by the <s>Tīrthikas</s>, and other scriptures [are disputed] among your own [followers] and by others. // <s>Bca</s> 9.44 //

body.text: savivādaṃ savipratipattikaṃ mahāyānam / kecid buddhavacanatayā pravṛttyaṅgamicchanti, kecit tadviparītasamāropānnecchanti, iti hetoḥ, cet yadi na grāhyam, tadā āgamaṃ tyaja, svāgamamapi vijahīhi, so 'pi pravṛttyaṅgaṃ na syāt / kasmāt? tīrthikairmīmāṃsakādibhiḥ savivādatvāt vipratipattisaṃbhavāt parityāgamarhati / na kevalaṃ tīrthikaiḥ, api tu svayūthyairityāha- svairiti / caturnikāyamaṣṭādaśabhedabhinnaṃ bhagavataḥ śāsanam / tatra ekasyaiva nikāyasya anekabhedasaṃbhavāt svayūthyairapi parasparavivādaḥ saṃbhavati / svairiti svanikāyāntargatabhedāntarāvasthitaiḥ / parairiti anyanikāyavyavasthitaiḥ / cakāraḥ pūrvāpekṣayā samuccayārthaḥ / savivādatvāt āgamāntaraṃ tyajeti saṃbandhaḥ / tvadabhyupagatādāgamādanya āgamaḥ āgamāntaram / tadapi savivādatvānna svīkāramarhati / tvadāgamasyāpi aparāpekṣayā savivādatvaṃ samānamiti parityāge tulya eva nyāyaḥ / athavā / svairiti ekabhedavyavasthitaiḥ sautrāntikābhidharmikavainayikaiḥ parasparaṃ savivādatvāt sūtrābhidharmavinayāḥ parityāgamarhanti / asti hi ekabhedāvasthitānāṃ sautrāntikādīnāmanyonyaṃ vivādaḥ / parairiti ekanikāyāśritabhedāntaragataiḥ / etena yaduktamguruparva[śiṣya?]krameṇāmnāyāyātaṃ buddhavacanamityādi, tadanenaiva pratyākhyātaṃ draṣṭavyam / na hi avismṛtasaṃpradāyānāmanyonyasya vivādo yuktaḥ / na ca sarvajñavacaneṣu parasparahatirasti / na ca sūtrābhidharmavinayānāṃ parasparamekavākyatā bhavataḥ saṃbhavati / tat kathaṃ sūtrādisaṃsyandanaṃ buddhavacanatve heturuktam? tasmād yatkiṃcidetat //
body.translated_text: 'Disputed' — subject to disagreement — is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Some accept it as forming part of [authentic] practice because it is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>; others do not, through the superimposition of the opposite — and for this reason, if it is not to be accepted, then abandon your own scripture too, give up your own scripture as well; it too should not form part of [authentic] practice. Why? Because it is disputed by the <s>Tīrthikas</s> — the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> and such — because disagreement is possible, it deserves to be abandoned. Not only by the <s>Tīrthikas</s>, but also by those of your own school — he says: 'by your own [followers].' The teaching of the Blessed One is divided into four <s>nikāyas</s> and the eighteen divisions. Since even within a single <s>nikāya</s>, the possibility of multiple divisions exists, disputes among one's own co-religionists are also possible. 'By your own' — by those belonging to other divisions within one's own <s>nikāya</s>. 'By others' — by those established in other <s>nikāyas</s>. The word 'and' is for conjunction with the preceding. Because of being disputed, 'other scriptures should be abandoned' — this is the connection. 'Other scripture' is scripture other than what you accept. That too, because of being disputed, does not deserve acceptance. Since the disputed character of your own scripture is the same when considered from another's perspective, the same logic applies for abandoning it. Or alternatively: 'by your own' — by the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>, <s>Ābhidharmikas</s>, and <s>Vaināyikas</s> within a single division, who dispute among themselves — therefore the <s>sūtras</s>, <s>abhidharma</s>, and <s>vinaya</s> deserve to be abandoned. For there is indeed mutual dispute among those within a single division, such as the <s>Sautrāntikas</s> and others. 'By others' — by those belonging to different divisions within a single <s>nikāya</s>. By this, the stated [criterion] — 'what has come down through the succession of teacher and disciple as the word of the <s>Buddha</s>' and so forth — should be seen as already refuted by this very [argument]. For mutual dispute is not justified among those whose tradition is unbroken. Nor is there mutual contradiction in the words of the Omniscient One. Nor is it possible for you that the <s>sūtras</s>, <s>abhidharma</s>, and <s>vinaya</s> are mutually consistent. So how was consistency with the <s>sūtras</s> and such stated as a criterion of being the word of the <s>Buddha</s>? Therefore, all this [argument of yours] amounts to nothing.

body.text: evaṃ samānaparihāradūṣaṇatāmabhidhāya punarviśeṣeṇa parasyābhyupagame dūṣaṇamudbhāvayannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus stated the equal counter-objection, he further raises a specific fault in the opponent's own position, saying —

body.text: śāsanaṃ bhikṣutāmūlaṃ bhikṣutaiva ca duḥsthitā /
body.translated_text: The teaching has monkhood as its root, and monkhood itself is difficult to maintain.

body.text: śāsanamityādinopakramate- śāsanaṃ bhagavatā hitāhitasvīkāraparihāradeśanālakṣaṇam / tacca bhikṣutāmūlam / athavā / āgamavipratipattimānuṣaṅgikīṃ parisamāpya yaduktam-
body.translated_text: He commences with 'the teaching' and so forth — 'The teaching' is the Blessed One's instruction characterized by the teaching of what is to be accepted and what is to be rejected as beneficial and harmful. And that is rooted in <s>bhikṣutā</s> (monkhood). Alternatively, having concluded the incidental [discussion of] disagreement regarding scripture, to that which was said —

body.text:
satyadarśanato muktiḥ śūnyatādarśanena kim /
[9.41]
body.translated_text:
'Liberation comes from seeing the truth — what is the purpose of seeing emptiness?'
[9.41]

body.text: iti nirācikīrṣannāha- śāsanamityādi / śāsanam- idaṃ kartavyamidaṃ na kartavyamityājñāpraṇayanam / tad bhikṣutāmūlam / bhikśubhāvo bhikṣutā, saiva mūlaṃ kando yasyeti tattathoktam, tatpratiṣṭhitatvāt / yathā kila dṛḍhamūlo vṛkṣaḥ ciramavasthitimanubhavan kāṇḍaśākhāpraśākhāpatrapuṣpaphalacchāyādānasaṃtāpādyapaharaṇasamartho bhavati, tathā bhagavato 'pi śāsanakalpapādapobhikṣutākandamāsādya smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgadhyānārūpyasamādhisamāpattibodhipākṣikāryāṣṭāṅgikamārgaśrāmaṇyaphalasaṃpannaḥ
body.translated_text: Wishing to refute this, he says 'the teaching' and so forth. 'The teaching' — the issuing of the injunction 'this is to be done, this is not to be done.' That is 'rooted in <s>bhikṣutā</s>' (<s>bhikṣubhāva</s>). <s>Bhikṣubhāva</s> (the state of being a monk) is <s>bhikṣutā</s>; that itself is the root, the base of which — it is so called because it is established upon that. Just as a tree with firm roots, enduring for a long time, becomes capable of producing branches, sub-branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, shade, and of removing heat and such — so too the wish-fulfilling tree of the Blessed One's teaching, attaining the root of <s>bhikṣutā</s>, endowed with the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of supernatural power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of awakening, the <s>dhyānas</s>, the formless absorptions and attainments, the factors conducive to awakening, and the Noble Eightfold Path, and the fruits of the <s>śramaṇa</s> life

body.text: ṛddhiprātihāryādibhiḥ kleśoṣmasaṃtāpādyapaharaṇapaṭurbhavati, iti bhikṣutāyā mūlasādharmyam / tatra saṃjñābhikṣuḥ, pratijñābhikṣuḥ, bhikṣaṇaśīlo bhikṣuḥ, jñapticaturthakarmaṇopasaṃpanno bhikṣuḥ, bhinnakleśo bhikṣuḥ iti pañcaprakāro bhikṣuḥ / tatra caturthapañcamaṃ dvayamagryam, itareṣāṃ samānābhidhānamātrābhidheyatvāt / tadubhayamapi śāsanāvasthānanidānamaviruddham / tatrāpi bhinnakleśo bhikṣuḥ pradhānam / tasyaiveha grahaṇam / tadbhāvo bhikṣutā / sā ca āryasatyadarśanato na saṃgacchate ityāha- bhikṣutaiva cetyādi / bhikṣutā bhinnakleśatā / kleśaprahāṇamiti yāvat / co vaktavyāntaraṃ samuccinvan hetau vartate / yasmāt sā bhikṣutaiva duḥsthitā, śūnyatādarśanamantareṇa asamañjasā kevalasatyadarśanato na yujyate / tasmāt satyadarśanato muktiriti na vaktavyamityabhiprāyaḥ / keṣāṃ sā duḥsthitā? sāvalambanacittānāmiti / sahāvalambanena vastvabhiniveśena vartate iti sāvalambanam, tattādṛśaṃ cittaṃ yeṣāṃ yogināṃ te tathoktāḥ, teṣāmiti / yataḥ te duḥkhādisatyaṃ kleśavisaṃyogaṃ ca vastutvenāvalambante iti mataṃ bhavatām / atasteṣāmupalambhadṛṣṭīnāṃ duḥsthitā, na nirālambanacittānām //
body.translated_text: — becomes adept at removing the heat of the afflictions and such through miraculous displays and such: this is the similarity of <s>bhikṣutā</s> as a root. Therein, a <s>bhikṣu</s> is fivefold: a <s>bhikṣu</s> by name, a <s>bhikṣu</s> by declaration, a <s>bhikṣu</s> by mendicancy, a <s>bhikṣu</s> by ordination through a ceremony of declaration with three announcements, and a <s>bhikṣu</s> by destruction of the afflictions. Of these, the fourth and fifth pair is preeminent, since the others are merely designated by the same name. And both of those are non-contradictory as the foundation for the continuance of the teaching. Even among these, the <s>bhikṣu</s> whose afflictions are destroyed is primary. It is that which is taken [as the referent] here. Its state is <s>bhikṣutā</s>. And that does not accord with the [mere] seeing of the <s>Āryasatyas</s> (Noble Truths) — he says 'and <s>bhikṣutā</s> indeed' and so forth. '<s>Bhikṣutā</s>' is the destruction of the afflictions, that is, the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s>. The particle 'and' (<s>ca</s>), while including other [points] to be stated, functions in the sense of a reason. Because that very <s>bhikṣutā</s> 'is ill-established' — without seeing emptiness, it is unsound, not justified through the mere seeing of the truths. Therefore, the purport is: it should not be said that 'liberation comes from seeing the truth.' For whom is it ill-established? 'For those whose minds have an object' — a mind that operates together with an object, with clinging to things — is 'with an object'; those yogins whose minds are such are so called; for them. Because they grasp suffering and such truths and the disjoining from the afflictions as real things — this is your view. Therefore, for them who have the view of apprehension, it is ill-established — not for those whose minds are without an object. //

body.text: yatpunaruktaṃ- satyadarśanato muktiriti, tadvikalpanīyam / dvidhā hi satyadarśanaṃ saṃbhāvyate, paramārthataḥ saṃvṛtito vā / tad yadādyo vikalpaḥ, tadā nāsmākaṃ vipratipattiḥ, asmatpakṣasya pradhānatvāt, sarvadharmāṇāmasmābhiḥ paramārthato darśanābhyupagamāt / atha dvitīyaḥ, tanna sahāmahe, yuktivirodhāt / na hi saṃvṛtisatyadarśanānmuktirutpadyate, sarvasattvānāṃ muktiprasaṅgāt / tathā hi yuktyāgamābhyāṃ tattvātattvavivecanāt, paramārthasatyamevātra kleśaprahāṇāya niścīyate na saṃvṛtisatyam / tacca sarvadharmānupalambhalakṣaṇam / na hi tadantareṇa saṃkleśanivṛttiryujyate / yāvadbhāvābhiniveśaḥ, tāvat kalpanā na nivartate, yāvacca kalpanā tāvadakhaṇḍitamahimānaḥ saṃkleśāḥ cittasaṃtānamadhyāvasanti / yāvacca saṃkleśāḥ tāvat karmanirmitajanmaparaṃparāprasavaḥ saṃsāro 'pi sutarāmavyāhataprasaraḥ pravartate / tasmāt sarvadharmaśūnyataiva avidyāpratipakṣatvāt saṃsārasaṃtativicchittiheturavasīyate, na kevalaṃ satyadarśanam / idameva ācāryapādairuktam-
body.translated_text: As for what was stated — 'liberation comes from seeing the truth' — that is to be analyzed. For seeing the truth is conceivable in two ways: ultimately or conventionally. If the first alternative [is intended], then there is no disagreement from us, since our position is primary — because we accept the seeing of all <s>dharmas</s> as ultimate. But if the second [is intended], that we cannot tolerate, because it contradicts reason. For liberation does not arise from the seeing of conventional truth, since the absurd consequence would follow that all beings would be liberated. For through reasoning and scripture, through the discrimination of what is real and what is not, it is determined that <s>paramārthasatya</s> alone is what effects the abandonment of the afflictions — not <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>. And that [<s>paramārthasatya</s>] is characterized by the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. For without that, the cessation of defilement is not justified. As long as there is clinging to things, conceptualization does not cease; and as long as conceptualization [continues], the defilements, with their power unbroken, inhabit the mental continuum. And as long as there are defilements, <s>saṃsāra</s> too — which is the proliferation of the succession of births produced by <s>karma</s> — proceeds all the more with unimpeded momentum. Therefore, the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> alone, being the antidote to ignorance, is determined to be the cause of severing the continuum of <s>saṃsāra</s> — not the mere seeing of the truths. This very [point] was stated by the Master —

body.text: muktistu śūnyatādṛṣṭestadarthāśeṣabhāvanā //
body.translated_text: 'Liberation comes from the seeing of emptiness; to that end is the cultivation of all [dharmas].'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: yathāāryasatyāni satyadvaye 'ntarbhavanti tathopadarśitameva prāk / ityalamatiprasaṅgena / api ca-
body.translated_text: How the <s>Āryasatyas</s> are included within the two truths has already been shown above. Let there be no more digression. Moreover —

body.text: sāvalambanacittānāṃ nirvāṇamapi duḥsthitam // Bca_9.45 //
body.translated_text: Even <s>nirvāṇa</s> is ill-established for those whose minds have an object. // Bca_9.45 //

body.text: iti na kevalaṃ bhikṣutā, kiṃ tarhi nirvāṇamapi, ityaperarthaḥ / nirvāṇaṃ kleśavisaṃyogānnirupadhiśeṣaṃ duḥsthitaṃ durghaṭam //
body.translated_text: Not only <s>bhikṣutā</s>, but even <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the meaning of 'also.' <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — the <s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s> (without remainder) [<s>nirvāṇa</s>] — through the disjoining from the afflictions — is 'ill-established,' difficult to accomplish. //

body.text: tatra bhikṣutāyāstāvadasaṃgatimāha-
body.translated_text: Therein, he first states the unsoundness of <s>bhikṣutā</s> —

body.text: kleśaprahāṇānmuktiścettadanantaramastu sā /
body.translated_text: If liberation [comes] from the abandonment of the afflictions, let it exist immediately after that.

body.text: yadi ca āryasatyadarśanataḥ kleśāḥ prahīyante, tato vimuktirupajāyate, tadā tadanantaraṃ kleśaprahāṇāt samanantaramevāstu sā muktirbhavastu / bhavatu evam / ko vai nāma anyathā brūte? naitadasti, kuta ityāha-
body.translated_text: If the afflictions are abandoned through the seeing of the <s>Āryasatyas</s>, and from that liberation arises, then let that liberation exist immediately after — immediately following the abandonment of the afflictions; let it come into being. Let it be so. Who indeed says otherwise? This is not so. Why? — he says —

body.text: dṛṣṭaṃ ca teṣu sāmarthyaṃ niṣkleśasyāpi karmaṇaḥ // Bca_9.46 //
body.translated_text: Yet the power of <s>karma</s> is observed in them, even of one free from afflictions. // Bca_9.46 //

body.text: co hetau / dṛṣṭaṃ pratipannam / āgamataḥ / yasmāt teṣu prahīṇakleśeṣu āryamaudgalyāyanāryāṅgulimālaprabhṛtiṣu sāmarthyaṃ phaladānaṃ prati śaktiḥ / tasmānna tadanantarameva muktirasti / kasya sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭam? karmaṇaḥ śubhāśubhalakṣaṇasya / kiṃ pūrvamanāryāvasthāyāṃ kleśasahitasya? netyāha- akleśasyāpi kleśasahakārirahitasyāpi karmaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'And' (<s>ca</s>) is in the sense of 'because.' 'Observed' — acknowledged, from scripture. Because in them — those who have abandoned the afflictions, such as the <s>Ārya</s> <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Ārya</s> <s>Aṅgulimāla</s>, and others — 'power' — capacity to produce results — has been observed. Therefore, liberation does not exist immediately after [the abandonment of afflictions]. The power of what was observed? 'Of <s>karma</s>' — of what is characterized as wholesome and unwholesome. Was it of <s>karma</s> formerly accompanied by afflictions, in the pre-<s>Ārya</s> state? No — he says: 'even of one free from afflictions' — even of <s>karma</s> devoid of the cooperation of afflictions. //

body.text: nanu ca satyadarśanādavidyādi prahīyate, tatprahāṇāt saṃskārādiprahāṇakrameṇa tṛṣṇāpi prahīyate / tṛṣṇāviparyāsamatī ca punarbhavotpattinimitte / tataśca tayorabhāvāt tuṣarahitasya bījasyeva karmaṇaḥ sadbhāve 'pi na kiṃcidvihanyate iti / taduktam-
body.translated_text: But through seeing the truth, ignorance and such are abandoned; from the abandonment of that, through the sequential process of abandoning formations and such, craving too is abandoned. And craving and mistaken views are the causes of rebirth. Therefore, due to the absence of both, even though <s>karma</s> exists, like a seed without its husk, nothing is harmed — this has been stated —

children.translated_text: 'Through the power of false knowledge, the craving and volition arisen from it,
there is rebirth in lower states; having abandoned these, one is not born again.'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: athavā / tṛṣṇaiva kevalā punarbhavakāraṇam, samudayākāratvāt / uktaṃ hi bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, craving alone is the cause of rebirth, since it has the aspect of origination [the second Noble Truth]. For the Blessed One said —

body.text: tatra katamat samudayāryasatyam? yeyaṃ tṛṣṇā paunarbhavikī nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhi-
body.translated_text: 'What is the Noble Truth of Origination? It is this craving — that which leads to rebirth, accompanied by delight and passion, seeking pleasure here and

body.text: nandinī, yaduta kāmatṛṣṇā bhavatṛṣṇā vibhavatṛṣṇā ceti //
body.translated_text: there — namely, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence.'

body.text: tadevaṃ yasya tṛṣṇā nāsti, tasya prahīṇasamudayasya kāraṇābhāvāt na punarjanmasaṃbhavaḥ / iti parābhiprāyamutthāpayannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, for one in whom craving does not exist, who has abandoned the [truth of] origination — due to the absence of a cause, rebirth is not possible. Presenting the opponent's view, he says —

body.text: tṛṣṇā tāvadupādānaṃ nāsti cetsaṃpradhāryate /
body.translated_text: If craving is the appropriation [for rebirth] — granted that it does not exist, it is ascertained —

body.text: avidyāprahāṇāt tṛṣṇā punarbhavopādānaṃ kāraṇaṃ tāvannāsti, na vidyate cedyadi saṃpradhāryate niścīyate, tadā naitadvaktavyam / yataḥ upalambhadṛṣṭīnāmavidyāprahāṇamanupapannam / tadbhāvāt tṛṣṇāprahāṇasyāpyabhāvāt / bhavatu vā, tathāpyabhidhīyate-
body.translated_text: Through the abandonment of ignorance, craving — the appropriation, the cause of rebirth — does not exist. If this is ascertained, determined — then this should not be said. Because for those who hold the view of apprehension, the abandonment of ignorance is unjustified, and since that [ignorance] exists, the abandonment of craving too is absent. But granted, let it be so; even then it is stated —

body.text: kimakliṣṭāpi tṛṣṇaiṣāṃ nāsti saṃmohavat satī // Bca_9.47 //
body.translated_text: Does not even non-afflicted craving exist in these [yogins], existing like delusion? // Bca_9.47 //

body.text: akliṣṭāpi satī kleśāsaṃprayuktāpi tṛṣṇā kimeṣāṃ bhavadyogināṃ nāsti na saṃbhavati / kathamiva? saṃmohavat akliṣṭājñānavat //
body.translated_text: Even non-afflicted — even unassociated with [active] afflictions — does craving not exist, not arise in these yogins of yours? How so? 'Like delusion' — like non-afflicted ignorance. //

body.text: itthamapi tṛṣṇā niṣeddhumaśakyetyāha-
body.translated_text: That craving cannot be denied even in this way — he says —

body.text: vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā vedanaiṣāṃ ca vidyate /
body.translated_text: Craving has feeling as its condition, and feeling exists in them.

body.text: sparśapratyayā vedanā, vedanāpratyayā ca tṛṣṇā / sā vedanā tṛṣṇākāraṇameṣāmasti / tṛṣṇā tu tatkāryam, avikale 'pi kāraṇe na samasti iti kathamabhidhātuṃ śakyate? niravidyasya vedanāyāmapi tṛṣṇā na bhavatīti cet, na / bhāvābhiniveśināṃ niravidyatvameva asiddham, ityuktam / tato yadi akliṣṭājñānavat nābhyupagamyate tṛṣṇā, tathāpi śūnyatādarśanamantareṇa nyāyabalādāpatati / ayamatra samudāyārthaḥ- yadā muktasaṃtāne 'pi karmaṇaḥ phaladānasāmarthyamupalabhyate,
body.translated_text: Contact is the condition for feeling; feeling is the condition for craving. That feeling, the cause of craving, exists in them. Craving is its effect — how can it be said that the effect does not exist even when the cause is complete? If one says that for one free from ignorance, craving does not arise even from feeling — no. It has been said that the absence of ignorance is itself unestablished for those who cling to things. Therefore, if non-afflicted craving, like non-afflicted ignorance, is not accepted, still, without seeing emptiness, it follows by force of logic. This is the combined meaning: when even in a liberated continuum the capacity of <s>karma</s> to produce results is observed

body.text: tṛṣṇā ca vedanāsadbhāve saṃbhāvyamānā, tadā kleśaprahāṇamapi saṃdihyamānaṃ kathamiva vimuktau niścayaṃ kuryāt? tasmānna śūnyatāmantareṇa bhikṣutā susthitā pratibhāsate iti / yaduktam-
body.translated_text: and craving is conceivable given the existence of feeling — then even the abandonment of the afflictions, being doubtful, how could it produce certainty regarding liberation? Therefore, without emptiness, <s>bhikṣutā</s> does not appear to be well-established. As was said —

body.text: sāvalambanacittānāṃ nirvāṇamapi duḥsthitam /
body.translated_text: 'Even <s>nirvāṇa</s> is ill-established for those whose minds have an object.'

body.text: iti, tadupapādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating this, he says —

body.text: sālambanena cittena sthātavyaṃ yatra tatra vā // Bca_9.48 //
body.translated_text: A mind with an object must abide in one thing or another. // Bca_9.48 //

body.text: sālambanena sopalambhena cittena sthātavyamāsaktavyam / yatra tatra vā yatra tatra āsaṅgasthāneṣu āryasatyādiṣu tadbhāvanāphaleṣu vā / āsaṅgasaṃbhāvanāyāṃ na punarjanmanivṛttiriti kathaṃ punarjanmasaṃbhāvanāyāṃ nirvāṇamapi na saṃdigdhaṃ syāt?
body.translated_text: A mind 'with an object' — with apprehension — must abide in, must be attached to, one thing or another — in whatever places of attachment such as the <s>Āryasatyas</s> and such, or in the fruits of their cultivation. When attachment is conceivable, the cessation of rebirth does not [follow] — so how, when rebirth is conceivable, would even <s>nirvāṇa</s> not be doubtful?

body.text: tasmāduktaśūnyataiva nirvāṇakāraṇamuktetyāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, the emptiness stated [above] alone is the cause of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — saying this, he states —

children.translated_text: Without emptiness, the mind, being bound, arises again,
just as in the attainment of non-perception — therefore one should cultivate emptiness. // Bca_9.49 //

body.text: vinā śūnyatayā śūnyatāmantareṇa cittaṃ vijñānaṃ sālambanaṃ baddhaṃ saṃyatam ālambanāsaṅgapāśena / utpadyate punaḥ, samādhibalāt kiyatkālaṃ nivṛttamapi punarutpattimad bhavati / kva punaridaṃ dṛṣṭamityāha- yathā asaṃjñisamāpattau iti / yathā asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ samāpadyamānānāṃ tāvatkālaṃ cittacaittanirodhe 'pi punastadutpattiḥ syāt, tathā anyatrāpi ityarthaḥ / upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat / yathā nirodhasamāpattāvityapi draṣṭavyam / atha vā / yathā asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ samāpadya asaṃjñiṣu deveṣu upapadyamānānāmanekakalpaśataṃ yāvanniruddhānāmapi tatsamāpattivipākaphalaparisamāptau cittacaittānāṃ punarutpattiḥ, tathā / yataḥ śūnyatāmantareṇa na bhikṣutā na nirvāṇamupapadyate, tataḥ ubhayārthināṃ śūnyataiva bhāvanīyetyāha bhāvayedityādi / yena kāraṇena vinā śūnyatayā cittaṃ baddhamutpadyate punaḥ, tena kāraṇena nirvāṇādyarthī śūnyatāmeva bhāvayet / tadbhāvanā hi kleśaprahāṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ cādhigamayati / na kevalaiva satyādibhāvaneti yāvat, sālambanatvāt / yaduktamāryavajracchedikāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyām-
body.translated_text: 'Without emptiness' — in the absence of emptiness — 'the mind,' cognition, being 'with an object,' is 'bound,' fettered by the noose of clinging to an object. It 'arises again' — even though suppressed for some time by the power of <s>samādhi</s>, it again comes into being. Where is this seen? — he says: 'just as in the attainment of non-perception.' Just as for those entering the attainment of non-perception, even though mind and mental factors have ceased for that duration, their arising again occurs — so too elsewhere: this is the meaning. And this is illustrative. 'Just as in the cessation-attainment' should also be considered. Or alternatively: just as for those who, having entered the attainment of non-perception, are reborn among the non-percipient gods — even though mind and mental factors have ceased for many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, upon the completion of the ripening fruit of that attainment, the arising again of mind and mental factors [occurs] — so too. Since without emptiness neither <s>bhikṣutā</s> nor <s>nirvāṇa</s> is possible, therefore — for those who desire both — emptiness alone should be cultivated — he says 'one should cultivate' and so forth. For the reason that without emptiness the mind, being bound, arises again — for that reason one who desires <s>nirvāṇa</s> and such should cultivate emptiness alone. For its cultivation leads to the abandonment of afflictions and the realization of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Not the mere cultivation of the truths and such alone — because of being 'with an object.' As stated in the <s>Āryavajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> —

body.text: tat kiṃ manyase subhūte api tu strotaāpannasyaivaṃ bhavati- mayā strotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptamiti? subhūtirāha- no hīdaṃ bhagavan / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi bhagavan kiṃcidāpannaḥ, tenocyate strotaāpanna iti / na rūpamāpanno na śabdān na gandhān na rasān na spraṣṭavyāni na dharmānāpannaḥ, tenocyate strotaāpanna iti / saced bhagavan strotaāpannasyaivaṃ bhavet- mayā strotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptamiti, sa eva tasya ātmagrāho bhavet sattvagrāho jīvagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāho bhavet / peyālaṃ / tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu arhata evaṃ bhavati- mayārhattvaṃ prāptamiti? subhūtirāha- no hīdaṃ bhagavan / tatkasya hetoḥ? na kaściddharmo yo 'rhannāma / sacedbhagavan arhata evaṃ bhavet- mayārhattvaṃ prāptamiti, sa eva tasyātmagrāho bhavet / peyālaṃ /
body.translated_text: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does a stream-enterer think thus: "The fruit of stream-entry has been attained by me"?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No indeed, Blessed One. Why? Because, Blessed One, nothing has been entered — therefore he is called a stream-enterer. He has not entered form, not sounds, not smells, not tastes, not tangible objects, not <s>dharmas</s> — therefore he is called a stream-enterer. If, Blessed One, a stream-enterer were to think "The fruit of stream-entry has been attained by me," that would be his grasping at a self, grasping at a being, grasping at a soul, grasping at a person.' And so forth. 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does an <s>Arhat</s> think thus: "<s>Arhatship</s> has been attained by me"?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No indeed, Blessed One. Why? Because there is no <s>dharma</s> called <s>Arhat</s>. If, Blessed One, an <s>Arhat</s> were to think "<s>Arhatship</s> has been attained by me," that would be his grasping at a self.' And so forth.

body.text: bhagavānāha- tasmāttarhi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evamapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam, na kvacit pratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam, na rūpapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam, na śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyamiti /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should generate a mind that is thus non-abiding; a mind that does not abide anywhere should be generated; a mind that does not abide in form should be generated; a mind that does not abide in sound, smell, taste, or tangible objects should be generated."

body.text: tasmācchūnyataiva bodhimārga iti sthitam //
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that emptiness alone is the path to awakening.

children.translated_text: If a statement that enters into a <s>sūtra</s> is accepted as spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: mahāyānaṃ bhavatsūtraiḥ prāyastulyaṃ na kiṃ matam // Bca_9.50 //
children.translated_text: why is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, which is mostly similar to your <s>sūtras</s>, not so accepted? // Bca_9.50 //
If the whole is faulty because of one [part] not being accepted,

children.text: ekena sūtratulyena kiṃ na sarvaṃ jinoditam // Bca_9.51 //
children.translated_text: why is not everything spoken by the <s>Jina</s>, because of one [part] being similar to a <s>sūtra</s>? // Bca_9.51 //
The utterance not fathomed even by the foremost, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> and others —
who will deem it not to be grasped, merely because you have not understood it? // Bca_9.52 //

body.text: yatsūtre 'vataredityādi anuṣṭuptrayaṃ kenacit pratikṣiptamiva lakṣyate, apakramaniveśitatvāt / āgamavipratipattirasya vicārasya prastāvaḥ / śāsanaṃ bhikṣutetyādiṣu āgamavivādāt, prakramāntaratvāt pūrvameva vaktumucitam / anenāntaritasya vivādasya punarupakramo granthakārasya prastāvākauśalaṃ syāt / yatpratyayetyādinā ca prāktanavṛttadvayārthasyābhihitatvāt / mahākāśyapamukhyairityādivacanasyāślīlatvāt granthakārāprayuktamiti niścitam / tasmāt prakṣepa evāyamiti //
body.translated_text: The three <s>anuṣṭubh</s> verses beginning with "if a statement that enters into a <s>sūtra</s>" appear to have been interpolated by someone, since they are inserted as a deviation [from the flow]. The dispute over scriptural authority is the occasion for this discussion. Due to the scriptural dispute in [the section beginning with] "the teaching has monkhood" and such [9.42–49], since it is a different topic, it should have been stated earlier. To bring up a dispute that has been interrupted would show the author's ineptness in occasion. And since the meaning of the previous two verses has [already] been stated with "whatever reason" and so forth. And since the statement "not fathomed even by <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> and others" is unseemly, it is certain that this was not composed by the author. Therefore, this is indeed an interpolation.

body.text: syādetat- yathā sālambanacittasyāsaṅgasaṃbhavāt na muktiḥ syāt, tathā śūnyatāyāmapi bhayamupajāyāte / tadvaramubhayaparihāreṇa saṃsāra eva sthitiryuktetyāha-
body.translated_text: One might think: just as there is no liberation because of the impossibility of non-attachment for a mind with an object, so too fear arises regarding emptiness. It would be better to simply remain in <s>saṃsāra</s>, avoiding both — to this he says —

children.translated_text: Through fear of attachment, liberation is hindered; it follows that one remains in <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: mohena duḥkhināmarthe śūnyatāyā idaṃ phalam // Bca_9.53 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of emptiness — through delusion, for the sake of those who suffer. // Bca_9.53 //

body.text: saktirāsaṅgaḥ / trāso bhayam / śūnyatāśravaṇāt, tadarthāparijñānāt / saktitrāsamiti samāhāraḥ / tasmādubhayapakṣaparihāreṇa saṃsāre traidhātukasvabhāve sidhyati sthitiravasthānamupajāyate / tuśabdaḥ punardoṣaparihārārtham / idaṃ tu śūnyatābhyupagame dūṣaṇaṃ syāt / sādhāraṇaṃ dūṣaṇamiti yāvat / kutaḥ? anirmuktyā / hetau tṛtīyā / mukterabhāvādityarthaḥ / katameṣām? duḥkhināṃ pañcagatisaṃsāre jātyādiduḥkhapīḍitānāṃ satām / katham? arthe arthaviṣaye / mohena avidyayā / ālambanāsaṅgeneti yāvat / ataḥ śūnyatāyā idaṃ phalam, yat punarapi nivṛtya saṃsāre 'vasthānam / ayamabhiprāyaḥ- yathā śūnyatāvyatirekeṇa upalambhadṛṣṭerna muktiḥ syāt, tathā viṣayāsaṅgasukhacetāḥ sarvadharmaśūnyatābhayabhītakātaraḥ varaṃ saṃsāra evāvasthānamiti manyamāno bālaḥ praśamasukhavimukho vinivṛtya jātyādiduḥkhamanubhavan punastatraivāvatiṣṭhate iti kimanayā prasādhitamiti //
body.translated_text: "Attachment" — clinging. "Fear" — terror, from hearing emptiness, from not understanding its meaning. "Attachment-and-fear" — this is a collective compound. From that, by avoiding both sides, one's remaining in <s>saṃsāra</s>, of the nature of the three realms, results — one's abiding comes about. The word "but" is for the purpose of removing [the opponent's] objection. But this would be the objection to accepting emptiness — a common objection, that is. From what? "Through non-liberation" — the third [case ending] is in the sense of cause; meaning, due to the absence of liberation. Of whom? Of those who suffer — of beings afflicted by the suffering of birth and such in <s>saṃsāra</s> of the five destinies. How? "For their sake" — in the matter concerning them. "Through delusion" — through ignorance, through the apprehension of objects by means of convention. Therefore, this is the fruit of emptiness — that even upon turning back, one remains in <s>saṃsāra</s>. The intent is: just as without emptiness there would be no liberation for one with the view of apprehension, so too a fool, his mind [attached to] the pleasure of clinging to objects, terrified and fearful of the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, thinking "it is better to remain in <s>saṃsāra</s>," turning away from the happiness of peace, experiencing the suffering of birth and such, remains right there — so what has been accomplished by this [objection]?

body.text: anye tu saktitrāsāntanirmuktayeti pāṭhaṃ manyamānā evaṃ vyācakṣate- sakterhetutvāt saktirāsaṅgasthānam / trāsahetutvāt trāso bhayasthānam / tāveva antau saktitrāsāntau /
body.translated_text: Others, however, accepting the reading "saktitrāsāntanirmuktayā," explain it thus: since it is the locus of attachment, it is "the end of attachment"; since it is the locus of fear, it is "the end of fear." Those very two are the two ends — the ends of attachment and fear.

body.text: śāśvatocchedāntau ityarthaḥ / tathā hi- śāśvatadṛṣṭerāsaktiḥ, ucchedadṛṣṭeśca trāso jāyate / tayornirmuktayā parityāgena / pūrvavat tṛtīyā / yat paramārthavicāreṇa śāśvatāntavivarjanam, saṃvṛtisatyābhyupagamena ca ucchedāntaparityāgaḥ, iti samāropāpavādāntaparihārānmadhyamā pratipattiriyamupadarśitā bhavati / tathā ca kiṃ saṃpadyate ityāha- saṃsāre sidhyati sthitiḥ / prajñayā saṃsāradoṣāliptasya karuṇāparatantratvāt saṃsāre sidhyati niṣpadyate sthitiravasthānam / kimartham? duḥkhināmarthe paraduḥkhaduḥkhitayā duḥkhināṃ saṃsāriṇāmarthe, tadduḥkhasamuddharaṇābhilāṣāt //
body.translated_text: That is, the extreme of eternalism and the extreme of nihilism — this is the meaning. For from the view of eternalism, attachment arises; and from the view of nihilism, fear arises. "Through liberation from those two" — through their abandonment. The third [case ending] is as before. That which is, through investigation of ultimate reality, the avoidance of the extreme of eternalism, and through the acceptance of conventional truth, the abandonment of the extreme of nihilism — this middle way, through the avoidance of the extremes of superimposition and denial, has been demonstrated. And what then is accomplished? He says: "one remains in <s>saṃsāra</s>." For one untainted by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> through wisdom, due to being under the power of compassion, one's remaining, one's abiding, in <s>saṃsāra</s> results. For what purpose? "For the sake of those who suffer" — with compassion that suffers from others' suffering, for the sake of those who suffer, the <s>saṃsāric</s> beings — from the desire to rescue them from that suffering.

body.text: nanu saṃsāriṇo nāma paramārthato na santyeva, tat kathaṃ tadavasthānamityatrāha- mohena viparyāsena saṃvṛtyā sattvasyopalambhāt / etacca "duḥkhavyupaśamārthaṃ tu kāryamoho na vāryate" [9.77] ityatra paścād vyaktīkariṣyate / tasmācchūnyatāyā idaṃ phalam, yatkaruṇayā saṃsāre 'vatiṣṭhamāno 'pi śūnyatādarśanāt saṃsāradoṣairna lipyate / idamapratiṣṭhitanirvāṇatā śūnyatāyāḥ phalam, śūnyatāmantareṇa asyābhāvāt / tasmādāsaṃsāraṃ sattvārthamavasthānamicchadbhiḥ śūnyataiva bhāvayitavyā //
body.translated_text: Now, <s>saṃsāric</s> beings do not ultimately exist at all — so how is there remaining [in <s>saṃsāra</s>] for their sake? To this he says: "through delusion" — through distortion, through the perception of beings by means of convention. And this will be clarified later in "but delusion for the purpose of pacifying suffering is not prevented" [9.77]. Therefore, this is the fruit of emptiness: that even while remaining in <s>saṃsāra</s> through compassion, one is not tainted by the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> through seeing emptiness. This — non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> — is the fruit of emptiness, since without emptiness it would be impossible. Therefore, those who wish to remain for the welfare of beings throughout <s>saṃsāra</s> should cultivate emptiness alone.

body.text: etat sarvamupasaṃhāreṇopadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Showing all this in summary, he says —

body.text: tadevaṃ śūnyatāpakṣe dūṣaṇaṃ nopapadyate /
body.translated_text: Thus, the objection against the position of emptiness does not hold.

body.text: tadetat evamuktakrameṇa śūnyatāpakṣe uktaṃ dūṣaṇam- śūnyatāyāṃ trāsāt saṃsārāvasthānalakṣaṇaṃ nopapadyate na saṃgacchate vakṣyamāṇasamādhānāt / iti prathamapakṣe yojanā / yata evam-
body.translated_text: "Thus" — in the manner stated — the objection stated against the position of emptiness — the objection characterized by remaining in <s>saṃsāra</s> due to fear of emptiness — does not hold, does not stand, because of the resolution that will be stated. This is the construal in the first interpretation. Since this is so —

body.text: tasmānnirvicikitsena bhāvanīyaiva śūnyatā // Bca_9.54 //
body.translated_text: Therefore, emptiness should be cultivated without hesitation. // Bca_9.54 //

body.text: nirgato vicikitsāyā nirvicikitsaḥ niḥsaṃdehaḥ / tena satā bhāvanīyaiva abhyasanīyaiva śūnyatā sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatā anupalambhayogena //
body.translated_text: One free from doubt is "without hesitation" — without uncertainty. By such a one, emptiness — the lack of intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s> — should indeed be cultivated, should indeed be practiced, through the yoga of non-apprehension.

body.text: etena yaduktam- "na vinānena mārgeṇa" [9.41] tadupasaṃhṛtaṃ bhavati / yatpunaruktam "śūnyatādarśanena kim", tatra śūnyatāyā viśeṣamāha-
body.translated_text: By this, the statement "there is no [awakening] without this path" [9.41] is concluded. And as for what was said "what use is seeing emptiness," regarding the particular [excellence] of emptiness, he says —

children.translated_text: Emptiness is indeed the antidote to the darkness of the obscurations of affliction and knowable things.

children.text: śīghraṃ sarvajñatākāmo na bhāvayati tāṃ katham // Bca_9.55 //
children.translated_text: How can one who desires omniscience quickly not cultivate it? // Bca_9.55 //

body.text: kleśā rāgādayaḥ / jñeyaṃ pañcavidham / āvṛtiśabdastu ubhayatra saṃbadhyate / kleśā evāvṛtiḥ / jñeyaṃ ca āvṛtirāvaraṇamiti vibhajya yojanīyam / jñeyameva samāropitarūpatvādāvṛtiḥ, saiva tama iva tamaḥ, vastutattvāvaraṇāt, tasya pratipakṣaḥ prahāṇahetuḥ / hi yasmāt śūnyatā, tasmāt śīghraṃ tvaritaṃ sarvajñatāyāṃ buddhatve kāmo 'bhilāṣo yasyāsau tathoktaḥ / sarvajñatāṃ kāmayate iti vā sarvajñatākāmaḥ / na bhāvayati tāṃ kathamiti, tāṃ śūnyatāṃ kathaṃ na bhāvayati nābhyasyati? api tu mahatā yatnena bhāvayedeva //
body.translated_text: "Afflictions" — desire and such. "The knowable" — of five kinds. The word "obscuration" connects with both. "Afflictions themselves are obscuration"; and "the knowable is obscuration" — thus it should be construed by division. The knowable itself, being of a superimposed nature, is obscuration; that very thing is like darkness, darkness, because it obscures the reality of things. Its "antidote" — the cause of elimination. "Indeed" — because emptiness [is so], therefore one who desires, who has aspiration for, omniscience, <s>Buddhahood</s> — quickly, swiftly — such a one is so described. Or: one who desires omniscience is a "desirer of omniscience." "How does he not cultivate it" — how does he not cultivate, not practice, that emptiness? Rather, he should cultivate it with great effort.

body.text: yadapyuktam- trāsācchūnyatāyāṃ pravṛttirna syāt, tadapi na yuktamityāha- yadduḥkhetyādi / dvitīyapakṣe punaritthamavatāraṇīyam- astyeva śūnyatāyāmeṣo 'nuśaṃsaḥ, kevalaṃ prathamata eva tatra saṃtrāsātpravṛttirna syāditi / āha-
body.translated_text: As for the statement that through fear, engagement in emptiness would not occur — that too is unjustified — he says with "whatever produces suffering" and so forth. In the second interpretation, the introduction is as follows: there is indeed this benefit in emptiness; however, from the outset, engagement would not occur due to fear of it. He says —

children.translated_text: Let fear arise from that thing which produces suffering;

children.text: śūnyatā duḥkhaśamanī tataḥ kiṃ jāyate bhayam // Bca_9.56 //
children.translated_text: emptiness pacifies suffering — why then does fear arise from it? // Bca_9.56 //

body.text: yadvastu duḥkhajananaṃ pīḍākaram, tasmādvastunaḥ sakāśāt trāsaḥ bhayaṃ jāyatāṃ nāma / śūnyatā punaḥ pratyuta duḥkhaśamanī sarvasāṃsārikaduḥkhāpahantrī / tataḥ tasyāḥ śūnyatāyāḥ kiṃ kiṃnimittaṃ abhayasthāne kātarasya janasya bhayaṃ jāyate? sarvaguṇanidānatvāt premaiva tasyāmucitamiti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Whatever thing produces suffering, causes affliction — from that thing, let fear arise. But emptiness, on the contrary, pacifies suffering — removes all <s>saṃsāric</s> suffering. From it — from that emptiness — why, for what reason, does fear arise for a person who is timid before what is not a source of fear? Since it is the source of all virtues, love alone is appropriate toward it — this is the meaning.

body.text: ātmagrahajanitāhaṃkāraprasūtaṃ hi bhayamatattvavidāmutpadyate / sa cātmā kalpanāsamāropitamūrtiriti ahaṃkāro 'pi tadabhāvādanāspada ityupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: For indeed, fear born from the ego-sense produced by the grasping of self arises for those who do not know reality. And that self is of a form superimposed by conceptualization — therefore the ego-sense too, due to its non-existence, is without basis — showing this, he says —

children.text: yatastato vāstu bhayaṃ yadyahaṃ nāma kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: Let fear arise from anything whatsoever, if there is something called "I";

children.text: ahameva na kiṃciccedbhayaṃ kasya bhaviṣyati // Bca_9.57 //
children.translated_text: if the "I" itself is nothing, whose fear will it be? // Bca_9.57 //

body.text: yatastato vā bhayābhayasthānāt astu bhavatu bhayam / kadā? yadi ahaṃ nāma kiṃcana / ahamiti ahaṃpratyayasya viṣayaḥ kathitaḥ / ahaṃ nāma ahaṃpratyayavedyaṃ yatkiṃcana kiṃcidvastu syāt / avyaktanirdeśānnapuṃsakatā / tadā yuktameva bhayam / yadā punarahameva na kiṃcit na vastusat vicāryamāṇamahaṃ kiṃcit śabdavikalpamātrādanyata, tadā bhayaṃ kasya? ahamityasyābhāvāt / bhaviṣyati utpatsyate / ito 'pi vicārāt trāso nivartate iti bhāvaḥ / taduktam-
body.translated_text: From anything whatsoever — from any source of fear or fearlessness — let there be fear. When? If there is something called "I" — "I" refers to the object of the I-notion. "Something called I" — if there were any thing, any entity, cognizable as the object of the I-notion. The neuter gender is from the indeterminate reference. Then fear would indeed be justified. But when the "I" itself is nothing — when, upon examination, the "I" is nothing other than a mere word and concept — then whose fear? Due to the non-existence of the "I." "Will be" — will arise. Even from this analysis, fear is removed — this is the meaning. As stated —

children.text: nāsmyahaṃ na bhaviṣyāmi na me 'sti na bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: "I am not, I shall not be; nothing is mine, nothing will be mine" —
this is the terror of the fool, the destruction of fear for the wise.

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: yathā ca ahaṃpratyayaviṣayasya kalpanāmātropadarśitatvādasattvam, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And just as the non-existence of the object of the I-notion has been shown as being merely conceptual, so he establishes this —
