body.translated_text: 'Honored' — worshipped; 'despised' — treated with contempt; 'by whom will anyone come to be?' In the absence of the intrinsic nature of things, no one is anything to anyone — this is the meaning.

body.text: kutaḥ sukhahetorabhāvāt sukhaṃ vā, kuto duḥkhaṃ vā duḥkhahetorabhāvāt? anyonyasamuccayārtha ubhayatra vāśabdaḥ / yatprāptiparihārārthamāyāsaḥ kriyate / kiṃ priyaṃ vā kiṃ vallabhaṃ vā? priyarūpatāyāḥ kalpitatvāt / kimapriyaṃ kimanabhilaṣaṇīyam? apriyamapi na paramārthataḥ kiṃcit vidyate, iti kimarthaṃ priyāpriyasaṃyogaviyogārthaṃ prayatnaḥ kriyate? kā tṛṣṇā yayā lābhādyarthaṃ tṛṣyati janaḥ? kutra sā tṛṣṇā, kva punarāsaṅgasthāne vastuni tṛṣṇā? mṛgyamāṇā svabhāvataḥ, anviṣyamāṇā svarūpataḥ / tadviṣayasyābhāvāt nirviṣayatayā tasyā apyabhāvaḥ, yadvaśāt tattat karma samuccīyate //
body.translated_text: 'From where' — due to the absence of the cause of happiness — 'pleasure,' or — 'from where pain' — due to the absence of the cause of suffering? The word '<s>vā</s>' in both cases is for mutual conjunction. That for the obtaining and avoidance of which exertion is made — 'what is dear' — what is beloved? Because the nature of being dear is fabricated. 'What is not dear' — what is undesirable? Even the not-dear does not ultimately exist as anything — so for what purpose is effort made for the conjunction with and separation from the dear and not-dear? 'What is craving' — that craving by which people thirst for gain and such? 'Where is that craving' — in what object of attachment is craving found? 'When sought in terms of intrinsic nature' — when investigated as to its own nature. Due to the absence of its object, that [craving] too is absent through being objectless — and on account of which the various <s>karmas</s> are accumulated.

body.text: vicāre paramārthasvarūpanirūpaṇe sati jīvalokaḥ sattvalokaḥ kaḥ? naiva kaścit / tadabhāvāt ko nāmātra mariṣyati? jīvalokasya vicāreṇa asatsvabhāvatvāt ko nāmātra jīvaloke mariṣyati, uparatajīvitendriyo bhaviṣyati? ko bhaviṣyati, ka utpatsyate? ko bhūtaḥ pūrvamutpannaḥ? ityatītādivyavahāraḥ kālpanika eva / ko bandhuḥ, kaḥ svajanaḥ? kasya kaḥ suhṛt, kiṃ mitraṃ kasya? atreti sarvatra yojanīyam / yadabhiṣvaṅgeṇa akuśalamapi na gaṇyate?
body.translated_text: 'Upon examination' — when the investigation of ultimate reality is undertaken — 'what is the world of the living,' the world of sentient beings? It is simply nothing at all. Due to its absence, 'who will die here?' Since the world of the living is, upon examination, of unreal nature, who indeed in this world of the living will die — will become one whose life-faculty has ceased? 'Who will come to be' — who will be born? 'Who has been' — who was previously born? Thus, the conventional usage regarding the past and such is merely fabricated. 'Who is a relative' — who is a kinsman? 'Who is a friend to whom' — whose companion is who? The word 'here' should be connected everywhere. On account of attachment to which, even the unwholesome is disregarded?

body.text: evaṃ svabhāvaśūnyatvāt kalpanāsamāropitameva tattvamityāha sarvamityādi-
body.translated_text: Thus, since [everything] is empty of intrinsic nature, the reality is merely superimposed by conceptual fabrication — he says with 'everything' and so forth —

children.translated_text: Let those like me comprehend that everything is like space.
They become angry and rejoice due to causes of quarrel and celebration. // <s>Bca</s> 9.155 //

body.text: sarvametaduktam, anyacca / ākāśasaṃkāśaṃ samāropitatattvaśūnyatvādākāśakalpam / parigṛhṇantu avidyamānameva tu svarūpamāropya madvidhā iti granthakāraḥ ātmānameva nidarśanaṃ karoti / mādṛśāḥ aparijñātaparamārthatattvā bālajanāḥ asadvitarkākulitacetasaḥ prakupyanti, mithyābhiniveśāt kopaṃ yānti / prahṛṣyanti alīkalābhayogāt pramuditā bhavanti / kaiḥ? kalahotsavahetubhiḥ kalahahetubhiḥ vivādahetubhiḥ, utsavahetubhirānandahetubhiḥ yathāyogam / tasmādanadhigataparamārthatattvāḥ sāṃvṛtameva vasturūpaṃ satyatayābhiniviṣṭāḥ sarvametanmanyante, na tu paramārthavedinaḥ iti / taduktam-
body.translated_text: 'Everything' — what has been stated, and other things too. 'Like space' — like space, through the emptiness of superimposed reality. 'Let them comprehend' — 'those like me' — here the author makes himself the example — by superimposing an existence that is not [actually] there. Those like me — childish people who have not comprehended ultimate reality, whose minds are agitated by false reasoning — 'become angry,' go to anger through false attachment; 'rejoice,' become delighted through illusory gain. By what? 'By causes of quarrel and celebration' — by causes of quarrel, causes of dispute, and by causes of celebration, causes of joy, respectively. Therefore, those who have not realized the ultimate truth, being attached to the mere conventional form of things as if it were real, regard all this [as real] — but not those who know the ultimate. As was stated —

body.text: etāvaccaiva jñeyaṃ yaduta saṃvṛtiḥ paramārthaśca / tacca bhagavatā śūnyataḥ sudṛṣṭaṃ suviditaṃ susākṣātkṛtam / tena sarvajña ityucyate / tatra saṃvṛtirlokapracāratastathāgatena dṛṣṭā / yaḥ punaḥ paramārthaḥ, so 'nabhilāpyaḥ anājñeyo 'vijñeyaḥ adeśitaḥ aprakāśitaḥ, yāvat akriyaḥ akaraṇaḥ, yāvat na lābho nālābho na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ na yaśo nāyaśaḥ na rūpaṃ nārūpamityādi /
body.translated_text: 'Just this much is to be known: namely, the conventional and the ultimate. And that has been well seen, well known, well directly realized by the Blessed One as empty. Therefore he is called omniscient. Therein, the conventional was seen by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in accordance with worldly practice. But the ultimate — that is inexpressible, unknowable, incomprehensible, not taught, not revealed, and so on up to — without action, without making, and so on up to — neither gain nor non-gain, neither pain nor pleasure, neither fame nor infamy, neither form nor formlessness,' and so forth.

children.text: tatra jinena janasya kṛtena saṃvṛti deśita lokahitāya /
children.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Jina</s> — accomplished for the benefit of people — taught the conventional for the welfare of the world,
by which beings might generate faith and happiness in the presence of the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: saṃvṛti prajñapayī narasiṃhaḥ ṣaṅgatayo bhaṇi sattvagaṇānām /
children.translated_text: The <s>Narasiṃha</s> (Lion among Men) designated the conventional: he declared the six destinies for the groups of beings —

children.text: narakagatīśca tathaiva ca pretān āsurakāya narāṃśca marūṃśca //
children.translated_text: the destiny of hell-beings, and likewise hungry ghosts, the bodies of <s>Asuras</s>, humans, and gods.

body.text: nīcakulāṃ tatha uccakulāṃśca āḍhyakulāṃśca daridrakulāṃśca //
body.translated_text: Low births and high births, wealthy families and poor families.

body.text: ityādi //
body.translated_text: And so forth.

body.text: idamapi tattvānadhigamasya phalamityāha śokāyāsairityādi-
body.translated_text: He states that this too is a result of the failure to realize the truth — with 'by grief and toil' and so forth —

children.translated_text: By grief, toil, despair, and by mutual cutting and breaking,
those who desire their own happiness spend their time in great misery, through evil deeds. // <s>Bca</s> 9.156 //

body.text: putrakalatrādiviprayogakṛtāḥ śokāḥ / sukhaduḥkhaprāptiparihāranimittapariśramā āyāsāḥ / taiḥ śokāyāsairmadvidhāḥ yāpayanti sukṛcchreṇeti saṃbandhaḥ / viṣādaiśca lābhasatkārādiviṣādairdaurmanasyaiḥ / mithaśchedanabhedanaiḥ, mithaḥ parasparaṃ chedanāni karacaraṇaśironāsikākarṇaprabhṛtīnām, bhedanāni bāhujaṅghoruvakṣaḥpārśvodarādīnām / cakāro 'nuvartate / taiśchedanabhedanaiśca yāpayanti, kālakrameṇa āyuḥsaṃskārān kṣayapanti / sukṛcchreṇa mahatā kaṣṭena kathaṃcillabdhāśanapānavasanāḥ / kiṃbhūtāḥ santaḥ? pāpairātmasukhecchavaḥ, pāpairakuśalaiḥ karmabhiḥ, ātmanaḥ svasya sukhecchavaḥ sukhābhilaṣaṇaśīlāḥ //
body.translated_text: Grief produced by separation from sons, wives, and such. Toil — the exertion caused by the obtaining and avoidance of pleasure and pain. By those griefs and toils, those like me 'spend their time in great misery' — this is the connection. 'By despair' — by despondencies over gain, honor, and such, by dejection. 'By mutual cutting and breaking' — 'mutual' means reciprocal; 'cutting' of hands, feet, head, nose, ears, and such; 'breaking' of arms, shins, thighs, chest, sides, belly, and such. The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) carries over. By those cuttings and breakings too they 'spend their time' — they exhaust the life-<s>saṃskāras</s> over the course of time. 'In great misery' — having somehow obtained food, drink, and clothing with great difficulty. Being of what character? 'Those who desire their own happiness through evil deeds' — through unwholesome <s>karmas</s>, desiring happiness for themselves — habitually craving their own pleasure.

body.text: tathāvidhaiśca samācāraviśeṣaiśca-
body.translated_text: And through such particular modes of conduct —

body.text: mṛtāḥ patantyapāyeṣu dīrghatīvravyatheṣu ca /
body.translated_text: Having died, they fall into the lower realms, where suffering is long and intense.

body.text: mṛtāḥ jīvitendriyavimuktāḥ / patanti gacchanti apāyeṣu narakapretatiryakṣu / kiṃbhūteṣu? dīrghatīvravyatheṣu ca, dīrghā cirakālabhāvinī, tīvrā atiduḥsahavedanīyavipākatvāt, vyathā yeṣvapāyeṣu te tathoktāḥ, teṣu ca / cakāra uktasamuccaye bhinnakrame vā / kena prakāreṇetyāha āgatyāgatyetyādi-
body.translated_text: 'Having died' — released from the life-faculty. They 'fall,' they go, 'into the lower realms' — into the hells, the hungry ghost realm, and the animal realm. Of what character? 'Where suffering is long and intense' — 'long' means enduring over a great length of time; 'intense' because the ripening involves extremely unbearable sensation; the lower realms in which there is such suffering are so called. The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is for the accumulation of what was stated, or for variation in sequence. In what manner? He says with 'having come again and again' and so forth —

body.text: āgatyāgatya sugatiṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā sukhocitāḥ // Bca_9.157 //
body.translated_text: Having come again and again to the happy destinies, having become accustomed to pleasure — // <s>Bca</s> 9.157 //

body.text: sukhasaṃvardhitā bhūtvā bhūtvā / katham? āgatyāgatya sugatim, śobhanāṃ devamanuṣyagatiṃ prāpya prāpya //
body.translated_text: 'Nurtured by happiness, having become [so] again and again.' How? 'Having come again and again to the happy destiny' — having attained, having reached the good destiny of gods and humans.

body.text: punarapi tathābhūtānāṃ duḥkhapaṃraparāsāgaranimajjanonmajjanamādarśayannāha bhava ityādi-
body.translated_text: Again showing the sinking and surfacing in the boundless ocean of suffering of beings in such a state, he says with 'in existence' and so forth —

children.translated_text: In existence there are many precipices, and therein such unreality prevails.
Therein there is mutual conflict — such is the nature of reality. // <s>Bca</s> 9.158 //

body.text: bhave saṃsāre kāmarūpārūpyasvabhāve bahuprapātaśca bahutara upaghātaśca / tatra cāsattvamīdṛśam, tatra ca bhave prapāte vā atattvamīdṛśaṃ vyāmohavijṛmbhitametādṛśaṃ sarvajanasādhāraṇaṃ yathāvidhaṃ pratipāditaṃ paridṛśyamānaṃ vā / tatrānyonyavirodhaśca, tatra evaṃvidhe atattve sati
body.translated_text: 'In existence' — in <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose nature encompasses the desire, form, and formless realms — 'there are many precipices,' abundant calamities. 'And therein such unreality' — therein, in existence or in the precipice, such unreality — such bewilderment-manifestation — of such a kind, common to all beings, as has been described or as is observed. 'Therein there is mutual conflict' — in such unreality, when it prevails,

body.text: anyonyavirodhaḥ parasparavipratipattiḥ / kena kāraṇena na bhavettatvamīdṛśamiti / tasmādvasturūpametādṛśamanekākārasamāropāt //
body.translated_text: mutual conflict — reciprocal opposition. For what reason? 'Such is the nature of reality' — because reality is of such a nature, through the superimposition of manifold forms upon things.

body.text: tatra cānupamāstīvrā anantā duḥkhasāgarāḥ /
body.translated_text: And therein there are incomparable, intense, infinite oceans of suffering.

body.text: tatra ca evamapi / anupamāḥ tadaparasadṛśaduḥkhābhāvādupamātumaśakyāḥ / tīvrā atyugravedanāḥ / anantā anavadhikālavipākatayā aparyantā vā duḥkhānāmativipulatayā mahāyānamanadhigamya nistarītumaśakyatvāt, sāgarāḥ / tathāpi kathaṃcit mahatā vīryeṇa kuśalapakṣopacayāt bhūyasā kālena sugatiṃ prāpya kṣapayituṃ śakyante ityata āha tatraivamityādi-
body.translated_text: And therein, even so — 'incomparable' (<s>anupamā</s>) means incapable of comparison due to the absence of anything else resembling such suffering; 'intense' (<s>tīvrā</s>) means extremely fierce sensations; 'endless' (<s>anantā</s>) means without limit due to ripening over an immeasurable period of time, or boundless due to the vast extent of sufferings. Because without attaining the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, they cannot be crossed over. 'Oceans' (<s>sāgarāḥ</s>) — even so, somehow, through great effort, through the accumulation of merit, after a long time, having attained a fortunate rebirth, they can be exhausted. Therefore he says 'therein, thus' and so forth —

body.text: tatraivamalpabalatā tatrāpyalpatvamāyuṣaḥ // Bca_9.159 //
body.translated_text: Therein, thus, there is weakness of power; and therein too, the lifespan is short. // <s>Bca</s> 9.159 //

children.translated_text: And therein too, with activities for sustaining life and health, with hunger, fatigue, and exhaustion,
with sleep, with calamities, and with fruitless association with the foolish — likewise. // <s>Bca</s> 9.160 //

body.text: vṛthaivāyurvahatyāśu vivekastatra durlabhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Life passes swiftly and in vain; discernment is rare therein.

body.text: tatra tathārūpe samāveśe evaṃ paridṛśyamānarūpā alpabalatā / hīnavīryateti yāvat / tatrāpyalpatvamāyuṣaḥ / tatrāpi evaṃbhūte satyapi / alpatvaṃ stokatvam, āyuṣaḥ āyuḥsaṃskārāṇām / tatrāpi jīvitārogyavyāpāraiḥ snānābhyañjanaprabhṛtibhiḥ / ārogyasya ārogyāya vārogopaśamāya vyāpāraiḥ viśeṣeṇa kaṭutiktabhaiṣajyakaṣāyapānādibhiḥ / kuśalopārjanamantareṇa vṛthā caiva āyurvahatyāśu iti vakṣyamāṇena saṃbandhaḥ / tathā kṣutklamaśramaiḥ, kṣut bubhukṣā, klamo glāniḥ, śramo mārgakhedādi, taiḥ / nidrayā upadravaiḥ, nidrayā svapnena, upadravairhāsyotprāsaviheṭhanādikṛtaiḥ sarīsṛpavyālamṛgadaṃśamaśakādikṛtaiḥ badhabandhanatāḍanādilakṣaṇaiḥ / tathā bālasaṃsargairniṣphalaiḥ, tathā bālānāṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ saṃsargaiḥ saṃparkaiḥ / kiṃbhūtaiḥ? niṣphalaiḥ ātmotkarṣādisaṃbhinnapralāpādibahulaiḥ / tatheti na kevalaṃ pūrvoktakrameṇa, itthamapi vṛthaivāyurvahatyāśu, vṛthaiva niṣphalameva kuśalapakṣopacayarahitatvāt āyurvahati yāti āśu śīghram, asadvayāpāraprasaṅgāt tvāritameva parikṣayāt / evamapi vartamānānāṃ vivekastu sudurlabhaḥ, vivekastu heyopādeyajñānaṃ vyāsaṅgaparityāgo vā, sudurlabhaḥ, kathamapi atikṛcchreṇāpi na labhyate / bhavatu nāma evam, tathāpi yadi kathaṃcit samādhānaṃ jāyate, tadā kalyāṇaṃ syāt, tadapi nāstītyāha tatrāpītyādi-
body.translated_text: Therein — in such a condition — 'weakness of power' (<s>alpabalatā</s>) of the kind that is thus observed. It means deficiency of vigor. 'And therein too, the lifespan is short' — therein too, even when this is so, 'shortness' means brevity, 'of lifespan' means of the vital forces. 'And therein too, with activities for sustaining life and health' — with bathing, anointing, and such; 'for health' means for the sake of health, or for the remedy of disease — activities, specifically drinking of pungent, bitter medicines and decoctions, and so forth. Without the earning of merit, 'life passes swiftly and in vain' — this connects with what will be stated. Likewise, 'with hunger, fatigue, and exhaustion': 'hunger' (<s>kṣut</s>) is the desire for food; 'fatigue' (<s>klama</s>) is weariness; 'exhaustion' (<s>śrama</s>) is travail from the road and such — by these. 'With sleep and calamities': 'with sleep' (<s>nidrayā</s>) means with slumber; 'with calamities' (<s>upadravaiḥ</s>) — those caused by laughter, mockery, and harassment, and those caused by serpents, wild beasts, biting insects, and mosquitoes, and those characterized by injury, imprisonment, and beating. 'And with fruitless association with the foolish': the associations, contacts, with the foolish, with ordinary persons. Of what kind? 'Fruitless' — full of idle chatter mixed with self-aggrandizement and such. 'Likewise' (<s>tathā</s>) means not only in the previously stated manner; in this way too, 'life passes swiftly and in vain' — 'in vain' means fruitlessly, because of the lack of accumulation of the wholesome; 'life passes,' goes, 'swiftly,' quickly, because involvement in worthless activities hastens its complete exhaustion. Even for those living thus, 'discernment is extremely hard to find' — 'discernment' (<s>viveka</s>) is knowledge of what is to be abandoned and adopted, or the abandonment of attachment; 'extremely hard to find' — even with the greatest difficulty, it cannot be obtained. Let this be so; still, if somehow mental concentration arises, then it would be well. Even that does not exist — he says with 'therein too' and so forth —

body.text: tatrāpyabhyastavikṣepanivāraṇagatiḥ kutaḥ // Bca_9.161 //
body.translated_text: Therein too, whence the means to avert habitual distraction? // <s>Bca</s> 9.161 //

body.text: tatrāpi māro yatate mahāpāyaprapātane /
body.translated_text: Therein too, <s>Māra</s> strives to cast [beings] into the great lower realms.

body.text: tatrāpi evamavasthāṃ gate 'pi abhyastavikṣepaḥ pariśīlitamauddhatyaṃ tasya nivāraṇaṃ nivartanaṃ tasya gatiranupraveśaḥ kutaḥ? naivāsti / tatrāpi evamanarthaparaṃparāyāṃ sthitānāṃ kathaṃcit kuśalapakṣaṃ samīkṣya māro yatate mahāpāyaprapātane, kleśamāro devaputramāro vā yatate udyacchate
body.translated_text: Therein too — even when one has arrived at such a state — 'habitual distraction' (<s>abhyastavikṣepa</s>) is well-practiced restlessness; its 'averting' is its removal; the 'means' for that, the approach — whence? It simply does not exist. Therein too — for those situated in such a succession of calamities — somehow perceiving the wholesome, '<s>Māra</s> strives to cast [them] into the great lower realms' — the <s>kleśa-māra</s> (affliction-<s>Māra</s>) or the <s>devaputra-māra</s> (god-son <s>Māra</s>) 'strives,' exerts himself,

body.text: mahāpāyaprapātane prapātananimittam / avīcyādinarakaprakṣepaṇārthamiti yāvat / evamapi kadācit satyaratnādiṣu abhisaṃpratyayavaśāt kathaṃcit kalyāṇamupajāyate ityāha tatrāsanmārgetyādi-
body.translated_text: 'to cast into the great lower realms' — as the cause of their downfall. That is to say, for the purpose of hurling them into hells such as <s>Avīci</s>. Even so, sometimes, through the power of faith in the true jewels and such, somehow something wholesome arises — he says with 'therein, false paths' and so forth —

body.text: tatrāsanmārgabāhulyādvicikitsā ca durjayā // Bca_9.162 //
body.translated_text: Therein, due to the abundance of false paths, doubt too is hard to conquer. // <s>Bca</s> 9.162 //

children.translated_text: And again, the opportunity of a [favorable] moment is rare; the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is extremely rare;
the flood of afflictions is hard to hold back — alas, what a succession of sufferings! // <s>Bca</s> 9.163 //

body.text: tatra evaṃ daśāṃ prāpnoti- samyagdṛṣṭivipakṣasya asanmārgasya cārvākamīmāṃsakādiparidīpitasya bāhulyāt bhūyastvāt vicikitsā sanmārge vimatiśca durjayā, kathaṃcidapi vicikitsā tyaktuṃ na śakyā / kathaṃcit sugatipratilambhe 'pi punaśca kṣaṇadaurlabhyam, aṣṭākṣaṇavinirmuktasya kṣaṇasya daurlabhyaṃ paramadurlabhatvam
body.translated_text: Therein, one reaches such a condition — due to the 'abundance,' the prevalence, 'of the false path,' the opponent of right view, illuminated by <s>Cārvākas</s>, <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, and others, 'doubt' — uncertainty regarding the true path — 'is hard to conquer'; doubt cannot be abandoned even with difficulty. Even when a fortunate rebirth is somehow obtained, 'and again, the opportunity of a [favorable] moment is rare' — the rarity of a moment free from the eight unfavorable conditions (<s>aṣṭākṣaṇa</s>), its extreme difficulty of attainment —

body.text:
mahārṇavayugacchidrakūrmagrīvārpaṇopamam /
[4.20]
body.translated_text: comparable to a turtle thrusting its neck through the hole in a yoke floating on a great ocean. [4.20]

body.text: kathaṃciditarakṣaṇasaṃbhave 'pi buddhotpādo 'tidurlabhaḥ, buddhānāṃ [bhagavatāṃ]samastajagadālokakāriṇāṃ sarvaduḥkhanidānabhūtakleśaśalyāpahāriṇāmutpādaḥ prādurbhāvaḥ atidurlabhaḥ / kathaṃcit karhicit udumbarapuṣpaprāyaḥ saṃsārasāgarottaraṇopāyabhūtaḥ / kathaṃcit buddhotpādasaṃbhave 'pi kleśaughaḥ [jātijarāmaraṇā] dīnāmoghaḥ avicchinnaḥ pravāhaḥ / sa durnivāraḥ, duḥkhenāpi nivārayitumaśakyaḥ / ityaho duḥkhaparaṃparā / ityevam / aho iti khede / duḥkhasya kaṣṭasya paraṃparā, ekasmādduḥkhādvinirgame 'pi aparasmin duḥkhe prapatanāt //
body.translated_text: Even when somehow a favorable moment does arise, 'the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is extremely rare' — the arising, the appearance, of <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones who illuminate the entire world and remove the thorn of afflictions that is the cause of all suffering, is 'extremely rare.' Somehow, at some time, like the flowering of the <s>udumbara</s>, it is the means for crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Even when somehow the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> occurs, 'the flood of afflictions' — the uninterrupted stream of birth, old age, death, and such — 'is hard to hold back,' impossible to avert even with difficulty. 'Thus, alas, what a succession of sufferings!' — thus indeed. 'Alas' (<s>aho</s>) expresses distress. 'A succession of suffering' — of misery — because even upon escaping from one suffering, one falls into another. //

body.text: sāṃpratamevaṃ sattvān suduḥkhitān samīkṣya karuṇāmreḍitahṛdayaḥ paraduḥkhaduḥkhī śāstrakāraḥ sattvānāṃ duḥkhaṃ śocayannāha aho bateti-
body.translated_text: Now, observing beings thus deeply afflicted, the author, whose heart overflows with compassion, who suffers at the suffering of others, lamenting the suffering of beings, says with 'alas' and so forth —

body.text: aho batātiśocyatvameṣāṃ duḥkhaughavartinām /
body.translated_text: Alas, how exceedingly pitiable are these beings caught in the flood of suffering!

body.text: nipātasamudāyaḥ khede / atiśocyatvamatiśayena śocanīyatvam / eṣāṃ hitāhitaparijñānavikalānāṃ sattvānāṃ duḥkhasāgarakallolaparaṃparānimajjanonmajannākulacetasām / ke punaramī sattvāḥ śocanīyā ityāha ye ityādi-
body.translated_text: The collection of particles expresses distress. 'Exceedingly pitiable' (<s>atiśocyatva</s>) means the state of being supremely worthy of lamentation. 'Of these beings' — of beings who lack the discernment of what is beneficial and harmful, whose minds are agitated by the waves of the ocean of suffering, constantly sinking and rising. Who then are these pitiable beings? He says with 'who' and so forth —

body.text: ye nekṣante svadauḥsthityamevamapyatiduḥsthitāḥ // Bca_9.164 //
body.translated_text: Who do not perceive their own wretched state, though being thus extremely wretched. // <s>Bca</s> 9.164 //

body.text: ye sattvā avidyāndhīkṛtajñānalocanāḥ nekṣante na paśyanti svadauḥsthityaṃ svasya ātmano duḥkhāvasthitatvam / evamapyatiduḥsthitāḥ evamuktakrameṇa atiduḥsthitā atiśayena duḥkhāvasthitāḥ / duḥkhaparyāpannā iti yāvat //
body.translated_text: 'Who' — those beings whose eye of knowledge has been blinded by ignorance — 'do not perceive,' do not see, 'their own wretched state,' the state of being established in suffering of themselves. 'Though being thus extremely wretched' — being, in the manner stated, supremely established in suffering. That is, they are encompassed by suffering. //

body.text: etadanurūpadṛṣṭāntena spaṣṭayannāha snātvetyādi-
body.translated_text: Illustrating this with a fitting analogy, he says with 'having bathed' and so forth —

children.translated_text: Just as someone, having bathed again and again, would enter fire repeatedly,
they consider themselves to be well-situated, though being thus extremely wretched. // <s>Bca</s> 9.165 //

body.text: snātvā snātvā jalāvagāhanaṃ kṛtvā kṛtvā yathā kaścidupahatabuddhiḥ śītārtaḥ sukhābhilāṣī / viśet praviśet / bahnimagnim / muhurmuhuḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ punaḥ punarvā / tathā ete 'pi
body.translated_text: 'Having bathed again and again' — having plunged into water again and again — 'just as someone' — someone of impaired understanding, afflicted by cold, desirous of comfort — 'would enter,' would go into — 'fire' — a blaze — 'repeatedly,' at every moment, again and again. Likewise, these too

body.text: sattvāḥ svasausthityam / ātmasukhasaṃpattiṃ ca manyante avabudhyante / evamapyatiduḥsthitāḥ evamanena pratipāditakrameṇa atiduḥsthitāḥ duḥkhāgnijvālākavalīkṛtāḥ //
body.translated_text: beings 'consider themselves to be well-situated' — they understand [themselves to have] happiness and prosperity of the self — 'though being thus extremely wretched' — in the manner thus demonstrated, being supremely wretched, consumed by the flames of the fire of suffering. //

body.text: aho bata atibahulatarājñānāndhakārākramaṇamamīṣāṃ yadātmagatamapi pramādaṃ na paśyantītyāha ajaretyādi-
body.translated_text: Alas! What an exceedingly dense darkness of ignorance envelops these [beings], that they do not see even the heedlessness that pertains to themselves — he says with 'as if ageless' and so forth —

children.translated_text: For these beings who live as if ageless and immortal,
terrible calamities will come, with death at the forefront. // <s>Bca</s> 9.166 //

body.text: na vidyate jarā jīrṇatā yeṣāṃ te ajarāḥ / na mriyante ye te amarāḥ / teṣāmajarāṇāmamarāṇāmiva līlā viceṣṭitaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ / teṣāmevamanayā līlayā viharatāṃ niścitaṃ vicaratāṃ satām / āyāsyanti ḍhaukiṣyante āpado nirantaram / sarve te duḥkhahetavaḥ jarāvyādhivipattayaḥ / ghorā atīva bhayaṃkarāḥ / kathamāyāsyanti? kṛtvā maraṇamagrataḥ, maraṇamapratīkāraparihāraṃ mṛtyumagrataḥ purataḥ kṛtvā / etaccoktaṃ rājāvavādakasūtre-
body.translated_text: Those for whom old age does not exist are 'ageless' (<s>ajarāḥ</s>). Those who do not die are 'immortal' (<s>amarāḥ</s>). Those whose 'sport' (<s>līlā</s>), whose conduct, is as if they were ageless and immortal — they are so called. 'For those living' — assuredly moving about — 'in this manner, with this sport' — 'calamities will come,' will approach, ceaselessly — all those causes of suffering: old age, disease, and misfortune — 'terrible' (<s>ghorāḥ</s>), exceedingly frightful. How will they come? 'With death at the forefront' — having placed death — irremediable, unavoidable death — 'at the front,' before them. And this was stated in the <s>Rājāvavādaka-sūtra</s> —

body.text: tadyathā mahārāja catasṛbhyo digbhyaścatvāraḥ parvatā āgaccheyuḥ, dṛḍhāḥ, sāravantaḥ, akhaṇḍāḥ, acchidrāḥ asuṣirāḥ, susaṃvṛttāḥ ekaghanāḥ nabhaḥ spṛśantaḥ, pṛthivīṃ collikhantaḥ, sarvaṃ tṛṇakāṣṭhaśākhāparṇapalāśādisarvasattvaprāṇabhūtān nirmathnantaḥ / tebhyo na sukaraṃ javena vā palāyitum, balena vā dravyamantrauṣadhairvā nivartayitum / evameva mahārāja catvārīmāni mahābhayāni āgacchanti, yeṣāṃ na sukaraṃ javena vā palāyitum, balena vā dravyamantrauṣadhairvā nivartanaṃ kartum / katamāni catvāri? jarā vyādhirmaraṇaṃ vipattiśca / jarā mahārāja āgacchati yauvanaṃ pramathamānā / vyādhirmahārāja āgacchati ārogyaṃ pramathnan / maraṇaṃ mahārāja āgacchati jīvitaṃ pramathamānam / vipattirmahārāja āgacchati sarvāḥ saṃpattīḥ pramathnantī / tat kasmāddhetoḥ? tadyathā mahārāja siṃho mṛgarājo rūpasaṃpanno javasaṃpannaḥ sujātanakhadaṃṣṭrākarālo mṛgagaṇamanupraviśya mṛgaṃ gṛhītvā yathākāmakaraṇīyaṃ karoti / sa ca mṛgarājo 'tibalaṃ vyālamukhamāsādya vivaśo bhavati / evameva mahārāja viddhasya mṛtyuśalyena apagatamadasya atrāṇasya apratiśaraṇasya aparāyaṇasya marmasu cchidyamāneṣu māṃsaśoṇite pariśuṣyamāṇe parituṣitavihvalavadanasya karacaraṇavikṣepābhiyuktasya akarmaṇyasya asamarthasya lālāsiṃghāṇakapūyamūtrapurīṣopaliptasya īṣajjīvitāvaśeṣasya karmabhavāt punarbhavamālambamānasya yamapuruṣabhayabhītasya kālarātrivaśagatasya caramāśvāsapraśvāseṣūparudhyamāneṣu ekākino 'dvitīyasya asahāyasya imaṃ lokaṃ jahataḥ paralokamākramataḥ mahāpathaṃ vrajataḥ mahākāntāraṃ praviśataḥ mahāgahanaṃ samavagāhamānasya mahākāntāraṃ prapadyamānasya mahārṇavenohyamānasya karmavāyunā nīyamānasya nimittīkṛtāṃ diśaṃ vrajato nānyat trāṇaṃ nānyat śaraṇaṃ nānyat parāyaṇamṛte dharmāt / dharmo hi mahārāja tasmin samaye trāṇaṃ layanaṃ śaraṇaṃ bhavati / tadyathā- śītārtasyāgnipratāpaḥ, agnimadhyagatasyāpi nirvāpaṇam, uṣṇārtasya vā śaityam, adhvānaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Suppose, great king, four mountains were to come from the four directions — solid, substantial, unbroken, without cracks, without hollows, compact, of one mass, touching the sky and scraping the earth, crushing all grasses, wood, branches, leaves, foliage, and all living beings. From these, it would not be easy to flee by speed, nor to turn them back by strength, substances, mantras, or medicines. Even so, great king, these four great fears approach, from which it is not easy to flee by speed, nor to effect their turning back by strength, substances, mantras, or medicines. What four? Old age, disease, death, and misfortune. Old age, great king, approaches, crushing youth. Disease, great king, approaches, crushing health. Death, great king, approaches, crushing life. Misfortune, great king, approaches, crushing all prosperity. For what reason? Just as, great king, a lion, king of beasts, endowed with beauty, endowed with speed, with well-formed claws and fangs, having entered a herd of deer and seized a deer, does with it as he pleases — yet that king of beasts, encountering an overwhelmingly powerful and ferocious face, becomes helpless — even so, great king, for one pierced by the arrow of death, whose pride has departed, who is without protection, without refuge, without recourse, whose vital points are being severed, whose flesh and blood are drying up, whose face is parched with distress and bewilderment, who is engaged in throwing about hands and feet, who is incapable of action, who is powerless, who is smeared with saliva, mucus, pus, urine, and excrement, in whom but a trace of life remains, who from one existence grasps at another existence through <s>karma</s>, who is terrified by the fear of <s>Yama</s>'s messengers, who has fallen under the power of the night of death, whose final inhalations and exhalations are being obstructed, who is alone, without a second, without a companion, abandoning this world, entering the next world, traveling the great road, entering the great wilderness, plunging into the great thicket, entering the great desert, being carried by the great ocean, being driven by the wind of <s>karma</s>, going toward the destined direction — there is no other protection, no other refuge, no other recourse except <s>Dharma</s>. For <s>Dharma</s>, great king, at that time becomes protection, shelter, and refuge. Just as — for one afflicted by cold, the warmth of fire; for one caught in the midst of fire, its extinguishing; for one afflicted by heat, coolness; for one who has set out on a journey, a garden with cool shade; for one who is thirsty, cool water; for one who is hungry, excellent food; for one who is ill, physician, medicine, and attendants; for one who is terrified,

body.text: pratipannasya suśītalacchāyopavanam, pipāsitasya suśītalaṃ salilam, bubhukṣitasya vā praṇītamannam, vyādhitasya vā vaidyauṣadhaparicārakāḥ, bhayabhītasya balavantaḥ, sahāyāḥ sādhavaḥ pratiśaraṇā bhavanti // iti vistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: powerful ones, companions, virtuous ones become refuge.' Thus in detail. //

body.text: tasmādetadbhayaparihārārthaṃ kuśalapakṣeṣveva prajñāpariśodhiteṣu yatnaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, for the purpose of averting this fear, effort should be made only in the wholesome practices purified by wisdom. //

body.text: idānīṃ jātyādiduḥkhaduḥkhināṃ duḥkhāpaharaṇāya svāśayamāśaṅkayannāha evamityādi-
body.translated_text: Now, expressing his own aspiration for removing the suffering of those afflicted by the sufferings of birth and such, he says with 'thus' and so forth —

children.translated_text: When shall I bring peace to those scorched by the fire of suffering,
with my own provisions of happiness, arising from clouds of merit? // <s>Bca</s> 9.167 //

body.text: evamanantaroktayā nītyā duḥkhāgnitaptānām, duḥkhānyeva agnayaḥ tai saṃtāpitānāṃ sattvānāṃ śāntiṃ jātyādiduḥkhānalatāpapraśamanam / kuryāmahaṃ kadā, kasmin kāle kuryāṃ vidadhyām / katham? sukhopakaraṇaiḥ / sukhasyopakaraṇāni sukhasādhanāni vastrābharaṇānulepanaśayanāsanaprabhṛtīni / kiṃ tadupārjitaireva? netyāha- svakaiḥ svātmīyaiḥ / mayā svayamupārjitairityarthaḥ / kiṃ nirmāṇādipradarśitaiḥ? netyāha- puṇyameghasamudbhūtaiḥ, puṇyānyeva meghāḥ sarvaduḥkhasaṃtāpārtiśamanasukhopakaraṇaśītalavṛṣṭipradānanimittatvāt / tebhyaḥ samudbhūtāni nirjātāni, taiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, by the method just stated, for those scorched by the fires of suffering — the sufferings themselves being the fires, for beings heated by them — 'peace,' the quelling of the burning of the sufferings of birth and such — 'shall I bring,' at what time shall I bring about, shall I accomplish? How? 'With provisions of happiness' — the provisions, the means for happiness: garments, ornaments, ointments, beds, seats, and the like. Are these acquired by those [beings] themselves? No, he says: 'my own' — belonging to myself. Meaning: acquired by me personally. Are they displayed through magical creation and such? No, he says: 'arising from clouds of merit' — merits themselves are the clouds, because they are the cause of bestowing cool rains of provisions of happiness that quell the burning affliction of all suffering. 'Arising from those' — produced, come forth from them.

body.text: evamabhyudayasaṃpadi pareṣāṃ ceto vidhāya niḥśreyasasaṃpadi pradarśayannāha kadetyādi-
body.translated_text: Having thus directed the mind toward the worldly welfare of others, indicating [his aspiration] for the welfare of ultimate liberation, he says with 'when' and so forth —

children.translated_text: When shall I teach emptiness to those with views of apprehension,
through conventional [truth] and non-apprehension, with devotion to the accumulation of merit? // <s>Bca</s> 9.168 //

body.text: kadā kasmin kāle upalambhadṛṣṭibhyo bhāvagrāhābhiniviṣṭebhyo deśayiṣyāmi prakāśayiṣyāmi / śūnyatāṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatām / katham? saṃvṛtyā vyavahāreṇa / anyathā vikalpāviṣayatayā paramārthaśūnyasya śūnyatāyā deśayitumaśakyatvāt / evaṃ niḥśreyasahetujñānasaṃbhāranimittamupadarśitam / tatkāraṇaṃ puṇyasaṃbhāranidānamupadarśayannāha- puṇyetyādi / puṇyasya jñānādeḥ saṃbhāraṃ kadā upalambhadṛṣṭibhyo deśayiṣyāmīti saṃbandhaḥ / ādarāditi mahatā gauraveṇa / satkṛtya na yadṛcchayā / kena prakāreṇa? anupalambhena, deyadāyakapratigrāhakāditritayānupalambhayogena / trikoṭipariśuddhyeti yāvat / evamupacitaḥ puṇyasaṃbhāro buddhatādhigamāya jāyate / tadevamanena sarveṇa aśeṣasaṃkleśahetusarvasamāropavikalpapratipakṣatayā sarvāvaraṇaprahāṇopāyatvāt samastatathāgatādhigamahetutvācca sarvaduḥkhopaśamopāyaprajñā upajāyate ityupadarśitaṃ bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: 'When' — at what time — 'to those with views of apprehension' — to those attached to grasping at entities — 'shall I teach,' shall I illuminate — 'emptiness' — the absence of intrinsic nature in all <s>dharmas</s>. How? 'Through the conventional' — through everyday discourse. Because otherwise, since the ultimately empty emptiness, being beyond the scope of conceptual construction, cannot be taught. Thus the cause for the accumulation of knowledge, which is the means for ultimate liberation, has been indicated. Indicating the cause for the accumulation of merit, he says with 'merit' and so forth. 'The accumulation of merit' — of knowledge and such — 'when shall I teach to those with views of apprehension?' — this is the connection. 'With devotion' — with great reverence. Respectfully, not casually. In what manner? 'Through non-apprehension' — through the practice of non-apprehension of the triad of gift, giver, and recipient. That is to say, through the purity of the three spheres (<s>trikoṭipariśuddhi</s>). The accumulation of merit thus cultivated becomes the cause for the attainment of Buddhahood. Thus, by all of this, it has been shown that there arises the wisdom that is the means for the cessation of all suffering, because it is the antidote to all conceptual superimposition that is the cause of all affliction, because it is the means for the abandonment of all obscurations, and because it is the cause for the attainment of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.translated_text: Those wise ones whose sharp wisdom, penetrating the profound method, has removed error,
who are elevated by stainless knowledge on the side of purification from affliction —

children.text: te santo guṇadoṣayorapi ca taiḥ sāraṃ vimiśrādato
children.translated_text: they being virtuous, and from them the essence, distinguishing between qualities and faults, should be taken from what is mixed;

children.text: grāhyaṃ sarvamakalmaṣaṃ viṣamiva tyājyaṃ duruktaṃ yadi //
children.translated_text: everything that is pure should be accepted, and if there be any ill-spoken words, they should be discarded like poison.

children.text: na yuktamuktaṃ kimapīha yanmayā paraṃ prajātaṃ skhalitaṃ tadeva me /
children.translated_text: Whatever I have said here that is not well-stated, that alone is my error, having been produced through transgression.

children.text: nanu grahīṣyanti mamātra sādhavo matiṃ mayānena kṛtena sāṃpratam //
children.translated_text: Surely the good will understand my intention now, through this work I have composed.

body.text: api ca-
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: yaḥ saṃvṛtyā vrajati manaso gocaratvaṃ kathaṃcit
children.translated_text: That which somehow, conventionally, enters the range of the mind —

children.text: tādṛśyarthe skhalati na matiḥ kasya vai mādṛśasya /
children.translated_text: in a matter of such [profundity], whose understanding does not stumble, one such as I?
For those who possess discernment of the meaning of well-spoken words, who are recipients of the <s>Madhyamaka</s> tradition —
seeing here some small portion of merit, may there arise the attitude of acceptance.
Having composed this exposition of <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom), adorned with lucid explanatory words,
by me, for the pacification of the dense delusion of views opposed to right knowledge —

children.text: yatpuṇyaṃ samupārjitaṃ hitaphalaṃ tenāśu sarvo jano
children.translated_text: whatever merit has been earned, yielding the fruit of benefit — by that, may all people quickly
become, like <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the sole abode of excellent qualities, a mine of wisdom!

body.text:
iti prajñākaramativiracitāyāṃ bodhicaryāvatārapañjikāyāṃ
prajñāpāramitāparicchedo navamaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Thus, in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā</s> composed by <s>Prajñākaramati</s>,
the ninth chapter on the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: kṛtiriyaṃ paṇḍitabhikṣuprajñākara[mati]pādānām //
body.translated_text: This is the work of the learned monk (<s>paṇḍita-bhikṣu</s>) <s>Prajñākaramati</s>.

body.text:
* * * *
[lekhakaviracitā praśastiḥ]

children.translated_text: This commentary, supreme, with well-composed words, pure, delighting the mind,
is like a boat-vessel for people crossing to the other shore of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: āśu prāptikarī jinasya padavīṃ sādya likhitvā mayā
children.translated_text: Swiftly bringing attainment of the path of the <s>Jina</s>, having been properly written by me,

children.text: prāptaṃ yatkuśalaṃ susaṃpadi padaṃ tenāstu buddho janaḥ //
children.translated_text: whatever wholesome merit has been gained — by that, may people attain the state of auspicious <s>Buddha</s>hood!

body.translated_text:
* * * *
[Colophon composed by the scribe]

children.translated_text: In the year connected with ninety-eight [and] a hundred [i.e., 198],
on the dark [fortnight] of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, on the fifth day, on Tuesday —
In the reign of the glorious <s>Śaṅkaradeva</s>, who is victorious,
this auspicious [manuscript] has been written, the commentary called <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s>[-ṭīkā].
In the lovely city of <s>Śrī Lalitapura</s>, at the [place] called <s>Śrī Mānīśvala</s>,
in the <s>vihāra</s>, the abode of the <s>Sugata</s>, of the one named <s>Śrī Rāghava</s> (?),
this is the blessed book of the elder monk (<s>sthavira-bhikṣu</s>) <s>Buddhacandra</s> (?);
by the merit of that, may one attain <s>Bodhisattva</s>-hood, the supreme state.
May the clouds release water as desired,
may the earth be endowed with abundant crops (?),

children.text: avatu narapatiḥ prajā vināmrāḥ (?) bhavatu rayanapateḥ sukhātivṛddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: may the king protect the people who bow humbly (?), may there be great increase of happiness for the lord of wealth!

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: / kāyasthaḥ bhuvanākara[va]rmaṇa[ṇā]likhitamiti //
body.translated_text: Written by the scribe <s>Bhuvanākara[va]rman</s>.

body.text: 10. pariṇāmanāparicchedo daśamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 10. The tenth chapter, on Dedication (<s>Pariṇāmanā</s>).

children.translated_text: Whatever wholesome [merit] I have [gained] by contemplating the Entrance into the Conduct of Awakening (<s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s>) —

children.text: tena sarve janāḥ santu bodhicaryāvibhūṣaṇāḥ // Bca_10.1 //
children.translated_text: by that, may all people become adorned with the conduct of awakening. // <s>Bca</s> 10.1 //
In all directions, as many as are afflicted by suffering of body and mind —
may they obtain, through my merits, oceans of happiness and joy! // <s>Bca</s> 10.2 //
May their happiness never diminish throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>;
may the world unceasingly attain the happiness of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.3 //
Whatever hells there are in the world-realms —
may the beings therein rejoice with the joys and delights of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.4 //
May those suffering from cold obtain warmth; may those suffering from heat become cool,
through oceans of water arisen from the great clouds of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.5 //
May the Sword-Leaf Forest become for them radiant like the <s>Nandana</s> garden;
may the thorny <s>śālmalī</s> trees become wish-fulfilling trees! // <s>Bca</s> 10.6 //
With lakes lovely with the delightful clamor of <s>kādamba</s> geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, swans, and others,
with abundant lotus fragrance — may the regions of hell become delightful! // <s>Bca</s> 10.7 //

children.text: so 'ṅgārarāśirmaṇirāśirastu taptā ca bhūḥ sphāṭikakuṭṭimaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: May those heaps of burning coals become heaps of jewels; may the scorching ground become a crystal floor;
may the Crushing Mountains become celestial mansions of worship, filled with <s>Sugatas</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.8 //
May the rain of burning coals, heated stones, and weapons henceforth become a rain of flowers;

children.text: tacchastrayuddhaṃ ca paraspareṇa krīḍārthamadyāstu ca puāpayuddham // Bca_10.9 //
children.translated_text: may their mutual fighting with weapons henceforth become a playful battle with flowers! // <s>Bca</s> 10.9 //
Those whose flesh has entirely fallen off, with bodies of white bones like <s>kunda</s> flowers,
plunged into the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> [river] whose waters are like fire —
by the power of my wholesome [merit], having attained divine embodiment,
may they dwell at the <s>Mandākinī</s> [river] together with celestial maidens! // <s>Bca</s> 10.10 //

body.text:
trastāḥ paśyantvakasmādiha yamapuruṣāḥ kākagṛdhrāśca ghorā
dhvāntaṃ dhvastaṃ samantātsukharatijananī kasya saumyā prabheyam /
body.translated_text: Let them look in wonder — 'why have <s>Yama</s>'s servants, the terrible crows and vultures here suddenly become frightened? The darkness is dispelled all around — whose is this gentle, joy-producing radiance?'

body.text: ityūrdhva prekṣamāṇā gaganatalagataṃ vajrapāṇiṃ jvalantaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus gazing upward, seeing blazing <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> stationed in the vault of the sky,

body.text: dṛṣṭvā prāmodyavegādvayapagataduritā yāntu tenaiva sārdham // Bca_10.11 //
body.translated_text: with the force of their joy, their sins departed, may they go with him! // <s>Bca</s> 10.11 //

children.translated_text: A rain of lotuses falls, mixed with fragrant water,
and is seen extinguishing the fires of hell —
'What is this?' — suddenly flooded with happiness —
may the vision of <s>Kamalapāṇi</s> (Lotus-Handed One) appear to the hell-beings! // <s>Bca</s> 10.12 //

children.text: āyātāyāta śīghraṃ bhayamapanayata bhrātaro jīvitāḥ smaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Come, come quickly! Cast away fear! Brothers, we are alive!
There has arrived among us this radiant <s>Cīrīkumāra</s> (ever-youthful one), whoever he is, whose hand [gesture grants] fearlessness;
by whose power all suffering has departed, torrents of joy have flowed forth,

children.text: jātaṃ saṃbodhicittaṃ sakalajanaparitrāṇamātā dayā ca // Bca_10.13 //
children.translated_text: the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) has been born, along with compassion, the mother that rescues all beings.' // <s>Bca</s> 10.13 //
'Behold him, whose lotus-feet are worshipped by the diadems of a hundred gods,
whose gaze is moist with compassion, upon whose head falls a shower of abundant flowers,
with delightful mansions resounding with the praise of thousands of celestial women singing —'

children.text: dṛṣṭvāgre mañjughoṣaṃ bhavatu kalakalaḥ sāṃprataṃ nārakāṇām // Bca_10.14 //
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> before them, may there arise an uproar [of joy] among the hell-beings! // <s>Bca</s> 10.14 //
Thus, through my wholesome [merit], seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-clouds, headed by <s>Samantabhadra</s>, unobscured,
with rains of pleasant, cool, fragrant breezes — may those hell-beings rejoice! // <s>Bca</s> 10.15 //
May the intense sensations of hell-beings be pacified, and their fears;
may all dwellers in the lower realms be freed from the lower realms! // <s>Bca</s> 10.16 //
May the fear of mutual devouring among animals depart;

children.text: bhavantu sukhinaḥ pretā yathottarakurau narāḥ // Bca_10.17 //
children.translated_text: may the hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>) become happy, like the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.17 //

children.text: saṃtarpyantāṃ pretāḥ strāpyantāṃ śītalā bhavantu sadā /
children.translated_text: May the <s>pretas</s> be satisfied, may they be bathed, may they always become cool,
by the streams of milk flowing from the hand of noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.18 //

children.text: andhāḥ paśyantu rūpāṇi śṛṇvantu badhirāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: May the blind see forms; may the deaf always hear;
may pregnant women give birth painlessly, like <s>Māyādevī</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.19 //
Garments, food, drink, garlands, sandalwood, and ornaments —
may they obtain everything desired by the mind, conducive to welfare! // <s>Bca</s> 10.20 //
May the fearful become fearless; may those afflicted with sorrow gain joy;

children.text: udvigrāśca nirudvegā dhṛtimanto bhavantu ca // Bca_10.21 //
children.translated_text: may the anxious be free from anxiety and become resolute! // <s>Bca</s> 10.21 //
May the sick have good health; may they be freed from all bondage;

children.text: durbalā balinaḥ santu strigdhacittāḥ parasparam // Bca_10.22 //
children.translated_text: may the weak become strong, with hearts full of affection for one another! // <s>Bca</s> 10.22 //

children.text: sarvā diśaḥ śivāḥ santu sarveṣāṃ pathivartinām /
children.translated_text: May all directions be auspicious for all travelers on the road;

children.text: yena kāryeṇa gacchanti tadupāyena sidhyatu // Bca_10.23 //
children.translated_text: whatever purpose they travel for, may it be accomplished by [appropriate] means! // <s>Bca</s> 10.23 //
May those who have embarked on boats and ships have their wishes fulfilled;

children.text: kṣemeṇa kūlamāsādya ramantāṃ saha bandhubhiḥ // Bca_10.24 //
children.translated_text: having safely reached the shore, may they rejoice with their kinfolk! // <s>Bca</s> 10.24 //
May those who have fallen onto wrong paths in the wilderness find the company of a caravan;
and may they travel without fatigue, free from fear of thieves, tigers, and the like! // <s>Bca</s> 10.25 //
For those asleep, intoxicated, or heedless, in the distress of illness, wilderness, and such,
for the helpless, the young, and the old — may the deities provide protection! // <s>Bca</s> 10.26 //
May they be freed from all unfavorable states, endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion,
possessed of good appearance and conduct, and always remembering their former lives! // <s>Bca</s> 10.27 //
May their treasuries become inexhaustible, like the storehouse of the sky;
free from conflict and hardship, may they be of independent livelihood! // <s>Bca</s> 10.28 //
May beings of little splendor become of great splendor;
may those who are deformed and wretched become endowed with beauty! // <s>Bca</s> 10.29 //

children.text: yāḥ kāścana striyo loke puruṣatvaṃ vrajantu tāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever women there are in the world, may they attain manhood;

children.text: prāpnuvantūccatāṃ nīcā hatamānā bhavantu ca // Bca_10.30 //
children.translated_text: may the lowly attain high station, and may the proud become humble! // <s>Bca</s> 10.30 //
By this merit of mine, may all beings without exception,

children.text: viramya sarvapāpebhyaḥ kurvantu kuśalaṃ sadā // Bca_10.31 //
children.translated_text: desisting from all evil deeds, always perform the wholesome! // <s>Bca</s> 10.31 //
Never separated from <s>bodhicitta</s>, devoted to the conduct of awakening,
embraced by the <s>Buddhas</s>, and free from the works of <s>Māra</s> — // <s>Bca</s> 10.32 //
May all those beings have immeasurable lifespans;

children.text: nityaṃ jīvantu sukhitā mṛtyuśabdo 'pi naśyatu // Bca_10.33 //
children.translated_text: may they always live happily, and may the very word 'death' perish! // <s>Bca</s> 10.33 //
May all directions become delightful, with gardens of wish-fulfilling trees,
filled with <s>Buddhas</s> and sons of <s>Buddhas</s>, with enchanting sounds of <s>Dharma</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.34 //
Free from pebbles and such, level, smooth as the palm of a hand,

children.text: mṛdvī ca vaiḍūryamayī bhūmiḥ sarvatra tiṣṭhatu // Bca_10.35 //
children.translated_text: soft and made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) — may the earth everywhere abide! // <s>Bca</s> 10.35 //
May the great assemblies of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> sit everywhere in circles,
adorning the surface of the earth with their own radiance! // <s>Bca</s> 10.36 //
From birds, from all trees, from rays of light, and from the sky —
may the sound of <s>Dharma</s> be heard unceasingly by all embodied beings! // <s>Bca</s> 10.37 //
May they always encounter <s>Buddhas</s> and sons of <s>Buddhas</s>;
with infinite clouds of offerings, may they worship the Teacher of the world! // <s>Bca</s> 10.38 //
May the god rain at the proper time, and may the harvest be abundant;

children.text: sphīto bhavatu lokaśca rājā bhavatu dhārmikaḥ // Bca_10.39 //
children.translated_text: may the world be prosperous, and may the king be righteous! // <s>Bca</s> 10.39 //

children.text: śaktā bhavantu cauṣadhyo mantrāḥ sidhyantu jāpinām /
children.translated_text: May medicines be efficacious, and may <s>mantras</s> succeed for those who recite them;
may <s>ḍākinīs</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and others be filled with compassion! // <s>Bca</s> 10.40 //

children.text: mā kaścidduḥkhitaḥ sattvo mā pāpī mā ca rogitaḥ /
children.translated_text: May no being be unhappy, may none be sinful, may none be ill;

children.text: mā hīnaḥ paribhūto vā mā bhūtkaścicca durmanāḥ // Bca_10.41 //
children.translated_text: may none be debased or despised, and may no one ever be despondent! // <s>Bca</s> 10.41 //
May the monasteries be well-established, resounding with recitation and study;

children.text: nityaṃ syātsaṃghasāmagrī saṃghakāryaṃ ca sidhyatu // Bca_10.42 //
children.translated_text: may the <s>Saṃgha</s> always be in harmony, and may the aims of the <s>Saṃgha</s> be accomplished! // <s>Bca</s> 10.42 //
May monks who desire the training obtain solitude;
may they meditate with workable minds, free from all distraction! // <s>Bca</s> 10.43 //
May nuns obtain their requisites, free from quarrels and troubles;
and may all renunciants likewise be of unbroken moral conduct! // <s>Bca</s> 10.44 //
May those of poor conduct be filled with remorse, ever devoted to the exhaustion of evil;
may they attain the happy destiny of a <s>Sugata</s>, and therein may their vows be unbroken! // <s>Bca</s> 10.45 //
May the learned be honored and receive alms;
may their mind-streams be pure, and may their fame extend in all directions! // <s>Bca</s> 10.46 //
Without experiencing the suffering of the lower realms, and without arduous austerities,
may the world attain <s>Buddhahood</s> with a single divine body! // <s>Bca</s> 10.47 //
May all <s>Samyak-saṃbuddhas</s> be worshipped by all beings in manifold ways;
may [all beings] be abundantly happy with the inconceivable bliss of a <s>Buddha</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.48 //
May the aspirations of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> for the welfare of the world be fulfilled;
whatever those Protectors intend — may that be accomplished for beings! // <s>Bca</s> 10.49 //
May the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> be happy, and likewise the <s>Śrāvakas</s>,
always being worshipped with reverence by gods, <s>asuras</s>, and humans! // <s>Bca</s> 10.50 //
May I always attain the memory of past lives and ordination,
up to the stage of <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyous), through the grace of <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>! // <s>Bca</s> 10.51 //
May I sustain myself with whatever posture, endowed with strength;
may I attain the requisites of dwelling in solitude in all my births! // <s>Bca</s> 10.52 //

children.text: yadā ca draṣṭukāmaḥ syāṃ praṣṭukāmaśca kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: And whenever I wish to see or ask about anything,
may I behold that very Protector, <s>Mañjunātha</s>, without obstruction! // <s>Bca</s> 10.53 //
In accomplishing the welfare of all beings throughout the ten directions to the ends of space,

children.text: yathā carati mañjuśrīḥ saiva caryā bhavenmama // Bca_10.54 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Mañjuśrī</s> conducts himself — may that very conduct be mine! // <s>Bca</s> 10.54 //
As long as space endures, and as long as the world endures,
so long may I endure, destroying the sufferings of the world! // <s>Bca</s> 10.55 //
Whatever suffering there is in the world — may all of it ripen upon me;
and through all the virtues of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, may the world be happy! // <s>Bca</s> 10.56 //
May the Teaching — the sole medicine for the world's suffering, the source of all prosperity and happiness,
accompanied by gain and honor — endure for a long time! // <s>Bca</s> 10.57 //
I pay homage to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, through whose grace the mind turns toward virtue;
I salute the spiritual friend, through whose grace it grows! // <s>Bca</s> 10.58 //

body.text: // bodhicaryāvatāre pariṇāmanāparicchedo daśamaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The tenth chapter on Dedication in the <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s>. //

body.text: // samāpto 'yaṃ bodhicaryāvatāraḥ / kṛtirācāryaśāntidevasya //
body.translated_text: // This <s>Bodhicaryāvatāra</s> is complete. The composition of Ācārya <s>Śāntideva</s>. //
